thereby providing privacy to the author attribute.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
Replacing slang words: When changing from teen
to adult, A4NT often replaces the slang words or incor-
rectly spelled words with standard English words, as seen
in category #2 in Table VII.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
For example, replacing “wad”
(what) with “deﬁnitely”, “wadeva” with “perhaps” and
“nuthing” with “ofcourse”.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
The opposite effect is seen
when going from adult to teenager, with addition of “diz”
(this) and replacing of “think” with “relized” (realized).
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
These changes are learned entirely from the data, and
would be very hard to encode explicitly in a rule-based
system due to the variety in slangs and spelling mistakes.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
Semantic changes: One failure mode of A4NT is
when the input sentence has semantic content which is
signiﬁcantly more biased to the author’s class.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
These
examples are shown in category #3 in Table VII.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
For
example, when an adult author mentions his “wife”, the
A4NT network replaces it with “crush”, altering the mean-
ing of the input sentence.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
Some common entity pairs
where this behavior is seen are with (school↔work),
(class↔ofﬁce), (dad↔husband), (mum↔wife), and so
on.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
Arguably, in such cases, there is no obvious solution
to mask the identity of the author without altering these
obviously biased content words.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
On the smaller speech dataset however, the changes
made by the A4NT model alter the semantics of the sen-
tences in some cases.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
Few example style transfers from
Obama to Trump’s style are shown in Table VIII.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
We
see that A4NT inserts hyperbole (“better than anybody”,
“horrible horrible”, “crooked”), references to “media” and
“system”, all salient features of Trump’s style.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
We see
that the style-transfer here is quite successful, sufﬁcient
to completely fool the identity classiﬁer as was seen in Ta-
ble III.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
However, and somewhat expectedly, the semantics
of the input sentence is generally lost.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
A possible cause is
that the attribute classiﬁer is too strong on this data, owing
to the small dataset size and the highly distinctive styles
of the two authors, and to fool them the A4NT network
learns to make drastic changes to the input text.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:

theA4NT outputs to score below the decision boundary,
while also not increasing the classiﬁer score compared to

title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

We see that for the most part all three A4NT models are
below or close to this ideal line.

As the input text gets
more difﬁcult (increasing attribute classiﬁer score), the
CycML and CycML+Lang slightly cross above the ideal
line, but still provide signiﬁcant improvement over the
input text (drop in classiﬁer score of about ∼0.45).

6
Conclusions
We presented a novel fully automatic method for protect-
ing privacy sensitive attributes of an author against NLP
based attackers.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
Our solution, the A4NT network, is de-
veloped using a novel application of adversarial training
to machine translation networks to learn to protect private
attributes.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
The A4NT network achieves this by learning
to perform style-transfer without paired data.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
A4NT offers a new data driven approach to authorship
obfuscation.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
The ﬂexibility of this end-to-end trainable
model means it can adapt to new attack methods and
datasets.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
Experiments on three different attributes namely
age, gender and identity, showed that the A4NT network
is able to effectively fool the attribute classiﬁers in all
the three settings.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
We also show that the A4NT network
also performs well against multiple unseen classiﬁer ar-
13


chitectures.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
This strong empirical evidence suggests that
the method is likely to be effective against previously
unknown NLP adversaries.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
We developed a novel solution to preserve the mean-
ing of input text using likelihood of reconstruction.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
Se-
mantic similarity (quantiﬁed by meteor score) of the
A4NT network remains high for easier sentences, which
do not contain obvious give-away words (school, work,
husband etc.), but is lower on difﬁcult sentences indicat-
ing the network effectively learns to identify and apply
the right magnitude of change.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
The A4NT network can be
operated at different points on the privacy-effectiveness
and semantic-similarity trade-off curve, and thus offers
ﬂexibility to the user.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
The experiments on the political
speech data show the limits to which style transfer based
approach can be used to hide attributes.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
On this chal-
lenging data with very distinct styles by the two authors,
our method effectively fools the identity classiﬁer but
achieves this by altering the semantics of the input text.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
In future work we would like to explore generator ar-
chitectures to extend A4NT framework to structured data
like code, to protect against code stylometric attacks.

text:
A
Appendix - Differentiability of discrete
samples
To obtain an output sentence sample
˜sy from the
A4NT network Zxy, we can sample from the distribution
p( ˜wt|sx), shown in (5), repeatedly until a special ‘END’
token is sampled.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
This naive sampling though is not suit-
able for training Z within a GAN framework as sampling
from multinomial distribution, p( ˜wt|sx), is not differen-
tiable.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
To make sampling differentiable we follow the ap-
proach used in [35] and use the Gumbel-Softmax approx-
imation [36] to obtain differentiable soft samples from
p( ˜wt|sx).
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
The gumbel-softmax approximation includes
two parts.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
First, the re-parametrization trick using the
gumbel random variable is applied to make the process of
sampling from a multinomial distribution differentiable
with respect to the probabilities p( ˜wt|sx).
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
Next, softmax
is used to approximate the arg-max operator to obtain
“soft” samples instead of one-hot vectors.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
This makes
the samples themselves differentiable.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
Thus, the gumbel-
softmax approximation allows differentiating through sen-
tence samples from the A4NT network enabling end-to-
end GAN training.
title: arXiv:1711.01921v3  [cs.CR]  19 Feb 2018

text:
Further details on gumbel-softmax
approximation can be found in [36, 47].

problem characterzing the integral Gauss curvature, which is introduced and
completely solved by Aleksandrov [1].

q-CRYSTALS AND q-CONNECTIONS
ANDRE CHATZISTAMATIOU
Abstract.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
We study how the category of q-connections depends on the choice
of coordinates.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
We exploit Bhatt’s and Scholze’s q-crystalline site, which is
based on a coordinate free formulation of q-PD structures, in order to re-
late q-crystals and q-connections in the p-adic setting.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
This yields a natural
equivalence between the the categories of q-connections for diﬀerent choices of
coordinates in the p-adic setting.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
The equivalence can be described explicitly
in terms of diﬀerential operators.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
In order to obtain a global equivalence, we patch the p-adic diﬀerential
operators to create a global one.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
The process is not entirely formal, and we
are only able to obtain a global equivalence after inverting 2.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
Introduction
The subject of this paper are Scholze’s conjectures about q-connections [Sch].
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
In
their simplest form q-connections are modules, satisfying a completeness condition,
over a certain subalgebra of the ring of diﬀerential operators.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
For example, let Rq = Z[x][[q −1]], and let Rq{∇x,q} be the (q −1)-completion of
the non commutative Rq-algebra generated by ∇x,q and satisfying ∇x,q · x −q · x ·
∇x,q = 1.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text: This is a q-deformation of the Weyl algebra Z[x]{∇x}.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
It is an arithmetic
phenomenon that this deformation depends on the coordinate x.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
Replacing Z by
Q would yield the trivial deformation of the Weyl algebra.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
The category of (q −1)-(derived) complete Rq{∇x,q}-modules is the category
of q-connections over Z[x] with respect to the coordinate x.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
According to the
conjectures of [Sch], this category does not depend on the choice of the coordinate x.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
For example, there should be a natural equivalence between the category of (q −1)-
(derived) complete Rq{∇x,q}-modules and (q −1)-(derived) complete Rq{∇x−1,q}-
modules, where ∇x−1,q · (x −1) −q · (x −1) · ∇x−1,q = 1.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text: Our paper exploits the notion of q-crystals introduced in [BS].
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
Our ﬁrst equiva-
lence is between q-crystals and q-HPD stratiﬁcations (Theorem 1.3.3).
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
Both notions
specialize to the respective classical notions in crystalline theory for q = 1, and the
proof of the equivalence follows from the crystalline formalism.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
The main obser-
vation, which allows us to run the crystalline formalism, is the existence of local
retractions in the q-crystalline site (Proposition 1.1.2).
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text: By deﬁnition, q-HPD stratiﬁcations depend on the choice of a “lifting”.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
Inde-
pendence of this choice is established via the identiﬁcation with q-crystals.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
The second equivalence is between (p, q−1)-completely ﬂat q-HPD stratiﬁcations
and (p, q−1)-completely ﬂat quasi-nilpotent q-connections (Proposition 2.1.4).
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
Indi-
rectly, it shows the independence of the choice of coordinates for (p, q−1)-completely
ﬂat quasi-nilpotent q-connections.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
By using diﬀerential operators, we can make this
independence explicit and extend it to all q-connections (Proposition 2.3.2).
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
All this
takes place in the p-adic setting and works for all primes.
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

This section heavily relies on [BS, §16].
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
Bhatt and Scholze introduce the notion
of a q-divided power algebra [BS, Deﬁnition 16.2], a q-divided power envelope [BS,
Lemma 16.10] and the q-crystalline site [BS, Deﬁnition 16.12].
title: arXiv:2010.02504v1  [math.AG]  6 Oct 2020

text:
These are major
innovations which allows them to glue a q-de Rham complex, prove some of the
conjectures in [Sch], and to relate their previous work on AΩ-complexes to prismatic
cohomology.

Abstract
For each s ∈{2, 4}, the generating function of Rs(n), the number of
partitions of n into odd parts or congruent to 0, ±s (mod 10), arises natu-
rally in regime III of Rodney Baxter’s solution of the hard-hexagon model
of statistical mechanics.

Introduction
A partition of a positive integer n is a sequence of positive integers whose sum
is n.

text:
The order of the summands is unimportant when writing the partitions
of n, but for consistency, a partition of n will be written with the summands
in a nonincreasing order [2].

given as:

ABSTRACT
Black hole environments often host plasmas that are fully collisionless or contain intrinsically col-
lisionless regions, including relativistic jets and coronae where particle energization is ubiquitous.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Capturing the physics of these systems requires numerical methods capable of modeling relativistic,
magnetized, collisionless plasmas in strong gravitational fields.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
In this work, we introduce the general-
relativistic module for the Entity – the first open-source, coordinate-agnostic performance-portable
particle-in-cell code.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
The code enables fast axisymmetric simulations of collisionless plasmas around
black holes on any modern high-performance computing architecture (both GPUs and CPUs).

INTRODUCTION
Black holes (BHs) are fundamental astrophysical ob-
jects whose influence extends across a vast range of
scales – from stellar environments to the intergalactic
medium – where they play a central role in regulat-
ing the formation and evolution of cosmic structures.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Because BHs cannot be observed directly, our under-
standing of them relies on interpreting their influence on
the surrounding plasma, which typically consists of elec-
trons, protons, heavier nuclei, and possibly positrons.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Significant progress in modeling such systems has been
made through magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simula-
tions, which assume that the plasma is in local ther-
modynamical equilibrium.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
General relativistic MHD
(GRMHD) further incorporates the effects of strong
gravity, essential for accurately describing physics in
curved spacetime (O.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
This framework
has already yielded numerous insights into the global be-
havior of plasmas around BHs.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
However, many phenomena associated with BHs re-
main poorly understood due to the numerical challenges
involved in modeling the relevant plasma regimes.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
A

prime example is the class of low-luminosity galactic
nuclei, including M87* and Sgr A*, which have been
imaged in unprecedented detail by the Event Horizon
Telescope.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
These systems exhibit hot accretion flows
(F.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Narayan 2014), where the plasma is es-
sentially collisionless: the mean free path for Coulomb
collisions exceeds the BH event horizon radius by about
six orders of magnitude.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Under such conditions, the
plasma cannot easily thermalize, rendering the assump-
tions underlying MHD formally invalid.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Nevertheless,
MHD remains a valuable tool for capturing the large-
scale dynamics governed by global conservation laws.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Furthermore, additional justification for the fluid ap-
proximation can arise from effective “fluidization” – that
is, effective collisionality induced by small-scale plasma
instabilities.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
In addition to their quiescent emission, many such
systems display episodic flaring activity characterized
by non-thermal spectra.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
For instance, Sgr A* produces
bright, multi-wavelength flares in the near-infrared, mid-
infrared, and X-ray bands (K.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Under-
standing these flares requires a detailed investigation
of the dynamics during such episodes, the mechanisms
arXiv:2511.17701v1  [astro-ph.HE]  21 Nov 2025


2
responsible for the generation of non-thermal particles,
and their resulting radiation.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Other regions of interest that are fundamentally colli-
sionless exist in both stellar-mass and supermassive BH
systems.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
A notable example is relativistic jets, which,
especially in the supermassive BH case, affect environ-
ments ranging from the immediate vicinity of the BH
to the intracluster medium.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Jet formation is widely
attributed to the Blandford–Znajek (BZ) mechanism
(R.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Znajek 1977), but interpreting
their morphology and emission requires modeling pair
loading, particle acceleration, and radiation mechanisms
– processes beyond the scope of standard GRMHD.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Another example is the X-ray-emitting corona of effi-
ciently accreting plasma flows, believed to be composed
of a hot, magnetized, collisionless plasma located in the
inner vicinity of the BH (A.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
The corona
likely dissipates magnetic energy through combination
of magnetic reconnection and turbulence.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
These considerations motivate the need for a frame-
work that treats the plasma as collisionless while still
incorporating the effects of strong gravity.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
Such an
approach is realized through the general-relativistic
particle-in-cell (GRPIC) method, first developed by K.

codes have been introduced (A.

first architecture-agnostic GRPIC code, which is pub-
licly available as part of the Entity framework.7

domain once they pass through the layer of cells where

and enter the ghost zone.

text:
SUMMARY
In this paper, we presented the general relativistic
module of the architecture-agnostic open-source PIC
code – Entity.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
The module implements a set of al-
gorithms which integrate the trajectories of charged
particles and the electromagnetic fields in the axisym-
metric (2.5D) curved spacetime using the 3+1 formal-
ism in Kerr–Schild coordinates, with an optional quasi-
spherical mapping.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
We demonstrated a set of standard
problem generators and tests, together with the relevant
parameter inputs, both of which are distributed with the
core of the code and are freely available10.
title: $\mathtt{Entity}$ -- Hardware-agnostic Particle-in-Cell Code for Plasma Astrophysics. II: General Relativistic Module

text:
While the
present release supports 2.5D axisymmetric Kerr-Schild
coordinates, future work will extend the method to 3D
using the cubed-sphere mesh.

Abstract
This document collects a written summary of all contributions presented at the workshop
“ αs(2019): Precision measurements of the strong coupling” held at ECT* (Trento) in Feb.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The workshop explored in depth the latest developments on the determination of
the QCD coupling αs from the key categories where high precision measurements are available:
(i) lattice QCD, (ii) hadronic τ decays, (iii) deep-inelastic scattering and parton distribution
functions, (iv) event shapes, jet cross sections, and other hadronic ﬁnal-states in e+e−collisions,
(v) Z boson and W boson hadronic decays, and (vi) hadronic ﬁnal states in p-p collisions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The
status of the current theoretical and experimental uncertainties associated to each extraction
method, and future perspectives were thoroughly reviewed.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Novel αs determination approaches
were discussed, as well as the combination method used to obtain a world-average value of the
QCD coupling at the Z mass pole.

Introduction
The strong coupling αs is one of the fundamental parameters of the Standard Model (SM), setting
the scale of the strength of the strong interaction theoretically described by Quantum Chromody-
namics (QCD).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Its value at the reference Z boson mass scale, in the conventional MS renormaliza-
tion scheme, amounts today to αs(mZ) = 0.1181 ± 0.0011 with a δαs/αs ≈1% uncertainty that
is orders of magnitude larger than that of any other fundamental coupling in nature.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Improving
our knowledge of αs is crucial, among other things, to reduce the theoretical uncertainties in the
high-precision calculations of all perturbative QCD (pQCD) processes whose cross sections or decay
rates depend on higher-order powers of αs, as is the case for virtually all those measured at the
LHC.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In the Higgs sector, our imperfect knowledge of αs (combined with that of the charm mass)
propagates today into total ﬁnal uncertainties of ∼4% for the H →gg (cc) partial width(s).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In the
electroweak sector, the input αs(mZ) value is the leading source of uncertainty in the calculation of
crucial precision pseudo-observables such as the Z boson width and its Z →bb (and other hadronic)
decay widths.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The QCD coupling plays also a fundamental role in the calculation of key quantities
in top-quark physics, such as the top mass, width, and Yukawa coupling.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The workshop “ αs(2019) – Precision measurements of the QCD coupling” was held at ECT*-
Trento in February 11–15, 2019 with the aim of bringing together experts from various ﬁelds to
explore in depth the latest developments on the determination of αs from the key categories where
high precision measurements and theoretical calculations are currently available.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The meeting
can be considered as the third one of a “series” that started with the “Workshop on Precision
Measurements of αs” (MPI, Munich, February 9–11, 2011; https://arxiv.org/abs/1110.0016),
and followed by the “High-Precision αs Measurements from LHC to FCC-ee” (CERN, Geneva,
October 2–13, 2015; https://arxiv.org/abs/1512.05194).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The presentations and discussions
focused on the following issues:
• What is the current state-of-the-art of each one of the αs determination methods, from the
theoretical and experimental perspectives?
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: • What is the status of those αs extractions that are not yet included in the world average?
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
• What is the current size of the theoretical (missing higher pQCD orders, electroweak correc-
tions, power-suppressed corrections, hadronization corrections,...) and experimental uncer-
tainties associated to each measurement?
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
• Are there improvements to be made in the combination of all αs extractions into the world
average αs of the Particle Data Group report?
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
One important goal of the workshop was to facilitate the discussion among the diﬀerent groups,
and in particular to give the speakers the opportunity to explain details that one would normally
not be able to present at a conference, but which have an important impact on the analyses.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

About
30 physicists took part in the workshop, and 25 talks were presented.

Pre-2019 Summaries of αs
Siegfried Bethke
Max-Planck-Institut f¨ur Physik, Munich
Abstract: Summaries of measurements of αs and determinations of world average values of
αs(mZ) are reviewed, spanning the time from 1989 to the latest update by the Particle Data Group
in 2016/2018.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Determinations of αs, the coupling parameter of the Strong Interaction between quarks and gluons,
became available since the early 1980’s, based on theoretical predictions of Quantum Chromody-
namics (QCD), in next-to-leading or higher order of perturbation theory, and on experimental data
at suﬃciently large energy scales.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Such determinations always were and continue to be challenging,
due to the relatively large perturbative and nonperturbative uncertainties which dominate most
of the measurements.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Determinations of αs, from diﬀerent physical processes, energy scales and
experiments, therefore do not necessarily agree with each other, within the quoted uncertainties of
results.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Therefore summaries of αs results and the determination of one overall “world average”
value became mandatory.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
One of the earliest and signiﬁcant of such summaries and extractions was published by Altarelli in
1989, resulting in αs(mZ) ≈0.11 ± 0.01, with an overall uncertainty of about 10% [1].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The latest
world summary of αs, in the 2016 and 2018 Reviews of Particle Physics edited by the Particle Data
Group (PDG) [2,3], quotes αs(mZ) = 0.1181±0.0011, with an overall uncertainty of just below 1%.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019
arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A (personal) selection of the history of summaries of αs is listed and referenced in Table 1 and
displayed in Figure 1.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: Details of the 2016 world summary of αs [2] are also presented in Ref.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Note that the overall uncertainty on αs(mZ) increased, from its 2014 to the 2016 value, which
is mainly due to an adjustment of the procedure to combine systematic uncertainties, as will be
discussed below.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In the following, a short recap of procedures used for deriving the most recent world average is
given.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019
arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

• the analysis must include reliable estimates of experimental, systematic and theoretical un-
certainties, based on commonly accepted procedures.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Next, the results are grouped into 6 classes of measurements that are based on similar or identical
types of data, calculations or procedures:
• decays of τ-leptons,
• deep inelastic lepton-nucleon scattering (DIS; until recently, only structure functions at
NNLO),
• lattice QCD,
• jets and hadronic event shapes in e+e−annihilation,
• electro-weak precision ﬁts,
• hadron collider results (so far, only tt cross section at NNLO),
and a pre-average is determined for each of these classes.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Finally, the world average is then de-
termined from these 6 pre-averages of classes.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Pre-averages are determined taking the unweighted
mean and average error.

The ﬁnal world average is then determined as the weighted mean of the class pre-averages, initially
treating their uncertainties as being uncorrelated and of Gaussian nature.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This determines the
ﬁnal world average value of αs(mZ).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The overall uncertainty of the world average is then adjusted
according to the following procedure:
If the overall χ2 is smaller than 1 per degree of freedom (d.o.f.), an overall correlation coeﬃcient
is introduced in the error matrix and adjusted such that χ2/d.o.f.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
is
larger than 1, all uncertainties are enlarged by a common factor such that χ2/d.o.f.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Note that
in both cases, adjusting a common correlation factor or enlarging all individual uncertainties, the
ﬁnal uncertainty of the average value increases with respect to the initial, “uncorrelated” starting
value!
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The results included in the 2016 and 2018 world summary of αs(mZ), together with the respective
pre-averages of classes and the ﬁnal world average, are displayed in Figure 2.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Note that in two of
the classes, no pre-averaging has been applied as only one individual result was available in each
case, at the time of the analysis (2016).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
As shown in Table 1 and Figure 1, the overall quoted uncertainty of αs(mZ) increased from 0.0006 (in
the review of 2014) to 0.0011 (review of 2016).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The reason for this increase was mainly procedural:
in 2014, pre-averages were not determined by taking the linear average of individual results and
their uncertainties, but by a method called “range-averaging”.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
There, pre-averages were determined
by taking the central value of the range of input values and half of this range interval, as central
value and its uncertainty, respectively.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
For the lattice results, which were expected to be essentially
uncorrelated with each other, the pre-average was determined using the χ2 method.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Figure 3 summarises the history and values of pre-averages of αs(mZ) for the diﬀerent classes of
measurements.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Note that the change in error determinations predominantly aﬀected the class of

text:

lattice results, whose uncertainty thus increased by a factor of two, using the most recent method
of taking the unweighted mean and error instead.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This, in turn, aﬀected the overall uncertainty of
the world average, which was (and still is, albeit to a lesser extent) dominated by the inﬂuence of
the lattice results.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The current status of determining the world average value of αs(mZ) is rather satisfying, showing
consistency and agreement within the quoted overall uncertainty of about 1%.

To my personal opinion, signiﬁcant improvements in the precision of measurements of αs, below
the 1% level, may mainly (only?) be expected from improved lattice calculations, and from high
statistics measurements of the Z0 lineshape (also called Giga-Z or Tera-Z), at future high-energy
e+e−collider projects.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
However, and maybe even more important from the viewpoint of testing the fundamental theory of
Strong Interactions, the successful and precise conﬁrmation of the concept of Asymptotic Freedom
and thus, the experimental “proof” of the key feature of QCD, is regarded to be one of the most
remarkable achievements of both, theoretical and experimental particle physics, see Figure 4.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: There are similarities and diﬀerences to the PDG approach [4].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The main diﬀerence is
that FLAG formulates a set of criteria, that computations have to pass in order to enter the average
of a given quantity of phenomenological interest [2].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These are based on whether the simulations
cover a range of parameters that allow to achieve a satisfactory control of systematic uncertainties
(labeled ⋆) a reasonable attempt can be made at estimating systematic uncertainties (◦), or it is
unlikely that systematic uncertainties can be brought under control ( ■).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The appearance of a
■
even in a single source of systematic error of a given lattice result, disqualiﬁes it from inclusion in
the global average.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
For the computations of αs, the usual criteria for chiral and inﬁnite volume extrapolations are
somewhat relaxed as they do not play a dominant role.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Instead criteria on perturbative behaviour
and renormalization scale try to make sure that the computation is at reasonable high µ, the
perturbative knowledge is suﬃciently good (i.e.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
the number of known loops, nl, is suﬃciently high)
and µ could be varied over some range in order to conﬁrm the perturbative µ-dependence.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The
general idea is that these criteria try to make sure that the available Monte Carlo data have a
few points located suﬃciently low in the landscape of Fig.

requires us to not be too far on the right.

Further progress
Finally, we collect some lessons that we have learned in our forming of a lattice world average of
αs.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: The basic problem is simple and has been spelled out often, phrased in varying words.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In order
to have a precise value with an error that can be estimated by perturbation theory itself, large
energy scales µ have to be reached and theory assumptions have to be kept at a minimum.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Further
progress will be limited if we include processes where non-perturbative contributions have to be
ﬁtted or removed by complicated analyses in order to make lower energies accessible.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Dealing with
non-perturbative physics is always based on assumptions – if only where the expansion in 1/µ
applies and lowest-order terms (1/µ)Nmin dominate.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We should therefore separate the determination of αs at high enough µ, simple theory, from tests
of perturbation theory, with resummations, studies of higher-twist contributions, etc.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The concept of criteria introduced by FLAG is very useful in this respect, and we advocate to
consider such a procedure for phenomenological determinations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
One should at least consider a
criterion on minimum values of µ, paired with suﬃciently high perturbative order.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In FLAG these
are the “renormalization scale” / “perturbative behaviour” criteria.

text:
In summary, the determination of αs from the moments of quarkonium correlators, while promising
also appears to be challenging.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
One of the challenge is the control of the continuum extrapolations,
which requires many calculations at small lattice spacings.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
So far this requirement is only met
in the 3-ﬂavor calculations with HISQ action [10].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Despite this, there seems to be an agreement
between the continuum extrapolated lattice results on the moments of the quarkonium correlators
from diﬀerent groups.

text:
This implies that diﬀerences in the quoted αs values are not caused by
problems in the lattice calculations, but rather the way lattice and perturbative calculations are
combined to obtain αs.

Introduction
The recent result for αs by the ALPHA collaboration relies on the combination of various tools and
techniques that have been developed and improved over the last 20–30 years.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A crucial ingredient is
the recursive step-scaling method [3] applied to QCD couplings renormalized in a ﬁnite Euclidean
space-time volume.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This allows us to overcome the typical limitation of lattice QCD, whereby
large scale diﬀerences cannot be resolved on a single lattice without incurring large computational
costs [4].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
As will become clear in this and in Mattia Dalla Brida’s companion contribution [2],
we have covered a range of energy scales diﬀering by 2–3 orders of magnitude, thus connecting
hadronic scales of O(100) MeV with electroweak scales of O(100) GeV.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The scale evolution of QCD
couplings in so-called Schr¨odinger functional (SF) schemes is obtained non-perturbatively and in
the continuum limit.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Given the good perturbative knowledge for the SF schemes one may assess at
which scale perturbative behaviour sets in and extract the Λ parameter.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In this way, the systematic
error due to the truncation of the perturbative series can be well-controlled and kept at a level that
remains subdominant compared to current statistical errors.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This is in contrast to many other
lattice determinations of αs where perturbative uncertainties arise at much lower energy scales and
are thus much harder to quantify.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: We remark that all our simulations are carried out for 3-ﬂavour QCD.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Therefore the result for
αs(mZ) in 5-ﬂavour QCD also relies on decoupling relations across charm and bottom quark thresh-
olds; I refer to [2] for references and a discussion.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The ALPHA collaboration’s strategy involves two
diﬀerent ﬁnite volume renormalization schemes for the 3-ﬂavour QCD coupling.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
At low energies,
a coupling based on the gradient ﬂow (GF) has advantageous properties (cf.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The high energy
regime is covered using a 1-parameter family of SF couplings, for which the 2-loop matching to the
MS-coupling and the 3-loop β-functions are known [5]–[8].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Our strategy then requires a matching
between the GF and SF couplings at an intermediate scale, µ0, which is implicitly deﬁned by the
SF coupling and turns out to be around 4 GeV in physical units.

Conclusion
We have studied the non-perturbative scale evolution of for a 1-parameter family of SF couplings
for energies between roughly 4 and 128 GeV.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We conclude that one needs to reach α ≈0.1 in order
to conﬁdently extract the Λ parameter with an error below 3%.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In a further consistency check we
ﬁrst converted the SF to the MS coupling and then varied the relative scale within a factor of two
either way around a preferred choice.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We note that this common recipe may nor may not capture
the true perturbative uncertainty.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This reinforces the general warning that perturbative truncation
errors are easily underestimated.

Conclusions
Lattice QCD oﬀers a very powerful framework for determining αs.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
By combining ﬁnite-volume
couplings and a step-scaling strategy, we were able to obtain a subpercent precision determination
of αs where all systematic uncertainties are under control.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These include the speciﬁc lattice QCD
systematics, i.e., discretization and ﬁnite-volume eﬀects, as well as the unavoidable uncertainties
originating from the use of perturbation theory in extracting αs.

Our result for αs in based on a
determination of ΛNf=3
MS
which relies on perturbation theory only at energy scales of O(100 GeV),
where we proved it accurate.

text:
The strong coupling was then extracted using perturbative decoupling
to match the Nf = 3 and Nf = 5 theories.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We argued that non-perturbative corrections to the
decoupling relations are not important at our level of precision.

thus much harder to reliably quantify.

In the ﬁrst part of this overview [1], we showed with concrete

Abstract: We present our latest determination of the strong coupling constant αs from the Quan-
tum Chromodynamics static energy: αs(mZ) = 0.1166+0.0012
−0.0008, extracted at three loops with leading
ultrasoft log resummation.

The determination is based on a combination of lattice data on the
static energy at small quark-antiquark distance and perturbative high-order calculations of the
static energy for small quark-antiquark distance.

coming extraction based on new lattice data, at smaller lattice spacings reaching shorter distances,
and on lattice data on the singlet free energy at ﬁnite temperature at very small distances.

The short-distance part

αs determination from static QCD potential with renormalon subtraction
Hiromasa Takaura
Department of Physics, Kyushu University, Fukuoka 819-0395, Japan
Abstract: In the current αs determinations based on lattice and perturbation theory, it is gen-
erally diﬃcult to take a wide enough matching range.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We avoid this problem by improvement of a
theoretical calculation: we use the OPE with renormalon subtraction, which is an extended frame-
work of perturbation theory.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This allows us to take the matching range widely as ΛQCDr ≲0.6,
where relatively low energy scales are included.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We obtain αs(mZ) = 0.1179+0.0015
−0.0014 from a reason-
able ﬁt for this wide range.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Introduction
The strong coupling αs is a fundamental parameter in the standard model, and its precision has an
impact on various studies of the standard model.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This parameter is determined by a matching of a
theoretical calculation and an experimental or lattice measurement of a QCD observable.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Among
determinations from various observables, the determinations using lattice data generally have small
errors.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In lattice determinations, however, the so-called window problem has been pointed out: it is diﬃcult
to take a wide enough matching range.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Accurate lattice simulation can be performed at the
scale well below its UV cutoﬀscale a−1, the inverse of the lattice spacing.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This lattice result
is matched with perturbation theory, where ﬁxed order results are currently accurate at Q ≳1–
2 GeV.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
With the typical lattice spacings available today, it is diﬃcult to take the range satisfying
1–2 GeV ≲Q ≪a−1 widely.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: The step-scaling method is known as a solution to the window problem.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This method enlarges the
validity range of the lattice simulations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: (The latest determination has been performed in Ref.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
[1].)
As an alternative approach, we enlarge the validity range of a theoretical calculation to lower energy
so that accurate lattice data (due to Q ≪a−1) are available.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
To this end, we use the operator
product expansion (OPE), which is an extended framework of perturbation theory.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: Perturbation theory suﬀers from an inevitable uncertainty known as renormalon uncertainty.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It is
induced from the divergent behavior of perturbative series where perturbative coeﬃcients typically
grow as ∼βn
0 n!
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
For the static QCD potential VQCD(r), the leading renormalon
uncertainty is O(ΛQCD), and the next-to-leading one is O(Λ3
QCDr2).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These errors are not negligible
at relatively long distances ΛQCDr ∼1, and give limitations of perturbation theory.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In the OPE, which can be regarded as an extension of perturbation theory, renormalon uncertainties
are considered to be eliminated.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In the following, we focus on the second renormalon uncertainty
rather than the ﬁrst one (which is r-independent and can be eliminated in the QCD force).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The
OPE of the static QCD potential is performed in the eﬀective ﬁeld theory, potential non-relativistic
QCD (pNRQCD) [2].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It is given in form of multipole expansion as
VQCD(r) = VS(r) + δEUS(r) + · · · ,
(1)
where the singlet potential VS(r) has a Coulomb-type potential and is the leading behavior at short
distances (VS(r) ∼1/r).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: A power correction in r is added as O(r2) (δEUS(r) ∼r2).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Since the
42


second term (and further higher order terms in r) are nonperturbative objects∗, a perturbative
expression of VS(r) coincides with that of VQCD(r).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Therefore, VS contains the renormalon uncer-
tainty of O(Λ3
QCDr2).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
An advantage of the OPE is that this renormalon is cancelled against that of
the second term δEUS(r).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: Then the OPE prediction has smaller error and has wider validity range than perturbation theory.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: However, it is diﬃcult to hold this advantage of the OPE in practical calculations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In particular,
with a naive perturbative calculation of VS, one again suﬀers from the renormalon uncertainty.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: Consider the case where one adds a power correction term of Ar2 to the perturbative result VS.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The ﬁtting parameter A [of O(Λ3
QCD)] can be extracted from the r2-term of VQCD(r) −VS(r).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
However, since VS has the error of O(Λ3
QCDr2), the nonperturbative eﬀect A has a signiﬁcant error.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
(The error is the same size as the nonperturbative eﬀect itself.) Thus, the introduction of the power
correction is almost meaningless because its coeﬃcient cannot be determined in practice.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: To avoid this feature, we use the OPE while subtracting renormalons in VS(r).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The use of such an
OPE allows us to use a wider range as shown below, and thus, it relaxes the window problem.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Our
ﬁt range is typically taken as 0.6 GeV ≲r−1 ≲4 GeV.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This is signiﬁcantly wider than previous
determinations from the static QCD potential, where typically 1 GeV ≲r−1 has been used.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Theoretical framework
We explain how we subtract renormalons and how we use the result in the OPE.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
First, we consider
renormalon subtraction from VS.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
VS(r) is given by
VS(r) = −4πCF

Conclusions
Lattice determinations often suﬀer from the window problem: a matching range cannot be taken
suﬃciently wide.

an extended framework of perturbation theory.

perturbation theory.

a reliable value of αs.

uncertainty.

Abstract: This contribution discusses two central problems in QCD: (a) the behavior of the
QCD running coupling αs(Q2) in both the nonperturbative and perturbative domains; and (b) the
elimination of perturbative QCD renormalization scale ambiguities.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Determining the QCD Coupling αs(Q2) at all Momentum Scales
The QCD running coupling αs(Q2) sets the strength of the interactions of quarks and gluons as
a function of the momentum transfer Q.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The dependence of the coupling at both small and high
momenta is needed to describe hadronic interactions at both long and short distances.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
As Grunberg has shown [1], the QCD running coupling can be deﬁned at all momentum scales
from a perturbatively calculable physical observable.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A particularly useful choice is the eﬀective
coupling αs
g1(Q2), which is deﬁned from Bjorken sum rule and is well measured [2].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
At high
momentum transfer, such “eﬀective charges” satisfy asymptotic freedom, obey the usual pQCD
renormalization group equations, and can be related to each other without scale ambiguity by
commensurate scale relations [3].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The “dilaton” soft-wall modiﬁcation of the AdS5 metric e+κ2z2, together with LF holography,
predicts the functional behavior of the running coupling in the small Q2 nonperturbative domain [4]:
αs
g1(Q2) = πe−Q2/4κ2.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Measurements of αs
g1(Q2) are remarkably consistent [2] with the Gaussian
form predicted by AdSQCD; the best ﬁt gives κ = 0.513 ± 0.007 GeV.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Deur, de T´eramond, and I [4,5,6] have shown how the parameter κ, which determines the mass scale
of hadrons and Regge slopes in the zero quark mass limit [6], can be connected to the mass scale Λs
controlling the evolution of the QCD coupling in the perturbative domain.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The high momentum
transfer dependence of the coupling αg1(Q2) is predicted by pQCD.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The matching of the high and
low momentum transfer regimes of αg1(Q2) – both its value and its slope – then determines a scale
Q0 = 0.87 ± 0.08 GeV which sets the interface between perturbative and nonperturbative hadron
dynamics.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This connection can, in fact, be done for any choice of renormalization scheme, such as
the MS scheme.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The result of this perturbative/nonperturbative matching is an eﬀective QCD coupling deﬁned at
all momenta.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The predicted value of ΛMS = 0.339 ± 0.019 GeV from this analysis agrees well
the measured value [7] ΛMS = 0.332 ± 0.017 GeV.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These results, combined with the AdS/QCD
superconformal predictions [8] for hadron spectroscopy, allow one to compute hadron masses in
terms of ΛMS: mp =
√
2κ = 3.21 ΛMS, mρ = κ = 2.2 ΛMS, and mp =
√
2mρ, meeting a challenge
proposed by Zee [9].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The mass scale κ underlying conﬁnement and hadron masses can thus be
connected to the parameter ΛMS in the QCD running coupling by matching the nonperturbative
prediction to the perturbative QCD regime.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We have also proposed that the value of Q0, which marks the interface of nonperturbative and
perturbative QCD, can be used to set the factorization scale for DGLAP evolution of hadronic
structure functions and ERBL evolution of distribution amplitudes [10].

text:
The Thrust Distribution in Electron-Positron Annihilation using
the Principle of Maximum Conformality
The Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC) [11,15,16,17,18] provides a rigorous, systematic
way to eliminate renormalization scheme-and-scale ambiguities for perturbative QCD.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Since the
PMC predictions do not depend on the choice of the renormalization scheme, PMC scale-setting
satisﬁes the principles of renormalization group invariance [19,20].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The PMC provides the underlying principle for extending the Brodsky-Lepage-Mackenzie (BLM)
scale-setting method [21] to all orders in pQCD.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The essential step is to identify the β terms at
each order of the pQCD series.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The PMC scales are ﬁxed at every order in pQCD by absorbing the
β terms that govern the behavior of the running coupling via the renormalization group equation
(RGE).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The divergent renormalon terms disappear, and thus the convergence of the pQCD series
is greatly improved.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The PMC method also sets the renormalization scales for observables that
depend on several invariants.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The number of active quark ﬂavors nf is set at each order, matching
the virtuality of the scattering process.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The PMC reduces in the Abelian limit, NC →0 [22], to
the standard Gell-Mann-Low method [23].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

µr = √s = mZ, and thus only one value of αs at scale mZ can be extracted.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The resulting
predictions does not ﬁt the measured thrust distribution, and it is incorrect for the QED analog.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
After using the PMC, we obtain a self-consistent determination of αs at diﬀerent scales over a wide
range of the thrust distribution.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Moreover, since the PMC predictions eliminate the renormalization
scale uncertainty, the extracted values for αs(Q2) are not plagued by any uncertainty in the choice
of µr.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Thus, remarkably, the PMC provides a new way to determine the running of αs(Q2) and
verify asymptotic freedom from the measurement of jet distributions in e+e−annihilation at a
single energy of √s.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In conclusion, the thrust variable in e+e−annihilation provides an ideal platform for testing the
52


QCD.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In the case of the conventional scale setting, the predictions are scheme-and-scale dependent,
and do not match the experimental results; the extracted coupling constant deviates from the
world average.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In contrast, after applying PMC scale-setting, we obtain a comprehensive and self-
consistent analysis for the thrust measurements, including both the diﬀerential distributions and
the mean values.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The PMC scale reﬂects the virtuality of the QCD dynamics, and it correctly sets
the number of active quark ﬂavors nf at every order as a function of the thrust.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It allows one
to determine αs(Q2) at diﬀerent momentum scales by comparing the PMC predictions with the
experiment measured at a single center-of-mass-energy √s.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: This analysis shows the importance of correct renormalization scale-setting.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The PMC method
rigorously eliminates an unnecessary theoretical uncertainty for all pQCD predictions, and it has
general applicability for all precision tests of QCD.

Asymptotic freedom, manifested by a decreasing coupling with increasing energy, can be considered
as the basic prediction of nonabelian gauge theories [11,12].

title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The ABMP16 PDF ﬁt [1] is based on a combination of experimental data on hadronic hard-
scattering processes: inclusive neutral-current (NC) and charged-current (CC) deep-inelastic scat-
tering (DIS), c- and b-quark production in the NC DIS, c-quark production in the CC DIS, and W-,
Z-boson and t-quark production in (anti)proton-proton collisions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A variety of processes provides
a complementary set of constraints on the PDFs and the parameters of QCD Lagrangian, which
are required for a consistent interpretation of the data, in particular, the heavy-quark masses and
αs.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The value of αs determined from this ﬁt is predominantly driven by the NC DIS data, which
cover a wide range of the momentum transfer squared Q2 = 2.5 ÷ 50000GeV2 and can be nicely
described by perturbative QCD with the corrections up to next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO)
taken into account [2] and the heavy ﬂavor corrections [3].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
However, at the lowest end of this range
the leading-twist (LT) PDF term is accompanied by substantial contributions from the higher-twist
(HT) operators [4].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The latter introduce an additional power-like dependence on Q2, which spoils
the purely logarithmic behavior of the leading-twist part and, as a result, shifts the ﬁtted value of
αs upwards [5].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Therefore in order to provide an unbiased determination one has to eliminate the
impact of the HT terms either by cutting on the potentially problematic kinematic region or by
parameterizing and ﬁtting them in parallel with the LT PDFs.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The ABMP16 ﬁt is based on the
latter approach, while it has also been checked that the former one provides a consistent value of
αs, cf.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The HT terms appear at large Bjorken x therefore their isolation can be performed
with a cut of W 2 > 12.5 GeV2, where W is the invariant mass of the hadronic system.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
However,
such a cut does not aﬀect the small-x part of the HT terms, which manifests itself in the NMC and
the HERA data [7].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Thus, in order to allow for a pure leading-twist theoretical treatment of the
available DIS data an additional cut of Q2 > 10 GeV2 is also required.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The values of αs preferred by four groups of the inclusive DIS data, SLAC, BCDMS, NMC, and
HERA, which are used in the ABMP16 ﬁt, are displayed in Fig.

are also more sensitive to the HT contribution because of the kinematic limitations caused by
the relatively low beam energy.

marginal sensitivity to the HT contribution.

Due to the update of the

text:
An important aspect of the small-x DIS data interpretation is to account for the heavy-quark
contribution.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In particular ﬁnal-state conﬁgurations including the c-quark are responsible for an
essential part of the NC inclusive cross section in the region of HERA kinematics.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Therefore, an
accurate treatment of this term is a necessary ingredient of the related phenomenology [10].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This
applies also to the extraction of αs from a combination of the DIS data, which include the small-x
HERA sample [11].

text:
In this part the ABMP16 ﬁt is based on the ﬁxed-number-ﬂavor (FFN) scheme,
which implies only massless partons, gluon and three light quarks, in the initial state, while the
heavy-quark contribution is computed within the photon-gluon fusion mechanism including the
higher-order QCD corrections up to the NNLO.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Furthermore, the MS deﬁnition of the heavy-
quark mass, which improves the perturbative convergence, is applied in the ABMP16 ﬁt [12].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The
relevance of the FFN approach in such a formulation is supported by a good description of the
Run I HERA data on the semi-incisive c-quark production used in the ABMP16 ﬁt and a good
agreement with the more recent Run I+II data [13].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Moreover, the MS value of the c-quark mass
mc(mc) = 1.252 ± 0.018 GeV
obtained in the ﬁt simultaneously with αs and the PDF parameters is in a good agreement with
other determinations [9] that also underpins the consistency of the FFN scheme in the application
to the analysis of existing data on c-quark DIS production.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The data on hadronic t-quark pair production cross sections, which are used in the ABMP16 ﬁt,
are also quite sensitive to αs since the leading order cross section of this process is proportional to
α2
s.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

At the same time it is also sensitive to the gluon distribution and value of the t-quark mass
mt.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

Therefore, in order to use the potential of these data in the determination of αs one has to ﬁx
these two ingredients.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

The gluon distribution at the relevant kinematics is conﬁned by other data
employed in the ABMP16 ﬁt, however, none of them are sensitive to mt.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

At present, the accurate
value of mt also cannot obtained by direct reconstruction in the experiment due to hadronization
eﬀects being still not fully under theoretical control [14].

In view of these limitations the value of
mt is ﬁtted simultaneously with αs and the PDFs.

As a result, impact of the t-quark data on αs
determination is greatly reduced.

αs from jet cross section measurements in deep-inelastic ep scattering
Daniel Britzger∗
Max-Planck-Institut f¨ur Physik, F¨ohringer Ring 6, 80805 M¨unchen, Germany
Abstract: The value of αs(mZ) is determined from inclusive jet and di-jet cross sections in
neutral-current deep-inelastic ep scattering (DIS) measured at HERA by the H1 collaboration using
next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) perturbative QCD predictions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Using inclusive jet and di-
jet data together, the strong coupling constant is determined to be αs(mZ) = 0.1157(20)exp(29)th.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Complementary, αs(mZ) is determined together with parton distribution functions of the proton
(PDFs) from jet and inclusive DIS data and the value is determined to be αs(mZ) = 0.1142(28)tot.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The running of the strong coupling is tested at diﬀerent
values of the renormalisation scale and the results are found to be in agreement with expectations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Introduction
Jet production cross sections in neutral-current deep-inelastic scattering (NC DIS) are measured in
the Breit frame, where the virtual photon and the proton collide head on.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These measurements are
directly sensitive to the value of αs(mZ), since the predictions in perturbative QCD are proportional
to O(αs) already at leading order.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Inclusive jet and di-jet cross sections have been measured by
the H1 experiment in ep collisions at HERA in the years 1995–2007 [1,2,3,4,5], at center-of-mass
energies of √s = 300 GeV and 320 GeV, and for a wide kinematic range in the photon virtuality Q2.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: For all data, jets are deﬁned using the kt jet-algorithm with a parameter R = 1.0.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Inclusive jet cross
sections have been measured double-diﬀerentially as a function of Q2 and jet transverse momenta,
P jet
T , with values typically exceeding P jet
T ≳5 GeV, and di-jet cross sections as a function of Q2 and
the average P jet
T of the two leading jets, ⟨P jet
T ⟩.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Already in the past, all these data have been used for
determinations of αs(mZ) using next-to-leading order pQCD predictions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In the work presented [6],
the cross section predictions are performed now for the ﬁrst time in next-to-next-to-leading order
(NNLO) accuracy.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These calculations are implemented in the program NNLOJET [7,8], and the
coeﬃcients are stored in the fastNLO format [9] to enable a repeated calculation with diﬀerent
values of αs(mZ).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Using these new and improved predictions, the strong coupling constant αs(mZ)
is determined in two approaches.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The αs-ﬁt
In the ﬁrst approach, which is denoted as ‘αs-ﬁt’, the value of αs(mZ) is determined in a ﬁt of
NNLO predictions to the inclusive jet and di-jet data, where a statistical goodness-of-ﬁt quantity,
χ2, is minimised.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In this ﬁt, both of the αs-dependencies in the predictions, namely in the partonic
cross sections and in the PDF, are taken into account.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The latter is accounted for by setting the
DGLAP-evolution starting-scale to µ0 = 20 GeV, and thus, the αs-dependence of the evolution
kernel can also be considered in the ﬁt.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: For the central result, the NNPDF3.1 PDF set is used [10].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The renormalisation and factorisation scales are chosen to be µ2
R = µ2
F = Q2 + P 2
T, where PT
denotes P jet
T
in case of inclusive jet cross sections, and ⟨P jet
T ⟩in case of di-jets.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Subsequently, a
∗On behalf of the H1 and NNLOJET collaborations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
66


representative scale value ˜µ, which is closely related to µR and µF, is assigned to each data point
and is used for additional cuts, as discussed below.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In the ﬁts of αs(mZ) to each of the nine individual data sets it is found that the results are all
consistent, and the data are all found to be well described by the NNLO predictions [6].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The smallest
experimental uncertainty (‘exp’) is then achieved in a ﬁt to all inclusive jet and di-jet cross section
data†, denoted as ‘H1 jets’, with a value αs(mZ) = 0.1143 (9)exp (43)th.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The theoretical uncertainty
(‘th’) comprises multiple uncertainties: various uncertainties of the PDFs (called ‘PDF’, ‘PDFαs’,
and ‘PDFset’), hadronisation uncertainties (‘had’), and scale uncertainties.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The latter are the
dominant source of uncertainty.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The main result of this approach is obtained from H1 jet data
restricted to ˜µ > 28 GeV.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In this ﬁt the value of αs(mZ) is determined to
αs(mZ) = 0.1157 (20)exp (3)PDF (2)PDFαs (3)PDFset (6)had (27)scale ,
while this ﬁt also exhibits a very good agreement of the NNLO predictions with the data, indicated
by χ2 = 63.2 for 91 data points.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The cut value of ˜µ > 28 GeV was chosen such that the scale
and experimental uncertainty are somewhat balanced: a lower cut on ˜µ would result in smaller
experimental uncertainties, but larger scale uncertainties, and vice-versa.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: The ﬁts are repeated with data samples restricted to adjacent small intervals in ˜µ.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The resulting
values of αs(mZ), together with the respective value of αs(µR), are displayed at a representative
value ˜µ in Fig.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This study provides an important consistency test of the data and predictions, and
the result nicely illustrates the running of αs.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The values are found to be in good agreement with
the expectation according to the RGE and with αs-determinations in other reactions at NNLO.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The PDF+αs-ﬁt
In a complementary approach, which is then denoted as ‘PDF+αs’ ﬁt, the value of αs(mZ) is
determined together with the non-perturbative PDFs.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
For this analysis, normalised inclusive jet
and di-jet cross sections [3,4,5], i.e.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
the jet data are normalised to the inclusive NC DIS cross
sections, are exploited, together with all of the H1 inclusive NC and CC DIS cross section data.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: The latter data samples are equivalent to the one used in the H1PDF2012 PDF ﬁt [11].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The ﬁt
ansatz for the determination of the PDF parameters and αs(mZ) follows closely the methodology
of previous PDF studies, such as HERAPDF2.0 [12] or H1PDF2012.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
PDFs are parameterised at a
starting scale with 12 ﬁt parameters and the DGLAP formalism is employed.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
All predictions are
again performed in NNLO QCD, and the value of αs(mZ) is determined in this PDF+αs ﬁt to
αs(mZ) = 0.1142 (11)exp,had,PDF (2)mod (2)par (26)scale ,
where ‘mod’ and ‘par’ denote the model and parameterisation uncertainties, similar to the HERA-
PDF2.0 approach.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The scale uncertainty is estimated by repeating the ﬁt with scale factors 0.5 and
2 applied to µR and µF for all calculations involved.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In this ﬁt, a good agreement of predictions
and data is found with a value χ2/ndof = 1539.7/(1529 −13).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Details of the resulting set of PDFs,
denoted as ‘H1PDF2017 [NNLO]’, are omitted here since this discussion is beyond the scope of the
workshop, but these are presented and discussed in greater detail in Ref.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Highlighting one of
these results, a simultaneous determination of αs and the PDFs from HERA inclusive data alone is
found not to be reliable, wheras good accuracy on both is reached when including HERA jet data.

text:
Summary
To summarise, the value of αs(mZ) has been determined using the new NNLO pQCD predictions for
jet production cross section in NC DIS, and analysing the vast majority of inclusive jet and di-jet
cross section data published previously by H1.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Alternatively, the entirety of inclusive NC and CC
DIS cross section data recorded by the H1 experiment, together with normalised jet data, has been
considered in an complementary approach, where also the PDFs are determined.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The results of the
PDF+αs-ﬁt and of the αs-ﬁt are presented in Fig.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
2, and compared to the world average value and
other analyses [13].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
All values are found to be consistent with each other, and the results are found
to be consistent with the world average value, although with a tendency to be a bit lower.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It was
found, that the results yield competitive experimental uncertainties in comparison to the present
uncertainty of the world average.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The jet data analysed here probe at high experimental and rea-
sonable theoretical precision the region of low scales from about 7 to 90 GeV, where precision data
are sparse.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Despite of the use of NNLO calculations for this analysis, the dominant uncertainties
for most of the results are the scale uncertainty associated to the NNLO predictions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Since the
scale uncertainties exceed considerably the experimental uncertainties, improved predictions may
yield signiﬁcantly smaller total uncertainties in the future.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Some improvements of the experimental uncertainties can be possibly achieved by including data
from the ZEUS experiment in the analysis.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Further improvements are expected from analysing
68


three-jet cross sections, which have an increased sensitivity to αs(mZ) since their LO predictions
are proportional to O(α2
s).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: Unfortunately, these three-jet predictions are not available yet in NNLO.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Event-shape measurements in NC DIS represent alternative observables, which may yield compet-
itive precision in αs(mZ).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In this case, such data are expected to have large overlap with the jet
data analysed here, and also a similar αs sensitivity.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Therefore, most important for future improve-
ments are ﬁrst of all further reductions of the dominant scale uncertainty, e.g.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
by adding additional
corrections beyond NNLO.
