text:
of Physics and Astronomy, Michigan State University, East Lansing, MI 48824-1116, USA
Abstract: The sensitivity of global parton distribution function (PDF) ﬁts to determine the value
of αs(mZ) is reviewed.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
There are over 3500 data points in modern global PDF ﬁts, including data from deep-inelastic
scattering (DIS), Drell–Yan (DY) production, inclusive jet and dijet production, and from top
production, the latter both singly diﬀerential and double-diﬀerential in the relevant kinematic
variables.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The state-of-the art is the production of parton distribution functions (PDFs) at NNLO,
although it is common to also produce sets at NLO and LO.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The NLO and NNLO PDFs are
typically very similar to each other, while the LO PDFs deviate substantially due to the absence of
critical higher order corrections.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
All of the processes in a global PDF ﬁt are sensitive to the value
of αs(mZ), with the power of αs(mZ) in the prediction depending on the process (and the order).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: Thus, a global PDF ﬁt can be used in the determination of αs(mZ).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
There are two philosophies in global PDF ﬁtting; either allow αs(mZ) to be free in the ﬁt, or to to ﬁx
its value at some standard, typically the value quoted by the Particle Data Group.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The widespread
standard is to use a central value of αs(mZ) of 0.118 (basically an approximation/truncation of the
PDG result) and an uncertainty (at the 90% conﬁdence level) of ±0.002, or ±0.0012 at the 68%
CL.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: This central value and uncertainty is typically used for both NLO and NNLO global PDF ﬁts.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: In LO PDF ﬁts, a much larger value is needed, typically in the range 0.130-0.140.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
(It is diﬃcult to
quote an uncertainty for αs(mZ) for LO PDF ﬁts, just as it is diﬃcult to quote an uncertainty for
the PDFs themselves, again due to the deﬁciencies of the LO matrix elements.) Thus, for example,
the PDF4LHC15 PDFs, a combination of the PDFs from the CT, MMHT and NNPDF groups,
uses this standard [1].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: But, as stated earlier, a global PDF ﬁt can be used for the determination of the αs(mZ).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:

previous determinations of αs(mZ) from the PDG have included the input from PDF ﬁts, though
mostly using DIS data [6].

text:
One diﬃculty, though, is that there is a correlation (or anti-correlation
depending on the parton x range) between the value of αs(mZ) and the strength of the gluon
distribution.

text:

PDFs, this can result in a relatively large uncertainty in the extracted value of αs(mZ), and thus
the philosophy among some groups of instead using the PDG standard value.

in intervals of a multiple of 0.001 above and below the central value, allowing the impact of a
diﬀerent value of αs(mZ) to be calculated, and thus a determination of the αs(mZ) uncertainty to
go along with the PDF uncertainty.

Adam Kardos1, Stefan Kluth2, Zolt´an Tr´ocs´anyi3,4, G´abor Somogyi3, Zoltan Tulipant1, and
Andrii Verbytskyi2
1Institute of Physics, University of Debrecen, 4010 Debrecen, Hungary

Abstract: We present a computation of energy-energy correlation in e+e−annihilation at next-
to-next-to-leading order accuracy in perturbative QCD matched with the next-to-next-to-leading
logarithmic resummed calculation for the back-to-back limit.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Using these predictions and state-
of-the-art Monte Carlo tools to model hadronization corrections, we perform an extraction of the
strong coupling from available data sets.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We also show next-to-next-to-leading order results for
soft-drop thrust, an observable speciﬁcally constructed to have reduced hadronization corrections.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We study the impact of the soft drop on the convergence of the perturbative prediction and ﬁnd
that generally grooming improves perturbative stability.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This improved stability, together with the
reduced sensitivity to non-perturbative corrections makes soft-drop thrust a promising observable
for precision measurements of the strong coupling at lepton colliders.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Introduction
Accurate measurements of event shape distributions in e+e−annihilation continue to be one of the
most precise tools for extracting the strong coupling αs value from data [1,2].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Such determinations
are typically based on the comparison of diﬀerential distributions with perturbative predictions
supplemented with hadronization corrections derived either from analytic models or Monte Carlo
tools.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
As new data for e+e−annihilation are not foreseen in the near future, progress in such
measurements relies solely on improved theoretical understanding of the e+e−→hadrons process.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
When discussing the accuracy of theoretical predictions for event shape distributions, two very dif-
ferent sources of uncertainty present themselves.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The ﬁrst of these is simply the uncertainty coming
from terms that are not evaluated exactly in perturbation theory.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These can be higher-order terms
in the coupling that are simply neglected in a ﬁxed-order calculation, or subleading logarithmic
terms that are not controlled in an all-order resummation.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A second source of uncertainty is that
associated with the description of the parton to hadron transition.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These two types of uncertainties have a rather diﬀerent nature and so their reduction must be
addressed in diﬀerent ways.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Clearly, uncertainties associated to the perturbative description of an
observable may be reduced, at least in principle, by increasing the perturbative and/or logarithmic
order at which the predictions are computed.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These days, state-of-the-art computations include
exact ﬁxed-order corrections at next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) accuracy for three-jet event
shapes [3,4,5], as well as next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic (NNLL) (see e.g., Ref.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
[6] and references
therein) and even next-to-next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic (N3LL) resummation [7,8,9] in the
two-jet limit.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
However, it is less obvious how non-perturbative uncertainties could be similarly
reduced.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In this respect, one idea is to investigate observables that are less sensitive to hadronization
corrections.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In particular, borrowing ideas from jet grooming, new event shape observables can be
deﬁned for which hadronization corrections are much reduced as compared to traditional ones [10].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
74


In this contribution we ﬁrst present an extraction of the strong coupling αs from the energy-energy
correlation of particles in e+e−collisions, highlighting the role that higher-order perturbative cor-
rections play in reducing the uncertainty of the measurement.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Then, we investigate soft-drop thrust,
an observable constructed to mitigate the impact of non-perturbative corrections.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In particular, we
point out that in addition to decreased hadronization corrections, this new observable also exhibits
an increased perturbative stability, making it an appealing candidate for a precise determination
of the strong coupling.

We now turn to the issue of how the uncertainty associated with the estimation of hadronization
corrections might be mitigated in measurements of αs.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
As mentioned in the introduction, one
possible approach is to construct observables with reduced sensitivity to non-perturbative eﬀects.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The idea is simple: if the overall size of the hadronization correction is small, then even a sizable
relative uncertainty on this contribution will correspond to a small overall uncertainty on αs.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Thus
the limited precision of the hadronization correction becomes less of an issue.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:

hadronization uncertainties.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

soft and wide-angle radiation from jets that are deﬁned in an event.

text:
Summary
In this contribution we examined potential ways of increasing the precision of αs measurements from
e+e−annihilation into hadrons.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
On the one hand, we stressed the important role that higher-order
perturbative corrections play in reducing the uncertainty of the determination.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We highlighted
this by presenting an extraction of αs from measurements of energy-energy correlation, based on
theoretical predictions with NNLO+NNLL accuracy and hadronization corrections derived using
modern Monte Carlo tools.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We ﬁnd that the inclusion of NNLO corrections has a dramatic eﬀect
on the uncertainty of the measurement, which is reduced by a factor of two as compared to the
result at only NLO+NNLL accuracy.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Our analysis provides a determination of αs(mZ) with the
highest numerical and theoretical precision obtained from this observable to date,
αs(mZ) = 0.11750 ± 0.00287 (comb.) .
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
On the other hand, we pointed out that a possible strategy for reducing uncertainties in measure-
ments of αs associated with the modeling of hadronization corrections is to employ observables for
which these corrections are small.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In particular, we examined soft-drop event shapes, observables
speciﬁcally tailored so as to show less sensitivity to non-perturbative eﬀects.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Through the exam-
ple of soft-drop thrust, we demonstrated that in addition to reducing hadronization corrections,
soft-drop grooming also enhances the perturbative stability of the theoretical predictions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These
features make soft-drop event shapes promising candidates for precision measurements of the strong
coupling at lepton colliders.

Abstract: We present a comparison of the computation of energy-energy correlations and Durham
algorithm jet rates in e+e−collisions at next-to-next-to-leading logarithmic accuracy matched
with the O(α3
s) perturbative prediction to LEP, PEP, PETRA, SLC, and TRISTAN data.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
With
these predictions we perform extractions of the strong coupling constant taking into account non-
perturbative eﬀects modelled with modern Monte Carlo event generators that simulate NLO QCD
corrections.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Introduction
The strong interaction in the Standard Model (SM) is described by Quantum Chromodynamics
(QCD), see Ref.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The theory successfully describes the interactions between quarks
and gluons and is a source of numerous predictions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
One of the precise QCD predictions that
depends strongly on the only theory parameter, the coupling constant of the strong interaction
αs, is the topology of the e+e−→hadrons events.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In these events at high energies, hadrons
predominantly appear in collimated bunches, called jets.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The topologies of e+e−→partons events
can be predicted with high precision in perturbation theory and the observables of the ﬁnal hadronic
state observed in the experiments are closely related to them.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The state of the art predictions for QCD for such observables currently includes exact ﬁxed-order
next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) corrections for the three-jet event shapes and jet rates.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The
specialized numerical matrix element integration codes allow a straightforward computation of any
suitable, i.e.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: collinear and infrared safe, event shape or jet observable.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In this paper we describe two analyses that utilise the NNLO predictions matched to next-to-next-
leading-log (NNLL) resummed calculations for the region with e+e−→2-partons topology.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: The ﬁrst analysis considers the energy-energy correlation (EEC).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

weighted cross section deﬁned in terms of the angle between two particles i and j in an event [2]:

Data sets

Abstract: We present a brief summary of our recent determination of αs from e+e−→hadrons,
in the region 3 ≤s ≤4 GeV2, with s the square of the center-of-mass energy.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In a recent paper [1], we used a new compilation of data for the R-ratio R(s), measured in the
process e+e−→hadrons, to extract a value for the strong coupling, αs, using ﬁnite energy sum rules
(FESRs).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This determination can directly be compared with the determination from hadronic τ
decays.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: Here we present a brief summary of this determination.

can be found in Ref.

αs from soft QCD jet fragmentation functions
Redamy P´erez-Ramos1,2∗and David d’Enterria3,†

Abstract: We present an extraction of the QCD coupling αs from the energy evolution of the ﬁrst
two moments (multiplicity and peak position) of the parton-to-hadron fragmentation functions at
low fractional hadron momentum z.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A ﬁt of the experimental jet data, from e+e−and deep-inelastic
e±, ν-p collisions, to NNLO∗+NNLL predictions yields αs(mZ) = 0.1205 ± 0.0010 (exp)+0.0022
−0.0000 (th),
in good agreement with the current αs world average.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Introduction
In the chiral limit of zero quark masses and for ﬁxed number of colours Nc, the αs coupling that
determines the strength of the interaction among quarks and gluons is the only parameter of
quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the theory of the strong interaction.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Starting at an energy scale
of order ΛQCD ≈0.2 GeV, where the perturbatively-deﬁned coupling diverges, αs decreases with
energy Q following a 1/ ln(Q2/Λ2
QCD) dependence at leading order.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The current ±0.9% uncertainty
of αs at the Z mass pole, αs(mZ) = 0.1181±0.011 [1], makes of the QCD coupling the least precisely
known of all fundamental constants in nature.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Improving our knowledge of αs is crucial in order to
reduce the uncertainties in perturbative-QCD calculations of higher-order corrections of all hadronic
cross sections and decays at colliders [2], as well as for precision electroweak ﬁts of the Standard
Model in indirect searches for new physics at future e+e−machines [3].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The parametric dependence
on αs accounts for a signiﬁcant fraction of the theoretical uncertainties in e.g.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
the calculations of
the Higgs boson H →bb, cc, gg partial widths [4].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The value of αs(mZ) and its evolution have also
far-reaching implications including the stability of the electroweak vacuum [5], the existence of new
coloured sectors at high energies [6], and our understanding of physics approaching the Planck
scales, such as e.g.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: on the precise energy at which the interaction couplings may unify.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Having at hand new independent approaches to determine αs, with experimental and theoretical
uncertainties comparable to (or, even better, smaller than) those of the methods currently used, is
crucial to reduce the overall uncertainty in the combined αs world-average value [2].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
[7], we
presented a novel technique to extract αs from the energy evolution of the moments of the parton-
to-hadron fragmentation functions (FFs) computed at increasingly higher degree of theoretical
accuracy, including up to approximate next-next-to-leading-order (NNLO⋆) ﬁxed-order and next-
to-next-to-leading-log (NNLL) resummation corrections.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We review here the latest NNLO⋆+NNLL
theoretical calculations for the jet-energy dependence of the hadron multiplicity and the FF peak
position.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A ﬁt of the analytical predictions to experimental jet measurements from e+e−and
deep-inelastic e±, ν-p collisions over Q ≈2–200 GeV provides a new high-precision extraction of
αs(mZ).

DGLAP+MLLA evolution of the fragmentation functions
The conversion of a quark and gluon (collectively called partons) into a ﬁnal jet of hadrons is
driven by perturbative dynamics dominated by soft and collinear gluon bremsstrahlung [8] followed
by the ﬁnal transformation into hadrons of the last partons produced in the QCD shower at non-
perturbative scales approaching ΛQCD.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The distribution of hadrons inside a jet is encoded in its
fragmentation function, Da→h(z, Q), describing the probability that an initial parton a eventually
fragments into a hadron h carrying a fraction z = phadron/pparton of the parent parton’s momentum.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Starting with a parton at a given δ-function energy Q, its evolution to any other energy scale Q′ is
driven by a branching process of parton radiation and splitting, a →b c, that can be perturbatively
computed.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
At large z ≳0.1 one uses the DGLAP evolution equations [9], whereas the Modiﬁed
Leading Logarithmic Approximation (MLLA) [10], resumming soft and collinear singularities, pro-
vides the proper theoretical framework at small z.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In the latter approach, describing the region of
low hadron momenta that dominates the jet fragments, one writes the FF as a function of the log
of the inverse of z, ξ = ln(1/z).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Due to colour coherence and interference in gluon radiation (known
as “angular ordering”), not the softest partons but those with intermediate energies multiply most
eﬀectively in QCD cascades, leading to a ﬁnal FF with a typical “hump-backed plateau” (HBP)
shape as a function of ξ.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Such an HBP can be described, without any loss of generality, in terms
of a distorted Gaussian (DG, Fig.

NNLO⋆+NNLL evolution of the FFs moments
As for the Schr¨odinger equation in quantum mechanics, the system of equations for the Da→h(z, Q)
FFs can be written as an evolution Hamiltonian that mixes gluon and (anti)quark states expressed
in terms of DGLAP splitting functions [9] for the branchings g →gg, q(¯q) →gq(¯q) and g →q¯q,
where g, q and ¯q are a gluon, quark, and anti-quark respectively.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:

diagonalized into two eigenvalues γ±± in the new D± basis.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

of the FF moments is γ++.

Abstract: A determination of the strong coupling constant αs from the single jet inclusive cross
section measurements at the LHC is envisaged, using theoretical predictions at next-to-next-to-
leading-order (NNLO) in QCD.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The observation of jet production at hadron colliders directly probes the basic parton-parton scat-
tering process in QCD.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
As such, a number of fundamental quantities can be inferred from these
measurements, such as, for example, the QCD coupling constant.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
As will be shown below, the
interplay between the sensitivity of the inclusive jet pT -spectrum to αs, and the experimental pre-
cision of the measurement is very favourable for a strong coupling extraction.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This stems from the
fact that for suﬃciently high-pT jets, the jet cross section has a large rate at the LHC and a clean
and simple deﬁnition, allowing jet measurements to become very precise.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Single jet inclusive measurements at the LHC have been performed by the ATLAS and CMS
experiments at √s = 7 TeV [1,2,3], √s = 8 TeV [4,5] and √s = 13 TeV [6,7].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
At present, the
systematic uncertainty in the measurement is dominated by the jet energy scale (JES) at the 1–
2% level, which, due to the steeply falling jet-pT spectrum, translates to a < 10% uncertainty
on the cross section as shown in Fig.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Over a wide range in jet-pT , it is similarly observed in
ATLAS and CMS a 5% systematic uncertainty in the measurement and a statistical uncertainty
at the subpercent level, which paves the way towards jet precision physics studies at the LHC.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
To
this end, the availability of multiple single jet inclusive datasets allows for an investigation of the
consistency of the data and a possible simultaneous inclusion in a combined αs determination.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In reference [4], an αs extraction from the single jet inclusive observable was performed using
19.7 fb−1 of data recorded by the CMS detector from pp collisions at √s = 8 TeV.

title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
To this end, in close collaboration with experts from the FASTNLO [12] and APPLGRID [13]
collaborations, an APPLFAST interface to the program NNLOJET [10] is in development to provide
a fast and ﬂexible way to reproduce the results of full jet cross sections at NLO and NNLO for the
ﬁrst time, in both FASTNLO and APPLGRID formats, which are suitable for state-of-the-art ﬁts
of PDF and αs with LHC jet data at NNLO.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It is anticipated that these results can substantially reduce the uncertainties on current determina-
tions of αs from jet production at the LHC, which are largely dominated by the scale uncertainty
of the NLO prediction.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The scale uncertainties at NNLO are below the 5% level, which, depending
on the jet-pT , correspond to a reduction by more than a factor of 2 with respect to NLO.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The
incorporation of NNLO corrections in αs ﬁts to jet cross sections at hadron colliders and a consis-
tent combination of the multiple datasets available at the LHC, can in this way, open up a new
contribution to the αs PDG average [14] with a target precision at the ∼1–2% level in the upcoming
years.

Jet substructure and a possible determination of the QCD coupling
Felix Ringer

Abstract: We review possible avenues toward an extraction of the QCD strong coupling αs using
jet substructure techniques.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A range of jet substructure observables have been measured recently at
the LHC with unprecedented precision.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In addition, theoretical advances make it possible to directly
compare LHC data and ﬁrst principles calculations in QCD.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
LHC jet substructure observables may
provide an independent handle on extracting αs and they are particularly well suited to complement
current extractions from electron-positron annihilation data.

title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Introduction
Jets and jet substructure are important tools for many analyses carried out at the LHC.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
For
example, jet substructure techniques are used extensively for tagging boosted W, Z, discriminating
between quark/gluon jets and for searches of particles beyond the standard model.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The development
of jet grooming techniques now also facilitate QCD precision studies using jet substructure.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Jet
grooming techniques are designed to remove soft wide-angle radiation from the jet.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These techniques
reduce the hadronization correction and remove the soft contamination from the underlying event
(mostly from multiparton interactions) leaving behind only the hard core of the jet.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In particular,
the soft drop grooming algorithm [1] allows for ﬁrst principles calculations within perturbative
QCD.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Despite the fact that most jet substructure observables are sensitive to very soft scales,
it is possible to make direct one-to-one comparisons between theory and data.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
For example, jet
substructure observables can be used for the tuning of parton showers, improving our understanding
of the fragmentation/hadronization mechanism, and jets can be used as a well calibrated probe of
the quark-gluon plasma in heavy-ion collisions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
See [2] for a recent review of jet substructure
techniques.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Recently, it has been proposed to measure the strong coupling constant αs using jet
substructure observables [3].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Such an extraction is particularly challenging due to the required
precision both from the experimental and the theoretical side.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Here, we ﬁrst review the soft drop
grooming procedure and the status of theoretical calculations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We then discuss possible avenues
toward an extraction of the QCD strong coupling constant.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Soft drop groomed jet substructure observables
We consider inclusive jet production pp →jet + X at the LHC where jets are identiﬁed in a given
transverse momentum pT and rapidity η interval and no further constraints are imposed on the
ﬁnal state conﬁguration.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The soft drop grooming algorithm was introduced in [1] which we brieﬂy
review here.

text:

where the distance metric between particles only depends on their geometric distance in the η–φ
plane.

Various jet substructure observables in proton-proton collisions have been calculated within per-

title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A class of observables which is
particularly well suited for the extraction of the QCD coupling constant are jet shape observables.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Similar to event shape observables in e+e−collisions, a single number is determined in order to
characterize the radiation pattern of the observed jet.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The close analogy to e+e−event shape
observables makes this class of observables particularly well suited for the extraction of the QCD
strong coupling constant (see for example [4,5,6]).

A possible determination of the QCD strong coupling constant
Observables that are well suited for an extraction of the QCD strong coupling constant should
be rather insensitive to nonperturbative eﬀects and, at the same time, retain the sensitivity to
αs.

exhibit a larger sensitivity to αs and observables such as jet broadening, a = 1 in Eq.

Given the current status of experimental results and theoretical
calculations, the overall uncertainty of an extraction of αs was estimated to be of the order of 10%.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: However, this estimate is expected to improve signiﬁcantly in the future.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
On the theoretical side, the accuracy of the existing calculations will have to be extended to full
NNLO+NNLL′ or even N3LL in order to achieve a competitive determination of αs.

On the

title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: However, this would require further theoretical eﬀorts to achieve the required precision.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Conclusions
Jet substructure techniques may help in the future to precisely constrain the QCD strong coupling
constant αs.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Soft drop grooming allows for ﬁrst principles calculations in perturbative QCD which
may be compared directly to data taken at the LHC.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The grooming procedure largely removes soft
wide-angle radiation making jet substructure observables robust in the complicated LHC environ-
ment while retaining the sensitivity to αs.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In addition, new insights into universality aspects of
the relevant nonperturbative physics may be obtained.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In the future, it will be important to make
further progress and achieve an improved precision both from the experimental and the theoretical
side.

Abstract: Signiﬁcant progress in experimental and theoretical techniques allow a determination
of the strong coupling constant αs from proton-proton collisions with much improved precision.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Results of the CMS experiment [1] at the LHC are reviewed, which are based on measurements of
jet and of top-quark pair production.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In hadron-initiated collisions jets are produced abundantly and oﬀer the opportunity to determine
αs(mZ), where mZ is the mass of the Z boson.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Moreover, the dependence of αs(µR) on the renor-
malisation scale µR can be studied up to the TeV range by identifying µR with the jet momenta
as relevant momentum or energy scale Q of the scattering process.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The CMS Collaboration has compared their measurements of the inclusive jet production cross
section at 7 and 8 TeV centre-of-mass energy [2,3], which reach up to 2.5 TeV of jet transverse mo-
mentum, to predictions of perturbative quantum chromodynamics (QCD) at next-to-leading order
(NLO) accuracy from NLOJet++ [4].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Including corrections for nonperturbative and electroweak
eﬀects, αs(mZ) has been determined to lie in the range 0.1164–0.1192 with uncertainties of 1.3 to
3.0% from all sources other than the truncation of the perturbative expansion, cf.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The
latter eﬀect of missing higher orders is conventionally estimated by varying the renormalisation
and factorisation scales µR and µF independently by factors of two avoiding the extreme cases
of µR/µF = 1/4 and µR/µF = 4.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
At NLO this scale uncertainty amounts to 2–5% and clearly
dominates the uncertainty of the extracted values of αs(mZ).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Since next-to-next-to-leading order
(NNLO) calculations for inclusive jet and dijet production have recently become available [5,6],
this uncertainty can be signiﬁcantly reduced in the future.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The determination of αs(mZ) from jet cross sections in hadron-initiated collisions cannot be in-
dependent of assumptions on the hadron structure.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
For proton-proton collisions in particular the
parton distribution function (PDF) of the gluon inside protons is correlated with the strong cou-
pling constant.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This eﬀect has been considered by CMS through either an additional uncertainty
(included in the column “other” in Table 1), or by performing a simultaneous ﬁt of αs(mZ) and the
proton PDFs using supplementary data on deep-inelastic scattering (DIS) from the H1 and ZEUS
experiments.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
All four results from inclusive jet measurements are consistent among each other
and with a simultaneous ﬁt to triple-diﬀerential dijet production as reported by CMS in Ref.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: The “running” of the strong coupling constant, i.e.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
its scale dependence αs(Q) as predicted by
perturbative QCD, is found to be consistent with the jet measurements ranging up to 2 TeV.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Requiring additional partons, respectively jets, in the ﬁnal state leads to 3-jet cross sections, which
are sensitive to α3
s instead of α2
s as for the previous jet cross sections.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Here, perturbative QCD is
available only up to NLO and electroweak corrections, important at momentum scales in the TeV
range, have been calculated only after the corresponding CMS publications on the 3-jet mass cross
section [8] and the 3- to 2-jet ratio R3/2 at 7 TeV [9] and 8 TeV [10] (preliminary).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Compared to
the 3-jet cross section the ratio R3/2 has the advantage that numerous uncertainties cancel at least
partially in the ratio.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
However, this comes at the price of an additional scale in the process, the
pT of the third jet, and a reduced sensitivity to αs.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The latter can be overcome by looking into
multi-jet production ratios.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: One complication of the σ(t¯t) observable is posed by its dependency on the top-quark mass mt.

αs(mZ) or do it the other way round.

Both has been performed by CMS as reported in the quoted
publications.

A strategy to remedy the mt dependence in t¯t production consists in the exploitation of many data
points of a multi-diﬀerential cross section.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Concretely, CMS studied in total 24 data points of the
normalised t¯t cross section as a function of the mass M(t¯t) and rapidity y(t¯t) of the top-quark
pair, and of the additional jet multiplicity Njet [14].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
From these three quantities it could be shown
that M(t¯t) and y(t¯t) are particularly sensitive to PDFs, M(t¯t) to mt, and Njet to αs(mZ).

The preliminary
results [14] reported here have in the meantime been ﬁnalised and submitted to a journal [15].

Abstract: Twenty-eight diﬀerent measurements of inclusive W± and Z cross sections in pp colli-
sions at the LHC are compared to the corresponding theoretical predictions, at NNLO accuracy in
perturbative QCD including NLO electroweak corrections, in order to extract the QCD coupling
at the Z pole, αs(mZ).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The theoretical cross sections are computed for four diﬀerent parton distri-
bution functions (PDFs): CT14, HERAPDF 2.0, MMHT14, and NNPDF 3.0.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The calculated cross
sections reproduce well the data within experimental and theoretical uncertainties.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A linear ﬁt of
the αs dependence of the theoretical cross sections is used to extract the αs(mZ) value that best
reproduces the measured cross sections.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The 28 αs(mZ) values extracted from each measurement
are combined into a single result by properly taking into account their uncertainties and correla-
tions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The following NNLO values of the QCD coupling for each one of the PDF sets are obtained:
αs(mZ) = 0.1181 ± 0.0016 (CT14), 0.1209 ± 0.0015 (MMHT14), and 0.1163 ± 0.0019 (NNPDF 3.0),
with a ﬁnal uncertainty at the 1.5% level, in good agreement with the αs(mZ) world average.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Introduction
The QCD coupling is the least accurately known of all fundamental interaction couplings: the
current world average at the Z boson mass, αs(mZ) = 0.1181 ± 0.0011, has a 0.9% uncertainty [1].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
New extraction methods with diﬀerent types of experimental and theoretical uncertainties than
those of the current determinations are needed in order to eventually improve the precision on
αs(mZ) through a combined analysis of all existing results [2].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In this context, we propose a
novel approach to extract αs(mZ) based on the comparison of inclusive W± and Z production
cross sections measured at the LHC [3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11] to next-to-next-to-leading-order (NNLO)
perturbative QCD (pQCD) calculations [12].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The method is similar to the one used to extract αs

Summary and conclusions
We have used 28 measurements of the inclusive ﬁducial W± and Z production cross sections in
proton-proton collisions at √s = 7, 8, and 13 TeV, carried out in the electron and muon decay
channels by the ATLAS, CMS, and LHCb experiments, to extract the QCD coupling at the Z mass
pole αs(mZ).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The procedure is based on a detailed comparison of the measured weak boson cross
sections to theoretical calculations computed at NNLO accuracy with the CT14, HERAPDF2.0,
MMHT14, and NNPDF3.0 parton densities.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The overall data–theory agreement is good within
the experimental and theoretical uncertainties, but the CT14 and MMHT14 parton densities seem
to provide the overall best description of all experimental data for the default value of the QCD
coupling, αs(mZ) = 0.118 in all PDF sets.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A procedure has been employed to combine the 28
individual αs extractions per PDF into a single value by properly taking into account all individual
sources of experimental and theoretical uncertainties and their correlations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The following QCD
coupling values are extracted at NNLO accuracy: αs(mZ) = 0.1181±0.0016 (CT14), 0.1209±0.0015
(MMHT14), and 0.1163 ± 0.0019 (NNPDF3.0).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The largest propagated uncertainties, combined
here in quadrature into a single uncertainty for each ﬁnal αs(mZ) value, are associated with the
experimental integrated luminosity and theoretical intra-PDF uncertainties.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In this preliminary
analysis, using the correlation matrices derived from the CMS experiment alone, the combination
procedure did not converge on a stable result for HERAPDF 2.0.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
All other three αs(mZ) extractions
appear robust and stable with respect to variations in the data and theory cross sections, their
uncertainties, and correlations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The ﬁnal values are fully compatible with the world average value,
and have competitive ∼1.5% uncertainties that are similar to those obtained with other precise
methods (e.g.

Determination of αs(mZ) from the Z-boson transverse momentum distribution
Stefano Camarda
CERN, EP Department, CH-1211 Geneva 23, Switzerland
Abstract: The strong-coupling constant αs(mZ) is measured from the transverse-momentum dis-
tribution of Z bosons measured at √s = 1.96 TeV with the CDF experiment, using predictions
based on qT-resummation at NNLO+NNLL, as implemented in the DYTurbo program.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The mea-
surement is performed through a simultaneous ﬁt of αs(mZ) and the non-perturbative Sudakov
form factor.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The strong-coupling constant has been measured at hadron colliders in ﬁnal states with jets [1,2,3],
and more recently from top-antitop production cross sections [4].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Such measurements allow probing
the strong coupling at high values of momentum transfer.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
However, they generally suﬀer from large
uncertainties, and do not provide a competitive determination of the strong coupling at the scale
of the Z-boson mass, αs(mZ).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This contribution aims at discussing a new technique for precisely
measuring αs(mZ) at hadron colliders from a semi-inclusive (i.e.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
radiation inhibited) observable:
the Z-boson transverse-momentum distribution.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This measurement has all the desirable features
for a precise determination of αs(mZ) [5]: large observables sensitivity to αs(mZ) compared to the
experimental precision; high accuracy of the theoretical prediction; small size of non-perturbative
QCD eﬀects.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Measuring αs(mZ), or equivalently ΛMS
QCD, from semi-inclusive Drell-Yan cross sections was ﬁrst
proposed in Ref.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
[6], by using Monte Carlo parton showers to determine ΛMC
QCD and later convert
it to ΛMS
QCD.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The conversion is based on resummation arguments showing that a set of universal
QCD corrections can be absorbed in coherent parton showers by applying a simple rescaling, the
so-called Catani-Marchesini-Webber (CMW) rescaling.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The Z-boson transverse-momentum distribution at small transverse momentum is one of such semi-
inclusive observables.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The recoil of Z bosons produced in hadron collisions is mainly due to QCD
initial-state radiation, and the Sudakov form factor is responsible for the existence of a Sudakov
peak in the distribution, at transverse-momentum values of approximately 4 GeV.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The position
of the peak is sensitive to the value of the strong-coupling constant.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
[6]
can be used to interpret the ATLAS result of a Pythia 8 Monte Carlo tuning to the Z-boson
transverse-momentum distribution [7] as a measurement of αs(mZ).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This naive result is missing important theory
uncertainties as PDFs and missing higher order corrections.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
However, this simple exercise already
shows a great experimental sensitivity and relatively small non-perturbative QCD uncertainties.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: Turning this idea into an actual measurement poses several challenges.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In order to achieve higher
precision, it is highly desirable to employ for the measurement analytic predictions of the Z-boson
transverse-momentum distribution including resummation of large logarithmic corrections of the
form log(pT/m).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Such qT-resummed predictions are available since long time, and they have re-
cently reached N3LL logarithmic accuracy [8].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The measurements of Z-boson transverse-momentum
distribution have small experimental uncertainties, at the level of 2% at the Tevatron and 0.5%
at the LHC.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
High numerical precision of the theory predictions is required to match such small
uncertainties, which is a great challenge for these complicated high-order QCD calculations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Large
correlations between αs(mZ) and non the perturbative QCD eﬀects would spoil the measurement.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Small correlations were observed with the Pythia 8 model, but they need to be studied also in
the case of analytic predictions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
At the LHC, signiﬁcant heavy-ﬂavour initiated production, at the
level of 6% for cc →Z and and 3% for bb →Z introduce additional uncertainties.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
For the measurement of αs(mZ) from the Z-boson transverse-momentum distribution it is necessary
to rely on fast computing codes which allow the calculation of variations in the input parameters
with small numerical uncertainties.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: To this end, the DYTurbo program has been created.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It aims
to provide fast and numerically precise predictions of fully-diﬀerential Drell–Yan production cross
sections, for phenomenological applications such as QCD analyses and extraction of fundamental
parameters of the Standard Model.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The enhancement in performance over previous programs is
achieved by overhauling pre-existing code, by factorising the fully-diﬀerential cross section into
production and decay variables, and by introducing the usage of one-dimensional and multi-di-
mensional numerical integration based on interpolating functions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The DYTurbo program is a
reimplementation of the DYRes [9] program for the small-qT resummed cross sections at up to next-
to-next-to-leading-logarithmic (NNLL) accuracy.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
As an example of fast and numerically precise
predictions, DYTurbo can compute the Z-boson transverse-momentum distribution at 13 TeV in full-
lepton phase space, in 100 equally-spaced bins from zero to 25 GeV, with a target relative numerical
uncertainty of 10−4, in 4 min.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
at NLO+NLL and 3.4 h at NNLO+NNLL, using simultaneously 20
parallel threads.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The great majority of the computation time is spent in evaluating the LO or NLO
V +jet term.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: However, it is possible to use ApplGrid [10] interfaced to MCFM for this term.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Once
this is done, the computation requires 6 s (10 s) at NLO+NLL (NNLO+NNLL).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The CDF measurement of Z-boson transverse-momentum distribution [11] at the Tevatron collider
is ideal for testing the extraction of αs(mZ) with DYTurbo predictions.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This measurement was
performed with the angular coeﬃcients technique, which allows extrapolating the cross section
to full-lepton phase space with small theoretical uncertainties.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The full-lepton phase space cross
section allows fast predictions and avoid any theoretical uncertainties on the modelling of the Z-
boson polarisation.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Another advantage of this measurement with respect to similar measurements
performed at the LHC is the fact that Tevatron is a proton-antiproton collider, and the Z-boson
production has reduced contribution from heavy-ﬂavour-initiated processes compared to proton-
proton collisions at the LHC.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The CDF measurement is performed in the electron channel, with central (|ηe| < 1.1) and forward
(1.2 < |ηe| < 2.8) electrons, allowing a coverage up to Z-boson rapidity of |y| = 2.8, and a small
extrapolation to the full rapidity range |ymax| ≈3.1 of Z-boson production at √s = 1.96 TeV.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The data sample is characterised by low values of the average number of interactions per bunch
126


crossing, and by good electron resolution, at the level of 0.9 GeV for central electrons, and 1.1 GeV
for forward electrons.

In

with zeros at s = s0 of suﬃciently high order (“pinching”) would provide suﬃcient suppression
of contributions from the region near the Minkowski axis to allow DVs to be safely neglected.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

This assumption is predicated on the expectation that ΠDV will be maximal in the vicinity of the

one expects Im ΠDV (s) ∼e−γs × (oscillation), in analogy to the way the asymptotic renormalon

but this could then fail to provide enough pinching to be able to safely neglect DVs.

David d’Enterria1,∗

Abstract: The extraction of the QCD coupling αs from the comparison of experimental data
on inclusive W and Z bosons hadronic decays to state-of-the-art perturbative QCD calculations is
reviewed.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The relatively small amount of W data from e+e−→W+ W−collisions at LEP leads
today to an non-competitive extraction of the strong coupling at the Z mass from the measured
RW ratio of hadronic-to-leptonic branching fractions, αs(mZ) = 0.117±0.042exp±0.004th±0.001par
with a ∼35% propagated experimental uncertainty.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Analysis of the much more abundant hadronic
results at the Z pole leads to αs(mZ) = 0.1203±0.0030, with a 2.5% uncertainty by combining three
diﬀerent pseudo-observables (ratio of hadronic-to-leptonic widths RZ, hadronic peak cross section
σhad
Z
, and total width Γtot
Z ).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
An αs determination with per mille uncertainty requires high-statistics
W and Z bosons data samples at future e+e−colliders, such as the FCC-ee, combined with even
higher precision (N4LO) pQCD calculations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Introduction
The strong coupling αs is one of the fundamental parameters of the Standard Model (SM), and its
value not only directly aﬀects the stability of the electroweak vacuum [1] but it chieﬂy impacts the
theoretical calculations of all scattering and decay processes involving real and/or virtual quarks and
gluons [2].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Known today with a 0.9% precision, αs is the worst known of all fundamental interaction
couplings in nature [3], and such an imprecision propagates as an input parametric uncertainty in
the calculation of many important physics observables, in particular in the electroweak (EW), Higgs,
and top-quark SM sectors [4].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The current world-average value, αs(mZ) = 0.1181 ± 0.0011 [3], is
derived from a combination of six subclasses of approximately-independent observables measured
in e+e−collisions (hadronic Z boson and τ decays, plus event shapes and jet rates), deep-inelastic
scattering DIS (structure functions and global ﬁts of parton distributions functions PDFs), and p-p
collisions (inclusive top-pair cross sections), as well as from lattice QCD computations constrained
by the empirical values of hadron masses and decay constants.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In order to be combined into the
αs(mZ) world-average, the experimental (or lattice) results need to have a counterpart perturbative
QCD (pQCD) prediction at next-to-next-to-leading-order NNLO (or beyond) accuracy.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In principle, among the theoretically and experimentally “cleanest” αs extractions are those based
on the hadronic decays of electroweak bosons.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This is so because (i) the inclusive hadronic W and
Z decays can be very accurately measured in e+e−collisions provided one has large enough data
samples, (ii) the corresponding theoretical predictions can be computed with a very high theoretical
accuracy, today up to O(α4
s), i.e.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
N3LO, in pQCD [5], plus mixed O(ααs) pQCD-EW [6,7] and (in
the Z case) the full two-loop O(α2) EW corrections [8], and (iii) non-pQCD eﬀects are suppressed
thanks to the large energy scale given by the electroweak masses (mW,Z ≫ΛQCD ≈0.2 GeV).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The
common high-precision hadronic observables used to extract αs in e+e−annihilation at the W and
Z boson masses can be schematically decomposed as follows:

149


Summary of the workshop discussions
All workshop participants listed in page 2
Abstract: A summary of the main points raised during the talks discussions and their follow-up
questions, as well as in the round table of the last day of the workshop, is presented.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The discussions
not only focused on particular issues aﬀecting each one of the individual αs extractions, but also on
the current PDG categorization of αs measurements and on the methods used to average them into
a single αs(mZ) value.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Most of the listed points are open and sources of potential controversies,
which we highlight here as one might expect that ongoing progress in the ﬁeld will lead to their
clariﬁcation and resolution.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The results of the discussions during the presentations and round-table session on the last day of
the workshop, are summarized here ordered according to αs extraction category.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
An important
point of discussion was the organization of αs determination categories, the incorporation of new
developments, and the methodology used for the αs(mZ) averaging in the PDG review [1].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The last
point of this contribution deals with those latter issues.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
We note that the topic of αs determinations
was also discussed in a 2018 workshop [2] where complementary details can be found.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
• Lattice QCD:
The lattice-QCD practitioners suggested the PDG αs review to include an expert member of
this community.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Alternatively, the αs(mZ) average of the FLAG collaboration report [3] could
be incorporated into the lattice-QCD PDG chapter and propagated as input into the world-
average value.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Despite the fact that it is diﬃcult to reach full agreement on the averaging of
a very broad range of observables, FLAG has gathered the expertise of a large fraction of the
lattice collaborations in its team in order to reach a rough consensus.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The fact that the most
recent FLAG report provides subaverages for the various diﬀerent αs extractions, helps to
carry out reanalyses of these results if desired.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It was pointed out that several lattice results
are now dominated by higher-order uncertainties in the pQCD counterpart observables mostly
computed at NNLO accuracy, except for the static QCD energy that uses a N3LO result [4].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Thus more eﬀorts should be put on the perturbative side of the calculations in the coming
years in order to understand and reduce these errors, in parallel to evaluating observables
non-perturbatively at higher and higher scales.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It was emphasized that the lattice community
considers that their αs subcategories are as diﬀerent from each other as e.g.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Therefore it was suggested that the PDG average includes the results
of the lattice QCD subcategories as categories parallel to τ-decays, DIS, etc.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
• Hadronic τ decays:
It was proposed to collect the latest results from τ decays as well as the novel low-energy e+e−
annihilation (Re+e−) extraction [5] under one single αs group labelled “τ and e+e−continuum
below charm” (or similar) as they share many theoretical and experimental coincidences.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The αs extraction from hadronic τ decays is signiﬁcantly aﬀected by the spectral functions
measured with limited precision by ALEPH and OPAL in e+e−collisions at LEP.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It was
stressed the need to discuss with the BaBar/BELLE-II communities the use of large τ decays
data samples from B-factory experiments to improve on the αs(mτ) determination.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Although,
up until now, all recent extractions of αs have been based on the same data, they diﬀer mainly
in the treatment of non-perturbative physics.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In particular, there is the need to resolve the
150


duality violation treatment and pinching strategy in connection with the properties of the
Operator Product Expansion.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
• e-p scattering and ﬁts of parton distribution functions:
First, it was pointed out that the current “Deep inelastic lepton-nucleon scattering (DIS)”
label of this extraction category should be changed to “e-p scattering and global PDF ﬁts” (or
similar) to properly include all available αs determinations in this domain.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In particular, to
take into account the fact that there are new αs determinations from HERA data, e.g.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
based
on NNLO jets in DIS and in (anticipated) photoproduction studies, which will be included
into the world average.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
A discussion followed on how to properly merge the novel DIS jets
αs(mZ) result together with the more inclusive structure function results [6].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The question
was raised on what to do with novel NNLO hadron collider extractions, e.g.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
based on jet or
electroweak boson production at the LHC, that have a strong explicit PDF dependence.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It
seemed that the inclusive W, Z cross sections should go under the “hadron collider” category,
as those are total cross section like the tt ones that are not explicitly included into the global
PDF ﬁts, whereas any extraction based on diﬀerential jet cross sections at NNLO should be
rather included as part of the αs determinations derived in parallel with the future global
PDF ﬁts that include these jet spectra too.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It was reminded that there is currently no consensus on how to reliably estimate theoretical
uncertainties of αs extractions, from missing higher-order corrections in NNLO PDF+αs ﬁts.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This complicates not only the comparison with other categories, but also comparisons within
this category to some extent.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
• Hadronic ﬁnal states in e+e−annihilation:
The novel results from e+e−annihilation based on energy-energy correlations (EEC) and jet
rates (R2) [7], further justify organizing the αs subgroup extractions of this category based on
the hadronization correction method employed, i.e.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
based on Monte Carlo event generators
or on analytic models for the non-perturbative eﬀects.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
New developments in jet substructure
techniques [8] applied to e+e−studies will reduce the hadronization corrections and, once they
reach NNLO accuracy, will allow to reanalyze the LEP data with smaller non-perturbative
uncertainties.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
These latest more precise results open up the potential substitution of older
LEP analyses, with larger uncertainties, from the world average.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
New applications of the
Principle of Maximum Conformality (PMC) for determining renormalization scales in αs
extractions via e+e−event-shape variables were discussed during the workshop [9].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The
PMC renormalization scales depend on the event-shape kinematics, reﬂecting the virtuality
of the underlying QCD subprocess.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Work is ongoing to provide a systematic evaluation of
the theory uncertainties of the PMC predictions for pQCD at high orders.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
• Hadronic Z and W boson decays:
Why does the PDG world-average for this category prefer the αs value derived from the global
electroweak (Gﬁtter) SM ﬁt, rather than the value derived from stand-alone analysis of the
pseudo-observables directly measured at the Z boson pole?
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The result from the global SM
ﬁt, αs(mZ) = 0.1194 ± 0.0029 with a ∼2.4% uncertainty, is only slightly more precise than
the latter, αs(mZ) = 0.1203 ± 0.0028 with ∼2.5% uncertainty, but the former is more prone
to potential biases from new physics present in other sectors of the SM [10].
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
151


• Hadronic ﬁnal states at pp, p¯p colliders:
The breadth of LHC data and the associated recent NNLO pQCD theoretical developments
have provided various new αs extractions from pp collisions, including inclusive pp →tt, W,
and Z [11] production cross sections, as well as diﬀerential jets cross sections.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The question
was raised whether adding more measurements could lead to not improving the world aver-
age with the currently used linear pre-averaging method.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
To be able to fully exploit all the
experimental data, via e.g.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
a χ2-based blue-type average [12,13], the correlation matrices
among measurements must be provided by the experimental collaborations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It has also been
stressed that (future) systematically improved parton showers, if possible including correc-
tions at NLL (or beyond) accuracy, are essential to fully gain control of the MC uncertainties
involved in these analyses and also for αs determinations based on e+e−data.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
One of the strengths of the LHC data is the possibility to test asymptotic freedom at high
energy scales, in the TeV regime, never explored before.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In this context, it was pointed out
that e.g.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
some ATLAS analyses of data from pp collisions covering scales at large total event
energy (HT ) seem to run (evolve with scale) faster than expected.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
This eﬀect can depend
on the choice of renormalization scale setting in the extraction of αs, and this should be
carefully checked for each chosen observable.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The αs running plots in the PDG summary
should incorporate the pp →jets results at NNLO that extend the range up to about 2 TeV
at the proper scale of each observable (leading jet pT , sum of jet pT ’s,...).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
For the αs running
in the low energy range, the lattice results should be added.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Last but not least, it was not
clear, i.e.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
not explicitly documented in the publications, if all analyses at scales above the
top quark production threshold used the proper number of active free ﬂavours nf = 6 in the
prediction and the evolution calculations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
• αs categorization, combination and averaging of αs(mZ) results:
The current αs(mZ) PDG world-average [1] is derived from diﬀerent measurements grouped,
ﬁrst, into subcategories that are subsequently combined into six overall categories.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The
individual subcategories are grouped following experimental measurements and theoretical
methods (e.g.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
sharing a similar treatment of hadronization corrections), and the overall cate-
gories share basically the same underlying physical process.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Suggestions were made to change
some of the labels of the categories and/or to rearrange them to include newly available αs ex-
tractions (see more detailed cases discussed above).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In order to enter into the world average,
the current conditions are that the αs analysis has at least an NNLO theoretical accuracy,
includes reliable estimates of experimental, systematic, and theoretical uncertainties, and the
results are published in a peer-reviewed journal.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It was discussed the possibility to drop
relatively old analyses (e.g.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
from LEP e+e−ﬁnal states), because the same data have been
reanalized in newer studies and/or because old hadronization corrections may have been su-
perseded.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Although the large αs(mZ) uncertainties of the oldest results likely have a small
numerical impact on the ﬁnal world-average, the results of more recent developments could
be considered instead.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In any case, it was emphasized, as done now in the PDG, that one
should clearly study and deﬁne beforehand the rules for the selection of the analyses to be
incorporated into the world average, and then follow them strictly to avoid any bias.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It was highlighted that the individual lattice-QCD results have total 0.5 to 1% uncertainties,
which are a factor of 2–4 smaller than all other αs(mZ) individual extractions (with 1.5–4%
uncertainties).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
What does this imply for averaging, which will be driven by the most precise
result?
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
One way to control this (as already performed in recent αs combinations) is to drop
categories from the average and check the consistency of the results by explicitly quoting
152


αs(mZ) averages without a subset of the measurements.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
The possibility to eventually use the
lattice extraction as the single αs(mZ) PDG world-average, as it is the most precise value, it is
based on experimental data (hadron masses and decays), and now contains also the running
up to high scales, was considered.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Some people expressed concerns on that proposal, given the
need to always cross-check the lattice-QCD extraction with hadronic data in the explicitly
perturbative regime.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
It was also pointed out that there are a number of dedicated high-
precision determinations of the strong coupling from various methods that may eventually
be inconsistent with the lattice-QCD results (if their derived central αs(mZ) values do not
change, and the uncertainties shrink).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
In addition to the discussion on the averaging, were
concrete decisions on the weight of these analysis have to be made, future average analyses
should also point out these discrepancies factually to motivate further studies and progress.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text: The technical averaging procedure was also discussed.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Currently it uses linear preaverages for
the subcategories, then χ2-average with ﬂoating correlation with the PDF “χ2 reweighting”
prescription (enlarged uncertainties, if needed, until χ2/dof = 1).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
a χ2 average in the groups with a correlation model following the blue or
convino approaches [12,13], were suggested, in particular to combine LHC measurements
(see above).
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Values obtained with alternative methods should be provided together with
the “default” world-average to check the overall robustness and stability of the ﬁnal αs(mZ)
averaging procedure.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
All in all, the meeting featured lively and stimulating discussions among diﬀerent experts on con-
troversial issues, as well as on technical details, whose clariﬁcation will ultimately have an impact
on more accurate and precise αs determinations.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Novel ideas to extract αs, estimation of expected
reductions in the theoretical and experimental uncertainties of each method, as well as issues to be
addressed in the coming future to improve the combination of all results, were discussed.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
There
was a common agreement of the usefulness of organizing similar dedicated αs workshops every ∼2
years, following the 2011 [14] and 2015 [15] meetings.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

text:
Whereas the strong force decreases with
energy, the scientiﬁc interest in the QCD interaction clearly increases with time.
title: arXiv:1907.01435v1  [hep-ph]  2 Jul 2019

Abhijit Guha Roya,b∗, Shayan Siddiquia,b∗, Sebastian P¨olsterla∗, Nassir Navabb,c, Christian Wachingera
aArtiﬁcial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (AI-Med), Department of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, LMU M¨unchen, Germany.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text: bComputer Aided Medical Procedures, Department of Informatics, Technical University of Munich, Germany.

text: cComputer Aided Medical Procedures, Johns Hopkins University, Baltimore, USA.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Abstract
Deep neural networks enable highly accurate image segmentation, but require large amounts of manually annotated data
for supervised training.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Few-shot learning aims to address this shortcoming by learning a new class from a few annotated
support examples.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We introduce, a novel few-shot framework, for the segmentation of volumetric medical images with
only a few annotated slices.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Compared to other related works in computer vision, the major challenges are the absence
of pre-trained networks and the volumetric nature of medical scans.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We address these challenges by proposing a new
architecture for few-shot segmentation that incorporates ‘squeeze & excite’ blocks.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Our two-armed architecture consists
of a conditioner arm, which processes the annotated support input and generates a task-speciﬁc representation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This
representation is passed on to the segmenter arm that uses this information to segment the new query image.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
To
facilitate eﬃcient interaction between the conditioner and the segmenter arm, we propose to use ‘channel squeeze &
spatial excitation’ blocks – a light-weight computational module – that enables heavy interaction between both the arms
with negligible increase in model complexity.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This contribution allows us to perform image segmentation without relying
on a pre-trained model, which generally is unavailable for medical scans.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Furthermore, we propose an eﬃcient strategy
for volumetric segmentation by optimally pairing a few slices of the support volume to all the slices of the query volume.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text: We perform experiments for organ segmentation on whole-body contrast-enhanced CT scans from the Visceral Dataset.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Our proposed model outperforms multiple baselines and existing approaches with respect to the segmentation accuracy
by a signiﬁcant margin.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text: The source code is available at https://github.com/abhi4ssj/few-shot-segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Keywords:
Few-shot learning, squeeze and excite, semantic segmentation, deep learning, organ segmentation

Introduction
Fully convolutional neural networks (F-CNNs) have
achieved state-of-the-art performance in semantic image
segmentation for both natural (J´egou et al., 2017; Zhao
et al., 2017; Long et al., 2015; Noh et al., 2015) and medi-
cal images (Ronneberger et al., 2015; Milletari et al., 2016).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Despite their tremendous success in image segmentation,
they are of limited use when only a few labeled images
are available.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
F-CNNs are in general highly complex mod-
els with millions of trainable weight parameters that re-
quire thousands of densely annotated images for training
to be eﬀective.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
A better strategy could be to adapt an
already trained F-CNN model to segment a new semantic
class from a few labeled images.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This strategy often works
well in computer vision applications where a pre-trained
model is used to provide a good initialization and is sub-
sequently ﬁne-tuned with the new data to tailor it to the
new semantic class.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
However, ﬁne-tuning an existing pre-
trained network without risking over-ﬁtting still requires a

text:
When dealing in an extremely low data regime,
where only a single or a few annotated images of the new
class are available, such ﬁne-tuning based transfer learning
often fails and may cause overﬁtting (Shaban et al., 2017;
Rakelly et al., 2018).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Few-shot learning is a machine learning technique that
aims to address situations where an existing model needs
to generalize to an unknown semantic class with a few ex-
amples at a rapid pace (Fei-Fei et al., 2006; Miller et al.,
2000; Fei-Fei, 2006).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The basic concept of few-shot learn-
ing is motivated by the learning process of humans, where
learning new semantics is done rapidly with very few obser-
vations, leveraging strong prior knowledge acquired from
past experience.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
While few-shot learning for image classi-
ﬁcation and object detection is a well studied topic, few-
shot learning for semantic image segmentation with neural
networks has only recently been proposed (Shaban et al.,
2017; Rakelly et al., 2018).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
It is an immensely challeng-
ing task to make dense pixel-level high-dimensional pre-
dictions in such an extremely low data regime.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
But at
the same time, few-shot learning could have a big impact
on medical image analysis because it addresses learning
from scarcely annotated data, which is the norm due to

In this article, we propose a few-shot seg-

A key to achieve this goal is to
