text:
Background on Few-Shot Segmentation
Few-shot learning algorithms try to generalize a model
to a new, previously unseen class with only a few labeled
examples by utilizing the previously acquired knowledge
from diﬀerently labeled training data.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
1 illustrates
the overall setup, where we want to segment the liver in
a new scan given the annotation of liver in only a single
slice.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
A few-shot segmentation network architecture (Sha-
ban et al., 2017; Rakelly et al., 2018) commonly consists
of three parts: (i) a conditioner arm, (ii) a set of interac-
tion blocks, and (iii) a segmentation arm.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
During infer-
ence, the model is provided with a support set (Is, Ls(α)),
consisting of an image Is with the new semantic class (or
organ) α outlined as a binary mask indicated as Ls(α).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In addition, a query image Iq is provided, where the new
semantic class is to be segmented.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The conditioner takes
in the support set and performs a forward pass.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This gen-
erates multiple feature maps of the support set in all the
intermediate layers of the conditioner arm.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This set of
feature maps is referred to as task representation as they
encode the information required to segment the new se-
mantic class.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The task representation is taken up by the
interaction blocks, whose role is to pass the relevant infor-
mation to the segmentation arm.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The segmentation arm
takes the query image as input, leverages the task informa-
tion as provided by the interaction blocks and generates a
segmentation mask Mq for the query input Iq.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Thus, in-
teraction blocks pass the information from the conditioner
to the segmenter and form the backbone for few-shot se-
mantic image segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Existing approaches use weak
interactions with a single connection either at the bottle-
neck or the last layer of the network (Shaban et al., 2017;
Rakelly et al., 2018).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Challenges for Medical Few-Shot Segmentation
Existing work in computer vision on few-shot segmen-
tation processes 2D RGB images and uses a pre-trained
model for both segmenter and conditioner arm to aid train-
ing (Shaban et al., 2017; Rakelly et al., 2018).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Pre-trained
models provide a strong prior knowledge with more power-
ful features from the start of training.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Hence, weak inter-
action between conditioner and segmenter is suﬃcient to
train the model eﬀectively.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The direct extension to med-
ical images is challenging due to the lack of pre-trained
models.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Instead, both the conditioner and the segmenter
need to be trained from scratch.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
However, training the
network in the absence of pre-trained models with weak
interaction is prone to instability and mode collapse.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Instead of weak interaction, we propose a strong inter-
action at multiple locations between both the arms.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The
strong interaction facilitates eﬀective gradient ﬂow across
the two arms, which eases the training of both the arms
without the need for any pre-trained model.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For eﬀectu-
ating the interaction, we propose our recently introduced
‘channel squeeze & spatial excitation’ (sSE) module (Roy
et al., 2018b,a).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In our previous works, we used the sSE
2


blocks for adaptive self re-calibration of feature maps to
aid segmentation in a single segmentation network.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Here,
we use the sSE blocks to communicate between the two
arms of the few-shot segmentation network.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The block
takes as input the learned conditioner feature map and
performs ‘channel squeeze’ to learn a spatial map.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This
is used to perform ‘spatial excitation’ on the segmenter
feature map.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We use sSE blocks between all the encoder,
bottleneck and decoder blocks.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
SE blocks are well suited
for eﬀectuating the interaction between arms, as they are
light-weight and therefore only marginally increase the
model complexity.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Despite its light-weight nature, they
can have a strong impact on the segmenter’s features via
re-calibration.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Existing work on few-shot segmentation focused on 2D
images, while we are dealing with volumetric medical
scans.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Manually annotating organs on all slices in 3D im-
ages is time consuming.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Following the idea of few-shot
learning, the annotation should rather happen on a few
sparsely selected slices.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
To this end, we propose a vol-
umetric segmentation strategy by properly pairing a few
annotated slices of the support volume with all the slices
of the query volume, maintaining inter-slice consistency of
the segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Few-Shot Learning
Methods for few-shot learning can be broadly divided
into three groups.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019
arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
These
approaches are often prone to overﬁtting as they attempt
to ﬁt a complex model on a few new samples.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Methods in
the second group aim to predict classiﬁers close to the base
classiﬁer to prevent overﬁtting.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The basic idea is to use
a two-branch network, where the ﬁrst branch predicts a
set of dynamic parameters, which are used by the second
branch to generate a prediction (Bertinetto et al., 2016;
Wang and Hebert, 2016).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The third group contains al-
gorithms that use metric learning.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
They try to map the
data to an embedding space, where dissimilar samples are
mapped far apart and similar samples are mapped close to
each other, forming clusters.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019
arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Few-Shot Segmentation using Deep Learning
Few-shot image segmentation with deep neural networks
has been explored only recently.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In one of the earliest
work, Caelles et al.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
(2017) leverage the idea of ﬁne-tuning
a pre-trained model with limited data.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The authors per-
form video segmentation, given the annotation of the ﬁrst
frame.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Although their model performed adequately in this
application, such approaches are prone to overﬁtting and
adapting a new class requires retraining, which hampers
the speed of adaptation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
(2017) use a 2-arm
architecture, where the ﬁrst arm looks at the new sample
along with its label to regress the classiﬁcation weights for
the second arm, which takes in a query image and gen-
erates its segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Dong and Xing (2018) extended
this work to handle multiple unknown classes at the same
time to perform multi-class segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
(2018) took it to an extremely diﬃcult situation where
supervision of the support set is provided only at a few se-
lected landmarks for foreground and background, instead
of a densely annotated binary mask.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Existing approaches
for few-shot segmentation were evaluated on the PASCAL
VOC computer vision benchmark (Shaban et al., 2017;
Rakelly et al., 2018).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
They reported low segmentation
scores (mean intersection over union around 40%), con-
ﬁrming that few-shot segmentation is a very challenging
task.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
All of the above mentioned papers depend on pre-
trained models to start the training process.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Although
access to pre-trained models is relatively easy for computer
vision applications, no pre-trained models are available for
medical imaging applications.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Moreover, they use 2D RGB
images, whereas we deal with 3D volumetric medical scans.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This is more challenging, because there is no established
strategy to select and pair support slices with the query
volume.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This can lead to situations where the query slice
can be very diﬀerent from the support slice or may not
even contain the target class at all.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In the domain of medical image segmentation, recently
Zhao et al.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
used a learnt transformation
to highly augment a single annotated volume for one-
shot segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This diﬀers from our approach in
two aspects: (i) they use a single fully annotated volume,
whereas we use annotations of only a few slices, (ii) they
use a learnt representation to highly augment the single
3


annotated volume for segmentation, whereas we use sep-
arate dataset with annotations provided for other classes.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We follow the experimental setting deﬁned in computer vi-
sion PASCAL VOC benchmarks by Shaban et al.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Method
In this section, we ﬁrst introduce the problem setup,
then detail the architecture of our network and the training
strategy, and ﬁnally describe the evaluation strategy for
segmenting volumetric scans.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

{(Ii
T , Li
T (α))}N
i=1 comprises N pairs of input image IT and
its corresponding binary label map LT (α) with respect to
the semantic class (or organ) α.

text:
All the semantic classes
α which are present in the label map Li
T ∈DTrain belong
to the set LTrain = {1, 2, .
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Here κ
indicates the number of classes (organs) annotated in the
training set.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The objective is to learn a model F(·) from
DTrain, such that given a support set (Is, Ls(ˆα)) /∈DTrain
for a new semantic class ˆα ∈LTest and a query image Iq,
the binary segmentation Mq(ˆα) of the query is inferred.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
1 illustrates the setup for the test class ˆα = liver in
a CT scan.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The semantic classes for training and testing
are mutually exclusive, i.e., LTrain ∩LTest = ∅.

text:
One fundamental diﬀerence of few-shot segmentation
to few-shot classiﬁcation or object detection is that test
classes LTest might already appear in the training data as

title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For instance, the network has al-
ready seen the liver on many coronal CT slices as part
of the background class, although liver was not a part of

title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This potentially forms prior knowl-

title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Architectural Design
As mentioned earlier, our network architecture consists
of three building blocks: (i) a conditioner arm, (ii) interac-
tion blocks with sSE modules, and (iii) a segmenter arm.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The conditioner arm processes the support set to model
how a new semantic class (organ) looks like in an image.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
It eﬃciently conveys the information to the segmenter arm
through the interaction blocks.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The segmenter arm seg-
ments the new semantic class in a new query image by uti-
lizing the information provided by the interaction blocks.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
2 and 3 illustrate the architecture in further detail,
which is also described below.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In our framework, we choose the segmenter and condi-
tioner to have a symmetric layout, i.e., both have four en-
coder and decoder blocks separated by a bottleneck block.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The symmetric layout helps in having a strong interaction
between matching blocks, as feature maps have the same
spatial resolution.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In existing approaches, conditioner and
segmenter only interact via the ﬁnal layer, before generat-
ing segmentation maps (Shaban et al., 2017; Rakelly et al.,
2018).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Such weak interaction at a single location was suf-
ﬁcient for their application, because they were able to use
a pre-trained model, which already provides reasonably
good features.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
As we do not have a pre-trained network,
we propose to establish a strong interaction by incorporat-
ing the sSE blocks at multiple locations.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Such interactions
facilitate training the model from scratch.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Conditioner Arm
The task of the conditioner arm is to process the support
set by fusing the visual information of the support image Is
with the annotation Ls, and generate task-speciﬁc feature
maps, capable of capturing what should be segmented in
the query image Iq.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We refer to the intermediate feature
maps of the conditioner as task representation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We pro-
vide a 2-channel input to the conditioner arm by stacking
Is and binary map Ls(α).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
(2017), where they multiplied Is and Ls(α) to gen-
erate the input.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Their motivation was to suppress the
background pixels so that the conditioner can focus on
the patterns within the object (like eyes or nose patterns
within a cat class).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This does not hold for our scans due
to the limited texture patterns within an organ class.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For
example, voxel intensities within the liver are quite homo-
geneous with limited edges.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Thus, we feed both parts of
the support set to the network and let it learn the optimal
fusion that provides the best possible segmentation of the
query image.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The conditioner arm has an encoder-decoder based ar-
chitecture consisting of four encoder blocks, four decoder
blocks, separated by a bottleneck layer, see ﬁg.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Both
encoder and decoder blocks consist of a generic block con-
stituting a convolutional layer with kernel size of 5 × 5,
stride of 1 and 16 output feature maps, followed by a
parametric ReLU activation function (He et al., 2015) and
a batch normalization layer.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In the encoder block, the
generic block is followed by a max-pooling layer of 2 × 2
and stride 2, which reduces the spatial dimension by half.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In the decoder block, the generic block is preceded by an
unpooling layer (Noh et al., 2015).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The pooling indices
during the max-pool operations are stored and used in the
corresponding unpooling stage of the decoder block for
up-sampling the feature map.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Not only is the unpooling
operation parameter free, which reduces the model com-
plexity, but it also aids to preserve the spatial consistency
for ﬁne-grained segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Furthermore, it must be
noted that no skip connections are used between the en-
coder and decoder blocks unlike the standard U-net ar-
chitecture (Ronneberger et al., 2015).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The reason for this
important design choice is discussed in Sec.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Interaction Block using ‘Squeeze & Excitation’ mod-
ules
The interaction blocks play a key role in the few-shot
segmentation framework.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
These blocks take the task rep-

text:
The block takes a conditioner
feature map Ucon and a segmenter feature map Useg as inputs.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
‘Channel squeeze’ is performed on Ucon to generate a spatial map
σ(q), which is used for ‘spatial excitation’ of Useg, which promotes
the interaction.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
resentation of the conditioner as input and convey them
to the segmenter to steer segmentation of the query im-
age.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Ideally these blocks should: (i) be light-weight to
only marginally increase the model complexity and com-
putation time, and (ii) ease training of the network by
improving gradient ﬂow.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We use the recently introduced ‘Squeeze & Excitation’
(SE) modules for this purpose.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
SE modules are compu-
tational units to achieve adaptive re-calibration of feature
maps within any CNN (Hu et al., 2018).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
SE blocks can
boost the performance of CNNs, while increasing model
complexity only marginally.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For classiﬁcation (Hu et al.,
2018), the feature maps are spatially squeezed to learn a
channel descriptor, which is used to excite (or re-calibrate)
the feature map, emphasizing certain important channels.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We refer to it as spatial squeeze and channel excitation
block (cSE).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In our recent work, we extended the idea
to segmentation, where re-calibration was performed by
squeezing channel-wise and exciting spatially (sSE), em-
phasizing relevant spatial locations (Roy et al., 2018a,b).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In both cases, SE blocks are used for self re-calibration, i.e,
the same feature map is used as input for squeezing and
excitation operations.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
However, here we propose to use
SE blocks for the interaction between the conditioner and
the segmenter.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The conditioner feature maps are taken as
input for the squeezing operation and its outputs are used
to excite the segmentation feature maps as detailed below.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Segmenter Arm
The goal of the segmenter arm is to segment a given
query image Iq with respect to a new, unknown class α,
by using the information passed by the conditioner, which
captures a high-level information about the previously un-
seen class α.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The sSE modules in the interaction block
compresses the task representation of the conditioner and
adaptively re-calibrate the segmenter’s feature maps by
spatial excitation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The encoder-decoder architecture of the segmenter is
similar to the conditioner, with a few diﬀerences.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Firstly,
the convolutional layers of both the encoder and decoder
blocks in the segmenter have 64 output feature maps, in
contrast to 16 in the conditioner.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This provides the seg-
menter arm with a higher model complexity than the con-
ditioner arm.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Sec-
ondly, unlike the conditioner arm, the segmenter arm pro-
vides a segmentation map as output, see Fig.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Thus
a classiﬁer block is added, consisting of a 1 × 1 convolu-
tional layer with 2 output feature maps (foreground, back-
ground), followed by a soft-max function for inferring the
segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Thirdly, in the segmenter, after every en-
coder, decoder and bottleneck block, the interaction block
re-calibrates the feature maps, which is not the case in the
conditioner arm.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Training Strategy
We use a similar training strategy to Shaban et al.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We simulate the one-shot segmentation task with
the training dataset DTrain as described below.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
It con-
sists of two stages (i) Select a mini-batch using the Batch
Sampler and (ii) Training the network using the selected
mini-batch.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
To simulate the one-shot segmentation
task during training, we require a speciﬁc strategy for se-
lecting samples in a mini-batch that diﬀers from tradi-
tional supervised training.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For each iteration, we follow
the steps below to generate batch samples:
1.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text: We ﬁrst randomly sample a label α ∈LTrain.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Next, we randomly select 2 image slices and their cor-
responding label maps, containing the semantic label
α, from training data DTrain.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The label maps are binarized representing semantic
class α as foreground and the rest as background.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
One pair constitutes the support set (Is, Ls(α)) and
the other pair the query set (Iq, Lq(α)), where Lq(α)
serves as ground truth segmentation for computing
the loss.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The
network
receives
the
support
pair
(Is, Ls(α)) and the query pair (Iq, Lq(α)) as a batch
for training purpose.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The support pair (Is, Ls(α)) is
concatenated and provided as 2-channeled input to the
conditioner arm.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The query image Iq is provided as input
to the segmentation arm.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
With these inputs to the two
arms, one feed-forward pass is performed to predict the
segmentation Mq(α) for the query image Iq for label
α.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We use the Dice loss (Milletari et al., 2016) as the
cost function, which is computed between the prediction
Mq(α) and the ground truth Lq(α) as
LDice = 1 −
2 P
x Mq(x)Lq(x)
P
x Mq(x) + P
x Lq(x)
(2)
where x corresponds to the pixels of the prediction map.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The learnable weight parameters of the network are opti-
mized using stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with mo-
mentum to minimize LDice.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
At every iteration, the batch
sampler provides diﬀerent samples corresponding to dif-
ferent α and the loss is computed for that speciﬁc α and
weights are updated accordingly.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
With the target class α
keeps changing at every iteration, the network converges.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Thus, after convergence we can say that the prediction be-
comes agnostic to the chosen α.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
That is for a new α, the
network should be able to perform segmentation, which is
what we expect during inference of a one-shot segmenta-
tion framework.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Volumetric Segmentation Strategy
As mentioned in the previous section, the network is
trained with 2D images as support set and query.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
But,
during the testing phase, a 3D query volume needs to be
segmented.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Therefore, from the support volume, we need
to select a sparse set of annotated slices that form the
support set.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
A straightforward extension for segmenting
the query volume is challenging as there is no established
strategy to pair the above selected support slices to all of
slices of the query volume, which would yield the best pos-
sible segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In this section, we propose a strategy
to tackle this problem.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Assume we have a budget of annotating only k slices in
the support volume, a query volume is segmented following
procedure:
1.

text:
Given a semantic class, we ﬁrst indicate the range of
slices (along a ﬁxed orientation) where the organ lies
for both support and query volume.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Let us assume

text:
The overall process of volumetric evaluation is illus-

In our experiments, we observed that
if the support slice and query slice are similar, segmen-
tation performance is better than if they were very dis-
similar.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Therefore, it is beneﬁcial if the overall contrast
of the scans (i.e.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
the intensity values or mutual informa-
tion) is similar.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

This can be intuitively understood as the
quality of the support the slice has a major impact on the

title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

In our evaluation strategy, for
a ﬁxed budget k, we made sure that the dissimilarity be-

text:
It must be noted that in the evaluation strat-

text:
In our
experiments, we pre-computed them using the label mask

title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In practice, this could be done either
manually by quickly scanning the slices, or using a simple
automated tool that can be trained for this purpose.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Dataset Description
We choose the challenging task of organ segmentation
from contrast-enhanced CT (ceCT) scans, for evaluating
our few-shot volumetric segmentation framework.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We use
the Visceral dataset (Jimenez-del Toro et al., 2016), which
consists of two parts (i) silver corpus (with 65 scans) and
(ii) gold corpus (20 scans).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
All the scans were resampled
to a voxel resolution of 2mm3.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Problem Formulation
As there is no existing benchmark for few-shot image
segmentation on volumetric medical images, we formulate
our own experimental setup for the evaluation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We use the
silver corpus scans for training (DTrain).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For testing, we
use the gold corpus dataset.

text:
One volume is used to create
the support set (Volume ID: 10000132 1 CTce ThAb), 14
volumes were used as validation set and 5 volumes as test
set.

text:
The IDs of the respective volumes are reported at the
end of the manuscript.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

these results to determine the architectural conﬁguration,
and number of support slices.

Finally, we use these results
and compare against existing approaches on the test set in
Sec.

text:
‘Squeeze & Excitation’ based Interaction
In this section, we investigate the optimal positions of
the SE blocks for facilitating interaction and compare the
performance of cSE and sSE blocks.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Here, we set the num-
ber of convolution kernels of the conditioner arm to 16 and
the segmenter arm to 64.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We use k = 12 support slices
from the support volume.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Since the aim of this experi-
ment is to evaluate the position and the type of SE blocks,
we keep the above parameters ﬁxed, but evaluate them
later.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
With four diﬀerent possibilities of placing the SE
blocks and two types cSE or sSE, we have a total of 8 dif-
ferent baseline conﬁgurations.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The conﬁguration of each
of these baselines and their corresponding segmentation
performance per fold is reported in Tab.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Firstly, one observes that BL-1, 3, 5, 7 with sSE have
a decent performance (more than 0.4 Dice score), whereas
BL-2, 4, 6, 8 have a very poor performance (less than 0.1
Dice score).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This demonstrates that sSE interaction mod-
ules are far superior to cSE modules in this application of
few-shot segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
It is very diﬃcult to understand
the dynamics of the network to say for certain why such
a behavior is observed.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Our intuition is that the under-
performance using channel SE blocks is associated with
the global average pooling layer it uses, which averages
the spatial response to a scalar value.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In our application
(or medical scans in general), the target semantic class
covers a small proportion of the support slice (around 5-
10%).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
When averaged over all the pixels, the ﬁnal value
is highly inﬂuenced by the background activations.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The
role of the interaction blocks is to convey the target class’s
semantic information from conditioner to segmenter.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
By
using channel SE as global average pooling the class in-
formation is mostly lost, thus cannot convey the relevant
information to the segmenter.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
3 is that out of all the
possible positions of the interaction block, BL-7, i.e., sSE
blocks between all encoder, bottleneck and decoder blocks,
achieved the highest Dice score of 0.567.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This result is con-
sistent across all folds.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
BL-7 outperformed the remaining
baselines for Fold-1 (liver), Fold-2 (spleen), Fold-3 (L/R
kidney) and Fold-4 (L/R psoas muscle) by a margin of 0.1
to 0.8 Dice points.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This might be related to the relative
diﬃculty associated with each organ.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Due to the contrast
and size, the liver is relatively easy to segment in compari-
son to spleen, kidney, and psoas muscles.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Also, BL-1, 3 and
5 performed poorly in comparison to BL-7.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This indicates
that more interactions aids in better training.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Comparing
BL-1, BL-3 and Bl-5, we observe that BL-1 provides bet-
ter performance.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This indicates that encoder interactions
are much powerful than bottleneck or decoder interactions.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
But, as BL-7 has a much higher performance than BL-1,
BL-3 and BL-5, we believe that encoder, bottleneck and
decoder interactions provide complementary information
to the segmenter for more accurate query segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
From these results, we conclude that interaction blocks
based on sSE are most eﬀective and we use sSE-based in-
teractions between all encoder, bottleneck, and decoder
blocks in subsequent experiments.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Eﬀect of Skip Connections in the Architecture
Due to the success of the U-net architecture (Ron-
neberger et al., 2015), using skip connections in F-CNN
models has become a very common design choice.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
With
skip connections, the output feature map of an encoder
block is concatenated with the input of the decoder block
with an identical spatial resolution.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In general, this con-
nectivity aids in achieving a superior segmentation per-
formance as it provides a high contextual information in
the decoding stage and facilitates gradient ﬂow.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In our

experiments, we intuitively started oﬀwith having skip
connections in both the conditioner arm and the segmenter
arm, but observed an unexpected behavior in the predicted
query segmentation masks.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
By including skip connections,
the network mostly copies the binary mask of the support
set to the output.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This is observed for all the folds both
in train and test set.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We refer to this phenomenon as
the copy over eﬀect.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Qualitative examples are illustrated
for each fold in Fig 5, where we see that, despite of the
support and the query images having diﬀerent shapes, the
prediction on the query image is almost identical to the
support binary mask.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We also performed a quantitative
analysis to observe the eﬀect on Dice scores due to this
copy over eﬀect.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Table 4 reports the performance with and
without skip connections, where we observe a 3% decrease
in Dice points due to the addition of skip connections.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We also performed experiments by separately adding the
skip connections in the conditioner and the segmenter arm.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We observe that the inclusion of skip connections only in
the conditioner arm reduced the performance by 6% Dice
points, whereas adding them only in the segmenter arm
made the training unstable.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For this evaluation, the num-
ber of convolution kernels for conditioner and segmenter
were ﬁxed at 16 and 64, respectively, and the evaluation
was conducted with k = 12 support slices.

Model Complexity of the Conditioner Arm
One important design choice is to decide the relative
model complexity of the conditioner arm compared to the
segmenter arm.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
1.1, the conditioner
takes in the support example and learns to generate task
representations, which are passed to the segmenter arm

This is utilized by the seg-
menter to segment the query image.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We ﬁx the number of
kernels of the convolutional layers (for every encoder, bot-
tleneck, and decoder) for the segmenter arm to 64.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We use
this setting as this has proven to work good in our prior
segmentation works across diﬀerent datasets (Roy et al.,
2019, 2018a).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Next, we vary the number of kernels of the
conditioner arm to {8, 16, 32, 64}.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The number of support
slices remains ﬁxed to k = 12.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We report the segmentation
results of these settings in Table 5.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The best performance
was observed for the conditioner with 16 convolution ker-
nels.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
One possible explanation of this could be that too
low conditioner complexity (like 8) leads to a very weak
task representation, thereby failing to reliably supporting
to the segmenter arm.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Whereas higher conditioner arm
complexity, 32 and 64 kernels (same as segmenter com-
plexity), might lead to improper training due to increased
complexity under limited training data and interaction.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We ﬁx the number of conditioner convolution kernels to
16 in our following experiments.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Eﬀect of the number of Support Slice Budget
In this section, we investigate the performance when
changing the budget for the number of support slices k
selected from the support volume for segmenting all the
query volumes.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Here, k can be thought of as the ‘num-
ber of shots’ for volumetric segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In all the pre-
vious experiments we ﬁx k = 12.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Here, we vary k be-
tween {1, 3, 5, 7, 10, 12, 15, 17, 20} and report the per-fold
and overall mean segmentation performance on validation
set in Table 7.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The per-fold performance analysis reveals
that the minimum number of slices needed for a decent
accuracy varies with the size of the target organ to be
segmented.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For Fold-1 (liver), one-shot volume segmentation (k =
1) yielded a Dice score of 0.678, which increased to 0.701
with k = 20.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We observed a saturation in performance
(Dice score of 0.70) with only 12 slices.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The segmentation
performance only marginally increased with higher values
of k.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For Fold-2 (spleen), the segmentation performance
initially increases with the increase in the value of k, then
the performance saturates with k ≥10 at a Dice score of
0.60.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The spleen is more diﬃcult to segment than liver,
thus requires more support.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For Fold-3 (right/ left kid-
ney), we observe behavior similar to Fold-2.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The segmen-
tation performance increases initially with increase in the
value of k and then saturates at a Dice score of 0.46 (this
is the mean between the two classes, left and the right kid-
ney) at k ≥10.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Also for Fold-4 (right/ left psoas muscle),
we see the Dice score saturates at 0.50 for k = 10.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The
overall mean Dice score across all the folds also saturates
at 0.56 with k = 10.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Based on these results, we conclude that k = 10 is the
maximum number of support slices required for our appli-
cation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Thus, we use this conﬁguration in the next exper-
iments.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:

text:
Comparison with existing approaches
In this section, we compare our proposed framework
against the other existing few-shot segmentation ap-
proaches.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
It must be noted that all of the existing methods
were proposed for computer vision applications and thus
cannot directly be compared against our approach as ex-
plained in Sec.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Hence, we modiﬁed each of the existing
approaches to suit our application.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Also, we evaluate the results on the 5
test query volumes.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text: First, we try to compare against Shaban et al.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Their main contribution was that the conditioner arm re-
gresses the convolutional weights, which are used by the
classiﬁer block of the segmenter to infer the segmentation
of the query image.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
As we do not have any pre-trained
models for our application, unlike Shaban et al.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
(2017),
we use the same architecture as our proposed method for
the segmenter and conditioner arms.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
No intermediate in-
teractions were used other than the ﬁnal classiﬁer weight
regression.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We attempted to train the network on our
dataset with a wide range of hyperparameters, but all the
settings led to instability while training.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
It must be noted
that one possible source of instability might be that we do
not use a pre-trained model, unlike the original method.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Thus, we were not able to compare our proposed method
with this approach.

Next, we compare our approach to Rakelly et al.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Again, this approach is not directly comparable to our ap-
proach due to the lack of a pre-trained model.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
One of
the main contributions of their approach was the interac-
tion strategy between the segmenter and the conditioner
using a technique called feature fusion.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
They tiled the
feature maps of the conditioner and concatenated them
with the segmenter feature maps.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Their implementation
introduced the interaction only at a single location (bottle-
neck).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We tried the same conﬁguration, but the network
did not converge.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Thus, we modiﬁed the model by intro-
ducing the concatenation based feature fusion (instead of
our sSE modules) at multiple locations between the con-
ditioner and segmenter arms.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
As we have a symmetric
architecture no tiling was needed.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Similar to our proposed
approach, we introduced this feature fusion based interac-
tion at every encoder, bottleneck, and decoder block.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In
this experiment, we are comparing our spatial SE based
interaction approach to the concatenation based feature
fusion approach.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We
observe 21% higher Dice points and 10 mm lower average
surface distance for our approach.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Next, we attempted to create hybrid baselines by com-
bining the above adapted feature fusion approach (Rakelly
et
al.,
2018)
with
classiﬁer
weight
regression
ap-
proach (Shaban et al., 2017).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We observe that by doing so
the performance increased by 3% Dice points.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Still, it had
a much lower Dice score (18% Dice points) in comparison
to our proposed approach.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
As a ﬁnal baseline, we compare our proposed frame-
work against the ﬁne-tuning strategy similar to Caelles
et al.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For a fair comparison, we only use the sil-
ver corpus scans (DTrain) and 10 annotated slices from the
support volume (10000132 1 CTce ThAb) for training.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
As
an architectural choice, we use our segmenter arm with-
out the SE blocks.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We pre-train the model using DTrain to
segment the classes of LTrain.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
After pre-training, we use
the learnt weights of this model for initialization of all the
layers, except for the classiﬁer block.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Then, we ﬁne-tune it
using the 10 annotated slices of the support volume having
a new class from LTest.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We present the segmentation per-
formance in Table 8.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Fine-tuning was carefully performed
with a low learning rate of 10−3 for 10 epochs.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The 10
selected slices were augmented during the training process
using translation (left, right, top, bottom) and rotation (-
15, +15 degrees).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Except for fold-1 (liver, Dice score 0.30)
all the other folds had a Dice score < 0.01.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Overall, this
experiment substantiated the fact that ﬁne-tuning under
such a low-data regime is ineﬀective, whereas our few-shot
segmemtation technique is much more eﬀective.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Comparison with upper bound model
In this section, we investigate the performance of our
few-shot segmentation framework to the fully supervised
upper bound model.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
For training this upper bound model,
we use all the scans of the Silver Corpus (with annotations
of all target organs) and deployed the trained model on the
Gold Corpus.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We use the standard U-Net (Ronneberger
et al., 2015) architecture for segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Segmentation
results are shown in Table 9.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We observe that this upper bound model has 20-40%
higher Dice points and 1-7 mm lower average surface dis-
tance in comparison to our few-shot segmentation frame-
work.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
It must be noted that this kind of diﬀerence in
performance can be expected as all slices from 65 fully
annotated scans were used for training.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In contrast, only
10 annotated slices from a single volume were used in our
approach.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
If access to many fully annotated volumes is
provided, it is always recommended to use fully super-
vised training.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Whenever a new class needs to be learnt
from only a few slices, our framework of few-shot segmen-
tation framework excels.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
It is also worth mentioning that
this drop in performance can also be observed in the PAS-

Dependence on Support set
In
all
our
previous
experiments,
one
volume
(10000132 1 CTce ThAb) was used as a support vol-
ume and the remaining 19 as query volumes for evaluation
purposes.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In this section, we investigate the sensitivity
of segmentation performance on the selection of the
support volume.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In this experiment, we randomly choose
5 volumes as support set from the validation set.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We
select one at a time and evaluate on the remaining 15
volumes (rest of the validation set and test set combined)
and report the per-fold and global Dice scores in Table 10.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We observe that changing the support volume does have
an eﬀect on the segmentation performance.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In Fold-1
(liver), the performance varies by 6% Dice points across
all the 5 selected support volume.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This change is 5%, 8%
and 5% Dice points for Fold-2 (spleen), Fold-3 (R/L kid-
ney), Fold-4 (R/L psoas muscle), respectively.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The overall
mean Dice scores vary by 4% points.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We conclude that
it is important to select an appropriate support volume
that is representative of the whole query set.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Yet, a good
strategy for making the selection remains as a future work.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Nevertheless, our framework shows some robustness to the
selection.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Discussion on spatial SE as interaction blocks
One concern regarding the use of spatial SE blocks for
interaction might be the spatial alignment of the target
class between the support and query images.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Although
in our application, there exist some partial overlap of the
target organ between the support and query slice, we be-
lieve the sSE based interaction is also capable of handling
cases where there is no such overlap.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We acknowledge
that similarity in spatial location does help in our appli-
cation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
However that is not the only factor driving the
segmentation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In Table 3, we present experiments for a
conﬁguration denoted as BL-3.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In this design, we only
keep the sSE block interaction at the bottleneck between
Segmenter and Conditioner.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Note that the spatial resolu-
tion in bottleneck feature map is very low (size: 16 × 32
for our case).
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This conﬁguration can be considered as a
spatially invariant fusion.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In this scenario, we also achieve
a decent segmentation score.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:

title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
One impor-
tant aspect of the sSE is it has a sigmoidal gating function
at the end before excitation.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
That means at any loca-
tion, it has the capacity to saturate all the neurons (i.e.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
all the output feature map activations becomes 1) which
keeps the segmenter feature maps unchanged.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Consider
such a case where at the encoder/ decoder feature maps
are unchanged and just the bottleneck is calibrated.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
This
would be similar to the BL-3 experiment which shows de-
cent performance.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Thus, we believe the sigmoidal gating
would control the sSE blocks only to re-calibrate the fea-
ture maps at scales it is necessary.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Conclusion
In this article, we introduced a few-shot segmentation
framework for volumetric medical scans.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
The main chal-
lenges were the absence of pre-trained models to start
from, and the volumetric nature of the scans.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We proposed
to use ‘channel squeeze and spatial excitation’ blocks for
aiding proper training of our framework from scratch.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
In
addition, we proposed a volumetric segmentation strat-
egy for segmenting a query volume scan with a support
volume scan by strategic by pairing 2D slices appropri-
ately.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We evaluated our proposed framework and several
baselines on contrast-enhanced CT scans from the Vis-
ceral dataset.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We compared our sSE based model to the
existing approaches based on feature fusion Rakelly et al.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text: (2018), classiﬁer regression Shaban et al.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Our framework outperformed all previous
approaches by a large margin.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Besides comparing to existing methods, we also provided
detailed experiments for architectural choices regarding
the SE blocks, model complexity, and skip connections.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
We also investigated the eﬀect on the performance of our
few-shot segmentation by changing the support volume
and the number of budget slices from a support volume.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Our proposed few-shot segmentation has the following
limitations.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Firstly, for a new query volume the start and
end slices need to be indicated for a target organ to be seg-
mented.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Secondly,
a very precise segmentation cannot be achieved using few-
shot segmentation due to extremely limited supervision
and the level of diﬃculty of this task.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
If the application
demands highly accurate segmentation, we recommend go-
ing the traditional supervised learning way by acquiring
more annotations for training.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:
Inspite of the limitations, the exposition of our proposed
approach is very generic and can easily be extended to
other few-shot segmentation applications.
title: arXiv:1902.01314v2  [cs.CV]  11 Oct 2019

text:

Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience
Arshad Ali*, Ashiq Anjum**, Tahir Azim*, Julian Bunn***, Ahsan Ikram*, 
Richard McClatchey**, Harvey Newman***, Conrad Steenberg***, Michael Thomas***, Ian Willers****
*National University of Sciences and Technology, Rawalpindi, Pakistan 
{arshad.ali, ahsan, tahir}@niit.edu.pk
**CCS Research Centre, University of the West of England, Bristol, UK, 
{ashiq.anjum, richard.mcclatchey}@cern.ch
***California Institute of Technology,   Pasadena, CA 91125, USA, 
{conrad,newman, thomas}@hep.caltech.edu, Julian.Bunn@caltech.edu
****CERN, CH-1211, Geneva 23, Switzerland Ian.Willers@cern.ch
ABSTRACT
This paper presents the design and implementation of a 
Grid-enabled physics analysis environment for handheld 
and other resource-limited computing devices as one 
example of the use of mobile devices in eScience.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Handheld devices offer great potential because they 
provide ubiquitous access to data and round-the-clock 
connectivity over wireless links.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Our solution aims to 
provide users of handheld devices the capability to launch 
heavy computational tasks on computational and data 
Grids, monitor the jobs’ status during execution, and 
retrieve results after job completion.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Users carry their jobs 
on their handheld devices in the form of executables (and 
associated libraries).
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Users can transparently view the 
status of their jobs and get back their outputs without 
having to know where they are being executed.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
In this 
way, our system is able to act as a high-throughput 
computing environment where devices ranging from 
powerful desktop machines to small handhelds can employ 
the power of the Grid.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
The results shown in this paper are 
readily applicable to the wider eScience community.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Keywords: Grid computing, Handheld Computing, Physics 
Analysis, Context-aware job submission.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
1
INTRODUCTION
Handheld computing and wireless networks hold a great 
deal of promise in the fields of ubiquitous data access and 
in particular for the eScience community.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
However, the 
analysis and processing of information to produce useful,
filtered results is a much larger challenge, since it requires 
not just network connectivity, but considerable processing 
power as well.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Most mobile and handheld devices, and 
even many laptop and desktop machines are extremely 
limited in the processing power they offer.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Many tasks are 
themselves so CPU-intensive and time-consuming that a 
single machine seems quite insufficient for them.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Grid
computing is poised to become the technology that will 
address this limitation.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
We present here a brief description 
of a Grid-enabled analysis environment for handheld 
devices that we are developing specially for the high-
energy physics (HEP) community.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
In this paper, we 
describe the architecture, design, and implementation of 
this Grid-enabled system for the handheld and mobile 
devices.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Such an architecture is readily adaptable to other 
data-intensive eScience analyses.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
The CMS (Compact Muon Solenoid) experiment [1] at 
CERN, due to commence in 2007, will use Grid-based 
data stores for the gigabytes of data it will generate each 
minute.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
In its raw form, the data cannot be used to 
generate significant results, because of its sheer quantity 
and complexity.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
The only way of analyzing this data is by 
using analysis applications to render it in the form of 2D 
and 3D diagrams, examinable on handheld devices, which 
scientists can use much more effectively in understanding 
the physics taking place in CMS.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
At the same time, 
efficient processing of data is required in order to make the 
analysis process as fast and as interactive as possible.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Our aim in this work is to develop a set of physics 
analysis applications for handhelds and to optimize them 
for maximum performance on the handheld devices.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
At the 
same time, we have been developing a Java-based 
framework, called JClarens, for hosting Web and Grid
services.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
The JClarens framework (described in [2]) allows 
users a single point of access to Grid services, such as data 
storage and replication services, monitoring services and 
job submission services.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Using JClarens, users can search 
for data on the Grid and can launch analysis jobs on the 
datasets from handheld and mobile devices.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
We not only 
use the handheld devices as a powerful data centric 
visualization tool but we also monitor the progress of the 
Grid jobs from these devices thereby helping the users to 
access and monitor the information and devices “on-the-
fly”.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
This research aims at making the power of Grid
computing available to resource-limited devices such as 
laptops and PDA’s, especially the Pocket PC and Palm.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
At 
the same time, we have been working on porting popular 
physics analysis applications to PDAs.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Due to the 
processing power and resources generally required by 
physics applications, none of the applications has yet been 
ported to the low resource (usually 32MB RAM) and slow 
processing (typically 200MHz to 400MHz) handheld 
devices.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Moreover, the slow, unreliable and sometimes 
intermittent nature of wireless connections has been a 


concern.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Combining 
mobile 
computing 
and 
Grid
computing should allow mobile and PDA users to submit 
jobs on the Grid and access its processing which is of great 
potential interest in the field of distributed scientific 
applications.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
This paper is organised as follows: in the next section 
we propose a Grid and mobile computing architecture 
which is suited for distributed physics analysis.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
This is 
followed by discussion of both the server-side and client-
side design aspects of this architecture in sections 3 and 4.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Thereafter we consider related work and outline the future 
direction of our work before drawing conclusions.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
2
ARCHITECTURE OF THE ANALYSIS 
ENVIRONMENT
The analysis environment, shown in Figure 1, consists of 
two entirely decoupled components.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
On one side are the 
resource-limited handheld devices and the applications 
specifically designed for these devices; on the other side is 
the JClarens Grid service host, which provides the 
facilities offered by the Grid to the handheld devices.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
The 
clients comprise simple, portable applications for handheld 
and desktop devices, which communicate with JClarens, 
using SOAP/XML-RPC.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
They can be programmed in 
C++, Java or any other language supporting XML-RPC.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Once logged on to JClarens, the clients can access the 
services offered by it.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
A detailed overview of the services 
offered by Clarens, and the way its clients communicate 
with it is described in [3].
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
As noted earlier the server 
basically acts as a Grid service host.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
It hosts any services 
and methods that have to be deployed on the Grid
communicating with clients using the lightweight XML-
RPC protocol.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
This allows clients to be made extremely 
simple, and abstracts away all the complexity of the hosted 
Grid services from the client.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
To provide Grid functionality on the handheld device, a 
separate service for job submission has been implemented 
in JClarens.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
This service (hosted on the resource broker) 
receives job submission requests from clients, and then 
attempts to determine the most suitable farm available for 
job submission, using monitoring information received 
from all the connected farms (or standalone computers).
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Once this has been located, a job ID is assigned to that 
particular job, the job submission request is forwarded to 
that particular farm, and a record of where the request was 
forwarded is stored in a database.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Any subsequent 
requests for checking the job status, for killing the job or 
for retrieving its outputs are forwarded to the JClarens 
server on the farm concerned.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Once a job request is 
forwarded to a particular farm, the JClarens server on that 
farm creates a temporary staging directory for Condor on 
the server machine.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
The executable, required libraries, a 
dynamically generated submit file and input files are 
copied into the staging directories, and “condor_submit” is 
called to submit the job to the Condor pool on the farm.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
The clients can subsequently check the status of their jobs 
(which can be running on any one of the available farms) 
at any time, without having to know where the jobs are 
actually being executed.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience

text:
Once the jobs are complete, the 
user can retrieve the results of his jobs at any time, using 
the relevant XML-RPC calls.
title: Mobile Computing in Physics Analysis - An Indicator for eScience
