text:
INTRODUCTION 
Cloud computing has sparked a huge amount of interest in the IT 
industry.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The market research and analysis firm IDC suggests that 
the market for cloud computing services was $16bn in 2008 and 
will rise to $42bn/year by 2012 [20].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Moreover, there has been a 
sharp rise in the number of cloud computing workshops and 
conferences recently and it is clear that academia is starting to 
take an interest in the new research challenges posed by cloud 
computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
There are many whitepapers and general introductions 
to cloud computing [e.g.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
9, 44, 49, 52], and a number of authors 
have previously discussed research challenges in cloud computing 
[e.g.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
However, these works have mostly 
focused on technical problems and little has been written about 
the research challenges for cloud computing from an enterprise or 
organizational perspective.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
This paper discusses some of these 
research challenges and puts them in context by reviewing the 
existing body of literature in cloud computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
We hope that this 
paper can act as a key resource for researchers in this fast moving 
field.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text: There seems to be many definitions of cloud computing [e.g.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The US National Institute of Standards and Technology 
(NIST) has published a working definition [37] that seems to have 
captured the commonly agreed aspects of cloud computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
This 
definition describes cloud computing using: 
• 
Five characteristics: on-demand self-service, broad 
network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, and 
measured service.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
Four deployment models: private clouds, community 
clouds, public clouds, and hybrid clouds.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
Three service models: Software as a Service (SaaS), 
Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Infrastructure as a 
Service (IaaS).
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Large enterprises inevitably have a large number of computing 
systems that have been developed over a long period of time.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
These depend on different technologies, have different ‘owners’ 
within the enterprise and have complex dependencies both 
between the systems themselves, the data that they process, the 
middleware used and the platforms on which they run.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Business 
processes have evolved to make use of the portfolio of systems 
available and these often rely on specific system features.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Normally, there is no individual or group within the enterprise 
who knows about all of the systems that are in use and 
dependencies are often discovered by accident when something 
simply stops working after a change has been made.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
For 
international companies, different jurisdictions mean that the 
same system in different countries has to be used and supported in 
different ways.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Furthermore, IT provision is profoundly affected by political 
considerations.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Senior management in the enterprise may set IT 
policies but these are left to individual parts of the enterprise to 
enact in their own way.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Managers naturally tend to adopt 
strategies that benefit their part of the company and vice versa.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The tension between central IT provision and end users has been 
constant since the 1960s with the constant complaint from users 
that central services are unwilling or unable to respond quickly to 
changing user requirements.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
It is important to highlight cloud computing research challenges 
from an enterprise perspective because cloud computing is not 
simply about a technological improvement of data centers but a 
fundamental change in how IT is provisioned and used [13].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Enterprises need to consider the benefits, risks and the effects of 
cloud computing on their organizations and usage-practices in 
order to make decisions about its adoption and use.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
In the 
enterprise, the “adoption of cloud computing is as much 
dependent on the maturity of organizational and cultural 
(including legislative) processes as the technology, per se” [19].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Companies such as Amazon, Google and Microsoft have invested 
vast sums of money in building their public clouds and they seem 
to be leading the way in the technological innovation of clouds by 
releasing frequent updates and new features for their services.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
For 
example, a quick look at Amazon Web Services’ (AWS) news 
archive1 shows that they rolled-out over ten new and 
technologically impressive features to their cloud offerings in 
2009.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
AWS also released a Security2 and an Economic3 center on 
their website, which shows that there is user demand for advice 
about the new economic and security implications of cloud 
computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
There is an opportunity for the academic community 
to address this demand by providing independent and impartial 
advice, tools and techniques to enterprise users who are interested 
in cloud computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Large organizations are inherently complex and for cloud 
computing to deliver real value to the enterprise rather than 
simply be a platform for simple tasks such as application testing 
or running product demos, the issues around migrating application 
systems to the cloud and satisfying the requirements of key 
system stakeholders have to be explored.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
These stakeholders 
include technical, project, operations and financial managers as 
well as the engineers who are going to be developing and 
supporting the individual systems.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
In enterprise, even desktop 
migration, which seems unproblematic from a cloud computing 
view, is challenging as we shall discuss later on.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Small startup 
companies are unlikely to face many of the issues discussed in 
this paper as they have no legacy systems or existing business 
procedures; they can simply start building their systems in the 
cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
From an enterprise perspective, costs are important but so 
too are customer relationships, public image, flexibility, business 
continuity and compliance.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Enterprises need to understand how 
cloud computing affects all of these but this paper focuses on the 
following specific topics:  
• 
The organizational change brought about with cloud 
computing (discussed in Section 2).
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
The economic and organizational implications of the 
utility billing model in cloud computing (discussed in 
Section 3).
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
The security, legal and privacy issues that cloud 
computing raises (discussed in Section 4).
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Each section of this paper starts by reviewing the existing body of 
literature in cloud computing and commenting on the work from

2 http://aws.amazon.com/security/ 
3 http://aws.amazon.com/economics/ 
an enterprise perspective.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
A number of research challenges are 
then highlighted within each section and these challenges are 
further discussed in Section 5.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
ORGANIZATIONAL CHANGE  
In early 2008, Nicholas Carr’s book titled The Big Switch: 
Rewiring the World, from Edison to Google was published [7], 
this was the first authorative text to accessibly popularize cloud 
computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
In it, Carr pointed out that the current mode of 
delivery for most IT systems is similar in some respects to that of 
electricity, circa 1910.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Back then, manufacturers had to build and 
maintain their own power generators even though that was not 
their main business.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Today, most corporations build and maintain 
their own data centers even though that is not their main 
expertise.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The result is a large number of “terribly inefficient” 
data centers [16].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Cloud computing could potentially solve this 
problem by enabling computing facilities such as storage, 
compute power, network infrastructure and applications to be 
delivered as a metered service over the internet, just like a utility.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
However, currently the typical enterprise IT department is not 
used to a utility billing model across shared infrastructures; 
resource sharing across such infrastructures requires a certain 
level of cultural and organizational process maturity, and the 
move towards cloud computing will require significant changes to 
business processes and organizational boundaries [19].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Therefore, 
users need to consider the benefits, risks and the effects of cloud 
computing on their organizations and usage-practices in order to 
make decisions about its adoption and use: the potential for

2.1 Research Challenges 
The research done so far has provided some glimpses of the ways

discussed in the literature to any significant extent is how to plan 
and design the actual organizational changes that will be required 
as IT provision changes as applications are migrated to the cloud, 
and as cloud services replace current desktop services.

3.3 Research Challenges 
In our view, the vast majority of current discussions on costs are 
simplistic when considered from an enterprise perspective.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
They 
simply consider the direct costs of computing provision, such as 
hardware and software costs and the costs of IT support.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Few 
discussions of cost consider the economic issues around 
application migration.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Nor do they consider existing procurement 
policies.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
How should these policies and processes be changed to 
accommodate the use of cloud computing in enterprise?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
And, if 
this is an interdisciplinary problem, how well is the field doing at 
collaborating with economists and business schools?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
They might 
already have answers to these questions, but the existing literature 
shows little signs of collaboration.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Currently, capital and operational budgets are often separately 
owned in many organizations, and procurement costs have to be 
known in advance before approval can be gained.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Furthermore, 
specific signatories may be required to approve procurement and 
this mitigates against the use of ‘on demand’ systems.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The utility 
billing model of cloud computing has a certain degree of 
uncertainty that goes against current procurement policies.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The 
uncertainty relates to usage patterns and deployment options, and 
although some providers such as Google allow limits to be set on 
costs, this might not be enough.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
For example, an enterprise 
system deployed in the cloud that reaches its cost limit and stops 
working at a critical time is not going to be acceptable.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Cost 
uncertainty is not regarded as an advantage in enterprise, so could 
cloud computing be compared with other utilities such as 
electricity and gas where usage patterns are mostly known and 
peaks can be anticipated?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Will IT usage peaks need to be 
investigated to allow the costs of running systems in the cloud to 
be more accurately predicated?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Currently, cloud providers such as AWS do not have features to 
enable the allocation of costs to individual organizational units or 
projects, and Amazon’s current model allows an AWS account to 
be used to purchase other goods and services from Amazon’s 
shopping site.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Some European businesses are asking AWS to post 
paper invoices to them9.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
These types of issues highlight the 
importance of auditability and compliance with financial 
regulations for enterprises who want to use cloud computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
However, these are all short term problems that can be addressed 
by cloud service providers, and the literature review provided in 
the previous sections show that academia is more interested in 
verifying the cost saving claims made by cloud providers.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The 
research done so far has provided a good insight into the 
economics of cloud computing but further work is required to 
develop tools and techniques that allow users to examine the true 
costs of using cloud computing for their own purposes.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
While costs are, of course, important for all enterprises, for 
individual managers, optimizing costs may not be their priority.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Rather, their concerns are to ensure that they deliver what they 
have promised.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The losses associated with failure to do so may far 
outweigh any costs savings from cloud migration and hence their 
priority is risk avoidance rather than cost saving.

text:
The main risks 
are mostly related to the security, legal and privacy issues that

there are only a small number of very big cloud providers?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
We 
should not forget that it used to be explicit IBM strategy to only 
lease equipment between the 1880s to 1950s because it was more 
profitable for them and less so for the customer.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
This was only 
stopped by anti-monopoly actions from the US government [12].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
SECURITY, LEGAL AND PRIVACY 
ISSUES  
Security, legal and privacy issues are widely acknowledged as 
being important in cloud computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Most of the security and 
privacy issues in cloud computing are caused by users’ lack of 
control over the physical infrastructure.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
This leads to legal issues 
that are affected by a cloud’s physical location, which determines 
its jurisdiction.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Furthermore, multitenancy brings the need for 
new solutions towards security and privacy.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
[27] 
provided an overview of the technical security issues in cloud 
computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Most of these issues are not specific to cloud 
computing as they relate to the underlying security problems of 
web services and web browsers.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
However, these security issues 
become more significant as cloud computing makes heavy use of 
web services and users rely on browsers to access services offered 
in the cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
For example, denial of service (DoS) attacks were a common 
concern even before cloud computing became popular, but when 
an application is targeted by a DoS attack in the cloud, the user or 
owner could actually end-up paying for the attack through their 
increased resource usage.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
This could be significantly higher than 
the peak usage of that application in an in-house data-center with 
limited resources.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
In fact, Jesper [28] recently reported this 
scenario with their application running on Amazon’s AWS cloud 
but they did not mention if they were charged for the usage 
generated or if Amazon waived the extra costs incurred as a result 
of the attack.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Such incidents and other security concerns have resulted in the 
establishment of the Cloud Security Alliance, which is an 
industrial group with members from corporations such as 
Microsoft and HP.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
They have published a set of best practices and 
guidelines for organizations adopting cloud computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
These 
guidelines come in the form of problem statements and issues that 
need to be considered by cloud service consumers.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
They cover a 
wide range of areas including encryption and key management, 
portability and interoperability, and risk management [11].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The 
European Network and Information Security Agency (ENISA) 
has also published a report about security issues in cloud 
computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
They identified 35 risks of using cloud computing [8], 
which are split into the following categories: 
• 
Policy and organizational risks such as vendor lock-in, 
loss of governance, compliance challenges, and cloud 
provider acquisition.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
Technical risks such as data leakage, distributed denial 
of service attacks, loss of encryption keys, and conflicts 


between customer hardening procedures and cloud 
platforms.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
Legal risks such as data protection and software 
licensing risks.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
Risks not specific to the cloud such as network 
problems, unauthorized access to data centers, and 
natural disasters.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
In addition to the above risks, ENISA’s report pointed out that 
security becomes cheaper to implement on a larger scale.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Therefore cloud providers could potentially provide greater 
security measures such as hardening VM instances or hiring 
experts that can deal with particular threats [8].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Others have also considered the security benefits of using cloud 
computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
[1] discussed the security levels of 
systems deployed in local data centers and compared this with the 
potential security of using a cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
In conclusion, they believe 
that systems deployed in the cloud could be made as secure as 
systems deployed in local data centers.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
They supported their 
hypothetical argument by mentioning the possible use of 
technologies such as encrypted storage to improve the security of 
a system deployed in the cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
This work needs extension as it 
falls short of analyzing potential weaknesses of running systems 
in the cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
One of the strengths of using SaaS applications in 
the cloud is that intruders do not have access to the application 
source code; this could be seen as a security advantage over non-
SaaS applications where intruders have full access to the binary 
code [53].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Start-up companies could use cloud computing to 
eliminate the costs of developing a secure infrastructure.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Kaufman 
[30] discussed security responsibility and asked if using cloud 
computing will result in security being a joint responsibility with 
the cloud providers.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The question of responsibility was also raised 
in Mansfield-Devine [35], who highlighted the lack of control and 
checks over third parties who develop applications on top of the 
PaaS layer of the cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text: Pearson [42] reviewed the main privacy risks in cloud computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
She summarized the risks from the perspective of individuals and 
organizations who wish to use cloud computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
From an 
individual’s perspective, cloud computing presents risks of 
personal data exposure, and lack of awareness regarding the 
location and jurisdiction of their data.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
From an organization’s 
perspective, cloud computing presents risks of legal liability, in 
addition to loss of reputation and user-trust in case of data loss.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Pearson outlined a set of privacy requirements that need to be 
considered when developing applications or services using the 
cloud, including giving users notice of the information being 
collected and how it will be used, and allowing them to opt-out of 
their information being collected.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The requirements were used to 
develop a number of design guidelines and “top tips” for software 
engineers developing cloud-based applications, these tips include 
minimizing the transfer of personal information to the cloud, and 
giving users control and choice over their data.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
[29] provided an in-depth review of the legal issues 
that UK-based organizations should consider when using cloud 
computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
These include three of the eight principles of the UK’s 
Data Protection Act (DPA), a law which came into place to 
protect personal data.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
For example, the first DPA principle 
requires organizations to ask for individual’s permission before 
processing personal data.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The use of cloud computing makes it 
difficult to provide individuals with full details of how and where 
their data will be processed.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
This lack of knowledge or 
transparency makes it difficult for individuals to reach “informed 
consent” [29].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
pointed to legal issues 
regarding confidentiality, copyright, and specific rules that govern 
businesses that are regulated by the Financial Services Authority 
in the UK.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
highlighted the main legal issues 
that need to be considered, it is difficult to provide detailed 
guidelines as each cloud usage scenario is different.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Physical data location is important as there are no internationally 
agreed rules about data protection and privacy.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
For example, 
Amazon offer their cloud services from both U.S.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
and European-
based data centers to be able to deal with differences in each 
region’s rules and regulations.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
[26] reviewed a range 
of issues that are affected by the geographic location of a cloud, 
i.e.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text: the location of the physical data centers.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
emphasized the importance of locality by pointing out that cloud 
computing increases the control of governments and corporations 
over resources.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
This is because cloud computing brings together 
vast amounts of data and computing resources in centralized data 
centers, compared to the current situation of hosting in 
geographically dispersed locations.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
While the location of the 
cloud has a significant effect on the rules and regulations that 
govern it, it is unclear “whether a cloud will be considered to 
legally be in one designated location [...] or in every location that 
has a data center that is part of the cloud” [26].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
It is unlikely that 
these jurisdiction issues will stop the use of cloud services; 
however, they will have long-term implications that need to be 
considered by users.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Nelson [41] wrote a report as an advisory document for the US 
government.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Nelson stressed the important role that governments 
can play in advancing the use of cloud computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Just as 
procurement decisions made by the U.S.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
government in the 1980s 
were fundamental in the development of the Internet, 
governments have the power to advance cloud computing usage 
by being “model users” [41].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Nelson also provided advice to 
governments and policy makers on how to proceed; this included 
the need for governments to update their IT procurement rules to 
support procurement of systems with a cloud service model, as 
well as the need for them to encourage experimentation with the 
cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
There are some signs that governments are taking on this 
type of advice, for example, the U.S.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Federal Government has 
issued a Request for Information regarding IaaS offerings [23].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
4.1 Research Challenges 
From an enterprise perspective, security and regulatory issues are 
critical.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Inevitably and understandably, most enterprises are likely 
to be cautious in moving their applications to the cloud simply 
because they do not really understand the security and regulatory 
issues involved.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The difficulties in understanding the issues are 
exacerbated by the complexity of their systems – some data may 
have to be maintained within a specific jurisdiction, some data 
may be transferable to the cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Even where models of existing 
systems, their data and their dependencies exist, such information 
has simply not been required up till now and collecting such 
information is likely to be costly.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The work done so far has identified some of the security, legal 
and privacy issues that arise as a result of using cloud computing, 


and this is an area where academia could be taking the lead.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
These 
are critical issues and their urgency is such that cloud users and 
their commercial providers might develop negotiated solutions in 
the immediate future.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The legal issues could eventually be 
addressed by governments who might change existing regulations 
or introduce new ones.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Some of the security issues such as DoS 
attacks are not specific to cloud computing but have new 
implications that need to be investigated.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Such security breaches, 
and failures in general, seem harder to hide in the cloud as shown 
by the widely discussed Google Mail outages.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Security is about perceptions, many worry about security in the 
cloud because of a lack of control, while others argue that systems 
deployed in the cloud could be made as secure as systems 
deployed in local data centers [1].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Some organizations might be 
over confident about their internal security policies, but liability 
issues need to be resolved before enterprises start migrating 
applications to the cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The addition of third parties into the 
provider-consumer relationship introduces liability issues.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
For 
example, who is going to be liable for an incident that occurs 
while an enterprise ‘bursts out’ of their private cloud onto a public 
cloud?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Regulations relating to data protection may place 
constraints on the movement of data and the national jurisdictions 
where it may be maintained.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Furthermore, the cost and time to 
move data around could be a major bottleneck in the cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Enterprises with large volumes of data may therefore wish to 
specify where that data should be made available, when it may be 
moved around, etc.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The practical issues that affect data migration 
in the cloud need to be investigated.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Another issue with data migration is compliance, which is 
especially challenging to satisfy when sensitive data is involved.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
For example, companies in the financial and health sectors have 
many regulatory requirements that restrict data movement.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Compliance departments are likely to be conservative in their 
interpretation of the regulations and will require very detailed 
evidence that any movement of data outside the enterprise does 
not have associated compliance risks.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Some interesting issues arise when an organization wishes to 
control (in some way) the behavior of its staff using technological 
means.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
This may be a particular problem where the company uses 
a mixture of in-house systems and cloud-based systems.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
An 
example of an issue might be the inclusion of a link in a document 
to a site that is blocked by in-house systems but which can be 
accessed from documents in the cloud-based system.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
If this site 
distributes malware, there is then a security threat to the 
organization.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
How will companies react to this and will they be 
aware of the problems?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
How can individual users be made aware 
of the issues and what can be done if they do not follow the 
accepted rules?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Of course, it may be that cloud providers will 
allow filters and rules to be applied to files that they manage.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
This 
might be fine if a company moves its services to the cloud 
provider as a whole but problems might arise when only some 
services are hosted on the cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
DISCUSSION 
For sure, the cloud is a disruptive technology that will change the 
ways in which individuals and enterprises work.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
So, what does 
cloud computing mean for enterprises that have large-scale 
complex IT systems which are, in general, long-lifetime 
organizational, systems of systems?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The difficult problems 
around such systems are:  
• 
Understanding the requirements of diverse stakeholders, 
who are often uninterested in the system, until it is 
delivered and disrupts their lives.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
Understanding how processes and organizations have to 
change to make effective use of a system.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
So-called 'brownfield development' where new systems 
have to inter-operate with a range of existing systems 
[25].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
Designing for resilience so that essential services will 
be provided with a high level of availability [24].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text: So where does the cloud affect practice here?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The issue of 
resilience is certainly one area – disaster recovery is potentially 
cheaper using external on-demand facilities.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
But how can the 
cloud contribute to other areas?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Well, things that might help are: 
• 
Easier prototyping and parallel operation.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Systems can 
be installed on an external cloud for experiment then 
migrated to an internal server for operation.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
A common 
problem is that old and new systems cannot currently be 
run together because this requires hardware replication.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text: Incremental development and delivery should be easier.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Issues of poor performance 
are common with new systems because the actual load 
is different from the predicted load.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Obviously, the 
cloud makes it easier to provide extra facilities but it 
may also make it easier to do load simulations.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
However, sharing internal and external servers may 
introduce new problems because of the time required 
for data transfer to external systems.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Lots of problems 
with existing systems arise because the data models 
produced are rigid.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
If we have lots of available 
computational power, can we escape from this rigidity 
and design systems that have a much more flexible data 
model but which can maintain integrity by doing more 
computation?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
Breaking down barriers created by current sandboxed 
IT systems.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The cloud facilitates more mobile and more 
diffused organizations.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Will using the cloud mean that 
the physical manifestations of many organizations are 
dramatically reduced (i.e.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Are there 
political issues here – might managers lose their visible 
empires?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Does the cloud make it easier or harder to 
make work visible?
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
However, the problem with researching such organizational issues 
is that they are quite hard to investigate.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The issues can certainly 
be flagged-up as we have done here in this paper, but some 
enterprises need to lead the way and take the plunge before these 
issues can be studied in real-life organizations.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Making decisions 
about migrating parts of a large-scale complex IT system to the 
cloud is not that simple because a range of issues need to be 
considered, including: 


• 
The effects of cloud computing on the work of IT 
departments and other parts of the organization.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
• 
The costs, risks and benefits of running systems in the 
cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
These issues have a significant impact on migration decisions, and 
more research needs to be done in this area.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
It is important to note 
that the migration of IT systems to the cloud is not going to be 
done overnight – some predict that it could take between 10 to 15 
years before enterprise makes this shift [48].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Therefore we are 
currently at the start of a transition period during which many 
decisions need to be made with respect to the migration of IT 
systems to the cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
New tools and techniques need to be 
developed to help managers in enterprise make migration 
decisions.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
One approach that could help decision making would be to 
develop a system modeling framework that can be used to model 
relevant attributes of large-scale IT systems.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The framework 
would need a range of models such as models of application 
portfolios, models of data, cost models etc.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
These models could 
then be used to reason about and investigate migration decisions.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
For example, by modeling a system’s hardware infrastructure and 
applications (at the executable level), it becomes possible to 
estimate the costs of running parts of that system in a cloud.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
However, costs alone are not sufficient to aid decision making – 
the risks and benefits of migration must also be included in the 
model.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Furthermore, it would also be useful to include system 
stakeholders in the model as it would help identify the effects of 
migration on their work.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Extending existing modeling notations such as UML and SysML 
might be one way to achieve this.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Relevant background for 
modeling applications and application portfolios includes work on 
modeling systems of systems [5, 57], enterprise system modeling 
[39, 43] and visualizing application portfolios [46].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Once 
applications are migrated to the cloud, the integration of legacy 
applications with cloud applications and the migration of data to 
the cloud must also be addressed [60].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Some enterprises have already started migrating desktop 
applications to the cloud [56].
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Even though this seems to be one 
relevant use of cloud computing, it can be challenging to integrate 
such desktop applications with legacy systems.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
For example, 
some organizations use Microsoft Excel as a front-end to access 
legacy systems, which often do the actual data processing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
It is 
unclear how the migration of such desktop applications, for 
example from Microsoft Office to Google Docs, is going to affect 
the integration of these applications with legacy systems.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
In conclusion, this paper discussed various research challenges for 
cloud computing from an enterprise perspective, and put them in 
context by reviewing the relevant literature.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
Cloud computing as a 
research field is still in its early years.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
There seems to be an 
increasing number of workshops and conferences that are 
dedicated to the research challenges posed by cloud computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
It 
is encouraging to see such interest from the academic community 
and it is hoped that this paper can act as a good starting point for 
researchers interested in the research challenges for enterprise 
cloud computing.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
The message here in our paper should not be taken as a negative 
comment on the use of cloud computing for enterprise, but that 
the research challenges highlighted here cannot be looked at from 
a purely technical perspective.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
These research challenges are 
interdisciplinary in nature, and there is a need for more co-
operation between researchers, cloud users, and service providers.
title: Proceedings Template - WORD

text:
As previously mentioned, cloud computing is more than just a 
technological change and the issues that have been discussed in 
this paper have the potential to influence wider adoption of cloud 
computing.

title: Cloud Computing

text:
Abstract— Computing as you know it is about to change, your applications and documents are going to move from the desktop 
into the cloud.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
I’m talking about cloud computing, where applications and files are hosted on a “cloud” consisting of thousands of computers 
and servers, all linked together and accessible via the Internet.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
With cloud computing, everything you do is now web based 
instead of being desktop based.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
You can access all your programs and documents from any computer that’s connected to the 
Internet.
title: Cloud Computing

text: How will cloud computing change the way you work?
title: Cloud Computing

text: For one thing, you’re no longer tied to a single computer.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
You can take 
your work anywhere because it’s always accessible via the web.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
In addition, cloud computing facilitates group collaboration, as 
all group members can access the same programs and documents from wherever they happen to be located.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Cloud computing 
might sound far-fetched, but chances are you’re already using some cloud applications.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
If you’re using a web-based email 
program, such as Gmail or Hotmail, you’re computing in the cloud.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
If you’re using a web-based application such as Google 
Calendar or Apple Mobile Me, you’re computing in the cloud.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
If you’re using a file- or photo-sharing site, such as Flickr or Picasa 
Web Albums, you’re computing in the cloud.
title: Cloud Computing

text: It’s the technology of the future, available to use today.
title: Cloud Computing

text:

Computing Advantage and Disadvantage, Who Benefits from Cloud Computing, Cloud Computing for Everyone, Using cloud 
computing Services, Computing on the Cloud & Privacy, Security, and standards Compliance.

1 INTRODUCTION
irst, cloud computing isn’t network computing.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
With 
network computing, application or documents are 
hosted on a single company’s server and accessed 
over the company’s network.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Cloud computing is a lot 
bigger than that.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
It encompasses multiple companies, 
multiple servers, and multiple networks.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Plus, unlike 
network computing, cloud services and storage are ac-
cessible from anywhere in the world over an Internet 
connection; with network computing, access is over the 
company’s network only.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Cloud computing also isn’t traditional outsourcing, 
where a company farms out (subcontracts) its computing 
services to an outside firm.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
While an outsourcing firm 
might host a company’s data or applications, those doc-
uments and programs are only accessible to the compa-
ny’s employees via the company’s network, not to the 
entire world via the Internet.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
So, despite superficial simi-
larities, networking computing and outsourcing are not 
cloud computing.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
What does cloud 
computing mean for the way you use a computer?
title: Cloud Computing

text:
What 
are the top cloud computing applications?
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Good ques-
tions all, and all answered in this paper, Cloud Compu-
ting.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
That Change the Way You Work and Collaborate 
Online.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
I don’t pretend to answer every question you may 
have (the overly technical ones in particular), but I do try 
to give you a good solid overview of the cloud computing 
phenomenon, and introduce you to some of the more 
popular cloud applications—in particular, those that faci-
litate group collaboration.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
And that’s where cloud com-
puting really shines.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Whether you want to share photo-
graphs with family members, coordinate volunteers for a 
community organization, or manage a multifaceted 
project in a large organization, cloud computing can help 
you collaborate and communicate with other group 
members.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
You’ll have a better idea of how this works af-
ter you read the book, but trust me on this one—if you 
need to collaborate, cloud computing is the Sway to do it.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Key to the definition of cloud computing is the “cloud” 
itself.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
For our purposes, the cloud is a large group of in-
terconnected computers.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
These computers can be person-
al computers or network servers; they can be public or 
private.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
For example, Google hosts a cloud that consists of 
both smallish PCs and larger servers.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Google’s cloud is a 
private one (that is, Google owns it) that is publicly ac-
cessible (by Google’s users).
title: Cloud Computing

text:
This cloud of computers ex-
tends beyond a single company or enterprise.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
The appli-
cations and data served by the cloud are available to 
broad group of users, cross-enterprise and cross-platform.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Any authorized user can access 
these docs and apps from any computer over any Internet 
connection.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
And, to the user, the technology and infra-
structure behind the cloud is invisible.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
It isn’t apparent 
(and, in most cases doesn’t matter) whether cloud servic-
es are based on HTTP, HTML, XML, JavaScript, or other 
specific technologies.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
It might help to examine how one of 
the pioneers of cloud computing, Google, perceives the

text:
From Google’s perspective, there are six key prop-
erties of cloud computing as below, 
1) Cloud computing is user-centric.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Once you as a user 
are connected to the cloud, whatever is stored there—
documents, messages, images, applications, whatever—
becomes yours.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
In addition, not only is the data yours, 
but you can also share it with others.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
In effect, any device 
that accesses your data in the cloud also becomes yours.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Instead of focusing 
on the application and what it can do, the focus is on 
what you need done and how the application can do it for 
you., Traditional applications—word processing, spread-
sheets, email, and so on—are becoming less important 
than the documents they create.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Connecting hundreds 
or thousands of computers together in a cloud creates a 
wealth of computing power impossible with a single 
desktop PC.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Because data 
is stored in the cloud, users can instantly retrieve more 
information from multiple repositories.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
You’re not li-
mited to a single source of data, as you are with a desktop 
PC.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
With all the various 
data stored on the computers in a cloud, data mining and 
analysis are necessary to access that information in an 
intelligent manner.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Many of the tasks 
necessary with cloud computing must be automated.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
For 
example, to protect the integrity of the data, information 
stored on a single computer in the cloud must be repli-
cated on other computers in the cloud.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
If that one com-
puter goes offline, the cloud’s programming automatical-
ly redistributes that computer’s data to a new computer 
in the cloud.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
All these definitions behind us, what constitutes 
cloud computing in the real world?
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Internet-accessible, 
group-collaborative applications are currently available, 
with many more on the way.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Perhaps the best and most 
popular examples of cloud computing applications today 
are the Google family of applications—Google Docs & 
Spreadsheets, Google Calendar, Gmail, Picasa, and the 
like.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
All of these applications are hosted on Google’s 
servers, are accessible to any user with an Internet con-
nection, and can be used for group collaboration from 
anywhere in the world.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
In short, cloud computing enables 
a shift from the computer to the user, from applications to 
tasks, and from isolated data to data that can be accessed 
from anywhere and shared with anyone.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
The user no 
longer has to take on the task of data management; he 
doesn’t even have to remember where the data is.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
All that 
matters is that the data is in the cloud, and thus imme-
diately available to that user and to other authorized us-
ers.
title: Cloud Computing

3 UNDERSTANDING CLOUD ARCHITECTURE 
ECTIONS 
Cloud architecture, the systems architecture of the soft-
ware systems involved in the delivery of cloud compu-
ting, comprises hardware and software designed by a 
cloud architect who typically works for a cloud integra-
tor.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
It typically involves multiple cloud components 
communicating with each other over application pro-
gramming interfaces, usually web services.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
This closely resembles the Unix philosophy of having 
multiple programs each doing one thing well and work-
ing together over universal interfaces.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Complexity is con-
trolled and the resulting systems are more manageable 
than their monolithic counterparts.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Cloud architecture extends to the client, where web 
browsers and/or software applications access cloud ap-
plications.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Cloud storage architecture is loosely coupled, often 
assiduously avoiding the use of centralized metadata 
servers which can become bottlenecks.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
This enables the 
data nodes to scale into the hundreds, each independent-
ly delivering data to applications or users.

The key to cloud computing is the “cloud”—a massive 
network of servers or even individual PCs interconnected 
in a grid.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
These computers run in parallel, combining the 
resources of each to generate supercomputing-like power.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Put simply, the cloud is a 
collection of computers and servers that are publicly ac-
cessible via the Internet.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
This hardware is typically owned 
and operated by a third party on a consolidated basis in 
one or more data center locations.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
The machines can run 
any combination of operating systems; it’s the processing 
power of the machines that matter, not what their desk-
tops look like.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
As shown in Figure 1.1, individual users connect to the 
cloud from their own personal computers or portable 
devices, over the Internet.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
To these individual users, the 
cloud is seen as a single application, device, or document.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
The hardware in the cloud (and the operating system that 
manages the hardware connections) is invisible.

4 WHY COMPUTING ADVANTAGE AND 
DISADVANTAGE:- 
Any serious analysis of cloud computing must address 
the advantages and disadvantages offered by this burge-

What’s good—and what’s bad—about 
cloud computing?
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Advantage as below,     
We’ll start with the advantages offered by cloud compu-
ting—and there are many.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
1) Lower-Cost Computers for Users 
2) Improved Performance 
3) Lower IT Infrastructure Costs 
4) Fewer Maintenance Issues 
5) Lower Software Costs 
6) Instant Software Updates 
7) Increased Computing Power 
8) Unlimited Storage Capacity 
9) Increased Data Safety 
10) Improved Compatibility Between Operating Systems 
11) Improved Document Format Compatibility 
12) Easier Group Collaboration 
13) Universal Access to Documents 
14) Latest Version Availability 
15) Removes the Tether to Specific Devices 
Disadvantage as below, 
That’s not to say, of course, that cloud computing is with-
out its disadvantages.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
There are a number of reasons why 
you might not want to adopt cloud computing for your 
particular needs.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Let’s examine a few of the risks related 
to cloud computing.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
1) Requires a Constant Internet Connection 
2) Doesn’t Work Well with Low-Speed Connections 
3) Can Be Slow 
4) Features Might Be Limited 
5) Stored Data Might Not Be Secure 
6) If the Cloud Loses Your Data, You’re screwed.
title: Cloud Computing

text: Let’s face it, cloud computing isn’t for everyone.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
What 
types of users, then, are best suited for cloud compu-
ting—and which aren’t?
title: Cloud Computing

text:
1) Collaborators 
2) Road Warriors 
3) Cost-Conscious Users 
4) Cost-Conscious IT Departments 
5) Users with Increasing Needs 
Collaborators:- 
If you often collaborate with others on group projects, 
you’re an ideal candidate for cloud computing.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
The abili-
ty to share and edit documents in real time between mul-
tiple users is one of the primary benefits of web-based 
applications.
title: Cloud Computing

text: it makes  collaborating easy and even fun.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Road Warriors:- 
Another prime candidate for cloud computing is the 
road warrior.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
When you work at one office today, at 
home the next day, and in another city the next, it’s tough 
to keep track of all your documents and applications.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
You 
may end up with one version of a document on your 
work PC, another on your laptop, and a third on your 
home PC—and that’s if you remember to copy that doc-
ument and take it with you from one location to the next.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Now that you know a little bit about how cloud compu-
ting works, let’s look at how you can make cloud compu-
ting work for you.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
By that I mean real-world examples of 
how typical users can take advantage of the collaborative 
features inherent in web-based applications.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
We’ll start our real-world tour of cloud compu-
ting by examining how an average family can use web-
based applications for various purposes.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
As you’ll see, 
computing in the cloud can help a family communicate 
and collaborate—and bring family members closer to-
gether.

7 USING CLOUD COMPUTING SERVICE:- 
Services provided by cloud computing can be split into 
three major categories.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
i)Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS):- 
Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) like Amazon Web Ser-
vices provides virtual servers with unique IP addresses 
and blocks of storage on demand.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Customers benefit from 
an API from which they can control their servers.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Because 
customers can pay for exactly the amount of service they 
use, like for electricity or water, this service is also called 
utility computing.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
ii) Software-as-a-Service (SaaS):- 
Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) is the broadest market.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
In 
this case the provider allows the customer only to use its 
applications.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
The software interacts with the user through 
a user interface.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
These applications can be anything from 
web based email, to applications like Twitter or Last.fm.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
7 COMPUTING ON THE CLOUD:- 
Cloud computing is offered in different forms as below, 
1) Public Cloud.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
2) Private Cloud

3) Hybrid cloud which combine both Public & Private.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Public Cloud:- 
Public cloud or external cloud describes cloud computing 
in the traditional mainstream sense, whereby resources 
are dynamically provisioned on a fine-grained, self-
service basis over the Internet, via web applications/web 
services, from an off-site third-party provider who shares 
resources and bills on a fine-grained utility computing 
basis.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Hybrid cloud:- 
A hybrid cloud environment consisting of multiple in-
ternal and/or external providers "will be typical for most 
enterprises".
title: Cloud Computing

text:
A hybrid cloud can describe configuration 
combining a local device, such as a Plug computer with 
cloud services.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
It can also describe configurations combin-
ing virtual and physical, colocated assets—for example, a 
mostly virtualized environment that requires physical 
servers, routers, or other hardware such as a network 
appliance acting as a firewall or spam filter.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Private cloud:- 
Private cloud and internal cloud are neologisms that 
some vendors have recently used to describe offerings 
that emulate cloud computing on private networks.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
These 
(typically virtualisation automation) products claim to 
"deliver some benefits of cloud computing without the 
pitfalls", capitalising on data security, corporate gover-
nance, and reliability concerns.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
They have been criticized 
on the basis that users "still have to buy, build, and man-
age them" and as such do not benefit from lower up-front 
capital costs and less hands-on management, essentially 
"[lacking] the economic model that makes cloud compu-
ting such an intriguing concept".
title: Cloud Computing

text:
While an analyst predicted in 2008 that private cloud 
networks would be the future of corporate IT, there is 
some uncertainty whether they are a reality even within 
the same firm.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Analysts also claim that within five years a 
"huge percentage" of small and medium enterprises will 
get most of their computing resources from external 
cloud computing providers as they "will not have econo-
mies of scale to make it worth staying in the IT business" 
or be able to afford private clouds.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Analysts have re-
ported on Platform's view that private clouds are a step-
ping stone to external clouds, particularly for the financial 
services, and that future datacenters will look like internal 
clouds.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
The term has also been used in the logical rather than 
physical sense, for example in reference to platform as a 
service offerings, though such offerings including Micro-
soft's Azure Services Platform are not available for on-
premises deployment 
9 PRIVACY, SECURITY, AND STANDARDS 
COMPLIANCE:- 
A major issue in cloud computing, especially with public 
clouds, is protection of user data.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
One concern is that 
cloud providers themselves may have access to custom-
ers' unencrypted data - whether it's on disk, in memory, 
or transmitted over the network.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
To limit this exposure, 
many sources recommend never giving providers access 
to unencrypted data or keys.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
A second concern is that 
many public cloud providers are unable or unwilling to 
allow auditing of their physical or network security 
measures.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
This can preclude them, and thus their custom-
ers, from meeting standards such as the US government's 
HIPAA or Sarbanes-Oxley, the European Union's Data 
Protection Directive, or the credit card industry's PCI 
DSS.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
The extent of some public clouds across multiple 
legal jurisdictions further complicates this issue; see "Le-
gal Issues" for more detail.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
These concerns are considered 
key obstacles to broader adoption of cloud computing, 
making them areas of active research and debate among 
cloud computing practitioners and advocates.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
10 CONCLUSION: - 
We are observes that cloud computing has been defined 
as "everything that we currently do".
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Many technologies 
that have been branded as "cloud computing" have ex-
isted for a long time before the "cloud" label came into 
existence.
title: Cloud Computing

text:
Examples include databases, load balanced on-
demand web hosting services, network storage, real time
