text:
In this case, parallel programming using POSIX
threads or OpenMP APIs would be hard.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
We see
at least three problems with the user or compiler-
initiated multithreading model:
(1) Maintaining
scalable number of threads while optimizing paral-
lelization is diﬃcult.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
(2) Thread creation and de-
stroy overheads may be signiﬁcant, where threads
are temporary objects.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
By using the proposed streaming model, compu-
tations are deﬁned by stream entities.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Each com-
ponent in Figure 7 can be built with stream enti-
ties through addition, concatenation, and composi-
7


tion operations.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
At runtime, the micro scheduler
deﬁned in Section 5.3 keeps a dynamically scalable
number of worker threads in a browser, and sched-
ules stream entities as execution units.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Isolation is
enforced through memory coloring in the browser’s
virtual address space.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
7
Related Works
All directly related works have been mentioned in
the previous sections.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
What we discuss here are
publications that may provide alternative solutions
to various aspects of the problems we try to solve,
or are noteworthy references to earlier works.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
We
skip publications on virtualization, threads schedul-
ing and thread models, because they are highly spe-
cialized topics concerning implementations.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
A school of analytical models, represented by the
most recent Multi-BSP [62], provides theoretical
abstractions that bridge parallel algorithm designs
with multicore architectures.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
One common trait of
such models is their emphasize on portable perfor-
mance.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
However, such motivation may not ensure
engineering success, as there are more imminent con-
cerns, such as indeterminacy, synchronization over-
head, and scalability, that highlight the weaknesses
of current parallel programming tools.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
In the Multi-
BSP case, the model should be useful in analyzing
a given parallel computing system in some multi-
core architectures, but the model does not provide
enough engineering guidance in designing such a sys-
tem.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
It is not surprising that the Multi-BSP model’s
hierarchically nested component structures resemble
the stream entity hypergraphs in our model, but our
stream entities have richer engineering implications.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Someone has suggested that the GeneSC model
that we promote was a rediscovery of Kahn’s Process
Networks [29, 30].
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
But that’s a misunderstanding, if
one can ignore the superﬁcial resemblance in our use
of certain terminologies.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
The simple language Kahn
deﬁned and discussed is both synchronous and deter-
ministic, due to the language’s blocking primitives
such as “wait” and “send”, which build the language’s
FIFO queuing model for communication.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
The Kahn
model suits concurrent tasks, but has little emphasis
on high performance computation.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
We argue that a
concurrent computing model should convey intrin-
sic data and task precedence constraints but should
not sacriﬁce asynchronism when it is possible.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
The
ﬂexibility provided by asynchronism is essential for
achieving high-performance through out-of-order ex-
ecution, thus is needed by a broader range of appli-
cations.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
In his thesis on StreamIt [58], Thies summarized
languages from Kahn’s Process Networks to syn-
chronous dataﬂow [38] and CSP (Communicating
Sequential Processes) [27].
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Such languages have a
common feature that is the pipe-lining of concurrent
task-executions.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
StreamIt also experimented on the
idea of stream graph that allows compiler optimiza-
tions.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Our main reservation with such languages is
their weak power in modeling data parallelism.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Jade [55] represents an important experiment on
parallel programming language design.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Jade pre-
serves the serial semantics of a program, implicitly
exploits task parallelism, and moves data closer to
processors.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
However, if it was designed for a smooth
transition from sequential programming to parallel
programming, Jade’s dependence on its type system
and explicit object-access control still exposes low-
level synchronizations to programmers.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
While ar-
guably such low-level controls provide programming
ﬂexibility, not all the details are essential to algo-
rithm design.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
On the other hand, we might consider
that Jade lacks the power for deﬁning concurrent
execution structures in a larger program-scope.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Another parallel programming language that has
limited adoption in the academia is UPC [61].
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
UPC
is another multithreading language that extends C.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
The two most noteworthy features of UPC include
the partitioned global address space model and the
memory consistence model, where the latter is im-
plemented using explicit access controls to shared
objects.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Again, the weakness of UPC might be its
explicit synchronizations exposed to programmers.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Chapel [14] is a complex parallel programming
language that supports global level data and control
abstractions, architecture-aware locality mapping,
object-oriented programming and generic program-
ming.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
What impressed us most are the language’s
global views on data and control, and its ability to
map the global views onto data/control aﬃnity ab-
stractions called locales.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Though we do not have ex-
perience with Chapel programming, by studying its
ancestor ZPL [57], we see one motivation that em-
phasizes both performance and portability on var-
ious parallel architectures.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
For that purpose, ZPL
and Chapel may strike for a balance between ab-
straction and expressiveness.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
The emphasis of our
GeneSC model, however, is (high-level) concurrency
structures in problems’ solutions.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Therefore, we can
rely on extensions to existing languages to achieve
concurrency structure abstraction, and delegate per-
formance concerns (e.g.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
the mapping to parallel ar-
chitectures) to languages and compilers that imple-
ment the kernel functions encapsulated by a stream
entity.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
8


We’ve mentioned Cilk++ earlier but consider that
it deserves more attention.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
First, Cilk++ is inter-
esting because of its theoretical foundation and its
internal handling of both task-parallelism and data-
parallelism.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Cilk++ has a provable threading model
that can be analyzed using DAG (Directed Acyclic
Graph).
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Conceptually, a Cilk++ strand is like a
stream entity of our model, though Cilk++ does
not have an explicit construct for strand.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Second,
Cilk++ uses only two language constructs, namely
cilk_spawn and cilk_for, to deﬁne task paral-
lelism and data parallelism at language level, though
Cilk++ language constructs have scope restrictions
that make C++/Cilk++ mixed-language program-
ming cumbersome [15].
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Finally, Cilk++ has re-
stricted but innovative debugging model and hyper-
objects support.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
In a survey [43] on parallel computing languages
for multicore architectures, McCool compared and
contrasted existing programming language mod-
els and computing paradigms.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
One shared inter-
est is about stream computing, particularly the
“SPMD stream processing model”, implemented on
the RapidMind platform [46].
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Three of the plat-
form’s major contributions may be summarized as
follows.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
First, at language level, RapidMind adopts
a type-system approach inlining with Jade, CUDA
and OpenCL; but the type system is much simpler
and exposes no synchronization nor access control
details.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Second, at runtime level, RapidMind sched-
ules and load-balances the executions of concurrent
“program objects” through backend (runtime) sup-
ports, which identify and parallelize the program ob-
jects.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Noticeably, a program object has similar pur-
pose as our stream entity but lacks of precedence
constraints.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Third, the RapidMind platform sup-
ports heterogeneous multicores.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
One needs to be
reminded, however, that while it does not relying
on conventional threads, RapidMind’s implementa-
tion of the SPMD stream processing model limits the
platform to applications that show data parallelism.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
In [53], the authors proposed a close-to-metal sub-
strate called “lithe”, which uses a primitive named
“hart” and its context to carry out application-level
threads in multicore processors.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Lithe also has an
interface layer that allows processor allocation and
thread scheduling through runtime systems.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
The
motivation was to control hardware resources sub-
scription and to support parallel library composi-
tions.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
As an alternative OS-level thread implemen-
tation, Lithe has been used to run existing multi-
threading libraries such as OpenMP.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Bläser in [8] reported a component-based language
and operating system that supported concurrent and
structured computing.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
In that system, a component
encapsulates data and computing, which are deﬁned
as services to be produced by one component and
consumed by another.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
The emphasis on relations
among components is like ours, except that com-
munications among related components use explicit
message passing.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Finally, the GeneSC model is for concurrent
computing at instruction-block level.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Hardware-
dependent considerations, such as supports to many-
core and heterogeneous multicore, will rely on imple-
mentations, particularly those at runtime and oper-
ating system levels, such as those in [7, 41, 50].
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
8
Concluding Remarks
In this paper, we discuss a generalized stream com-
puting model, known as the GeneSC model, for
concurrent computing.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
This model is not about
yet another programming technique or a program-
ming paradigm, but an abstract design guidance for
parallel programming languages, compilers, runtime
and/or operating systems for multicore.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
We high-
light the beneﬁts of the model through operational
analysis, and demonstrate its power through an en-
abled programming framework and example design
considerations that support the framework.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Speciﬁ-
cally, the GeneSC model brings in a non-distributive
execution unit called stream entity, and uses it as
the foundation for designs at programming language
level, compiler level, and operating system level.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Be-
sides stream entity, two other crucial additions un-
like traditional practices are also introduced: a new
hypergraph section in a program’s runtime layout,
and operating system kernel initiated threads that
form stream-entity/stream-data pipelines to multi-
core processors.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
The signiﬁcance of the GeneSC
model is that, by harnessing concurrency informa-
tion expressed in algorithms and by applying the in-
formation to runtime scheduling, the model provides
tractable, concurrent operations; and may serve as
a natural extension of the von Neumann model for
parallel computing architectures.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
Our GeneSC model facilitates a high-level abstrac-
tion of concurrency in computing, yet does not incur
a deep learning curve because the kernel of a stream
entity is the encapsulation of a single-/multiple-
procedure function that can be implemented in ex-
isting sequential languages.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
By delegating many
of the tough issues (e.g.
title: arXiv:1012.1641v1  [cs.PL]  7 Dec 2010

text:
synchronization and task
scheduling) in concurrent computing to platform
software such as compilers and operating systems,
programmers can focus more on analyzing their ap-
9


plication problems, designing algorithms, and deﬁn-
ing concurrency structures of the solutions—a shift
from machine-oriented programming to application-
oriented programming; at the meantime, sequen-
tial programming develops smoothly into concurrent
programming.

1
(MC2)2: A Generic Decision-Making Framework
and its Application to Cloud Computing
Michael Menzel, FZI Forschungszentrum Informatik Karlsruhe, menzel@fzi.de
Marten Sch¨onherr, Telekom Laboratories Berlin, marten.schoenherr@telekom.de
Jens Nimis, FZI Forschungszentrum Informatik Karlsruhe, nimis@fzi.de
Stefan Tai, KIT Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, stefan.tai@kit.edu
Abstract—Cloud computing is a disruptive technology, repre-
senting a new model for information technology (IT) solution en-
gineering and management that promises to introduce signiﬁcant
cost savings and other beneﬁts.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The adoption of Cloud computing
requires a detailed comparison of infrastructure alternatives,
taking a number of aspects into careful consideration.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Existing
methods of evaluation, however, limit decision making to the
relative costs of cloud computing, but do not take a broader range
of criteria into account.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
In this paper, we introduce a generic,
multi-criteria-based decision framework and an application for
Cloud Computing, the Multi-Criteria Comparison Method for
Cloud Computing ((MC2)2).
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The framework and method allow
organizations to determine what infrastructure best suits their
needs by evaluating and ranking infrastructure alternatives using
multiple criteria.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Therefore, (MC2)2 offers a way to differentiate
infrastructures not only by costs, but also in terms of beneﬁts,
opportunities and risks.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
(MC2)2 can be adapted to facilitate
a wide array of decision-making scenarios within the domain of
information technology infrastructures, depending on the criteria
selected to support the framework.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Index Terms—Cloud computing, comparison, decision-making,
multi-criteria, requirements, evaluation, cost, information tech-
nology (IT) support, framework, method, IT supported process,
IT-based, IT infrastructures.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
INTRODUCTION
T
HE use of cloud computing services promises to elim-
inate large upfront capital investments and to reduce
operational costs.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Associated with these objectives are further
beneﬁts of improved innovation processes and a faster time-to-
market.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
To which extent such cost savings and beneﬁts can be
achieved, however, and whether these are in conﬂict with other
criteria, must be carefully evaluated.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Criteria include technical
criteria such as workload management patterns, scalability
requirements, data volumes and data access patterns, as well
as non-technical criteria ranging from strategic outsourcing
models to regulatory compliance and legal issues.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Alternatives
to a Cloud-based solution are, for example, traditional on-
premise IT infrastructures.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The decision whether or not to use Cloud computing ser-
vices must take the diversity of relevant criteria into account.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The set of criteria and their respective weight nevertheless
varies from organization to organization, and from case to
case.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Therefore, a generic framework that can be tailored to
speciﬁc organizations and application cases is needed.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The
(MC2)2 method and framework introduced in this paper
aims to address this problem and to ﬁll the current void
for a multi-criteria decision framework for evaluation and
comparison of Cloud-based and non-Cloud IT infrastructure
solutions.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
In this paper, we introduce (MC2)2: a generic
decision-making framework and its application for Cloud
Computing, (MC2)2 ﬁlls the current void for a multi-criteria
decision framework that supports a systematic evaluation and
comparison of Cloud-based with non-Cloud IT infrastructure
solutions.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
After a reﬂection of
related works in Section II, we introduce the decision-making
framework and its central process in Section III.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The frame-
work describes an IT supported process that helps to build a
method to evaluate IT solutions for speciﬁc scenarios.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Next,
we give an example of how to use the framework to deﬁne
an evaluation method to compare different IT infrastructure
options for the scenario of new software deployment.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
This
example serves as a concrete use case that compares Cloud-
based with non-Cloud, traditional IT infrastructure solutions.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
We discuss future work in Section IV and conclude in Section
V.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
RELATED WORK
A common, recommended approach to evaluate arbitrary
alternatives is to use multi-criteria decision methods.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
How-
ever, generic decision-making methods have to be customized
for the domain of IT infrastructure solutions.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Customization
is non-trivial, as multi-criteria decision-making methods do
not advise on how to ﬁnd eligible criteria and factors that
have an inﬂuence on the evaluation and decision making.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Current approaches to IT infrastructure decision-making that
involve important criteria have been developed in operations
research, in particular in the ﬁeld of outsourcing theories [?].
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Ngwenyama and Bryson [?] introduced a transaction costs-
based approach that allows to analyze information systems
outsourcing decisions.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
However, this approach only supports
a limited set of relevant factors, and is not open to extensions
needed to incorporate new criteria for outsourcing alternatives
in the ﬁeld of cloud computing.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
There have also been attempts
to evaluate IT infrastructures and especially to support the
decision making of whether to move information systems into
the cloud or not.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Two different approaches are described by
Armbrust et al.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
propose a
simple formula to compare the costs of a cloud service with
those of a datacenter based on hours of use, whereas Walker
proposes a net present value based approach to compare the

2

costs of leasing and purchasing a CPU over several years.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Both
works focus only on a single cost aspect in the broad spectrum
of relevant IT infrastructure criteria.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
In our previous work, we proposed the CloudTCO frame-
work [?] to widen the range of costs considered when compar-
ing IT infrastructure options.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
CloudTCO, however, is limited
to addressing non-technical requirements and focuses on costs,
but does not compare beneﬁts.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Moreover, the resulting values
can hardly be compared in a ratio scale but more in an interval
or ordinal scale.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Thus, concluding comparison statements such
as ”alternative 1 is two times better that alternative 2” are
impossible to express.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
THE (MC2)2 FRAMEWORK
The (MC2)2 framework is an evolution of the CloudTCO
approach introduced by Klems et al.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
(MC2)2 extends
the basic CloudTCO idea by supporting a wider range of
diverse criteria, including beneﬁtial factors .
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Further, while
CloudTCO uses an utility function to compare result values
(MC2)2 allows to evaluate IT infrastructure alternatives on a
ratio scale.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
(MC2)2 has been designed as a generic framework
that can be customized to deﬁne different, evaluation methods
that are focused in scope and address a diverse set of criteria.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
(MC2)2 proposes an abstract, linear process to step-wise
deﬁne a concrete evaluation method.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The process incorpo-
rates several steps from scenario and alternatives deﬁnition
to evaluation and ranking.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Additionally, the process includes
the consideration of an organizations internal and external
information resources, and considers the integration and use
of various software systems that can support the process, for
example:
• Knowledge bases within the organization, e.g., wikis,
reporting and document management software systems,
databases with explicit knowledge
• Business intelligence systems, e.g., data mining and text
mining tools
• Survey creation, deployment and analysis software sys-
tems
The process suggests a step-by-step order to build a con-
crete, customized evaluation method.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
First, a scenario and a
number of alternatives are deﬁned.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Next, relevant criteria and
requirements are identiﬁed.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
A multi-criteria decision-making
method is then chosen and subsequently conﬁgured; this sets
the criteria and requirements as parameters of the selected
decision-making method.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The result is a custom evaluation
method that can be used to evaluate the alternatives under
consideration.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Figure 1 depicts the process steps, each of which is de-
scribed in further detail below.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Deﬁne Scenario
A scenario speciﬁes the particular situation under consider-
ation, describing the business and IT context, environment,
constraints and requirements, and at the same time setting
the goals.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The description of the scenario sets the scope and
goals for the evaluation method to be created.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Comprehensive
expertise and experience is required to deﬁne the scenario, and
Fig.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The Process within the (MC2)2 Framework
sufﬁcient effort should be spent to facilitate the subsequent
method steps.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Deﬁne Alternatives
When using our framework, at least two alternatives must
be deﬁned for a given scenario.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Every alternative aims at being
a solution to the scenarios goals.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Each alternative is deﬁned
by many attributes.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
An attribute is a name of a characteristic
common to all alternatives and can be assigned a value.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Every
pair of alternatives differs in at least one attribute.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Otherwise,
an additional attribute in which both alternatives differ must
be introduced.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
To derive alternatives the given situation and deﬁned goals
must ﬁrst be studied.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Finding alternatives for a scenario
involves expertise, creativity and experience, which ideally
is pooled organization-wide.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
This can be supported by IT
systems such as:
• Expert search systems to set up expert panels or for
consulting purposes
• Work collaboration systems to collaboratively ﬁnd alter-
natives
• Internal databases with externalized knowledge about
experiences, for instance:
– Pages in an internal wiki system about related topics
– Internal documents with past experiences and reports
about related decisions and evaluations
It is possible to perform this search process systematically
by ﬁrst searching for a set of important attributes and then
assigning values to each attribute, for each alternative.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
At the
end, each alternative is deﬁned by the values assigned to the
set of attributes.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
A value for an attribute can be an exact
measured value, or an explanation or description in natural
language.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
A detailed scenario description can signiﬁcantly ease
the search for attributes.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
A comprehensive scenario description
may already reveal different options and variables within the
scenario.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text: Each option or variable is a potential attribute.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text: FULL VERSION PUBLISHED IN PROCEEDINGS OF INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON CLOUD COMPUTING AND VIRTUALIZATION, GSTF, MAY 2010.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
3
Besides analyzing the scenarios description, again expertise
and experience usually leads to the identiﬁcation of many
important attributes.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
By considering information resources
from within or from outside the organization the attribute
identiﬁcation process can make use of existing externalized
knowledge.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
(For reasons of focus, this paper, however, will not
examine possible information resources and speciﬁc knowl-
edge management techniques useful to externalize experiences
made during the process.)
C.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Deﬁne Criteria
Alternatives deﬁned by attributes do not necessarily provide
sufﬁcient information for an evaluation.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The introduction of
criteria extends attribute deﬁnitions with scales and makes
them usable in evaluation methods.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
This is why one of the
essential steps within (MC2)2 is the deﬁnition of criteria.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Having completed this step, requirements can be derived from
the criteria and the multi-criteria decision-making method of
choice can be conﬁgured and applied.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The set of attributes determined during the deﬁnition of
alternatives serve as a starting point to derive the set of
criteria.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text: Criteria are different from attributes in their form.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
A criterion consists of a topic or question to be examined
and a type which is either qualitative or quantitative.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
In case
of a quantitative criterion a scale of measurement has to be
deﬁned.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Expect some multi-criteria decision-making methods
to restrain the choice of measurement scales.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
This implies
that depending on the multi-criteria decision-making method
of choice quantitative criteria that do not fulﬁll the scale
restrictions will have to be excluded from the set of criteria
and, thus, will not be considered by the resulting evaluation
method.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Qualitative criteria do not necessarily rely on a scale as
they are not easily measurable.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Some multi-criteria decision-
making methods do not support qualitative criteria and require
transforming qualitative criteria into quantitative criteria by
creating a scale.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Furthermore, criteria do not always inﬂuence a decision
positively but negatively as well.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
According to Saaty [?]
criteria can typically be clustered into the four types beneﬁts,
opportunities, costs, and risks.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
While criteria of the types
beneﬁts or opportunities are positive, criteria of the types
costs and risks are negative.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Nevertheless, other criteria type
categories are possible as well.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Deﬁne Requirements
Prior to the evaluation step, requirements are deﬁned.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Re-
quirements help to ﬁlter out alternatives that are not feasible
within the constraints of the given scenario.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
A requirement of a
scenario is expressed as a minimal or maximal constraint that
has to be attained by an alternative regarding one criterion.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Every alternative with at least one criterion value lower than
a minimum or higher than a maximum constraint is not
realizable and, hence, ﬁltered out.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
An alternative that has been
ﬁltered out will not be considered in the evaluation method.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The procedure of ﬁltering can be performed for minimum
constraints with a conjunctive satisﬁcing method and respec-
tively for maximum constraints with a disjunctive satisﬁcing
method [?].
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Typically, the conjunctive method is applied to
restrictions on positive criteria and the disjunctive method to
restrictions on negative criteria.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Optionally, there might be
restrictions that should not be considered as criteria, but as
a requirement only.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
In this case a new criterion needs to be
introduced which is only considered as a requirement, but not
as a criterion in the set of criteria.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
As in criteria deﬁnition IT-based information resources and
software systems are capable of supporting this step.

text:
Choose Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Method
Many multi-criteria decision-making methods are eligible
upon which the custom evaluation method can be deﬁned.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
An
overview and comparison of different multi-criteria decision-
making methods can be found in [?] [?].
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The method has to
be chosen according to the preferences of an organization and
depending on the case.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
It is required that application of the
method results in values, and not just a ranking.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
We suggest the Analytic Network Process (ANP) [?] [?]
method as the favorable evaluation method due to its ability
to incorporate complex criteria networks during the evalua-
tion.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
More complex criteria networks enable a more realistic
modeling of criteria dependencies.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
In ANP, criteria networks
not only include weights, but feedback loops and clusters
as well.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Moreover, ANP employs pair-wise comparisons and
normalization to support the use of qualitative criteria.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The
combination of pair-wise comparisons and normalization suc-
ceeds to assign values to quantitative and qualitative criteria
on a ratio scale.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
However, qualitative criteria values still are
derived from subjective ratings.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Conﬁgure Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Method
Before an evaluation method can be build and the evaluation
results can be computed with that method in the ﬁnal step
of the process, it may be required to conﬁgure the multi-
criteria decision-making method.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
This typically means setting
parameters such as alternatives, requirements, and criteria, and
deﬁning weights and relations for the set of criteria.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Whether
a conﬁguration is needed or not depends on the evaluation
method of choice.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Setting parameters for an evaluation method mostly means
balancing parameters to customize the method to ﬁt the needs
of the scenario and goals.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
For most multi-criteria decision-
making methods this step consists of deﬁning criteria weights
and relations.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
In doing so, many multi-criteria decision-making
methods allow setting focus on several criteria within the
set of criteria by assigning weights.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Thereby the inﬂuence
of a criterion is intensiﬁed and other criteria’s inﬂuence is
weakened.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The weight describes the relative importance of a
criterion compared to all other criteria.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The process of deﬁning criteria interdependencies, and in
particular criteria networks can also be supported by IT based
information resources and software systems, especially when
complex criteria networks are desired to model the real world
situation.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Moreover, repositories of criteria network patterns
are helpful.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Resulting Evaluation Method
The process of the resulting rational evaluation method
and its inputs is depicted in Figure 2: Requirements are
used to ﬁlter out all alternatives that cannot fulﬁll each of
the requirements.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Following, all remaining alternatives are
evaluated by the given criteria considered in the multi-criteria
decision-making method of choice.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
To rank the alternatives
the alternatives can be sorted by their evaluation results.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The
alternative ranked as #1 is the optimal decision according to
its overall value.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Process of a Resulting Evaluation Method
The resulting evaluation method is reusable with changing
alternatives for decisions in the deﬁned scenario’s context.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Apply Resulting Evaluation Method
In the ﬁnal step the resulting, custom evaluation method is
applied to ﬁlter out the realizable alternatives and calculate the
evaluation results.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The calculation results in a rank and a value
assignment for each of the alternatives.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The assigned value is
according to the method of choice either absolute or a ratio
value relative to the other alternatives.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
We suggest to choose
a multi-criteria decision-making method that returns values on
a ratio scale.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The ﬁnal result of the custom evaluation method can be used
to make a substantiated, rational decision for an alternative
representing a solution in a scenario.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Section 8 in the appendix
examines the Analytic Network Process (ANP) which is a
comprehensive evaluation method that provides a ranking of
alternatives and value assignments on a ratio scale when
applied within a custom method created with the (MC2)2
framework.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
The ANP serves not only as an example for
a possible multi-criteria decision-making method that can
be applied within a custom methods process, but is also
the favorable multi-criteria decision-making method that we
suggest.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
As mentioned in Subsection III-F ANP allows to
deﬁne complex criteria networks and it results in an evaluation
on a ratio scale, which makes it a favorable basis for an
evaluation method.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
DISCUSSION & FUTURE WORK
The use of ANP to evaluate alternatives of IT infrastructures
raises several questions.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
First of all, pair-wise comparisons
with qualitative criteria are not trivial and must be done
subjectively as qualitative criteria are not measurable.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Group
evaluations might be a successful approach to strive for more
objective results in evaluations with many qualitative criteria.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Also, values of measurable quantitative criteria must be
collected ﬁrst.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Support for this step is not included in the
framework yet.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Later works to intensify the IT support within

5
the framework might include a support for data measurement
and collection or a list of adequate information resources might
be provided.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Nevertheless, further research on IT support for
the framework is needed.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
In particular, we aim to design easy-
to-use systems that support (MC2)2 and which integrates a
set of relevant existing information systems as information
resources or tools.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Especially, a list of suitable information
systems that serve as information resources to support the
deﬁnition of alternatives, criteria and requirements is an im-
portant future task.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
This should also include a categorization
of the information resources regarding different aspects, like
e.g., their usefulness.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Furthermore, ﬁelds of future work include research of
applicable sensitivity analysis tools and the integration into
the (MC2)2 framework, and a comparison of the advantages
and applicability of different multi-criteria decision-making
methods.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Moreover, an evaluation of the framework is an
important future step.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
CONCLUSIONS
Cloud Computing presents an opportunity to organizations
of all kinds, the beneﬁts, risks, and promises of which must
be carefully considered.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Adopting Cloud Computing is a
decision-making problem that requires identiﬁcation of criteria
and value-driven comparison of alternatives with respect to
the criteria selected.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
In this paper, we introduced (MC2)2: a
generic decision-making framework and an evaluation method
for Cloud Computing as its instantiation.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
(MC2)2 is a multi-
criteria decision framework that deﬁnes a systematic, step-wise
process that can be tailored to speciﬁc needs and preferences.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
To our knowledge, (MC2)2 is the ﬁrst comprehensive
decision making framework and method speciﬁcally in sup-
port of Cloud Computing scenarios.
title: Generic Decision-Making Framework Application Cloud Computing

text:
Nevertheless, (MC2)2 is
not restricted to Cloud Computing or even IT infrastructure
solutions, but has been designed as a generic approach that
can be applied to other complex decision-making processes
also.

Cactus Computational Framework
The Cactus framework [9,10] was designed and developed to enhance programming pro-
ductivity in large-scale science collaborations.
title: A Massive Data Parallel Computational Framework for Petascale/Exascale Hybrid Computer Systems arXiv:1201.2118v1  [cs.DC]  10 Jan 2012

text:

engineers to develop independent components for Cactus without worrying about porta-
bility issues on computing systems.
title: A Massive Data Parallel Computational Framework for Petascale/Exascale Hybrid Computer Systems arXiv:1201.2118v1  [cs.DC]  10 Jan 2012

text:
The common infrastructure provided by Cactus also
enables developing scientiﬁc codes that work across different disciplines.
title: A Massive Data Parallel Computational Framework for Petascale/Exascale Hybrid Computer Systems arXiv:1201.2118v1  [cs.DC]  10 Jan 2012

text:
This approach
emphasizes code re-usability, and greatly simpliﬁes constructing sound interfaces and

title: A Massive Data Parallel Computational Framework for Petascale/Exascale Hybrid Computer Systems arXiv:1201.2118v1  [cs.DC]  10 Jan 2012

title: A Massive Data Parallel Computational Framework for Petascale/Exascale Hybrid Computer Systems arXiv:1201.2118v1  [cs.DC]  10 Jan 2012

MPI-Based Data Parallelism in Cactus
The Cactus framework adopts the idea of data parallelism in its design and implemen-
tation.
title: A Massive Data Parallel Computational Framework for Petascale/Exascale Hybrid Computer Systems arXiv:1201.2118v1  [cs.DC]  10 Jan 2012

title: A Massive Data Parallel Computational Framework for Petascale/Exascale Hybrid Computer Systems arXiv:1201.2118v1  [cs.DC]  10 Jan 2012

title: A Massive Data Parallel Computational Framework for Petascale/Exascale Hybrid Computer Systems arXiv:1201.2118v1  [cs.DC]  10 Jan 2012

Abstract—Cloud computing systems promise to offer

title: untitled

text:
With the increased demand

need to offer differentiated services to users and meet their 
quality expectations.
title: untitled

text:
Existing resource management 
systems in data centers are yet to support Service Level 
Agreement (SLA)-oriented resource allocation, and thus 
need to be enhanced to realize cloud computing and utility 
computing.
title: untitled

In addition, no work has been done to 
collectively 
incorporate 
customer-driven 
service 
management, 
computational 
risk 
management, 
and 
autonomic resource management into a market-based 
resource management system to target the rapidly 
changing enterprise requirements of Cloud computing.
title: untitled

text:
This paper presents vision, challenges, and architectural 
elements of SLA-oriented resource management.
title: untitled

text:
The 
proposed architecture supports integration of market-
based provisioning policies and virtualisation technologies 
for flexible allocation of resources to applications.
title: untitled

text:
The 
performance results obtained from our working prototype 
system shows the feasibility and effectiveness of SLA-based 
resource provisioning in Clouds.

Keywords: Cloud Computing, Data Centers, Service Level

title: untitled

text:
INTRODUCTION  
“The data center is the computer,” wrote Professor David 
Patterson of the University of California, Berkeley in an 
issue of the Communications of the ACM [1].
title: untitled

text:
He noted 
that “There are dramatic differences between developing 
software for millions to use as a service versus distributing 
software for millions to run their PCs.” 
The above quote illustrates the challenges faced by 
software developers today because of recent advances in 
Information and Communications Technology (ICT), such 
as the emergence of multi-core processors and distribution 
of 
networked 
computing 
environments.
title: untitled

text:
These 
technological advances have led to the adoption of new 
computing paradigms which include Cloud computing, 
Grid computing [2], and P2P computing [3].
title: untitled

text:
The next computing paradigm is envisioned to be 
utility computing [4] – the offering of computing services 
whenever users need them, thus transforming computing 
services to more commoditized utilities, similar to other 
utilities such as water, electricity, gas, and telephony.
title: untitled

text:
With 
this new outsourcing service model, users no longer have to 
invest heavily on or maintain their own computing 
infrastructure, and are not constrained to specific 
computing service providers.
title: untitled

text:
Instead, they just have to pay 
for what they use whenever they want by outsourcing jobs 
to dedicated computing service providers.
title: untitled

text:

text:
Since users pay for using services, they want to define 
and expect their service needs to be delivered by computing 
service providers.
title: untitled

text:
Recently, yet another new computing 
paradigm called Cloud computing has emerged [35].
title: untitled

text:
In 
Cloud computing, computing infrastructure and services 
should always be available on computing servers (which 
are distributed among all continents) such that companies 
are able to access their business services and applications 
anywhere in the world whenever they need to (Figure 1).
title: untitled

text:
Hence, Cloud computing can be classified as a new 
paradigm for dynamic creation of the next-generation data

centers by assembling services of networked virtual 
machines.
title: untitled

text:
To realize Cloud computing, service providers such as 
Amazon [5], are deploying data centers distributed in 
various locations worldwide to provide backup and ensure 
reliability in case of a single site failure because data 
centers are crucial to sustain the core business operations of 
companies.
title: untitled

text:
In addition, companies with global operations 
require faster response time and thus save time by 
distributing workload requests to multiple data centers in 
various locations at one time.
title: untitled

text:
Currently, most computing 
servers in data centers comprise clusters of computers as 
they offer high-performance, high-availability, and high-
throughput processing at a lower cost compared to 
traditional High Performance Computing (HPC) systems.
title: untitled

text:
A 
well-known example of a company using clusters in 
distributed data centers is Google [6].
title: untitled

text:
Google use clusters 
to provide replicated storage and backup servers for 
satisfying huge quantity of web and database requests 
originating from anywhere in the world.
title: untitled

text:
CHALLENGES AND REQUIREMENTS  
Resource management issues such as SLAs (Service Level 
Agreements) involved in delivering software for a million 
users to use as a service via a data center is a lot more 
complex as compared to distributing software for a million 
users to run on their individual personal computers.
title: untitled

text:
There 
are several challenges involving SLA-oriented resource 
allocation – to differentiate and satisfy service requests 
based on the desired utility of users.
title: untitled

text:
A classification of 
these challenges is shown in Figure 2.
title: untitled

text:
By using SLAs to 
define service quality parameters that are required by the 
users from the provider, the Cloud providers know how 
users value their service requests and hence can provide 
feedback mechanisms to encourage and discourage service 
request submissions.
title: untitled

text:
In particular, finding efficient 
solutions for the following challenges is critical to design a 
fully service-oriented resource management for Cloud 
computing environments.
title: untitled

text:
Customer-driven Service Management 
Yeo et al.
title: untitled

text:
[7] have highlighted customer satisfaction as a 
crucial success factor to excel in the service industry and 
thus proposed three user-centric objectives in the context of 
a computing service provider that can lead to customer 
satisfaction.
title: untitled

text:
However, there are many service quality 
factors that can influence customer satisfaction [20][21].
title: untitled

text:
Factors that provide personalized attention to customers 
include enabling communication to keep customers 
informed and obtain feedback from them, increasing access 
and approachability to customers, and understanding 
specific needs of customers.
title: untitled

text:
Other factors that encourage 
trust and confidence in customers are security measures 
undertaken against risks and doubts, credibility of provider, 
and courtesy towards customers.
title: untitled

text:
Therefore, a detailed 
study of all possible customer characteristics needs to be 
done to determine if a data center needs to consider more 
relevant characteristics to better support SLA-oriented 
resource allocation.
title: untitled

text:
Computational Risk Management 
Cloud computing is considered as the first fully accepted 
and implemented solution for providing computing as a 
utility.
title: untitled

text:
Having a commercial focused in offering computing 
services, there are several examples of elements in their 
resource management [7] that can be perceived as risks.
title: untitled

text:
For 
example, if SLA with a customer is violated to fulfill 
Quality of a request of another customer, there is a risk of 
penalty and customer dissatisfaction.
title: untitled

text:
Hence, risk analysis 
from the field of economics can be identified as a probable 
solution to evaluate these risks.
title: untitled

text:
However, the entire risk 
management process [22][23] comprises many steps and 
thus need to be studied thoroughly so as to fully apply its 
effectiveness in managing risks.
title: untitled

text:
The risk management 
process comprises the following steps: establish the 
context, identify the risks involved, assess each of the 
identified risks, identify techniques to manage each risk, 
and finally create, implement, and review the risk 
management plan.
title: untitled

text:
Autonomic Resource Management 
Service requirements of users can change over time and 
thus may require amendments of original service requests.
title: untitled

text:
As such, a data center must be able to self-manage the 
reservation process continuously by monitoring current 
service requests, amending future service requests, and 
adjusting schedules and prices for new and amended 
service requests accordingly.
title: untitled

text:
There are also other aspects 
of autonomy, such as self-configuring components to 
satisfy new service requirements.
title: untitled

text:
Hence, more autonomic 
and intelligent data centers are essential to effectively 
manage the limited supply of resources with dynamically 
changing service demand.
title: untitled

text:
For users, there can be brokering 
systems acting on their behalf to select the most suitable 
providers and negotiate with them to achieve the best 
service contracts.
title: untitled

text:
Thus, providers also require autonomic 
resource management to selectively choose the appropriate 
requests to accept and execute depending on a number of 
operating factors, such as the expected availability and 
2


demand of services (both current and future), and existing 
service obligations.
title: untitled

text:
SLA-oriented Resource Allocation Through Virtualization 
Recently, 
virtualization 
[24][25] 
has 
enabled 
the 
abstraction of computing resources such that a single 
physical machine is able to function as multiple logical 
VMs (Virtual Machines).
title: untitled

text:
A key benefit of VMs is the 
ability to host multiple operating system environments 
which are completely isolated from one another on the 
same physical machine.
title: untitled

text:
Another benefit is the capability to 
configure VMs to utilize different partitions of resources on 
the same physical machine.
title: untitled

text:
For example, on a physical 
machine, one VM can be allocated 10% of the processing 
power, while another VM can be allocated 20% of the 
processing power.
title: untitled

text:
Hence, VMs can be started and stopped 
dynamically to meet the changing demand of resources by 
users as opposed to limited resources on a physical 
machine.
title: untitled

text:
In particular, VMs may be assigned various 
resource management policies catering to different user 
needs and demands to better support the implementation of 
SLA-oriented resource allocation.
title: untitled

text:
Service Benchmarking and Measurement 
Recently several Cloud providers have started offering 
different type of computing services.
title: untitled

text:
Therefore competition 
in the IT industry is increasing to maximize their market 
share.
title: untitled

text:
From the customer perspective, it is essential to have 
a service measurement standard to find out most suitable 
services which satisfy their needs.
title: untitled

text:
In this context recently, 
Cloud Service Measurement Index Consortium (CSMIC) 
has identified measurement indexes (Service Measurement 
Index - SMI) that are important for evaluation of a Cloud 
service [36].
title: untitled

text:
For the performance evaluation of these 
services, there is essential requirement of real Cloud traces 
from various public archives such as PlanetLab and 
probability distributions to model application and service 
requirements respectively.
title: untitled

text:
This is because there are 
currently no service benchmarks available to evaluate 
utility-based resource management for Cloud computing in 
a standard manner.
title: untitled

text:
Moreover, there can be different 
emphasis of application requirements such as data-intensive 
and workflow applications, and service requirements such 
as reliability and trust/security.
title: untitled

text:
Therefore, it is necessary to derive a standard set of 
service benchmarks for the accurate evaluation of resource 
management policies.
title: untitled

text:
The benchmarks should be able to 
reflect realistic application and service requirements of 
users that can in turn facilitates the forecasting and 
prediction of future users’ needs.
title: untitled

text:
System Modeling and Repeatable Evaluation 
The proposed resource management strategies need to be 
thoroughly evaluated under various operating scenarios, 
such as various types of resources and customers with 
different service requirements in order to demonstrate their 
effectiveness.
title: untitled

text:
However, it is hard and almost impossible to 
perform performance evaluation of resource management 
strategies in a repeatable and controllable manner since 
resources are distributed and service requests originate 
from different customers at any time.
title: untitled

text:
Hence, we will use 
discrete-event simulation to evaluate the performance of 
resource management strategies.
title: untitled

text:
For our initial work [25], we have successfully used 
CloudSim [26] to evaluate the performance of resource 
management policies.
title: untitled

text:
CloudSim is a toolkit for modeling 
and simulation of Cloud resources and application 
scheduling.
title: untitled

text:
It allows easy modeling and simulation of 
virtual resources and network connectivity with different 
capabilities, configurations, and domains.
title: untitled

text:
It also supports 
primitives 
for 
application 
composition, 
information 
services for resource discovery, and interfaces for assigning 
application tasks to resources and managing their 
execution.
title: untitled

text:
Hence, these collective features in simulation 
toolkits such as CloudSim can be leveraged to easily 
construct simulation models to evaluate the performance of 
resource management strategies.
title: untitled

text:
SLA-ORIENTED CLOUD COMPUTING VISION 
To meet aforementioned requirements of SLA-based 
resource allocation of Cloud applications, future efforts 
should focus on design, development, and implementation 
of software systems and policies based on novel SLA-
oriented resource allocation models exclusively designed 
for data centers.
title: untitled

text:
The resource provisioning within these Cloud data 
centers will be driven by market-oriented principles for 
efficient resource allocation depending on user QoS 
(Quality of Service) targets and workload demand patterns.
title: untitled

text:
In the case of a Cloud data center as a commercial offering 
to enable crucial business operations of companies, there 
are many critical QoS parameters to consider in a service 
request, such as reliability and trust/security.
title: untitled

text:
In particular, 
QoS requirements cannot be static and need to be 
dynamically updated over time due to continuing changes 
in business operations and operational environments.
title: untitled

text:
In 
short, there should be greater importance on customers 
since they pay for accessing services in data centers.
title: untitled

text:
The 
approach for realization of this research vision consists of 
the following: 
• 
support for customer-driven service management 
based on customer profiles and QoS requirements; 
• 
definition of computational risk management 
tactics to identify, assess, and manage risks 
involved in the execution of applications with 
regards to service requirements and customer 
needs; 
• 
derivation of appropriate market-based resource 
management strategies that encompass both 
3


customer-driven 
service 
management 
and 
computational risk management to sustain SLA-
oriented resource allocation; 
• 
incorporation of autonomic resource management 
models that effectively self-manage changes in 
service requirements to satisfy both new service 
demands and existing service obligations; 
• 
leverage of Virtual Machine (VM) technology to 
dynamically assign resource shares according to 
service requirements; and  
• 
implementation 
of 
the 
developed 
resource 
management strategies and models into a real 
computing server in an operational data center.
title: untitled

text:
STATE-OF-THE-ART  
Traditional Resource Management Systems (RMSs) such 
as Condor [8], LoadLeveler [8], Load Sharing Facility 
(LSF) [10], and Portable Batch System (PBS) [11], still 
adopt system-centric resource allocation approaches that 
focus on optimizing overall cluster performance.
title: untitled

text:
These 
cluster RMSs currently maximize overall job performance 
and system usage of the cluster.
title: untitled

text:
For example, they aim to 
increase processor throughput and utilization for the 
cluster, and reduce the average waiting time and response 
time for the jobs.
title: untitled

text:
They still assume that all job requests are 
of equal user importance and thus neglect actual levels of 
service required by different users.
title: untitled

text:
Hence, they are not able 
to support Cloud computing and utility computing where 
commercial customers’ service requirements are crucial 
and needs to be fulfilled.
title: untitled

text:
Some of these batch schedulers 
have even extended to enable the deployment of 
applications across Clouds (such as EC2) dynamically.
title: untitled

text:
However, these resource management systems do not 
provide any SLA-based differentiated services to end users.
title: untitled

text:
Recently, the large growth of Cloud computing led to the 
development of several virtual machine management 
platform solutions such as Eucalyptus [30] and OpenStack 
[12].
title: untitled

text:
Apache VCL [27] is one of the first open-source 
systems for dynamic provision and reservation of 
computational resources for diverse applications within a 
data center through a simple web interface.
title: untitled

text:
Citrix 
Essentials [31] is a commercially available solution for 
infrastructure virtualization and management of data center 
that provides an abstraction layer between servers’ 
hardware and the operating system.
title: untitled

text:
The main goal of this 
system is to provide automatic configuration and 
maintenance of data centers.
title: untitled

text:
Enomaly Elastic Computing 
Platform [29] offers a Web-based customer solution that 
allows users to fully control the life cycle of VMs.
title: untitled

text:
The 
Eucalyptus framework [30] is another open-source project 
that focuses on building IaaS clouds.
title: untitled

text:
The Eucalyptus 
provides same external interface as Amazon EC2 API and 
is designed to allow third-party extensions through modular 
software framework.
title: untitled

text:
The Nimbus toolkit [32] is built on 
top of the Globus framework having an EC2-compatible 
front-end API.
title: untitled

text:
OpenNebula [28] is also an open-source 
toolkit used to build private, public and hybrid clouds.
title: untitled

text:
Its 
key feature comes from scheduler module that offers 
dynamic resource allocation features via Haizea lease 
scheduler.
title: untitled

text:
It is possible to integrate different scheduling 
objectives 
and 
provisioned 
resources 
in 
advance.
title: untitled

text:
Manjrasoft Aneka [33] is a platform for building and 
deploying distributed applications on Clouds.
title: untitled

text:
It provides a 
rich set of APIs for transparently exploiting distributed 
resources and expressing the business logic of applications 
by using the preferred programming abstractions.
title: untitled

text:
With advent of market-based resource management, 
many computational economy based systems [4][13] have 
been proposed by researchers to manage allocations of 
computing resources since it has been successfully adopted 
in the field of economics to control the supply and demand 
of goods.
title: untitled

text:
Market-based resource management is expected 
to regulate supply and demand of limited computing 
resources at market equilibrium, provide feedback in terms 
of economic incentives for both users and providers, and 
promote 
SLA-oriented 
resource 
allocation 
that 
differentiates service requests based on their utility and thus 
caters to users’ needs.
title: untitled

text:
Therefore, market-based resource 
management 
has 
been 
proposed 
across 
numerous 
computing platforms  that include clusters [14], distributed 
databases [15], Grids [16], parallel and distributed systems 
[17], peer-to-peer [18], and World Wide Web [19].
title: untitled

text:
However, none of these market-based systems have yet 
considered and incorporated customer-driven service 
management, 
computational 
risk 
management, 
and 
autonomic 
resource 
management 
into 
market-based 
resource management, which is critical to sustain enterprise 
service demand in Cloud and utility computing.
title: untitled

text:
In this paper, we propose a SLA-oriented resource 
management system built using Aneka [33] for Cloud 
computing.
title: untitled

text:
Aneka act as a market-oriented Cloud platform 
and allows building and scheduling of applications, 
provisioning and monitoring of resources with facilities 
such as pricing, accounting, and QoS/SLA services in 
private and/or public (leased) Cloud environments.
title: untitled

text:
SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE 
Figure 3 shows the high-level architecture for supporting 
SLA oriented resource allocation in Cloud computing [37].
title: untitled

text:
There are basically four main entities involved:  
• 
Users/Brokers: In general, the user interact with the 
Cloud management systems through an automatic 
systems such as brokers or schedulers who act on users 
behalf to submit service requests from anywhere in the 
world to the Clouds to be processed.
title: untitled

text:
4


• 
SLA Resource Allocator: The SLA Resource 
Allocator acts as the interface between the Cloud 
computing infrastructure and external users/brokers.
title: untitled

text:
It 
requires the interaction of the following mechanisms to 
support SLA-oriented resource management:  
 
Figure 3.
title: untitled

text: High-level system architectural framework.
title: untitled

text:
o 
Service Request Examiner and Admission Control: 
The user service request is first interpreted by the 
Service Request Examiner and Admission Control 
mechanism that understands the QoS requirements 
before determining whether to accept or reject the 
request.
title: untitled

text:
It ensures no SLA violation by reducing 
the chances of resource overloading whereby many 
service requests cannot be fulfilled successfully 
due to limited resources available.
title: untitled

text:
Therefore, it 
also needs the latest status information regarding 
resource 
availability 
(from 
VM 
Monitor 
mechanism) and workload processing (from 
Service Request Monitor mechanism) in order to 
make resource allocation decisions effectively.
title: untitled

text:
Then, it assigns requests to VMs and determines 
resource entitlements for allocated VMs.
title: untitled

text:
 Autonomic Resource Management: This is 
the key mechanism that ensures that Cloud 
providers can serve large amount of requests 
without violating SLA terms.
title: untitled

text:
It dynamically 
manages the resources by using VM migration 
and consolidation.
title: untitled

text:
For instance, when an 
application requires low amount of resources, 
its VM is migrated to a host with lower 
capability, so that new requests can be served.
title: untitled

text:
o Pricing: The Pricing mechanism is a way to 
manage the service demand on the Cloud resources 
and maximize the profit of the Cloud provider.
title: untitled

text:
There are several ways in which service requests 
can be charged.
title: untitled

text:
For instance, requests can be 
charged based on submission time (peak/off-peak), 
pricing rates (fixed/changing) or availability of 
resources (supply/demand).
title: untitled

text:
Pricing also serves as a 
basis for managing computing resources within the 
data center and facilitates in prioritizing resource 
allocations effectively.
title: untitled

text:
Therefore, Cloud providers 
offer sometimes same/similar services at different 
pricing models and QoS levels.
title: untitled

text:
The two of the 
most prominent ones which are practically 
employed by Cloud providers: posted pricing and 
spot market.
title: untitled

text:
o 
Accounting 
and 
SLA 
Management: 
SLA 
Management is the component that keeps track of 
SLAs of customers with Cloud providers and their 
fulfillment history.
title: untitled

text:
Based on SLA terms, the 
Accounting mechanism maintains the actual usage 
of resources by requests so that the final cost can 
be computed and charged from the users.
title: untitled

text:
In 
addition, 
the 
maintained 
historical 
usage 
information can be utilized by the Service Request 
Examiner and Admission Control mechanism to 
improve resource allocation decisions.
title: untitled

text:
o 
VM and Application Monitor: Depending on the 
services provided, the resource management 
system has to keep the track of performance and 
status of resources at different levels.
title: untitled

text:
If service 
provided is compute resources, the VM Monitor 
mechanism keeps track of the availability of VMs 
and their resource entitlements.
title: untitled

text:
While in the case 
of application software services, the performance 
is continuously monitored to identify any breach in 
SLA and send a notification trigger to SLA 
Resource Allocator for taking appropriate action.
title: untitled

text:
o 
Dispatcher: 
The 
Dispatcher 
deploys 
the 
application on appropriate virtual resource.
title: untitled

text:
It also 
takes the responsibility of creating Virtual machine 
image and their initiation on selected physical 
hosts.
title: untitled

text:
o 
Service Request Monitor: The Service Request 
Monitor mechanism keeps track of the execution 
progress of service requests.
title: untitled

text:
• 
Virtual Machines (VMs): Multiple VMs can be 
started and stopped dynamically to meet accepted 
service requests, hence providing maximum flexibility 
to configure various partitions of resources on the same 
physical machine to different specific requirements of 
service requests.
title: untitled

text:
In addition, multiple VMs can 
concurrently run applications based on different 
operating system environments on a single physical 
machine since every VM is completely isolated from 
one another on the same physical machine.
title: untitled

text:
• 
Physical Machines: The data center comprises 
multiple computing servers that provide resources to 
meet service demands.
title: untitled

text:
SLA PROVISIONING IN ANEKA 
To illustrate how the aforementioned architecture can be 
delivered in practice, we describe in this section how SLA 
provisioning is implemented in Aneka [33].
title: untitled

text:
Figure 4 
depicts the general Aneka architecture.
title: untitled

text:
Aneka is a Platform 
as a Service framework that is composed of an API for 
development of elastic applications supporting many 
programming models (Task, Thread, MapReduce), and 
management layer for private Clouds.
title: untitled

text:
The core unity of 
Aneka is the Container, which hosts one or more services 
such as security, scheduling, programming models, 
accounting, provisioning, etc.
title: untitled

text:
The management layer is 
able to handle a myriad of resources, including clusters, 
publics and private Clouds, and Desktop Grids.
title: untitled

text:
Services in Aneka are completely decoupled from each 
other, and services communicate via messages sent 
between services.
title: untitled

text:
Services are designed in such a way that 
they are resilient to lack of reply from other services; This 
way, if for some reason a service is not enabled in an 
Aneka installation, other services keep their regular 
operations that are independent from the disabled services.
title: untitled

text:
Figure 5 presents the Class diagram for services 
implementation.
title: untitled

text:
The interface IService defines all methods 
that an Aneka service has to implement.
title: untitled

text:
This interface is 
implemented by the abstract class ServiceBase, which 
implements methods that are common to all services, 
namely activation, deactivation, pausing/unpausing, and 
logging.
title: untitled

text:
ServiceBase also defines abstract methods that 
Aneka services extending ServiceBase have to implement.
title: untitled

text: Basically, these methods are handlers for events.
title: untitled

text:
Moreover, 
different messages can also have different types of 
payloads, which are known to other services.
title: untitled

text:
The two most important services for realization of SLA 
oriented framework are the Scheduler service and the 
Provisioning service.
title: untitled

text:
They both extend ServiceBase and 
define messages that are used for enabling SLA-driven 
execution of applications and provisioning of resources.
title: untitled

text:
SLAs are defined in terms of deadline for execution of 
applications.
title: untitled

text:
The deadline, along with an estimation of 
execution time of each task of the application is supplied by 
the user during a job submission.
title: untitled

text:
This process is briefly 
described in Algorithm 1.
title: untitled

Aneka handles the process of dynamic provisioning to 
meet user SLAs in autonomic manner.

Additional resources 
are provisioned for applications when required and are 
removed when they are not necessary.

When the Scheduler 
service receives a completed task or a new job, it estimates 
if the deadline can be achieved with the current number of 
6

Moreover, because the initial 
estimation given by the user about execution time of tasks 
may be inaccurate, estimation is updated with data obtained 
from the actual execution of tasks.

If the Scheduler decides whether the

as

A 
detailed 
description of the Resource provisioning process in Steps
