text:
Grid System 
1) Grid Middleware 
Grid middleware is a software that glues diverse 
local resources of various organizations to form a 
higher-level, bigger, global resource.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Grid middleware 
offers following services: (1) remote process/job 
management to submit and to monitor, (2) allocation 
and co-allocation of resources, (3) access to storage 
devices and data management, (4) information service 
(kind of yellow page service) including resource 
discovery, 
resource 
registration, 
and 
resource 
information update, and (5) security service including 
authentication, authorization, delegation, and single-
sign on.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Example of Grid middleware are as follows: 
Globus [8], Legion [9], and Unicore [7].
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Globus is a de 
facto standard software for building Grid computing 
and it has been widely used in many Grid 
deployments.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
2) Batch Queue Controlled Resources 
In most Grid deployments, individual resources of 
a single organization are centrally managed using 
batch queue oriented local resource management 
system (LRM).
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
In such system, user submitted batch 
jobs are introduced into the queue of LRM, from which 
resource scheduler decides about execution of jobs, see 
Section IV,A.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Examples of such LRMs include PBS [18], 
LSF [19], Condor [20], Sun Grid Engine [21], NQE [22], 
Maui [23] and Load Leveler [24].
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
A resource scheduler 
is also known as low-level scheduler or local scheduler.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
For compute resources, LRM can be configured for (i) 
which user is allowed to run jobs (ii) what policies are 
associated with selection of jobs for running, and (iii) 
what policies are associated with individual machines 
for considering them to be idle.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
A LRM manages two types of jobs: local jobs 
generated inside a resource domain and jobs generated 
by external users, i.e.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
The 
common purpose of any LRM is to manage, control, 
and schedule batch processes on the resources under 
its control.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Since, LRM deals with distributed 
resources, it is also called Distributed Resource 


Manager.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Basic features of any LRM include following: 
(1) scripting language for defining batch job, (2) 
interfaces for submission of batch jobs, (3) interfaces to 
monitor the executions, (4) interfaces to submit input 
and gather output data, (5) mechanism for defining 
priorities for jobs, (6) match-making of jobs with 
resources, and (7) scheduling jobs present in queue(s) 
to determine execution order of jobs based on job-
priority, resource status, and resource allocation 
configuration.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Advance reservation based LRMs are 
also used in Grid.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Examples of such LRMs include 
Platform LSF, PBS Pro/Torque, Maui, and SGE.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
3) Connecting Resources of different organizations into 
a VO 
Grid allows use of heterogeneous LRMs through a 
common interface.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
In Globus based Grid, which is 
widely used, GRAM (Globus Resource Allocation 
Manager) interface is used for job submission on 
heterogeneous LRMs.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
GRAM is a standardized way of 
accessing any LRM, as it is LRM neutral.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
GRAM 
messages remain same irrespective of LRM, whether it 
is PBS, LSF, or Condor.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Each LRM can be connected 
into a Globus based Grid using Globus-LRM adapter.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Clients submit job requests using GRAM protocol and 
GRAM-LRM connector can translate those messages 
into a language understood by a specific LRM.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
For 
example, GRAM5 supports Condor, PBS, and LSF; 
similarly, Unicore supports SGE, LoadLeveler and 
Torque.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Resource Monitoring Infrastructure 
Resource monitoring helps to Grid scheduler in 
taking appropriate decision on available resources.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text: Many resource monitoring frameworks are available.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
We discuss two widely used resource monitoring 
systems: one provides information on individual 
resources and another provides information on 
connection between resources.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Network Weather 
Service (NWS) and Ganglia are most widely used 
network 
performance 
and 
resource 
monitoring 
systems in real Grid or cluster test-beds.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
1) Ganglia 
Ganglia 
monitoring 
system 
[25] 
provides 
information on individual resources of Clusters or 
Grids.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Ganglia exploits scalability, redundancy, and 
decentralization features of distributed computing 
system.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Ganglia system has hierarchical design, which 
is made of gmond and gmetad component sub-systems.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
The gmond (Ganglia monitoring daemon), which runs 
on each node of a cluster, enables monitoring on a 
single cluster through listen/announce protocol.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
A 
collection of hierarchical gmetads federate multiple 
clusters through a tree of TCP connections to prepare 
aggregated view.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Ganglia uses XML to represent 
client's response, XDR for quick data transport and 
efficient storage, and RRDtool for round robin data 
storage and visualization of time series data.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Ganglia 
provides command line access through gmetric 
command and programming access through client side 
library.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
The gmond supports two types of metrics: (1) 28 
to 37 standard/in-built metrics, depending upon 
operating system, and (2) user-defined metrics.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Ganglia 
has been used in clusters, Grids, and Planetary-scale 
systems.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Ganglia also provides PHP based web front-
end, which enables various views of monitoring data 
rendered through RRDtool.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
2) Network Weather Service 
Network Weather Service (NWS) [26] provides 
dynamic characteristics of networked computing 
resources.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Moreover, 
it 
can 
also 
forecast 
[27] 
performance of resources.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Resource monitoring and 
performance prediction provided by NWS is useful to 
higher level services to enable scheduling and QoS 
guarantees in Grid or cluster computing environments.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Its implementation is based on Unix/Linux platform 
using TCP/IP socket based communication among 
distributed processes.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
NWS is made of four component 
systems: (1) Persistent State process, (2) Name Server 
process, (3) Sensor process, and (4) Forecaster process.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
The Persistent State process stores measurements in 
persistent 
storage.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It 
also 
provides 
access 
of 
measurements 
to 
their 
users.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
NWS 
supports 
measurements of following variables: fraction of CPU 
availability time, connection time of TCP socket, end-
to-end network latency of TCP, and end-to-end 
network bandwidth of TCP.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
NWS implements CPU 
availability sensor as passive sensor, which itself does 
not measure any characteristics, rather relies on vmstat 
utility.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
The network sensor is implemented as active 
sensor, 
which 
explicitly 
measures 
network 
performance 
related 
measures 
by 
using 
active 
measurement probes.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Application Scheduling Systems 
We discuss two types of scheduling systems: 
scheduling system for independent tasks applications 
and 
scheduling 
system 
for 
dependent 
tasks 
applications.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
1) Independent Tasks Scheduling Systems 
Scheduling of application, whether independent 
tasks or dependent tasks, in Grid computing involves 
following steps: resource discovery, resource selection, 
schedule generation, and application execution.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
In case 
of dynamic scheduling, the process may involve 
additional step of rescheduling or schedule adaptation.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
General architecture of Grid supporting scheduling of 
application is discussed in Section II,A,2.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Examples of 
systems supporting scheduling of independent tasks 
applications are as follows: Nimrod-g [10], AppLeS 
[28], NetSolve/GridSolve [29] and ICENI [30].
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
2) Dependent Tasks Scheduling System---Workflow 
Management Systems 
A workflow management system (WMS) is used to 
schedule dependent tasks applications.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
A workflow 
contains a sequence of tasks that are to be carried out in 
the defined order in order to generate desired end-
result.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
There are two common types of workflows: 
Business Workflow and Scientific Workflow.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
The 
business workflow is related to business application.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It 
automates a business process fully or partially.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Some 
business workflow may include human decision to 
make further processing steps of the workflow.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
In 
Business workflow, documents, information, and 
business decision are passed from one participant to 
another.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Scientific workflow automates executing 
computation tasks of scientific application.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
The analytical steps may involve one 
or more of following: database access and querying 
steps, mathematical processing steps, data analysis and 
mining steps, and many other steps that involve any 
computationally intensive activities.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Workflow model 
is graphical representation of the workflow steps.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Two 
types of workflow are mainly used: Data flow (DAG 
based) and Control flow (Petri-net) based.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
DAG based 
is mainly used in current Scientific Workflow in which 
loops and control structures by definition are not 
available.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Control flow (Petri-net based) is mainly used 
in business workflows.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Workflow language bridges the 
gap between graphical workflow model and the 
workflow engine, which executes the workflow.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text: Workflow engine understands workflow language.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
A 
workflow can be written directly in the workflow 
language without preparing workflow model by GUI.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Most workflow languages are XML based for both 
scientific and business workflows.For representation of 
workflow.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Various Workflow Management Systems (WMSs) 
support either Directed Acyclic Graph based workflow 
or Control Flow Graph based workflow or both.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Triana 
[31], GridAnt [32] or Karajan [33], UNICORE [7], 
Askalon [34], and ICENI [35] are Control Flow Graph 
based WMSs and DAGMan [36], Taverna [37] , GrADS 
[38] GridFlow [39], Gridbus [40] , and Pegasus WMS 
[41] are DAG based WMSs.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Most of the mentioned 
systems are Globus based except Taverna, GridFlow, 
and UNICORE.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Furthermore, a few systems also 
support web-services.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Only a few systems are active in 
further development of WMSs and providing help or 
support to their users.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
We redirect readers elsewhere, 
for example, to [3], for understanding of various 
WMSs.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Grid Simulation Tools 
Scheduling algorithms in Grid can be evaluated 
using Grid simulation tools also.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
However, accuracy of 
simulation 
results 
depends 
on 
how 
accurately 
simulator mimics real system entities in simulation.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
There is another approach of performance evaluation 
called mathematical analysis; however, for beginners it 
is not advisable unless they have sound understanding 
of mathematical representation and queuing based 
mathematical analysis [42].
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
There exists many simulation tools or simulation 
frameworks that support simulation based study in 
Grid environment.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
However, they differ based on kind 
of studies supported by them.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
We briefly mention each 
Grid simulation tool with supported study details.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text: Following are various open source simulation tools.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
SimGrid [43] is a C language based generalized toolkit 
supporting DAG applications and MPI applications.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
GridSim [44] is a Java language based generalized 
framework 
supporting various entities 
of 
Grid 
computing.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
OptorSim [45] is Java language based 
simulator and it can simulate compute Grid and data 
Grid [46].
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It focuses on data replication strategies and 
replica optimization.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Alea [47] is Java language based 
simulator.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It supports study of various resource (Local) 
scheduling algorithms.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
GSSIM [48] is Java language 
based  framework.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It can support concept of 
scheduling at local/resource level and Grid level.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Moreover, GSSIM can understand existing workloads 
generated using real Grid environment.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It also 
supports generating synthetic workload.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
MaGate [49] 
is a Java language based simulator that supports peer-
to-peer (P2P) Grid.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Study using MaGate includes 
resource discovery algorithms in P2P Grid and bio-
inspired community scheduling algorithms.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
CLASSIFICATION OF THE SCHEDULING USED IN 
GRID ENVIRONMENT 
Two main types of scheduling are involved in Grid, 
one at local resource level and another at application 
level.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
We concisely explore them in following 
discussion.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Resource Scheduling 
Two types of scheduling: time sharing and space 
sharing are involved at local resource level.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Time 
sharing 
scheduling 
is 
used 
by 
each 
machine 
(computer) of the cluster, for example, CPU scheduler 
of the Operating System on each machine that is part of 
batch system, whereas space sharing scheduling is 
used  by Local Resource Manager to schedule the job 
present in batch queue on idle machine of the cluster.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Resource scheduling is used to increase utilization of 
resources or balance load on the resources.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Generally a 
Grid site contains a batch queue controlled cluster, see 
Figure 1.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Resource scheduling is not complicated as it 


considers each submitted task an independent unit and 
therefore the scheduler can mix in with or order with 
tasks of other applications, either submitted from the 
same Grid site or from other Grid sites.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
The resource scheduling involves taking two 
decisions: job selection from a queue/bag of jobs and 
node selection for selected job from available nodes.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Figure 2 provides classification of algorithms under the 
two main decision operations, which execute as part of 
resource scheduling.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text: Classification of Resource Scheduling in Grid Computing.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Job Selection Algorithms: 
Job selection algorithm selects a job from a queue of 
jobs.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
The simplest type of job selection algorithms are 
Dispatching Rules based.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
FCFS [51] schedules jobs as per 
submission order (time).
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Shortest Processing Time First 
or Short-Job-First (SJF) assigns highest priority to the 
job that has shortest processing time.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Longest Processing 
Time First or Largest-Size-First (LSF) assigns highest 
priority to the job that has longest processing time.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Earliest Deadline First (EDF) assigns highest priority to 
the process that has expected execution time in the 
most near future or the specified deadline is in the 
most near future.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
In dynamic dispatching rules based 
scheduling, decision changes depending upon passage 
of time.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Minimum slack based algorithm is of type 
dynamic dispatching rules based scheduling.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
In this 
algorithms, jobs are ordered according to their 
remaining slack, which is defined as  slack = max(dj - pj - 
t, 0), where dj is deadline, pj is processing time, and t is 
the current time.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Backfilling is an optimization of FCFS 
algorithm.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
If the oldest job in the queue cannot be 
executed due to non-availability of enough/required 
resources, the older jobs are started without delaying 
the oldest queued job though the older job arrived 
latter than oldest job.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Condor [52], LSF [19], and PBS 
[18] supports backfilling based resource scheduling 
algorithm.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
In Advance Reservation based Algorithm 
[51], user of resource sends reservation-request for 
using resource in future time.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
This advance reservation 
based algorithm can guarantee that required resource 
will be available to user for use; moreover, jobs do not 
need to wait in queue.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Examples of systems supporting 
advance reservation based algorithms are as follows: 
Platform LSF, PBS Pro/Torque, Maui, and SGE.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Preemption based resource scheduling algorithm can 
stop execution of low priority job when high priority 
job arrives.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Node Allocation Algorithms: 
Best Fit selects the node that has the fewest available 
resources and still can finish the job.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
First Fit schedules 
the job on the first suitable resource in the list of 
available resources.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Fastest Resource First selects fastest 
available resource in the list of available resources.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Min 
Loaded First selects the resource having maximum 
unused CPU power or CPU utilization.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Application Scheduling 
Grid scheduler, to which users submit their 
applications, performs application scheduling, in 
which the scheduler takes scheduling decision about 
tasks of whole application.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Various terms are used for 
the term Grid scheduler.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
These terms include super-
scheduler, 
meta-scheduler, 
global 
scheduler, 
application 
broker, 
and 
application 
scheduler.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Important difference between resource scheduling and 
application scheduling is that application level 
scheduler assigns a Grid site to a job whereas resource 
scheduler allocates a machine of a cluster to a job.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Figure 3 provides broad classification of application 
scheduling algorithms based on various criteria.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Classification of Application Scheduling in Grid 
Computing.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Based on time at which scheduling decision is 
taken, scheduling can be categorized into two: Static 
scheduling and Dynamic scheduling.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Static scheduling: It determines schedule of all the 
tasks of application before application starts to run.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Static scheduling is applicable to both independent 
tasks and dependent tasks applications.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It is applicable 
when the environment is assumed to be static or non-
changing and when it is possible to estimate the 
execution times of tasks (jobs).
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Dynamic scheduling [53]: It determines schedule of 
a task of an application only when the task becomes 


ready for execution.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
For scheduling of independent 
tasks application, all tasks can be scheduled at the 
same time and in any order; however, for scheduling of 
dependent tasks application, a task becomes ready 
only when all its predecessor tasks have completed 
their execution.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Dynamic scheduling is used when the 
environment is dynamic/changing.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It is used when it is 
impossible to determine the execution time or when 
tasks (jobs) are coming online (real-time).
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Exact algorithm always produces an optimal 
solution if exists.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Heuristic produces a feasible and 
nearly optimal, but not necessarily optimal solution.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
The important difference between heuristic and meta-
heuristic is mentioned below.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Heuristics: This approach develops a scheduling 
algorithm that fits a particular kind of problem.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Examples of heuristics include following: Myopic, 
Batch 
scheduling, 
List 
scheduling, 
Clustering/grouping 
based 
scheduling, 
and 
Duplication based scheduling [54].
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Meta-heuristics: This approach develops a general 
approach of developing a specific heuristic to fit a 
particular kind of problem, for example, Genetic 
Algorithm, Simulated Annealing, Tabu Search, and 
Particle Swarm Optimization [54].
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Based on characteristics of application, scheduling 
can be categorized into independent tasks scheduling 
and dependent tasks/workflow scheduling.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Independent tasks scheduling: In independent 
tasks application, all tasks of applications are 
independent 
of 
each 
other 
in 
terms 
of 
any 
dependencies.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Therefore they can be scheduled in any 
order by scheduler.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Examples of independent tasks 
scheduling algorithms [55] include MET (Minimum 
Execution Time), MCT (Minimum Completion Time), 
Min-min, Max-min, and Suffrage [56].
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Dependent tasks scheduling: In dependent tasks 
application, there exists dependencies among tasks of 
applications.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Therefore the application scheduler has to 
respect 
these 
dependencies 
among 
tasks while 
scheduling them on resources.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
There are three types of 
heuristics [55]: list-scheduling, clustering/grouping 
based, and duplication based for scheduling of 
dependent tasks scheduling [55].
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Whether resource has associated cost of usage or 
not, scheduling can be divided into following two 
categories.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Cooperative/volunteer access based scheduling: 
Scheduler tries to minimize the execution time 
ignoring other factors.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
This approach is currently used 
by most Grid projects present in the world.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
In this type 
of scheduling, the resource consumers can use 
resources freely.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
QoS and SLA based scheduling: In this type of 
scheduling, which is also called utility based Grid 
computing [57],  resource consumers need to pay to 
resource providers for usage of resources.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Thus, 
monetary cost is also involved as decision factor for 
taking scheduling decision [58].
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Based on how many objectives are involved in 
scheduling decision, scheduling can be divided into 
following two broad categories.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Single objective scheduling: In this scheduling, the 
scheduler has to focus on only one objective while 
taking scheduling decision.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Example of scheduling 
objectives 
are 
time 
minimization 
and 
cost 
minimization.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Multiple objective scheduling: In this scheduling, 
the scheduler has to focus on multiple objective at the 
same time while taking scheduling decision.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Example 
of multiple objective scheduling is cost and time 
minimization scheduling.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Based on characteristic of objective function, 
scheduling can be divided into following two broad 
categories.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Minimization 
based 
scheduling: 
In 
this 
scheduling, the scheduler tries to minimize objective.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Objective could be minimization of make-span or 
minimization of cost.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Constrained based scheduling: In this scheduling, 
the scheduler is given information about upper-bound 
on the value of the objective and the scheduler has to 
generate schedule that satisfies objective value within 
the specified upper-bound.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
METHODOLOGY TO EVALUATE PERFORMANCE OF 
SCHEDULING ALGORITHMS 
A proposed scheduling algorithm can be evaluated 
by one of two approaches: implement the proposed 
algorithm in a real scheduling system and evaluate for 
performance or implement the proposed algorithm in a 
simulator and evaluate for performance.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Depending 
upon type of scheduling: resource or application, 
appropriate simulation tool or real system should be 
chosen.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
When a real system is to be built for evaluation 
of the proposed scheduling algorithms, it is very 
important to decide about what combination of 
available 
Grid 
middleware 
software 
and 
Grid 
application scheduler system can address the proposed 
algorithms.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
There are many options such as Globus, 
Condor-G, LSF, GridbusBroker, Pegasus, Kepler, 
Taverna, Triana, Grid(Lab) Resource Management, 
Nimrod-G,  Sun Grid Engine, etc., see Section III.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
This 
section addresses methodology of carrying out 
evaluation of scheduling algorithms with focus on 
generalized 
steps, 
various 
types 
of 
test 
data, 


configuration of test environment, and performance 
evaluation metrics.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Generalized steps of evaluation of scheduling 
algorithms 
Configuration of simulator is generally found to be 
easy; however, the exact way of configuration of a real 
system depends on selection of application scheduling 
software and grid middleware software.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
In following, 
we try to point out general steps of experimentation.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Step 1: Choose Grid system/WMS/simulation tool 
for carrying out scheduling.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Step 2: Choose test applications or batch-jobs or 
workflows or task-graphs.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Step 3: Choose scenarios for evaluation of 
algorithms.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Step 
4: 
Choose 
performance 
metrics 
for 
comparison.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Step 5: (If needed,) Instrument system or tool for 
gathering data of interest for chosen metrics.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Step 
6: 
Perform 
different 
experiments 
with 
manipulating independent variables.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Include best, 
known 
(benchmark) 
scheduling 
algorithm 
for 
comparison with.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Step 7: Gather and analyze data or result through 
instrumented code or log records or trace records.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Test data/input for evaluation of scheduling algorithms 
We focus on only testing of workflow applications.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Following are two main ways of generating test 
input data: 
Use well-known DAGs: A few examples of well-
known DAGs/workflows include EMAN (Electron 
Micrograph Analysis) BLAST (Basic Local Alignment 
Search Tool), Gaussian Elimination (Provides solution 
of a system of linear equations), Fast Fourier 
Transform, Montage, LIGO, and Galactic Plane.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Prepare input data using DAG generator: Use 
DAG generator to prepare random task graphs by 
varying following parameters: the total number of 
tasks, 
amount 
of 
communication, 
amount 
of 
computation, the number of parallel tasks, and degree 
of parallelism.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
We need to configure resources/system to enable 
different test scenarios.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It should be noted that in real 
system, it won't be possible to configure resources to 
achieve certain behavior.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
However, in simulation, we 
can vary the number of resources and characteristics of 
resources.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
In characteristics of resources, we can vary 
computation speed of resource, network bandwidth of 
resource, resource availability, and resource failure.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
For exhaustive evaluation, different task graphs 
with known and unknown characteristics can be 
prepared and can be used in experimentation.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
A 
research paper on Benchmarking the Task Graph 
Scheduling Algorithms by Yu-Kwong Kwok and Ishfaq 
Ahmad in [59] provides details of benchmark task 
graphs.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
We concisely present them below, which 
researchers 
can 
choose 
from 
depending 
upon 
availability of task-graphs with them and feasibility of 
getting required ones with extra efforts.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Peer set graph: Use example task graphs used by 
various researchers and those are documented in 
publications.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Random Graphs with optimal schedules: Use task-
graphs for which we have obtained optimal solutions 
using a branch-and-bound algorithm.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Random Graphs with Pre-Determined Optimal 
Schedules: This method generates graphs with known 
optimal schedules.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Random Graphs without Optimal Schedules: Use 
random graphs having large number of tasks (50 to 
500) with varying value of  size, communication-to-
computation ratio  (CCR),  and  parallelism.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Traced Graphs: Use task-graphs that are produced 
using a parallelizing compiler on some numerical 
parallel application programs.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Performance evaluation metrics of scheduling 
algorithms 
This sub-section presents various performance 
evaluation metrics that are used for evaluation of 
resource 
scheduling 
algorithms 
and 
application 
scheduling algorithms.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Performance evaluation metrics 
for resource scheduling algorithms are as follows.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
System utilization: It indicates percentage of time 
the resource is busy.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Throughput: It indicates the number of jobs 
processed/finished in a given time period.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Turnaround time: It is also called response time of 
a job.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It is defined as the sum of waiting time and 
execution time of the job.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Job slowdown: it is defined as the ratio of the 
response time of a job to its actual run time.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It 
primarily occurs due to a long waiting time for 
execution of job.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Economic Profit: In utility based resource usage, it 
indicates profit earned by resource.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Performance evaluation metrics for application 
scheduling are as follows.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Make-span: It is calculated by subtracting actual 
start time of the first job of application from the actual 
finish time of the last job of the application.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Schedule Length Ratio [60]: This metric is obtained 
by dividing the make-span of an application by the 
expected time needed to execute the tasks present on 
the Longest Computation Path on the fastest resource.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Scheduling time [60]: It depends on the time-
complexity of the scheduling algorithm.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
It indicates 


how much time is taken by scheduling algorithm for 
making decision on assignment of jobs onto resources.
title: Scheduling in Grid Computing Environment

text:
Speedup [60]: It indicates how faster an application 
runs on multiple resources as compared to running it

a

of 
various

and software used at Cluster computing level.

text:
The fundamental unit of work-done in Grid 
computing is successful execution of a job.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
A job in

with user while it is running.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

Higher-level Grid

in 
Grid 
computing 
environment.

LOCAL RESOURCE MANAGER 
In most Grid deployments, individual resources of 
a single organization are centrally managed using 
batch queue oriented local resource management 
system (LRM).
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
In such system, user submitted batch 
jobs are introduced into the queue of LRM, from which 
resource scheduler decides about execution of jobs.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Examples of such LRMs include PBS [6], LSF [7], 
Condor [8], Sun Grid Engine [9], and Load Leveler [10].
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
A resource scheduler is also known as a low-level 
scheduler or local scheduler, as it deals with the jobs 
submitted in a single administrative domain.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
For 
compute resources, LRM can be configured for (i) 
which user is allowed to run jobs, (ii) what policies are 
associated with selection of jobs for running, and (iii) 
what policies are associated with individual machines 
for considering them to be idle.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
An LRM manages two types of jobs: local jobs 
generated inside a resource domain and jobs generated 
by external users, i.e.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
The common purpose 
of any LRM is to manage, control, and schedule batch 
processes on the resources under its control.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Since, 
LRM deals with distributed resources, it is also called 
Distributed Resource Manager.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Basic features of any 
LRM include following:  
• 
Scripting language for defining batch job 
• 
Interfaces for submission of batch jobs 
• 
Interfaces to monitor the executions 
• 
Interfaces to submit input and gather output 
data 
• 
Mechanism for defining priorities for jobs 
• 
Match-making of jobs with resources 
• 
Scheduling 
jobs 
present 
in 
queue(s) 
to 
determine execution order of jobs based on job-
priority, resource status, and resource allocation 
configuration.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Advance reservation based LRMs are also used in 
Grid.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Advance reservation allows reserving resources 
in advance for their use in future.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Examples of such 
LRMs include Platform LSF [7], PBS Pro/Torque [11], 
[12], Maui [13], and SGE [9].
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Grid allows use of heterogeneous LRMs through a 
common interface.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
In Globus based Grid, which is 
widely used, GRAM (Globus Resource Allocation 
Manager) interface is used for job submission on 
heterogeneous LRMs.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
GRAM is a standardized way of 
accessing any LRM, as it is LRM neutral.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
GRAM 
messages remain same irrespective of LRM, whether 
LRM is PBS, LSF, or Condor.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Each LRM can be 
connected into a Globus based Grid using Globus-LRM 
adapter.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Clients submit job requests using GRAM 
protocol and GRAM-LRM connector can translate 
those messages into a language understood by a 
specific LRM.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
For example, GRAM5 supports Condor, 
PBS, and LSF; similarly, Unicore [14] supports SGE, 
LoadLeveler and Torque.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
We use HTCondor as LRM in our test Grid 
computing environment.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Therefore, we concisely 
discuss about it.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
HTCondor [15], which is formerly 
known as Condor [8], is a set of daemons and 
commands that enable to implement concept of batch-
queue controlled Cluster computing [2] of jobs.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
HTCondor is available for various platforms including 
Unix, Linux, and Windows OSes.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
We use HTCondor 
and Condor interchangeably to refer to the same thing.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
The main goal of HTCondor is to provide high 
throughput distributed computing infrastructure that 
transparently executes a large number of jobs over a 
long period.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Though, HTCondor allows use of 
computing power of a computing machine to users, it 
is the owner of the computing machine that defines 
under which conditions Condor can allow use of the 
computing machine to batch jobs.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
For example, 
HTCondor can be configured to run a job when 
keyboard and CPU are idle.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Condor implements 
ClassAds 
(Class 
Advertisements) 
to 
describe 
requirements of jobs and specification of computing 


resources.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Computing 
resources 
advertise 
their 
resource properties such as available memory, CPU 
type, CPU speed, virtual memory size, physical 
location, and current load average.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Interaction with 
Condor system for various activities is done through 
command interface.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
While a job is under execution, 
input/output files of the job can be transferred using 
Condor I/O, which redirects I/O related system calls 
of a job to the job submit machine.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
GRID COMPUTING ENVIRONMENT 
Grid computing enables utilization of idle time of 
resources that are available at geographically diverse 
locations [14], [16], [17].
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Grid computing can allow 
access of resources such as storage, sensors, application 
software/code, databases, and computing power.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
In 
Grid, resources are autonomous and heterogeneous.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Current Grid computing, in most deployments, is on 
collaborative manner, in which resources exhibit 
varying availability.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
However, QoS oriented Grid 
computing [18] is also possible.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Grid computing has 
been used in drug discovery, GIS processing, sky 
image processing, industrial research, and scientific 
experiments.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Use of Grid computing infrastructure can 
be done by converting traditional applications into 
Grid 
applications, 
which 
have 
form 
of 
either 
independent tasks application or dependent tasks 
application.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
The 
independent 
tasks 
applications 
include 
Parameter 
Sweep 
and 
Task 
farming 
(embarrassingly parallel) problems [19], e.g.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Dependent tasks applications include 
workflow [20] applications, e.g., Montage [21].
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Grid computing field started as an extension of 
Cluster computing.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Both Cluster computing and Grid 
computing are used to utilize idle computing 
resources; however, there are differences between two.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
If Grid computing is compared with cluster computing, 
cluster computing has resources under central control 
and cannot connect resources that are present across 
boundary of the organization.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Whereas, using Grid 
computing it is possible to connect, share, and use 
resources that are present in other organizations.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Moreover, Grid allows heterogeneous resources, 
whereas Cluster does not.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
To enable use of diverse, idle 
resources, Grid computing field started in mid 90's 
with the term Meta-Computing.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Two projects: Globus 
Project [22], at Argonne National Laboratories and the 
University of Chicago, and Legion [23], [24], at 
University of Virginia, are considered to be starting 
points for Grid computing field.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
To implement Grid computing, we need Grid 
middleware.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Grid middleware is a software that glues 
different local resources of organization(s) to form a 
higher-level, 
bigger, 
global 
resource.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
A 
Grid 
middleware offers following services: 
• 
Submission and monitoring of remote jobs 
• 
Allocation and co-allocation of resources  
• 
Access to storage devices and data management 
• 
Information service (kind of yellow page 
service) 
• 
Resource 
discovery, 
resource 
registration, 
resource information update 
• 
Security service: authentication, authorization, 
and delegation 
Most Grid deployments are based on Globus, which 
is a de-facto middleware software for implementing 
Grid computing.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Globus toolkit 5.2.3 (GT 5) [25], which 
we have used for experimentation in this paper, offers 
following components.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
• 
Grid 
Security 
[26] 
(Certificate 
based 
authentication, authorization and single signon) 
and Simple CA certificate authority for signing 
host and user certificates.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
• 
GSI (Certificate) based GridFTP [27] (client and 
server) for transferring data (files) on Grid sites 
(machines) 
• 
GRAM client and GRAM server to allow 
remote job submission and execution using 
standard protocol (GRAM).
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

A Grid computing 
environment involves various Grid sites, generally one 
organization is considered as one Grid site.

Each 
organization generally contains batch-queue controlled 
cluster, which is exposed to external organizations 
through Grid computing services and protocols.

Each 
Grid site contains a Head node, which is accessible 
through 
network, 
generally 
Internet.

For 
implementation of Grid environment, we prepare three 
Grid sites in virtual Grid computing environment 
inside Oracle VirtualBox and prepare three Grid sites 
in real, physical Grid computing environment made of 
three computers connected through a network switch.

Ubuntu OS only once on virtual machines (VMs), and

cloning existing one.

Using 
Virtual environment, we can do even network related 
activities without having physical network.

In a single 
computer, we can create many virtual machines 
working as Grid nodes; however, we can have only

Available main memory limits the

text:
MAJOR PROBLEMS AND TROUBLE-SHOOTINGS  
Problem 1 and Trouble-shooting: Not using 
matching 
software 
component 
depending 
upon 
Operating System.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Major Grid computing software are 


targeted for Unix or Linux derivative Operating 
Systems.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Different Linux distributions might use 
different binary libraries to carry out certain activities.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Software related to Grid computing are available in 
source-code form.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
If we use source-code and prepare 
binary files for target machine by compiling them, then 
there is less probability of having mismatch among 
various software components.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
However, if we want to 
use binary versions, but binary version of the software 
is not available, then, we try to use software targeted 
for other matching Linux distributions.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Such problem 
generally occurs between software for Ubuntu  and 
software for Debian.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Problem 2 and Trouble-shooting: Trying to run a 
job without creating proxy credentials.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Grid computing 
uses X.509 certificate based authentication, it does not 
use authentication through user name and password.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
When a user wants to use any remote resource for job 
execution, then the user has to provide its identity to 
the resource.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Therefore, user must create proxy 
credential to allow successful authentication for the 
submitted job.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Before doing any job submission 
activity, user can check whether proxy credentials are 
created or not using grid-proxy-info command.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text: Problem 3 and Trouble-shooting: Certificate error.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Certificate error occurs when the clock-time of 
submitting machine is ahead of the clock-time of target 
machine.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
This error reads as “You have sent a 
certificate with future date/time”, as certificate always 
include validity period, including starting date-time 
and ending date-time.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
This problem occurs due to 
mismatch in clock timings of machines that are present 
in the Grid computing environment.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
In our test 
environment, we alleviate this timing problem by 
using 
Network 
Time 
Protocol, 
which 
does 
synchronization of clocks with reference server, in our 
test environment it is grid-b machine.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Problem 4 and Trouble-shooting: Unable to 
understand problem occurring in working of some 
functionality.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
We must understand internal working of 
particular functionality.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
For example, when we try to 
test submission and execution of a remote job, nothing 
happens, i.e., command hangs.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
As Grid computing 
environment involves computer network, there might 
be some delay in getting output of remote job 
execution.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
However, if you do not see any output after 
much longer period than expected, then there is 
possibility that some internal software component is 
not working properly.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
The important thing is we must 
understand whether problem has occurred due to error 
in LRM software or error in Grid software.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Problem 5 and Trouble-shooting: Unable to 
understand cause of the problem.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

text:
Once the location of 
any problem, either LRM or Grid, is known, the next 
thing we must understand is what the cause of the 
error is.
title: Experimental Study of Remote Job Submission and Execution on LRM through Grid Computing Mechanisms

Ashraf A.
title: Polymorphic Worms Collection in Cloud Computing

text:
Shahin1, 2 
1Department of Computer Science, Al Imam Mohammad Ibn Saud Islamic University (IMSIU), Kingdom of 
Saudi Arabia
