2 
waste heat from a discrete device and the limited battery life 
of a mobile device.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The parallel software development framework that we will 
utilize in this work is the Open Computing Language 
(OpenCL) [14].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This is because OpenCL is a free, open 
standard and is vendor and platform neutral.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
It allows one to 
write high performing, yet, portable parallel code that 
executes on a wide variety of processor architectures including 
CPUs, GPUs, FPGAs, DSPs, SoCs and the Xeon Phi.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
All 
major processor vendors (Nvidia, AMD, Altera, TI, 
Qualcomm, ARM, IBM, Intel, etc.) have adopted the OpenCL 
standard and have released support for it on their hardware.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The availability of the OpenCL parallel programming 
framework on such a wide variety of compute hardware, 
including consumer-grade gaming GPUs, allows for the 
possibility of easily evaluating such hardware for scientific 
computation.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This article is organized as follows: Section II provides a 
description of the metrics and the scientific application 
benchmarks we consider in this work; Section III includes 
detailed information on the hardware devices we evaluate; 
Section IV focuses on a discussion of the results we obtained 
and finally in Section V we end with some conclusive 
remarks.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
We also include a detailed Appendix that includes all 
the explicit data that our benchmarking generated.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
SCIENTIFIC APPLICATIONS 
In this section, we present a brief introduction to the 
scientific applications we utilize to evaluate the overall 
performance of the gaming hardware under consideration in 
this work.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
We will not only study the overall performance 
delivered by the different gaming devices under consideration 
in this work, but also compare the associated costs involved 
through common efficiency metrics such as performance-per-
dollar (a measure of the cost of procurement) and 
performance-per-Watt (operating costs).
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The latter is also an 
important current consideration in the context of “green” 
computing with the mission of not only making the research 
computing enterprise more eco-friendly, but also to enable the 
next generation of (exascale) supercomputing.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
SHOC Benchmark  
 
The 
Scalable 
Heterogeneous 
Computing 
(SHOC) 
benchmark [15] is a scientific computing kernel suite based on 
OpenCL.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
It targets multi-core CPUs and many-core GPUs in a 
single or (message-passing based) clustered environment.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
For 
the purposes of this work, we only focus on a single device 
benchmark leaving the cluster-based study for future 
exploration.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Below is the detailed list of compute kernels in 
the SHOC suite with a brief explanation:  
 
Level 0 - Feeds & Speeds 
• Bus Speed Download and Readback---This kernel 
measures the bandwidth of the interconnection bus between 
the host CPU and the GPU device.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• Peak FLOPS---This kernel measures the peak floating-
point (single or double precision) operations per second.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• Device Memory Bandwidth---This kernel measures 
bandwidth for all types of GPU memory (global, local, 
constant, and image).
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• Kernel Compilation---This benchmark measures average 
compilation speed and overheads for various OpenCL kernels.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Level 1 – Basic Parallel Algorithms 
• FFT---This benchmark measures the performance of a 2D 
Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) for both single- and double- 
precision arithmetic.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• GEMM---This kernel measures the performance on a 
general matrix multiply BLAS routine with single- and 
double- precision floating-point data.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• MD---This kernel measures the speed of the Lennard-
Jones potential computation from molecular dynamics (single- 
and double- precision tests are included).
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• Reduction---This kernel measures the performance of a 
sum reduction operation using floating-point data.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• Scan---This kernel measures the performance of the 
parallel prefix sum algorithm on a large array of floating-point 
data.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• Sort---This kernel measures performance for a very fast 
radix sort algorithm that sorts key-value pairs of single 
precision floating point data.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• SpMV---This benchmark measures performance on sparse 
matrix with vector multiplication in the context of floating-
point data, which is common in some scientific applications.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• Stencil2D---This kernel measures performance for a 
standard 2D nine-point stencil calculation.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• Triad---This benchmark measures sustainable memory 
bandwidth for a large vector dot product operation on single 
precision floating-point data.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Level 3 – Real Application Kernels 
• S3D---This benchmark measures performance in the 
context of a simulation of a combustion process.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
It computes 
the rate of chemical reactions on a regular 3D grid.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Einstein@Home 
 
Laser Interferometer Gravitational Wave Observatory 
(LIGO) [16] is a National Science Foundation (NSF) funded 
facility dedicated to the experimental detection of gravitational 
radiation.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
It is part of an international network of detectors 
located across the globe (two LIGO sites in the United States, 
GEO/Virgo in Europe, TAMA/KAGRA in Japan and soon 
LIGO-India/IndIGO in India).
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Critical to a successful 
detection is the use of theoretical signal template banks from 
likely sources (like binary black hole systems) for the purpose 
of matched-filtering [17] (mainly due to the fact that the 
signal-to-noise ratio in the data streams is very low).
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
LIGO 


PREPRINT 
 
3 
has recently made the first-ever direct detections [18,19] of 
gravitational waves – “ripples in the fabric of spacetime” that 
Einstein predicted precisely 100 years ago as a consequence of 
his new theory of general relativity.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
These observatories 
generate data at the rate of several petabytes per year and they 
require highly computationally intensive data analysis [20].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Einstein@Home [21] is an open-source, NSF funded, public 
distributed computing project that offloads the big data 
analysis associated to these observatories to volunteers 
worldwide.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The 
goal 
of 
Einstein@Home 
is 
finding 
gravitational waves emitted from neutron stars, by running a 
brute force search for different waveforms in an extremely 
large data-set.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Thus, this project plays an important role in 
providing crucial data analysis capabilities to a very large and 
significant, international experiment and also deeply engaging 
the public in the relevant science.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Since 2009 the project 
expanded its search for pulsar candidates to include radio-
telescope data, and has had considerable success [22].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Einstein@Home involves over 430,000 participants with 
over 7 million client computers and has a total compute 
capability of over 2.2 PFLOPS.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
In addition to engaging 
citizens deeply into the science, the project has also 
discovered over 20 new pulsars through the radio-data search 
[23].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
One of the authors has been a volunteer developer for the 
project since its inception in 2005 and has contributed to the 
development of the code on Apple PowerPC systems, PS3s 
and also GPUs [24,25].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
With the major shift towards usage of 
low-power, battery-operated, mobile compute devices by 
everyday users, such volunteer-based computing projects are 
likely to suffer a significant setback in terms of the donated 
compute cycles.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
However, this challenge can be largely 
overcome if high-performing video-gaming hardware, which 
has significant longevity in the consumer market, is brought 
into the fold.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
HARDWARE SPECIFICATIONS 
In this section, we document full details on the list of the 
video-gaming hardware devices we evaluated using the SHOC 
and the Einstein@Home benchmarks.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
We also include a high-
end HPC GPGPU accelerator and a multi-core CPU for 
reference.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Basic hardware specifications for the devices tested are 
included in Table I.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The Tegra X1 SoC, Radeon Fury GPU 
and the A10 APU are technologies commonly found in (or 
targeted at) consumer-grade gaming (high-end and mobile) 
devices, while the Tesla K40 GPGPU and x86 multi-core 
CPUs are utilized in HPC servers.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

The Nvidia Tesla K40 uses the Kepler GK110B GPU, a 7.1 
billion-transistor chip manufactured by TSMC on a 28 nm 
process [27].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This discrete GPGPU was selected for its raw 
computational power and convenient actively cooled PCIe 
form factor.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Nvidia specifically targets the HPC market with 
the Tesla series, particularly those segments that require ECC 
memory with the capability to correct single bit errors and 
detect double bit errors.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
However, enabling ECC results in a 
modest loss of memory capacity and performance.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Molecular 
Dynamics 
simulations 
carried 
out 
on 
the 
XSEDE 
supercomputer Keeneland point to the questionable value of 
ECC memory for some areas of scientific computing [28].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The Nvidia Tegra X1 is a SoC device manufactured by 
TSMC on a 20 nm process and tested using the Jetson TX1 
development board, the first of this class of devices to reach 
terascale performance [29].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Nvidia designed the Tegra 
processor with mobile devices in mind using quad core ARM 
Coretex A57 and A53 processors in a big.LITTLE design 
coupled with their latest power efficient Maxwell GM20B 
GPU.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Nvidia is making a push into new markets with this 
device collaborating with numerous tablet and automotive 
manufactures.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Note that OpenCL is currently not supported on 
the Tegra device.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Therefore, we use Nvidia’s own GPGPU 
framework (CUDA) to perform our tests.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The AMD Radeon R9 Fury X uses Fiji XT GPU that has 
8.9 billion transistors and is manufactured by TSMC on a 28 
nm process [30,31].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This enthusiast level discrete gaming 
GPU was the first to market with High Bandwidth Memory 
(HBM) that offers improvements in bandwidth and power 
efficiency compared to GDDR5 that is currently used in other 
GPUs.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The AMD A10-7850K APU uses a four core Steamroller 
based CPU and an eight core Radeon R7 Sea Islands based 
Graphics Core Next (GCN) GPU fused on the same die 
[32,33].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
In total, the APU is a 2.41 billion transistor SoC 
manufactured by Global Foundries on a 28 nm process.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The 
current generation video-gaming consoles (Sony’s PlayStation 
4 and Microsoft’s Xbox One) utilize this APU technology and 
intend to continue to do so in upcoming updates.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This 
processor represents a big step forward for devices 
conforming to the newly instituted Heterogeneous System 
Architecture (HSA) where a system’s main memory is shared 
between all compute cores rather then being segregated for 
CPU and GPU use [34].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The AMD FX-9590 is a traditional x86 CPU that features 
eight Piledriver Cores in the Vishera family [35].
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This CPU 
was noteworthy in its capability to turbo clock up to 5 GHz 
while dissipating 220 Watts of heat.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This CPU offers 


PREPRINT 
 
4 
reasonable performance on single threaded applications, its 
computational performance places it well below the other 
devices tested, and is included in our study purely for the sake 
of comparison.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
RESULTS AND DISCUSSION 
In this section we present the detailed results of our extensive 
testing.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
In the appendix of this article, we include a table that 
enlists all the raw data generated by the SHOC benchmark 
suite.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This may serve as a useful reference for readers 
interested in different types of applications.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
However, in the 
following section we focus on a select few benchmarks that 
are representative of the entire suite.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Discrete GPU devices (Tesla K40 and Radeon Fury)  
 
Nvidia first popularized the term GPU in 1990 before the 
release of their GeForce 256.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This unit marked the beginning 
of a transition where 3D modeling processes such as graphical 
transform and lighting calculations were offloaded from the 
CPU to a discrete device.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This proved advantageous for 
scientific computing as the processing power required to 
perform rapid large-scale calculations could be harnessed to 
run code containing parallel algorithms.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Consumer demands for increased realism in 3D games 
coupled with the development of low priced high-resolution 
displays has created a large and highly competitive market for 
GPU devices.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Even today this demand continues to be pushed 
by 4K displays and virtual reality headsets.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The Nvidia K40 and AMD Fury X represent the highest 
performance discrete devices from both companies at the time 
of their release.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Figure 1 below depicts the (single-precision 
floating-point) performance of these two devices in GFLOPS 
on a representative subset of SHOC benchmarks.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The two 
devices offer remarkably similar performance despite 
substantial differences in their architecture, targeted market, 
and price points, showing the viability of gaming hardware for 
scientific computing.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
While close, the Fury X holds a slight 
lead over the K40 in all four single precision (SP) benchmarks 
as seen in Figure 1.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The log-scale on the GFLOPS axis should 
be noted.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Figure 1 
Since there are commonly expressed concerns on the 
double-precision (DP) floating-point performance of video-
gaming devices, we also performed extensive testing in that 
context.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
In Figure 2 below, we show the same subset of SHOC 
benchmarks using double-precision data and operations 
instead.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
We note that the specialized HPC GPGPU Tesla K40 
device does indeed perform better on most benchmarks, but its 
overall performance is on the same scale as the consumer-
grade GPU Radeon device (whereas, its price is not).
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Figure 2 
The benchmark results are in line with expectations as the 
K40 was designed with scientific computing in mind having a 
1:3 DP to SP FLOP ratio.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The gaming oriented Fury X has a 
1:16 DP to SP FLOP ratio but still manages to come out ahead 
in the MD benchmark.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The Nvidia GeForce 780 is a Kepler 
architecture based discrete gaming GPU with an introductory 
price matching the Fury X, but has 1/8th the DP to SP FLOP 
ratio of the K40 which would further erode its performance in 
DP benchmarks so was not included in the testing.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Future 
generations of Nvidia GPUs are expected to further increase 
the gap in DP performance between the Tesla and GeForce 
lines.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
One big drawback to a discrete card is the bottleneck 
imposed by PCIe bandwidth.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Although each successive 
generation of PCIe has increased bandwidth, data transfer 
rates to-and-from the GPGPU are an order of magnitude lower 
than the system’s internal main memory bandwidth.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The 
limitations imposed by this low PCIe bandwidth are clearly 
seen in the SHOC L1 benchmarks shown in Figure 3, where 
each test is run with and without accounting for PCIe transfer 
time.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
PREPRINT 
 
5 
 
Figure 3 
To emphasize the negative impact PCIe bandwidth can 
have, the results in Figure 3 are scaled to the best result for 
each test.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Both MD and FFT show significant slowdown when 
PCIe bandwidth is taken into account, while GEMM N is less 
impacted.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Comparing the performance of the multi-core CPU on the 
same tests (data available in the appendix), one clear outcome 
is that GPU computing offers order-of-magnitude gains in 
overall performance over CPUs for a wide variety of scientific 
computing kernels.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Moreover, this GPU-enabled acceleration 
can be achieved at very low cost, especially if the video-
gaming class GPU that we mention in this section is utilized, 
as opposed to a specialized HPC GPGPU variant.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
There is a 
clear order-of-magnitude cost difference between these two 
devices, despite the performance being in the same ballpark.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
SoC and APU devices (Tegra X1 and APU A10)  
 
Heterogeneous System Architecture (HSA) is a framework 
where more than one kind of processor or core can operate on 
the same tasks using a common bus with shared memory.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This 
offers 
significant 
performance 
advantages 
and 
completely avoids PCIe bottlenecks, as a CPU and GPU can 
exist on the same substrate and calculations are performed in a 
unified memory space.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
It should be noted that we do not take 
advantage of this feature in this work; that requires OpenCL 
2.0 which our current benchmark tests do not support.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
APUs and SoCs are included in the HSA framework and are 
represented in this article by a “top down” design intended for 
a desktop computer in the AMD A10-7850K, that integrates a 
traditional x86-64 CPU and a GCN GPU.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Also tested is a 
“bottom up” design intended for the tablet and mobile 
computing market in the Nvidia Tegra X1 featuring ARM 
cores in a big.LITTLE design and a Maxwell architecture 
based GPU.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Results for the single-precision SHOC SP L0 and L1 
benchmarks are presented in Figure 4, with the A10-7850K 
and the X1 showing similar levels of performance despite 
being designed for very different markets.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Figure 4 
While the A10-7850K leads slightly in the select 
benchmarks shown in Figure 4, the performance of the X1 is 
particularly impressive with a power consumption that is nine 
fold less than the A10-7850K!
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The  double-precision SHOC 
DP L0 and L1 benchmarks follow a similar pattern with the 
A10-7850K performing particularly well on the GEMM 
benchmark as seen in Figure 5.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Figure 5 
Once again, it is noteworthy that even the APU and SoC 
devices are powerful enough to deliver performance 
advantages in common scientific application kernels, as 
compared with multi-core CPUs.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This is especially the case, 
when the power consumption of the devices is taken into 
account.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The Tegra device’s performance-per-Watt is two 
orders-of-magnitude higher than traditional CPUs.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
It is now 
common to assemble large clusters using thousands of 
compute devices for scaled up performance.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Such clustered 
systems are severely limited by their significant power 
consumption and therefore, cooling needs.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
APU and SoC 
devices may offer interesting alternatives for power-efficient 
clustered supercomputing.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Einstein@Home Performance  
 
SHOC benchmarks may provide valuable insight into the 
computational power of a device, particularly if one’s code 
mimics one of the included synthetic benchmarks.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
However, 
it is often useful to study the overall performance of a compute 
device on a complete end-to-end scientific application.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
In this 
section, we present such performance results using a single 


PREPRINT 
 
6 
representative Einstein@Home binary radio pulsar (Parkes 
PMPS XT) work unit and present the results in Table II.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
TABLE II 
Einstein@Home BRP6 Work Unit Completion Time 
Device 
Time (kiloseconds) 
AMD A10-7850K APU 
23.8 
AMD Radeon R9 Fury X 
2.30 
Nvidia Tegra X1 
23.5 
Nvidia Tesla K40 
3.46 
 
The Fury X is particularly well suited for the OpenCL 
implementation of the Einstein@Home application with the 
K40 taking 1.5x as long to complete a work unit.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The two SoC 
devices take nearly the same time to complete a work unit, but 
an order of magnitude longer than the discrete GPUs.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
A particularly illuminating way to compare performance 
results on Einstein@Home are presented in Figure 6 where 
the actual energy necessary to complete a unit of work is 
found by multiplying the average completion time with the 
rate of power consumption (Watts) of the device.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Figure 6 
The tremendous effort made by Nvidia to improve 
performance per Watt is clearly apparent here with the Tegra 
X1 coming in 2.4x more efficient than the next closest device.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This method of calculation does not account for the efficiency 
of power supplies or the power consumed by the CPU and 
components necessary to support the discrete GPUs.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Those 
factors are highly dependent on the choice of components in a 
system and would only serve to increase the gap between the 
Tegra X1 and other devices.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
While offering significant advantages in terms of 
performance per Watt, there is still a substantial difference in 
raw computational power with the Fury X completing 10x as 
many Einstein@Home work units as the Tegra X1 in the same 
period of time.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This order-of-magnitude performance 
difference raises a host of additional issues including space 
and networking.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
A 4U server may hold as many as 8 GPUs 
while an equivalently powerful group of Tegra X1s may take 
up an entire rack of space.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Network complexity would also see 
a substantial increase using Tegra X1s and potential upgrades 
to lower latency interconnects would be both limited and 
expensive.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
For this generation of SoCs, the best way to 
leverage their tremendous energy efficiency is to use them in a 
highly 
distributed 
“grid” 
like 
fashion 
such 
as 
the 
Einstein@Home project.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
CONCLUSIONS 
In this article we present the results of our detailed 
evaluation of a variety of video-gaming hardware, repurposed 
for scientific supercomputing.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
We use efficiency metrics like 
the 
measured 
performance, 
performance-per-Watt 
and 
performance-per-dollar to compare the considered hardware 
devices with more traditional supercomputing hardware.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
The 
power efficiency metric, performance-per-Watt is considered 
vital currently because it is the key towards enabling the next 
generation of supercomputing.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
We summarize the results of our study in the following list: 
• GPUs offer significant performance advantages---Many-
core GPUs typically perform an order-of-magnitude better 
over multi-core CPUs for a wide variety of scientific 
computational kernels.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
These benefits are present, not only in 
raw compute performance, but also when cost and power 
consumption is taken into account.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• 
Video-gaming 
GPUs 
offer 
similar 
application 
acceleration to HPC GPGPUs at much lower cost---
Consumer-grade GPUs targeted at the video-gaming market 
offer similar performance to high-end, specialized HPC 
GPGPUs but at a small fraction of the cost.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
This is true even 
in the context of double-precision floating-point performance.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
• Mobile-device SoCs offer the best power-efficiency---
Unsurprisingly, technologies developed to operate on battery 
power (like phone and tablet hardware) has the best power-
efficiency, 
by 
a 
significant 
margin.
title: VolkemaKhanna2016v4

text:
Harnessing 
this 
performance advantage for large-scale supercomputing is yet 
to be seen, although some exploratory projects have begun 
[26].

Yield Estimation in Hydroponic Sprouts 
from High-Frequency RGB Imaging
Danylo Abramov1,3, Eimantas Zaranka1,3, Rūta Juozaitienė1,3,

Hydroponic fodder production requires reliable and cost-effective yield 
monitoring to optimize irrigation and lighting.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This study investigates 
whether high-resolution RGB imaging, without additional multispectral 
sensors, can provide accurate yield estimation for short-cycle wheat 
sprouts.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Trays were continuously weighed and photographed every 
five minutes in a controlled environment over multiple 7-day cycles.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

revealing any information about the original version.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

combines verifiability and privacy, offering a possible foundation for pri-
vacy-preserving image authentication systems.

text:

image transformations.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

and Nova, which make it possible to generate compact proofs that can 
be quickly verified even for complex computations.

text:

sumptions, proof sizes, verification speeds, and scalability.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

and contrast adjustment, or filtering as arithmetic circuits, the study

for zero-knowledge verification.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

given output image truly results from a valid transformation of some 
original image, without ever revealing that original.

generation time, peak memory use, proof size, and verification speed.

Institute of Data Science and Digital Technologies
Vilnius University

In highly imbalanced domains such as credit card fraud detection, model 
explanations are often dominated by a few seemingly influential features.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
However, the importance of these features can vary considerably when 
data distribution, model architecture, or random initialization changes, 
raising concerns about reproducibility and trustworthiness.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To address 
this, we introduce the Feature Stability Index (FSI), a unified metric 
that quantifies the robustness of feature importance patterns across 
different experimental conditions.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
FSI is not a feature selection method but a diagnostic measure that 
evaluates how consistently a feature set maintains its relevance under 
three axes of variation: model choice, random seed, and temporal 
data window.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The metric aggregates axis-specific stability components 
Smodel, Swindow, and Sseed into a single interpretable score, weighted by 
parameters α, β, and γ.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Two complementary formulations are proposed: 
FSI-CV, which measures numerical consistency of feature importance 
magnitudes, and FSI-IE, which assesses the stability of feature set 
inclusion frequencies through entropy analysis.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Experiments using credit card transaction data demonstrate that 
FSI effectively distinguishes stable from unstable importance signals.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Features with high FSI values exhibit consistent relevance across models 
and resampling, while unstable features fluctuate significantly, indicating 
potential sensitivity to model design or data drift.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Unlike traditional overlap-based stability indices such as Jaccard or 
Kuncheva, FSI captures both numeric and inclusion stability and attri-

butes instability to specific axes, providing a deeper understanding of 
model behavior.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The proposed FSI framework supports robustness au-
diting of feature importance results and contributes to more reliable 
model interpretation in dynamic, high-risk environments such as finan-
cial fraud detection.

Chest X-rays are a high-volume, time-critical modality, yet interpretation 
remains resource-intensive and error-prone in the context of radiologist 
shortages, motivating AI “second reader” systems to reduce turnaround 
time and inter-reader variability.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This work presents MCADS, a multi-label 
deep-learning system that detects 18 chest radiographic abnormalities 
from a single image and explains predictions using Grad-CAM, extending 
common 14-label setups (e.g., ChestX-ray14, CheXpert) by combining 
broader label coverage with interactive explainability and an end-to-end 
web application.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
MCADS implements embedded case-level prioritization 
based on mean predicted abnormality probability, with three triage 
bands-insignificant (≤19%), moderate (20-30%), and significant (≥31%)-
to surface potentially urgent cases for earlier review.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The system is 
evaluated across eight public datasets (NIH ChestX-ray14, CheXpert, 
MIMIC-CXR with CheXpert labels, Google DS1, RSNA Pneumonia, SIIM-
ACR Pneumothorax, PadChest, and VinDr-CXR), using AUC-ROC per 
pathology as the primary performance metric.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The model is based on DenseNet-121 from the TorchXRayVision 
library with sigmoid output heads for 18 labels, pretrained on a multi-
dataset chest X-ray corpus and followed by post-hoc temperature 
scaling and per-label decision thresholds to improve calibration.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
For 
each predicted abnormality, Grad-CAM heatmaps are generated and 
stored alongside probabilities, enabling transparent visual review and 
supporting quality-assurance workflows.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
MCADS is deployed as a Django 
(ASGI) web application with Celery/Redis asynchronous workers, Nginx/
Gunicorn serving, and PostgreSQL plus media storage for persistence.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The clinical workflow, implemented as a single-page interface, follows 
a BPMN-modeled pathway: the technologist acquires the chest X-ray, 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
23
MCADS performs preprocessing, multi-label inference, and Grad-CAM 
generation, and the radiologist reviews, confirms, or edits the findings 
before forwarding the report to a lung disease specialist for treatment 
planning; history and administrative views are included.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
MCADS achieves strong cross-dataset discrimination for many 
labels, for example AUC-ROC up to 0.93 for cardiomegaly and 0.95 
for effusion on PadChest, 0.93 for pneumothorax on VinDr-CXR, and 
0.84 for pneumonia on CheXpert, while maintaining state-of-the-art 
DenseNet-121 performance when served through the web application 
without observable degradation due to integration.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The system 
generalizes across all eight datasets without retraining, and on a 
2-core CPU the inference latency after warm-up is approximately 5-30 
seconds per image, with model caching reducing subsequent latency; 
Grad-CAM heatmaps typically align with relevant anatomical regions 
(e.g., consolidation regions, pleural spaces), supporting clinician trust 
in the explanations.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Current limitations center on the reliability and 
coverage of the system: Grad-CAM heatmaps can produce misleading or 
“hallucinated” saliency patterns that visually emphasize non-pathologic 
regions, and there is no dedicated edge-case detection mechanism, 
so rare or atypical studies may not be identified as such and can be 
misclassified or under-triaged.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Future work is planned on prospective 
clinical validation, improved robustness across institutions, and 
multimodal fusion with additional clinical data.

In today’s digital world, the importance of cybersecurity is increasing rap-
idly.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The evolution of technology and AI enables various threat actors to 
evolve malware as well as the methods of evading malware detection.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In 
this study, we aim to analyze modern malware evasion methods pres-
ently used in the wild.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
It’s important to identify such methods so that they 
can be analyzed and studied by security researchers for the purpose of 
improving the defense infrastructure of software systems.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Traditionally, 
machine learning based analysis of Windows Portable Executable (PE) file 
static features uses datasets that have either two classes (benign or ma-
licious), or multiple malware classes (e.g., worms, Trojans, ransomware, 
spyware), and one benign software class.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Our proposed method and da-
taset (DOI:10.18279/MIDAS.265677) focus on the analysis of multiple cat-
egories of benign software (office tools, security, media, etc.) and just one 
class of malware.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These categories are used to train a classifier that can 
distinguish benign software based on its static features.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Our concept is 
that for a given malware sample, it is possible to identify a benign category 
corresponding to the lowest expected detection rate.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This approach ana-
lyzes the similarity between each malware sample and multiple categories 
of benign software.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
For each instance of malware, we identify the clos-
est benign category and then inject the most characteristic static features 
of that benign cluster into the malware sample to trick the classifier and 
maximize the evasion rate.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Preliminary results indicate that, after injecting 
features from the category of benign files selected based on similarity, 
the initial classifier demonstrates a decrease in the detection rate of such 
concealed malware in comparison to the original malware file.

ungrounded variants across events,

a formatter across tasks.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

used as extractors: entity linking (Qwen-2.5-72b + Llama-3.1-8b), framing

terpart and larger ungrounded Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, also aligned bet-

tologies and linked data from natural-language text).

tion was recall-limited (ranking-insensitive) with modest precision (micro

0.50/0.45 for disinformation/trustworthy news, accordingly), while ‘critic’

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

2023, covering 11,577 student records.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The dataset includes information 
on students’ academic background, teachers’ experience, and school-level 
characteristics.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
For prediction, the focus was placed on subjects with the 
most frequently recorded grades since these subjects provide enough 
data to allow reliable forecasting.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The goal of prediction was to estimate 
the final average grade of a subject at the end of the current semester.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Several experimental setups were tested: forecasting 20, 30, 40, 50, and 
60 days before the end of the semester; forecasting the next semester 
based on the previous one; forecasting the upcoming year based on 
the past year; and making long-term forecasts up to three years ahead.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Different modeling strategies were compared, including semester-
specific, subject-specific, grade-specific, and universal approaches.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The 
universal strategy was ultimately selected for its scalability and stronger 
generalization across different cases.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
A variety of regression models 
were tested, including linear models and ensemble methods such as 
random forest, gradient boosting, and CatBoost.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Model performance 
was evaluated using standard metrics: mean squared error (MSE), 
root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), and the 
coefficient of determination (R²).
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Across all experiments and prediction 
horizons, CatBoost consistently outperformed the other models.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
For 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
35
instance, in short-term forecasts made 20 days before the end of the 
semester, the best-performing models achieved R² values higher than 
0.95.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text: Longer-term predictions remained reasonably accurate.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These 
results indicate that ensemble learning methods, particularly gradient 
boosting approaches such as CatBoost, are effective for forecasting 
student performance based on e-diary data.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The model achieves high 
accuracy across multiple time horizons, providing valuable support for 
data-driven educational decision-making.

Ernestas Filatovas1, Remigijus Paulavičius1,

Numerous variants of the vehicle routing problem (VRP) are important 
in operations research and practice.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Last-mile delivery problems 
attract particular attention because of the large numbers of customers, 
products, and vehicles involved.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These problems are usually formulated 
as mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) or other combinatorial 
optimization models.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Real-life problems of large scale, as they appear 
in business and logistics, are often not solvable with traditional MILP 
or heuristic algorithms due to their high computational complexity, 
especially when realistic constraints such as time windows, vehicle 
capacities, service priorities, or multi-depot structures must be taken 
into account.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The rapid progress of quantum computing in recent years 
has enabled the first experimental applications of quantum methods 
to routing and logistics.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Quantum annealing, in particular, has shown 
promise for handling larger problem instances and for delivering 
high-quality heuristic solutions within short runtimes.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This makes it 
suitable for hybrid approaches, where many smaller subproblems 
are decomposed from a large initial model and solved on a quantum 
device, while the overall coordination relies on classical optimization.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
At 
the same time, important challenges remain, such as limited solution 
accuracy, overhead of mapping logical variables to physical qubits, 
and restricted problem sizes.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These challenges continue to constrain 
applicability, while the adequate representation of rich real-world 
constraints in quantum formulations is still an open research issue.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This talk reviews the state of the art in applying quantum computing to 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
37
solving large-scale VRPs.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We describe first examples of realistic problem 
solving, outline the potential for building real-world applications with 
the emphasis on last-mile delivery, and highlight current hardware and 
algorithmic approaches.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The relative advantages of quantum annealing 
devices are discussed, along with key challenges that must be addressed 
before practical adoption becomes possible.

The automatic annotation of large-scale datasets is an important step 
for developing reliable computer vision systems.

Eyeglasses detection 
plays a significant role in biometric preprocessing, demographic 
analysis, and downstream facial recognition applications.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Manual 
labeling of eyeglasses in large datasets is labor-intensive and prone to 
inconsistencies, motivating the use of multimodal AI models to automate 
this process.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This research investigates the effectiveness of state-of-the-
art vision–language models (VLMs) in automatically labeling eyeglasses 
within facial image datasets.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We benchmark five representative VLMs 
– Gemini  2.0 Flash, Gemini  2.5 Flash, Gemini  2.5  Pro, Mistral, and 
Gemma 3 – on two widely used face datasets: CelebAMask-HQ and FFHQ.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The evaluation framework examines detection accuracy and labeling 
consistency across varied demographic attributes and image conditions.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Robustness is further assessed under challenging factors such as partial 
occlusions, reflections, and stylistic variations of eyewear.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Beyond 
quantitative performance, we analyze model outputs for systematic 
biases and misclassification patterns, offering insights into the reliability 
of VLMs in automated annotation pipelines.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The findings demonstrate 
the potential of modern VLMs to serve as effective, scalable, automated 
tools for dataset labelling, reducing human effort while improving 
annotation consistency.

This study provides comparative benchmarks 
and methodological insights to support the integration of multimodal AI

In recent years, long waiting times for healthcare services have been 
a major policy concern in most OECD countries, according to a 2020 
OECD report.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Healthcare service providers often face challenges in 
managing patient queues, leading to longer waiting times, negative 
patient experience, and inefficient resource utilization.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Traditional 
queue management approaches are often insufficient within clinical 
environments due to dynamic patient flow, varying service durations, and 
limited medical resources.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This study examines outpatient appointment 
scheduling and queue modelling strategies in order to reduce patient 
waiting times and evaluate service efficiency, using the open-access 
Hangu clinic dataset.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This dataset contains service time records with 
heterogeneous features such as patient demographics, medical 
problems, and previous visit information.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The analytical part of the 
investigation involves exploratory data analysis and clustering of patient 
data to identify groups with different service durations.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The optimal 
number of clusters was selected based on the silhouette coefficient 
and the elbow method, using k-means and k-median methods.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Three 
patient clusters with associated service durations and inter-arrival 
times were used as input for a discrete-event simulation to evaluate 
queue dynamics.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The proposed model allows the prediction of different 
scenarios of patient flow intensities and the assessment of physician 
workload through the resource utilization coefficient.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

Furthermore, 
the prototype of the queue management system was developed using

The simulation was enhanced with the scikit-fuzzy library for wait time

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Also, real-time queue visualization and QR code-based 
tracking were implemented.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The simulation results demonstrated that 
scheduling appointments according to patient cluster characteristics can 
reduce average waiting times.

Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) has become one of the key 
components in ensuring transparency and accountability in AI systems.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
However, the evaluation of XAI methods remains inconsistent and 
fragmented.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Here, we analyse the categorisations, methodologies, and 
properties of various evaluation metrics to highlight key differences in 
evaluation approaches and the lack of consensus across studies.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

Our 
findings emphasise challenges such as inconsistent definitions, limited 
implementation, and the absence of standardised evaluation frameworks.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

gaps and provide insights to support the development of more robust 
and comparable XAI evaluation methodologies.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Finally, we highlight 
underexplored application areas beyond classification, such as semantic 
segmentation, as promising directions for evaluation research.

Conventional segmentation methods often fail to capture these subtle 
spatial cues, resulting in incomplete or inaccurate delineation.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

search explores the potential of using single-view depth estimation as 
an additional method to improve the segmentation of eyeglass temples.

text:
We benchmark state-of-the-art monocular depth estimation models to 
evaluate their generated depth maps in the context of the fine-grained 
geometry of eyeglass temples.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Our analysis involves quantitative and 
qualitative evaluations across various datasets with different lighting, 
pose, and occlusion conditions.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Based on the benchmarking outcomes, 
we propose novel depth map integration strategies that exploit geomet-
ric information derived from single-view depth to reinforce segmenta-
tion robustness.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These strategies include depth-guided attention mech-
anisms and adaptive fusing of depth and RGB features.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

results demonstrate that incorporating single-view depth maps yields 
improvements in segmentation accuracy.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We establish a standardized 
evaluation protocol for assessing the contribution of depth features to 
segmentation performance, providing reproducible benchmarks for fu-
ture research.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The findings highlight the significance of leveraging mon-
ocular depth cues for enhancing robustness in eyeglass temple extrac-
tion tasks.

E-learning has a long tradition.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In an e-learning environment, a computer 
system aids students to learn online, providing exercises and learning 
material.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text: Recommender systems also have a long tradition.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
They are 
known in platforms providing entertainment like Netflix and products 
like Amazon.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Clients obtain suggestions for the next products based on 
their past behaviour.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text: Recommender systems are relatively new in e-learning.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
On one hand, 
we have the assessment material on question and study material and on 
the other hand, a database of user profiles which record the background 
of the student and the history of how questions were answered and how 
long it took them.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In a European research project called iMath, we investigated various 
ways to create a recommender system for e-learning on mathematical 
subjects based on several methodologies.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The aim was to facilitate 
learning and understanding for a student.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This provided a discussion of how to measure performance in learning 
indicators of the system; when is this successful?
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In the discussions 
about the effectiveness, we decided that methods should aim to predict 
which next question or which new material (video, description) may help 
the student further in obtaining insight, where success is measured 
as getting the next question well answered.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This means we measure 
whether the next question is answered correctly.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Moreover, we had a discussion about concept maps; how do we 
know that students cover all the concepts available in the topic to be 
learned, and is there a logical order?
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Like in other recommender systems, given past information of users 
in a database, machine learning methods like Random Forest have been 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
44
suggested and implemented.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Another way is to simply classify questions 
on their difficulty level, given the success rate of the answers.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Machine 
learning methods like random forest are data and energy-hungry.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text: Instead, we implemented methods for collaborative filtering.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The 
recommendations are based on other users of the system who followed 
a similar path, and for which some questions have been successful.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The computation does not require learning of systems, but is based on 
matrix factorization methodologies, which require far less computation 
and energy.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Our investigation goes in the direction of comparing the machine 
learning ideas with matrix factorization methods, measuring effective-
ness and efficiency.

One of the most common types of genetic variation is the single 
nucleotide polymorphism (SNP).
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
It refers to the presence of a particular 
nucleotide at a specific position in the genetic code.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Such genetic 
variations are often associated with various phenotypes and are 
commonly investigated in genome-wide association studies (GWAS) 
to uncover genotype–phenotype relationships [1].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Genetic variations 
might span regions of genetic code.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This study aims at identifying target 
genetic variations with respect to mathematical properties of genetic 
code.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Genetic sequence of interest is encoded as integer number 
sequence comprising of the first 4 natural numbers, each assigned to 
a particular nucleotide.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In this way a gene, chromosome or any other 
genetic sequence could be further analyzed mathematically.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Patterns, 
variability, statistical distribution, etc.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
could be assessed using a number 
of methods.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Here Shannon entropy and generalized permutation 
entropy are computed for moving windows of the encoded sequence.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Entropy based features are a proven class of methods for genetic data 
analysis [2].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
For example, differences in entropy had been used to 
detect mutations in the virus DNA [3].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The aforementioned numerical 
features here are analyzed as a new sequence.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Local extreme values 
(peaks) are identified and corresponding SNPs are selected.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These are 
the target genetic positions to be further analyzed by experts in order to 
determine possible common aspects.

Detecting Maritime Anomalies  
Using LSTM and XGBoost Quantile 
Regression-Powered Prediction Interval 
Models and Dynamic Thresholding
Lukas Janušauskas, Robertas Jurkus, Julius Venskus
Institute of Applied Mathematics
Vilnius University
lukas.janusauskas@mif.stud.vu.lt
Since October of 2023 Baltic undersea cables have been damaged numer-
ous times, some of these incidents are suspected to be an act of sabotage 
[1, 3].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Such was the case of the 2024 November 17-18 submarine cut inci-
dent, when a bulk carrier, Yi Peng 3, lowered its anchor, dragged it on the 
sea floor for approximately 160 kilometers and cut a telecommunications 
cable between Sweden and Lithuania [4].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This case, along with other inci-
dents of cable disruption, illustrates the importance of maritime anomaly 
detection systems, which would allow for swift and reliable detection and 
response to irregular vessel behavior.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We analyzed the Automatic Iden-
tification System (AIS) data of the Yi Peng 3 vessel at the time of the inci-
dent.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This analysis heavily influenced the proposed approach to maritime 
anomaly detection.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The main finding of the analysis was that the differ-
ence between heading and course was much larger than what would be 
expected normally, under meteorological conditions at the time and place 
of the incident.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Thus, the proposed anomaly detection method revolves 
around the difference between heading and course.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Using both AIS and 
meteorological data, we trained machine learning models to estimate pre-
diction intervals of this measurement in a future window of 25 minutes.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We trained eXtreme Gradient Boosted decision trees (XGBoost) and Long-
Short Term Memory (LSTM) neural networks with a quantile loss function, 
which enables models to produce estimates of the conditional quantiles.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This allowed us to obtain prediction intervals easily and subsequently 
have an anomaly detection mechanism.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In this study, the effectiveness of 
XGBoost and LSTM models at maritime anomaly detection was compared 
using metrics specific to prediction intervals, such as prediction interval 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
48
coverage probability (PICP) and prediction interval normalized average 
width (PINAW).
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
It was determined that LSTM models have a PICP of 97.77 
% and PINAW of 0.022, while XGBoost achieved an inferior performance, 
having a smaller PICP of 94.09 % and an approximately equal PINAW of 
0.019.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Regarding the actual anomaly detection mechanism, simple predic-
tion interval-based anomaly flagging was deemed as an insufficient ap-
proach due to the numerous false positives it produced.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To mitigate this 
problem, we used the Dynamic Thresholding method [2], which enables 
us to determine the anomaly threshold without previous knowledge of 
the percentage of anomalous cases within the dataset and can be used 
for anomaly pruning, which will be expanded upon in further research.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Most importantly, the model evaluated Yi Peng 3 AIS and meteorologi-
cal data, and the anomaly was successfully identified using model output 
and threshold, obtained from Dynamic Thresholding.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In conclusion, we 
propose an approach to maritime anomaly detection that can flag anoma-
lies with a low false positive rate.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The method is shown to be effective at 
detecting anomalous behavior in the Yi Peng 3 Baltic Sea cable disruption 
case.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
However, the set of known anomalies, which could be used for the 
evaluation of this system, is incredibly small, therefore, reliable ways for 
generating synthetic anomalous vessel movements will be investigated in 
further research.

Agent-Based Modelling in Sustainable 
Finance: A Systematic Literature Review
Megang N.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

Junile, Audrius Kabasinskas
Kaunas University of Technology
junmeg@ktu.lt
Sustainable finance requires simultaneous optimization of financial re-
turns and sustainability outcomes, creating modelling challenges that 
traditional financial approaches cannot adequately address.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This sys-
tematic review examines agent-based modelling (ABM) applications in 
sustainable finance, analyzing 45 studies published between 2005 and 
2025 following PRISMA guidelines.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Environmental dimensions dominate (47% of studies), while social and 
governance aspects remain underrepresented.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Nearly half of all studies 
(49%) lack clear alignment with EU sustainability frameworks, 93.3% rely 
on single validation methods, undermining policy credibility.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Geographi-
cally, research concentrates in developed countries, with Africa, South 
America, and Australia absent.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Methodologically, 67% of possible agent-
interaction-network combinations remain unexplored.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These findings 
highlight urgent priorities for future research: implementing multi-vali-
dation approaches, expanding geographic coverage to underrepresent-
ed regions, strengthening alignment with regulatory frameworks, and 
developing integrated ESG models.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Addressing these gaps is essential 
for realizing ABM’s potential to inform sustainable finance policy and 
support global sustainability transitions.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

50
Toward a Multi-Dimensional Assessment 
of Blockchain Decentralization:  
Empirical Evidence and MCDM-Based 
Integrative Framework
Mindaugas Juodis, Ernestas Filatovas,  
Remigijus Paulavičius
Institute of Data Science and Digital Technologies
Vilnius University
mindaugas.juodis@mif.vu.lt
Blockchain decentralization remains one of the most debated and 
multidimensional topics in distributed systems research.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Although 
decentralization is often referred to as a core blockchain property, its 
quantitative assessment across different system perspectives (wealth, 
network, consensus, transactions, etc.) is still fragmented.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This work 
contributes to the ongoing academic effort to establish a measurable 
and comparable framework for evaluating decentralization from 
multiple perspectives.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We already examined wealth decentralization 
by analyzing cryptocurrency ownership concentration across major 
blockchains, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Layer-2 networks such 
as Arbitrum, Optimism, and Polygon.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The results revealed structural 
concentration patterns in asset distribution when analyzed with classical 
inequality measures (e.g., Gini coefficient, Shannon entropy, Herfindahl–
Hirschman Index).
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We also introduced a randomized group-sampling 
estimation approach that provides more robust concentration estimates 
across heterogeneous blockchain ecosystems.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We also investigated 
transaction-level concentration patterns across UTXO- and account-
based models using various metrics and compared Bitcoin, Ethereum, and 
multiple Layer-2 solutions, uncovering systemic dependencies between 
transaction-flow structure and the underlying ledger architecture.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Building on these findings, our current research agenda expands to 
three additional aspects of decentralization: consensus, governance, 
and network.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Each aspect is approached through distinct empirical 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
51
analyses – validator and staking concentration in consensus protocols, 
voting power and proposal diversity in governance systems, and node 
distribution across geographies, ISPs, and client implementations in 
network topology.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Finally, we outline an ongoing effort to integrate 
all five aspects – wealth, transactions, consensus, governance, and 
network – into a unified Composite Decentralization Index (CDI).
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The CDI 
will be developed using multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) methods, 
enabling weighted aggregation of diverse indicators and comparative 
evaluation across blockchain ecosystems.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This approach is expected to 
yield an empirically grounded and methodologically coherent measure 
of holistic decentralization, bridging the gap between theoretical 
definitions and observable blockchain behavior.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

52
A Dynamical Network Framework  
for Relational State Analysis
Rūta Juozaitienė1, Ernst C Wit2
1 Vytautas Magnus University, Kaunas, Lithuania
2 Università della Svizzera italiana, Lugano, Switzerland
ruta.juozaitiene@vdu.lt
Dynamic networks are often analysed as binary structures, where ties 
are either present or absent.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
However, many real-world systems evolve 
through richer trajectories of relational states —such as acquaintance, 
friendship, and close friendship— whose dynamics contain substantive 
information.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To address this, we introduce a continuous-time model-
ling framework for relational state networks, in which each edge oc-
cupies one of several substantively distinct states and evolves by tran-
sitioning between them over time.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Transition intensities are driven by 
state-dependent covariates that might be decomposed into anchoring 
effects reflecting the influence of the current state and pulling effects 
associated with the attractiveness of the target state.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Both linear and 
smooth non-linear dependencies are accommodated through a gener-
alised additive model (GAM) representation.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We consider two common 
observation schemes.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
When complete event histories are available, we 
employ a Cox-type partial likelihood with nested case–control sampling, 
yielding efficient estimation of both parametric and smooth covariate 
effects.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
When only repeated cross-sectional snapshots are observed, we 
derive a binary-case likelihood that has the potential to be generalised 
to a multi-state setting.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Simulation studies demonstrate that the pro-
posed estimators recover parameters with high accuracy across diverse 
scenarios.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Furthermore, an empirical application to the Teenage Friends 
and Lifestyle Study illustrates that our approach reproduces substantive 
findings of established modelling techniques, while offering substantial 
gains in computational efficiency.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Overall, the proposed framework pro-
vides a scalable approach to analysing persistent relational states.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
It re-
tains the interpretability of classical network effects, generalises them to 
multi-state ties, and supports estimation under both ideal (full-history) 
and more realistic (panel) observation designs, thereby broadening the 
empirical scope of dynamic network analysis.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

53
Clustering Dynamic Proximity Graphs  
to Profile Vessel Traffic Density over Time 
in a Baltic Sea Case Study
Robertas Jurkus1, Povilas Treigys2, Julius Venskus1
1	 Institute of Applied Mathematics
	 Vilnius University 
2 	Institute of Data Science and Digital Technologies
	 Vilnius University
robertas.jurkus@mif.vu.lt
Maritime traffic in dynamically evolving coastal regions such as the 
Baltic Sea is characterised by continuously shifting vessel interactions 
that reflect operational intent, navigational constraints, and seasonal or 
traffic-driven changes in behaviour.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Understanding these interactions 
not at the level of individual trajectories, but as evolving maritime 
interaction networks, is increasingly recognised as a critical foundation 
for situational awareness, traffic monitoring, and future autonomous 
navigation support systems.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In this study, we model vessel interactions 
as time-indexed proximity graphs, where nodes represent vessels and 
edges are formed whenever two vessels are within a defined nautical-mile 
encounter threshold.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Instead of analysing individual vessels in isolation, 
we extract connected graph components at each time step, representing 
localised, interaction-driven traffic formations.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
For each such component, 
we compute a rich set of graph-level structural descriptors, including node 
density, degree distribution statistics, clustering properties, connectivity 
and path efficiency measures, and centrality-based interaction intensity 
indicators.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These feature vectors, one per traffic formation per time step, 
are then processed using unsupervised clustering methods, allowing us 
to discover and categorise recurring traffic regimes without imposing 
prior assumptions regarding vessel types, traffic rules, or temporal 
segmentation.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The resulting clusters capture distinct and interpretable 
maritime traffic states, ranging from sparse and fragmented motion to 
dense, hub-like and coordinated interaction structures.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This provides a 
data-driven characterisation of macroscopic traffic behaviour over time 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
54
and enables the identification of stable or recurrent traffic patterns 
that could aid in traffic monitoring, seasonal analysis, and maritime 
traffic complexity assessment.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
A Baltic Sea AIS (Automatic Identification 
System) case study confirms the practical viability and scalability of the 
proposed framework and highlights its potential as a foundation for 
higher-level maritime intelligence, including situational classification, 
strategic planning, or predictive traffic state modelling in future work.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

Council of Lithuania (LMTLT), agreement No S-MIP-24-117.

This study investigates whether sentiment analysis of financial news, 
retrieved through the Yahoo Finance API, can enhance the prediction 
of price movement directions across diversified asset classes including 
stocks, cryptocurrencies, and commodities.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
A sentiment indicator 
ranging from –1 to 1 is derived from news headlines and integrated with 
traditional financial metrics.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Four machine learning models – XGBoost, 
Random Forest, Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Logistic Regression – 
are employed to predict directional price movements.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To ensure 
transparency and interpretability, Explainable AI techniques (SHAP 
and LIME) are applied to decompose model predictions, revealing the 
contribution of sentiment versus financial features in driving investment 
signals.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Using a multicriteria decision-making framework reinforced by 
machine learning predictions, the study evaluates the effectiveness of 
sentiment-driven indicators in guiding portfolio decisions.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The results 
demonstrate the potential of combining sentiment analysis with 
interpretable machine learning to enhance decision-making frameworks 
in volatile and complex markets, while XAI ensures that model 
recommendations remain actionable and trustworthy for investors.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

Artificial Intelligence and Multimodal Data 
Fusion System for Assessing and Detecting 
Fraud in Applicants’ Videos
Diana Kalibatiene, Algirdas Laukaitis, Kęstutis Normantas,
