When applying to international universities, an applicant must go through 
the admission process, which includes submitting documents about the 
school previously attended, documents confirming language skills, an ap-
plication for admission, and a recording of an interview.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The applicant’s 
admission data is collected in different formats: paper format, scanned 
images, text documents (word, pdf), and video recordings.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Processing 
such multimodal data is a time-consuming and human resource-intensive 
process, often carried out by one person, which is why selection decisions 
may be subjective and do not reveal the real level of preparation of the ap-
plicant.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The aim of this research is to mitigate biases and enhance the pre-
cision of applicant assessments, ensuring that suitable candidates are not 
overlooked due to limitations in conventional manual evaluation meth-
ods by integrating multimodal data and applying advanced deep learning 
models for image analysis and natural language processing.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Automated video interviews (AVIs), which use machine learning (ML) 
algorithms to assess applicants, are becoming increasingly popular [1] 
because they improve efficiency and reduce the influence of human 
bias [1-4] and speed up the assessment process [5].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Such algorithms 
automatically infer applicant knowledge, skills, abilities, and other char-
acteristics [6], such as personality traits [7].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
While ML promises to ef-
ficiently and accurately infer applicant interviews, there is little empiri-
cal evidence to support the validity of algorithmic methods for applicant 
evaluation and personnel assessment [1].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Moreover, fairness problems 
in automatic interview assessment systems, especially video-based au-
tomated interview assessments, have less been addressed despite their 
prevalence in the recruiting field [3].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The data collected by VILNIUS TECH, such as certificates submitted for 
admission, copies of diplomas, and students’ achievements in individual 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
57
study subjects, provide a unique opportunity to automate and unify the 
objective assessment of all applicants.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
By applying the newest deep learn-
ing models, we have the opportunity to search for connections between 
assessments in certificates, the nature of which varies in different coun-
tries and universities.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Moreover, application of deep learning allows us 
to search for connections between the achievements of graduates from 
various countries and assess the possibilities of effectively studying one or 
another study program in Lithuania, and recommend a study program or 
field to students, depending on their achievements at school or a univer-
sity in another country.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

cants` videos“ (FAIR-VID).

Anonymization Corpus for  
Automated Anonymization/Encoding  
of GDPR-Relevant Data  
Danguolė Kalinauskaitė1,2, Milita Songailaitė1,2,  
Justina Mandravickaitė1,2, Justinas Dainauskas1,2,  
Agnė Paulauskaitė-Tarasevičienė3, Tomas Krilavičius1,2
1 Vytautas Magnus University
2 Centre for Applied Research and Development
3 Kaunas University of Technology 
tomas.krilavicius@vdu.lt
The The enforcement of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) 
has significantly reshaped personal data processing practices.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Its 
implementation has required data controllers to reassess and adapt 
the methodologies and tools previously used in handling personal 
data.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These changes have led to a growing need for effective data 
anonymization, making the automation of this process increasingly 
important, particularly for data processing entities managing large 
volumes of data.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
However, the implementation of this task presents 
considerable challenges, as effective automation of data anonymization 
requires access to large datasets to efficiently train machine learning or 
deep learning models to identify and anonymize different categories 
of personal information.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Furthermore, the training process often has 
to start entirely from scratch, since annotated corpora suitable for the 
intended training scenarios are scarce or, in some cases, unavailable.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To address the aforementioned issues, we present our project 
aimed at developing a specialized anonymization corpus of at least 10 
million words, annotated with GDPR-relevant data categories that reflect 
general personal information pertaining to real-world individuals.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The 
final annotated corpus will be used for automated data anonymization/
encoding in accordance with GDPR requirements, as well as for training 
machine learning or deep learning models.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The corpus annotations 
will encompass two types of data relevant under the GDPR framework: 
(1) data of general categories, comprising personal identifiers such as 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
59
names, surnames, usernames, identification numbers, phone numbers, 
demographic characteristics, locations, and other related attributes; 
and (2) data of special categories, including information concerning 
religious or philosophical beliefs, political views or memberships, sexual 
orientation, and other sensitive aspects.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Data of the first category will 
represent up to 98% of all annotated data in the corpus, while those of 
the second category will constitute 2-5% of the total annotations.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The 
final corpus will be composed of texts of different genres: 80% will consist 
of administrative documents from various fields, 10% - media articles, 
and 10% - scientific articles.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
For 
this task, tools will be developed that enable training machine learning 
or deep learning solutions (e.g., language technology solutions) using 
the anonymization corpus and demonstrating their performance with a 
certain level of accuracy.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The prepared anonymization corpus will be publicly available on 
dedicated open-access platforms.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
For this purpose, a methodology will 
be developed to hide personal information annotated in texts and, at the 
same time, ensure the integrity and coherence of the texts.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

onymization Corpus” implemented from the funds of the Economic Recovery 
and Resilience Plan “New Generation Lithuania”, project No.

Lithuanian Summaries Corpora for 
Automatic Text Summarization
Danguolė Kalinauskaitė1,2, Milita Songailaitė1,2,  
Justinas Dainauskas1,2, Justina Mandravickaitė1,2,  
Virginijus Marcinkevičius3, Tomas Krilavičius1,2
1 Vytautas Magnus University
2 Centre for Applied Research and Development
3 Vilnius University 
danguole.kalinauskaite@vdu.lt
Every text conveys certain information that substantially defines the idea 
and essence of that text.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Creating a concise representation of a source 
text while maintaining the essential information and the meaning of 
the content is known as text summarization.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Manual text summarizing 
is a time-consuming and overwhelming task, especially when working 
with large volumes of text.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Therefore, the ability to automatically obtain 
the most important information from texts is of particular importance 
for many different practical applications, such as text summarization 
for research purposes (e.g., to process and analyze large amounts of 
content), text classification, question answering, finding key points 
in legal documents or big paragraphs, analyzing messages conveyed 
by texts to detect disinformation in media or other sources, creating 
headlines, etc.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
There are two primary types of text summarization techniques: 
(1) extractive summarization and (2) abstractive summarization.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The 
extractive method uses existing sentences from a text and combines 
them to create a summary, while the abstractive technique generates 
new sentences to convey key ideas from the original content, i.e., 
rephrases information in a more concise and coherent manner.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We 
present our work in progress on creating and validating Lithuanian 
summaries corpora, which are intended to be used as resources for 
training deep learning-based automatic summarization systems to 
produce high-quality summarized textual content.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
For our corpora, we 
use texts from 4 different areas, namely, media, law, health care, and 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
61
information technologies.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Texts in these areas differ in various aspects, 
which in turn allows us to provide the necessary diversity of texts in 
terms of their content, structure, length and topics covered.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To ensure 
a consistent corpora development process and measurable final results, 
a list of predefined requirements for corpora creation and validation 
was prepared.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
By presenting the outcomes of the corpora development 
process, we discuss different stages of preparing representative and well-
balanced corpora which are based on clear text selection principles.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We 
give a particular focus on the text annotation process, which determines 
the further successful use of the prepared new resources for training 
artificial intelligence models.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Finally, we discuss the main challenges we 
have already encountered in collecting, processing, and annotating the 
texts needed for our corpora.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To assess the suitability of the created corpora for building automatic 
summarization systems, tools will be developed that allow deep learning 
solutions to be trained using the new resources and demonstrate their 
operation.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text: We address this validation process as well.

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

New inventions replace old ones and introduce new

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

Influence Low Probability (HILP) events.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To assess how well a system is 
prepared to handle a HILP event, a metric called resilience can be used.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Resilience is a system’s ability to absorb the impact of a disruption, survive 
its consequences, and recover by restoring the system to its previous 
or improved state.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

resilience, nor is there a single way to measure it.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

full thermal-hydraulic simulations of DHS and digital twins, while others 
use various system attributes, such as flexibility or robustness, to create 
a single resilience metric.

nodes and 1504 edges, featuring over 1100 unique pipeline sections

blind and sighted listeners on a ternary AX discrimination task for 
assessing synthetic speech quality (using Lithuanian neural TTS).

text:

text:

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

whereas blind listeners were comparatively stable.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

“easy” and “hard” across groups, rather than increasing uniformly with 
nominal task complexity.

text:

“hard” items for each group.

text:

(LOW–HIGH or LOW–MEDIUM) that were z-normalized.

text:
For each group,

text:

informative for one group were uninformative, or even confusing, for 
the other, indicating distinct perceptual strategies.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

synthetic speech isn’t perceived the same way by all listeners.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

background shapes how speech is judged, even when intelligibility is high.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Accordingly, TTS evaluation should not collapse across heterogeneous 
listeners or across items.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

results, and inspect cue separability can expose asymmetric confusions 
that standard aggregate scores miss.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

text:

associated with a particular attraction basin.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

point belongs to the same attraction basin as its parent, the search 
process is identified as exploitation; otherwise, as exploration.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

basins for continuous problems.

In this work, the main goal is to present some results of the computational

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The descent-ascent principle-based 
algorithm was recently proposed in [1].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The core idea of this algorithm 
is that the greedy improving operations (moves between solutions) 
are interchangeably combined with the random non-improving moves 
(perturbations) during the optimization process.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
It should be noted that 
our context is the minimization problems, so the descent procedure 
means the improvement process, while the ascent procedure should 
be linked to the random perturbation operations.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
As a case study, 
we investigate the well-known, NP-hard combinatorial optimization 
problem – the quadratic assignment problem (QAP) [2].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This problem has 
a long history; it has quite many important practical applications and still 
continues to attract the attention of many researchers.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

As the main algorithm quantitative performance

tive function, which is calculated by the following formula: θ ̅=(z ̅-BKV)/

denotes the best known ((pseudo-)optimal) value of the objective func-
tion.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

how the methodical reconfiguration of the selected particular compo-
nents/parameters – guided by the designer’s expertise – well improves

nents and options of the algorithm – we can study their impact and in-
fluence on the behaviour of the algorithm.

Extracting algorithm parameters based on visual outputs presents a 
significant challenge, as the relationship between the appearance of an 
image and the underlying parameters that generated it is often non-linear 
and lacks clear statistical correlation.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Traditional supervised learning 
approaches, such as Convolutional Neural Networks, struggle with 
this task due to their reliance on direct feature-to-parameter mapping 
and can be harmed by noisy inputs which is detrimental especially in 
magnetic tweezer experiment data, where the images are both noisy 
and low resolution.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
While powerful, transformer-based models are often 
impractical for this domain due to their demand for large datasets.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To address these limitations, we propose a hybrid framework that 
combines Convolutional Neural Networks with Reinforcement Learning 
for precise parameter regression.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The method follows a multi-stage 
pipeline: first, a DnCNN-based denoising block is used to enhance the 
quality of the input image.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
By adaptively adjusting denoising parameters 
based on validation loss, this block achieved better performance than 
traditional denoising techniques in the context of analyzing diffraction ring 
images from magnetic tweezers experiments.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Next, a feature extraction 
CNN then processes this cleaned image to encode its characteristics into 
a compact representation.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
It serves as the initial state for a reinforcement 
learning model, specifically a policy gradient reinforcement learning 
approach, which predicts and refines the parameter vector.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The agent is 
fine-tuned through a feedback loop where its predictions are executed 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
96
by the external algorithm, and the resulting performance metric is used 
as a reward signal to guide further learning.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Experimental results demonstrate that our framework achieves 
superior regression accuracy compared to conventional CNN models, 
showing consistently lower error and greater prediction stability, while 
avoiding the data requirements of transformer models, making it suitable 
for a wide range of applications with limited training data.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Due to the 
denoising stage the proposed method is especially effective in domains 
dealing with low-resolution or noisy visual data such as microscopy.

Emotional speech synthesis is a complex area of ​research that aims to 
generate speech that sounds natural and conveys human emotions.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Despite the rapid progress of neural text-to-speech (TTS) methods, 
synthesis of emotional expression poses significant challenges in all 
languages, even high-resourced ones.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The main challenges are related 
to still clearly undefined acoustic features of emotions, different levels 
and types of emotions (e.g., cold anger and hot anger), mixed emotions, 
limited interpretability and control of the emotional speech synthesis 
process.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Lastly, the absence of an emotional speech corpus also restricts 
the capabilities of modern models.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
For low-resource languages (such as 
Lithuanian), these challenges and tasks become even more complex.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Recent literature has identified a shift from traditional rule-based 
and statistical parametric methods to deep generative approaches.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Emotional TTS systems are based on deep neural networks (DNNs), 
variational autoencoders (VAEs), generative adversarial networks (GANs), 
transformers, and diffusion models.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These models lead to the following 
emotional speech synthesis strategies: 
•	 Explicit training of models using an emotionally labelled speech 
corpus.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
•	 Transfer learning of emotional speech, thus avoiding the need for 
large amounts of data.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
•	 Semi-supervised training methods, based on learning from both 
unlabelled and labelled data.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To achieve synthesis control and interpretability, another paradigm 
should not be dismissed: modifying neutral synthesized speech to 
provide the desired emotional content.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This paradigm would require 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
98
a detailed analysis of emotional speech, a large corpus of emotional 
speech data, and additional models for the speech transformation.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Initiating the study of emotional Lithuanian speech synthesis, we 
began by assessing the State-of-the-Art methods in speech synthesis, 
the availability of emotional speech corpora, and model transferability.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This report summarizes the main trends, methods, and challenges 
identified in recent studies, outlining how these insights can be used 
in the development of emotional speech synthesis for the Lithuanian 
language.

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

can autonomously uncover clinically relevant stages of myocardial 
damage, highlighting the potential of AI-enabled texture analysis as a

Data augmentation techniques can be divided into traditional

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

While traditional

Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) is a prevalent sleep disorder character-

resulting in intermittent hypoxia and sleep fragmentation.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Early detec-
tion of OSA is crucial to prevent associated cardiovascular and meta-
bolic complications, however, the gold-standard diagnostic method, 
polysomnography (PSG), is expensive, complex, and limited in accessibil-
ity.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
As OSA induces alterations in autonomic nervous system activity, it 
can potentially be screened using low-cost wearable devices equipped 
with unobtrusive photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors, which are well-
suited for monitoring pulse rate and wave-related physiological fea-
tures.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

estimating OSA burden, using a robust evaluation framework based on

night long open-source -PSG datasets, MESA and OSASUD, were uti-
lized in this study.

were extracted: pulse wave interval (Tp), peak-to-peak amplitude (App), 
maximum slope of the PPG waveform (Smax), systolic time (ST), diastolic

Several ANN archi-
tectures were compared, including CNN-GRU and Inception1D models.

(balanced accuracy and F1-score) and the mean absolute error of apnea 
burden estimation.

To assess robustness, the signal sampling rate was

progressively reduced to simulate lower signal quality conditions.

Re-
sults: Out-of-distribution testing consistently yielded lower performance 
across all deep learning models compared to in-distribution evaluation 
(balanced accuracy: 74.8% vs.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

Models 
using either PPG features or SpO₂ alone achieved inferior OSA segment 
classification performance compared to those incorporating a fusion of

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

The CNN-GRU ar-
chitecture consistently outperformed Inception1D,.

Tomas Ruzgas, Karolina Armonaite

The identification of economically related groups of companies is an 
important element in the assessment of tax evasion risks.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This study 
proposes and applies a graph-theoretic approach to identify such groups 
using data from tax registers and company ownership networks.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Unlike 
traditional classifications based on legal or administrative criteria, the 
proposed method defines company groups as structural units derived 
from interconnected ownership links between legal entities.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The methodology is based on the construction of a directed graph, 
where each node represents a company, and the edges represent own-
ership relationships with assigned weights corresponding to ownership 
percentages.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Three graph-based grouping algorithms are explored and 
evaluated.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The first identifies weakly connected components (WCCs) in 
the graph, which ensures maximal inclusion of all indirectly related com-
panies.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The second and third approaches apply different graph filter-
ing techniques: one uses eigenvector centrality-based filtering, while the 
other removes edges below a specified ownership threshold, helping to 
eliminate insignificant or formal links.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The empirical analysis is based on 
a dataset of legal entities with shareholder information from Lithuania’s 
tax registry.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The study analyses the resulting group structures formed 
by each method, comparing the number of groups, their sizes, and 
structural characteristics.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The WCC-based approach yields fewer, larg-
er groups with high node connectivity, while threshold-based methods 
produce more granular clusters with stronger internal ownership links.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Groups are further analysed through the centrality of nodes to identify 
key companies within each group.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The proposed methodology enables visual representation of owner-
ship networks and supports the detection of business groups that may 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
112
operate in a coordinated manner for tax planning or evasion purposes.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Visual analysis of selected groups illustrates the effectiveness of central-
ity filtering in revealing economically meaningful substructures, such as 
hubs and branching ownership paths.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Overall, the study demonstrates the feasibility and interpretability of 
graph-theoretic techniques for identifying company groups.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These ap-
proaches provide useful insights for auditors, analysts, and policymak-
ers when assessing the complexity of inter-company relationships and 
detecting structures that may increase the risk of non-compliance or tax 
base erosion.

title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
While traditional QA models, such as those 
based on BERT architectures, excel at extracting specific spans of text, 
they often encounter difficulties with long, fragmented, and domain-
specific requirement texts [1-2].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) 
improves the precision of answers by using external knowledge during 
the inference stage [3].

In this research, we assess five RAG strategies 
for RE QA like sparse lexical retrieval with BM25 [4], dense vector-based 
retrieval using semantic embeddings [2], a hybrid semantic reranking 
process utilizing cross-encoders [1], and graph-enhanced retrieval le-
veraging concept-based knowledge expansion [5].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Furthermore, we 
implement a multi-hop retrieval extension that incorporates entity-level 
reasoning to uncover contextual evidence spanning multiple segments 
[6].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These methods are designed to alleviate information overload by 
pinpointing potentially relevant parts of requirement documents, po-
tentially enhancing answer precision and interpretability in subsequent 
reasoning activities.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We assess the models using a domain-specific RE 
dataset with four standard QA metrics: Exact Match (EM) and F1 score 
for span-level accuracy, ROUGE-L for lexical similarity, and BERTScore 
for semantic alignment.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The experimental outcomes indicate that re-
trieval-based approaches do not consistently surpass the non-retrieval 
BERT+LSTM baseline in all scenarios.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Although some configurations, es-
pecially dense and multi-hop retrieval, show localized improvements in 
semantic alignment and contextual relevance, other RAG variants per-
form similarly or worse.

These results imply that while retrieval augmentation can boost 
performance in particular cases, its efficacy is largely contingent on the 
retrieval strategy and the quality of context selection, underscoring the 
necessity for meticulous method design in RE-focused QA systems.

Visualizing and Controlling 
the Optimization Process of Geometric 
Multidimensional Scaling
Martynas Sabaliauskas
Institute of Data Science and Digital Technologies
Vilnius University
martynas.sabaliauskas@mif.vu.lt
Multidimensional Scaling (MDS) is a special technique for dimensionality 
reduction and data visualization, aiming to represent high-dimensional 
data in a low-dimensional Euclidean space.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The quality of this represen-
tation is typically improved by minimizing a stress function.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
However, the stress function is well-known for being non-convex, 
characterized by a complex surface with numerous local minima.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Tra-
ditional optimization algorithms, most notably SMACOF (Scaling by Ma-
jorizing a Complicated Function), often become trapped in these inferior 
solutions.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Furthermore, these algorithms operate as “black boxes”, pro-
viding researchers with little insight into the optimization process and 
no tools to identify or improve an inferior result.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The consistency of the 
outcome heavily depends on the random initial configuration, making 
MDS analysis often frustratingly unclear.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This research introduces a paradigm shift by leveraging the Geomet-
ric Multidimensional Scaling (GMDS) method to transform this unclear 
process into one that is transparent, interpretable, and controllable.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
GMDS is derived from a clear geometric interpretation of the optimi-
zation problem, where the iterative step is defined as the centroid of 
intermediate points representing ideal locations based on individual dis-
similarities.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Crucially, this geometric step has been proven to correspond 
exactly to the anti-gradient direction of the local stress function.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We uti-
lize this analytical foundation to deconstruct the optimization process.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
By employing dynamic visualization tools (Desmos, GeoGebra) and 
conducting a thorough asymptotic analysis of the GMDS iteration for-
mula, we map the optimization process.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The asymptotic analysis reveals 
that as a point approaches singularities (coinciding points) or diverges 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
116
to infinity, the subsequent GMDS steps converge to well-defined hyper-
spheres.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These hyperspheres form a “topographical map” of the stress 
structure, visualizing the basins of attraction.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
While this visualization provides profound insight, we found that 
visual inspection alone is insufficient to consistently differentiate global 
minima from local ones.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This motivated the development of a novel, 
analytically driven assessment and iterative improvement cycle.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This 
enhanced GMDS framework allows us to analytically determine whether 
any point in the configuration is trapped in a local minimum.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
If so, 
the algorithm systematically relocates the point to a globally superior 
position and re-optimizes the configuration.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Empirical studies demonstrate that this enhanced GMDS consistently 
outperforms SMACOF, achieving lower stress values.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Additionally, the 
intrinsic structure of GMDS is highly suitable for parallel computing, 
allowing for the efficient processing of large datasets.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
By integrating 
geometric intuition, visual analysis, and analytical precision, this work 
not only presents a superior algorithm but also fundamentally changes 
how researchers can interact with and control dimensionality reduction 
optimization problems.

Estimation of the remaining useful life (RUL) of bearings is usually 
performed using various methods, including machine learning, entropy-
based, or other more or less classical methods.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This study aims to use 
the ranks of the associated Hankel matrix.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Algebraic techniques in 
predictive diagnostics are still less common, although some applications 
of Hankel matrices, for example, have received more attention recently 
[2, 3, 4].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The study further adds to the development of Hankel matrix-
based applications in predictive diagnostics.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Bearing acceleration 
measurements with respect to the vertical axis (obtained from the 
scientific experimentation platform PRONOSTIA [1] are analysed.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
A 
fixed sliding window is used, and the list of associated Hankel matrices 
is formed.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
As in our previous research, the computation of the 
singular values of the Hankel matrices is carried out by using the SVD 
decomposition.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The optimal parameters for matrix size, threshold for 
singular value importance are determined previously.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
It must be noted 
that the pseudo-rank of the Hankel matrix is considered, since almost all 
real-world sequences are contaminated by noise.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To reduce said noise, 
the fixed window of the moving average is used.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In this way, pseudo-rank 
is employed as the property of a vibrational signal and a predictor of RUL.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
A new step in the study is the development of the prediction model to 
receive multidimensional input: a list of pseudo-ranks.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Analysis of real-
world diagnostic data shows that the correlation between pseudo-rank 
and remaining useful life could be seen when there was about 5 to 10 \% 
RUL left.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Thus, a one-dimensional predictor is only suitable for analysing 
short RUL.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We have constructed and trained an artificial neural network 
(ANN) with a single and then with multidimensional input, pseudo-

rank(s) of a Hankel matrix.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
A number of computational experiments are 
performed to compare the two approaches.

Causal Insights into Stroke  
Mortality Risk Reduction
Virgilijus Sakalauskas, Dalia Kriksciuniene
Kauno Kolegija 
virgilijus.sakalauskas@go.kauko.lt
Stroke Stroke is a disease with severe and lasting consequences for 
patients’ health, which necessitates the use of a broad variety of methods 
for health recovery.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The research for identifying the most effective 
treatment methods is crucial for reducing the impact of stroke outcomes.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Predictive machine learning models are widely applied for exploring 
indicators of patient survival; however, these models are limited in their 
explanatory power and ability to identify the most effective treatment.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In this study, we aim to apply causal inference and its explanatory power 
to clinical and demographic data of 944 stroke patients treated at the 
Clinical Centre of Montenegro.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Based on the research literature, we have selected eight variables 
for analysis, including treatment methods, age, health status, and stroke 
type.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Our goal was to assess the impact of treatment methods on stroke 
mortality rates.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To reduce bias and create fair comparisons, we applied 
Propensity Score Matching (PSM), which enabled us to form groups 
of patients with similar baseline characteristics.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To understand the 
different effects of treatments on various patients, we applied the causal 
forest algorithm.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Causal forests extend the random forest algorithm to 
estimate Conditional Average Treatment Effects (CATEs) at the individual 
level.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This not only quantifies the expected benefit of a treatment for a 
given patient profile but also helps to identify which subgroups benefit 
most—an essential step toward personalised medicine.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We evaluated the causal effect of three treatment strategies on 
stroke-related mortality using matched datasets and Causal Forests 
analysis.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The treatments compared were:
• 	Treatment 2: Antiplatelet therapy (ANTIAGREGAC)
• 	Treatment 1: Anticoagulant therapy (ANTIKOAG)
• 	Treatment 0: Other medications or no targeted treatment


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
120
The Antiplatelet therapy (treatment 2) consistently showed the most 
positive and reliable impact on survival after stroke, approximately 8.6% 
survival chance is higher compared to Anticoagulant therapy (treatment 
1), and 15% higher than No targeted treatment (treatment 0).
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
On the 
other hand, Anticoagulant therapy showed no consistent benefit, with 
CATE at -6.5%, possibly resulting in some harm, depending on the 
patient’s profile.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In Causal Forests, feature importance doesn’t indicate which variables 
predict outcomes (as in standard models) - it indicates which variables 
help explain the differences in treatment effects between patients.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Our calculations identified the Age and Health Status as the 
most influential features.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These findings highlight the importance of 
personalised treatment decisions, as patient characteristics - especially 
Age - strongly influence treatment response.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This research demonstrates the power of data science in making 
causal healthcare insights and supporting the design of targeted care 
pathways.

121
Context-Aware Modeling of Temporal 
Semantics for Deferred Reasoning
Juan C.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Hernández Gálvez, José Évora Gómez
Universidad de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain
juan.santanasantana@ulpgc.es
Temporal expressions in natural language are intrinsically uncertain: 
they carry ambiguity, vagueness, and cultural variability that cannot be 
reduced to deterministic timestamps without loss of meaning.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Traditional 
approaches to temporal processing in NLP have treated this uncertainty 
as a problem to be eliminated through immediate normalization into 
ISO 8601 formats.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Orchilla challenges this assumption by proposing a formal language 
that treats uncertainty as a representable and manipulable semantic 
entity – a first-class component of temporal meaning rather than a 
computational obstacle.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The framework introduces a compositional and 
operator-based modeling language that encodes temporal expressions 
as functional transformations over primitive temporal anchors.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Instead 
of enforcing premature disambiguation, it allows expressions such as 
“early spring,” “three days after Easter,” or “before Christmas” to retain 
their internal semantic structure and context-dependence through 
a set of formal operators.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This enables explicit reasoning about what 
is known, what remains underspecified, and how meaning evolves as 
contextual information accumulates.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The architecture integrates neural sequence labeling for temporal 
detection, symbolic decomposition into atomic components, and a de-
ferred inference engine that resolves formal representations only when 
sufficient context is available.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This complete architecture has been fully 
implemented as an experimental system to empirically validate the the-
oretical proposal, demonstrating its practical feasibility and the opera-
tional soundness of the deferred-inference paradigm.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Beyond quantita-
tive result Orchilla offers an explanatory contribution: it redefines uncer-
tainty as an operational dimension of meaning.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
By converting ambiguity 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
122
into a structured object of computation, the framework bridges linguistic 
theory, knowledge representation, and temporal reasoning.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This approach suggests a broader paradigm for temporal natural 
language understanding, one in which interpretive indeterminacy is 
not a source of error but a structured space of possible meanings that 
can be formally modeled, deferred, and resolved.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In doing so, Orchilla 
advances both the theoretical and computational foundations of 
temporal semantics in language.

Data Analysis Method for Understanding 
Human States Through Conversations:  
A Real-World Case in Diabetes Monitoring
Juan C.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Montiel
Universidad de Las Palmas de Gran Canaria, Spain
josejuan.hernandez@ulpgc.es
Monitoring daily lifestyle and emotional states in chronic disease 
management is essential, but conventional methods (manual diaries, 
structured forms) impose burdens on users and often yield sparse, low-
fidelity data.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In collaboration with a health-tech partner, we deployed 
a system for diabetic patients to submit voice notes describing their 
meals, physical activity, mood, and – for female participants – menstrual 
status.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
For instance, a patient might record: “Today I had toast with 
tomato and olive oil for breakfast, walked for 20 minutes, and I feel a 
bit stressed.” This single utterance encapsulates multiple overlapping 
pieces of information: nutrition, exercise, emotional state.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The challenge 
is to convert such noisy, unstructured, multimodal conversational data 
into structured, actionable records.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In this work, we present Semantic Sensoring, a data analysis frame-
work that transforms free-form conversational input into structured hu-
man state annotations via multi-label classification.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Rather than forcing 
a single label per message, our approach allows multiple tags simultane-
ously thus capturing the multifaceted nature of daily narratives.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The pipeline begins with automatic speech-to-text transcription 
optimized for healthcare vocabulary, followed by advanced tokenization 
designed for informal conversational syntax.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
A multi-label classification 
model assigns multiple semantic tags to each utterance, relying on 
low-resource learning strategies (few-shot, transfer learning, semantic 
augmentation) to confront the scarcity of labeled data.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Finally, the 
extracted tags are structured into machine-readable formats.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Applied to a pilot cohort of diabetic users, Semantic Sensoring suc-
cessfully identified combinations of nutrition events, activity, emotional 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
124
states, and menstrual indications with promising accuracy, even using 
limited training samples.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The resulting structured dataset can feed down-
stream models – such as personalized health monitors, alert systems, 
or behavioral analytics engines.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This case demonstrates how conversa-
tional inputs, even in voice form, can be leveraged as rich phenotypic 
sensors of human lifestyle and state.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
By bridging the gap between casual 
human communication and structured health data, Semantic Sensoring 
offers a new paradigm for data-driven health systems oriented around 
human narratives.

125
Multi-Agent System for Location  
of Park-and-Ride Hubs
Sathuta Piripun Sellapperuma, Algirdas Lančinskas
Institute of Data Science and Digital Technologies
Vilnius University
Sathuta.Sellapperuma@mif.vu.lt
Park-and-Ride (P&R) hubs are important elements of modern urban 
infrastructure.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
They help to reduce congestion and pollution by allowing 
travellers to leave their cars in easily accessible locations in the city 
and commute inside the city by bicycle, scooter, public transit, or other 
ecological vehicles.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Choosing locations for new P&R hubs can be a challenging task 
because it must consider competition between existing hubs, travel 
demand from many regions, customer (or travellers in our case) needs, 
available locations for the hubs, and other properties.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Customer 
behaviour adds additional uncertainty when locating P&R hubs.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Some 
travellers may always choose the most attractive hub, while others may 
distribute their choice among several hubs depending on their daily 
needs and the attractiveness of the hubs.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These different behaviour 
models lead to different estimates of hub utility.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To ensure that new hub locations perform well under different 
customer behaviours, it is necessary to find solutions that remain 
effective independent of the customer behaviour.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To address this 
need, it is not necessary to find the best solution for a single customer 
behaviour model, but rather a robust solution or set of them that are 
simultaneously good for different customer behaviour models.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This 
solution balances the trade-offs between different customer behaviours 
and provides a practical recommendation for city planners.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We propose a Multi-Agent System (MAS) to identify robust locations 
for a given set of new facilities from a given set of location candidates.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In 
this system, Customer Behaviour Agents represent different customer 
behaviour models and are able to propose solutions considering that 
customer behaviour.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Each customer behaviour agent uses reinforcement 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
126
learning to explore candidate solutions, learn from its experience in 
evaluating the utility of the solutions and propose solutions taking into 
account the negotiation status.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
A Mediator Agent coordinates interaction 
between customer behaviour agents and their negotiation process.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Agents follow negotiation strategies to identify optimal candidate 
locations in the context of different customer behaviour models and 
highlight the robust solution or a set of them.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

In this talk, a recent computational methodology is described (see 
[1,2]).
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
It has been introduced with the intention to allow one to work 
with infinities and infinitesimals numerically in a unique computational 
framework.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
It is based on the principle “The part is less than the whole” 
applied to all quantities (finite, infinite, and infinitesimal) and to all sets and 
processes (finite and infinite).
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The methodology uses as a computational 
device the Infinity Computer (a new kind of supercomputer patented 
in several countries) working numerically with infinite and infinitesimal 
numbers that can be written in a positional system with an infinite radix.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
On a number of examples (numerical differentiation, divergent series, 
ordinary differential equations, etc.) it is shown that the new approach 
can be useful from both theoretical and computational points of view.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The main attention is dedicated to applications in optimization (local, 
global, and multi-objective) (see [1‑7]).
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The accuracy of the obtained 
results is continuously compared with results obtained by traditional 
tools used to work with mathematical objects involving infinity.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text: For more information see the dedicated web page https://www.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The web page developed at the University of 
East Anglia, UK is dedicated to teaching the methodology: https://www.

Comparative Evaluation of Diffusion-
Based ECG Denoising and Hierarchical 
Kalman Filtering with Online Learned 
Evolution Priors
Simonas Šimėnas, Dmytro Klepachevskyi, Povilas Treigys, 
Jurgita Markevičiūtė, Jolita Bernatavičienė
Institute of Data Science and Digital Technologies
Vilnius University
simonas.simenas@mif.stud.vu.lt
ECG signal denoising is a crucial preprocessing task for accurate down-
stream cardiac analysis, as ECGs are susceptible to various noise interfer-
ences (e.g., baseline wander from respiration, muscle artifacts and elec-
trode motion) that hide meaningful morphological features.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This chal-
lenge is further amplified in wearable device conditions, where the envi-
ronment, motion and respiration introduce frequent and diverse noise 
sources compared to stationary clinical equipment.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Approaches like the 
Hierarchical Kalman Filtering With Online Learned Evolution Priors (HKF) 
[1] leverage adaptive state-space modelling of heartbeat dynamics to 
enhance signal quality, outperforming deep-learning methods, such as 
fully convolutional denoising Auto-Encoders, in tasks involving the noise 
removal of Additive Gaussian Noise (AGN).
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Recent diffusion-based gen-
erative models like: DMAM-ECG [2], BeatDiff [3] and DeScoD-ECG [4], 
have demonstrated state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance in denoising 
ECG signals corrupted by aforementioned noise interfaces.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
While HKF 
authors mention the model as an alternative to current deep-learning 
methods, no detailed comparison under real noise conditions between 
HKF and SOTA diffusion-based models currently exists.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This work pres-
ents a comparative analysis of diffusion-based models against HKF 
under identical training conditions.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
All models were trained under the 
same time constraints, tracking the performance of each model every 
10 epochs to ensure fair evaluation.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Standard error metrics like: Sum of 
Squared Distances (SSD), Percentage RMS Difference (PRD), Maximum 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
130
Absolute Distance (MAD), and Cosine Similarity (Cos Sim), were used to 
quantify the performance of each model.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We evaluated denoising per-
formance on the ECG signals from the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database [5], 
which were synthetically corrupted with three different noise types from 
the MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test Database [6]: baseline wander (BW), mus-
cle artifact (MA), electrode motion (EM), that appear in clinical settings.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Noise power is set randomly at signal-to-noise ratios (SNR) varying from 
20% to 200%.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We conducted the analysis of performance by stratifying 
by noise level to quantify the robustness of each model with the increase 
of noise.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In addition, we enforced inter-patient splits, ensuring no sub-
ject overlap in the training and testing sets, and the use of different noise 
segments, to prevent memorization and to evaluate the true general-
ization of models.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Experiments were conducted in matched-noise sce-
narios, where the model was trained and tested on the same noise type 
using an unbalanced dataset for training with the test set retaining the 
global class ratio, while hyperparameters for each of the methods were 
set based on the provided information in each of their corresponding 
papers.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Our results highlight the superior denoising results achieved by 
diffusion-based models in comparison to HKF under matched training 
(epoch/time) constraints, while at the cost of higher inference latency.

Cyber Incident Detection in Network  
Flow Utilising Machine Learning and 
Apache Kafka
Adrija Sipavičiūtė, Virgilijus Krinickij

Institute of Computer Science
Faculty of Mathematics and Informatics

adrija.sipaviciute@mif.stud.vu.lt
With cybercrime showing no signs of slowing down, passive network 
flow analysis is not enough, and implementing near real-time automated 
network traffic analysis is crucial to detect as many threats as possible.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Various algorithms have been used for intrusion or anomaly detection, 
including Smith-Waterman, Needleman-Wunsch, variations of Dynamic 
Time Warping, and negative selection algorithm V-detector, with inte-
gration of analytics engine for large-scale data processing.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These algo-
rithms typically concentrate on specific attributes.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Smith-Waterman and 
Needleman-Wunsch focus on sequence similarity, Dynamic Time Warp-
ing captures temporal alignment, and the V-detector extends the analy-
sis to multiple attributes.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Unfortunately, these algorithms, even with im-
provements, tend to be slow and require high computational resources 
to analyse large datasets, making them unsuitable for real-time network 
traffic analysis.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text: To overcome these obstacles, alternatives are sought.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
One of the possible options is applying supervised machine learn-
ing algorithms.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
After the initial training phase, machine learning models 
require far less computational power for inference compared to the re-
source-intensive traditional algorithms.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Furthermore, machine learning 
algorithms can incorporate a wider range of features such as packet size, 
protocol types, and even payload.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This enables richer analysis compared 
to sequence alignment methods, which focus mainly on sequence simi-
larity of two sequences.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This research addresses the fundamental problem that current 
algorithms and methods for network flow alignment are not capable of 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
133
effectively managing the scale and speed of real-time network flows.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In 
this work, we are working on analysing near real-time network traffic 
gathered in a safe laboratory environment.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The environment is built on 
a Proxmox hypervisor hosting multiple virtual machines and a network 
infrastructure.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The gathered datasets adhere to already existing synthetic 
data.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Network flow data is captured in real-time and stored directly 
in comma-separated (CSV) format, rather than the traditional packet 
capture (PCAP) format.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This approach ensures immediate compatibility 
with machine learning algorithms, reducing the need for time-consuming 
data format conversions.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Moreover, only relevant features are recorded 
at the point of collection, eliminating the overhead of post-processing 
feature engineering.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To handle the large-scale data efficiently, big data technologies are 
employed – Apache Kafka providing storage and real-time streaming, 
and Apache Spark enabling seamless integration with machine learning 
models.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Supervised classifiers, such as Random Forest, Naïve Bayes, and 
Gradient Boosting, are applied, selected for their ability to distinguish 
between normal and anomalous network traffic.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Model performance is 
evaluated using standard machine learning evaluation metrics and by 
measuring the time analysis takes in given computational resources.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

Survey of NLP Techniques for  
Detecting Alport Syndrome in  
Electronic Health Records
Gabrielė Skirmantaitė, Gražina Korvel
Institute of Data Science and Digital Technologies
Vilnius University 
gabriele.skirmantaite@mif.vu.lt
Rare diseases present significant challenges for healthcare systems 
worldwide due to their low prevalence, diverse clinical presentations, 
and considerable impact on patients.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Diagnosing these diseases is of-
ten delayed because symptoms commonly overlap with more preva-
lent conditions, complicating timely and accurate recognition.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Alport 
syndrome, a hereditary disorder affecting renal, auditory, and ocular 
systems, exemplifies the critical need for early and precise diagnosis to 
improve clinical outcomes.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The digitization of healthcare through electronic health records 
(EHRs) has resulted in extensive datasets combining structured patient 
information with voluminous unstructured clinical narratives such as 
progress notes and laboratory reports.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
While structured data allows 
straightforward computational analysis, much clinically relevant infor-
mation remains embedded in free-text formats, necessitating advanced 
analytical methods.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Natural language processing (NLP) offers a power-
ful framework for leveraging this unstructured data by automating tasks 
including named entity recognition, text classification, medical outcome 
prediction, and information retrieval.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
These tasks facilitate the identifica-
tion of relevant clinical phenotypes, patient stratification, and support 
evidence-based decision-making.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This work presents a systematic literature review surveying the 
application of NLP techniques for rare disease diagnosis using EHR 
data, with a focus on identifying challenges such as linguistic complexity, 
domain-specific terminology, scarcity of annotated datasets, and data 
privacy concerns.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Owing to the limited availability of research specifically 
addressing NLP for Alport syndrome, this rare disease is employed as a 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
135
motivating exemplar rather than the sole subject of analysis.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The review 
critically evaluates prevailing methodologies, highlights existing gaps, and 
outlines promising future directions, including data-efficient learning, 
cross-lingual model adaptation, and privacy-preserving collaborative 
frameworks.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
By consolidating insights from the literature, this study aims 
to inform the development of NLP-based tools to accelerate diagnosis 
and enhance personalized care for patients with rare diseases.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

Beyond Forgetting: How Elastic Weight 
Consolidation Enhances New Language 
Acquisition in LLMs
Vytenis Šliogeris
Neurotechnology
vytenis@neurotechnology.com
Large Language Models (LLMs) perform impressively in high-resource 
languages but falter in low-resource settings, such as Lithuanian, where 
they score worse on translated benchmarks compared to their English 
counterparts.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This suggests that the underlying domain knowledge 
is present but obscured by the model’s limited proficiency in the low-
resource language.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
However, directly attempting to enhance it through 
naïve continual pretraining (CP) on new data typically causes catastrophic 
forgetting.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We address these challenges by CP Gemma-2 (2B) on a 10% 
subset of the Lithuanian component of the CulturaX corpus, using Elastic 
Weight Consolidation (EWC) to preserve the model’s prior capabilities 
while aiming to unlock latent domain knowledge through enhanced 
Lithuanian fluency.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
EWC is a regularization framework that constrains 
updates to parameters deemed important for past tasks, thereby 
reducing their plasticity during CP.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Fisher information was estimated 
from the Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU) benchmark 
to identify domain-knowledge-critical parameters.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:

Disinformation remains one of the biggest problems in today’s infor-
mation environment.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Stories originating from Russia pose a significant 
threat to democracy in Eastern Europe.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
As more and more people rely 
on digital media, there is a growing demand for tools that can help peo-
ple critically evaluate the reliability of information that are easy to use 
and can be used by many people at once.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Large language models (LLMs) 
have shown great promise in this area, but most research so far has fo-
cused on closed, proprietary systems that are not available to everyone.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This research investigates the effectiveness of open weight LLMs, 
including Qwen 3, Gemma 3, Deepseek, LLaMA 3, and others, as 
practical tools for detecting deception, even on a smaller scale suitable 
for everyday applications.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We analyse three architectures that help 
assistants: basic one-shot prompting, contextually enriched few-shot 
prompting, and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Each is evaluated 
against media texts containing Russian disinformation narratives 
and neutral reporting, with a particular focus on Lithuanian-language 
sources, which pose special challenges due to low-resource linguistic 
settings.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Our goal is to show how open weight systems can be useful 
when reading the news by looking at not only how well they detect things 
but also how consistent, adaptable, and clear they are.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Preliminary results suggest that smaller open-source models, while 
less powerful than their commercial counterparts, can still provide 
meaningful guidance when carefully prompted or augmented.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Few-
shot prompting improves contextual awareness of manipulative 
patterns, while RAG architectures show promise in bridging knowledge 


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
139
gaps and grounding judgments in external evidence.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
However, the 
research highlights important limitations: sensitivity to prompt design, 
inconsistencies across different narrative framings, and notable 
difficulties in handling underrepresented languages.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Overall, the results 
indicate that open-source LLMs, when used correctly, could help improve 
media literacy and make democracies more resilient in regions where 
disinformation efforts are most prevalent.

Molecular compounds based on boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) 
have been shown to be promising candidates for microscopic, single-
molecule scale sensing of environment properties, such as viscosity or 
temperature [1].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
It is also possible to anchor the sensors to a specific 
type of microscopic environment, e.g., a lipid cell membrane, where 
the restricted molecular drift and its fluctuations result in a measurable 
estimate of the bulk viscosity and temperature, respectively [2].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This 
work builds upon an existing quantum-chemical model of microviscosity 
sensitivity applied to the snapshots of molecular dynamics simulations 
of a BODIPY sensor anchored in a bilayer lipid membrane [3].
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

Intensity 
and timescales of the dynamic changes in expected microviscosity 
sensitivity are evaluated by analysis of the results of the computations 
of the molecular properties with the aim to determine how much the 
bulk drift (spanning 2-12 ns) influences the fluorescence lifetime-based 
viscosity measurements of the sensors (0,1-5 ns).

Quantum-chemical 
computations and subsequent data analysis were performed using 
resources at the supercomputer “VU HPC” of Vilnius University in the

to Diverse Activation Stimuli

The mechanisms of ion transmission across the cell membrane have 
been extensively investigated over the decades through theoretical 
studies, computational modeling, and a wide range of experimental ap-
proaches aimed at elucidating ion channel function.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Among them, large-
conductance calcium- and voltage-activated potassium (BK) channels 
play a crucial role in regulating membrane excitability, calcium signaling, 
and cellular homeostasis.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Due to their dual activation by voltage and in-
tracellular calcium, BK channels exhibit highly complex gating behavior, 
which makes them an excellent model system for studying nonlinear dy-
namics in ion channel activity.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In this work, we analyze patch-clamp time series data recorded from 
BK channels activated by various modulators that increase the probabil-
ity of channel opening, under different experimental conditions such as 
varying membrane potentials.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
We identify time series patterns that dif-
ferentiate between distinct activation states and experimental setups, 
providing insight into how modulatory factors influence channel kinet-
ics as revealed by sequence dynamics.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Our approach integrates classical 
signal analysis techniques, feature extraction, frequency-domain charac-
terization, and machine learning to provide a comprehensive framework 
for studying ion channel gating.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
To enhance signal interpretability, the 
nonlinear mode decomposition was employed to isolate significant com-


16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS FOR SOFTWARE SYSTEMS
142
ponents from noisy data, enabling a more detailed signal characteriza-
tion and revealing subtle temporal dependencies.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The main objective of this study is to assess whether standard or 
advanced time series methodologies can effectively recognize distinct 
channel signatures that are characteristic of specific experimental con-
ditions.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
The comparative analysis of different approaches demonstrates 
which types of signal processing and analytical methods are most suit-
able for interpreting complex ion channel activity.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
In particular, the re-
sults indicate that although machine learning techniques can efficiently 
classify signals from different group, their limited interpretability con-
strains their utility in explaining the underlying physiological mecha-
nisms.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
Therefore, complementing data-driven models with interpretable 
features – such as power spectrum analysis, signal complexity measures, 
and temporal pattern evaluation – is essential for obtaining a more com-
prehensive understanding of channel behavior.
title: 16th Conference on DATA ANALYSIS METHODS for Software Systems

text:
This integrative strategy not only enhances the interpretative value 
of the results but also provides a robust framework for characterizing 
the multifaceted gating dynamics of ion channels, allowing for insights 
into various aspects of channel gating, such as sensitivity to modulatory 
factors and dependence on experimental conditions.

Michal Valko
