12: end if
• Desirable RRT (Tdesire): is the expected time for the
cloud service to complete the request from the robot.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
This
value is usually smaller than the local RRT Tl, which is
the response time when the robot executed this request
locally.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
• Maximal acceptable RRT (Tmax): is the maximal re-
quest response time that the robot can accept.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
These two values are sent to the cloud as a basis for
Cloudroid to allocate resources for the servant (cf.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
At the same time, the service stub utilizes these values
to decide whether to use the local copy or the cloud service.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The value Q in Algorithm 1 is an indicator of the degree of
satisfaction of this service, which is calculated collectively by
the RRT Tcurrent observed by the stub.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
If Qcurrent is lower
than a predeﬁned threshold Qt, the cloud service performance
cannot fulﬁll the QoS requirement.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
At this moment, starting
a local copy and invoking it instead of the cloud service may
be a wise choice.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
However, the stub still pushes the requests
to the cloud and measures Tcurrent, but it always chooses
the ﬁrst coming result between the local copy and the remote
service.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
When Qcurrent is higher than Qt, the stub stops the
local copy of the ROS package to save computing resources.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
This algorithm only starts the local copy when necessary,
which can save the limited resources of the robot’s onboard
computer in most cases.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Note that this algorithm is effective
only for stateless services, such as object recognition.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
For
stateful services such as robotic SLAM, the QoS is mainly
maintained by the mechanisms presented in Section III-B2.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
However, Algorithm 1 can also contribute by triggering the


5
failover mode when the network is down.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
In addition to RRT,
the SLA value can be deﬁned in other measurable forms such
as frames per second in a SLAM service.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
2) Cloud-side QoS Mechanism
The cloud-side QoS mechanism is mainly based on com-
puting resource scheduling and isolation.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
It is realized based
on the Docker container and the Docker Swarm2, the Docker
native clustering module.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
As mentioned, when a service is ﬁrst requested, the client
can specify the desirable SLA value.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Cloudroid uses this value
to determine the resources to be allocated to the corresponding
service servant.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
It is realized by looking through a dictionary
whose contents are a set of triples in the form of <Service, SLA
Value, Auxiliary Parameters, Resource Conﬁguration>.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
This
dictionary is built manually in advance based on experience.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Another approach to obtain the resource quota is for the client
to directly specify the number of CPU cores, memory size,
and other resource requirements to support the operation of
the ROS package, which implies the QoS requirements for
the wrapped service.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Then, a servant (i.e., the Docker image)
for this client with the determined computing resource quota is
dynamically instantiated.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
With the support of Docker Swarm,
the physical nodes in the cloud can be organized as a virtual
resource pool and scheduled globally.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
CLOUDROID IMPLEMENTATION
In this section, we brieﬂy introduce the implementation
of Cloudroid.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The design of Cloudroid is partially based
on our previous work, an early prototype presented in [17].
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
However, some essential differences exist between these two
works, including the reconstructed deployment approach, con-
cept of servant, runtime management function, automatic
stub generation, and all of the QoS-related mechanisms pre-
sented in this paper.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The Cloudroid architecture is depicted
in Fig.3, which consists of three parts: the runtime, the
deployment/management facilities, and the clients.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The Servant Clusters are the kernel of the Cloudroid run-
time, which provides the realization by the transparent services
wrapping of ROS packages.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Each servant is a self-contained
Docker instance.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
A service can be realized by a group of
servants in the back-end if necessary, in which each servant
serves a speciﬁc client.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The other details are provided in
Section III-A2.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The Choreographer manages the lifetime of
all servants and fulﬁlls the customized QoS requirements of
the client by allocating appropriate computing resources to the
corresponding service servant.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
As described in Section III-B2,
it is realized based on Docker Swarm.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The Service Portal
exposes the WebSocket and JSON-based service interfaces
to the outside world.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
It is also responsible for locating the
corresponding servant as a request arrives.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Through the Web-based deployment and management por-
tal, the deployers can submit ROS packages to Cloudroid as
well as manage the running servants manually.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The submitted
ROS packages are encapsulated as Docker images instantly
and placed into the Servant Repository for future instantiation.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
At the same time, a virtual service interface corresponding

of transparency and QoS awareness and then study a real-
world case with Cloudroid.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

by deploying onto Cloudroid a set of ROS packages widely
adopted by the robotic community, and then measuring the
performance gain of transparent computation outsourcing.

text:
The
QoS awareness is evaluated by analyzing the jitter of the test
results as well as the RRT of a typical robot application in a
highly unstable network.

title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
To validate this beneﬁt, we choose three typical
computation-intensive ROS packages widely adopted in the
robotic community as benchmarks:
• RGBD-SLAM [19]: This package takes continuous video
data with depth information as input, and reconstructs the
3D map of the environment incrementally as output.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
• RTAB-Map [20]: This package is a framework for loop
closure detection in SLAM, where robots check whether
the previous passed position has been re-entered.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
It has
taken speciﬁc optimization for low-end and memory
constrained device.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
• Single Shot MultiBox Detector (SSD) [21]: This pack-
age is a deep neural network algorithm for object recogni-
tion in images.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
We use the pre-trained SSD model based
on Caffe [22] that is a general framework for training and
prediction on deep neural network to perform detection
task on robots.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The experiment involves both the cloud-side and robot-
side hardware.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
To demonstrate the versatility of Cloudroid,
the experiment is conducted on a private cloud computing
infrastructure in our laboratory as well as on Aliyun5, a
well-known public cloud computing provider in China.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The
hardware of the cloud-side cluster is identical, consisting of
eight servers with two-way Intel Xeon E5-2640 CPUs and
64 GB memory.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Two types of robot onboard computers were
used, namely, ASUS X201E Ultrabook with Intel i3 CPU and
Raspberry Pi with an ARMv7 CPU, to demonstrate that the
5http://www.aliyun.com/
capability to support robots with different conﬁgurations.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The tested robot-side applications are standard ROS appli-
cations which are composed of a set of ROS packages.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
These
packages can be divided into two categories: the compute-
intensive package (RGBD-SLAM, RTAB-Map, and SSD) and
the other ROS packages that may interact with them.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
To
validate the transparent service wrapping feature, we deploy
the compute-intensive packages directly to Cloudroid.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The
automatically generated stubs are downloaded to replace the
corresponding package on the robot side.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
In this process,
no code-level modiﬁcation is involved.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
After validating the
function of the new cloud robotic applications, we compared
the performance before and after computation outsourcing.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
When a robot performs tasks, it sends a request to the
service and waits for response continuously.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
For RGBD-
SLAM and SSD, we choose to record each request response
time for measurement whereas for RTAB-Map, the total time
elapsed from the beginning of the test after each request
is chosen as the metric.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Because the map constructed after
data accumulating is growing, it needs more and more time
to answer a request for RTAB-Map.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
As shown in Fig.4,
signiﬁcant performance promotion can be obtained in all
these three applications after outsourcing computation to the
cloud with the help of Cloudroid.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
In particular, while the
servers in the cloud are equipped with GPU accelerators
(Tesla K80), Cloudroid shows 25.05 times speedup with the
native setup (i.e., all packages run locally and no computation
outsourcing is involved) on Ultrabook.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Note that Fig.4.e lacks
the result of the native setup, because SSD requires more than
1 GB memory and can not run on Raspberry Pi locally.

text:
The outsourcing of RGBD-SLAM is further studied with the
SLAMBench testsuite [2], an open-source SLAM performance
benchmark tool.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
According to SLAMBench, a SLAM process
can be divided into three phases: data acquisition, SLAM
computation, and map rendering.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
In our experiment, only the
computation phase in these three phases (i.e., the RGBD-
SLAM ROS package itself) is performed on the cloud.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
There is a notable performance
promotion with our Cloudroid compared with native setup,
even though the Cloudroid must transfer a large volume of
RGB-D data and the map over the network.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
QoS awareness evaluation
Another beneﬁt of Cloudroid is the QoS awareness in
cloud service invocation.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
To investigate this metric, we further
measure the Standard Deviation (SD) of the serving time
(t1, t2, ..., tN) during the previous experiments.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The smaller
SD value indicates less jitter in performance.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
We compare
the SD value of the three benchmarks under the four setups:
native, private cloud, public cloud, and private cloud with GPU
(only for SSD).
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
As shown in Fig.5, the public and private
clouds show nearly the same variances in each scenario.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
For SSD, if the GPU device is presented in Cloudroid, the
application obtains the most stable performance.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
An interesting
phenomenon being contrary to our intuition is that the SD
of the native setups (both the Ultrabook and the Raspberry
Pi) is always the highest.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The most likely reason is that all
these three ROS packages chosen are highly compute-intensive
and involve multiple threads in implementation.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
These threads
compete with the resources unexpectedly while the computing
capability is far from adequate, thereby resulting in huge
variance in the test results.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
To evaluate the cloud and robot cooperation in QoS as-
surance, we conducted the SSD experiment in a dynamic
network environment with the ”Cloudroid + Ultrabook” setup.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
In this experiment, the QoS of the cloud services in the form
of RRT is accidentally degraded because of some network
interferences.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
As shown in Fig.6, this kind of cloud-side QoS
degradation occurs from requests 24 to 45, 75 to 96, and 111
to 122.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The satisfaction line, in red, signiﬁcantly decreases
at the beginning of these periods, which triggers the robot to
start the local SSD package for emergency, as indicated by the
yellow stars.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Using the client-side QoS mechanisms, the robot
effectively copes with the uncertainty and maintains most of
the RRT within an acceptable range.

Real-world case study
We also conducted the RGBD-SLAM experiment in a real-
world indoor environment.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
A wheel-driven robot mounted with
a Microsoft Kinect camera collects RGB-D data while moving,
and the RGBD-SLAM ROS package runs on the private cloud
with Cloudroid or the robot natively.The robot is placed at the
center of the room.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
It spins four times to collect the RGB-D
data of the environment in front of it.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
In order to successfully
obtain the map in the native setup, we slow down the angular
rotation velocity at 0.33 times the standard velocity in both
setups.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Fig.7 shows the result map data of the native setup and
the private cloud setup.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Fig.7(b) shows that the Cloudroid has
reconstructed the basic structure of the room with recognizable
objects.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
However, in Fig.7(a), the native setup can only build
parts of the noisy and distorted map.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Having investigated the internal mechanism of RGBD-
SLAM algorithm, we learned that the native method results
in large quantities of building procedure failure, due to the
lower map-generation rate and less common features between
adjacent frames brought by the poor hardware conﬁguration.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The extra precision is purely obtained by employing our
solution.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
This case demonstrates that Cloudroid is capable of
promoting the robotic task efﬁciency by utilizing rich cloud
computing resources in real-life.

CONCLUSIONS
In this paper, we proposed a PaaS infrastructure called
Cloudroid, which aims to provide a general solution to enable
robots to outsource their computation to the cloud.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
With
Cloudroid, unmodiﬁed robot software packages can be directly
deployed as cloud services.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
Robot applications can invoke
those services in virtue of the automatically generated service
stub without any code-level modiﬁcation.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
And the local pack-
age restarting policy on the robot side and resource schedul-
ing/isolation mechanism on the cloud side can cooperate to
maintain the concerned QoS in this process.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The evaluation
and comparative results indicate that our solution is effective
and efﬁcient.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
The real-world case study also illustrates that
signiﬁcant beneﬁts can be obtained by introducing Cloudroid
into robot applications.
title: Cloudroid: Cloud Framework Transparent QoS-aware Robotic Computation Outsourcing

text:
In the future, we will investigate
further ﬁne-grained QoS strategies in the computation out-
sourcing process and verify our solution by more real-world
applications.

Abstract—The Internet of Mobile Things encompasses stream 
data being generated by sensors, network communications that 
pull and push these data streams, as well as running processing 
and analytics that can effectively leverage actionable 
information for transportation planning, management, and 
business advantage.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Edge computing emerges as a new 
paradigm that decentralizes the communication, computation, 
control and storage resources from the cloud to the edge of the 
network.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
This paper proposes an edge computing platform 
where mobile edge nodes are physical devices deployed on a 
transit bus where descriptive analytics is used to uncover 
meaningful patterns from real-time transit data streams.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
An 
application experiment is used to evaluate the advantages and 
disadvantages of our proposed platform to support descriptive 
analytics at a mobile edge node and generate actionable 
information to transit managers.

INTRODUCTION 
The fast growing of data streams generated by the 
Internet of Mobile Things (IoMT) poses several challenges 
in pulling this data from IoMT devices to remote clouds.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
[1] points out that one critical challenge 
in building the next generation of intelligent transportation 
systems is related to the harsh communication environment 
inside and/or outside a moving vehicle.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Solutions for 
vehicle-to-sensor, vehicle-to-vehicle, and vehicle-to-road 
infrastructure connectivity are stringently dependent on 
latency and reliability for controlling and monitoring 
purposes.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Moreover, mobility applications usually require 
seamlessly computation, storage, and connection services 
over a vast geographical area (e.g.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
entire transit system), 
challenging the network communication technology used 
between sensors and the core network in terms of issues such 
as becoming unreliable and error-prone as well as requiring 
an extensive amount of data storage [2].
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Finally, developing 
the appropriate analytical workflow for leveraging the data 
streams generated by moving vehicles in order to produce 
active information for decision making is still a challenge 
since the data streams might be unbounded, noisy, and 
incomplete.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Due to the unpredictable network latency, expensive 
bandwidth, resource-prohibitive and location-awareness 
concerns of the Internet of Mobile Things, edge computing 
emerges as a new paradigm that decentralizes the 
communication, computation, control and storage resources 
to the edge of the Internet [3]–[5].
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
For current transit 
network systems that produce a vast volume of data streams 
in real-time, edge computing brings the opportunity to 
analyze massive data streams related to any vehicle of a fleet 
at the time the data is being collected and deliver actionable 
information to support tactical and operational decisions of 
transit managers [6].
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Some examples in public transit 
analytics include computing the actual maximum/minimum 
transit route length, service demand frequency, and 
predicting dynamic bus stops in real-time.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Despite the advantages of edge computing, no previous 
research work could be found in the literature on building 
edge analytics platforms for supporting transit network 
systems.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
This paper proposes an edge computing platform 
where mobile edge nodes are physical devices deployed on a 
transit bus where descriptive analytics is implemented to 
analyze real-time transit data streams.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
The main contributions of this paper are summarized as 
follows.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
• 
We present an edge computing architecture that 
supports mobile edge nodes, i.e.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
edge nodes that are 
deployed inside a vehicle, in our case, a bus 
belonging to a transit network system.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
• 
We develop a set of descriptive analytics tasks to 
analyze real-time transit data streams at the edge of 
a network.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
• 
We run a real-time experiment to evaluate the 
advantages and disadvantages of our proposed 
platform to support transit managers with actionable 
information.

EDGE ANALYTICS PLATFORM 
Our edge computing platform consists of a mobile edge 
node.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
The main scenario can be described as a moving bus 
that generates real-time data streams (e.g.

text:
Automatic Vehicle 
Location (AVL) data feeds) which are fetched by a mobile 
edge node installed in this bus.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
The platform supports 
running different descriptive analytics tasks at the mobile 
edge node meanwhile the bus moves around a city.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Once the 
analytical results are generated, they provide actionable 
information about what is happening to a moving bus.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
The 
stream data lifecycle in our platform supports data pre-
processing tasks as well.

Real-Time Data Streaming  
The real-time data streams used in this research were 
provided by Codiac Transit which is responsible for 
delivering efficient transportation services with the aim to 
reduce private car dependency in the metropolitan area of 
Greater Moncton, Canada.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Codiac Transit currently operates 
30 regular routes from Monday to Saturday, some of which 
having additional evening and Sunday services.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Each bus is 
equipped with GPS receivers which generate geographic 
coordinates of the location of a bus every 5 seconds for each 
bus trip.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Moreover, telemetry data is generated with a total of 
17 data fields, including route name, trip identifier, start and 
finish time of a trip.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
The location and telemetry data is 
transmitted to the mobile edge node using 4G LTE Dual 
SIM.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
The bus route 51 was selected for evaluating our edge 
computing platform because it has the highest trip density 
during a day.

Mobile Edge Node 
Every bus running on route 51 generates 17 data fields 
every 5 seconds which are sent to its mobile edge node 
installed inside the bus.

text:
In this experiment, the mobile edge 
node known as Cisco IR829 Industrial Integrated Services 
Router was used, having an Intel Atom Processor C2308 
(1M Cache, 1.25 GHz) Dual Core X86 64bit, 2GB DDR3 
memory, 8MB SPI Bootflash, 8GB (4GB usable) eMMC

and IEEE 802.11a/b/g/n WLAN connections.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
It is resistant to 
shock, vibration, dust, humidity, and water spray, and a wide 
temperature range (-40°C to +60°C and type-tested at +85°C 
for 16 hours) [26].

text:
This mobile edge node comes with two operating 
systems, a Cisco IOS system that runs a standard Cisco IOS 
package which handles all routing, switching and networking 
traffic and a guest operating system IOx running on a virtual 
machine.

text:
The guest operating system IOx runs Linux Yocto 
which is used to perform the descriptive analytical tasks 
described in Section III.D.

text:
However, it is important to point 
out that developing analytical tasks for the mobile edge 
nodes involves a trade-off between analytical complexity and 
processing power.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Furthermore, it involves orchestrating 
highly dynamic, heterogeneous resources at different levels 
of network hierarchy to support low latency and scalability 
requirements of transit services.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Data Pre-Processing at the Mobile Edge Node  
When the data streams arrive online at the mobile edge 
node, they are potentially unbounded in size and data tuples 
may not come in the order.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
The data streams need to be pre-
processed in order to remove errors and inconsistencies.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
It is 
very difficult to ensure data quality for the continuous and 
high volume of data streams, and performing a pre-
processing task automatically is even more challenging 
because the streaming rate is highly dynamic.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
We 
implemented a Python script algorithm to handle five 
automated steps for dealing with (1) missing tuples, (2) 
duplicated tuples, (3) missing attribute values, (4) redundant 
attributes, and (5) wrong attribute values.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
1) Missing tuples: Too many missing tuples may affect 
to the final analytical results in the latter stages.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
So, we 
eliminated any bus trip that has in total 100 missing tuples 
and more.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
2) Duplicated tuples: When the data stream arrived at 
the edge node, the data tuples is sometimes transmitted 
twice or more.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
In this case, any duplicated tuple is 
automatically found using its timestamp and then removed.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
3) Missing attribute values: At arriving at the edge, each 
data tuple contains 17 data fields.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
However, it may arrive 
with less than 17.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
So, we fill up the missing field with 
“N/A” if it does not involve directly in the latter analytical 
task.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
4) Redundant Attributes: Opposing with the missing 
attribute values case, this case happens when new data field 
is introduced to the data tuple.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
In this case, the extra 
attribute is automatically deleted.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
5) Wrong attribute values: Any attribute might also 
contain a wrong value due to misspelling, illegal values, and 
uniqueness violation.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
In this case, the algorithm first try to 
standardize the wrong information.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Descriptive Analytics at the Mobile Edge Node  
Three descriptive analytical tasks have been developed to 
reduce the burden on the data hub as well as avoid 
bottlenecks due to lower network bandwidth.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
First, each data 
stream that arrives at the mobile edge node is immediately 
computed following a sequence of analytical tasks described 
as one of the following:   
 
Task 1 - Semantic Annotation: The aim of this task is to 
determine whether a bus is moving or not.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
The GPS 
coordinates which are sent to the mobile edge node every 5 
seconds are used for this computation.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
In this case, a fixed 
distance value between two consecutive points is used for 
determining stops and moves (Fig.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
This value was 
empirically determined as being 15m for a transit network.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
If 
the distance between the previous point and the current point 
is more than 15m, the current point is annotated as a move.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
In contrast, if the distance is less than 15m, the current point 
is annotated as a stop.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Task 2 – Temporal Aggregation: At the end of each trip, 
this task computes the actual duration and length of the trip, 
the total number of stops, and the total number of moves.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Other data fields such as Trip Identifier, Date, and Start Time 
are also used for the temporal aggregation.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
In summary, five 
data fields (Trip Id, Date, Start_Time, Total_Move, 
Total_Stop, Total_Time_Length) are generated and sent 
periodically to the data hub located at the Codiac Transit’s 
operation center through the telecommunication network at 
the end of each trip.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Computation of Moves and Stops of a moving bus 
 
Task 3 – Summary Function: It is used to compute the 
average trip time in the morning (5h-12h), afternoon (13h-
18h), and evening (19h-24h).
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Besides, the average of the 
total number of moves is also computed for the different 
times of the day (i.e.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
The same 
function is also used to compute all the stops.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Once the 


 
statistics are computed they are sent to the data hub located 
at the Codiac Transit’s operation center through the 
telecommunication network at the end of the day.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
During the 
week, these data could be further analyzed at the data hub for 
understanding the different mobility patterns during the 
week.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text: All the tasks have been implemented in Python 2.7.13.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
There are several basic libraries exploited such as time, 
timedate, csv.
title: Developing an edge computing platform for real-time descriptive analytics

text:
Besides, the library haversine was utilized to 
calculate the great-circle distance between two locations on 
the Earth surface.

title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
INTRODUCTION 
Mobility analytics using data generated from the Internet of 
Mobile Things (IoMT) is facing many challenges which range from 
the ingestion of data streams coming from a vast number of fog 
nodes and IoMT devices to avoiding overflowing the cloud with 
useless massive data streams that can trigger bottlenecks [1].
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Managing data flow is becoming an important part of the IoMT 
because it will dictate in which platform analytical tasks should run 
in the future.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Data flows are usually a sequence of out-of-order 
tuples with a high data input rate, and mobility analytics requires a 
real-time flow of data in both directions, from the edge to the cloud, 
and vice-versa.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Before pulling the data streams to the cloud, edge 
data stream processing is needed for detecting missing, broken, and 
duplicated tuples in addition to recognize tuples whose arrival time 
is out of order.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Analytical tasks such as data filtering, data cleaning 
and low-level data contextualization can be executed at the edge of 
a network.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
In contrast, more complex analytical tasks such as graph 
processing can be deployed in the cloud, and the results of ad-hoc 
queries and streaming graph analytics can be pushed to the edge as 
needed by a user application.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Graphs are efficient representations 
used in mobility analytics because they unify knowledge about 
connectivity, proximity and interaction among moving things.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
This poster describes the preliminary results from our 
experimental prototype developed for supporting transit systems, 
in which edge and cloud computing are combined to process transit 
data streams forwarded from fog nodes into a cloud.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The 
motivation of this research is to understand how to perform 
meaningfulness mobility analytics on transit feeds by combining 
cloud and fog computing architectures in order to improve fleet 
management, mass transit and remote asset monitoring [2].
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE 
Our prototype system architecture is shown in Fig.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
1 and 
consists of three-layers named as Fog Node Cluster (sensing layer), 
Aggregated Fog Node (access layer) and Cloud (core layer).
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The 
fog node cluster is a group of mobile fog nodes that pull data from 
sensors deployed in a transit vehicle.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Each mobile fog node is 
designed to be installed inside a transit vehicle belonging to a 
transit fleet.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The Cisco 829 GW-LTE-NA-AK9 was selected for the 
experiment because is designed for harsh environments including 
shock, humidity, and wide temperature range.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The transit data 
streams contain information including bus route identifier, bus 
route number, vehicle identifier, GPS coordinates and timestamp 
that are generated at different time granularities, including every 
5s, every 30min, or every day (Fig 2.) 
We selected an aggregated fog node for running the Edge Fog 
Fabric (EFF) platform in order to pass the data streams from the 
mobile fog node cluster to the cloud, and vice-versa [3].
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The EFF 
manages and ensures that there is an appropriate flow of unbounded 
tuples in both directions, and perform analytical tasks such as 
filtering, cleaning and contextualization.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The EFF is basically 
composed by a system administrator, dataflow editor and engine, 
system monitor, message broker, links, and IoT database (i.e.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text: The cloud is the core layer where the Neo4j database is situated.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
It is the place where mobility analytics is conducted based on the 
compressed and post-processed data coming from the EFF.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The 
mobility analytics is carried out using an integrated Apache Spark 
GraphX engine and Neo4J.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
2 illustrates the life cycle that takes place every time the 
tuples flow through the system, from the mobile fog nodes to the 
cloud.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
It consists of six steps: the data transportation, the data 
processing, the data leverage, the data control, the data acquisition, 
and the data storage.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Every tuple is sent (data transportation) and 
received by the destination mobile fog nodes (data acquisition).
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
After that, in order to process the tuple (data processing) and 
perform mobility analytics, the EFF controls the sets of tuples (data 
control)  by retaining (data storage) and retrieving (data leverage) 
them continuously.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
All the steps related in this life cycle of our 
prototype are operated through the ParStream [3].
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text: Life cycle for IoMT of the experimental system.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
People in Motion Lab, University of New Brunswick  
15 Dineen Drive, Fredericton, NB.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
MOBILITY ANALYTICS 
The mobility analytical workflow consists of: (1) data cleaning 
tasks deployed at the mobile fog nodes (sensing layer); (2) data 
contextualization tasks performed at the aggregated fog node 
(access layer), and (3) graph query running in the cloud (core layer).
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Data cleaning is always necessary in order to remove errors and 
inconsistencies from the tuples.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The data cleaning task is 
implemented using a Python script algorithm for processing five 
automated steps to handle (1) missing tuples, (2) duplicated tuples, 
(3) missing attribute values, (4) redundant attributes, and (5) 
wrong attribute values [5].
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The data contextualization task enriches the tuples from the 
previous data cleaning task using higher level concepts accordingly 
to a particular mobility context.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
In the current prototype, the 
geographical coordinates (x, y) and the timestamp t of each tuple 
are used for this contextualization.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
First, an empirical distance 
value of 15m is designated to compute stops and moves.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Second, 
the Euclidean distance between two consecutive points (i.e.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
If the distance between them is smaller than 15m, a 
new attribute containing the value “stop” is added to the second 
tuple.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
In contrast, if the distance is higher than 15m, the “move” 
attribute value is added to the second tuple.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Finally, time-varying graph queries using graph metrics such as 
shortest path, degree and page rank centrality are run in a Neo4j 
database in the cloud, which includes a master node and slave nodes 
that were deployed using the Compute Canada West Cloud [6].
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The 
query outputs are essentially a time-series of static graph snapshots 
based on a time tree, which is effective for online mobility analytics 
of large temporal graphs where handling speed and complexity is 
at the most importance.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
PRELIMINARY RESULTS 
The transit feeds generated by CODIAC transit network for the 
Greater Moncton area was used for the implementation of our 
prototype system.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The transit fleet consists of 642 bus stations 
belonging to 30 bus routes operating from Monday to Saturday, 
some of which also providing evening and Sunday services.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
3 shows the results after running a shortest-path query and 
retrieving the shortest bus trips at different peak hours on June 8th 
2016.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
In this figure, red nodes represent stops which might occur 
because of a traffic jam, accident, collecting passengers at a bus 
station, or a traffic light at one street intersection.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Green nodes 
represent moves that occur because a bus is moving on a street or 
passing by a bus station because there are no passengers to drop off 
or get on.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text: The trip dynamics of the same bus route over time.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
4 shows the degree and Page Rank query results for 
retrieving information about the dynamics of the bus stations of a 
bus route.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The largest number of stops (red nodes) clustered around 
a bus station (grey nodes) indicates where stopovers have occurred 
for collecting and dropping passengers.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The page rank score results 
show the busiest stations as being the ones located at the Plaza, 
Champlain Street and Main Street.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The moves (green nodes) shows 
the bus stations where buses passed by a bus station because there 
were no passengers to drop off or get on.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
FUTURE RESEARCHWORK 
This paper describes the potential of mobility analytics to be 
performed over data streams based on the concept of light-weight 
data processing at the edge, and heavy graph processing in the 
cloud.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The preliminary results are positive in paving the way for 
developing edge-cloud system architectures that can support data 
flows for specific purposes, e.g.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
a dataflow for processing, a 
dataflow for data storage, and a dataflow for data ingestion.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
Each 
dataflow must be designed taking into account a mobility analytics 
task.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text: We have implemented only one single dataflow (i.e.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
from 
mobile fog nodes to the cloud), therefore future research work will 
be focused on both directions.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
We have also implemented the EFF 
platform at the access layer, but we expect to deploy it at the other 
layers as well.
title: Combining edge and cloud computing for mobility analytics

text:
The research challenge will be to design a coherent 
mobility analytical workflow which can handle the scalability, 
speed and complexity issues of data streams.

to overcome many barriers, such as: 1) There is an increasing demand for data storage on cloud servers where the
analysis of the medical big data becomes increasingly complex; 2) The data, when communicated, are vulnerable to
security and privacy issues; 3) The communication of the continuously collected data is not only costly but also energy
hungry; 4) Operating and maintaining the sensors directly from the cloud servers are non-trial tasks.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: This book chapter deﬁned Fog Computing in the context of medical IoT.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Conceptually, Fog Computing is a service-
oriented intermediate layer in IoT, providing the interfaces between the sensors and cloud servers for facilitating con-
nectivity, data transfer, and queryable local database.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The centerpiece of Fog computing is a low-power, intelligent,
wireless, embedded computing node that carries out signal conditioning and data analytics on raw data collected from
wearables or other medical sensors and offers efﬁcient means to serve telehealth interventions.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We implemented and
tested an fog computing system using the Intel Edison and Raspberry Pi that allows acquisition, computing, storage
and communication of the various medical data such as pathological speech data of individuals with speech disorders,
Phonocardiogram (PCG) signal for heart rate estimation, and Electrocardiogram (ECG)-based Q, R, S detection.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The
book chapter ends with experiments and results showing how fog computing could lessen the obstacles of existing
cloud-driven medical IoT solutions and enhance the overall performance of the system in terms of computing intelli-
gence, transmission, storage, conﬁgurable, and security.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The case studies on various types of physiological data shows
that the proposed Fog architecture could be used for signal enhancement, processing and analysis of various types of
bio-signals.

2.1
Wearable Big Data in Healthcare
The medical data is collected by the intelligent edge devices such as wearables, wrist-bands, smartwatches,
smart textiles etc..
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The intelligence refers to knowledge of analytics, devices, clinical application and the con-
sumer behavior.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

Such smart data is structured, homogeneous and meaningful with negligible amount of noise
and meta-data [1].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The big data and quiet recently smart data trend had revolutionized the biomedical and
healthcare domain.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
With increasing use of wireless and wearable body sensor networks (BSNs), the amount of
data aggregated by edge devices and synced to the cloud is growing at enormous rate [32].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The pharmaceutical
companies are leveraging deep learning and data analytics on their huge medical databases.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
These databases
are results of digitization of patient’s medical records.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The data obtained from patient’s health records, clini-
cal trials and insurance programs provided an opportunity for data mining.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Such databases are heterogeneous,
unstructured, scalable and contain signiﬁcant amount of noise and meta-data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The noise and meta-data have
low or no useful information.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Cleaning and structuring the real-world data is another challenge in processing
medical big data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
In recent years, the big data trend had transformed the healthcare, wellness and ﬁtness in-
dustry.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Adding value and innovation in data processing chain could help patients and healthcare stakeholders
accomplish the treatment goals in lower cost with reduced logistic requirements [32].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Authors in [46] presented
the smart data as a result of using semantic web and data analytics on structured collection of big data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Smart
data attempts to provide a superior avenue for better decision and inexpensive processing for person-centered
medicine and healthcare.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The medical data such as diagnostic images, genetic test results and biometric in-
formation are getting generated at large scale.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Such data has not just the high volume but also a wide variety
and different velocity.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
It necessitates the novel ways for storing, managing, retrieving and processing such
data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The smart medical data demand development of novel scalable big data architecture and applicable algo-
rithms for intelligent data analytics.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Authors also underlined the challenges in semantic-rich data processing
for intelligent inference on practical use cases [46].

text: Speech Disorders affected approximately 7.5 million people in US [2].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Dysarthria (caused by Parkinson’s
disease or other speech disorders) refers to motor speech disorder resulting from impairments in human speech
production system.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: The speech production system consists of the lips, tongue, vocal folds, and/or diaphragm.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Depending on the part of nervous system that is affected, there are various types of dysarthria.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The patients
with dysarthria posses speciﬁc speech characteristics such as difﬁcult to understand speech, limited movement
in lips, tongue and jaw, abnormal pitch and rhythm.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
It also includes poor voice quality, for instance, hoarse,
breathy or nasal voice.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Dysarthria results from neural dysfunction.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
It might happen at birth (cerebral palsy) or
developed later in person’s life.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
It can be due to variety of ailments in the nervous system, such as Motor neu-
ron diseases, Alzheimer’s disease, Cerebral Palsy (CP), Huntington’s disease, Multiple Sclerosis, Parkinson’s
disease (PD), Traumatic brain injury (TBI), Mental health issues, Stroke, Progressive neurological conditions,
Cancer of the head, neck and throat (including laryngectomy).
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The patients with dysarthria are subjectively
evaluated by the speech-language pathologist (SLP) who identiﬁes the speech difﬁculties and decide the type
and severity of the communication deﬁcit [20].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Authors in [48] compared the perceived loudness of speech and self-perception of speech in patients with
idiopathic Parkinson’s disease (PD) with healthy controls.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Thirty patients with PD and fourteen healthy controls
participated in the research survey.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Various speech tasks were performed and nine speech and voice character-
istics were used for evaluation.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Results showed that the patients with PD had signiﬁcant reduction in loudness
as compared to healthy controls during various speech tasks.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
These results furnished additional information on
speech characteristics of patients with PD that might be useful for effective speech treatment of such popula-
tion [48].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Authors in [28] studied the acoustic characteristics of voice in patients with PD.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Thirty patients with
early stage PD and thirty patients with later stage PD were compared with thirty healthy controls for acoustic
characteristics of the voice.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: The speech task included sustained /a/ and one minute monologue.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The voice of
patients with early as well as later stage PD were found to have reduced loudness, limited loudness and pitch
variability, breathiness, and harshness.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
In general, the voice of patients with PD had lower mean intensity levels
and reduced maximum phonational frequency range as compared to healthy controls [28].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Authors in [50] studied and evaluated the voice and speech quality in patients with and without deep brain
stimulation of the subthalamic nucleus (STN-DBS) before and after LSVT LOUD therapy.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The goal of the
study was to do a comparative study of improvement in surgical patients as compared to the non-surgical
ones.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Results showed that the LSVT LOUD is recommended for voice and speech treatment of patients with
PD following STN-DBS surgery.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Authors in [22] performed acoustic analysis of voice from 41 patients with
PD and healthy controls.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The speech exercises included in the study were the sustained /a/ for two seconds
and reading sentences.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The acoustic measures for quantifying the speech quality were fundamental frequency,
perturbation in fundamental frequency, shimmer, and harmonic to noise ratio of the sustained /a/, phonation
range, dynamic range, and maximum phonation time.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Authors concluded that the patients with PD had higher
jitter, lower harmonics to noise ratio, lower frequency and intensity variability, lower phonation range, the
presence of low voice intensity, mono pitch, voice arrests, and struggle irrespective of the severity of the PD
symptoms.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: People suffering from Parkinson’s disease experience speech production difﬁculty associated with Dysarthria.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Dysarthria is characterized by monotony of pitch, reduced loudness, an irregular rate of speech and, imprecise
consonants and changes in voice quality [36].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Speech-language pathologists do the evaluation, diagnosis and
treat communication disorders.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Literature suggests that Lee Silverman Voice Treatment (LSVT) has been most
efﬁcient behavioral treatment for voice and speech disorders in Parkinson’s disease.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Telehealth monitoring is
very effective for the speech-language pathology, and smart devices like EchoWear [16] can be of much use in
such situations.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Several cues indicate the relationship of dysarthria and acoustic features.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Shallower F2 trajectories in male speakers with dysarthria is observed in [33].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Vowel space area was found to be reduced relative to healthy controls for male speakers with amyotrophic
lateral sclerosis [33].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Shimmers as described in [17] as a measure of variation in amplitude of the speech and it is an important
speech quality metric for people with speech disorders.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Like shimmers, Jitters (pitch variations) and loudness and sharpness of the speech signal can be used as a
cue for speech disorders [17].

3.1
Fog Computing Device
To transfer the audio ﬁle/other data ﬁle from a patient, we used socket streaming using TCP wrapped in Secure
Socket Layer/ Transmission Layer Security (SSL/TLS) sockets to ensure the secure transmission.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Sockets
provide communication framework for devices using different protocols such as TCP and UDP that could then
be wrapped in secured sockets.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Next, we describe these protocols and their usage in the proposed architecture.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
– Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) is a networking protocol that allows guaranteed and reliable de-
livery of ﬁles.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: It is a connection-oriented and bi-directional protocol.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
In other words, both devices could
send and receive ﬁles using this protocol.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Each point of the connection involved Internet Protocol (IP)
address and a port number so the connection could be made with a speciﬁc device.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Furthermore, we
wrapped the TCP sockets in SSL Sockets for ensuring the security and privacy of the data collected from
the users/patients.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
– Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) is a network communication protocol that allows encrypted authentication
for network sockets from the server and client sides.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
To implement it in the proposed Fog architecture, we
used two python modules, namely SSL and socket.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
To create the certiﬁcations for the server and client,
we also used the command line program called OpenSSL [42].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
OpenSSL is an open-source project that
provides a robust, commercial-grade, and full-featured toolkit for the Transport Layer Security (TLS) and
Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) protocols.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Once all the SSL certiﬁcation keys were built for client (the Android gateway devices/wearables) and server
(Fog computer e.g., Intel Edison or Raspberry Pi), we ran the secure sockets on the server and continuously
listened for a connection for ﬁle transfer.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We renamed the ﬁle with date and time stamps before it could be used
for further processing.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
As soon as the audio ﬁle was completely transferred, the connection was closed and
the processing began.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We used the python based Praat and Christian’s Library described for processing and
analysis of audio data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
For other healthcare data such as Phonocardiography (PCG) data and Electrocardiogram
(ECG) data etc., we implemented the associated methods using Python, C and GNU Octave.

3.5
Dynamic Time Warping
Dynamic time warping (DTW) is an algorithm for ﬁnding similar patterns in a time-series data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
DTW has been
used for time-series mining for a variety of applications such as business, ﬁnance, single word recognition,
walking pattern detection, and analysis of ECG signals.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Usually, we use Euclidean distance to measure the
distance between two points.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
For example, consider two vectors , x = [x1,x2,...,xn] and y = [y1,y2,...,yn]
d(x,y) =
q
(x1 −y1)2 +(x2 −y2)2 +(·xn −yn)2
(1)
Euclidean distance works well in many areas.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
But for some special case where two similar and out-of-phase se-
ries are to be compared, Euclidean distance fails to detect similarity.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
For example, consider two time series A =

In addition, there were no noise reduction done in previous stud-

The patholog-

Figure 14 shows the block diagram of pathological

text:
In our earlier studies, we computed features from the controlled clinical environ-
ment and performed Fog device trails in lab scenarios [19].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: This paper explored the in-home ﬁeld application.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: In-clinic speech data was obtained in quiet scenarios with negligible background noise.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
On the other hand, data
from in-home trials had huge amounts of time-varying non-stationary noise.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
It necessitated the use of robust
algorithms for noise reduction before extracting the pathological features.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
In addition to previously studied
features such as loudness and fundamental frequency, we developed more features for accurate quantiﬁcation
of abnormalities in patient’s vocalization.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The new features are jitter, frequency modulation, speech rate and
sensory pleasantness.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
In our previous studies, we use just three speech exercises (tasks t1, t2 and t3) for analysis
of algorithms.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: In this paper, we incorporated all six speech exercises.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The execution was done in real-time in
patient’s home unlike pilot data used in our previous studies [19,40].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Thus, Fog speech processing module is
an advancement over earlier studies in [16,19,40].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: The audio data was acquired and stored in wav format.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Using perceptual audio coding such as mp3 would
have saved transmission power, storage and execution time as the size of mp3 coded speech data is lower than
corresponding wav format.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The reason for not using mp3 or other advanced audio codecs is to avoid loss of
information.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Perceptual audio codes such as mp3 are lossy compression scheme that removes frequency bands
that are not perceptually important.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Such codecs have worked well for music and audio streaming.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
However,
in pathological speech analysis, patients have very acute vocalizations such as nasal voice, hypernasal voice,
mildly slurred speech, monotone voice etc..
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Clinicians do not recommend lossy coding for speech data as it
can cause confusion in diagnosis, monitoring, and evaluation of pathological voice.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Since we use the unicast
transmission from BSNs to fog computers, we employed Transmission Control Protocol (TCP).
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The data have
to be received in the same order as sent by BSNs.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We did not use User Datagram Protocol (UDP) that is more
popular for audio/video streaming as UDP does not guarantee receipt of packets.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
For videos/audios that are
perceptually encoded and decoded, small losses lead to temporary degradation in received audio/video.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We do
not have that luxury in pathological speech or PCG data that have to be guaranteed delivery even if delayed
and/or have to be re-transmitted.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The pathological data was saved as mono-channel audio sampled at 44.1 kHz
with 16-bit precision in .wav format.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Background Noise Reduction The audio signals from in-home speech exercises are highly contaminated with
time-varying background noise.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Authors developed a method for reducing non-stationary noise in speech [12].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: The audio signal is enhanced using noise estimates obtained from minima controlled recursive averaging.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We
performed a subjective evaluation for validating the suitability of this algorithm for our data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The enhanced
speech was later used for extracting perceptual speech features such as loudness, fundamental frequency, jitter,
frequency modulation, speech rate and sensory pleasantness (sharpness).
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We used the method developed in [12]
for reducing non-stationary background noise in speech.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
It optimized the log-spectral amplitude of the speech
using noise estimates from minima-controlled recursive averaging.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Authors used two functions for accounting
the probability of speech presence in various sub-bands.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
One of these functions was based on the time frequency
distribution of apriori signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and was used for estimation of the speech spectrum.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The
second function was decided by the ratio of the energy of noisy speech segment and its minimum value within
that time window.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Objective, as well as subjective evaluation, illustrated that this algorithm could preserve
the weak speech segments contaminated with a high amount of noise [12].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Figure 7 shows the spectrogram
of acquired speech signal from in-home trials and the spectrogram of corresponding enhanced speech signal.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Speech enhancement is clearly visible in the darker regions (corresponding to speech) and noise reduction in
lighter regions (corresponding to silences/pauses).
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Automated Trimming of the Speech Signal We used the method developed in [52] for automated trimming
of audio ﬁles by removing the non-speech segments.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
This method was validated to be accurate even at low
SNRs that is typical for in-home audio data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The low computational complexity of this algorithm qualiﬁes
it for implementation on Fog device with limited resources.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
After applying the noise reduction method on
acquired speech signal, we used voice activity detection (VAD) algorithm for removing the silences.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Authors
in [52] proposed a simple technique for VAD based on an effective selection of speech frames.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The short time-
windows of a speech signal are stationary (for 25-40 ms windows).
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
However, for an extended time duration

Fundamental Frequency Estimation We used the method proposed in [27] for estimation of the fundamental
frequency.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: It was found to be effective even at very low SNRs.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
It is a frequency-domain method referred as
Pitch Estimation Filter with Amplitude Compression (PEFAC).
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We used 25 ms time-windows with 10 ms
skip-rate for estimation of the fundamental frequency.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
In the ﬁrst step, noise components were suppressed
by compressing the speech amplitude.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
In the second step, the speech was ﬁltered such that the energy of
harmonics was summed.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Noise Reduction in PCG data The PCG signal was acquired at 800 Hz for capturing high ﬁdelity data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Some noise is inherently present in data collected using wearable PCG sensors.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We do low pass ﬁltering
using a sixth-order Butterworth ﬁlter with a cutoff frequency of 100 Hz.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
It reduces the noise leaving behind
spectral components of cardiac cycle.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We downsampled the low-pass ﬁltered signal to reduce the computational
complexity.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Teager Energy Operator for Envelope Extraction Teager Energy Operator (TEO) is a nonlinear energy
function [31].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: TEO captures the signal energy based on physical and mechanical aspects of signal production.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: It has been successfully in various applications [37,35].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
For a discrete signal x[n], it is given by
Ψ(x[n]) = x[n]∗x[n]−x[n+1]∗x[n−1]
(10)
where Ψ(x[n]) is the TEO corresponding to the sample x[n].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We applied TEO on the downsampled signal
(see Figure 17) to extract the envelope.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: The TEO output is further smoothed using Savitzky-Golay ﬁltering.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Savitzky-Golay ﬁlters are polynomial ﬁlters that achieve least-squares smoothing.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
These ﬁlters performed bet-
ter than standard ﬁnite impulse response (FIR) smoothing ﬁlters.

Heart Rate Estimation by Segmentation of Heart Sounds S1 The heart sound S1 marks the start of the
systole.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: It is generated by closure of mitral and tricuspid valves that cause blood ﬂow from atria to ventricle.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: It happens when blood has returned from the body and lungs.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The heart sound S2 marks the the end of systole
and the beginning of diastole.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
It is generated upon closure of aortic and pulmonary valves following which the
blood moves from heart to the body and lungs.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Under still conditions, the average heart-sound duration are S1
(70-150ms) and S2 (60-120ms).

The cardiac cycle lasts for 800 ms where systolic period is around 300 ms and
diastolic period being 500 ms [54].
