4.3
Case Study III: Electrocardiogram (ECG) Monitoring
Heart diseases are one of the major chronic illness with a dramatic impact on productivity of affected individu-
als and related healthcare expenses.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
An ECG sub-system is considerably for more out-of-hospital applications,
manufacturers face continued pressure to reduce system cost and development time while maintaining or in-
creasing performance levels.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The electrocardiogram (ECG) is a diagnostic tool to assess the electrical and
muscular functions of the heart.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The ECG signal consists of components such as P wave, PR interval, RR inter-
val, QRS complex, pulse train, ST segment, T wave, QT interval and infrequent presence of U wave.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Presence
of arrhythmias changes QRS complex, RR interval and pulse train.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
For instance a narrow QRS complex (¡120
milliseconds) indicates rapid activation of the ventricles that in turn suggests that the arrhythmia originates
above or within the his bundle (supraventricular tachycardia) and a wide QRS (greater than 120 milliseconds)
occurs when ventricular activation is abnormally slow.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The most common reason for a wide QRS complex is
arrhythmia of the ventricular myocardium (e.g., ventricular tachycardia) [5].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Figure 21 shows ECG time series
with P wave, T wave and QRS complex.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
These three patterns are search using DTW for a large number of ECG
data sets.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The last section of this case study will discuss the data reduction using DTW and GNU zip compres-
sion on ECG data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The goal of our experiment is to detect arrhythmic ECG beats or QRS changes using QRS
complex and the RR interval measurements.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The ECG data is fed to the Fog computer from Internet-based
database.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The Fog computer extracts QRS complex from ECG signals using real-time signal processing im-
plemented in Python on Intel Edison.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: The Pan Tompkins algorithm is used for detection of QRS complex [45].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Pan-Tompkins algorithm consists of ﬁve steps:
Band Pass Filtering The energy contained in QRS complex is approximated in 5-15 Hz range [5].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We apply
a band pass ﬁlter for extracting 5- 15 Hz content of ECG signals.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The band pass ﬁlter reduces muscle noise, 60
Hz power-line interference, baseline wandering and T wave interference.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
This ﬁlter achieve a 3dB pass-band
from about 5-12 Hz.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The high-pass ﬁlter is designed by subtracting the output of ﬁrst-order low-pass ﬁlter from
an all-pass ﬁlter with delay of 16 samples (80ms) [45].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: Derivation The output of band-pass ﬁlter is differentiated to get the slope.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
After
differentiation, the output signal is squared to get only positive values.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
It performs non-linear ampliﬁcation of
the output suppressing the values lower than 1.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: A moving-window integration is applied on output of last step.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: It smoothens the output resulting in multiple peaks within duration of QRS complex.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
It adapts to changes in the
ECG signal by estimating the signal and noise peaks for ﬁnding the R-peaks (Figure 22).
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The Pan-Tompkins
based QRS detection is implemented on ECG signals obtained from MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database [4].
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Fig-
ure 22 illustrates the QRS detection using Pan-Tomkins algorithm on Intel Edison using MIT-BIH Arrhythmia
data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: The ECG signal containing 2160 samples take 1 second of processing time on Intel Edison Fog computer.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: It shows that proposed Fog architecture is well suited for real-time ECG monitoring.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We used DTW based
pattern mining for P wave, T wave and QRS complex in ECG data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The DTW indices showing the location

Intel Edison Description
The Intel Edison platform used in this application was designed with a core system consisting of dual-core,
dual-threaded Intel Atom CPU at 500MHz and a 32-bit Intel Quark microcontroller at 100MHz, along with
connectivity interfaces capable of Bluetooth 4.0 and dual-band IEEE 802.11a/b/g/n via an on-board chip an-
tenna.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
This platform came with a Linux environment called Yocto, which is not an embedded distribution of
Linux itself, its true purpose is to provide an environment to develop a custom Linux distribution.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We did not
create a Linux distribution, instead we deployed a prebuilt distribution of Debian/Jessie for 32-bit systems.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
This decision was made such that we could deploy the same environment on both the Intel Edison and the
Raspberry Pi.

Fog Computing: Feature Extraction on Fog devices
The fog devices, the Intel Edison and Raspberry Pi, were both conﬁgured to run the same Debian/Jessie i386

that both gateway devices tracking system performance using the same tools.

Linux program top and the Octave function Proﬁler.

Load, Memory Usage, and run-times for processes or threads being managed by the Linux kernel.

text:
This was
used later to provide use with benchmarking for the system overall.

text:
The Octave function Proﬁler provided
insights into the run-times for each of section of the algorithm.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
This was used later determine which parts of
the algorithm required more time to complete.

6.2
Compatibility Issues
There were countless instances when we had to ﬁnd unconventional ways to establish intelligence in Fog.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
For
example, installing Praat python library on the Intel Edison was extremely difﬁcult.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
6.3
Security & Privacy
In this work, we presented how the fog computer could be conﬁgured for computation and database access.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We
also touched upon Fog security from the authenticated access point-of-view.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
However, we believe that security
needs can be addressed more rigorously since Fog allows us to conﬁgure the fog computing node remotely and
inject algorithms that could make the communication and storage more secure.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
6.4
Challenges in using Fog computing for Telemedicine
No system is perfect and fog computing is no exception.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
There are difﬁculties in deploying Fog architecture for
telemedicine applications.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Although the fog computing provides the data computation on the edge, reducing
the data signiﬁcantly, the data becomes non-reversible when only analytics are communicated to the cloud.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The
fog has a limited storage space such that it can only store data for days or weeks, depending on the type of data.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: In our case, the data were audio ﬁles that could easily exceed the storage limit on the fog within a few days.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
An alternative is to create a query mechanism to access the data on fog when the clinicians want to listen to the
audio ﬁles.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Furthermore, since the raw data was not communicated to the cloud, there was no way to perform
additional analysis in the cloud.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
In other words, it is necessary to ensure the reliability of the computational
models used for analysis of the data before they are injected into the fog computing resources.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
7
Conclusions
We presented a multi-layer telemedicine architecture of the fog-assisted Medical Internet-of-things that was
implemented on Intel Edison with layers for hardware, middleware (communication and software), and appli-
cation (with security services).
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
The Fog framework achieves intelligent gateway functions by processing audio
ﬁles using signal processing algorithms such as psychoacoustic analysis to extract the clinical features; storage
of raw data and features that are on-demand queryable by the cloud as well as the Fog interface.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
We also im-
plemented Android apps for stakeholders such as patients, healthcare providers and administrators who require
access to the backend database.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
This enabled speech-language pathologists (SLPs) to query the data showing
daily progress of their patients.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Our case study demonstrated that managing computations on Intel Edison (fog
computer) reduces the data by 99%; though less data reduction would occur if more features were analyzed.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Our study also showed that it is possible to perform high-ﬁdelity signal processing on the fog device to extract
pathological speech features and communicate them to the cloud database.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
Moreover, the paper not only provides a high level understanding of the fog-based IoT system, but also
provides details of how each layer was implemented including the tools and libraries used in the develop-
ment.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
If implemented appropriately, Fog has a great potential to provide more autonomy and reliability in
telemedicine applications driven by IoT.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text: In future, we plan to deploy Fog in patient’s homes.
title: arXiv:1706.08012v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jun 2017

text:
This will help us
face operational challenges when the fog computer is located remotely in a different network.

Abstract.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The article is devoted to the veriﬁcation of the BSF parallel
computing model.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The BSF-model is an evolution of the ”master-slave”
model and SPMD-model.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The BSF-model is oriented to iterative algo-
rithms that are implemented in cluster computing systems.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The article
brieﬂy describes the basics of the BSF-model and its cost metrics.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The
structure of the BSF program is shown in the form of a UML activity di-
agram.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The simulator of BSF-programs, implemented in C++ language
using the MPI-library, is described.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The results of computational experi-
ments conﬁrming the adequacy of the cost metrics of the BSF-model are
presented.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
Keywords: parallel computational model · BSF · Bulk Synchronous
Farm · scalability · parallel eﬃciency · distributed memory multiproces-
sors · simulation · validation
1
Introduction
The Sunway TaihuLight is the fastest supercomputer in the world according to
the TOP500 List (edition of June 2017) [1].
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
It uses 40,960 processors, each of
which contains 260 processing cores.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017
arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
Analysis of the growth dynam-
ics of the performance of supercomputers (see Fig.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
1) shows that in 8-9 years
the most powerful supercomputer becomes an ordinary system, and that in 5-
6 years we can expect the appearance of exascale computing.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The emergence
of such powerful multiprocessor computing systems brings to the fore issues re-
lated to the development of frameworks (templates) that allow creating highly
scalable parallel programs oriented to systems with distributed memory.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
In this
context, the most important problem is the development of parallel computa-
tion models allowing to estimate the scalability of the algorithm at an early
stage of implementing.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
In paper [2], a new parallel computation model called
BSF (Bulk-Synchronous Farm) was proposed.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The BSF-model is an evolution of

title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
the ”master-slave” model and focused on iterative algorithms executing on the
cluster computing systems.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
In this paper, the issue concerning to a veriﬁcation
of the BSF model is discussed.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
Section 2
is the description of the BSF-model.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
In Section 3, a cost metric of BSF-model is
given.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
In Section 4, the simulator of BSF-programs is described and computa-
tional experiments conﬁrming the adequacy of the cost metrics of the BSF-model
are presented.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
In Section 5, the results are summarized and directions for further
research are outlined.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text: Performance dynamics of supercomputers in TOP500.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
2
BSF-model
Parallel computation model BSF (Bulk Synchronous Farm) was proposed in [2].
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text: It extends the Master-slave paradigm [3,4,5] and the BSP computational model [6].
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text: The BSF-model is oriented on multiprocessor systems.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
BSF-computer is a set of
homogeneous processor nodes with private memory connected by the network
that provides data transfer from one node to another.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
Among the processor


nodes, there is one called a master node.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
BSF-computer must have at least one master node and one slave node
(K ≥1).
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text: The architecture of the BSF-computer is shown in Fig.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text: BSF-computer works according to the SPMD programming model [4,7].
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
BSF-program consists of a sequence of macro-steps and global barrier synchro-
nizations.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
Each macro-step is divided into sections of two types: master sections
and slave sections.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The order of such sections within the macro-step is not sig-
niﬁcant.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The data processed by the particular slave is determined by the number
of its node.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text: BSF-program includes the following sequential sections (see Fig.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:

title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
Initialization is a macro-step, during which the master and slaves read or
generate input data.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The initialization is completed by a barrier synchroniza-
tion.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The iterative process repeatedly performs its body until the exit condition
checked by the master becomes true.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
In the ﬁnalization macro-step, the master
outputs the results and ends the program.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017
arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text: In the ﬁrst macro-step, the master sends the same orders to all the slaves.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text: Then, the slaves execute the received orders (the master is idle at that time).
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
All the slaves execute the same program code but act on the diﬀerent data with
the base address depending on the slave-node number.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text: It means that all slaves spend the same time for calculating.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
During process-
ing the order, there are no data transfers between nodes.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The last is an important
property of the BSF-model.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
In the third macro-step, all slaves send the results to
the master.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text: After that, global barrier synchronization is performed.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
During the
last macro-step of iterative process, the master evaluates received results.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
After result evaluations, the master checks the exit
condition.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
If the exit condition is true then iterative process is ﬁnished, otherwise
the iterative process is continued.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The outline of the BSF-program in form of
UML activity diagram is shown in Fig.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The BSF-model was designed for the scalable iterative numerical methods
that have a high computational complexity of iteration with relatively low cost
of communications.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
A scalable iterative method is a method that allows iteration
to be splitted into subtasks that do not require data exchanges.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
An example of
such a method can be found in [8].
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

4
Veriﬁcation of BSF-model
To verify the cost metrics of the BSF-model, a simulator of BSF-programs
was designed and implemented in C++ with MPI-library.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The source code of
the simulator is freely available on Github, at https://github.com/nadezhda-
ezhova/BSF-simulator.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The simulator uses SPMD-model and includes both the
master and slave sections.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The master section is performed if MPI_Comm_rank
returns 0.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The slave section is performed if MPI_Comm_rank returns a value
greater than 0.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The order is an arbitrary string of speciﬁed length transferring
from the master to slave by the MPI_Isend command.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The slave reads the order
by the MPI_Irecv command.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The order processing is simulated by calling the
usleep(tv) function which causes the slave MPI-process to be suspended from
execution until the speciﬁed number of real-time microseconds has elapsed.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
After
processing, the master and all the slaves perform global barrier synchronization
by using MPI_Barrier command.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
As a result, the slave sends to the master an
arbitrary string of speciﬁed length using MPI_Send command.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The master reads
the results of all the slaves by MPI_Recv command.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The synchronization is per-
formed by MPI_Waitall command.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
Then, the master simulates evaluation of the
results by calling the usleep(tp) function which causes the master MPI-process


to be suspended from execution until the speciﬁed number of real-time microsec-
onds has elapsed.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
To verify the equation (2) determining the speedup, the parameter v =
lg (tw/ts ) connecting the values of tw and ts was introduced.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The following
values of the parameter were studied: 4, 4.5 and 6.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The speedup curves plot-

of numerical simulations performed via the BSF-simulator.

Conclusion
In the paper, the issue of the adequacy of the BSF parallel computing model was
studied.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
To verify the model, a simulator of BSF-programs in C++ language was
developed using the MPI library.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The emulator is implemented on the basis of the
”master-slave” model.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
As orders, the master sends slaves messages of a certain
length with arbitrary symbols.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
As a result, slaves are send to the master message
of a certain length with arbitrary symbols.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
Calculations are simulated using the
usleep() function.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
Via the simulator, computational experiments were carried
out for various parameters of the BSF-model.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The experimental and analytical
speedup curves are compared.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text:
The same comparison is made for curves of parallel
eﬃciency.
title: arXiv:1710.10835v1  [cs.DC]  30 Oct 2017

text: The obtained results conﬁrm the adequacy of the BSF-model.

TARCO: Two-Stage Auction for D2D Relay Aided
Computation Resource Allocation in Hetnet
Long Chen∗, Jigang Wu† , Xinxiang Zhang
School of Computer Science and Technology, Guangdong University of Technology, China
∗lonchen@mail.ustc.edu.cn,†asjgwucn@outlook.com
I.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
ABSTRACT
In heterogeneous cellular network, task scheduling for computation ofﬂoading is one of the biggest
challenges.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Most works focus on alleviating heavy burden of macro base stations by moving the computation
tasks on macro-cell user equipment (MUE) to remote cloud or small-cell base stations.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
But the selﬁshness of
network users is seldom considered.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Motivated by the cloud edge computing, this paper provides incentive
for task transfer from macro cell users to small cell base stations.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The proposed incentive scheme utilizes
small cell user equipment to provide relay service.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The problem of computation ofﬂoading is modelled as
a two-stage auction, in which the remote MUEs with common social character can form a group and then
buy the computation resource of small-cell base stations with the relay of small cell user equipment.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
A
two-stage auction scheme named TARCO is contributed to maximize utilities for both sellers and buyers
in the network.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The truthful, individual rationality and budget balance of the TARCO are also proved in
this paper.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In addition, two algorithms are proposed to further reﬁne TARCO on the social welfare of the
network.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Extensive simulation results demonstrate that, TARCO is better than random algorithm by about
104.90% in terms of average utility of MUEs, while the performance of TARCO is further improved up to
28.75% and 17.06% by the proposed two algorithms, respectively.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Keywords
Auction, Computation Ofﬂoading, HetNet, incentive, Relay.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
INTRODUCTION
With the proliferation of wireless communication devices such as smartphones, tablets, laptop computers
and so on, both spectrum and data transmission rate demands are becoming much higher.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
According to
the latest Cisco visual networking index report, the global mobile data trafﬁc will be about 30.6 exabytes
Working paper, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Services Computing, neighter the revised version nor ﬁnal version

per month by 2020 [1].
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
To accommodate such urging demands, deploying small cells underlaying macro
cells as well as device-to-device (D2D) communications are the dominant strategies for the emerging next
generation wireless communications (5G).
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
By deploying low transmission power small cells overlaid macro
cells, network coverage and capacity can be improved [2].
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Meanwhile, D2D communication in a small
cell can further enhance the spectrum utilization efﬁciency via spectrum reuse such that the interferences
between D2D transmission pairs as well as between D2D pair and small cell user are well controlled.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: Therefore, D2D based heterogeneous networks (HetNets) have been a hot research topic in recent years.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The prior art in D2D based HetNet mainly focused on coverage expansion [3], power control [4],
interference management [5], resource allocation [6], [7] and so on.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
As an effective solution to handle
channel fading and increase transmission rate in wireless communications, relay aided communication has
been widely used, including two-hop or multi-hop relaying and two-phase cooperative transmission [8].
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: Therefore, relay aided communication in D2D based HetNet can also improve the network performance.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
For example, by hiring a small cell user equipment (SUE), the macro cell base station (MCB) can reach
to the macro cell user equipment (MUE) in the downlink transmission, thus the coverage of the macro cell
can be extended [9].
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Authors in [10], [11] optimized the system spectrum efﬁciency and energy efﬁciency
via D2D relay as well as modes selection.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
A load balancing scheme for D2D-based relay communications
in HetNet is proposed by [12].
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
A small cell user relay aided downlink communication from macro base
station to remote macro cell user is proposed via D2D communication [13].
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In the D2D based HetNet
architecture, there are a few papers that address incentive mechanisms.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Authors in [14] proposed a D2D
based content sharing game to maximize cellular ofﬂoading.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
[15] came out with a contract
theory based scheme to attract user equipment delivering data for the cellular base station.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Recently, Mobile-Edge Computing (MEC) has been proposed and it is an emerging paradigm to improve
the quality of experience (QoS) of mobile devices at the edge of pervasive radio access networks [16].
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In
[17], a computation ofﬂoading mechanism for mobile users was implemented by ofﬂoading computation
tasks to a common server in HetNet.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
It is noteworthy that, in real applications, mobile devices are carried
by human with limited budget.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
A single resource user may not afford to buy the computation resources
on a single SCB.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
For example, a mobile user may just want to ofﬂoad the translation task consisting of a
single phrase, however, at that time the SCB may want to lease out a whole computation resources larger
than ﬁnishing the simple translation task.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In this case, the charging price of SCB may be very high and
it may not be motivated to execute the task due to small monetary revenue.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In real scenarios, although
different mobile user may have different application level computation tasks, people in the same area may
have the same level social relations [18] or perform similar tasks, they can form a small scale social group
[19] to buy the computation services offered by the SCB.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Group based auction [20] has been proposed


SUBMITTED TO IEEE TRANSACTIONS ON SERVICES COMPUTING
2
and is proved to be an effective mechanism to collect small bids and hiring a bid agent to buy resources
from resource owners.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
When more users are willing to participate in the group based resource sharing,
the beneﬁts of resource owners will also increase and the resource utilization efﬁciency will be enhanced.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: Meanwhile, the revenue of individual buyers can be enlarged due to price discount [21].
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
On the computation ofﬂoading problem in D2D based HetNet, it is noteworthy that, part of works [9]–
[13] are under the asumption that users are willing to cooperate, which is far from realistic.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In this paper,
we employ auction theory to provide incentive for mobile users.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Some works [14]–[17] do not take relay
inﬂuence into consideration.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
It should be noted that when mobile users are far from the target server, direct
communication may not ensure the communication consistency and user QoS may suffer.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Motivated by the
recent work [22] for mobile computing where master device is chosen to ofﬂoad the computation tasks of
mobile users via D2D communication in HetNet, in this paper, we provide incentive for idle SUEs within
small cells to act as relays by ofﬂoading computation tasks of MUEs to small cell base stations (SCBs), i.e.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Moreover, most of existing researches on HetNet focus on maximizing the revenue of the
network infrastructure to optimize the load of base stations, instead of mobile users.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Note that computation
tasks and resource demands are generally heterogeneous in real application.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Thus, it is difﬁcult to guarantee
the efﬁciency of mobile users, only by optimizing the base station’s trafﬁc burden.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Therefore, it is signiﬁcant
to investigate new network paradigm on the existing two-tier HetNet archietecture.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Inspired by the above
mentioned group based auction, this paper tries to group the MUEs in low signal area or far from the MCB,
and helps to select proper idle SUEs for each MUE group.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Different from [20] and [23], in this paper, we
design the scheme tailored for relay aided coputation ofﬂoading taking account of user’s demands, where
user’s demands are not properly addressed in [20] and [23].
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
To effectively ofﬂoad computation tasks of MUEs and design new mechanisms, we have to solve the
following challenges: (i) Running applications on MUEs are heterogeneous, such as text translation, video
decoding, machine learning tasks etc.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: Therefore, the budget and demand for each MUE are different.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Meanwhile, based on the distances from MUEs to SCBs, the valuation of each MUE for the computation
capability of SCBs is various.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: How to determine winning prices to attract MUEs is a challenge.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
(ii) From
the SCB’s perspective, ofﬂoading MUEs’ tasks will consume its power and computation cycles.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Meanwhile,
for idle SUEs, their service for relaying MUEs should also be motivated because of the selﬁshness nature.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: Therefore, how to provide monetary compensation should be carefully designed for both SUEs and SCBs.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: (iii) Auction should be truthful, budget balance, individual rational and efﬁcient.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
How to ensure the above
characteristics at the same time in a two-stage auction is a challenge.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The main contribution of this paper can be summarized as follows:
•
Different from traditional auctions, in this paper, the social relations among different MUEs and the

3
similarity between tasks are considered where MUEs can form a group with similar tasks or level of
social ties to buy computation resources from SCBs.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
•
To handle the selﬁshness nature of entities in the network and provide incentive for them, a group
based two-stage auction for relay aided computation ofﬂoading in HetNet (TARCO) is proposed.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
•
We prove the proposed scheme guarantees three important economic properties: truthful, budget
balance and individual rationality.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
•
To enhance the performance of TARCO, we design MWD and VITA algorithms to improve the social
welfare of the network.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Extensive simulation results demonstrate that TARCO is about 104.90% better
than RND algorithm on average utility of MUEs and VITA is 28.75% better than TARCO and MWD
outperforms TARCO for about 17.06%.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: Section V shows the detail of two-stage auction scheme.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In Section VI we prove the economic
properties of the auction scheme.

Then we propose improved schems to enhance the social warefare of the

title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
RELATED WORK
Recently, there has been related work on user association, computation or trafﬁc ofﬂoading in heteroge-
neous wireless networks.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: Both non-incentive based and incentive based schemes have been proposed.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In
the following, we summarize and compare the related work on the above categories.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Non-incentive based schemes
Some works study D2D based user association in HetNet [11] [24].
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
[11] proposed an energy
efﬁcient mode selection and user association scheme.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The MCB acts as a central controller to determine
which one of SCB and MCB that the mobile device should be attached to.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Meanwhile, D2D relay mode
and direct communication mode selection is also considered.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
[24] adopted a D2D two-hop relay
to help mobile users get access to neighbouring base stations.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In this paper, tasks on MUEs in the two-tier
HetNet are ofﬂoaded to SCBs instead of the far away MCB to conquer the high channel fading and low
signal obstacles of MUEs.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
[9] considered the downlink coverage extension from the MCB to MUEs via the D2D
cooperation between SUEs and MUEs in a single macro cell.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In this paper, we focus on the uplink
transmission by ofﬂoading the computation task from MUEs to SCBs.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The most recent work by Cao

et al.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
[25] designed a hybrid trafﬁc ofﬂoading scheme for HetNets where mobile users can get access to
SCBs with the help of mobile relays via D2D communication.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Their objective is to maximize the number
of mobile users admitted into the whole network, through MCB or SCBs.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The problem is formulated as an
integer linear programming and solved by dynamic programming.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Different from [25], this paper mainly
focuses on MUE’s tasks ofﬂoading to the SCB with help of SUE relays.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The beneﬁts of both SUEs and SCBs
can be ensured by the Tarco scheme.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In [26], a heuristic method was proposed to detour congested MCB
trafﬁc to uncongested SCBs with the help of D2D relay nodes.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
However, only skeletal numerical analysis
is given by [26], which cannot be directly deployed.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: Thus we carry out with a distributed implementation.

text:
Incentive based mechanisms
Recently, the incentive based schemes have been proposed.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
[27] proposed a truthful auction
framework for femtocell access between MUEs and femtocell base stations.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: [2] to ofﬂoad trafﬁc from the MCB to SCB service providers.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
However, both in [27] and [2],
relay is not used.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
[28] came out with a Stackelberg game based ofﬂoading mechanism by transferring part
of MUE’s data to the SCB via SUE relay nodes.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The MUE is the leader while candidate SUE relays are
followers.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: The optimal power allocation and relay selection is conducted via leader-follower pricing.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
[29] proposed a two-stage Stackelberg game for SCBs to admit MCB’s trafﬁc from the perspective
of network ﬁxed infrastructure, however, relay inﬂuence is not considered.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Meanwhile, they do not consider
SCB’s heterogeneity.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: Methods proposed by other literatures cannot be applied in this paper.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
[23] studied the
spectrum group auction in cognitive radio networks.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
[30] came out with a scheme to
allocate both channels and cooperative relay nodes for cooperative cognitive radio networks with two-stage
group auction.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: However, in their work, the ask price at each spectrum owner is same for different buyers.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In computation ofﬂoading, the tasks are different and for each SCB, the ask price may not be constant for
all buyers due to different location and channel fading conditions.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: [31] carefully designed an incentive-compatible auction scheme between cloudlets and mobile users.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The
cloudlets are edge servers to ofﬂoad trafﬁc of remote cloud.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Similar to [31], the SCBs can be regarded as
cloudlets to admit computation tasks sent from mobile users.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Based on the observations, to ofﬂoad the computation tasks of MUEs with relay SUEs and motivate both
SUEs and SCBs should be properly handled.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
New schemes should deal with heterogeneous computation
ofﬂoading tasks as well as SCB’s heterogeneity.

SYSTEM MODEL AND PROBLEM FORMULATION
In this section, ﬁrstly we present the system model, then the computation ofﬂoading problem of MUEs
is formulated as a two-stage auction.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
At last, we introduce related economic properties that auction scheme
should follow.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text: The basic notations are shown in table I.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Main Idea of TARCO Scheme
The main idea of our proposed TARCO scheme is to provide incentive and utilize D2D communications
to assist the computation ofﬂoading of MUEs to local SCBs, with the aim to maximize utilities of both SCBs
and MUEs.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
1 as an example, when there are some MUEs in the high channel fading area or low
signal region, they cannot directly to ofﬂoad their computation tasks to neighbour SCBs without the help of
SUE relays.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The proposed TARCO scheme allows MUEs to access the SCBs by relaying the computation
data via SUE relays in the coverage of corresponding SCBs.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Intuitively, TARCO can improve the system
performance by reducing the trafﬁc ﬂowed to MCB and reduce the MUE’s energy consumption with a
lower transmission power.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
It should be noted that for MUEs with high mobility and moving constantly, it
may get access to MCB to avoid frequent handover, which is out of the scope of this paper.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:

In our scenario, we assume all nodes stay static in a given auction period.

frequency bands [32].

tasks.

An auction will not be conducted until many economic properties are satisﬁed.

text:
An auction is truthful if any participant’s utility is maximized by submitting its
true valuation, regardless what others would like to behave.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
That is, no bidder can improve his utility by
misreporting his bids.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
An auction is budget balanced if total payment from buyers are no less
than the sum paying paid to sellers.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:

the auctioneer a non-negative utility, i.e.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
An auction is computational efﬁciency if the scheme can
terminate in polynomial time in terms of the input.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

In this paper, TARCO is designed to achieve truthful, individual rationality, budget balance and
computational efﬁciency.

In phase II of TARCO, the algorithm assigns SCB resources to the relay SUEs in a greedy manner, which
may result in low utilities for both parties.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:

resources and system performance may suffer.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In this section, we propose a VCG based utility improved
truthful auction (VITA) scheme to improve the utilities of both SUEs and SCBs.

TARCO is replaced by a VCG based auction shown in Algorithm 4 while phase I of TARCO remains
unchanged in the new scheme VITA.

matching graph to determin winners.

neglected, TARCO, MWD and VITA demonstrate good qualities to ensure higher social welfare than
the RND algorithm.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In real situations, the SCB is a ﬁxed network infrastructure, and is always full of
computation resources as well as energy abundant.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Therefore, TARCO, MWD and VITA can be deployed
to motivate SUEs leasing resources to assist the computation ofﬂoading of MUEs.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
CONCLUSION
In this paper, we have investigated the auction mechanism to jointly allocate the computation resources of
SCBs and SUE relay nodes efectively in HetNet.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
We model the joint resource allocation problem as a two-
stage auction where in the ﬁrst stage, each remote MUE node submits its valuation and demand to bid SUE
relay and the SCB.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
The SUE relay node collects bids from the social group within its range and conducts
a virtual auction between MUEs and SUEs.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Then the macro cell base station will perform a double auction
between SUEs and SCBs to allocate the computation resources, i.e.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Finally, the winning
SUE relays will execute the auction result of previous stage.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Based on the proposed scheme, we have
proposed three schemes TARCO, MWD and VITA.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
We prove that TARCO is truthful, individual rational,
budget balance and computational efﬁcient.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
We also prove that MWD and VITA schemes are truthful,
individual rational and computational efﬁcient.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Extensive numerical analysis demonstrate that for social
welfare, TARCO is about 12.05% better than RND and Compared with RND, MWD and VITA outperform
RND by 63.14% and 28.01% respectively.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
Note that in this work we assume SCBs have abundant resources
and each SUE social group may only be served by one SCB and the auction is executed for one time.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

text:
In the future, we would like to consider the auction with resource constraint SCBs and from a long time
multi-round perspective.
title: TARCO: Two-Stage Auction Relay Aided Computation Resource Allocation Hetnet

We present a computational model of creative design based on collabora-
tive interactive genetic algorithms.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In our model, designers individually 
guide interactive genetic algorithms (IGAs) to generate and explore poten-
tial design solutions quickly.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Collaboration is supported by allowing de-
signers to share solutions amongst each other while using IGAs, with the 
sharing of solutions adding variables to the search space.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We present ex-
periments on 3D modeling as a case study, with designers creating model 
transformations individually and collaboratively.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The transformations were 
evaluated by participants in surveys and results show that individual and 
collaborative models were considered equally creative.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
However, the use 
of our collaborative IGAs model materially changes resulting designs 
compared to individual IGAs.

text:
Dascalu
2
Introduction
Design is a goal-oriented, constrained decision-making activity, involving 
learning about emerging features [1].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
It is usually characterized by four 
phases – conceptual design, detailed design, evaluation, and iterative re-
design [2].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Within this context, creativity has the potential to occur when a 
designer purposely shifts the focus of the search space [3].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Speciﬁcally, the 
ability to perform goal-oriented shifts while brainstorming and exploring 
potential solutions is crucial to creativity in the design process.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
This is ac-
complished implicitly by the designer’s understanding of the problem 
changing over time, or explicitly by considering additional traits which 
may yield interesting solutions [3].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We present a computational model of creative design based on collabo-
rative interactive genetic algorithms (IGAs) which supports goal-oriented 
shifts by adding variables to the search space.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In our model, designers in-
dividually guide IGAs to generate and explore design solutions quickly 
[2].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The model allows designers to share solutions amongst each other by 
presenting designers with a sample of solutions generated by their peers.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
When a designer selects a solution from a peer, the solution is injected into 
his/her IGA population, with this injection adding new variables to the 
search space.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In our previous work [4], [5], we introduced our model of creative de-
sign and presented a pretest of the model for user guided design of ﬂoor-
plans, but without expanding the search space with additional variables.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The pretest results showed that ﬂoorplans created collaboratively were 
considered to be more original than ﬂoorplans created individually.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Fol-
lowing the pretest, we conducted a user study where we addressed the 
question of whether collaboration alone–without expanding the search 
space—introduced the potential to generate creative solutions [5].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Results 
showed that ﬂoorplans created collaboratively were considered to be more 
revolutionary and original than ﬂoorplans created individually.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In this paper, we present experiments where the search space is expand-
ed by adding variables during the evolutionary search.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We use 3D model-
ing as the case study for the experiments.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
However, rather than creating 3D 
models from scratch, we explore transformations of 3D models with vertex 
programs.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text: The rest of the paper is organized as follows.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We start by presenting a 
discussion of the computational model and the 3D modeling case study.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Next, the experimental setup is presented in detail, followed by user study 
results and discussions.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Collaborative Evolution of 3D Models
!3
Computational Model of Creative Design
Models of creative design presented by the research design community 
manipulate the search space through the use of techniques, including com-
bination, analogies, transformation, emergence, and ﬁrst principles [6].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Genetic algorithms provide a means for exploring a search space consist-
ing of potential solutions that meet a given set of requirements [7].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
How-
ever, there are times when it is difﬁcult, if not impossible to deﬁne a suit-
able ﬁtness function, especially when dealing with problems require sub-
jective evaluation.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
An interactive genetic algorithm empowers the user to 
drive evolution by replacing the ﬁtness evaluation [8], and enables users to 
guide evolution based on their sense of aesthetics, intuition, and domain 
expertise.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Our computational model of creative design leverages the exploration 
power of the GA, the visualization and subjective feedback integration of 
the IGA, and collaboration in order to allow designers to shift the focus of 
the search space during an evolutionary run.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages
3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
By using IGAs in our model, users can incorporate their personal prefer-
ence, sense of aesthetics, intuition, and expertise into the search process.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In 
addition, each user decides when to take solutions from peers, meaning 
that the user always remains in control of his/her own IGA.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Collaboration allows designers to share expertise, to be exposed to traits 
they may not have considered, and to complement each other in the task of 
exploring solutions which meet a given set of requirements.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In our model, 
designers start with different variable sets.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The designers are exposed to 
solutions being explored by their peers during collaboration and conse-
quently to the different effects resulting from different variable sets.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Tak-
ing solutions from peers allows designers to expand their search space by 
automatically incorporating the variables being explored by their peers.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text: Figure 1 illustrates our computational model of creative design.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The ﬁg-
ure illustrates three users collaborating with each other.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Each user interacts 
with a GA by acting as the subjective evaluation.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Evaluation may consist 
of subjective evaluation only, or a combination of subjective and objective 
evaluations.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The arrows between the IGAs represent the communication 
that takes place between the peers.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
If a user likes a design solution from 
one of his/her peers, then the user has the option to inject that solution into 
his/her population, thus introducing a search bias.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
For implementation de-
tails of the collaborative IGA model, see [4] and [5].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Dascalu
4
Our collaborative IGA computational model is a special case of a case 
injected genetic algorithm (CIGAR) [9], where (1) each user serves as a 
case base to peers, and (2) each user determines  when and how many in-
dividuals to inject into his/her population, instead of injection being done 
in an algorithmic fashion.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
When a user chooses to inject a solution from 
one of his/her peers, the introduced bias will not only become apparent in 
the user’s own population, but it will also be visible to his/her peers, since 
users can always see a subset of each others’ solutions.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
For example, as 
“user A” interacts with the IGA, the changes in the population of user A 
will be reﬂected on the screens of the peers of user A.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Thus, each user par-
ticipating in collaboration serves as a dynamic case base to his/her peers.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
1 Computational model of creative design
Typically in CIGARs a case base of solutions to previously solved prob-
lems is maintained.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Based on problem similarity, individuals similar to the 
best individuals in the current population are periodically injected from the 
case base, replacing the worst individuals in the population [9].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In our 
computational model, the designer plays the role of determining how 
many, when, and which individuals to inject at any step during the collabo-
rative evolutionary process.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
If the injected individuals make a positive 
contribution to the overall population, then they will continue to reproduce 
and live on, while injected individuals that do not improve the population 
performance will eventually die off.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Hence, the user is not penalized for 


Collaborative Evolution of 3D Models
!5
injecting subpar individuals.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We use ﬁtness biasing (linear scaling) to en-
sure that injected individuals survive long enough to leave a mark on the 
host population.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Creative Potential of Model 
Boden describes two types of creativity in design, P-creativity and H-cre-
ativity  [10].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
P-creativity  (personal  or  psychological  creativity)  occurs 
when the design is creative to the designer.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
H-creativity occurs when the 
design is creative when compared to all that has been created and produced 
historically by all of humanity.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
S-creativity (situated creativity), a third 
type which has also been presented, occurs when the resulting design is 
novel to that particular situation, but not necessarily be creative to the in-
dividual or creative historically [11].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In our model, at the individual level 
designers guide P-creative processes while interacting with the IGA.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Dur-
ing collaboration, the sharing of design solutions allows the designers as a 
group to guide the S-creative process.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Speciﬁcally, users can begin explo-
ration of distinct search spaces (deﬁned by different variable sets), and 
through collaboration, explore search spaces deﬁned by combinations of 
their variable sets.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
3D Modeling Representation
We use 3D modeling as the case study for our experiments.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Rather than 
creating 3D models from scratch, we perform modiﬁcations to existing and 
well-formed 3D models by evolving vertex programs.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The vertex pro-
grams allow for an operation to be applied on a per vertex basis for every 
vertex on a 3D model.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
For the experiments in this paper we used the 
OGRE 3D rendering engine and Cg as the GPU programming language for 
the vertex programs.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text: We evolve vertex programs with genetic programming (GP) [12].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
GP is 
an evolutionary computation technique where each individual in the popu-
lation is a computer program.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The computer program is represented using 
a tree structure (GP tree) and the operations of the GP tree are typically 
mathematical operations.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Figure 2 illustrates our representation of the vertex programs in the IGA 
as a bit encoded binary tree.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
A binary tree is a tree data structure in which 
each node has at most two child nodes.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
For example, a node with index i 
would have its children at indices 2i + 1 and 2i + 2.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Dascalu
6
all leaves are at the same depth and every parent node has two child nodes.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
From the perspective of GA encoding, storing a binary tree in an array has 
the advantage of being readily mapped to a bit string.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text: 2 Binary string representation of vertex programs.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In our implementation, parent nodes consist of binary operations on the 
children nodes, with these operations including addition, subtraction, mul-
tiplication, and division.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
It was seen in preliminary experiments that unary 
operators, such as the trigonometric functions, also created a wide range of 
interesting transformations of 3D models, and therefore a second array is 
used to store unary operators applied to each child node in the tree, as 
shown in Figure 2.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We use the trigonometric functions of sine, cosine, and 
tangent.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The leaf nodes in the tree consist of variables including the coor-
dinates of the current vertex (x, y, or z), the current simulation time loop-
ing from 0 to 2π, and random numbers between -10 and 10.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The binary 


Collaborative Evolution of 3D Models
!7
operations, the set of constants, and the unary operators are combined into 
a single bit string array manipulated by the IGA as illustrated in Figure 2.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The decoded equation of each individual in the population is written to a 
Cg ﬁle.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The decoded equation modiﬁes all of the x, y, and z coordinates 
with the same equation, or only one of the x, y, or z coordinates.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
For ex-
ample, equation (1) modiﬁes the x, y, and z coordinates of each vertex with 
the same equation:
p.xyz = p.xyz + (2.2 − (p.x/11)) + (7 ∗ cos(p.y));  (1)
where p.xyz represents the x, y, and z coordinates of the current vertex, 
p.x is the x coordinate of the current vertex, and p.y is the y coordinate of 
the current vertex.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The value of the equation on the right is added to each 
of the x, y, and z coordinates of the current vertex.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Thus, equation (1) is 
equivalent to the following:
p.x = p.x + (2.2 − (p.x/11)) + (7 ∗ cos(p.y));          
p.y = p.y + (2.2 − (p.x/11)) + (7 ∗ cos(p.y));        
p.z = p.z + (2.2 − (p.x/11)) + (7 ∗ cos(p.y));         
The vertex program representation enables us to have a ﬁrst set of users 
evolve programs that modify the x coordinate, and a second set of users 
evolve programs that modify the y coordinate, as illustrated in Figure 3.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Through collaboration, the ﬁrst set of users can inject solutions from the 
second set of users, resulting in their respective search spaces expanding 
from exploring equations that only modify the x and y coordinate, or only 
the y and z coordinate, to equations that modify all the coordinates of the 
3D model.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Experimental Setup
The experiments presented in this paper were conducted in an environment 
built with the OGRE rendering engine.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The goal of the experiments is to 
show that the use of our collaborative computational model results in solu-
tions that are more creative compared to solutions generated using a sim-
ple IGA.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
To this end, the experiment consisted of three phases: (1) creation 
of designs, (2) ﬁrst evaluation of the designs, and (3) online evaluation of 
the designs.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text: These are described in detail in the next subsections.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text: 3 Expanding design variable space through collaboration.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Design Creation 
A group of 20 students from the Computer Science Department at the 
University of Nevada, Reno, (“the design participants”) used simple IGAs 
and our collaborative model to create transformations of the 3D models 
individually and collaboratively.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
During the creation of the designs, partic-
ipants were split into pairs.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
When using our collaborative model, partici-
pants were only allowed to share solutions within each pair.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
During col-
laboration between users, the search space was expanded as shown in Fig-
ure 3.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We used an ABA experimental design to test the hypothesis that our col-
laborative model results in more creative solutions when compared to a 
simple IGA.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In the experimental design, the baseline condition (A) was 
participants creating solutions individually with a simple IGA, and the ex-
perimental condition (B) was participants creating solutions collaborative-
ly with our computational model of creative design.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The experiment con-
sisted of each design participant conducting an ABA session (individual 
session, collaborative session, individual session) followed by a BAB ses-
sion (collaborative session, individual session, collaborative session).
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The 
goal of this design is to show that the use of our computational model, 
rather than time, is the controlling variable if there is a change in behavior 
between baseline and experimental conditions [13].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Our hypothesis is that 
the resulting scores (from a 7-point Likert scale) would resemble a zig-zag 
pattern as illustrated in Figure 4, with the average scores of models gener-


Collaborative Evolution of 3D Models
!9
ated during individual trials being close to 7, and the average scores of 
models generated during collaborative trials being close to 1.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
4 Hypothesized comparison of scores between individual and collaboratively 
created models.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

Figure 5 shows the three models used in the user study: (1) a futuristic 
female model in a blue suit, (2) a green ninja, and (3) a white robot.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Half 
of the design participants were assigned to a ﬁrst design group, while the 
other half where assigned to a second design group.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The ﬁrst design group 
created transformations for the models in this order: (1) individual – fe-
male, (2) collaborative – ninja, (3) individual – robot, (ABA) and (4) col-
laborative – robot, (5) individual – ninja, and (6) collaborative – female 
(BAB).
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The second design group created transformations similarly to the 
ﬁrst design group, except that in trials 4-6 the second design group begins 
with the female model instead of the robot model: (4) collaborative – fe-
male, (5) individual – ninja, and (6) collaborative robot (BAB).
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

Each design participant created at least two transformations for each of 
the models during the collaborative and the individual sessions.

creative from each set of  models, for a total of six ﬁnal solutions from 
each design participant:  (1) female - individual, (2) female - collaborative, 
(3) ninja - individual, (4) ninja - collaborative, (5) robot - individual,  and 
(6) robot - collaborative.

This set of ﬁnal solutions was evaluated as de-
scribed in the next subsection.

text:
Evaluation 
Our evaluation is based on the work of Thang et al.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
[14], which consists of 
criteria derived from the Creative Product Semantic Scale [14], [15] and 
[16].
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The participants were asked to rate model transformations on a 7-
point Likert scale on the following criteria: creativity, novelty, surprising, 
workability, relevance, and thoroughness.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
However, instead of simply us-
ing the terms from this rating scale, we presented the users with ﬁve state-
ments, and participants speciﬁed the degree to which they agreed or dis-
agreed with the statements.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The evaluation participants were only in-
formed that a group of students had created a set of transformations of 
models, representing special effects for a video game.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The ﬁrst evaluation statement, related to creativity, was: “The transfor-
mation is creative.” Many deﬁnitions of creativity exist, and the deﬁnition 
largely depends on the context and problem domain.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Therefore, we provid-
ed the evaluation participants with the following deﬁnition to evaluate the 
created designs: “A creative transformation is a transformation that is new, 
unexpected, and valuable.” The statement could be answered by selecting 
between  “Extremely  Creative”  (coded  as  1)  versus  “Not  Creative  At 
All” (coded as 7), or with a number in between 1 and 7.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The rest of the evaluation statements did not use the terms workability, 
relevance, and thoroughness, to avoid ambiguity regarding the meaning of 
these terms.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Instead, the evaluation asked whether the transformation with 
or without tweaks could be used in a video game, which addressed worka-
bility, relevance, and thoroughness.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The other four statements in the evalu-
ation were: (1) The transformation can be used in a video game; (2) The 
transformation with minor tweaks can be used in a video game; (3) The 
transformation is novel; and (4) The transformation is surprising.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Users 
could  answer  these  questions  on  a  7-point  Likert  scale  as  “Very 
True” (coded as 1) versus “Not True At All” (coded as 7).
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The ﬁrst group of evaluation participants evaluated the ﬁnal solution 
sets created and selected by the design participants.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Each evaluation partic-

evaluated a total of 12 models.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text: After the ﬁrst evaluation, we conducted a second online evaluation.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
A 
total of 16 adult volunteers completed the online evaluation.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We selected 
the best six individually created models and the best six collaboratively 
created models for online evaluation.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We made a video of these 12 models, 
posted the video online, and collected data via an online survey.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The online 
survey used the same evaluation criteria as the ﬁrst evaluation phase, ex-
cept that we removed the statement asking whether the transformation with 
minor tweaks could be used in a video game to make the survey shorter.

Online Evaluation 
The ﬁrst evaluation phase showed that models created individually re-
ceived similar scores to models created collaboratively.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We believed that it 
would be difﬁcult to prove that every solution generated collaboratively 
would be more creative than a solution created individually.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In view of the 
results from the ﬁrst evaluation, we created an online evaluation in which 
users viewed a video and provided scores for the models in the video via 
an online survey.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The video ﬁrst presented the three original models, without any trans-
formations, so that participants could appreciate the differences that the 
transformations made.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The video then showed a ﬁrst row of individually 
created transformations, followed by a second row of collaboratively cre-
ated transformations.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The online survey used the same evaluation criteria 
from the ﬁrst evaluation phase, with one exception.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We removed the ques-


Collaborative Evolution of 3D Models
!17
tion asking whether the transformation with minor tweaks could be used in 
a video game to make the survey shorter.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The survey ﬁrst asked partici-
pants to evaluate the row of individually created models, followed by 
evaluation of the row of collaboratively created models.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
After both rows of 
models had been evaluated, participants were asked which of the two rows 
they liked the most and which of the two rows was the most creative.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text: We had a total of 16 completed online evaluations.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We aggregated the 
scores for all of the individual models per criterion and similarly for the 
collaborative models.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We compared the averages using the independent 
samples t-test and we found no statistically signiﬁcant differences in the 
results.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
With regard to which row participants liked the most, eight partici-
pants picked the row of individually created models, seven participants 
picked the row of collaboratively created models, and one participant did 
not answer.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
With regard to which row was the most creative, three partici-
pants picked the row of individually created models and 13 participants 
picked the row of collaboratively created models.
