text:
Discussion 
Figure 11 shows examples of two models generated by the design partici-
pants.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text: All of the effects on the models involved animation.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Thus, it was 
difﬁcult to capture the resulting effects in images.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Our observations were 
that while both individual and collaborative solutions were interesting, the 
collaborative solutions had more dramatic effects.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In addition, the collabo-
rative solutions tended to be more chaotic, and thus had a less polished 
look.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text: Figure 11(a) shows a blue female model created individually.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The fe-
male model starts by standing straight, and the evolved vertex program 
made the body of the female model curve from left to right in the shape of 
an “S.” Even though the model is curved, all parts of the original model 
can be identiﬁed, and overall the model has a smooth and aesthetically 
pleasing look.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Figure 11(b) shows a blue female model created collabora-
tively.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The evolved vertex program made the female model expand up-
wards, making the model look like the tail of a comet.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The interesting part 
of the model is that in the midst of the chaotic animation, the face of the 
model remains visible, along with some of the extremities, such as both 
legs and part of her arms.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Yet, this model, while exciting, does give the 
impression of being a work in progress.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
From the results from the ﬁrst evaluation phase we can deduce that 
models created individually were equally creative as models created col-


!
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
There are observations which we believe help explain some 
of the results obtained.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
First, we found that transformations on the blue 
female models resulted in the most interesting and aesthetically pleasing 
effects.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The geometry and the skeleton, which dictates how a model moves 
when  animated,  of  the  female  model  resulted  in  transformations  that 
looked polished and well-done compared to the transformations of the oth-
er two models.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Transformations on the female model tended to have 
smooth transitions, and many times the original model was deformed in a 
curved fashion, resulting in soft edges.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
On the other hand, transformations 
on the robot and ninja models tended to result in sharp and jagged edges.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In fact, we found that the same transformation applied to different models 
resulted in different effects due to the model geometry and the skeleton.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text: Overall, the ninja models resulted in the less interesting effects.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
This was 
particularly identiﬁed while we were building the sets of best individual 
models and best collaborative models for the online evaluation.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:

female model.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Regarding the online evaluation results, the fact that the majority of par-
ticipants identiﬁed the row of collaborative models as the most creative, 
yet the average evaluation scores of collaborative and individual models 
were not statistically different, suggests a couple of points.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
First, the struc-
ture of the survey may have created a learning confound.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In the online 
evaluation, the video was not included in the online survey web page.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Par-
ticipants had to follow a link to watch the video on an external web page.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Therefore, participants would have had to switch back and forth between 
the survey web page and the video web page, instead of being able to score 
the models with the video always in view.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
A further nuance was that the 


Collaborative Evolution of 3D Models
!19
video focused on each model for an average of 10 to 15 seconds.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
We had 
to impose this time limit in order to keep the video short.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
If participants 
wanted to watch one of the models in further detail, then they would have 
had to rewind the video to the right spot.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Finally, we do not know whether 
participants watched the entire video once and then ﬁlled out the online 
survey, or whether they scored each model in tandem with the video.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
All of 
these nuances may have resulted in a learning confound that negatively 
biased the results.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
Conclusions
In this paper we presented and evaluated the results of design evaluation 
on evolving a set of transformations on 3D models used in video games.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The evolution is based on a collaborative model of creative design that 
uses interactive genetic algorithm and collaboration via solution injection 
among peers.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
The study is a major extension of our previous work in 
evolving 2D architectural ﬂoorplans.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
In the present study we look at issue 
of expanding the design space by introducing new variables, which has the 
potential to lead to uncovering solutions (creative or otherwise) that would 
not have been possible otherwise.
title: 3D_Modeling_final.pages

text:
While the evaluation scores did not fully 
support our hypothesis that our computational model of creative design 
increases creative content of solutions, the use of our collaborative model 
materially changed the resulting designs due to the expansion of the search 
space via collaboration.

SUKHPAL SINGH GILL and RAJKUMAR BUYYA, The University of Melbourne, Australia  
The cloud computing paradigm offers on-demand services over the Internet and supports a wide variety of applications.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
With the recent growth 
of Internet of Things (IoT) based applications the usage of cloud services is increasing exponentially.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The next generation of cloud computing 
must be energy-efficient and sustainable to fulfil the end-user requirements which are changing dynamically.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Presently, cloud providers are 
facing challenges to ensure the energy efficiency and sustainability of their services.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The usage of large number of cloud datacenters increases 
cost as well as carbon footprints, which further effects the sustainability of cloud services.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In this paper, we propose a comprehensive taxonomy 
of sustainable cloud computing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The taxonomy is used to investigate the existing techniques for sustainability that need careful attention and 
investigation as proposed by several academic and industry groups.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, the current research on sustainable cloud computing is organized 
into several categories: application design, sustainability metrics, capacity planning, energy management, virtualization, thermal-aware 
scheduling, cooling management, renewable energy and waste heat utilization.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The existing techniques have been compared and categorized 
based on the common characteristics and properties.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
A conceptual model for sustainable cloud computing has been proposed along with 
discussion on future research directions.

text:
INTRODUCTION  
Cloud computing offers a flexible and powerful computing environment to provide on-demand, subscription-based 
online services over the Internet to host applications on a pay-as-you-go basis.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The various cloud providers such as 
Microsoft, Google and Amazon make extensive use of Cloud Data Centers (CDCs) to fulfill the requirements 
(memory, data, compute or network) of the digital world.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To reduce the service delay and maintain the Service 
Level Agreement (SLA), fault tolerance should be provided through replicating the compute abilities redundantly 
[1].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To ensure the availability and reliability of services, the components of CDCs such as network devices, storage 
devices and servers should be run 24/7 [2].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Large amounts of data are created by digital activities such as data 
streaming, file sharing, searching and social networking websites, e-commerce, sensor networks and that data can 
be stored as well as processed efficiently using CDCs [3] [4].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The energy cost is added by creating, processing and 
storing each bit of data, which increases carbon footprints that further impacts on the sustainability of cloud 
services.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Due to the large consumption of electricity by CDCs, the research community is addressing challenge of 
designing sustainable CDCs [5].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
With the continuous growth of Internet of Things (IoT) based applications, the usage of cloud services is increasing 
exponentially, which further increases the electricity consumptions of CDCs by 20-25% every year [6].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Existing 
studies claimed that 78.7 million metric tons of CO2 are produced by datacenters, which is equal to the two percent 
of global emissions [7].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
CDCs in USA consumed 100 billion kilowatt hours (kWh) in 2015, which is sufficient for 
Washington City [11].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: The consumption of electricity will reach 150 billion kWh by 2022 i.e.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Energy consumption in CDCs can be increased to 8000 terawatt hours (TWh) in 2030 if controlled mechanisms are 
not identified [122].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Due to underloading and overloading of resources in infrastructure (cooling, computing, 
storage, networking etc.), the energy consumption in cloud datacenters is not efficient and mostly the energy is 
consumed while some of the resources are in idle state, which increases the cost of cloud services [11].

1.1 Background 
The design of sustainable system is one of the greatest challenge of the 21st Century, the ecological transition 
coupled with the digital transformation.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
And it is scientifically difficult to decide on the benefit of a technique for 
improving the sustainability of a system.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: “Sustainability” by definition involves four areas of study, i.e.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

identify the different components of sustainable CDC to enable sustainable cloud computing economically 
(energy/electricity cost), socially (laws and regulations to establish cloud data centre) and technologically (data 
preservation, protection and retention) and environmentally (energy consumption/carbon footprints/greenhouse 
emissions).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
This systematic review deals mostly with energy in the environmental and economic spheres and by covering issues 
in how to run CDCs efficiently with minimal energy (minimum cost of energy) by harnessing renewable energy 
powered resources through holistic management of workloads and resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The main objectives of sustainable 
cloud computing are: i) to reduce energy consumption at datacenters and ii) to dispose hardware devices after their 
useful life.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Cloud computing accelerates our economy rapidly through the use of remote servers via the Internet 
instead of local servers.

Due to the availability of large number of datacenters, the user’s data is stored, managed 
and processed efficiently and swiftly but it increases carbon footprints, which effects sustainability [135].

SUSTAINABLE CLOUD COMPUTING: A TAXONOMY 
The ever-increasing demand of cloud computing services that are deployed across multiple cloud datacenters 
harness significant amount of power, resulting in not only high operational cost, but also high carbon emissions.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In 
sustainable cloud computing, the CDCs are powered by renewable energy resources by replacing the conventional 
fossil fuel based grid electricity or brown energy to effectively reduce the carbon emissions [2].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Employing energy 
efficiency mechanisms also makes cloud computing sustainable by reducing carbon footprints to a great extent 
[144].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Waste heat utilization from heat dissipated through servers and employing mechanisms for free cooling of 
the servers make the CDCs sustainable [3].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Thus, sustainable cloud computing covers the following elements in 


 
9 
 
making the datacenter sustainable [4]: i) using renewable energy instead of grid energy generated from fossil fuels 
ii) utilizing the waste heat generated from heat dissipating servers iii) using free cooling mechanisms and iv) using 
energy efficient mechanisms [145].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
All of these factors contribute in reducing the carbon footprints, the operational 
cost, and the energy consumption to make CDCs more sustainable [146].

3.1.2.2 Application Models: The complexity of applications is increasing day by day and the cloud platform can 
be used to handle user applications.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The different types of application models are developed for wide range of 
domains to satisfy the different types of customers for sustainable computing [25] [42-44] [125].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are seven 
types of application models as identified from literature [47] [48]: 1) thread-based, 2) task-based, 3) Map-Reduce 
model, 4) bag of tasks or parameter sweep tasks, 5) stream processing, 6) message passing and 7) graph processing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In thread-based model, one process is divided into multiple threads, which executes concurrently and sharing 
resources such as memory, network, processor to complete execution.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In task-based model, a large task is divided 
into small tasks and execute them parallelly on different non-sharable cloud resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Map-reduce tasks split the 
input data-set into independent chunks and parallel way of execution, which is used to execute the mapped tasks.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Further, the outputs of the maps are sorted and used as an input to the reduce tasks.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Bag-of-tasks or parameter 
sweep tasks refers to the jobs that are parallel among which there are no dependencies and are identical in their 
nature and differ only by the specific parameters used to execute them, for example: video coding and encoding.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Stream processing is a processing of small-sized data (in Kilobytes) generated continuously by thousands of data 
sources (geospatial services, social networks, mobile or web applications, online gaming and video streaming), 
which typically send data records simultaneously and an example of stream processing model can be video 
processing application.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Message Passing interface provides a communication functionality between a set of 
processes, which are mapped to nodes or servers in a language-independent way and it encouraged development of 
portable and scalable large-scale parallel applications.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Graph processing involves the process of analyzing, storing 
and processing graphs to produce effective outputs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.1.2.3 Workload Types: For workload management in sustainable cloud computing, there are mainly two types 
of IT workloads that are considered for sustainable computing: batch-style and critical interactive [32] [33].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Batch 
style workloads are those workloads which are submitted to a job queue, and it will be executed when resources 
become available.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Multiple batch jobs are often submitted without any deadline constraint together and are 
executed with maximum resource utilization.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The workloads that need immediate response but its execution should 
be completed before their deadline are called critical interactive workloads.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.1.2.4 Architecture: The architecture is an important component of sustainable cloud computing and there are 
basically two types of architectures: centralized and decentralized [46] [55] [58] [137].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In centralized architectures, 
there is a central controller, which manages all the tasks that are required to be executed, and further it executes 
the task using scheduled resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: The central controller is responsible for the execution of all tasks.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In 
decentralized architectures, resources are allocated independently to execute the tasks without any mutual 
coordination.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Every resource is responsible for their own task execution.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The performance of QoS parameters of different cloud applications is measured using different metrics as discussed 
in Section 3.2.

3.3 Capacity Planning 
Cloud service providers must involve an effective and organized capacity planning to enable sustainable computing.

text: The capacity planning can be done for power infrastructure, IT devices and cooling.

capacity cost, which makes cloud infrastructure more sustainable.

3.4 Energy Management  
Energy management in sustainable computing is an important issue for cloud service providers.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[5] 
reported that more than 2.4% of electricity is consumed by CDCs with a large economic impact of $30 billion 
globally.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: The energy requirement to manage the CDCs is also rising in proportion to the operational cost.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
IBM 
spends 45% of total expenses on electricity bills of CDCs and the consumption of electricity will be increased to 
101.5 Billion Kilo Watt Hour (kWh) by 2022 [10].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Sustainable cloud services are attracting more cloud customers 
and making it more profitable [62] [60].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Improving energy utilization, which reduces electricity bills and operational 
costs to enable sustainable cloud computing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The important requirements of sustainable cloud datacenters are 
optimal software system design, optimized air ventilation and installing temperature monitoring tools for adequate 
resource utilization, which improves energy efficiency [67] [74].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are mainly three levels where energy 
consumption can be optimized such as software level (efficient use of registers, buffers etc.), hardware level 
(transistors, voltage supply, logical gates and clock frequency) and intermediate level (energy-aware resource 
provisioning techniques) [80].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

circuitry systems are considering more by offline energy management [60].

During design time, the whole 
optimization happens at system level and it deals with factorization, path balancing, transistor sizing, instruction

text: Static energy management performs at two levels: System level and CPU level.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

Existing studies [125] [83] 
found that CPU offers big scope of optimization of energy consumption because computing components of the CPU 
consumes 35-40% of energy [3] [71].

text:
The optimization of energy at CPU level can be performed at instruction set 
level or register level.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Researchers designed different number of instruction set architectures to improve resource 
utilization like reduced bit-width architecture at instruction set level.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
On the other hand, the activities of register 
transfer level are optimizing to decrease energy consumption.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Energy cost and CO2 emission for static and dynamic 
energy management techniques [122] [144] [145] is shown in Figure 13.

text:

It is clearly shown that static energy management techniques consume more energy as well as produce more CO2 
emissions as compared to dynamic energy management techniques.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Other components of system along with CPU 
are software systems, network facility and memory components that consume large amounts of energy [143].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Researchers proposed different management techniques to optimize the power consumption of these components 
based on the setup techniques used to design a system.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
At design time, it is very difficult to select the right 
components to design a cloud system with maximum synchronization among the components [61] [62] [66].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Other 
important challenges during system design can be: i) type of application and software, ii) selection of operating 
system and iii) placement of severs to reduce delay.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Gordan and Fast Array of Wimpy Nodes (FAWN) [3] 
architecture has been designed to improve the performance of cloud systems by balancing the input-output 
activities and computation processes by coupling datacenter powering systems and local flash storage with low 
power CPUs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Energy consumption can be reduced by proper distribution of resources geographically and the 
selection of suitable network topologies and components with maximum compatibility.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In order to save energy when the CPU is idle, the CPU can be transferred into a low-power mode, which is called 
C-states or C-modes [61] [62].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The main motive of C-states is to cut the clock signal and power from idle components 
inside the Central Processing Unit (CPU).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The more units stop (by cutting the clock), the voltage is needed or even 
CPU becomes completely shut down, the more energy can save, but more time is required for the CPU to “wake up” 
and again be 100% operational [66].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are main seven cases: i) C0 mode (Operating State) - CPU is fully turned 
on and it consumes the maximum amount of energy, ii) C1 mode (Halt) - CPU main internal clocks are stopped via 
software and it consumes less amount of energy as compared to C0 mode but needs little time to make CPU 100% 
operational, iii) C2 mode (Stop Grant and Clock) - CPU main internal and external clocks are stopped via hardware 
and it consumes less amount of energy as compared to C1 mode but needs more time to make CPU 100% operational 
as compared to C1 mode, iv) C3 mode (Sleep) - Stops all internal and external clocks of the CPU, v) C4 mode (Deeper 
Sleep) - Stops all internal clocks of the CPU and Decreases voltage of CPU, vi) C5 mode (Enhanced Deeper Sleep) 
- Decreases voltage of the CPU even more and put off the memory cache and vii) C6 mode (Deep Power Down) - 
Decreases the internal voltage of the CPU to any value, including 0V and this state consumes the minimum amount 
of energy (depends on the voltage value), but this state needs the maximum time to make CPU 100% operational.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

So, 
existing research work mainly focused on optimization of energy consumption in CPU or processor and memory.

title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Based on the different values of voltage and operational frequency, CPU 
can run in different activity modes or C-modes in advance processor architectures.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
As supply voltage increases, the 
energy consumption increases quadratically in CMOS (Complementary Metal Oxide Semiconductor) circuits [3].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The values of linear relations can be exploited by changing operation frequency (DFS), voltage (DVS) or both 
simultaneously (DVFS) [60].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
DVFS is an energy optimization power management technique, which is basically the adjustment of frequency 
settings of the computing devices in order to optimize the resource allotment for tasks, and if resources are not 
required then DVFS minimizes the CPU frequency thus by supplying lower voltage to CPU, which maximize the 
power savings [60].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
DVFS technique is used for virtual machines hosted by physical machines along with the 
algorithm or scheduling mechanism to reduce the energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
DVFS system and workload planning can be joined in 
two different manners: (1) workload scheduling, and (2) slack reclamation.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In the schedule generation, DVFS-
empowered processors are used to (re)schedule tasks of the graph in a worldwide cost function including both 
makespan (execution time) and energy saving to meet both time and energy limitations in the meantime [3].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In 
slack reclamation, which fills in as post-preparing method on the yield of planning calculations, DVFS mechanism 
is utilized to limit the power utilization of undertakings in a timetable created by a different scheduler [25].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The 
current strategies in light of DVFS strategy, have two noteworthy inadequacies: (1) a large portion of them centre 
around schedule age and do not adopt enough the slack reclamation strategies into record to spare extra energy, 
and (2) the current slack reclamation techniques utilize just a single frequency for every task among all distinct 
arrangement of processor's frequencies.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Utilizing one frequency generally brings about revealed slack time where 
processor and different devices just waste energy [66].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
DVFS based energy management techniques reduce energy 
consumption, but response time and service delay are increased due to the switching of resources between high 
scaling and low scaling modes.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are number of methods proposed to control energy consumption by scaling down the high voltage supply, but 
the best way is to exploit the stall time.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The large amount of clock speed is wasted while waiting for the data because 
of the speed gap between processor and main memory.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Energy may be saved by reducing the processor frequency 
through manipulation of supply voltage.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
For different devices, semiconductor chip vendors optimizing energy 
consumption use different frequency scaling policies.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Eight different kinds of operational frequencies are available 
in Intel’s Woodcrest Xeon Processor [3].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Two CPU throttling technologies developed by AMD are PowerNow and 
CoolnQuiet [3] [125].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Another, SpeedStep CPU throttling technology is developed by Intel to control energy 
consumption [62].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: The cooling can be internal (fans) or external (as discussed in Section 3.7) for a cloud datacenter.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The management of storage devices like disk drives is handled by scalable storage systems to reduce energy 
consumption because disk drives consume significant amounts of energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The storage of data can be managed using 
either replication or caching.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Mechanical operations of storage components consume one third of the total 
electricity provided to the CDCs, and disks also consume one tenth during standby mode.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The need of storage 
components is increasing by 60% annually [66] [67], so this is a serious research issue to control energy 
consumption.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Disk drive utilizes only 25% of their storage space and it remains underutilized in large CDCs [3] 
[71].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: The power usage can be minimized by reducing underutilization by switching-off the unnecessary disks.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Large 
number of mechanisms are proposed to improve the energy efficiency of disk drives [2].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In large scale CDCs, memory 
component may be considered to decrease power usage, but it is a least addressed component by researchers.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Memory consumes 23% of energy consumption to run specific workload [83] [125].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The dynamic range for memories 
is 50% as discussed above, so there is a chance to improve energy consumption in this component [61] [62].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
DVFS 
is also applicable to memory components by reducing frequency and voltage.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Storage arrays are the most important 
components of DRAMs in which power consumption can be reduced.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
It is challenging to develop energy-aware 
memory components in cloud computing to reduce power consumption without degradation of performance.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Also, 


 
26 
 
it is difficult to manufacture energy-efficient memory devices with lesser cost.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Existing memory management 
infrastructures can minimize energy consumption up to 70% [6].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Resource consolidation is a technique for effective utilization of resources (processor, memory or network devices) 
to minimize the number of resources and the location of servers, which a cloud company requires to serve user 
requests [71].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Resource scheduler allocates resources to execute workloads dynamically to avoid over-utilization 
and under-utilization of resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Resource management is an important challenge because: i) heterogenous resources, ii) priced differently, iii) 
applications with varying requirements (compute, data, network, memory) and iv) user QoS requirements.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
An 
effective resource management includes resource allocation, resource scheduling and resource monitoring to 
effective utilization of resources [32].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are many questions that are required to be answered [32] [71]:  
a) How to allocate the resources in an energy-efficient manner for the execution of workloads?
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: b) When to migrate workloads from one machine to another to save energy consumption?
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: c) Which devices need to be switched off to save energy consumption without degradation of performance?
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Based on existing research, the number of existing techniques above discussed issues to improve energy utilization.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: These techniques are classified into following categories: a) Proactive, b) Reactive and c) Proactive and Reactive.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Proactive management manages the resources based on the future prediction of the performance of the system 
instead of its current state.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The resources are selected based on the previous executions of the system in terms of 
reliability, energy consumption, throughput etc.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The predictions are required to be identified based on previous 
data, and plan their appropriate action to optimize energy consumption during resource execution.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Reactive 
management works based on feedback methods and manages the resources based on their current state to optimize 
energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There is a need of continuous monitoring of resource allocation to find whether the energy is consumed less 
than its threshold value or not (threshold value can be based on energy as well as resource utilization).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
If power 
usage is higher than threshold value then corrective action will be taken to optimize the energy consumption.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The 
accuracy of the monitoring module improves the productivity of reactive management.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In case of underutilization 
of resources, energy consumption can be reduced through VM consolidation or migration as discussed in Section 
3.5.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Increase in energy consumption also requires effective cooling management because temperature is increasing 
due to large amounts of heat.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Reactive and proactive management manages the resources with minimum value of 
power usage and maximum value of resource utilization to handle every situation by i) monitoring the resource 
execution continuously and ii) performing the actions based on predicted failures.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In real time, it is challenging to 
accurately forecast the behavior of a system in proactive management.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In reactive management, there is a larger 
overhead which causes unnecessary delay as well as energy inefficiency [60].

title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5 Virtualization 
Virtualization technology is an important part of sustainable cloud datacenters to support energy-efficient VM 
migration, VM elasticity, VM load balancing, VM consolidation, VM fault tolerance and VM scheduling [88].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Operational costs can be reduced by using VM scheduling to manage cloud resources using efficient dynamic 
provisioning of resources [102].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
During the execution of workloads, VM load balancing is required to balance the 
load effectively due to decentralized CDCs and renewable energy resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Due to the lack of on-site renewable 
energy, VM techniques migrate the workloads to the other machines distributed geographically.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
VM technologies 
also offer migration of workloads from renewable energy based CDCs to the CDCs utilizing the waste heat at 
another site [105].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To balance the workload demand and renewable energy, VM based workload migration and VM 
consolidation techniques provide virtual resources using few physical servers.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
VM fault tolerance creates and 
maintains the identical secondary VM for the replacement of Primary VM in failover situation without affecting 
the availability of cloud service.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
VM elasticity maintains the performance of the computing system by providing the 
dynamic adaptation of computing resources or capacity to fulfill the changing requirements of workloads.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Waste 
heat utilization and renewable energy resources alternatives are harnessed by VM migration techniques to enable 
sustainable cloud computing [104].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
It is a great challenge for VM migration techniques to improve energy savings 
and network delays while migrating workloads between resources distributed geographically.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.1 Related Studies 
VM migration is the process of migrating VMs (where a VM is the software implementation of the computer that 
runs a number of applications and operating system) to another physical server without interrupting the running 
application operation.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
A virtualization takes place when the server is underutilized or over-utilized or in case of 
temperature overpass, which improves energy efficiency of CDC.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Also, the virtualization reduces the carbon 
emission by moving the workload to location having renewable energy supply.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[99] proposed Green-
aware VM migration (GVM) policy for the efficient utilization of energy coming from grid sources and optimizing 
the power consumption of cooling and IT devices.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, a statistical searching approach is used to find out the 
destination of migration and post-copy technique is used in GVM.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[88] proposed an Extended version 
of GVM (E-GVM) by replacing grid energy with renewable energy to make datacenters sustainable, which further 
reduces power cost and carbon emissions.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, VM consolidation-based resource allocation is improved using 
IT-enabled virtualization [100], which measures the variation of energy requirements during pre-copy and post-
copy of data from one server to another.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[103] analyzed the migration time of live migration of a number 
of VMs between physical machines.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The migration time is amount of data copied from one physical machine to 
another.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Further, it also estimates the interference effects during live migration.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Kernel-based Virtual Machine 
(KVM) is used to test the proposed technique to prove its effectiveness to calculate the migration time more 
accurately.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[106] developed a technique to improve the usage of renewable energy for Online Virtual 
Machine Migration (OVMM), from one physical server to another, to enable sustainable cloud computing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In this 
research work, an optimal offline algorithm and an online algorithm are proposed for VM migration [141].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The 
offline algorithm is effectively working when future information of renewable energy is known a priori and the 
online algorithm is used when future information is unavailable.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Ranjbari and Torkestani [159] proposed a Learning Automata-based VM Consolidation (LAVMC) algorithm to 
reduce energy consumption and SLA violation rate.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, LAVMC algorithm decreases the number of 
migrations, and shuts down idle servers to decrease the energy consumption of the CDC.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Similarly, Ashraf and 
Porres [160] proposed an Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) based VM Consolidation (ACOVMC) technique to reduce 
the number of VM migrations.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[101] proposed the VM Predication and Migration (VMPM) 
mechanism for overcommitted clouds to reduce the usage of physical machines through predication of virtual 
machines and run the datacenter sustainably, thus improving the energy efficiency of CDCs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, load 
balancing mechanism distributes the load effectively on physical machines.

3.5.2 Virtualization based Taxonomy  
Based on literature, virtualization consists of the following components: i) VM migration, ii) VM elasticity, iii) VM 
load balancing, iv) VM consolidation, v) VM fault tolerance and vi) VM scheduling as shown in Figure 15.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Each of 
these taxonomy components are discussed below along with their sub-components and relevant examples.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Figure 15: Taxonomy Based on Virtualization 
The comparison of existing techniques based on our virtualization taxonomy is given in Table 16 (VM Migration, 
VM Elasticity and VM Load Balancing) and Table 17 (VM Consolidation, VM Fault Tolerance and VM Scheduling).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.1 VM Migration based Taxonomy 
VM migration is a process of relocation of a running VM from one physical machine to another without affecting 
the execution of user application.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Based on literature [101] [102] [106] [164], VM migration consists of the following 
components: i) technique, ii) VM technology, iii) optimization criteria, iv) network technology and v) storage 
migration as shown in Figure 16.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Figure 16: Taxonomy Based on VM Migration 
3.5.2.1.1 Technique: VMs can be migrated from one place to another for better utilization of resources and it 
reduces the under-utilization and over-utilization of resources [99].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Three types of techniques have been proposed 
for VM migration: 1) Pre-copy, 2) Post-copy, 3) and Pre-copy and Post-copy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are two different phases of pre-
copy technique: a) warm-up and b) stop and copy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In warm-up phase, the hypervisor copies the state from source 
server to destination server, which contains the information about the memory state and the CPU state.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Stop and 
copy phase copies the pending files (if any file is modified during the warm-up phase) from source to destination 
servers and starts the execution at destination server [88].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In post-copy, it stops the VM at the source server, 
transfers all the details like CPU state and memory state to the destination server and starts execution.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Some VM 
migration mechanisms use both pre-copy and post-copy together to transfer states from one server to another.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.1.2 VM technology: There are three different types of technology that are available in literature for VM 
migration: KVM, Xen and VMware.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
KVM is a Kernel-based VM, which permits many Operating Systems (OSs) to 
share single resource or hardware.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Xen is working based on microkernel design to share the same resources to run 
multiple OSs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: VMware can be used for application consolidation to provide services through virtualization [101].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.1.3 Optimization criteria: It is identified that optimization criteria for virtualization technology can be 
compressed or write throttling.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
ESXi is an independent hypervisor, which offers memory compression cache to 
increase the performance of VMs and it further increases the capacity of the CDC [105].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Write throttling is used to 
perform write and incoming copy operations, which limit the transfer of data [106].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.1.4 Network technology: There are two different type of network technologies are used for VM migration: i) 
WAN and LAN.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Wide Area Network (WAN) is used to migrate VM geographically using wireless connection, while 
Local Area Network (LAN) is used to migrate VM from one server to another within limited area.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

3.5.2.1.5 Storage migration: In this technique, storage from one running server to another can be migrated 
without affecting the workload execution of VMs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Storage migration can also be used to upgrade storage resources 
or transfer service [101] [32].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: The distributed files systems can be used to provide shared storage space.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In virtualized cloud environments, VM migration is the mostly used mechanism to achieve energy efficiency at 
runtime [88].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The value of the migration time rapidly increases as the value of available network bandwidth reduces 
and also size of VM; but migration time can be decreased by consolidation of VMs, which improves resource 
utilization and effective utilization of resources can reduce energy consumption [101].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Furthermore, the energy 
consumption depends on the size of the VM, which is migrated.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Remarkably, for the similar set of VMs, different 
orders of migrations lead to different migration-time based on VM size [102] [106].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
So, there is a requirement to 
investigate the trade-off between energy cost and migration time of VMs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The followings are the important issues with VM migration in geographically distributed datacenters [88] [99] [105] 
[106]: 
• 
It is challenging to transfer VMs on shared bandwidth while maintaining the SLA of an application because 
memory size of VM is dynamic, which varies from 1 GB to 50+ GBs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
• 
WAN based VM migration has many issues such as higher packet drop ratio, larger communication distances, 
heterogeneous network architecture design, unpredictable network behavior, greater latencies and limited 
network bandwidth, which can increase the possibility of SLA violation.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
• 
VM migration complexity increases with the increase of WAN-based storage migration because live storage 
migration needs asynchronous and synchronous communication modes to transmit storage blocks from one 
CDC to another.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
• 
Moreover, existing VM migration techniques are not able to distribute load dynamically in a coordination 
manner among various CDCs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
• 
Due to longer communication distances, secure VM migration on heterogeneous CDCs is a challenging task.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Consequently, hijackers acquire hardware states, application sensitive data, currently hosted applications and 
OS kernel states for malicious activities.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Container as a Service (CaaS) such as Kubernetes, Docker etc.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
uses resource isolation features of Linux kernel such 
as Control groups (Cgroups) and kernel namespaces to allow independent containers to run within a single Linux 
instance to avoid substantial overhead of starting virtual machines on hypervisors [156].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The shifting to container-
based deployments can reduce overheads related to deployment of containers.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, CaaS can increase 
realization by supporting real-time workloads [40].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Container-based deployments outperforms VMs transition 
based deployment due to following reasons [37] [99]:  a) containers start up very quickly and their launching time 
is less than a second and b) containers have tiny memory footprint and consume a very small amount of resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Moreover, containers permit the host to support more instances simultaneously as compared to VM based cloud 
testbed.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.2 VM Elasticity based Taxonomy 
VM elasticity enables the automatic provisioning and de-provisioning of computing resources to fulfill the changing 
demand of workloads at runtime.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Based on literature [40] [37] [163] [164], VM elasticity consists of the following 
components: i) scope ii) policy, iii) objective and iv) mechanism as shown in Figure 17.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Figure 17: Taxonomy Based on VM Elasticity  
3.5.2.2.1 Scope: It defines the location, where the elasticity actions are managed, which can be application (SaaS) 
or platform level (PaaS) and infrastructure level (IaaS) [62].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
At IaaS level, the elasticity controller monitors the

application execution and perform different decisions based on resource (hardware) scalability.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
At SaaS or PaaS 
level, the elasticity controller is implanted in application or within the execution platform, which performs the 
dynamic scalability of cloud resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.2.2 Policy: There are two types of policies for the execution of elasticity actions: autonomic and non-autonomic 
[66].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In autonomic policy, cloud system or application controls the elasticity actions and performs action based on 
the SLA constraints.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In manual policy, user monitors the virtual environment and performs the elasticity actions 
accordingly.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.2.3 Objective: VM elasticity techniques have three main objectives: 1) improve performance, 2) increase 
infrastructure capacity and 3) reduce energy [67].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The main objective of VM elasticity techniques to improve 
performance such as optimal searching of VM, reduce task rejection rate and makespan.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The second objective is to 
reduce energy consumption of CDC during execution of workloads.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The third objective is to improve the 
infrastructure capacity by adding different resources at runtime to execute workloads within their specified budget 
and deadline.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.2.4 Mechanism: There are two different mechanisms for VM elasticity as identified form literature [83]: 
migration and replication.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To migrate the VM from one physical machine to another for effective utilization of 
application load using deconsolidation and consolidation of resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Replication refers to elimination and removal 
of instances (application modules, containers, VMs) from virtual environment.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.3 VM Load Balancing based Taxonomy 
VM load balancing refers to the optimization of utilization of VMs to reduce resource wastage due to underloading 
and overloading of resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
It helps to achieve QoS and maximize resource utilization to improve performance of 
cloud service.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Based on literature [88] [101] [162], VM load balancing consists of the following components: i) 
resource-aware and ii) performance-aware as shown in Figure 18.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Figure 18: Taxonomy Based on VM Load Balancing  
3.5.2.3.1 Resource-aware: CDC require different type of resources (memory, processor, cooling, storage, 
networking etc.) to execute user workloads [74].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Resource-aware load balancing algorithm execute workloads and 
it also monitors and analyses the different performance parameters related to resources such as energy 
consumption, degree of resource capacity imbalance and resource utilization to perform load balancing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are 
three different types of resource-aware load balancing algorithms: bin-packing, agent-based and dynamic cluster-
based.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In bin-packing, different bins are used to pack objects of different capacities and it uses minimum number 
of bins to provide the same capacity in a balanced way.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In agent-based, a software agent is used to monitor the 
performance of different components such as network devices, storage device and processor and balances the load 
effectively.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In dynamic cluster-based, resources are categorized automatically based on requirement and 
availability of resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, categorized resources are allocated for execution of workloads with maximum 
resource utilization and minimum energy consumption.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.3.2 Performance-aware: In performance-aware load balancing algorithms, different performance 
parameters are analyzed to make decisions for effective load balancing of VMs [80].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are two different types 
of performance-aware load balancing algorithms: adaptive and QoS-based.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In adaptive, performance is maintained 
using dynamic computing environment for execution of workloads with changing behavior.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In QoS-based, resources 
are provisioned and scheduled for workload execution by fulfilling the QoS requirements of applications such as 
energy efficiency, makespan, execution cost and response time.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

3.5.2.4 VM Consolidation based Taxonomy 
VM consolidation refers to the effective usage of VMs to improve resource utilization and reduce energy 
consumption [49].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Based on literature [99] [102] [159] [160], VM consolidation consists of the following components: 
i) resource assignment policy, ii) architecture, iii) co-location criteria and iv) migration triggering point as shown 
in Figure 19.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Figure 19: Taxonomy Based on VM Consolidation  
3.5.2.4.1 Resource assignment policy: It defines the mechanism to select resources for virtual machines within 
a CDC [125] and resource assignment policy can be static or dynamic.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In dynamic approach, VMs are reconfigured 
using dynamic attributes proactively based on the demand of workloads.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In static approach, maximum resources 
are pre-assigned to VM for workload execution.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.4.2 Architecture: There are two different types of architectures, which are used in VM consolidation 
techniques: centralized and decentralized as described in Section 3.1.2.4.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There is no risk of a single failure point 
in decentralized architectures, while centralized architectures are prone to single failure point.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.4.3 Co-location criteria:  There are two main types of co-location criteria in VM consolidation techniques, 
which is considered based on: resource availability and power [71].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
VMs can be co-located from one CDC to another: 
i) if there is less number of resources are available in current CDC or ii) if there is unavailability of adequate power 
to run CDC.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.4.4 Migration triggering point: VMs can be migrated from one CDC to another for consolidation and target 
CDC is identified using two different approaches [67]: historic data and heuristic based.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In historic data based 
approach, VM can be migrated to the most efficient CDC based on their historic data of previous performance.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In 
heuristic based approach, the most efficient CDC can be identified based on their performance parameters such as 
resource utilization, energy consumption and response time.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.5 VM Fault Tolerance based Taxonomy 
VM Fault Tolerance supports primary VM by maintaining the identical secondary VM to provide continuous 
availability of cloud service in case of VM failure.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Based on literature [105] [106] [157] [161], VM fault tolerance 
consists of the following components: i) redundancy, ii) failure semantics, iii) recovery and iv) failure masking as 
shown in Figure 20.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.5.1 Redundancy: In case of resource failure, redundancy provides redundant components to maintain the 
performance of computing system, which can be software or hardware [125].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
For hardware components, physical 
redundancy technique adds redundant hardware components to tolerate failures, which support computing system 
to continue its service in an efficient manner.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
For software components, two different types of processes are created: 
active (primary) and passive (backup).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The backup process is identical to the primary process and backup process 
will be active during the failure of primary process to maintain the performance of the system.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.5.2 Failure semantics: It refers to the selection of failure tolerance method based on the two types of failure 
modes [83]: arbitrary errors and crash failure errors.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
An arbitrary error occurs when communication service to lose 
or delay messages or message may be corrupted.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
A crash failure error occurs when system suddenly stops processing 
of instructions.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: To deal with both type of failures, computing system needs duplicate processor.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

3.5.2.5.3 Recovery: This mechanism replaces the erroneous state with stable state using different recovery 
mechanisms [122], which are Forward Error Recovery (FER) and backward (or rollback).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
FER mechanism tries to 
correct the errors to move the system into new correct state and this mechanism is effective when there is a need 
of continue service.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Backward Error Recovery (BER) or Rollback-recovery is widely used fault tolerance mechanism, 
which consists of two different methods: checkpoint and restart recovery.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Restart recovery mechanism performs the 
process of rebooting to recover or restore the system to correct state.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To incorporate fault tolerance into system, a 
snapshot of the application's state is saved, so that system can reboot from that point in case of system crash, this 
process is called checkpointing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Checkpoint can be performed at three different levels: application, user and system.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In application-level, a checkpointing code is inserted automatically into the application code if failure is occurred 
and checkpointing code can be write using single-thread or multi-thread programming.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In user level, an application 
program is linked to the library and Condo [20] and Esky [66] are library implementations.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, user can use 
patch to perform user level checkpointing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In system level, the process of checkpoint can be performed at OS kernel 
level and hardware level.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The digital hardware is used in hardware level checkpointing to modify a group of 
commodity hardware.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: OS kernel level checkpointing installs the available package for a particular OS.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.5.4 Failure masking: Failure masking technique ensures the availability of cloud service during failure of 
nodes without the user observing any interruption [144] [145].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are two types of masking techniques: flat and 
hierarchical group masking.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In flat group masking, individual workers are appearing as a single worker and hidden 
from the clients and a new worker will be selected using voting process [14] in case of failure.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In hierarchical group 
masking, a central coordinator controls the activities of different workers and coordinator selects the new worker 
in case of failure.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.6 VM Scheduling based Taxonomy 
VM scheduling algorithm schedules the virtual resources (local or remote) effectively for workload execution.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Based 
on literature [60] [61] [40] [157] [158], VM scheduling consists of the following components: i) application type, ii) 
operating environment and iii) objective function as shown in Figure 21.

3.5.2.6.1 Application type: Cloud application consist of different tasks, which needs computing resources for their 
execution [95] and it is of two types: workload and workflow.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
A workload is the execution of set of instances to 
achieve desired output and it can be either homogeneous (same QoS requirements) or heterogenous (different QoS 
requirements).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Workflow is a combination of interrelated tasks, which distributes on different resources to achieve 
a single objective.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.6.2 Operational environment: There are two types of operational environment: dynamic and distributed or 
it can be both [143].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In dynamic environment, VMs are scheduled for workload execution to reduce resource wastage 
and energy consumption.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In distributed environment, optimized VMs are scheduled from different CDC, which are 
distributed geographically to improve resource utilization for workload execution.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.5.2.6.3 Objective function: Literature reported that there are two types of objective functions for VM scheduling: 
1) to reduce energy cost and 2) to reduce power consumption.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The energy cost is a combination of monetary and non-
monetary costs associated with energy usage for scheduling of VMs [3].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The power consumption is the amount of 
electricity expended by resource to complete the execution of an application [62].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View
