For effective management of virtualized cloud datacenters, thermal-aware scheduling is required to execute 
workloads on energy-efficient computing resources, which further reduce the heat recirculation and therefore the 
load on the cooling systems.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.6 Thermal-aware Scheduling  
Cloud datacenters consist of chassis and racks to place the servers to process the IT workloads.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To maintain the 
temperature of datacenters, cooling mechanisms are used to reduce heat [86].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
So, there is a need of effective 
management of temperature to run the cloud datacenter efficiently.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Servers produce heat during execution of IT 
workload, so cooling-management is required to keep the stable temperature of room [92].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The processor is an 
important component of a server that consumes the most electricity.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Sometimes the heat generation of processors 
is higher than the threshold because servers are organized in a compact manner [93].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Both cooling and computing 
mechanisms are consuming a huge amount of electricity.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
It would be better to reduce the energy consumption 
instead of improvement of cooling mechanism [90].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To solve the heating problem of CDCs, thermal-aware 


 
36 
 
scheduling is designed to minimize cooling setpoint temperature, hotspots and thermal gradient.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Thermal-aware 
scheduling is better than heat modelling [142].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Thermal-aware scheduling based on heat modelling performs 
computational scheduling of workload.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Thermal-aware monitoring and profiling module monitors and assess the 
distribution of heat in CDCs while profiling maintains the details of computational workload, microprocessors and 
heat emission of servers.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
With the use of renewable energy, the load of cooling can be decreased to enable 
sustainable CDCs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

management of green datacenters.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Authors stated that the microprocessor is the most important part of the server, 
which consumes large amounts of electricity and produces heat continuously.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, efficient cooling 
management is required to avoid overheating of servers.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Moreover, thermal monitoring and profiling approaches 
provide different techniques for measuring both lower level (microprocessor) and upper level (datacenter) 
temperatures to reduce generation of heat [142].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Authors did not identify the effect of thermal-aware scheduling 
on sustainability and energy efficiency of CDCs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[84] analyzed that a sufficient amount of cooling is 
required to maintain the temperature for smooth working of sustainable datacenters.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, cloud workloads 
should be executed before deadline using available electricity but sharing of resources creates problems for the 
execution of different tasks on different cores of available resources [95].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Co-location, power and thermal-aware

resource allocation techniques have been proposed to execute a number of tasks.

Experimental results proved that 
this approach is effective in executing tasks before a deadline and under a temperature constraint.

[85] proposed the Energy-Efficient Workload Management (EEWM) approach for thermal-aware 
CDCs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Further, workloads and applications are managed effectively by creating their profile.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

Moreover, power-
aware resource scheduling mechanism has been proposed to execute the workloads, while optimizing energy 
consumption.

between power and cooling and execute user workloads in a sustainable cloud environment.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

3.6.2 Thermal-aware Scheduling based Taxonomy  
The components of thermal-aware scheduling are: i) architecture, ii) heat modelling, iii) thermometer, iv) 
scheduling, v) monitoring and awareness and vi) simulator as shown in Figure 23.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Each of these taxonomy elements 
are discussed below along with relevant examples.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The comparison of existing techniques based on our thermal-
aware scheduling taxonomy is given in Table 19.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Figure 23: Taxonomy Based on Thermal-aware Scheduling 
3.6.2.1 Architecture: Thermal-aware scheduling techniques have been designed based on different architectures: 
i) single core and ii) multicore [86] [92] [93].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Thermal-aware scheduling techniques execute workloads based on 
their priorities at different speed of processor for single-core architecture and for execution of high priority 
workload, current workload can be preempted.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Generally, high priority workloads are running at high speed and 
the temperature of processor can be reached to its threshold value.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To optimize the temperature of the processor, 
low priority workloads are running at lower speed to cool down the processor.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To improve the execution of thermal-
aware scheduling, multi-core processor is using in which a task is divided into number of threads and independent 
threads are running on different cores based on their priorities.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Multi-core processors are designed with thermal-
aware aspects such as intelligent fan control, clock gating and frequency scaling and these aspects are working in 
coordination to control the temperature within its operating limits.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
If one core is getting hot then a thread can be 
transfer to another cooler core to maintain the temperature.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.6.2.2 Heat-modelling: It is an effective mechanism in thermal-aware scheduling to develop a relationship 
between eventual heat dissipation and energy consumed by computing devices.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The scope of heat models is defined 
based on evaluation of environmental variables like temperature, air pressure and power.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The selection of the heat 
model also affects the energy efficiency.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The types of heat models used in existing literature are: i) thermodynamics 
model, ii) RC model, iii) thermal network and iv) heat recirculation.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Thermodynamics model is used to explore the heat exchange mechanisms in CDCs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The value of heat is quantified 
using law of energy conservation [89] [90].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Thermodynamic process produces the details about heat emissions, 
energy consumption and pass cold air to remove heat from the datacenter and researchers are still working on this 
process for further optimization.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
RC model is basically a Resistor–Capacitor (RC) circuit to make a relationship 
between electrical phenomena of RC circuit and heat transfer.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Temperature difference between two surfaces and 
energy consumption is used to find out the value of R and C for conductance and convention.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

parameters.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Thermal network is based on both RC model and thermodynamics model.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In thermal network, every 
node of CDC belongs to one of the network, which can be IT network or cooling network.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
A server executes workload 
by consuming energy and producing heat and server is part of both cooling and IT network.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Thermal network is 
efficient for heat modelling of heterogenous equipment of a datacenter.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Heat recirculation deals with mixing of hot 
air (coming from server outlets) and cold air (coming from the cooling manager).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Temperature of cold air is changing 
with time after entering into CDCs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To maintain the temperature of CDC, it is a great challenge to provide the 
uniform cold air temperature every time.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The resource utilization of servers which participates in heat recirculation 
will be reduced and performance of cloud datacenters is also affected in terms of QoS.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: 3.6.2.3 Thermometer: This is a device, which is used to measure the temperature of cloud datacenter.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are 
two types of thermometers have been identified from literature [14] [86] [92]: i) digital and ii) analog.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The digital 
or infrared thermometer is an electronic device, which uses digital sensor to provide a digital display.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Most digital 
thermometers are resistive thermal devices, which uses a function of electrical resistance to measure the 
temperature variations.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The analog thermometer contains alcohol, which falls or rises as it contracts or expands 
with temperature variations and temperature value is displaying in degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit, which is marked 
on glass capillary tube.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.6.2.4 Scheduling: The energy consumed by CDCs has been utilized for execution of workloads, but it is 
dissipated as heat.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Lower energy is used to remove heat while workloads are scheduling using thermal-aware 
aspects.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Thermal profiles of thermal-aware schedulers are used to find out the resource with minimum dissipation 
of heat in cloud datacenters.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The aim of thermal-aware scheduling is to reduce dissipation of heat from active 
servers and minimize the active servers by turning off idle servers.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Three types of thermal-aware scheduling are 
used in the existing literature [85] [86] [89] [92] are: i) QoS, ii) optimized, iii) reactive and proactive.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
QoS based 
thermal-aware scheduling schedules the energy-efficient resources to improve the performance of the cloud 
datacenter.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The scheduler controls the temperature and reduces the load of overcooling using dynamic thermal 
management techniques.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, a challenge of maintaining the SLA based on these QoS parameters is introduced 
and it requires the trade-off between cost saving and compensation or penalty in case of SLA violations.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Optimized 
thermal-aware scheduling schedule workloads using the concept of an autonomic computing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
These techniques are 
basically a combination of heat-recirculation and thermal-aware techniques.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The main aim of server based 
scheduling techniques is to reduce the peak inlet temperature which is increased by heat-recirculation.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Heat-
recirculation can be minimized by placing lesser workloads on servers that are nearer to the floor.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Processor based 
scheduling techniques execute the workloads by sustaining the steady core temperature called throttling.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Earlier, 
workloads are executed using zig-zag schemes till a temperature threshold is achieved.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Reactive management 
works based on feedback methods and manages the temperature based on their current state to maintain its 
temperature.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There is a need of continuous monitoring of thermal-aware scheduling to find whether the 
temperature is lower than its threshold value or not.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
If temperature is higher than a threshold value then corrective 
actions will be taken to make it stable.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The proactive approach manages the resources based on the prediction and 
assessment of temperature and thermal profiling.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Based on previous data, predictions have been identified and 
plan their required action to reduce temperature during scheduling.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.6.2.5 Monitoring and Awareness: Thermal monitoring and awareness is used to perform thermal-aware 
scheduling decisions.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The thermal profile is created based on resultant heat dissipation and power consumption for 
thermal-awareness, which is used to rank the servers for future scheduling decisions.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are three different 
methods of thermal monitoring and awareness as identified form literature [14] [32] [85] [86]: i) manual profiling 
and monitoring, ii) thermal gadgets and iii) thermal data filtering and predictions.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In manual profiling and 
monitoring, heat generation and recirculation, and power consumption of individual servers is noted manually to 
create thermal profile.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: If there is no real data available then simulation tools can be used for manual profiling.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Some thermal-aware scheduling techniques [89] [92] [93] [97] estimates the thermal index to evaluate the efficiency 
of different cloud datacenters and perform their ranking.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The thermal gadgets such as thermal cameras and sensors 
are used to generate the accurate and timely thermal information automatically.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The multiple sensors can be used 
per unit area and both onboard and externals thermal sensors can be used to collect thermal information.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In 
thermal data filtering and predictions, rise in temperature and resulting heat can be predicted for proactive 
thermal-aware scheduling, which helps to make effective decisions to minimize thermal gradient and peak outlet 


 
41 
 
temperature.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The advance prediction of temperature and heat can help to maintain the QoS during workload 
execution.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.6.2.6 Simulator: The results of thermal simulators can be used to create thermal profiles and there are three 
different simulators identified from literature [14] [86] [92] [14] [32] [85] [86]: i) CFD, ii) HotSpot and iii) FloVent.

modeling tool [14], which uses thermal resistances to design the architecture of cloud datacenter based on power

contamination distribution, heat transfer and 3D airflow for different types of cloud datacenters, which mainly

text:
3.7 Cooling Management 
The increasing demand for computation, networking and storage expands the complexity, size and energy density 
of cloud datacenters exponentially, which consumes large amount of energy and produces a huge amount of heat 
[14].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To make cloud datacenters more energy-efficient and sustainable, we need an effective cooling management 
system, which can maintain the temperature of cloud datacenters [21] The heat dissipation is a critical factor to be 
considered for cooling management of CDC, which affects the reliability and availability of the cloud service.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In 
cloud datacenter, high heat density causes high temperature, which needs to be controlled for smooth functioning 
of CDC [86].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
An effective cooling management can attain a complete environmental control including pollution 
concentration, humidity and air temperature [92].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
So, it is mandatory to discuss the existing and emerging 
technologies for data center cooling systems to find out the effective solution to maintain CDC’s working in a safe 
and reliable manner.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
42 
 
3.7.1 Related Studies  
Ndukaife and Nnanna [150] proposed a Split Air-Conditioning System (SACS) based cooling management 
technique, which investigates the characteristics of water consumption to test the performance.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, authors 
vary the thickness of cooling pad to investigate its effect on the coefficient of performance.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
SACS technique is 
efficient in maintaining the adequate quantity of humidity with same amount of water consumption while cooling 
the cloud datacenter.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: SACS technique helps to reduce the energy consumption using process of cooling.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Wu et al 
[151] proposed Weather-Aware Geo-Scheduling (WAGS) based cooling management technique, which reduces the 
energy consumption for cooling while distributing the load of end users among different datacenters.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
A workload 
distribution model is designed, which primarily focuses on the SLA constraints during workload execution.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Moreover, trace-driven experiments have been conducted on real clouds to test the performance of WAGS technique 
and experimental results show that the proposed technique performs effectively in terms of energy consumption 
and latency.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[152] proposed a Server Utilization-based Smart Temperature Monitoring (SUSTM) 
technique, which maintains the cooling of CDC.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In this technique, the concept of Mean Utilization Factor is used 
to find and control the amount of cool air to maintain the operating temperature in and around the servers within 
a CDC.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[153] proposed a Natural Convection based Liquid Immersion (NCLI) cooling technology for saving 
energy consumption and space.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
CFD simulator [86] is used to test the performance of NCLI technique and the 
experimental results show that the proposed technique is effective in improving the cooling-efficiency, which 
further improves the value of PUE.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[154] proposed a Cloud-Assisted Smart Temperature Control (CASTC) 
system, which uses IoT sensing technology to enable green data center air conditioning for cooling.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
CASTC system 
has two subcomponents: i) cloud management platform (which offers support to application layer and manage data 
effectively) and ii) datacenter air conditioning system (which includes ventilation and temperature control, air 
conditioning and environment monitoring).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
CASTC system effectively reduces the energy consumption of CDC 
without affecting the cooling management.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[155] proposed an Under-provisioning Datacenter 
Cooling (UDC) technique to reduce the cost of cooling by under-provisioning the infrastructure of cloud datacenter.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The authors developed a trade-off between cooling and QoS and they suggested that the processing capacity can be 
reduced in case of relaxed deadline by selecting the available cheapest provisioning.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The experimental results show 
that UDC technique is capable to reduce cooling cost.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.8 Renewable Energy 
Sustainable computing needs the energy-efficient workload execution by utilizing renewable energy resources to 
reduce carbon emissions [117].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Fossil fuels such as oil, gas and coal generate brown energy and it produces carbon-
dioxide emissions in large extent but green energy resources such as sun, wind and water generate energy with 
nearly zero carbon-dioxide emissions [121].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
One type of green energy is hydroelectricity, which is produced using 
hydraulic power.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Wind and solar energy can be purchased from off-site companies or can be generated using on-
site equipment [118].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In the next decade, the cost/watt will be reduced by half for renewable energy due to following 
reasons: i) government organizations provide monetary incentives for the incorporation of resources of renewable 
energy, ii) the storage capacity of rechargeable batteries will be increased and iii) advancement in technology to 
improve capacity of materials like photovoltaic arrays [124].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Workload migration and energy-aware load balancing 
techniques addressed the issue of unpredictability in the supply of renewable energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To make the 100% availability 
of cloud services, it is recommended to adopt hybrid designs of energy generation, which use energy from renewable 
resources and grid resources [117].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Mostly, sites of commercial CDCs are located away from abundant renewable 
energy resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Consequently, portable CDCs are placed nearer to the renewable energy sources to make it cost 
effective.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.8.1 Related Studies 
Running CDCs using renewable sources of energy like wind, solar, water etc.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
instead of energy generated from 
fossil fuels (grid electricity) result in lower carbon emissions and lower operational costs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Renewable energy results 
in almost zero carbon footprint, as compared to brown energy, which results reduction in metric tons of carbon.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Grid electricity contributes to high operational costs and high energy usage.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[18] identified that 
business operations of different cloud providers such as Microsoft, Google, Facebook, Intel, Amazon are consuming 
large amounts of electricity continuously, which are increasing the environmental impact on society.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To overcome 
this impact, green cloud computing is required, which can provide more sustainable cloud services.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Renewable 
resources of energy (wind or solar) can be utilized to produce electricity, which reduces cost due to grid electricity 
[8].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To make an effective use of renewable energy, datacenters should be located nearer to the source of energy to 
adopt green cloud computing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Even the use of mixed energy (renewable and non-renewable) generated will also 
increase cost by 13%.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Accenture [17] identified that datacenters produced 116 million tons carbon dioxide 


 
45 
 
equivalent (mtCO2e), telecom services produced 307 mtCO2e and IT devices produced 407 mtCO2e.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Due to the 
intermittent and unpredictable nature of renewable power supply, some mechanisms should be adopted for making 
the renewable supply constant as the most workload is dynamic and time sensitive in nature.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The two categories 
of managing renewable energy are: i) dynamic load balancing and ii) renewable energy-based workload migration.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.8.1.1 Dynamic load balancing technique: In this technique, a cloud datacenter is powered by two sources of 
energy: Green energy and Grid energy [118].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There is a server rack powered by renewable energy supply and server 
rack powered by grid electricity; switching of the workload between these two racks take place based on the energy 
supply.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There is a dynamic load balancing between Green electricity and Grid electricity according to i) renewable 
supply based on weather data and ii) workload demand based on workload traces [119].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Renewable energy supply 
is exploited if it is available even for deadline sensitive workloads.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In case of non- availability of renewable energy, 
workloads are served by grid supply instead of bringing the server in low power state [124].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The design implements 
hybrid grid-renewable supply design, where cloud datacenters are powered by either of the energies, VM migration 
is used to shift workload between the servers [121].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.8.1.2 Renewable energy-based workload migration: The workload is migrated between the geographically 
located cloud datacenter’s according to the availability of renewable energy [119] [126].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
This approach requires the 
availability of a number of cloud datacenters at different locations so the maximum amount of renewable energy is 
exploited according to the availability.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
A dynamic request routing mechanism is used to route the user request or 
workload towards the datacenter with abundant supply.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[117] proposed the Renewable Energy-Aware (REA) approach that chooses energy source (hydrogen fuel 
cell, lithium polymer battery and lead acid cell) to store power.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
This study identified that hydrogen fuel cell is 
effective in providing long life to stored energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, a sustainability index is designed based on factors such as 
environment, biological, technical and economic to identify the energy source based on user requirements to make 
it more eco-friendly.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[118] proposed an Industrial Metabolism Approach (IMA) to find out green gas 
production pathways for effective use of renewable energy to generate power for the smooth working of CDCs in a 
sustainable manner.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, a decentralized energy system is simulated using Material Flow Analysis [18] to 
calculate indirect material and energy requirements.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, temporal dynamics identify energy consumption, 
carbon footprint and environmental impact to find the sustainable pathway.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[119] proposed a 
Renewable-Aware Technique (RAT) for sustainable datacenters to perform load balancing of web applications 
geographically.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Based on the availability of renewable resources, load balancing of web application requests is 
distributed geographically and processed at different sites of resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Real traffic of Wikipedia is used as workload 
to test the proposed technique and experimental results prove that RAT is effective in utilization of green resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[120] investigated and analyzed available renewable energy-aware approaches for the sustainability 
of CDCs available in Malaysia and identified the available renewable energy sources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, it has been also 
concluded that the use of renewable energy sources reduces the carbon emissions and creates an eco-friendly 
environment.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[121] proposed the Multi-Criteria Model (MCM) to evaluate the feasibility of renewable energy and 
considered four types of energy sources like wind energy, solar energy, hydropower and biomass.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, different 
aspects of sustainability are considered such as economic, social and ecological aspects for development of 
renewable energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[122] analyzed the use of renewable and electrical energy for communication 
technology like social networking websites, mobile applications, banking websites etc.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
This study describes that 4G 
devices consume more energy as compared to 3G and 2G.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
It is challenging to quantify the sustainability of 
renewable energy resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To measure sustainability, grey rational analysis based an indicator is developed [123] 
by considering important aspects (economic, social and ecological) of sustainability.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[124] proposed a

3.8.2.1 Workload scheduling: The scheduling of workloads in renewable energy-aware techniques has been done 
in two ways: i) dynamic load balancing and ii) power preserving.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Dynamic load balancing is the most famous 
approach to make a balance between renewable energy and grid energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
These techniques supply renewable energy 
to execute workloads efficiently and predict the amount of energy that can be produced to run a CDC and the 
amount of energy that is needed to execute the workloads using that energy at the demand side.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There is a large 
requirement of renewable energy for deadline oriented workloads [121] [124].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
On the other side, workloads are 
scheduled using server power-preserving techniques.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
These techniques use power transition and voltage scaling to 
run the suitable workload using available renewable energy to balance demand-supply.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, DVFS based 
power-preserving techniques are also designed to control the energy based on operational frequency along with 
voltage scaling.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In these approaches [117] [118] [119], the workload (web application) requests are distributed to 
the specific datacenter by matching the workload demand with the available renewable energy across geo-dispersed 
CDCs by using a load balancing algorithm.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View
A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Each 
datacenter has autoscaler in addition to local load balancer that add/removes web servers dynamically in response 
to the request [124].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The incoming request is distributed among a geo-dispersed CDC based on the place that has 
a higher availability of renewable energy, so that maximum renewable energy is utilized for making datacenter 
sustainable.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In case of not having enough renewable energy the request is redirected to the location having cheap 
brown electricity.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The global load balancer, uses ‘weighted round robin’ load balancing algorithm to redirect the 
requests.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.8.2.2 Focus: There are three main objectives of renewable energy-aware techniques to: i) meet deadline, ii) reduce 
energy consumption and iii) improve renewable energy utilization [121] [126].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
SLA is an important component and 
workload should be executed without violation of SLA.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Cloud providers are mainly focused on the deadline of the 
workload during execution.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Other renewable energy-aware techniques focus on minimizing power usage of CDCs 
to execute workloads.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, renewable energy can be utilized effectively while placing the cloud datacenter 
nearer to the source of renewable energy to save more energy and utilized to process more work.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.8.2.3 Source of energy: There are three different kinds of energy sources as identified from literature [118] [117]: 
i) solar, ii) wind, iii) water and iii) hydrogen fuel cells.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The renewable energy can be generated using sun light or it 
can be generated using wind to run generator to produce electricity.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Some techniques used the combination of both 
solar and wind.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Other sources of renewable energy can be water as well as hydrogen fuel cells [117] [126].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.8.2.4 Location-aware: In renewable energy generation, energy can be stored using three different localities 
[121] [124]: i) on-site, ii) off-site and iii) co-location.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In on-site locality, utilization of renewable energy is done at 
same place where energy is produced.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In off-site, place of utilization of renewable energy is different than the place 
generating energy, means energy can be transported to off-shore site.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
On the other hand, CDCs are co-located from 
different places to sites where the chances of utilization of renewable energy are existing.

text:
3.9 Waste Heat Utilization 
 
 
Reuse of waste heat is becoming a solution for fulfilling the demand of energy in energy conservation systems 
because fossil fuel deposits are being reduced swiftly.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There is a need of cooling management to maintain the 
temperature of CDC in operational range due to generation of large amounts of heat during energy consumption.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: The cooling mechanism of CDC consumes large amount of electricity i.e.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Power densities of servers 
are increased by using stacked and multi-core server designs, which further increases the cooling costs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The energy 
efficiency of CDC may be improved by reducing the energy utilized in cooling.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There is a need to change the location 
of CDCs to reduce cooling costs and it can be done through placing the CDCs to that area which has availability of 
free cooling resources.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Due to consumption of large amount of energy, CDCs are acting as a heat generator [130] 
[131].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The vapor-absorption based cooling systems of CDCs can use waste heat, then it takes away the heat while 
evaporating.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Vapor-absorption based free cooling mechanisms can make the value of PUE ideal by neutralizing 
cooling expenses.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Low temperature areas can use the heat generated by cloud datacenters for heating facilities.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Literature reported [3] [71] [131] that there are two main solutions to control temperature of CDCs: 1) relocation 
of CDCs to nearby waste heat utilization recovery places, 2) vapor-absorption based cooling systems.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.9.1 Related Studies 
The waste heat dissipated from various electronic components (servers utilizes about 40-50% of the energy to cool 
down in CDCs) [132].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Nowadays a vast amount of waste heat is generated by the cloud datacenters due to rising 
demand of cloud based services and performance.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The concept of waste heat utilization is used to capture and reuse 
the waste heat (to heat power plant) thus reducing the load on cooling equipment’s that is used to cool the servers.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: It also contributes in reducing the carbon emissions and the operational costs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The waste heat recovery is better 
done on-site as the heat generated is not of good quality and large quantity of heat is wasted during the transfer to 
off-site heat recovery sites.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Thus, on site Waste Heat Utilization (WHU) is more beneficial.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The broad classification 
of waste heat utilization techniques is: i) Air Recirculation and ii) Power Plant Co-location.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: 3.9.1.1 Air recirculation: This technique enables the reuse of waste heat in a CDC.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In this technique, the servers 
are place with their front ends facing each others (known as cold aisles), so the back end of servers face each other 
(known as hot aisles).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The cool air from the CRAC (Computer Room Air Conditioning) unit is supplied to the cold 
aisles either through raised floor design or through diffused ceiling [143].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The warm air produced in the hot aisles 


 
49 
 
is captured and transferred to the CRAC unit.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The chiller absorbs the heat in CRAC and outlet the cool air which 
is then supplied back to the cold aisles [134].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
3.9.1.2 Power plant co-location: One of the common techniques for waste heat utilization is to co-locate the 
datacenter with power plant powered with fossil fuels.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: It helps in indirect power generation of the plants.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The heat 
dissipated from the datacenter is used to heat the power plant and contributes in reduction of fossil fuels and carbon 
footprints [133].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: The low-quality heat is used to preheat the boiler feed water.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
As a condenser counter flow heat 
exchanger transports the datacenter heat to the water of power plant.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, power plant efficiency is improved 
and reduces the cost in the form of carbon tax and coal.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Heat can be recovered form hot streams using an energy recovery heat exchanger to utilize this heat to generate 
energy, which can be used to run cloud infrastructures without affecting the environment [129].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Markides [63] 
analyzed the existing techniques of waste heat utilization to enable sustainable computing in UK.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, fossil 
fuel-based energy generators are compared with renewable energy sources and the role of power schemes, 
combining heat and pumped heat is discussed.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Load factor (heat-to-power demand ratio) calculates the efficiency 
of different WHU technologies such as power schemes, combined heat and pumped heat.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
It has been found that 
pumped heat is effective way to transfer waste heat to useful work as compared to others.

[128] designed 
a technique to assess the available techniques for the utilization of waste heat in an eco-industrial park to make it 
eco-friendly and economical.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Due to continuous increase in oil price globally, it is a challenging to fulfil the demand 
of energy consumption of multinational companies to run CDCs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
This study remarked that quantity of waste heat 
and energy cost can be decreased by developing more eco-industrial parks, which will be helpful to maintain 
sustainable environment.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[130] proposed a Biomass Co-location Aware (BCA) waste heat utilization 
technique to produce energy from waste heat.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
This technique is working by utilizing computational fluid dynamics 
at high temperature.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[131] proposed a Solar Organic Rankine Cycle (SORC) based indirect power

title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

another.

5.2 Implications for Research and Practice  
The systematic review has suggestions for perspective research scholars and practitioners who are already working 
in the area of sustainable cloud computing and looking for new ideas.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
A lot of research challenges are described for 
perspective researchers and professional experts.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There is a need to integrate the different categories of sustainable 
cloud computing for better management of open issues related to cloud data center.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Figure 37 shows the interactions 
among different categories of sustainable cloud computing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
We have identified two different types of interaction 
among different categories: weak interaction (if any category depends the other category indirectly then it is 
considered as weak) and strong interaction (if one category depends the other category directly then it is considered 
as strong).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Based on the existing research work and their citations, we have identified the importance of an induvial 
category along with their sub-categories.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, future hotspot areas have been identified among different 
categories.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The 360 Degree View (global and complete view) of the taxonomy of sustainable cloud computing is 
provided at the end of this research paper.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

Sustainable cloud services are attracting more cloud customers and making it more profitable.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

Improving energy 
utilization, which reduces electricity bills and operational costs to enables sustainable cloud computing [14] [15].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

Microsoft, Google, and Amazon are replicating services, which needs additional resources and increases energy 
consumption.

text:
To overcome this impact, a trade-off between energy consumption and reliability is required to 
provide cost-efficient cloud services.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Existing energy efficient resource management techniques consume a huge 
amount of energy while executing workloads, which decreases resources leased from cloud datacenters [33].

5.4 Emerging Trends and their Impact 
Emerging trends can be observed in three different contexts: (1) applications (e.g., Big Data), (2) technologies (e.g., 
Software-defined network), and (3) techniques (e.g., deep learning).
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
They either present significant business 
opportunity for Cloud service providers (to offer new SaaS services using Clouds by supporting emerging 
applications) in many interesting ways or help them in efficient management and utilization of their Cloud 
infrastructures in reliable and energy-efficient manner.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
With the enormous success of Cloud computing, there are many emerging applications such as big data and smart 
cities [166] are harnessing it.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
These applications can be created using existing application/programming models 
such as those discussed in Section 3.1 (Application Design) or new ones to support the rapid creation of applications 
or ease of programming.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
When new application design/programming models are proposed, there is a need for new 
approaches for resource management and application scheduling to ensure the delivery of services of these Cloud 
applications in an energy efficient manner.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: All these factors will impact Cloud software platforms [167].
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Furthermore, new technological trends [168] such as Software-Defined Networks [165], Internet of Things (IoT), 
and Containers are presenting new opportunities for better management of data centres to support execution of 
emerging applications in an energy efficient manner.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
For example, Internet of Things (IoT)-based sensors and 
actuators help better management of cooling systems of CDC infrastructures.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The success of Cloud computing is also leading to the creation of larger CDC infrastructures, which is contributing 
to growing complexities in the management of CDCs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To better manage their resources and monitor application 
execution and resource status, recently works as [167] are starting to use deep learning approaches for detecting 
anomalies.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Such deep learning techniques need to be developed for better management of resources and workloads 
of emerging application models in a reliable and energy efficient manner without affecting the quality of service 
delivered to users.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
SUSTAINABLE CLOUD COMPUTING ARCHITECTURE: A CONCEPTUAL MODEL 
To resolve the above-mentioned challenges, there is a requirement of cloud computing architectures that can 
provide sustainable and reliable cloud services.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[19] and Guitart [87] have been very 
innovative, but as the research has persistently grown in the field of sustainable cloud computing, there is a 
necessity for new conceptual model to cover other important aspects of sustainability.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
[19] is only focused on cooling management of cloud datacenters and energy storage management, while a 
model proposed by Guitart [87] is focused on management of cooling, infrastructure and workloads.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Therefore, our 
model augments the previous aspects and covers all the important components such as i) layered architecture which 
comprises of software (application management), platform (workload and VM/Resource management) and 
infrastructure management, ii) cooling management, iii) energy management (renewable and grid energy) and iv) 
thermal-aware aspects of cloud datacenter and describes the interactions among them.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Figure 38 shows the 
conceptual model for sustainable cloud computing in the form of layered architecture, which offers holistic 
management of cloud computing resources to make cloud services more energy-efficient, sustainable and reliable.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The three main components of proposed architecture are as follows: 
1.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Software as a Service (SaaS): At this layer, application manager is deployed to handle the incoming user 
workloads, which can be interactive or batch style and transfer to workload manager for further action.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
At SaaS 
level, the QoS requirements of different applications can be defined in terms of SLA.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
QoS requirements for an 
application can be deadline, budget etc.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
For example, different encoding techniques can be used for video on-
demand application based on the QoS requirements of cloud user.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Platform as a Service (PaaS): At this layer, controller or middleware is deployed to control the important aspects 
of the system.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Resource manager and scheduler follows different provisioning and scheduling policies for 
efficient management of cloud resources, which can improve energy efficiency and resource utilization to make 
CDCS more sustainable.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There are four sub units of controller: workload manager, VM/resource manager, and 
manager and their functions are described below:  
 
a) Workload manager manages the incoming workloads from the application manager and identifies the 
QoS requirement for every workload for their successful execution and transfer the QoS information of 
workload to the VM/resource manager.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
b) VM/resource manager provisions and schedules the cloud resources for workload execution based on 
QoS requirements of workload using physical machines or virtual machines.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
c) Manager controls the two modules of infrastructure: i) Green energy resource manager and ii) cooling 
manager 
 
 
Figure 38: Conceptual Model for Sustainable Cloud Computing 
 
3.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS): This layer contains the information about cloud datacenters and virtual 
machines.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
VM migrations are performed to balance the load at virtualization layer for efficient execution of 
workloads.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The proactive temperature aware scheduler is used to monitor the temperature variation of different 
VMs running at different cores.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Power Management Unit (PMU) is integrated to power all the hardware 
executing the VMs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Dynamic Random-Access Memory (DRAM) stores the current states of VMs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Thermal 


 
61 
 
profiling and monitoring techniques are used to analyze the temperature variations of CDCs based on the value 
of temperature as monitored by thermal sensors.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Thermal alerts will be generated if temperature is higher 
than the threshold value and heat controller will take an action to control the temperature without affecting 
the performance of the CDC.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
The electricity coming from Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) is used to run 
the cooling devices to control the temperature.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
District heating management is integrated in which, the 
temperature is controlled by using chiller plant, outside air economizer and water economizer.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Green energy 
resource manager controls the power generated from renewable energy resources and fossil fuels.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To enable 
sustainable cloud environment, renewable energy is more preferred as compared to grid energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
If there is 
execution of deadline oriented workloads, then grid energy can be used to maintain the reliability of cloud 
services.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: The sources of renewable energy are solar and wind.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Batteries are used to store the renewable energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Automatic Transfer Switch (ATS) is used to manage the energy coming from both sources (renewable and non-
renewable) and forward to UPS.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, Power Distribution Unit (PDU) is used to transfer the electricity to 
all the CDCs and cooling devices.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
SUMMARY AND CONCLUSIONS 
The usage of large number of cloud datacenters results in a huge amount of energy consumption and produces 
significant amount of carbon footprints, which has become the greatest challenge of the 21st century.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
On the other 
hand, the utilization of a combination of grid and renewable energy to run cloud datacenter in smart cities can save 
energy to a large extent.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Consequently, there is a need to manage both energy and QoS together to enable 
sustainable and energy-efficient cloud services.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Existing energy-aware resource management techniques and 
policies mainly focus on VM consolidation to reduce energy consumption of servers only, but other resources such 
as networks, storage, memory and cooling consume a huge amount of energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
There is a need for an efficient 
scheduling of the traffic flows between servers in the cloud datacenter to save energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Therefore, holistic 
management of all the resources (networks, memory, processors, cooling and storage) is required to enable 
sustainable cloud computing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, the effect of QoS on SLA is required to be addressed in holistic management 
techniques.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Moreover, self-aware or autonomic management of cloud resources in a holistic manner can manage 
both energy consumption and QoS simultaneously, which can improve the sustainability of cloud computing 
systems.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In addition, dynamically changing the variable clock rates of processor can also optimize the usage of 
energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
It has also been recommended that follow the renewable can motivate the cloud providers to locate their 
cloud datacenters nearer to green energy resources and load can be distributed geographically.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
However, 
geographical distribution of resources affects the QoS of networks, which is an open research challenge for the 
community.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Unfortunately, the requirement for processing of a huge amount of data and high performance 
simultaneously can also consume large amounts of energy.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
To solve this problem, there is a need to manage energy 
consumption, SLAs and QoS at same time.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Further, there is a need of self-aware management of cloud resources 
holistically to address these research issues.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Currently, research community is working in this direction, but more 
advanced research is required to ensure the energy efficiency and sustainability of cloud services.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
In this paper, we proposed a taxonomy of sustainable cloud computing to analyze existing techniques for 
sustainability such as application design, sustainability metrics, capacity planning, energy management, 
virtualization, thermal-aware scheduling, cooling management, renewable energy and waste heat utilization for 
CDCs.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text: Further, the taxonomy mapping based comparison has been described.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
A conceptual model for sustainable 
cloud computing has been proposed.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Through a detailed analysis of the related studies in the context of taxonomy, 
we are able to identify and propose various future research directions.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
Following facts can be further concluded: 
• 
VM consolidation techniques can minimize energy consumption of servers.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
• 
Optimization scheduling of traffic flows between servers is required.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
• 
There is a need of dynamic task scheduling for energy and QoS optimization.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
• 
New system architectures and algorithms can geographically distribute the CDC.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
• 
There is a need of interplay between IoT-enabled cooling systems and CDC manager.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
• 
Maximum utilization of renewable energy powered resources is required for holistic management of 
resources and workloads.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View

text:
62 
 
We hope that this systematic review will be helpful for practitioners and researchers who want to pursue research 
in any area of sustainable cloud computing.
title: A Taxonomy and Future Directions for Sustainable Cloud Computing: 360 Degree View
