Arhuaco: Deep Learning and Isolation Based Security for Distributed
High-Throughput Computing
A.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Kebschull · for the ALICE Collaboration
Received: date / Accepted: date
Abstract Grid computing systems require innovative meth-
ods and tools to identify cybersecurity incidents and per-
form autonomous actions i.e.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
They also require methods to isolate and trace job
payload activity in order to protect users and ﬁnd evidence
of malicious behavior.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We introduce an integrated approach
of security monitoring via Security by Isolation with Linux
Containers and Deep Learning methods for the analysis of
real time data in Grid jobs running inside virtualized High-
Throughput Computing infrastructure in order to detect and
prevent intrusions.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
A dataset for malware detection in Grid
computing is described.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We show in addition the utilization
of generative methods with Recurrent Neural Networks to
improve the collected dataset.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We present Arhuaco, a pro-
totype implementation of the proposed methods.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We empir-
ically study the performance of our technique.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The results
show that Arhuaco outperforms other methods used in In-
trusion Detection Systems for Grid Computing.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The study
is carried out in the ALICE Collaboration Grid, part of the
Worldwide LHC Computing Grid.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Keywords Grid Computing Security · Intrusion Detection
and Prevention · Deep Learning · WLCG · Isolation ·
Malware Detection
1 Introduction
The Worldwide LHC Computing Grid (WLCG) is one the
most remarkable examples of High-Troughput Computing
(HTC) distributed infrastructure for scientiﬁc applications.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Kebschull
IRI group, Goethe-University Frankfurt
E-mail: andres.gomez@cern.ch
L.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Betev
CERN, Geneva, Switzerland
The WLCG is the global Grid that analyzes data from the
Large Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN, with 170 sites in
40 countries.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Due to their size, complexity, reputation and
required access by Internet these systems are continuously
exposed to attackers.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Authenticated users have the freedom
to execute arbitrary code and to transfer arbitrary data that
is required for their experiments.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
External or insider attack-
ers may take advantage of the Grid functionality to carry out
unauthorized activities such as running malware or mining
cryptocoins.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The Grid is a heterogeneous and dynamic en-
vironment where it is difﬁcult to adapt traditional rule based
Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The distributed usage of High-throughput Computing
(HTC) farms for data processing tasks - known as Grid
Computing - has been very successful in High Energy
Physics (HEP), weather forecasting, brain research and as-
tronomy research, just to mention a few examples.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Scientists
can submit jobs composed of custom code and experimental
data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The computing Grid has been envisioned as an analogy
for the electrical Grid, for computing resources on demand.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The Worldwide LHC Computing Grid (WLCG) enables the
scientists to analyze massive amounts of physics data and
it allowed for the experimental validation of the existence
of the Higgs boson [10].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The WLCG integrates computer
centers worldwide that provide computing and storage re-
source into a single infrastructure accessible by all Large
Hadron Collider (LHC) physicists.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Currently, it combines
the power of nearly 170 sites in 40 countries, connected with
10-100 Gb links, with more than 600.000 processing cores
and 700 PB of storage capacity.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It is capable of process-
ing more than 2 million jobs per day.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The ALICE (A Large
Ion Collider Experiment) Collaboration has built a dedicated
detector to exploit the unique physics potential of nucleus-
nucleus collisions at LHC energies.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Its aim is to study the
physics of strongly interacting matter at the highest energy
densities reached so far in the laboratory [12].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
As a mem-
arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018


2
A.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
ber of the WLCG, the ALICE experiment has developed the
ALICE production environment (AliEn) [3], implementing
many components of the Grid computing technologies that
are needed to store, process and analyze the collected data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Through AliEn, the computing centers that provide CPU and
storage resources for ALICE can be seen and used as a sin-
gle entity - any available node executes jobs and ﬁle access is
transparent to the user, wherever in the world a ﬁle might be
located.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text: Figure 1 represents the ﬂow of data in the WLCG.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
1 Real time grid data ﬂow around the world
Authorized users of Grid computing systems have the
freedom to carry out research on experimental data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
They
are able to execute arbitrary code and transfer any required
data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This means that potential insider attackers have the
same capabilities.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The focus of this study is on the security
issues related to the Grid job execution environment inside
site worker nodes.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Frequently in HEP Grids [5], the jobs run-
ning in the worker nodes have access rights that are beyond
of what is actually required, restricted only by one or sev-
eral local Linux accounts.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
When multiple jobs are executed
with the same account, an attacker with control over one job
could tamper another user jobs, blaming the owner of any
malicious activity.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
These processes could also have access
to sensitive server data and restricted networks.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Therefore,
Security by Isolation (SbI) mechanisms for processes and
networks are important requirements for Grid computing.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
An insider attacker may misuse the power of the Grid
for activities not related to physics data analysis.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Complex
HTC infrastructure such as WLCG are attractive targets for
external attackers as well.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
An attacker might take advantage
of the Grid functionality to tamper with user jobs, escalate
privileges, access sensitive server conﬁguration data, setup
a Denial of Service (DoS) attack or mine cryptocoins, to
name a few of the possibilities.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This could be accomplished
by exploiting unknown or unﬁxed software or hardware vul-
nerabilities, listen to user network trafﬁc to gather sensitive
clear text information or by guessing weak user credentials
among other possibilities.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Millions of jobs might be running
in Grids like the WLGC every day.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The user’s ability to run
arbitrary code and the lack of proper isolation make detect-
ing intrusions a more challenging task than in other systems.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Traditional Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) require rules
written by security professionals.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Those rules need to be up-
dated constantly which requires an important amount of ef-
fort.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Rule based IDS are difﬁcult to adapt to very dynamic
environments such as the Grid [18].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Machine Learning al-
gorithms can help to automate the way IDS are built and up-
dated, by using security monitoring data collected from the
protected systems [60].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In the Grid, the amount of this mon-
itoring data is huge due to the number of running jobs.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Deep
Learning methods may help to analyze this data to improve
the IDS detection accuracy.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We introduce Arhuaco, a framework that adopts Linux
Container (LC) technology to provide SbI and security mon-
itoring by applying Deep Learning for detection and pre-
vention of abnormal activities based on multiple sources of
monitoring data such as network connections and system
calls.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Arhuaco gives researches the ability to generate com-
plementary training data by a Recurrent Neural Network.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This can be used to improve the detection performance and
adapt the detector to new environments.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
A dataset for Ma-
chine Learning (ML) training of malware detection on Linux
based Grid computing is described.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Some of the most popu-
lar Grid systems are just starting to explore the usage of SbI
and IDS for security monitoring [65].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
As we describe in the
related work section there are no studies that leverage the
capabilities of Linux Container isolation and monitoring in
combination with Deep Learning and data generation for In-
trusion Detection.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We also show in the next section that there
is no tool implementing the mentioned techniques for Grid
job payload monitoring in order to detect intrusions.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We de-
scribe the design, implementation decisions and tests of our
proposed methods in the ALICE Collaboration Grid, part of
the WLCG.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We demonstrate that the selected algorithms and
techniques outperform other methods used on IDS for Grid
Computing.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Section 2
presents the state of the art on ML and isolation based secu-
rity methods applied to distributed environments especially
in Grid computing.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Section 3 provides background informa-
tion on the SbI approach and an overview of the classiﬁca-
tion task in Machine Learning and generative models.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Sec-
tion 4 and 5 describe the Arhuaco design and implemen-
tation based on our ideas.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Section 6 shows the results ob-
tained from testing our approach.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Finally section 7 and 8
summarize our ﬁndings and indicate directions of our future
research.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Arhuaco: Deep Learning and Isolation Based Security for Distributed High-Throughput Computing
3
2 Related work
2.1 Security by Isolation in Grid Computing
Virtual Machines (VM) have been suggested many times
to solve the isolation problems in Grid computing [20].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
VMs are emulated machines with their own kernel while
Linux Containers (LC) can share a single kernel.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Several
researchers - [18] and [17] - have proposed the usage of
LCs to provide a level of isolation between the Grid jobs
and the underlying system and network.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Saving system re-
sources in High-throughput Computing (HTC) applications
is critical, and LC help to reduce the overall performance
impact.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[67] presents a comparison of the performance of
several virtualization technologies including VM, and shows
that container based systems have a near-native performance
of CPU, memory, disk and network.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[49] analyzes LCs and
VMs and ﬁnds similar results in terms of performance and
scalability.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[7] shows a success real experience for LCs pro-
viding isolation in a Grid site at the ALICE High Level Trig-
ger (HLT).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text: Our study further extends this direction.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In par-
ticular, we are interested in how this isolation mechanism
can be integrated with a security monitoring system, that
provides methods to enforce Intrusion Prevention and De-
tection in Grid computing.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
2.2 Intrusion Detection
In [29] an extensive review of Intrusion Detection Systems
is presented.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Intrusion is deﬁned as the attempt to compro-
mise conﬁdentiality, integrity and availability and Intrusion
Detection as the process of monitoring the events occurring
in a computer system or network, and analyzing them for
signs of intrusions.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The cited study presents several open
source technologies as the most used solutions for IDS such
as SNORT [44] and OSSEC [21].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
False positive and false
negative are two very common metrics to assess the degree
of accuracy.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text: Relevant features can be sets of audit trails (e.g.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
system logs, system commands) on a host, network pack-
ets or connections, wireless network trafﬁc and application
logs.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Machine Learning has been proposed in many studies to
improve IDS.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[60] summarizes the state of the art on ML
techniques applied to Intrusion Detection and prevention.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It
states that the most commonly used techniques in the topic
have been K-nearest neighbor (K-NN), Support Vector Ma-
chines (SVM), Artiﬁcial Neural Networks, self-organizing
maps, decision trees, Na¨ıve Bayes networks, genetic algo-
rithms and fuzzy logic for one single classiﬁer approaches.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
On the other hand for hybrid classiﬁers, using several clas-
siﬁers, neuro-fuzzy techniques, clustering-based approaches
have been used especially for parameter tunning and clas-
siﬁcation.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Single classiﬁers with K-NN and SVM are very
popular, mainly the second one.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
For hybrid approaches an
integrated framework, where a method is used for feature
selection while another method is used for classiﬁcation is
common.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
KDD99 [45] is presented as the standard database
for testing ML based IDS.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[66] shows an overview on the
usage of computational intelligence research on IDS.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Ac-
cording to the review, misuse detection approach is widely
adopted in the majority of commercial systems, because it is
simple and effective, but it can not detect novel or targeted
attacks.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text: The other common method is anomaly detection.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It
extracts patterns from behavioral habits of end users, or us-
age history of networks and hosts.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In the intrusion detection
ﬁeld, supervised learning usually produces classiﬁers for
misuse detection from class labeled training datasets.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Un-
supervised learning satisﬁes the requirement of anomaly de-
tection, hence it is usually employed in anomaly detection.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The authors present two benchmarks, the DARPA-Lincoln
datasets [31] and the KDD99 datasets [45] as the most uti-
lized.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
According to their work, the most commonly used
algorithms are Neural Networks like Feed forward Neural
Networks, Radial basis function neural networks, Recurrent
Neural Networks, Self-organizing maps and Adaptive reso-
nance theory.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
2.3 Methods used in Grid related Intrusion Detection
There are previously proposed methods for IDS in Grid
computing.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Some of them describe schemes that are not re-
lated to Machine Learning nor computational intelligence.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
For example [58] employs a relational grid monitoring ar-
chitecture, [14] presents a bottleneck veriﬁcation approach,
[50] describes a streaming database approach, [61] utilizes
gossip algorithms, [69] represents a multi-agent approach,
and [34] introduces a web services correlation service.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
On
the other hand, some articles are focused on ML topics such
as [59], that adopts learning vector quantization Neural Net-
works, [47] and [62] utilize feed forward Neural Networks,
[25] applies auto immune systems and [57] also makes use
of learning vector quantization neural networks, all of them
with a single classiﬁer approach.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[68] utilizes a hybrid ap-
proach, with a soft computing based self-organize map di-
mension reduction technique, a fuzzy Neural Network and a
genetic algorithm.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
None of the previously presented studies applies Secu-
rity by Isolation to further improve security incident de-
tection.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Neither of them makes use of Deep Learning ap-
proaches that allow researchers processing huge real time
streams of data produced in Grids like the WLCG.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In addi-
tion, we could not ﬁnd the usage of generative methods by
Recurrent Neural Networks to improve the training datasets.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
2.4 Grid IDS related datasets
Grid computing is a unique environment with special re-
quirements.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text: We analyze the behavior of the job payloads.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Therefore, using standard datasets for ML based IDS could
be ineffective.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We could not ﬁnd any available dataset for
IDS training in Grid computing.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
However several studies
describe custom metrics employed.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In [58] and [50], the au-
thors generate a dataset consisting of one or more log ﬁles.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[14] uses an operating system kernel module to gather sys-
tem calls.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In [47] the measurements are extracted from au-
dit data of low level IDS.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
To identify misuse committed by
insider attackers, their system analyzes the behavior by re-
source usage data like CPU time and memory usage.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The
authors gather audit data from HIDS, also extracting operat-
ing system data throughout the grid middleware and the sys-
log protocol.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In the implementation level they use OSSEC-
HIDS and Snort.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[61] uses Snort alerts as the input met-
rics by the intrusion detection exchange protocol.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[25] pro-
poses user-level data built from user ID, role, type and quan-
tity of resources being consumed, and system-level data is
composed of CPU usage rate, states of main and the sec-
ondary memory and attributes of system ﬁles.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The identi-
ﬁcation, type, priority, status of processes and the states of
CPU when they are running are organized into process-level
data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
IP address and port number of source and destination,
type of protocol, ﬂags are grouped into network-level data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[69] analyses the network log data of its own monitoring
area.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In [68] the extracted features are system calls (ID, re-
turn value, return status), process (ID, IPC ID, IPC permis-
sion, exit value, exit status) and ﬁle access (mode, path, ﬁle
system, ﬁle name, argument length).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The extracted informa-
tion is normalized between 0 and 1 for the input of SOM.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[57] describes a method using generated log ﬁles as a host
based intrusion detection.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
None of the mentioned datasets
was made publicly available for other researchers, therefore
we decided to collect our own dataset.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
2.5 Malware Detection
The focus of this study is to run Grid jobs securely and an-
alyze the payloads behavior in order to detect intrusions.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Therefore, we use Linux malware samples to test our en-
vironment and collect a dataset of malicious data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This is
a more practical approach than creating our own set of bi-
naries with a limited set of malicious characteristics.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
There
are several web sites that collect malware samples and make
them available for the research community such as [63] and
[64].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In the same direction [42] and [43] explore Machine
Learning for malware classiﬁcation, using system calls as
main features for their classiﬁer.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
[15] explores the usage of
Deep Learning for static analysis of malware samples for
classiﬁcation.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We use a similar approach, however, our goal
is to provide real time misbehave detection in Grid comput-
ing, by analyzing huge ﬂows of data that can be generated
by the millions of jobs running in the Grid.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
3 Background
3.1 Security by Isolation
Security by Isolation is a technique that enforces component
separation (hardware or software) in a way that if one of
them is compromised by an attacker, other components still
remain safe [30].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
There are several implementations provid-
ing SbI such as Virtual Machines, Linux containers and the
Unix multiuser scheme.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
There are even security focused Op-
eration Systems [48] built with SbI as one of their core fea-
tures such as [54], [37] and [51].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
3.2 Linux Containers
An LC is a set of processes running on top of a shared kernel
[67].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
They are isolated from the rest of the machine and can
not affect the host or other containers, with the exception of
exploitable vulnerabilities in the kernel or the container en-
gine.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It takes advantage of namespaces to have a private view
of the system (network interfaces, PID tree, mount points).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Cgroups are also applied to have a limited assignment of re-
sources.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
LC can be seen as an extension of the virtual mem-
ory space concept to a wide system scope.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
They provide a
set of features that have advantages over other virtualization
technologies.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
They are lightweight, fast on booting, have
a small memory footprint, and close to bare metal perfor-
mance.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Figure 2 describes a set containers working together,
isolated and sharing the same kernel.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In opposition, Virtual
Machines have several kernels on top of a hypervisor.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:

3.5 Deep Learning
DL is a sub area of Machine Learning that has solved in-
creasingly complicated applications with increasing accu-
racy [19].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Deep Learning architectures such as Convolu-

cessing, among other areas.

They have produced some re-

They are es-

Traditional Machine Learning models used for classiﬁcation

4 System design
In this study, we propose the integrated usage of Security
by Isolation (SbI) with Linux containers and Deep Learning
methods to analyze real time monitoring data of processes
running inside virtualized HTC infrastructure, as well as the
utilization of generative methods to improve the required
training data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We introduce a hybrid supervised classiﬁca-
tion approach using word2vec for feature selection and pre-
processing and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) for
discrimination between normal and malicious classes.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Our
study also employs Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) for
data generation on the training steps.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Arhuaco was designed
as a proof of concept implementation based on this proposed
methods, with focus on Grid computing.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Therefore it is de-
signed to provide security with a Grid based threat model
approach based on the one introduced in [18].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This can be
applied to other types of distributed HTC environments.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In
a computing Grid, an adversary may have several goals:
– Steal sensitive data such as private encryption keys,
user’s certiﬁcates, tokens or credentials.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
– Compromise user’s machines to distribute malware and
steal valuable user information.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
– Abuse the Grid computational resources for criminal or
not allowed activities, for instance, to deploy botnets or
mining crypto-coins.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
– Damage the organization reputation by using resources
to attack other organizations.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
To achieve these goals, an attacker could use several
methods:
– Exploit unknown or not ﬁxed software/hardware vulner-
abilities.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
– Listen to user network to gather sensitive clear text in-
formation.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text: – Access sensitive server conﬁguration data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In the next subsections, a detailed information about the
design and implementation of Arhuaco is given, based on
our proposed contributions.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We also describe how our sys-
tem works under the described threat model.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
4.1 Linux Containers for Isolation
We require an isolation technology easily adaptable to the
Linux powered Grid computing for High Energy Physics
(HEP).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Linux Containers (LC) were selected to provide SbI
given their security vs performance balance [13].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
LCs pro-
vide in addition a very important feature, network isolation.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
They make it possible to create an encrypted virtual net-
works inside a physical or another virtual network, in order
to restrict processes running inside to access sensitive assets.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This is fundamental in Grid computing, where sites may be


Arhuaco: Deep Learning and Isolation Based Security for Distributed High-Throughput Computing
7
sharing resources with other projects or experimental infras-
tructure.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
For instance, there is a Grid site at the ALICE HLT
cluster, sharing physical resources with the sensitive LHC
experiment network [6].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Therefore virtual network isolation
is used to avoid breaches.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Another fundamental feature of
Linux Containers for our this study is the monitoring power
they grant.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Since it is possible to encapsulate a set of pro-
cesses with their own view of the entire system, it is also
possible to capture speciﬁc per process metrics that allow
us to analyze their isolated behavior.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We are able to capture
resource consumption data such as CPU, memory and disk,
network connection data, and system calls for a speciﬁc con-
tainer and as a consequence for each Grid job.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Therefore,
we can detect with better precision the source of a security
incident or even collect forensics data for further analysis.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text: Figure 4 is a schema of the desired isolation characteristics.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
On the left, Grid jobs run without isolation, being able to af-
fect other jobs or the underlying system.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
On the right, Grid
jobs are isolated by LCs, each one of them run in a reduced
version of the whole system, so they have no access to other
jobs or sensitive resources in the working nodes.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
4 Desired isolation scenario
Traditional Grid systems use batch engines such as Con-
dor [55] for scheduling jobs in distributed environments.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
To
run containers instead of standard batch jobs, we need mod-
ern orchestration tools that concede us the ability to exe-
cute containers over a shared cluster.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
There are several pop-
ular alternatives including Google Kubernetes [41], Apache
Mesos [22], and Docker Swarm [32].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In the system im-
plementation section, we describe the reason for selecting
Docker Swarm to be the ﬁrst container engine that Arhuaco
interacts with.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
4.2 Deep Learning for Grid job classiﬁcation
Popular industrial IDS such as Snort and OSSEC [44] and
[21] use ﬁxed rules and search for known attack signatures
in order to ﬁnd possible attacks.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
They have problems when
unknown or slightly different intrusion methods are em-
ployed, so they need to be constantly updated [27].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Machine
Learning has been commonly suggested in Intrusion Detec-
tion for the modeling and analysis of log and network data
for autonomous classiﬁcation of security incidents.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
As de-
picted in Figure 5, in this research we apply dynamic analy-
sis of Grid jobs monitoring data for real time intrusion detec-
tion, which means analysis of operation system (Linux) pro-
cesses.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
A supervised classiﬁcation approach is implemented
in Arhuaco.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We propose the usage of a Convolutional Neu-
ral Network architecture based on the one introduced in [26]
for English sentences classiﬁcation and utilized in [15] for
static binary ﬁle classiﬁcation according to their x86 ma-
chine code instructions.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
5 Flow of Grid data processing for classiﬁcation
4.3 Feature extraction
As mentioned before, this study employs system calls and
network connection traces as input data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
They are encoded
in a human readable format, thus Natural Language Pro-
cessing (NLP) methods allow us to build a convenient lan-
guage model.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Recently introduced Deep Learning methods
for NLP implement learning word vector representations by
neural language models [4].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In these vectors, words are pro-
jected from a 1 −of −V encoding, where V is the number
of different words available (vocabulary size), in a lower di-
mensional vector space using Neural Network hidden lay-
ers [26].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Therefore, semantically close words in the train-
ing corpus are mathematically close in the lower dimen-
sional vector space.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The word2vec algorithm [16] was cho-
sen for Arhuaco to create the input features.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It is a predic-
tive model for learning word embeddings.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Word2vec vectors
create suitable inputs for Convolutional Neural Networks
since they allow to treat input data as matrices, similar to
the array of pixels in an image.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Here we refer to tokens in-
stead of words since our dataset can also contain numbers,
paths, IP addresses, among other type of data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
As a preprocessing step for the traces, characters that do
not increase the amount of available information are deleted.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Each trace line of system calls is composed of the type of op-
eration, the opcode number and all its parameters.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
For net-
work connection information each line has the DNS request,


8
A.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text: IP addresses and ports used per connection.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
These lines have
a variable size, therefore we take only the ﬁrst m tokens per
line, adding a padding token when a line is shorter.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Then l
consecutive lines are taken, which gives us a sequence of
n = m×l total tokens, from which we extract our input fea-
ture vector.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
ai ∈Rk is a k-dimensional token vector corre-
sponding to the i-th token in our sequence.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This sequence
can be described as:
a1:n = a1 ⊕a2 ⊕...⊕an,
(7)
where ⊕is the concatenation operator, and ai:i+j is the con-
catenation of tokens ai,ai+1,...,ai+j.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
These embedding vec-
tors are the result of applying word2vec method on our text
input data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
4.4 Convolutional Neural Network
In the context of this research, a convolution operation in-
volves a kernel or ﬁlter G ∈Rhk, which is applied to a win-
dow of h tokens to produce a new feature.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
For example, a
feature zi is generated from a window of words ai:i+h−1 by:
zi = f(G·ai:i+h−1 +b),
(8)
where b ∈R is a bias term and f is a non-linear function.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This ﬁlter is applied to each possible window of tokens in
the sequence {a1:h,a2:h+1,...,an−h+1:n} to produce a feature
vector z = [z1,z2,...,zn−h+1], with z ∈Rn−h+1.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
A max-over-
time pooling operation is then applied to the feature vector,
taking the maximum value z∗= maxz as the only feature re-
sulting from this ﬁlter.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The most important feature, one with
the highest value, is kept for each feature map.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The same
process is repeated with multiple ﬁlters of different window
sizes, to obtain multiple features.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
These features are passed
to a fully connected ReLu layer whose output goes to the
last dense layer with Sigmoid activation with outputs corre-
sponding to the probability distribution over labels (normal
and malicious in our problem setup).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
For the contrasted classiﬁcation method - the Support
Vector Machine (SVM) - we used the well established Bag
of Words (BoW) model [39] to create its input feature vec-
tors.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In the BoW we ﬁrst create a vocabulary with the list
of all possible tokens is the training set.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Then we reduce this
vocabulary by using only the most used tokens.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We created a
vector where each component is the number of times a given
token appears in the analyzed set.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
An alternative method is
the Continuous Bag of Words (CBOW), which predicts tar-
get words from source context words.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
4.5 Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) for training data
generation
A character level language model has been selected as a gen-
erative method for Arhuaco.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The objective of this model is
to predict the next character in a sequence.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Given a training
corpus (c1,...,cT), where ci is a single character and T is
the total number of characters.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
A Long Short Term Mem-
ory (LSTM) RNN is utilized to determine the sequence of
its output vectors (o1,...,oT) by a sequence of distributions
P(ct+1|c ≤t) = σ(ot).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Here σ is the softmax distribution
deﬁned by:
P(σ(ot) = j) =
exp(oj
t )
∑k exp(okt ).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
(9)
The objective function is to maximize the total log proba-
bility of the training sequence ∑T−1
t=0 logP(xt+1|x ≤t).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This
implies that the LSTM learns a probability distribution over
sequences.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We can then sample from the conditional distri-
bution P(xt+1|x ≤t) to get the next character in a generated
string and provide it as the next input to the LSTM [52].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
After the training process has ﬁnished we can generate new
data that can be used as extra training data in order to ex-
tend the generalization capabilities of a classiﬁcation system
[15].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
4.6 Arhuaco design architecture
A diagram of Arhuaco architectural components is shown in
Figure 6.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The execution engine provides an interface with a
selected container scheduling engine according to conﬁgu-
ration parameters.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Then, the executed containers are mon-
itored, extracting real time data for security analysis.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The
data is processed by the previously described feature ex-
traction mechanism.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Furthermore, these preprocessed input
feature vectors are sent to the classiﬁcation and generative
modules.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Any sus-
picious incident is processed by the response engine.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This
can be conﬁgured with predeﬁned actions, such as sending
alerts to administrators, stopping suspicious jobs, or collect
information for ofﬂine analysis (forensic).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
5 Implementation
The Arhuaco prototype was developed in Python.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It pro-
vides interfaces for Grid frameworks, container engines and
data collection tools.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Among the alternatives for Linux Con-
tainer engines, to the most popular belong Docker [32],
Rocket [33], Singularity [28], and LXC [8].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Arhuaco sup-
ports Docker in its ﬁrst stage, given its broad adoption in
industrial applications and its default security measures.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
To
be able to execute grid jobs inside LCs, three solutions were
tested: Kubernetes [41], Apache Mesos [23], and Docker
Swarm.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Docker Swarm was chosen due to its simplicity
and fast deployment in testing environments.

In addition, it

A custom CentOS 6 based Docker

CVMFS [2] was installed on the hosts and shared

One job per container is ex-

title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

Besides, it is the natural micro ser-

For the training and validation of our proposed classiﬁ-

text:

6 Evaluation
In this section, an empiric evaluation of the performance im-
pact, classiﬁcation ability and data generation effectiveness
for the methods implemented in Arhuaco is described.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Here
the goal was to answer the following questions:
– Does using LC for isolation and system call monitoring
create a big performance impact?
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
If that is the case, is it
critical in comparison to the increment in security pro-
vided?
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
– Does the CNN for classiﬁcation of job traces provide
better accuracy and false positives rates than the tradi-
tional SVM?
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
– Does the LSTM Network for data generation improve
the training results?
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
6.1 Evaluation methods
We have deployed two type of performance tests.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The ﬁrst
with the Linpack benchmark as introduced in [13] to test the
throughput.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The second measures the performance impact
in processing times.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
For the ﬁrst test, we ran Linpack jobs
while for the secong the job is a production ALICE script.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We have prepared 3 evaluation scenarios: running jobs on
a Linux machine, then in Docker containers and ﬁnally in
Docker containers with system call interception and pro-
cessing by Arhuaco.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
In our performance analysis, the impact
of collecting network data from the job is not measured.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Loss, Accuracy (ACC) and False Positive Rate (FPR) are
the measurements for the correctness of the compared clas-
siﬁcation methods.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The overall performance of the trained
classiﬁers is evaluated by the Accuracy.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This measures the
number of instances that were correct, which are both the
True Positives and True Negatives, over the entire size of the
dataset, which is the number of True Positives (TP), True
Negatives (TN), False Positives (FP), and False Negatives
(FN).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It is calculated as:
Accuracy(ACC) =
(TP+TN)
(TP+TN +FP+FN),
(10)
FalsePositiveRate(FPR) =
FP
FP+TN ,
(11)
where False Positives (FP) is the number of misclassiﬁed in-
stances of a certain category over the number of all instances
that are classiﬁed as that category.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The ACC and FPR values
are deﬁned in the range [0,1], where 1 is the best possible
value for ACC and the worst for FPR.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
On the other hand, 0 is
the best value for FPR and the worst for ACC.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
They can also
be interpreted as percentage values in the range [0%,100%].
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:

6.4 Generative model results
As shown in Table 6, the SVM classiﬁcation results for net-
work connection information produced the worst accuracy
in all our tests.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Therefore we utilized this same case to prove
the effectiveness of the proposed generative technique.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The
Deep RNN was trained with the available network data cor-
pus and then modiﬁed to generate 20% new training data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The new data was concatenated to the original data to create
a new training set.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Further, the SVM is trained again to mea-
sure the new accuracy.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The validation data utilized belongs
to the original data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Figures 17 and 18 provide a new com-
parison of the SVM accuracy and FPR after being trained
with the additionally generated data.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
A noticeable improve-
ment can be seen regarding the training with the original
data in Figures 15 and 16.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This demonstrates the practical
beneﬁts of using LSTM for modeling and generating data in
the context of Intrusion Detection Systems.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The obtained accuracy for the SVM trained with the
newly generated data, applied to unseen network data from
the original dataset was 0.8201.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
There was a 2.38% im-
provement rate as expected with our approach, in compar-
ison the original value from Table 6, 0.8011.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This validates
the results obtained in the training steps.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
7 Discusion and future work
Regarding the ﬁrst question we have deﬁned in our evalua-
tion, the performance tests present an execution time over-
head of 0.4% when using Linux Containers in comparison
with the Linux runs for the Linpack throughput test, and
0.5% when using Arhuaco monitoring.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This can be consid-
ered as a very small impact.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The impact is more considerable
when testing the execution time for the ALICE Grid job.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text: The Docker container generates up to 8.634% of overhead.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It is higher, an extra 2.535% when monitoring by Arhuaco
is added on top.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Although this overhead is not critical, we
have implemented some ideas to reduce it.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We have a two
layers approach, based on user conﬁguration.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Arhuaco can
detect malicious activities by ﬁrst intercepting and analyzing
network connections and then it can make a deeper analysis
by a second layer using the system calls, after suspicious
processes detection.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Another conﬁgurable option is to ran-
domly analyze a small set of jobs running in the Grid, which
still can contribute to have an improved level of security.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It
is important to notice that containers are being increasingly
utilized in Grid computing collaborations and as we have
shown, adding extra monitoring and analysis by Arhuaco
creates an acceptable performance impact.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Another point to
consider is that there are studies [13] that compare Linux
Containers against Virtual Machines (VMs).
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
They demon-
strate that VMs create a bigger overhead in the performance
than LCs.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The classiﬁcation algorithm implemented in Arhuaco
improves the detection of malicious activities running in-
side the grid, compared to traditionally employed methods,
which responds to the second research question.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Convolu-
tional Neural Networks demonstrate a better classiﬁcation
ability than Support Vector Machines for system calls as
well as for network connections in Grid jobs.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Since our gath-
ered malicious network data is rather small, we have suc-
cessfully generated new data by a Recurrent Neural Net-
work.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We described how it allowed us to improve the clas-
siﬁcation results for the SVM, giving an answer to the third
evaluation question.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
An interesting point to remark is that
our approach of analyzing input as a text data by Natu-
ral Language Processing approaches can be easily extended
from system calls and network data to inputs from other In-

It could also be easily adapted beyond HTC, for in-
stance to monitor Cloud services running in containers over

title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We still have some limitations and topics for further
analysis.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We will investigate optimizations that we can in-
troduce in Arhuaco for reducing the overhead.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This seems
feasible given the results for Linpack.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Our framework has
not been tested in a production environment yet.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The ob-
tained False Positive Rate, although small, is still signiﬁcant
if we consider the huge amount of jobs running in the World-
wide LHC Computing Grid, close to 300.000 at any given
instant.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We should improve the results in this area and also
research into methods to inform about the possible security
incidents detected.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We will explore techniques to protect the
privacy of our datasets in order to avoid leaks of sensitive
information.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We will also investigate in how to employ the
distributed nature of the Grid to improve the distributed de-
tection of intrusions.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This can be useful for instance, to au-
tonomously inform other Grid sites IDS about security in-
cidents that could spread in the Grid.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We are working on
further enhancing the isolation provided in our containers
by using kernel hardening such as grsecurity.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Besides we
are currently testing the integration with other container so-
lutions and HTC engines.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
8 Conclusions
We have presented Arhuaco, a security monitoring tool for
High-Throughput Computing.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It employs Security by Isola-
tion for executing and monitoring Grid jobs inside Linux
Containers based on multiple sources of monitoring data
such as network connections and system calls.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It applies
Convolutional Neural Networks to classify Grid jobs data as
normal or malicious.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
It also utilizes a Recurrent Neural Net-
work to learn a data model in order to generate new training
samples.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
The proposed algorithms implemented in Arhuaco
improve the security incident detection in Grid computing
systems, since it is able to identify the source of an intru-
sion with higher accuracy.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Arhuaco can analyze the huge
ﬂow of real time data that monitoring Grid jobs generate.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
This makes Arhuaco suitable for environments such as the
WLCG, the global Grid that analyzes data from the Large
Hadron Collider (LHC) at CERN, where millions of jobs
are executed every day.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
By a set of tests carried out in the
ALICE Grid as part of the WLGC, we have shown how the
proposed algorithms outperform other methods used in In-
trusion Detection Systems for Grid Computing.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
Datasets and software
Arhuaco is under development.
title: arXiv:1801.04179v1  [cs.DC]  12 Jan 2018

text:
We are discussing the pos-
sibility to release it and the training dataset as Open Source
software and data.

A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization
of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing
Klervie Tocz´e, Simin Nadjm-Tehrani
Abstract—Edge computing is promoted to meet increasing performance needs of data-driven services using computational and
storage resources close to the end devices, at the edge of the current network.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
To achieve higher performance in this new paradigm
one has to consider how to combine the efﬁciency of resource usage at all three layers of architecture: end devices, edge devices, and
the cloud.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text: While cloud capacity is elastically extendable, end devices and edge devices are to various degrees resource-constrained.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text: Hence, an efﬁcient resource management is essential to make edge computing a reality.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
In this work, we ﬁrst present terminology and
architectures to characterize current works within the ﬁeld of edge computing.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Then, we review a wide range of recent articles and
categorize relevant aspects in terms of 4 perspectives: resource type, resource management objective, resource location, and
resource use.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text: This taxonomy and the ensuing analysis is used to identify some gaps in the existing research.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Among several research
gaps, we found that research is less prevalent on data, storage, and energy as a resource, and less extensive towards the estimation,
discovery and sharing objectives.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
As for resource types, the most well-studied resources are computation and communication
resources.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Our analysis shows that resource management at the edge requires a deeper understanding of how methods applied at
different levels and geared towards different resource types interact.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Speciﬁcally, the impact of mobility and collaboration schemes
requiring incentives are expected to be different in edge architectures compared to the classic cloud solutions.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Finally, we ﬁnd that
fewer works are dedicated to the study of non-functional properties or to quantifying the footprint of resource management techniques,
including edge-speciﬁc means of migrating data and services.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text: Index Terms—Resource management, Survey, Edge computing, Fog computing.

INTRODUCTION
R
ECENTLY, the edge computing paradigm, which con-
sists in having network nodes with computational and
storage resources close to the devices (mobile phones, sen-
sors), at the edge of the current network, has attracted
interest from both industry and researchers, carrying the
promise of a new communication era in which industry can
meet the rising performance needs of future applications.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Indeed, with a forecast of 9 billion mobile subscriptions
in the world by 2022, of which 90% will include mobile
broadband, coupled to an eightfold increase in mobile trafﬁc
and 17.6 billion of Internet of Things (IoT) devices also
sending data [1], there will be a considerable strain put on
the network.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
The current network technologies need to un-
dergo a paradigm shift in order to handle this situation [2].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Therefore, the aim is to avoid overwhelming the network up
to the cloud, and, when possible, move some computing and
data analysis closer to the users, to enable better scalability
[3].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Thus, the main idea of edge (or fog) computing is to have
intermediate computing facilities between the end devices
and the current cloud.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
[4], this would also enable the current telecom network
operators to reduce their operational costs.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
In addition to this, moving computing and storage to the
edge of the network has other beneﬁts [3] such as reducing
the latency and jitter [5], which is especially important for
•

real-time applications such as self-driving cars.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Moreover, it
enables more privacy for the users by making it possible to
keep private data at the edge and enforce privacy policies
for the data sent to the cloud (such as blurring sensitive
info on a video [2]).
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Finally, edge networking makes the
applications more resilient by being able to process requests
at the edge even if the central cloud is down.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
In order to achieve this and to make edge computing
a reality and a success, there is a need for an efﬁcient
resource management at the edge.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Indeed, mobile devices
or IoT devices are resource-constrained devices, whereas
the cloud has almost unlimited but far away resources.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Providing and/or managing the resources at the edge will
enable the end device to spare resources (e.g.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
stored energy
in batteries), speed up computation, and allows using re-
sources it does not possess.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Moreover, keeping data close
to where it was generated enables better control, especially
for privacy-related issues.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Finally, being located close to
the user, edge computing makes it possible to increase the
quality of provided services through the use of proﬁling
within a local context, without compromising the privacy or
having to handle a large number of users.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Even though this is still an emerging research area, there
is a lot of work ongoing under different denominations
including mobile cloud computing [6], fog computing [7],
edge computing [3], mobile edge computing [8], path com-
puting [9], mobile edge cloud [10], mobile edge network
[4], inﬁnite cloud [11], follow-me cloud [12], mobile follow-
me cloud [13], multi-tier cloud federations [14], small cell
cloud [15], fast moving personal cloud [16], CONCERT [17],

text: distributed clouds [18], and femtoclouds [19], [20].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Independently of the terminology chosen, which might
follow the current naming trend, a common concept here is
an intermediate level between the device and the traditional
cloud.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
It is possible to ﬁnd in the literature numerous
surveys about those paradigms in general [6], [10], [21],
[22], [23], [24], [25], speciﬁc aspects of them such as security
[8], [26] or speciﬁc techniques such as Software-Deﬁned
Networking (SDN) [27].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
However, those typically do not
consider the resource aspect.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
The existing surveys about
resources either consider it at a high level [28] or consider
only resource/service provisioning metrics [29].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
One area that is of high importance and present in
many use-cases in edge computing is ofﬂoading.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
This is the
idea of executing a task on another device than the cur-
rent execution target, typically one having more powerful
computational capacities or being less energy-constrained.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Resource management is tightly connected to ofﬂoading
since in order to take a decision to ofﬂoad one needs to
have knowledge about system resources.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
This knowledge is
provided by resource management techniques.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
For example,
resource discovery can be used as an input for taking an
ofﬂoading decision while resource allocation techniques can
be used to perform the ofﬂoading decision.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
To the best of
our knowledge, existing surveys about resource manage-
ment for ofﬂoading at the edge focus on an end device
perspective [30], [31], on the resource allocation part of
resource management [32], [33] or on a single-user/multi-
user perspective [34].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
We aim to complement those surveys by providing a
more comprehensive perspective.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
That is, (a) we consider
allocation as one among ﬁve resource management objec-
tive, (b) we consider edge resources in addition to end
device or cloud resources, (c) we address multiple types of
resources and interrelations amongst them, (d) we review
aspects related to locality and what the resource is intended
for.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
In selecting the survey papers, work considering direct
interactions from a device to a cloud [35], or focusing on
cloud performance by ofﬂoading to the edge [36] are not
considered.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
However, ofﬂoading between edge devices, or
from the edge to the cloud when edge resources are also
considered, are included.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
All included papers consider the
notion of edge which we attempt to characterize by deﬁn-
ing edge-speciﬁc architectural instances.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
This will be done
independently of the terminology the authors chose to use.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
This paper is a substantial extension of our previous much
shorter review [37].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
In the remaining parts of this paper, we will ﬁrst present
the terminology used, deﬁne edge-speciﬁc architectures,
and present the proposed taxonomy in Section 2.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
The taxon-
omy is then exempliﬁed by an extensive review of papers,
which are categorized using the taxonomy elements intro-
duced, namely resource type (Section 3), resource manage-
ment objective (Section 4), resource location (Section 5), and
resource use (Section 6).
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
We then discuss research challenges
in Section 7 and conclude in Section 8.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
2
ARCHITECTURES AND RESEARCH TAXONOMY
Edge computing is an innovative area bringing together
diverse business sectors such as telecommunication actors,
vehicle vendors, cloud providers, and emerging application
or device providers e.g.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Therefore,
the terminology used in research works is diverse and still
evolving and multiple architectures are considered.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
In this section, we present ﬁrst the relevant terminology
associated with edge computing that will be used in the
rest of the paper.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Then, we discuss the current architectures
used and present an architectural breakdown that will be
the basis for classifying existing research.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Finally, we present
our proposed research taxonomy and use it to classify the
surveyed works.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
2.1
Terminology
Following the development of the IoT, it is nowadays not
only computers or smartphones which can be connected
to the network, but a large variety of things such as cars,
sensors, drones, robots, or home appliances.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
In this survey,
all those objects located at the user end of the network,
which produce data or need cloud/edge resources will be
called end devices.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Devices installed at the edge speciﬁcally for edge com-
puting purposes are called edge devices.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
We also include
under this term the devices that are already now connecting
the end devices to the rest of the network, for example, home
routers, gateways, access points, or base stations which are
becoming increasingly powerful [38].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Finally, physical components of the cloud are referred to
by the term cloud devices.

We use those network device classiﬁcations to create

Resources which are managed are

These

title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

2.2
Current status of edge architectures
There is currently no standard architecture for edge comput-
ing, although industry and research initiatives exist such as
the Open Edge Computing1 community, the Open Fog Con-
sortium 2, and a European Telecommunications Standards
Institute (ETSI) standardization group working on Multi-
access Edge Computing3.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Current standardization efforts
coming from the ETSI group have been reviewed in detail
by Mao et al.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
[34] also
present edge standardization efforts within the 5G standard.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Therefore, current research on edge computing is using
several different architectures and there is ongoing work
