6.1
Functional properties
Edge computing is promoted as a means of getting access
to a given service in most of the surveyed articles, i.e.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
for
satisfying functionality in an application.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
There are numer-
ous articles in the literature providing an overview of edge
applications, including [6], [7], [10], [23], [27], [34], [41], [89].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Such applications range over augmented reality, connected
vehicles, disaster recovery, and a lot of others.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
When looking at the different applications used in the
surveyed articles presented in the earlier sections, the ﬁrst
ﬁnding is that the majority of them (66%) do not consider
a speciﬁc application in their study.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Instead, they refer to
generic applications such as IoT services [59], real-time ap-
plications [68], latency-sensitive applications [58], or name
some applications but only as an illustration.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Table 5 presents the remaining papers according to
which type of application they consider.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
We can distinguish
seven areas in which the described applications can be
categorized.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Note that in the Generic category we place
papers that although not ﬁxed towards one domain of
application refer speciﬁcally to classes of applications that
they exemplify clearly.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
6.2
Non-functional properties
In addition to enabling functionalities when using the
edge computing paradigm the very organization of the
edge architecture and realizing desirable properties requires
some kind of resource management too.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
This additional
work is not directly related to the service to obtain, i.e.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
it is a non-functional property (also referred to as extra-
functional properties).
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Obviously, papers that are focusing
on a functional property can also be interested in some non-
functional property.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
This subsection is related to the categories of objectives
for resource management we have already discussed in sec-
tion 4.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Achieving the objectives in that section was evaluated
using metrics that are often representative for measuring
non-functional properties.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Examples of metrics and their related non-functional
property that are encountered more often are:
• response time as a measure of timeliness.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text: • energy consumption as a measure of energy efﬁciency.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Generic metrics related to a non-functional property used in the
surveyed articles.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
• admission ratio, or its equivalent blocking probability, as
a measure of availability of the edge service.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
• CPU/network utilization as a measure of computa-
tion/communication resource efﬁciency.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
• Monetary cost paid to an infrastructure owner as a
measure of cost efﬁciency.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
The list of metrics is not exhaustive, but we have focused
on the more prevalent ones.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Figure 4 shows how popular the
above metrics are in the context of the works studied so far.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
It is not surprising that those metrics that relate to
timeliness or availability or resource efﬁciency are well-
represented.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
As we have noticed earlier, the same paper can deal
with multiple resources, multiple objectives, and also clearly
seen in this ﬁgure, multiple non-functional properties.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
This
illustrates the complex trade-offs involved when dealing
with resources in a multi-stakeholder distributed system.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
7
RESEARCH CHALLENGES
In this section, we present the research challenges not sub-
stantially addressed which could be of interest for further
research in the ﬁeld.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
From the previous sections, we noted that the architec-
ture with three active and distinct levels (Edge server) is
predominant.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
We also noted that the resource objectives
allocation and optimization were well-studied.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Moreover,
computational and communicational resources are the most
commonly addressed, typically being stationary and located
within a single level.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Therefore, research is less prevalent on
data, storage, and energy as a resource, and less extensive
towards the estimation, discovery and sharing objectives
(especially the ﬁrst two).
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Furthermore, new works should
consider mobility and multi-level locality on the supply
side.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Elaborating on mobility, the new phenomenon at the
edge is that the supply side can also be mobile, and not


17
only the demand side as it was the case in classic clouds.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Indeed, edge systems will have to deal with a greater variety
of mobility, with end devices that are often mobile (like
vehicles) but can also be stationary (e.g.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
video-surveillance
cameras), as well as mobile edge devices.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
It is however
not obvious that the mobility patterns of all those devices
will be similar, especially between end and edge devices.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Considering the large variety of edge applications, their
characteristics can potentially vary greatly.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
For example, an
edge solution intended to serve networks of cars moving
on a road network will probably be quite different from an
edge solution intended to serve persons within a shopping
mall.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Hence, it is critical to have efﬁcient, and thus tailored
solutions.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
But should each application domain rediscover
the wheel?
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Obviously, there is going to be generic wisdom
that is transferable across the domains if adequate charac-
terizations of resource requirement patterns are formulated.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
More work is needed on collecting mobility traces from the
different edge applications to see if present patterns can in
a generic way be used to create pertinent edge mobility
models at both levels of the architecture, the end and the
edge level.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
These can then become a basis for repeatable
evaluations of resource management strategies.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Another aspect which will be critical to solving is col-
laboration.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
There are new papers appearing where mul-
tiple operators at the edge level are modeled, and this
introduces new challenges.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
At the end level, we have seen
that different incentives can be provided to enable resource
sharing [64], [81], and similarly at the edge level [74].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Such
collaboration is especially good for managing workload
churns and is interesting for infrastructure owners.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
The
next challenge would be to do multi-level collaboration
with a hierarchy of incentive schemes at different levels
assuring that they do not cancel out each other’s beneﬁts.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Moreover, ﬁnding more advanced incentive schemes that
take both resource efﬁciency and security into account is
needed.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Current solutions either choose to not collaborate
for security- or privacy- sensitive tasks [44] or rely on classic
trust establishment [74] but this will not be enough for a
wide collaboration at the edge.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Context adaptation is also one of the properties expected
from edge computing and advocated as a good reason
to choose this paradigm [90].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Providing tailored service
depending on the user’s physical location of course has to
be taken care of at the application level.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
However, it also
impacts resource management as those applications will
require resources to provide those services, in particular
considering data (about supply mobility and abundance) as
a resource.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Security, and its subcomponents availability, conﬁden-
tiality, and integrity, is a key point for edge computing, to-
gether with privacy with respect to sensitive end-user data.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Although similar, security and privacy have distinct charac-
teristics and should be addressed in depth and separately,
which is not the case in the current surveyed works [44],
[74].
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Regarding availability, most of the works considered
focus on admission ratio but do not consider the fact that
resources could disappear while executing due to mobility,
misuses, or attacks.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
A notable exception is the work by
Habak et al.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
[20] who propose and evaluate a task check-
pointing mechanism which performs result replication to
mitigate in case a device disappears.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Focusing on availabil-
ity, several works always consider that the cloud is available
as a last fall-back for providing an edge service.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
due to overload, attack, or natural disaster)
the availability of the edge service will be impacted.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
More
works in those directions and quantifying edge-speciﬁc
availability metrics are required.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Edge computing will most
certainly be interesting for critical infrastructure because of
its beneﬁts and those require high standards on security.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Research in this direction can be found for the mobile cloud
paradigm, for example [91], [92], but they consider scenarios
where the edge level is absent.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
End-to-end timeliness requires quantiﬁcation of latencies
from an end device towards the cloud (or somewhere at the
edge) all the way back to the same device (or to another de-
vice).
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
This means traversing the edge networking services,
including what we referred to as resource management
services in this paper.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Since estimation, discovery, sharing,
allocation (including migration) are complex algorithms in
such networks, these must also be evaluated in terms of
their own resource footprint, and thereby their own impact
on timeliness and QoS.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
In the surveyed articles, computing
time of the solution is only evaluated by Gomes et al.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Since edge computing cannot become
widely used without strong security and privacy properties,
it is especially important to research on the resource over-
head for providing those properties as well.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Too high an
overhead can signify a technology which is not feasible in
practice.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
As shown in Section 3, resources managed at the edge
are most often a combination of different resource types.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
This implies that there will be some interrelations among
resource utilization levels, which can create new challenges.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Considering resource afﬁnity as in the work by Yousaf et
al.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
[48] may be a start but more research is needed to un-
derstand and address the complexity of such multi-resource
problems in the edge context.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
As mentioned in Section 2, edge computing brings to-
gether diverse business sectors, with their existing tech-
niques for solving relevant problems in those areas.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Tech-
niques previously applied in only one of those domains
may be applicable to edge computing with the required
adaptations.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
For example, performing resource migration
requires efﬁcient techniques for this purpose.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
[93]
study container migration and found that the hand-off time
decreased by 56% to 80% in comparison to state-of-the-
art VM migration for the edge.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Results like this should be
exploited in the new edge era, and utilize technologies that
may bring added beneﬁt to edge computing.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Another enabler for resource-efﬁcient edge computing
is the development of tools for testing the new proposals
in relevant conditions and setups.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
In the surveyed articles,
the most common method used for validating a model or
a proposed algorithm is to use an analytical tool (e.g.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Another common
approach is to use a simulator, either a generic network
simulator such as OMNeT++5, or one designed for regular
cloud environments such as CloudSim [94], most often
with some custom extensions.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
https://omnetpp.org/


18
simulator designed for fog computing, called iFogSim [95],
which extends CloudSim, but this one currently has limita-
tions, e.g.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
no mechanisms for ofﬂoading or communication
between two nodes at the same level.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
A third way of evalu-
ating in the surveyed works is the use of physical testbeds.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Such evaluations provide invaluable insights into problems
that are easy to oversee in simulation and investigate their
impact.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
However, a big challenge for testbeds is to get
them to scale, which is to some extent also a problem for
simulations.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Therefore, there is a need for creating open
research testbeds and simulation tools so that conﬁgurable
architectures and application/domain-speciﬁc edge com-
puting methods can be efﬁciently compared.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Coming back
to a previous point, such tools should be able to handle
mobility of end and edge devices and should obviously be
scalable for evaluation of real-world scenarios.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
8
CONCLUSION
The past decade has created tremendous expectations on
IoT changing the landscape of data-driven services with
beneﬁts for multiple societal sectors.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Many researchers have
contributed to the development of technologies and ad-
dressed challenges that come with resource scarcity in the
end devices.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
Other researchers with a background in cloud
computing have looked at how to carry the data generated
by the massive IoT deployments and how to efﬁciently use
the cloud resources.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
The area of edge computing brings
these two ends of the same service together in an emerging
ecosystem and creates a means to discuss resource adequacy
from an end-to-end perspective.
title: A Taxonomy for Management and Optimization of Multiple Resources in Edge Computing

text:
In this paper we have tried
to provide an overview, not from a cloud perspective, or an
IoT device perspective, but with a focus on edge resource
management.

SAGE (Percipient StorAGe for Exascale Data Centric Computing) is a European Commission funded project towards the era of
Exascale computing.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Its goal is to design and implement a Big Data/Extreme Computing (BDEC) capable infrastructure with associated
software stack.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The SAGE system follows a storage centric approach as it is capable of storing and processing large data volumes at the
Exascale regime.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: SAGE addresses the convergence of Big Data Analysis and HPC in an era of next-generation data centric computing.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
This
convergence is driven by the proliferation of massive data sources, such as large, dispersed scientific instruments and sensors where
data needs to be processed, analyzed and integrated into simulations to derive scientific and innovative insights.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
A first prototype of
the SAGE system has been been implemented and installed at the Jülich Supercomputing Center.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The SAGE storage system consists of
multiple types of storage device technologies in a multi-tier I/O hierarchy, including flash, disk, and non-volatile memory technologies.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: The main SAGE software component is the Seagate Mero Object Storage that is accessible via the Clovis API and higher level interfaces.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: The SAGE project also includes scientific applications for the validation of the SAGE concepts.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The objective of this paper is to present the SAGE project concepts, the prototype of the SAGE platform and discuss the software
architecture of the SAGE system.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

INTRODUCTION
The next-generation Exascale supercomputers will be available to the community sometime in the 2021-2023 timeframe
and it will be capable of delivering up to 1018 floating point operations per seconds to support traditional HPC compute-
intensive applications.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
With the emergence of new HPC data centric applications, such as workflows and data analytics
workloads, the definition of Exascale computing is now broadening to include storage and processing of an order of an
exabyte of data.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
In fact, Big Data Analysis and HPC are converging as massive data sets, such as very large volumes of
data from scientific instruments and sensors, needs to be processed, analyzed and integrated into simulations.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
For this
reason, we envision that Exascale supercomputers will be capable to be exploited by applications and workflows for
science and technological innovation.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Computing infrastructure innovation has been driven by Moore’s law and the development of even more parallelism
with multi-core, many-core and accelerator processing to accommodate the increasing performance requirements of
Exascale.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: However I/O and storage have lagged far behind in computational power improvement.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Storage performance
in the same time period is predicted to have improved for only 100 times, according to early estimates provided by
Vetter et al.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
In fact, at the time of publication of this work, the performance of disk drives per unit capacity is
actually decreasing with new very high capacity disk drives on the horizon [28].
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Simultaneously, the landscape for
storage is changing with the emergence of new storage device technologies, such as flash (available today) and the
promise of non-volatile memory technologies available in the near future [15, 19].
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The optimal use of these devices
(starting with flash) in the I/O hierarchy, combined with existing disk technology, is only beginning to be explored in
HPC [4] with burst buffers [10].
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: The SAGE project is a European Commission funded project to investigate Exascale computing [14].
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
It supports
a storage centric view of Exascale computing by proposing hardwares to support multi-tiered I/O hierarchies and
associated software.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: They provide a demonstrable path towards Exascale.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Further, SAGE proposes a radical approach in
extreme scale HPC by moving traditional computations, typically done in the compute cluster, to the storage system.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: This has the potential of significantly reducing the energy footprint of the overall system [22].
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: The primary objective of this paper is to present the initial hardware and software architecture of the SAGE system.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Section 2 presents the initial development of the SAGE platform.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Section 3 describes
the SAGE platform architecture and software stack.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Finally, Section 6 summarizes
the paper and outlines the future work.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

A STORAGE CENTRIC ARCHITECTURE
The SAGE storage system developed by the SAGE consortium provides a unique paradigm to store, access and process
data in the realm of extreme-scale data centric computing.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: The SAGE platform consists of multiple tiers of storage device technologies.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
At the bottom of the stack is the Unified
Object-Based Storage Infrastructure.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The system does not require any specific storage device technology type and
accommodates upcoming NVRAM, existing flash and disk tiers.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
For the NVRAM tier, we are using Intel 3D XPoint
technology [2] in our Tier-1.

We will also use emulated NVDIMMs (Non-Volatile DIMMs) in Tier-1 because of the lack

SAGE SOFTWARE STACK
Together with the development of SAGE storage centric prototype platform, we designed and developed software
capable of taking advantage of the SAGE infrastructure.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
A simplified diagram of the SAGE software stack is presented
in Figure 2.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
3.1
Mero
Mero is at the base of the SAGE software stack, providing the Exascale-capable object storage infrastructure that
drives the storage hardware [3].
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Mero is a distributed object storage platform.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Lustre file system, NFSv4 and database
technology are the the main sources of inspiration for the Mero design.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
An emerging consensus is that traditional file
system properties (hierarchical directory namespace, strong POSIX consistency guarantees, etc) pose a major obstacle
for the performance and scalability of Exascale systems.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Mero controls a cluster of nodes connected by a network.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Some nodes have persistent storage attached to them.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Mero
distinguishes various types of persistent stores including rotational drives, SAS-attached non-volatile memory devices
and PCIe-/memory bus attached non-volatile memory devices.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Mero presents a collection of services to applications.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Manuscript submitted to ACM


The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing
5
Mero Object store has a "core" providing - scalable re-writable fault-tolerant data objects, Index store with scalable
key-value indices, and, resource management capabilities for caches, locks, extents, etc.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Extreme scale features such as containers and function shipping are built on top of the core.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Mero also features a
Distributed transaction manager, which makes it possible to use other services in a consistent manner in the face of
hardware and software failures, which is also an extreme scale feature on top of the core.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Mero also has an Extension mechanism which allows the addition of new functionalities without modification to the
core, called the FDMI, or File Data Manipulation Interface.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
New services such as Information lifecycle management (ILM),
indexing, search, etc can hence be built as extensions by third parties leveraging the core.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
A Mero application can be a traditional user space application, running standalone on a node, a large MPI job running
on multiple nodes, a cluster management utility monitoring the state of the system, or a NFS/CIFS daemon (a front-end)
exporting Mero objects to non-Mero clients, etc.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Containers are the main way of grouping objects in various ways.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
They virtualize the
object name space by providing the capability to label objects in various ways.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
There can be containers based on data
formats (for example, HDF5 containers, etc) and containers based just on performance (for example, high performance
containers which are mapped to objects in higher tiers, etc).
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
It is possible to do operations such as function shipping,
pre/post processing on a given containers.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Existing systems and data [25] indicate that we can expect many hardware failures
per second at Exascale, in addition to software failures resulting in crashed nodes.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
To maintain service availability in the
face of expected failures, a global state (or configuration) of the cluster is maintained.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
This may need to be modified by
the means of repair procedures in response to failure events.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The HA subsystem for SAGE will perform such automated
repair activities within storage device tiers.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The HA subsystem thus monitors failure events (inputs) throughout the
storage tiers and then decides to take action based on collected events.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Distributed Transaction Management (DTM).
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
In Mero, all I/O and metadata operations are, ultimately, organized
into transactions.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Transactions are atomic with respect to failures.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
In other words, either all or none of the updates
corresponding to a transaction are visible to other users.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
A related property is
failure atomicity, i.e.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: either all or none of the updates corresponding to a transaction survive a failure.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
A group of
updates that must atomically survive a failure is called a distributed transaction.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Mero implements a Distributed Transaction Manager (DTM) that guarantees efficient management of system state
consistency in an environment in which dependent data and metadata are scattered over multiple nodes to provide
fault tolerance and scalability.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
DTM provides the necessary interface to group a collection of object store updates into a
distributed transaction and guarantees that, in the event of a server node failure and restart, the effects of distributed
transactions that have updates for the affected server are either completely restored after restart or completely eliminated.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: A layout is a mapping of different parts or regions of an object to storage tiers.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Each object has a layout
attribute that defines how the object is stored in the cluster.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Mero provides a flexible, hierarchical description to map
object subcomponents to physical locations, or storage tiers.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
This mapping allows for compact formulaic expressions,
as well as data transformations, such as erasure coding, de-duplication, encryption and compression.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Layouts also
describe data redundancy models, like simple replication or Server Network Striping.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
As an example of a layout, an
object can have some extents mapped to Tier-1, other extents mapped to Tier-2 and a few others mapped to Tier-3.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Further, each of set of extents mapped to a certain tier can have its own "sub-layout".
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Function shipping in Mero provides the ability to run application functions directly on storage
nodes.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
This addresses one of the big bottlenecks foreseen for Exascale systems, which is the overhead of moving data to
Manuscript submitted to ACM


6
S.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Indeed moving very large quantities of data from storage to compute is extremely energy intensive and
energy is one of the prime candidates to address for Exascale systems.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Well defined functions within the use cases are
registered on the storage nodes and are invoked by the use cases using remote procedure calls.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Function shipping is
accomplished through extensions of the Mero Clovis API (see next section).
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Modern storage systems are increasingly heterogeneous.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
This means not only multitude of data
sources and data formats, but also the multitude of applications accessing shared data sets with different access patterns,
multitude of various storage policies (retention, access control, provenance, etc.) and multitude of conflicting goals
that the storage system must balance (latency vs.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Historically, providing an
interface that allowed different applications to access shared data often resulted in great benefits both for application
and system developers, the two most famous examples being UNIX "everything-is-a-file" and relational models.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Data
stored in Mero are accessible to multiple applications using various existing storage interfaces (e.g., POSIX, pNFS, S3,
HDF5).
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
A component of Mero called Lingua Franca (LF) implements common meta-data formats and interfaces that
enables interoperability between multiple external interfaces and internal meta-data users.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
LF is a mechanism to share the same sets of storage entities (objects, indices and containers) between multiple
applications with different access interfaces.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Its straightforward use is to provide interoperability between different
front-ends.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Together with other Mero features, like containers and function shipping, it can be used to implement a
very flexible access arrangement to the data.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
3.2
Clovis
Mero’s application programming interface (API), known as Clovis, provides a library of functions that applications and
front-end programs can use for accessing and manipulating storage resources in Mero.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Access to storage resources
by outside applications is strictly controlled via Clovis; no other interfaces exist.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The Clovis API contains optimized
functions to manage performance and scalability for modern extreme scale computing applications as well as legacy
applications.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
We expect higher-level applications, as part of development work related to accessing Mero storage
resources, to build their own APIs on top of Clovis.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
In other words, we do not expect computational scientists to directly
interface with the Clovis interface.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Higher-level interfaces include HDF5, POSIX via pNFS, and others.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The Clovis API is implemented in the C programming language, but equivalent versions of the API are planned in
other popular programming languages such as Java, Python, etc.

The Clovis API supports asynchronous transactions,
i.e.

For clarity, the API is divided into three sub-APIs: the Clovis Access API, the Clovis Management API and the Clovis
Extension API.

text: Clovis provides the following abstractions, shown in Figure 3.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Short descriptions of the abstractions are provided
below:
• Object is an array of fixed size blocks of data
• Index is a key-value store
• An entity is an object or an index
• Realm is a spatial and temporal part of the system with a prescribed access discipline
• Operation is a process of querying and/or updating the system state
• Objects, indices and operations live in realms
• Transaction is a collection of operations that are atomic in the face of failure

freeing the resources the objects use).

3.3
Higher-Level I/O Interfaces
At the top of the software stack, we further develop widely-used HPC legacy APIs, such as MPI and HDF5, to exploit
the SAGE architecture.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The goal of the Partitioned Global Address Space (PGAS) programming model is to provide processes
with a global view of the memory and storage space during the execution of a parallel application.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
This is similar to
what a Shared Memory model provides in a multithreaded local environment.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
In the PGAS approach, remote processes
from different nodes can easily collaborate and access memory addresses through load / store operations that do not
necessarily belong to their own physical memory space.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
In SAGE, we propose an extension to the MPI one-sided
communication model to support window allocations in storage: MPI storage windows [23, 24].
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Our objective is to define
a seamless extension to MPI to support current and future storage technologies without changing the MPI standard,
allowing to target either files (i.e., for local and remote storage through a parallel file system) or alternatively address
block devices directly (i.e., as in DRAM).
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
We propose a novel use of MPI windows, a part of the MPI process memory
that is exposed to other MPI remote processes, to simplify the programming interface and to support high-performance
parallel I/O without requiring the use of MPI I/O.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Files on storage devices appear to users as MPI windows (MPI storage
windows) and seamlessly accessed through familiar PUT and GET operations.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Details about the semantics of operations
on MPI storage windows and the implementation are provided in Ref.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: MPI Streams for Post-Processing and Parallel I/O.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
While PGAS I/O library addresses the challenge of heteroge-
nous storage and memory, streams can be used to support function-shipping for post-processing and highly scalable
parallel I/O.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Streams are a continuous sequence of fine-grained data structures that move from a set of processes, called
data producers, to another set of processes, called data consumers.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
These fine-grained data structures are often small in
size and in a uniform format, called a stream element.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
A set of computations, such as post-processing and I/O operations,
can be attached to a data stream.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Stream elements in a stream are processed online such that they are discarded as soon
as they are consumed by the attached computation.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
In particular, our work in SAGE focuses on parallel streams, where data producers and consumers are distributed
among processes that require communication to move data.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
To achieve this, we have developed a stream library, called
MPIStream, to support post-processing and parallel I/O operations on MPI consumer processes [13, 16, 17].
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
More details
about MPI streams operation semantics and MPIStream implementation are provided in Ref.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Typically, data formats in HPC provide their own libraries to describe data structures and their relations
(including I/O semantics).
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The HDF5 data format needs to be supported in SAGE, and is layered directly on top of
Clovis.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The HDF5 will use the Virtual Object Layer Infrastructure within HDF5 (used to interface HDF5 with various
object formats), to interface with Clovis.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
3.4
Tools
A following are a set of tools for I/O profiling and optimized data movement across different SAGE platform tiers at the
top of the SAGE software stack.

title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

Flink connectors for Clovis are
currently under development to enable the deployment of data analytics jobs on top of Mero.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Parallel file system access is the traditional method of accessing storage in HPC.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Many
of the SAGE applications and use cases need the support of POSIX compliant storage access.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
This access is provided
through the pNFS gateway built on top of Clovis.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
However, pNFS requires some POSIX semantics to be developed by
leveraging Mero’s KVS.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: For instance, an abstraction of namespaces on top of Mero objects is needed.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Hierarchical storage management and Data Integrity.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
In SAGE, an Hierarchical Storage Management (HSM)
is used to control the movement of data in the SAGE hierarchies based on data usage.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Advanced integrity checking
overcomes some of the drawbacks of well known and widely used file system consistency checking schemes.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

ADDB telemetry records from the Clovis management interface are directly fed to ARM Forge
performance report tools that reports overall system performance for SAGE.

5
RELATED WORK
To the best of our knowledge SAGE is the first HPC-enabled storage system to implement new NVRAM tiers, flash and
disk drive tiers as part of a single unified storage system.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The SAGE Architecture progresses the state of the art from
Blue Gene Active Storage [6] and Dash [9], which use flash for data staging.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
It also progresses the state of the art from
Burst Buffer technologies as discussed earlier.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
When compared to the FastForward Project [4], SAGE highly simplifies storage, developing a solution for deep I/O
hierarchies, including NVRAM technologies.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
A major difference between SAGE and FastForward is the FastForward
solution is evolutionary as it tries to make use of an existing storage solution, namely, Lustre [26] used for the last
20 years or so.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Lustre was really designed for the previous era, when use cases and architectural assumptions were
different.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
On the hand, SAGE and Mero are the product of a complete redesign in consideration of the new requirements
arising out of the Extreme scale computing community.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
Mero, the object store in SAGE, extends the state of the art in existing object storage software such as Ceph [30]
and Open Stack Swift [27] by building Exascale components required for extreme scale computing.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
While Ceph and
Openstack swift are designed for supporting mainly cloud storage, Mero is built to meet the needs of the extreme scale
computing community.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
6
CONCLUSIONS
The SAGE project objective is to design and implement an I/O system capable of supporting I/O workloads of Exascale
supercomputers.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: The SAGE platform has been recently installed at Jülich Computing center.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
It supports a multi-tiered
I/O hierarchy and associated software stack, to provide a demonstrable path towards Big Data analytics and HPC
convergence.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The SAGE software stack consists of four main software layers: the Seagate Mero object-storage, the
Clovis API, high-level interfaces and tools.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text: Current ongoing work focuses on the performance characterization of various new NVRAM device technologies.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
We
also currently investigating lower level software and Operating System (OS) infrastructure requirements to exploit
these new devices types, below Mero in the SAGE stack.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
We clearly recognize that various NVRAM technologies have
their own performance characteristics and limitations.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
New NVRAM technologies can be part of the SAGE hardware
tiers based on where they ultimately are on the performance and capacity curve.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The SAGE stack and Mero indeed is
designed to be agnostic of storage device types as long as adaptations are in place within the OS.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
The next steps will be to quantify the benefits of the various features of the SAGE stack on the SAGE prototype
system currently installed at Jülich Supercomputing Center, with focus on providing results for the remaining SAGE
components and the SAGE architecture as a whole.
title: The SAGE Project: a Storage Centric Approach for Exascale Computing

text:
As a part of this external organizations outside of the SAGE
consortium ( eg: from Climate and Weather, Astronomy, etc) will soon be granted access to study how their codes and

INTRODUCTION
The exponential rate of hardware miniaturization, emer-
gence of low cost and low power sensing modalities coupled
with rapid developments in communication technologies
are driving the world towards a future where tiny scale
computing will be more pervasive and seamlessly inte-
grated with everyday life.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
This sea of change is driven
by the increasing ability of tiny computing platforms to
connect people and things to the Internet—the Internet-
of-Things (IoT) [1]—enabling transformative applications
ranging from healthcare [2], [3] to preventing counterfeiting
[4], [5].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Despite the magnitude of possibilities, the basic
architecture of those IoT devices are quite similar; micro-
controllers, transceivers, sensors, batteries, and sometimes,
actuators are coupled with the most important component,
the application speciﬁc software or more simply ‘code’ which
endows the ‘Things’ with the ability to communicate with

However, a
signiﬁcant challenge materializes from the need to patch,
update or reprogram the application speciﬁc software in
the form of ﬁrmware without the supervisory control of
an operating system; to do so, a physical connection to a
device is required.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Unfortunately, a wired connection not
only negates the beneﬁt of the battery-free feature and
makes the process unscalable when potentially millions of
devices need to be updated, but is a more acute problem
in the context of deeply embedded devices, such as a blood
glucose monitor, where physical access to the device poses
practical challenges and risks to the end-user.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
1.1
Problem
We deﬁne ﬁrmware update as the transfer of partial or
entire executable code from the prover P to the non-volatile
memory of the CRFID device, referred to as the token T .
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The ﬁrmware update aims to, e.g., enhance CRFID device’s
computational or storage performance, impart new func-
tionality, ﬁx software bugs or address system compatibil-
ity.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The ﬁrmware update is conducted either by physically
connecting a download cable or in a wireless manner.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Our
work considers the more desirable but challenging secure
wireless ﬁrmware update to eschew the cumbersome and,
often impractical, cable-connected download method.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The fundamental problem of a wireless ﬁrmware up-
date for CRFID devices was addressed in two recent ap-
proaches [12], [13]; both focused on transmission reliability,
miniaturization of ﬁrmware code size, and energy efﬁciency.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
None of them addressed the difﬁcult problem of assuring
the security of wireless ﬁrmware updates, although Tan et
al.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
[12] highlighted that secure wireless code dissemination
remains the most urgent need to be addressed.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
This implies
that both wireless approaches allow any party, irrespective
of their trustworthiness, to remotely and wirelessly install
code on a CRFID device.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Consequently, malicious ﬁrmware
injection from an adversary remains a direct threat that can
lead to, for example, private information leakage such as
health condition to unauthorized parties or the installation
of malicious code in deeply embedded hardware such as
a blood glucose monitor with devastating consequences
for the victim.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Addressing the research questions above requires over-
coming a number of challenges.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We brieﬂy outline the key
challenges below:
• Receiving and writing ﬁrmware to non-volatile mem-
ory (NVM) by a token requires considerable amount
of energy [15] when operating on harvested power,
even before we consider a secure update mechanism.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Battery-free CRFID transponders harvest energy from
incident radio waves and the available energy is further
inﬂuenced by a range of factors such as propagation
path loss from the radio source to the transponder
and shadowing effects created by intervening objects
along the radio wave propagation path.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Hence, de-
vices that operate on harvested power, such as CRFID
transponders, are always constrained by energy and
computation capability as illustrated in Fig.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
There-
fore, security must be realized under severe energy and
computational resource limitations of a token.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text: • Frequent state loss—as illustrated in Fig.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
2—results
from interruptions to powering and the transient nature
of power availability [12].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
This is especially problematic
when updating executable code.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Careless handling of
state loss may lead to unrecoverable ﬁrmware cor-
ruption or leave the token vulnerable to attacks [16].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, a ﬁrmware update mechanism should be
robust even under state loss.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text: • Security mechanisms rely on secure storage of keys.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Traditional key storage methods in NVM is readily
vulnerable to various attacks without expensive protec-
tion, for example, protective coatings and active tamper
sensing circuity requiring batteries.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Low-end IoT de-
vices are usually lack of a secure NVM to maintain the
key security.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, a secure key storage method
without additional hardware overhead, modiﬁcations
and costs is highly desirable.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
• A secure update protocol design must overcome the
common difﬁculty of transferring large chunks of data
to a transponder over narrow bandwidth wireless chan-
nels while still being compliant with existing stan-
dards and interface protocols for communicating with
devices.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Standards compliance will not only ensure
successful adoption in practice but also interoperability
with existing technologies.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
1.2
Contributions
Our work takes the ﬁrst step towards secure code dissemi-
nation for resource constrained and intermittently powered
CRFID devices through a systematic approach that com-
bines theory and judicious cryptographic engineering.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We
summarize the contributions of our work below and defer
comparison of prior work to Section 6.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
• A ﬁrst secure wireless ﬁrmware update protocol: Se-
cuCode is the ﬁrst secure wireless ﬁrmware update or
reprogramming method for CRFID devices to prevent
malicious ﬁrmware injection attacks1.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
• Lightweight physically obfuscated key derivation
mechanism: We develop a key derivation mechanism
using a physical unclonable function (PUF).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A PUF
converts hardware instance speciﬁc random variations
such as gate and wire delays of circuitry to a binary
value.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In particular, we take advantage of the random
start-up state of intrinsic Static Random Access Mem-
ory (SRAM) on microcontrollers to extract key mate-
rial on the ﬂy without extra hardware overhead and
modiﬁcations.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The key derived from such an SRAM
PUF is therefore: i) intrinsically tamper-resistant (un-
clonability) compared to a permanently stored key in
non-volatile memory; ii) unique, through the hardware
instance speciﬁc nature of SRAM cells’ startup state;
iii) unpredictable, through the physical randomness
leading to random startup states of SRAM cells; and
iv) never stored permanently in NVM as it is derived
on the ﬂy and discarded after usage.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Our contribution
here is to address the challenges faced in realizing a
1.

prevents an attacker from injecting malicious code.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We achieve this aim
by establishing the integrity and authenticity of a ﬁrmware.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
To reduce the
burden on a resource limited device, we do not consider the provision
of conﬁdentiality protection.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

3
lightweight, reliable and secure2 key generator using an
on-chip SRAM PUF on a resource constrained device.

of power availability.

We develop a tool (SecuCode
App) to update ﬁrmware and conduct a complete end-

• Host to Reader.

An application on the host machine
constructs LLRP commands to build an ROSpec and
AccessSpec to control the reader and transmits these
speciﬁcations to a reader.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
As part of the anti-collision algo-
rithm in the media access control layer, the reader must
ﬁrst singulate a CRFD device and obtain a handle,
RN16.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Singulation is achieved as part of the inven-
tory operation to discover RFID devices in the pow-
ering and reading range of a reader.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Inventory is per-
formed through a combination of Query, QueryRep,
and QueryAdjust commands.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
At the start of the in-
ventory cycle the reader transmits a Query command,
this notiﬁes any devices in range, the beginning of
a new inventory session.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Each device then selects a
random slot counter between zero and an upper value,
Q, deﬁned by the Query command.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
If the selected slot
counter is zero, then the tag backscatters its handle,
RN16, to the reader, otherwise the tag remains silent.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
On receiving a QueryRep, the tag decrements its slot
counter and backscatters a response if the resulting
counter value is zero.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
On receiving a QueryAdjust,
the tag adjusts the Q value and regenerates its slot
counter.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A singulated transponder can subsequently be queried
using a range of Access commands such as BlockWrite
used to write data to a transponder memory.

Our approach
is to realize a standard compliant secure ﬁrmware update
