4
2.2
Physically Obfuscated Key Derivation
In our secure wireless ﬁrmware update method, the in-
tegrity and authenticity of the ﬁrmware is dependent on the
secure storage of a private key on a CRFID device.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A phys-
ical unclonable function (PUF) is a cost-efﬁcient security
primitive for deriving volatile physically obfuscated keys on
demand for resource and power limited devices.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore,
we provide a brief overview on PUFs and introduce the
reverse fuzzy extractor to realize secure and lightweight key
derivation from slightly noisy PUF responses (key material).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
2.2.1
Physical Unclonable Functions
A PUF reacts with an instance-speciﬁc response (output) by
exploiting manufacturing randomness when it is queried
by a challenge (input) [19].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
It is widely employed for
cryptographic key generation and lightweight authentica-
tion applications, including low-end resource-constrained
devices [20]–[22].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In this paper, we exploit the on-chip SRAM
to act as a PUF.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Notably, the SRAM PUF is an intrinsic
PUF; i.e.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
the realization of the PUF does not require a
custom design, additional chip area overhead, or hardware
modiﬁcations [23], [24].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Typically, one single SRAM cell con-
sists of two cross-coupled inverters functioning as a latch.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The initial power-up state of each SRAM cell is random
but reproducible [25], thus, the power-up pattern of bits
generated from an SRAM memory—referred as an SRAM
PUF—can be viewed as a unique identiﬁer.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In such a PUF,
the address of the SRAM cell acts as the challenge, the initial
power-up state—‘1’/‘0’—acts as the response.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
It is worth
mentioning here that, instead of the power-up state of the
SRAM cells, the data retention voltage (DRV) of SRAM cells
can also be characterized and exploited as PUF responses—
the so-called DRV PUF [26], [27].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In our study, we employ
the power-up state of SRAM to build a PUF due to the
simplicity of the response readout method at power-up.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, use of SRAM PUF responses as key material is
challenged by inconsistent regeneration of response bits and
potential response bias, which are addressed in Section 4.3.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
2.2.2
Reverse Fuzzy Extractor
PUF response regeneration is noisy as it is vulnerable to ﬂuc-
tuations in environmental conditions such as thermal noise
and power supply and temperature variations.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Thus, PUF
responses cannot be directly used as a key and requires error
correction to rectify ﬂipped response bits (errors) in relation
to a reference response.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In this case, a fuzzy extractor (FE)
is usually deployed to derive a key by using helper data to
correct regenerated responses at a later time.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A fuzzy extractor FE is described by two algorithms—
see detailed descriptions in Section 3.1: i) key generation
or enrollment algorithm FE.Gen; and ii) key reconstruction
algorithm FE.Rec.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, the computational complexity
of computing the helper data by FE.Gen and the key recon-
struction by FE.Rec using the helper data is asymmetric.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, here we construct a reverse fuzzy extractor [21]
to ensure the lightweight FE.Gen implementation is on the
resource-constrained CRFID device while the computation-
ally expensive FE.Rec is implemented at the resource-rich
server (or prover P in our case).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In general, a reverse fuzzy extractor’s FE.Gen function is
implemented on the device.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Then the device applies a ran-
dom challenge c sent by a server to obtain a noisy response
r from an on-device PUF and uses the generator function
FE.Gen to compute helper data h for the noisy response r.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Subsequently, the
server uses the helper data to reconstruct the response r
with a securely stored response r′ that is evaluated during
a secure provisioning phase for the given challenge c [21].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
3
SECUCODE: PROTOCOL DESIGN
We ease into the design of the protocol by ﬁrst describing
the notations used in the protocol followed by a formal
description of the SecuCode protocol.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
3.1
Notations
The notations used in the rest of the paper, following that
in [20], is described below:
• A bold lowercase character is used for a vector, for
example, a challenge applied to a PUF is c.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A bold
uppercase character is used for a set, for example, a
challenge set C, where c ∈C.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
• True Random Number Generator TRNG outputs a
truly random number when invoked.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
• Physical Unclonable Function PUF takes a challenge c
as input and reacts with a corresponding response r as
output, where r ←PUF(c).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
• Message Authentication Code MAC computes a bit
string s of ﬁxed length to establish the authenticity and
the integrity of a message.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Speciﬁcally, s ←MAC(m,
sk) computes a MAC from a message m—to prevent
replay attacks, a nonce can be concatenated with the
message—and a key sk.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
• Fuzzy Extractor A fuzzy extractor FE is deﬁned by two
functions: key generation algorithm FE.Gen and key
reconstruction algorithm FE.Rec.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The FE.Gen takes a
variable z as input and produces key sk and helper data
h.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The FE.Rec algorithm recovers the sk assisted with
h by taking the z′ as input if the Hamming distance
HD(z, z′) is sufﬁciently small, i.e.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
HD(z, z′)≤t with t a
ﬁxed parameter—correctness of reconstruction guarantee.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
If HD(z, z′)≤
t for input z and min-entropy [28] of
z ≥|h|, the fuzzy extractor provides key sk that is
statistically close to a uniformly distributed random
variable in {0, 1}|sk| although helper data h is exposed
to an adversary—security guarantee.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Fuzzy extractors
are generally built with an error-correction method [29].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
3.2
Adversary Model
In this paper, our focus is on the communication between
the Reader and the CRFID transponder or Token T .
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We
assume that the communication between a Host and a
Reader is secure using standard cryptographic mechanisms
for securing communication between two parties over a
network [5]; hence a Host computer and a Reader are
considered as a single entity, the Prover, denoted as P.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
There is no previous CRFID ﬁrmware update protocol
that considers security.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, no existing adversary


5
model has been reasoned.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In this initial secure wireless
ﬁrmware update investigation, we follow a relevant model
and assumptions in PUF-based authentication protocols de-
signed for resource-constrained platforms [20], [21].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Notably, a wireless ﬁrmware update of a CRFID device
is only possible after: i) the commissioning of the device
whereby an immutable program called the bootloader is
installed on the device; and ii) the prover P has enrolled—
extraction and secure storage of—SRAM PUF responses in a
secure environment using a one-time access wired interface.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We assume that the wired interface is disabled after the
installation of the bootloader and enrollment of the PUF
responses.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In other words, the adversary A cannot directly
access the SRAM PUF responses, only the immutable boot-
loader maintains this access at power-up and for a very
short duration of time.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
After the commissioning of the
device, both a trusted party and the adversary A must use
the wireless interface for installing new ﬁrmware on a token.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Subsequent deployment of a token T will place it in an
adversarial environment where only the prover P remains
trusted.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We assume that the attacker A can eavesdrop on
the communication channel, isolate the CRFID transponder
from the system and carry out a man-in-the-middle attack
and forward tampered information from P to T and vice
versa.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Further, following the assumptions in [20], within
the adversarial environment, the adversary A may obtain
any data stored in the NVM of the devices.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, as
in [20], the adversary A cannot mount implementation
attacks against the CRFID, nor gain internal variables stored
in the registers, for example, using invasive attacks and side-
channel analysis.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Similar to other adversarial models, we
do not consider Denial of Service (DoS) attacks because, in
practice, it is not possible to defend against an attacker that,
for example, disrupts or jams the wireless communication
medium [30], or attempts to heat the intrinsic SRAM cells to
prevent a ﬁrmware update as a result of the proposed con-
ditional ﬁrmware update method (detailed in Section 4.3.1).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
3.3
SecuCode Protocol
SecuCode protocol described in Fig.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
4 relies on the simplic-
ity of transmitting the ﬁrmware in plaintext and assumes
the adversary A can gain full knowledge of the ﬁrmware—
this is consistent with our adversary model which assumes
that an adversary can read the contents of the NVM of
a CRFID device.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Our focus is to prevent malicious code
injection attacks.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
SecuCode achieves this goal by facilitating
the authentication of the prover by the token and ensuring
the integrity of the ﬁrmware by the token before accepting
the ﬁrmware.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, only ﬁrmware issued by the trusted
prover will be accepted.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The SecuCode protocol is designed to be implemented
over the EPC Gen2 protocol.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We employ the recently de-
ﬁned extended Access command features for supporting fu-
ture security services on RFID transponders.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Consequently,
ﬁrmware update initializations employs TagPrivilege
and Authenticate while downstream data transmissions
in SecuCode are carried out by employing the EPC Gen2
protocol speciﬁcation of BlockWrite and SecureComm
commands.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The SecureComm command speciﬁcation al-
lows the encapsulation of other EPC Gen2 protocol com-
mands, such as BlockWrite but the payload is encrypted.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Hence, we employ the SecureComm command to transport
the message authentication code to the token.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We employ
BlockWrite command to write ﬁrmware to a memory
space, or download area, allocated and managed by the
bootloader on a CRFID transponder.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Although the speciﬁca-
tion of TagPrivilege, Authenticate and SecureComm
commands are deﬁned in the EPC Gen2 protocol, it is
important to mention here that these commands are yet to be
supported on CRFID transponders and this also constitutes
one of the tasks in this study.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The key phases in our
proposed SecuCode protocol are summarized below:
• Prover initialization phase in a secure environment:
This phase is carried out in a secure environment.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A
publicly known unique ID string is stored in a token’s
NVM.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The prover P enrolls in a database DB the ID
string of the target token T as well as the challenge-
response pairs (CRP) from the PUF (also known as
the enrollment phase [19]).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The bootloader, immutable
program stored in a write protected memory space,
is installed on the token T
by the prover P and,
subsequently, the physical interface to T is disabled.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The bootloader is responsible for the SecuCode protocol
implementation on the token.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
• Firmware update phase in a potential adversarial en-
vironment: For each code dissemination session, there
will be a compiled ﬁrmware at the prover P to be
transmitted along with a setup proﬁle which describes
the size of the ﬁrmware, starting memory address and
the MAC method for the token T .
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In particular, the
following occurs: i) lightweight physically obfuscated
key derivation on the token and the subsequent trans-
mission of the token generated random challenge seed
c and helper data h to the prover; ii) ﬁrmware up-
date which includes the wireless transfer of ﬁrmware
to the token, the establishment of the veracity of the
ﬁrmware on the token to accept/abort the ﬁrmware
update issued by the prover and update of ﬁrmware
on the token.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
3.3.1
Lightweight Physically Obfuscated Key Derivation
After the token T harvests adequate power from the prover
P, a nonce is generated for use in the ﬁrmware update
session, meanwhile a random number ci is generated as the
seed challenge; ci can be viewed as a challenge seed that
determines the starting index into a byte level address in
a block of highly reliable and unbiased SRAM PUF cells;
for a detailed discussion please refer to Section 4.3.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
These
responses are subsequently readout; ri ←PUF(ci).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We propose a conditional ﬁrmware update method
based on evaluating the on-chip temperature prior to the
key derivation phase since response reliability of SRAM
PUFs are more sensitive to changes in temperature than
supply voltage.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
This is to signiﬁcantly reduce the compu-
tational burden on the PUF key generation overhead while
meeting error correction and security bounds—details in
Section 4.3.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Immediately before key derivation, the TEMP()
function sets an over-temperature ﬂag (TOF) if the in-built
chip thermometer reports a temperature outside of a legal
range ( 0◦C to 40◦C is the chosen legal range in this
work).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Setting OTF will result in aborting key derivation
and triggering a re-booting of the token.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A token T operating under a legal temperature range
will execute the private key ski derivation and helper data
bfhi generation as (ski,hi)←FE.Gen(ri).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The private key
ski is used in the following ﬁrmware update process and
only retained in the SRAM on the token T for the duration
of the protocol session and discarded: i) at the completion
of a session; or ii) during a power loss event.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
3.3.2
Firmware Update
The ID of the token T is checked by the prover P to select
the target token and once the target is conﬁrmed to be
visible to the prover and is singulated, the prover P can em-
ploy Access commands Authenticate, BlockWrite and
SecureComm—see Figure 3 for an illustration of the EPC
Gen2 protocol behavior—to execute the ﬁrmware update.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The prover issues an Authenticate command to de-
liver setup parameters.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The token responds with the nonce,
ci and hi back to the prover.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The prover P reconstructs the
private key ski through ski ←FE.Rec(r′
i, hi); here, r′
i is
the enrolled response corresponding to ci.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Now the prover
P and the token T have a shared private key.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The ﬁrmware cannot generally be sent to the token
T
in a single transaction.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The EPC Gen2 protocol im-
plies a limitation on the length of a payload string to
255 words; this can be inadequate to encapsulate a prac-
tical CRFID ﬁrmware [12].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, we partition the
ﬁrmware input into n chunks {ﬁrmware0, ﬁrmware1,
ﬁrmware2, ..., ﬁrmwaren} and transmit sequentially in-
dexed chunks {seq0, seq1, ..., seqn} to the token T using
the BlockWrite command.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Here, seqi indicates the rela-
tive offset of ﬁrmware chunk ﬁrmwarei.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Before the ﬁrmware update is applied, the token T
must validate the authenticity of the prover P and the
integrity of the ﬁrmware.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
First, a message authentication
code s′ is computed by the prover P using a MAC function
as s′ ←MAC(ﬁrmware∥nonce, ski), with ski the recon-
structed PUF key.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text: Second, the prover sends s′ to the token.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The token computes s = MAC(firmware∥nonce, ski)
locally to compare s and s′.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
If s and s′ match, the token
T accepts and applies the ﬁrmware update.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Success of a
ﬁrmware update is signaled to the prover P by the token
backscattering an ACK.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
This process ensures:
1) The integrity of the received ﬁrmware at the token T .
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Any corruption or mutation will lead to the failure of
the integrity check on the token owing to the MAC and
subsequent discarding of the ﬁrmware.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Only the trusted prover
can obtain same secret key ski to issue a valid MAC s′.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

4
IMPLEMENTATION
In this section:
1) We generalize the SecuCode control-ﬂow on a token
T and provide an overview of the required functional
blocks.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
2) We describe the challenges in instantiating the func-
tional blocks and propose approaches to address them.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
3) We complete the end-to-end implementation based on
the instantiated functional blocks
We have selected the open-hardware and software im-
plementation of WISP5.1-LRG [14] CRFID transponder as
our token T
for a concrete implementation and experi-
ments.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
This intermittently powered CRFID transponder is
built using the ultra-low power microcontroller unit (MCU)
MSP430FR5969 from Texas Instruments.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, when
required, we provide speciﬁc implementation examples
on a CRFID transponder based on the WISP5.1-LRG and
MSP430FR5969 MCU in the discussions that follow.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Regardless of the acceptance
or rejection decision, the token exits the Firmware Update
mode by triggering a power-on-reset.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
13
If a ﬁrmware update is not required, the token
T
executes the user code,
14
if the token receives a
TagPrivilege command, indicating entry into ﬁrmware
update mode, the token restarts in ﬁrmware update mode
by setting a ﬁrmware update ﬂag—FirmwareUpdate—and
triggering a power-on-reset.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Whenever the token T
is
rebooted by a TagPrivilege command to enter the
Firmware Update mode, nonce and derived key ski is
refreshed.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The ski changes because: i) the challenge seed
is refreshed; and ii) a varying response is produced even for
the same challenge as a consequence of the naturally noisy
nature of the response bits.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A power failure such as a brownout event, as shown in
Fig.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
2, during the execution of the protocol will result in a
reset and rebooting of the token T .
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In such an event, the im-
mutable bootloader’s functionality is preserved.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore,
a prover P can attempt another secure ﬁrmware update.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In
the following sections, we describe the instantiation of each
functional block shown in Fig.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
4.2
Random Number Generator
Our implementation of the SecuCode protocol shown in
Fig.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text: 4 employs an 8-bit challenge seed and a 128-bit nonce.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
As with other low-end computing platforms, acquiring true
random numbers on a CRFID device is challenging given
the lack of resources to implement a cryptographically se-
cure random number generator (RNG).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Ideally, the RNG
should be a true random number generator (TRNG) and its
implementation should require no modiﬁcations to existing
hardware.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We evaluate and summarize the performance of
three RNGs in Table 4 in terms of random bits per request,
time overhead, power consumption and required hardware
modules in Appendix A.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We can see that the SRAM TRNG, implementation based
on the study in [20], outperforms the rest with regards to
time and energy overhead.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Most importantly, it requires
no extra hardware.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, an SRAM TRNG is chosen for
implementing the SecuCode protocol.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
4.3
Lightweight Physically Obfuscated Key Derivation
Deriving and sharing a private key between the prover
P and the token T should also be: i) lightweight; and ii)
secure.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Realizing both requirements on a resource limited
token is challenging.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Thus we: i) employ an SRAM PUF
to derive a key instead of a stored key in non-volatile
memory—prone to extraction through physical means and
requiring expensive secure NVM—with the ability to refresh
the key between protocol sessions; and ii) employ a reverse
fuzzy extractor to realize a lightweight FE.Gen on the
token to compute helper data necessary for the server to
independently reconstruct the shared key with very high
probability of success.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In particular, we propose the follow-
ing mechanisms to derive a lightweight and secure PUF key:
• Enhancing reliability of key material: Time complex-
ity of the generator function FE.Gen and security—
information leakage—is related to the amount of helper
data needed to correct noisy SRAM PUF response bits.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, we winnow SRAM PUF responses with high
bit speciﬁc reliability using response pre-selection with an
on-chip selection meta-data storage structure together with
our conditional ﬁrmware update method to signiﬁcantly
reduce the demand on helper data (see Section 4.3.1).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
• Removing information leakage through response
bias: PUF response bias, an imbalance between the
number of zeros and ones, has shown to leak additional
information [28], [29].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, to guarantee the secu-
rity bounds of the reverse fuzzy extractor, we propose
a Hamming weight based response de-biasing method
to eliminate response bias (see Section 4.3.2).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
8
4.3.1
Enhancing Reliability
We consider a syndrome based construction as in [21]
and use a BCH(n, k, t) linear block code encoder to build
FE.Gen.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The FE.Gen function is responsible for generating
the helper data h used by the prover to reconstruct the PUF
response extracted by the token using a previously enrolled
response that is securely stored at the prover.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Here, t de-
notes the number of errors a BCH(n, k, t) code is capable
of correcting, n denotes the number of bits extracted from a
PUF or the length of the response ri where the length of the
helper data is |h| = (n −k)— which also deﬁnes the well
known upper bound on information leakage.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Although we can select a BCH(n, k, t) code with ap-
propriately large parameter values to achieve the desired
attack complexity, error correcting capability to achieve an
industry standard key failure rate of less than 10−6 and
number of key bits k, the computational time complexity
of a BCH encoder, O(n2), forces the use of parallel blocks
of BCH(n, k, t) code with smaller values of n.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
For |ri|/n
parallel blocks of BCH(n, k, t) code using a syndrome con-
struction, the complexity of ﬁnding ri is 2k|ri|/n [29].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The key failure rate when employing a BCH(n, k, t)
code is expressed as:
P1 = 1 −binocdf(t, n, BER)
(1)
where binocdf is the binomial cumulative distribution
function, BER (bit error rate) is the response unreliability
expressed as [31]:
BER = 1

(2)
where m is the number of response evaluations under
a given operating corner (a combination of voltage and
temperature), r is the reference response (typically the nom-
inal operating voltage and temperature), and r′
t is the tth
regenerated response under different operating corner.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
As
we use multiple blocks, the failure rate when |ri|/n blocks
are employed is expressed as:
PFail = 1 −(1 −P1)|ri|/n
(3)
Therefore, we can see that it is imperative to reduce
BER to signiﬁcantly decrease the key failure rate PFail and
reduce the complexity of the BCH encoder required.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We
devise the following two methods to signiﬁcantly reduce
the complexity of the BCH encoder required on the resource
constrained token: i) response pre-selection together with
on-chip selection meta-data storage structure; and ii) a con-
ditional ﬁrmware update strategy.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
As shown by detailed
experimental evaluations in Section 5.1, our approaches
signiﬁcantly reduce the expected BER to be < 1%.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Pre-selection: SRAM PUF pre-selection was ﬁrst noted by
Hofer et al.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The idea is to locate SRAM cells which
tend to generate stable PUF responses.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
During the enroll-
ment phase, unstable responses are identiﬁed and discarded
for key generation [33].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We employ an approach similar to the multiple-readout
method in [33].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Given that a microcontroller’s SRAM mem-
ory is byte addressable, we employ a byte-level response
selection method illustrated in Fig.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In particular, we
ﬁrst select response bytes that are reliably reproduced un-
der repeated measurements generated under two corner
temperatures—selected as 40°C and 0°C in our implemen-
tation.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Subsequently, under nominal temperature (25°C),
the former response bytes are further subjected to multiple
readouts and majority voting (e.g., if 8 out of 10 readouts of
a bit yields logic ‘1’, then this bit is enrolled as a logic ‘1’) is
applied enrol values for the response bytes.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Conditional ﬁrmware update: It is recognized that the BER
of SRAM PUF is sensitive to temperature but insensitive
to supply voltage variations [34].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, in addition to
reliable response pre-selection, we propose performing a
conditional ﬁrmware update based on the core operating
temperature of the token.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A ﬁrmware update is executed
only when the core temperature of the chip is within a legal
temperature range; considering most practical applications,
we selected 0°C to 40°C range for SecuCode.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Without extra
hardware overhead, we take advantage of the available tem-
perature sensor within the MSP430FR5969 microcontroller
used by the CRFID transponder to sample the tempera-
ture before the PUF responses are readout.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A temperature
breaching the legal range terminates further execution and
triggers a power-on-reset.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
4.3.2
De-biasing
Most studies assume that PUF responses are uniformly dis-
tributed and hence an n-bit response has the fully entropy of
n bits.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Using a BCH(n, k, t) code, (n −k)-bit helper data h
will be publicly known.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Under the disclosure of helper data
h, there is no less than k-bit entropy remaining.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However,
as highlighted recently [28], [35], response bias incurs extra
entropy loss.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Thus, the k-bit min entropy bound guaranteed
by a BCH(n, k, t) encoder might be decreased.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
To prevent
extra entropy leakage, response de-biasing methods can
be employed [35], [36].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In general, de-biasing converts a
response rx into an unbiased enrolled response ry, where
response rx might have a bias and |rx|
≥
|ry|.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
De-
biasing needs to consider four aspects: i) de-biasing should
not deteriorate or increase response error rate; ii) efﬁciency; iii)
information leakage; and iv) reusability [28], [35]; to this end,
we propose the following Hamming weight (HW) based de-
biasing method.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
HW-based De-biasing: In our application scenario, there
are three design speciﬁc requirements: i) minimize the de-
biasing computational overhead on the token T ; ii) avoid
any additional data transmission overhead between the
prover P and the token T ; and iii) reduce additional de-
biasing information stored on the token T .
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We discuss how
we achieve the ﬁrst two goals in this section and explain
how we achieve the third goal in Section 4.3.3.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
To achieve the ﬁrst two goals, we ofﬂoad the compu-
tational burden to the prover P by performing a one-time
de-biasing during the enrollment phase.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In the Pre-selection
stage described in Section 4.3.1, stable SRAM PUF bytes are
identiﬁed.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We further winnow HW balanced bytes from
those stable bytes in our one-time de-biasing process.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In
general, we determine the address of bytes which are not
only reliable but also HW balanced; HW close to 0.5.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

This
approach leads to PUF responses—a linear combination of

text:
Remark: Our HW-based scheme does not deteriorate reli-
ability of PUF responses, eschews leakage from potential
bias and enables re-usability.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
As a trade-off, efﬁciency is
decreased as the |rx|
|ry| is low as demonstrated by our exper-
imental results in Appendix B.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, efﬁciency is not
a concern in our implementation of SecuCode as there are
always sufﬁcient SRAM responses while we only need to
use a small fraction of them.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In [35], due to the de-biasing
method—i.e.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
classic von Neumann de-biasing (CVN)—the
token T generates different de-biasing data for each re-
evaluation of the response rx.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Thus, multiple observation
of the de-biasing data given the regeneration of rx leads to
extra entropy loss.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, the key generator based on
such a de-biasing method is not reusable unless further op-
timization, e.g., pair-output VN de-biasing with erasures (ϵ-
2O-VN), is implemented to prevent extra entropy loss from
the multiple production of the de-biasing data.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In contrast,
in our HW-based de-biasing method, the de-biasing data is
generated only once during the enrollment phase, we do not
generate multiple de-biasing data and thus incurs no further
entropy leakage from the de-biasing data.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
This implies that
our HW-based de-biasing is reusable.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
4.3.3
On-chip meta-data storage structure
It is inefﬁcient to store the absolute addresses of winnowed
bytes post pre-selection and de-biasing process, described in
Figure 6, on the CRFID device and to subsequently perform
an exhaustive search to ﬁnd them on demand.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We propose
the data storage structure named CRP-block map to refer to
those reliable and HW balanced SRAM PUF responses.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The CRP-block map data structure is illustrated in Fig-
ure 6(c).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The CRP-block data structure divides the SRAM
memory into multiple blocks.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Each block has an integer
index such as Block 0, Block 1, and Block 2.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The size
of each block may vary, however, each block is designed
to contain an equal number of reliable and HW balanced
bytes required for the physically obfuscated key derivation
mechanism.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
To map a CRP-block into a physical memory
address, each block has an absolute starting address and
several offsets pointing to the winnowed bytes.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The starting
address of each block and the offsets are stored in a look up
table (LUT) in a token’s NVM indexable via block number.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
To produce a PUF key, the TRNG generates a seed challenge
that is a block number.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Consequently, a look up of a block
number will resolve the targeted block’s starting memory
address and the offsets point to the response bytes.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Hence
a random challenge ci can be used to select a CRP-block
and, subsequently, the power-up states of the bytes in the
selected CRP-block are readout and concatenated as the
response ri that is both highly reliable and unbiased.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
4.4
Message Authentication Code
SecuCode requires one cryptographic primitives: a keyed
hash function to build a message authentication code (MAC)
to realize the MAC() function.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The two dominant factors
determining their selection are:
1) The CPU clock cycles required for execution.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
1 that at a 50 cm distance,
we may not expect more than 500,000 to 600,000 clock
cycles before harvested power is exhausted.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Since available on-chip mem-
ory is shared by the RFID communication stack, sensor
data, user code, and SecuCode, the state space available
for a cipher execution is limited.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, power and memory efﬁcient primitives are
highly desirable.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The construction of a secure, computation
and power efﬁcient message authentication code MAC() on
the token is extremely challenging as the entropy compres-
sion task is resource intensive and attacks, such as birthday
attacks, demand that we use a MAC function with a large
enough output size.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Given the lack of MAC benchmark data for MSP430
microcontroller series, we selected and implemented a set
of existing secure keyed hash functions expected to yield
a computationally efﬁcient software implementation.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We
implemented and evaluated: BLAKE2s-256, BLAKE2s-128,
and HWAES-GMAC and HWAES-CMAC for comparison;
here HWAES- functions beneﬁted from the AES hardware
accelerator module on the MSP430 MCU.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The results of our
study are detailed in Appendix C.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Based on these results,


10
we selected a 128 bit MAC using HWAES-CMAC, Cipher-
based Message Authentication Code 4 built using AES since
it yields the lowest clock cycles per byte.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
4.5
Intermittent Execution Model
The nature of intermittently powered devices that rely on
harvested power is typically described by a power harvest-
ing and charging phase where energy is generally stored in
a reservoir capacitor and then released for powering compu-
tations.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We refer to this cycle as the IPC—Intermittent Power
Cycle.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A brownout event can occur when the available
energy in an IPC subceeds the energy needs of the computa-
tions, and the power harvester is unable to replenish energy
as rapidly as it is consumed.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
A brownout results in state
loss and termination of the execution thread as highlighted
in Fig 2.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
4.5, we cannot always
expect to continue a computation task to completion.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Studies such as Alpaca [37], Mementos [38], CCCP [39]
and Clank [40] consider the problem of continuing the
thread of execution over periods of power loss.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In general,
these studies employ checkpoint based methods with vari-
ous degrees of programmer support.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The basic concept is to
save state—checkpoint—and to restore state to a previously
valid checkpoint to allow the resumption from a previous
state of execution after a power loss event.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
With the ex-
ception of CCCP, state is saved in a device’s non-volatile
memory; CCCP proposes the saving of state in an untrusted
server.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, in SecuCode, process state such as the PUF
key is intentionally volatile to eliminate the need to protect
key storage.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
If power-loss or brownout does occur, all un-
ﬁnished process state based on old key material should be
discarded.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, approaches to save and restore state
from non-volatile sources are not desirable.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Further, writing
to NVM is energy intensive and we would like to avoid
the additional overhead of checkpointing.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In contrast, Dew-
drop [41] considers execution under frequent power loss by
attempting to prevent a brownout event by solving a task
scheduling problem; execute tasks only when they are likely
to succeed by monitoring the available harvested power.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Dewdrop provides an elegant dynamic scheduling method,
however, requires the overhead of sampling the harvester
voltage within the application code and task scheduling.

text:
In order to deal to with frequent intermittent power

on the basic concept of a task in Alpaca [37]—a code block
proportioned to execute to completion under a minimum
number of available clock cycles or energy— and the con-

title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:

in the ﬁrmware, and construct an execution plan based
on factoring the function to subtasks.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
These subtasks are
then interleaved with low power sleep states in the code.

sleep state from the target microcontroller such that the
memory state is maintained during sleep.

This is because the CRFID device has no supervi-
sory control of an operating system and is designed in the
manner of a low-end and low-cost device.

text:
Our bootloader is based on TI’s bootloader framework,
MSPBoot [17].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The Comm interface is designed to operate on
trusted data and therefore should not directly communicate
with the RFID Media Access Control layer.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Instead, the re-
ceived ﬁrmware is buffered in a Download Area in memory.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
After the SecuCode protocol veriﬁes the authenticity and the
integrity of the ﬁrmware, it is passed to the MSPBoot via
the Comm interface.

text:
In our implementation, we adopted the
WISP5 ﬁrmware5 for the RFID Media Access Control layer.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In order to realize an immutable bootloader, we consid-
ered the full memory protect mode (FMPM) and partial
memory protect mode (PMPM) offered by the microcon-
troller together with setting an e-Fuse [43] to disable the
potential for wired re-programming using the on-chip JTAG
interface after deployment in the ﬁeld.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In FMPM, the MPU
(memory protection unit) is conﬁgured to prevent writing
to the bootloader.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Most importantly, the MPU is locked
from being accessed.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
These actions are performed during
the initialization process, before execution of user code, and
therefore it is infeasible for the bootloader to be modiﬁed
in FMPM mode.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In PMPM, writing to the bootloader is still
prevented, however, the MPU is not locked.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Such an MPU
conﬁguration provides basic protection for the bootloader
against programming errors, while still allowing the boot-
loader to be remotely updated.

a cold start-up initialization process and potentially lead to
unsuccessful device start-ups at the initiation of a ﬁrmware
update.

overhead of a key derivation operation.

and MAC functions under wireless powering conditions—
different distances from a wireless powering source, i.e.

RFID reader antenna—and intermittent operating settings

MAC Computation
We deﬁne MAC function latency as the time interval between
calling a MAC function to perform a calculation over a
block of pre-loaded data on the CRFID transponder and
the generation of a valid result.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

Following the deﬁnition in [45], the data size is

text:
In this experiment, a random
string of 1,280 bytes is used.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

the size of the largest ﬁrmware update used in our experi-
ments.

text:
Since the hardware AES accelerator is very efﬁcient
in terms of clock cycles, instead of considering each AES
compression round as a subtask, we employ 32 rounds of
AES computations as a subtask in our IEM implementation.

5.4
Summary
Our results demonstrate: i) the practicability and robustness
of the developed SecuCode protocol; ii) the relationship be-
tween operating conditions, intermittent operation settings
and protocol performances; and iii) the effectiveness of the
proposed IEM on realizing successful secure ﬁrmware up-
dates under intermittent powering from harvested energy.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
5.5
Security Analysis
We analyze the security of SecuCode under the adversary
model detailed in Section 3.2 in the following.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Man-in-the-middle attack: Here, security is related to the
complexity of the adversary A fooling the token T in order
to inject malicious code.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Such an adversary is faced with
the task of determining the secret key ski and therefore, we
evaluate the security of the reverse fuzzy extractor which
leaks helper data during a ﬁrmware update session.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We employ a reverse fuzzy extractor where the helper
data computation is placed on the resource-constrained
token T .
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In this context, different helper data corresponding
to the same response ri will be generated during different
ﬁrmware update sessions; thus, multiple helper data are
exposed.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
It has been proved that the entropy leakage from
the helper data is independent of the number of enrollments
for SRAM PUF [46].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In other words, one can evaluate the
entropy leakage from the helper data of the reverse fuzzy
extractor for a single helper data generation case; or the
entropy leakage from multiple helper data observations is
same as the entropy leakage from a single helper data
observation, as with a traditional fuzzy extractor.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Further,
we assume that the debiasing mask does not leak infor-
mation.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
This is a reasonable assumption as the mask is
limited to indicating the reliable CRP-blocks only and not
the response itself.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In addition, it has been demonstrated
through extensive experiments that modern SRAM PUFs
possess good uniqueness properties [47].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In other words,
the highly reliable bits are not correlated across different
instances of SRAM PUFs.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, knowledge of an SRAM
PUF instance’s mask can safely be assumed to not leak
responses information of other SRAM PUFs.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Then, given the BCH(n,k,t) code used to implement the
reverse fuzzy extractor helper data computation, no more
than (n−k)-bit entropy is leaked.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
To be precise, the residual
min entropy [28] of the n-bit response is given by Hmin =
−n·log2(max(b, 1−b))−(n−k) when the helper data
is public, where the PUF response bias—the probability of
a single PUF response being ‘0’— is b.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, as we have seen, PUF responses can display
a slight bias.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore to guarantee the (n −k)-bit entropy


15
leakage we employed the de-biasing method proposed in
Section.4.3.2.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
As we use 8 blocks of BCH(31,16,3) code, we achieve
a key ski with 128-bit entropy—strictly, 127.6 bits entropy
considering the experimentally evaluated bias of 0.4990 post
our de-biasing method.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, without knowledge of
ski, the probability of fooling the token T
to update a
malicious ﬁrmware by A is no more than the brute-force
attack probability of 2−127.6.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We are aware of helper
data manipulation attacks based on exposed helper data
reported in [29], [48].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, both works acknowledge
that such an attack is error correction code dependent and
cannot be mounted on a linear code such as BCH employed
in SecuCode [29], [48].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Further, mounting such an attack on
SecuCode is difﬁcult; in the ﬁrst place, we notice that such a
helper data manipulation attack is very easy to be detected
by the prover P.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The reasons are as follows:
1) The frequency of normal ﬁrmware updates is very
low in comparison with other services that are built
with reverse fuzzy extractors, such as authentication or
attestation services.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, helper data manipulation
attacks require a large number of queries.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Recall, that
helper data is generated by the token T
and then
sent to the prover P and the ﬁrmware update pro-
cess is initiated by the prover.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Hence the opportunity
to mount a helper data attack is limited to the few
occasions during which a ﬁrmware update is required
by the prover.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In a reverse fuzzy extractor attack, the
adversary is forced to perform a trial-and-error measure
by continually sending malicious helper data to the
resource-rich prover P.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The prover can perceive such
malicious behavior and stop responding to a ﬁrmware
update session that is hijacked by an adversary.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
2) There exists a built-in throttling and obfuscation mech-
anism that prevents rapid helper data submissions
needed for such an attack.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Recall that in a man-in-the-
middle attack where the adversary is able to submit ma-
nipulated helper data, the success or failure is masked
by failure from external factors such as powering and
the determination of success or failure is only evident
at the near conclusion of the update session—this can
be 2-4 seconds.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
3) Under tampered helper data queries, the failure rate
of reconstructing the key sk will signiﬁcantly increase.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Thus, the prover P can detect such an abnormal failure
rate as a potential attack [49].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
This can deem the target
CRFID as being compromised.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Alternatively, detection
can also be achieved by extending the protocol to allow
a request to the token T to send back MAC(nonce∥hi,
ski) that the prover P can subsequently compare using
its computed ski from the securely stored response r′
and the provided helper data hi.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We are also aware that modeling at-
tacks on the reverse fuzzy extractors have been shown
in [50], [51].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
These attacks are applicable to arbiter PUFs
(APUFs) [19], mainly due to the fact that the responses from
APUFs are correlated.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, modeling attacks cannot
be mounted on SRAM PUFs [20] because PUF responses are
information-theoretically independent since each response
is derived from a spatially separate SRAM cell.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
6
RELATED WORK AND DISCUSSION
For emerging battery-free computing devices such as CR-
FID platforms including WISP [9], MOO [10] and Farsens
Pyros [11], ﬁrmware updates are usually done with a wired
programming interface; for example by way of a JTAG [10]
interface or a Serial interface [55].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The main difﬁculties
that hinder CRFID platform to be reprogrammed using
a wireless method are: i) the transiently powered nature
where encountering power failures are highly likely [12]; ii)
reprogramming code memory such as FLASH that require
the device attaining an adequate voltage level from har-
vested power [15]; and ii) the lack of supervisory control of
an operating system for managing a devices’ tasks [52].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We
have seen recent efforts to bring wireless reprogramming
to CRFID transponders [12], [15], [52], [53], however, to
the best of our knowledge, SecuCode is the ﬁrst work
to resolve the requirement for security for wireless code
dissemination for intermittently powered passive CRFID
devices.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, in the following we review studies to: i)
develop a bootloader and modify application behavior; and
ii) progress towards developing on-the ﬂy wireless ﬁrmware
update methods.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We summarize the key characteristics of
these studies in Table 6 and provide benchmark results
for SecuCode with the non-secure wireless update method,
Wisent [12], in Appendix F.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
6.1
In-application behavior modiﬁcation
An early version of a bootloader for a CRFID platform,
Bootie was proposed by Ransford in [52].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Bootie was de-
signed to accept two (or more) ﬁrmware and cross-compile
them into one executable to be preloaded onto a CRFID
transponder.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The compiled ﬁrmware was then downloaded
and tested on Olimex MSP430-H2131 minimum system
board.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The author showed that Bootie could be used as a
basis for wireless ﬁrmware updates.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, as a proof-
of-concept, Bootie only enables the platform to execute pre-
loaded ﬁrmwares one-by-one and did not allow responding
to user demands nor operating conditions to determine the
switching between ﬁrmware.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The FirmSwitch scheme was later demonstrated in [53] to
offer ﬁrmware ﬂexibility for CRFID transponders.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
This ap-
proach allowed a user to switch between pre-loaded ﬁrmware
instances on a CRFID platform using downstream com-
mands to the CRFID transponder.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, FirmSwitch
was not developed to support wireless ﬁrmware updates.

6.2
Wireless code dissemination
More recently, the Wisent method by Tan et al.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
[13], [15] demonstrated a robust
wireless ﬁrmware update method for CRFID transponders
using WISP platforms.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In particular, R3 was implemented
on three different types of CRFID transponders.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
[54] proposed a fast Multi-
CRFID wireless ﬁrmware transfer protocol that involves
ignoring the RN16 handle sent from an RFID transponder
(i.e.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
the tags still save the downstream data even if their
handle does not match the one speciﬁed by the reader).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Stork enables an RFID Reader to simultaneously program
multiple CRFID devices in the ﬁeld to reduce the time to
update multiple devices.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Although these works achieved on
the ﬂy wireless update of ﬁrmware along with a bootloader
design, none of wireless ﬁrmware update approaches ad-
dress the issue of security and the trustworthiness of the
prover, therefore, malicious ﬁrmware injection remains an
open issue.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In late 2016, Brown and Pier from Texas Instrument (TI)
presented an application port [17] extending TI’s previous
work, MSPBoot [56].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
In this work, wireless updating was
demonstrated in two examples; using UART or SPI bus to
interconnect an MSP430 16-bit RISC microcontroller and a
CC1101 sub-1GHz RF transceiver.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The enhanced bootloader
design supported: i) application validation; ii) redirecting
interrupt vectors; and iii) code sharing via preconﬁgured
callbacks.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Additionally, a dual image failsafe mechanism is
introduced; here, before the application in executable area is
overwritten, the new image would be veriﬁed in a down-
load area.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore any interruption in communication
would not affect the function of the device.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
However, like
other bootloaders and wireless ﬁrmware update methods,
security is not considered.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
7
CONCLUSION
We have presented the ﬁrst secure wireless ﬁrmware update
scheme, SecuCode, for resource-constrained and intermit-
tently powered CRFID devices.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
We derived a volatile secret
key on demand and discard it after usage to remove the
difﬁculty of permanent secure key storage in NVM.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Our Se-
cuCode protocol only allows an authorized party to perform
a wireless ﬁrmware update and does not require any hard-
ware modiﬁcations whilst being standards compliant.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
As
noted in [20], cryptographic engineering of a protocol must
consider the complex environment for physical devices,
such as noise and energy constraints, performance and cost
of protocol instantiations.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
To this end, we have successfully
addressed security and implementation challenges, realized
an end-to-end SecuCode implementation on the popular
CRFID transponder and extensively evaluated the cost and
performance of our realization, including an application
case study along with a complete public release of code and
experimental data.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text: Limitations: Our study is not without limitations.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Since our
main focus is to develop a secure end-to-end solution for
wireless updates, we have only investigated an intermittent
execution model based on preventing power loss where we
used ﬁxed intermittent operating settings (low power deep
sleep duration) for the FE.Gen and MAC functions.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
These
settings are determined when the bootloader is provisioned
and can, unnecessarily, slow down ﬁrmware updates at
short operating distances.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
While we have addressed the problem of malicious
code injection attacks, the ﬁrmware is sent as plaintext and
privacy or intellectual property protection goals are not
addressed by SecuCode.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Although Stork [14] provides a
method for simultaneous non-secure dissemination of code
to multiple CRIFD devices, as a ﬁrst method, our approach
to securely update a large number of CRFID devices re-
quires the dissemination of code to each single device at
a time.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Future Work: Since our main focus in this paper is security,
we opted for an intentionally simple IEM approach where
we use a ﬁxed intermittent operating setting for the two
security building blocks.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Future work will investigate dy-
namic task scheduling where the intermittent operating set-
ting can be set optimally as in Dewdrop [41] to provide per-
formance improvements such as increasing the operational
range and the rate at which ﬁrmware can be transferred to
a CRFID device.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Such a dynamic task scheduling approach
can investigate exploiting the decay of SRAM [57] to gather
time intervals between power loss events to determine
optimal task schedules.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
This could potentially provide an
attractive solution where SRAM intrinsic to the MCU is used
to determine task schedules.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Additionally, in future work, we will consider the prob-
lem of secure and simultaneous code dissemination to mul-
tiple RFID devices.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
While an approach that excludes the
requirement for key protection may provide a simpler code
dissemination problem, the use of a PUF in such a context
to beneﬁt from the inherent key protection, is a challenging
problem.

APPENDIX A
RANDOM NUMBER GENERATOR COMPARISON
We provide a summary of the random number generator
methods we have evaluated.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
CTR-DRBG: Texas Instrument has demonstrated a Counter
Mode Deterministic Random Byte Generator (CTR-DRBG)
in [58] to meet the needs of security mechanisms on MSP430
MCUs.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The CTR-DRBG is developed by National Institute
of Standard and Technology (NIST) in NIST SP 800-90A [59]
and is built upon a block cipher algorithm (e.g., AES256).
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022
arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Thermal noise: Thermal noise (Johnson–Nyquist noise) has
been exploited [60] [61] [62] as an entropy source for a
TRNG.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Thermal noise results in unpredictable small voltage
ﬂuctuations in resistive components at any temperature
above 0°K.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
The least signiﬁcant bit (LSB) of sampled data
is signiﬁcantly affected by thermal noise over other bits [63]
[64].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Therefore, random bits can be extracted by sampling
the LSB from a noisy sensor.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Random number genera-
tors from this method has passed the NIST randomness
tests [65].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Noisy SRAM responses: The noisy SRAM PUF responses
can be used to generate true random numbers; this method
has been extensively studied, for example in [20], [66].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Sufﬁcient entropy can be extracted through, e.g., XOR and
bit shift operations [20], [66] over a number of SRAM PUF
responses.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
Random bit streams from this method has passed
the NIST random number generator test suite [66].
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

text:
APPENDIX B
SRAM PUF PRE-SELECTION EFFICIENCY
Efﬁciency evaluates the ratio of number of the selected

We devised a simple method to evaluate the success rate.

We
used the ratio of the number of occurrences of backscatter
events immediately after a cold start for a ﬁxed number of
cold-start attempts as the success rate.

was realized with an RFID reader interrogation signal; i.e.
title: arXiv:1807.10463v4  [cs.CR]  21 Sep 2022

order to mitigate the possible network delays in using
a networked RFID reader connected to host machine to
determine the delays, we employed two oscilloscope probes
directly connected to the CRFID device to measure reservoir
capacitor voltage and backscatter events to determine the
time at which the backscatter event is initiated as well as to
determine if the backscatter event immediately followed a

text:
On the Effect of Task-to-Worker Assignment in Distributed Computing
Systems with Stragglers
Amir Behrouzi-Far1 and Emina Soljanin2
Abstract— We study the expected completion time of some
recently proposed algorithms for distributed computing which
redundantly assign computing tasks to multiple machines in
order to tolerate a certain number of machine failures.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
We
analytically show that not only the amount of redundancy but
also the task-to-machine assignments affect the latency in a
distributed system.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
We study systems with a ﬁxed number
of computing tasks that are split in possibly overlapping
batches, and independent exponentially distributed machine
service times.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
We show that, for such systems, the uniform
replication of non-overlapping (disjoint) batches of computing
tasks achieves the minimum expected computing time.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
INTRODUCTION
Distributed computing has gained great attention in the
time of big data [1].
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
By enabling parallel task execution,
distributed computing systems can bring considerable speed
ups to e.g.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
matrix multiplication [2], model training in
machine learning [3] and convex optimization [4].
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
However,
implementing computing algorithms in a distributed system
introduces new challenges that have to be addressed in
order to beneﬁt from paralleziation.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
In particular, since the
failure rate and/or slow down of the system increase with
the number of computing nodes, robustness is an essential
part of any reliable distributed computing/storage algorithm
[5].
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
For achieving robustness, redundant computing/storage
is introduced in the literature [5], [6].
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Redundancy in a
distributed computing system enables the system to generate
the overall result form the computations of a subset of all
computing nodes, which provides robustness to failed and/or
slow nodes, known as stragglers.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
A number of algorithms for distributed computing which
tolerate the failure of some computing nodes have recently
appeared in the literature.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
For example, in [7] used error
correcting codes and, for distributed gradient descent, authors
established lower bound on the degree of redundancy for
tolerating a speciﬁc number of node failures, and intro-
duced some data-to-node assignment methods that achieve
the lower bound.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
In [8], Reed-Solomon codes are studied
for distributed gradient descent, and the code construction,
decoding algorithm and an asymptotic bound on the compu-
tation time are provided.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
In [9], a random data assignment
to computing nodes is proposed, and claimed to outperform
the deterministic method in [7] in terms of average per-
iteration computing time.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Fault-tolerant distributed matrix

amir.behrouzifar@rutgers.edu

title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
In this line of work,
authors focus on failure tolerance capability of their proposed
algorithms without considering the resulting computing time.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
The effect of the replicated redundancy on the distributed
computing latency was studied in [11], where it is shown that
delayed replication of the straggling tasks could reduce both
cost and latency in the system.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Moreover, authors in [12]
analyzed the latency of the system with coded redundancy,
where instead of simple replication of the straggling tasks a
coded combination of them would be introduced.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
The anal-
ysis of the same work shows that, coded redundancy could
achieve the same latency with less cost of the computing.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
In
[13] authors show that relaunching straggling tasks could
signiﬁcantly reduce the cost and latency in a distributed
computing system.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
In these works, the delay of computing is
considered without looking into the effect of task assignment
in the timing performance.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
In this paper, we study the computing time of the failure-
tolerant distributed computing algorithms.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
We speciﬁcally
focus on the algorithms proposed by [7] and [9], which
used error correcting codes and random task assignment
respectively, and show that how the task assignment could
improve the expected computing time of the same methods.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
We consider a distributed computing system consisting of
multiple worker nodes, which perform a speciﬁc computation
over a sebset of a possibly huge data set, and a master
node, which collects the local computations from worker
nodes and generates the overall result.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
The original data
set is (redundantly) distributed among worker nodes and
the subset of data at each worker is called a data batch.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Through analysis, we show that, with a ﬁxed number of
computing tasks and exponentially distributed service time of
worker nodes, the lower bound of the expected computing
time among different data distribution policies is achieved
by the balanced assignment of non-overlapping batches.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
We
also derived this lower bound and veriﬁed it by simulations.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text: The organization of this paper is as follows.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
In section
II, we introduce the model for system architecture, comput-
ing task, data distribution and service time of the worker
nodes.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
The data distribution policies, non-overlapping and
overlapping batches, are described in section III.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
In section
IV we provide analysis of the computing time for each
data distribution policies.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
The numerical results and the
concluding remarks are provided in section V and section
VI, respectively.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018


II.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Distributed Computing Architecture
We study the system given in Fig.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
1, which will be referred
to as System 1 in the rest of the paper.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
The system consists of
a data set with S data blocks, a batching unit which partitions
the data blocks into B batches, a batch assignment unit
which allocates data batches among N worker nodes, each
performing a speciﬁc computing task on its data batch, and a
master node which collects local (coded) computations from
worker nodes and computes the overall result accordingly.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
For a given data set, a ﬁxed number of identical worker nodes
and a master node, the average computing time of the system
depends on how the data is distributed among workers, what
the service time model of the worker nodes is, and how each
worker codes its computations before sending it to the master
node.

In this work, we consider data-intensive jobs that could
be divided into smaller tasks to be executed in parallel.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Each task is assigned to a worker node which performs
computations over a subset of the entire data and sends its
local result to the master node.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

After receiving the local
results from a large enough number of workers, the master
node generates the overall result.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
This is a well applicable
and widely used model for different algorithms, e.g.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
matrix
multiplication [2] and gradient based optimizers [4], [7].

text:
Data Distribution
To ensure reliable computations, each block of the data
set is stored redundantly among workers.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
The redundant
distribution of data among the worker nodes is abstracted
into a two-stage process.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
In the ﬁrst stage, the data set is
stored in equal-sized batches and in the second stage batches
get assigned to the workers.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Note that, the batches could be
non-overlapping, when the data set is simply chopped into
smaller parts, or they could overlap, if each data block is
available in more than one batch.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Nevertheless, the batch
sizes will be the same in both cases.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Therefore, there would
be more batches if they overlap.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Assuming the batch size is
S/B, where B divides S, the number of batches is an integer
in the range of [B, N].
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Service Time Model
We deﬁne Ti,j as the time that worker j takes to perform
computing over data batch i and communicate the result to
the master node.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
We assume that Ti,j are all independent and
exponentially, identically distributed:
Ti,j ∼exp(λ),
(2)
where λ is the service rate of the worker nodes and is
identical for all of the workers.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
DATA DISTRIBUTION
The data distribution policies could be categorized as: 1)
non-overlapping batches, or 2) overlapping batches.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
We will
discuss each policy in detail in the following.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Non-overlapping Batches
Under this batching policy, the data set of S blocks is split
into B equal-size batches, giving batch size S/B.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
When B <
N, batches can be assigned redundantly to the N worker
nodes, in order to enable failure and/or straggler tolerance in
the system.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Since the intersection of the batches are empty,
the data at each worker either completely overlap or do not
overlap at all with the data at any other worker.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Therefore, for
acquiring the computations over a speciﬁc batch, the master
node should receive the local results from at least one of the
workers hosting that batch.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
The random batch assignment in which each worker draws
a batch, uniformly at random, with replacement from the pool


of batches was studied in [9], and can be naturally modeled
as the Coupon Collection (CC) problem.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
It was shown in [9]
that the random assignment reduces the computation time
per iteration compared to deterministic assignment in [7].
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
We
will show in the following section that the imbalance data
distribution among workers, which results from the random
assignment, adversely affects the computation time.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
On the
other hand, since some of the batches will be drawn only
once, there will be no failure tolerance for a worker if its
data is not replicated at any other worker.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Furthermore, by
random assignment, there is always a non-zero probability
that some batches not get selected, leading to an inaccurate
computation result.
title: arXiv:1808.02838v1  [cs.DC]  8 Aug 2018

text:
Let n be the number of workers for covering all the
batches in random assignment policy.
