text:
Accelerator Virtualization in Fog Computing:
Moving From the Cloud to the Edge
Blesson Varghese∗1, Carlos Rea˜no1, and Federico Silla2
1School of Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science, Queen’s University Belfast, UK
2Department of Computer Engineering, Universitat Politecnica de Valencia, Spain
Hardware accelerators are available on the Cloud for enhanced analytics.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Next generation
Clouds aim to bring enhanced analytics using accelerators closer to user devices at the edge
of the network for improving Quality-of-Service by minimizing end-to-end latencies and
response times.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The collective computing model that utilizes resources at the Cloud-Edge
continuum in a multi-tier hierarchy comprising the Cloud, the Edge and user devices is
referred to as Fog computing.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This article identiﬁes challenges and opportunities in making
accelerators accessible at the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
A holistic view of the Fog architecture is key to pursuing
meaningful research in this area.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Introduction
The Internet paved the way for providing computing
as a utility service to customers.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Customers pay for
Cloud-based services ranging from infrastructure to
software services.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Infrastructure services are oﬀered
via Virtual Machines (VMs), a virtualization tech-
nology that makes remote servers accessible to users.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Software services make speciﬁc applications, such as
Augmented Reality (AR) available to users.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Many services beneﬁt from the use of accelerators,
such as Graphics Processing Units (GPUs), which are
specialized processors that reduce execution times of
workloads on the Cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
GPUs oﬀer signiﬁcant com-
puting power for a relatively small power per FLOP
(Floating-Point Operation) ratio.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Computational resources oﬀered by traditional
Clouds are hosted in centralized facilities, referred
to as data centers.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
At present, traﬃc in the form
of images, videos and text generated by user devices
is usually transmitted to the Cloud for processing.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
For example, consider an AR use-case for cognitive
wearable assistance in which a smart glass worn by a
person provides instructions for navigating.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Since the
environment rapidly changes there is always a steady
stream of images that needs to be processed in the
Cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This will simply not be sustainable in the
future.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
It is anticipated that tens of billions of user de-
vices, such as smartphones, tablets, appliances
and wearables will be connected to the Inter-
net in the next decade and consequently tril-
lions of gigabytes of data will be generated [1].
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
It would be practically impossible to transmit
the traﬃc generated by all devices to the net-
work core for processing.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Using the Cloud for the AR use-case will not meet
real-time requirements due to latencies for rapidly re-
sponding to the change in environment as captured
by the smart glass.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
For achieving latencies below 1
millisecond, and given the speed of light, servers must
be located within 93 miles from every device in the
best case.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Therefore, a fundamentally new design of
the Cloud is required.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Redesigning
data
centers
is
a
central
chal-
lenge in achieving sustainability for next generation
∗Corresponding Author; Email: b.varghese@qub.ac.uk; Web: http://www.blessonv.com
1
arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018


Figure 1: A multi-tiered Fog computing model using accelerators.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The user device layer at the bottom,
the Edge layer comprising nodes and micro-cloud in the middle, and the Cloud layer at the top.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The Edge
nodes host weak accelerators, which may be located along with routers or wireless access points.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Edge
micro-clouds that provide support for larger accelerators may be hosted on base stations or facilities of or-
ganizations.Support for accelerator virtualization is highlighted for the Edge node hosting ‘Accelerator 4’;
the Edge node can access the physical accelerator hosted on it as well as make use of a single or multiple
instances of the virtual accelerator.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Remote virtual accelerators located on the micro-cloud or the Cloud can
also be used.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
One strategy is to decentralize resources,
so that computing can be made available at the edge
of the network, which is closer to users than a dis-
tant data center.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Data generated by user devices can
be processed at the Edge on existing nodes, such as
routers, switches or wireless access points by adding
low power and low cost computing capabilities on
them or by using a small dedicated cluster of compute
nodes in the form of micro-clouds.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Processing user
requests at the Edge will reduce end-to-end latency,
reduce traﬃc beyond the ﬁrst hop of the network and
improve overall Quality-of-Service (QoS) [3].
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Instead
of using the Cloud for the AR use-case Edge resources
can be used to reduce latencies and minimize traf-
ﬁc towards the Cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Furthermore, an Edge-based
approach will pave the way for a more sustainable
Internet.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Utilizing compute resources at the Cloud to Edge
continuum in a multi-tiered hierarchy comprising the
Cloud, the Edge and user devices is referred to as Fog
computing [4].
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The objective of Fog computing is not
to replace the Cloud, but rather to make resources,
including accelerators, available closer to user devices
for enhanced analytics.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Figure 1 illustrates a Fog
computing model using accelerators.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The bottom layer comprises user de-
vices.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The hierarchical Edge layer comprises Edge
nodes that host accelerators, which are weak both in
2


terms of power and computational capabilities, and
micro-clouds that may host relatively larger acceler-
ators.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The top most layer is the Cloud, which has
virtually unlimited powerful resources, but may be
more distant from the user.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Edge nodes are designed to be power eﬃcient since
they have a limited power budget.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Hence, the accel-
erators on Edge nodes may be small and weak.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
To
use accelerators on an Edge node eﬃciently, multiple
virtual instances of the accelerator on the Edge node
(similar to multiple VMs of the same processor) may
be used to share the accelerator among multiple ap-
plications.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
We refer to the technology that facilitates
the use of multiple virtual instances of the accelerator
on a node as ‘accelerator virtualization’.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Since there may be relatively fewer power restric-
tions on micro-clouds, they can host larger accelera-
tors.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Given the resource limitations on an Edge node,
the accelerator virtualization technology can enrich
computational capabilities available on an Edge node
by providing access to accelerators located in a micro-
cloud or even in the Cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
These accelerators are
remotely located and we therefore refer to this as ‘re-
mote accelerator virtualization’ [5].
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
When the remote accelerator virtualization
technique is leveraged, the CPU and acceler-
ator components of the same application may
be executed on diﬀerent nodes.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
For instance,
an application running on an Edge node may
use powerful accelerators located in the micro-
cloud or even in the Cloud instead of using
weaker accelerators on the Edge node.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Both
accelerator and remote accelerator virtualiza-
tion optimize the use of accelerators in a typ-
ical resource-scarce and resource-constrained
environment, such as the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Current Fog research usually focuses on generic
processors and does not extend the use of accelera-
tors to the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The OpenFog reference architec-
ture notes the beneﬁt of accelerators for the Edge,
but there is limited discussion on how accelerators
can be made accessible on the Edge [6].
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The focus
of this article is to consider the research challenges
and opportunities in making accelerators accessible
at the Edge via virtualization for quickly processing
user requests.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Challenges
The main challenge in making accelerators accessible
on the Edge is to holistically view the Fog system.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Current research has developed independent subsys-
tems within the Fog that are not interoperable and
cannot be easily connected together.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
In the context
of accelerators for the Edge and their use via virtu-
alization, we anticipate that six challenges presented
in this section will need to be addressed.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Figure 2
highlights the challenges and how they map on to
the opportunities that are considered in this article.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The ﬁrst three challenges are generic and inﬂuence
the remaining three challenges.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Challenge 1 - Embracing Accelerators in Edge
Stacks
Typically, the CPU is the primary consideration in
the development of technology stacks.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Support for
accelerators in the stack is bolted on as an after
thought, often resulting in a less adaptable core tech-
nology.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The design of an end-to-end technology stack
from the Cloud down to the Edge is ﬂawed by the
same approach.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Therefore, the design approach needs
to be changed by taking accelerators into account as
primary processors or co-processors in the computing
stack.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
One potential avenue to explore in Edge stack de-
sign would be the inclusion of a decision layer and a
scheduling layer at the bottom of the stack.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The deci-
sion layer, operating at a macro-level, would be used
to identify whether the service using an accelerator is
available on a given Edge node.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The scheduling layer,
operating at a micro-level, would decide whether the
accelerator could actually be made available for an in-
coming request based on system properties, such as
resource availability.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
These layers should be designed
considering the requirements of the broader Fog ar-
chitecture in order to implement optimal decision-
making algorithms at the decision and scheduling lay-
ers.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Challenge 2 - Lack of Real Test-beds
Research on Edge environments is rapidly evolving,
but real practical physical test-beds are not yet avail-
able.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
We note that current research is fragmented in
3


Figure 2: Challenges and the opportunities in making accelerators accessible in Fog computing.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Firstly, middleware and hard-
ware solutions for potential Edge nodes are available,
but end-to-end solutions are sparse at best.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Nonethe-
less as a starting point, technologies such as Open-
Stack Edge [7], OpenStack++ [8] and AWS Snow-
ball [9] that support the use of the Edge are a start-
ing point.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
These tools can be used to provide in-
sight on the behaviour of workloads in the Fog archi-
tecture.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Secondly, simulation frameworks available
for Edge environments are recycled in that they were
once employed to study the Cloud and are now ex-
tended for the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Given that there are no practical
test-beds yet, the simulation models cannot be vali-
dated.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Thirdly, experimental evaluation presented in
the literature usually employs bespoke and private
test-beds that are crafted for speciﬁc applications.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
While this provides insight into how an application
may perform, it is not fully representative of Edge
infrastructure that is envisioned to be publicly acces-
sible in the future.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Consequently, it is diﬃcult to understand from a
research perspective the scale of applications or the
resources really available in the Edge ecosystem al-
though the business case for Fog computing is com-
pelling and already well articulated.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This translates
into a lack of knowledge about the behaviour (com-
munication between diﬀerent levels at the Edge, be-
tween the Edge and the Cloud, and between the Edge
and the users as well as computation that occurs
at each layer) of real workloads.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This obviously af-
fects how a real application can be distributed across
the Edge and the Cloud accelerators for maximizing
computing performance but at the same time reduc-
ing the overall end-to-end energy consumed.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Under-
standing these trade-oﬀs will remain a challenge until
end-to-end experimental test-beds can be publicly ac-
cessed.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Challenge 3 - Vendor Neutral Multi-tenant
Systems
Ideal service oriented systems, including Edge-based
systems, are multi-tenant; that is, they host diﬀerent
services and serve multiple users.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Conceptually, in
the context of making accelerators accessible, virtual-
ization at the Edge is a way to achieve multi-tenancy.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
4


However, this is a multi-faceted challenge: Firstly,
there are no generic solutions to share accelerators,
for example GPUs, among multiple users or applica-
tions.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Current solutions available in the market are
targeted for vendor speciﬁc GPUs.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Vendor neutrality
is a goal that remains to be achieved for GPU virtu-
alization solutions and is essential for multi-tenancy
on the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Vendor neutrality may be achieved via
API forwarding, which is a technique used to provide
wrappers for functions which make use of the accel-
erator.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
These wrappers forward all function calls to
the appropriate GPU.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
However, API forwarding raises a second chal-
lenge in that additional middleware is required on the
Edge nodes.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Because Edge nodes are likely to host
small and low power accelerators, the more powerful
accelerators will instead need to be located on micro-
clouds.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Although API forwarding would be necessary
to reap the beneﬁts of remote GPUs, the communi-
cation overheads would need to be minimized.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Ad-
ditionally, developing the technology for virtualizing
small GPUs without signiﬁcant resource footprint re-
mains an open challenge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Challenge 4 - Scheduling Applications in the
Face of Heterogeneity
Edge environments are anticipated to be heteroge-
neous in at least two ways.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Firstly, the Edge may
comprise nodes ranging from resource constrained in-
dividual nodes to small clusters, such as micro-clouds.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Secondly, multiple CPU and accelerator architectures
may be used at the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This however raises an
important question - ’how can applications be dis-
tributed and scheduled by taking heterogeneity into
account?’.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This is challenging because there are mul-
tiple diﬀerent combinations of layers and nodes in an
Edge environment that could potentially be used by
a scheduler to distribute an application.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Scheduling
becomes complex because weak and powerful acceler-
ators co-exist at the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
In addition, the network
conditions and the state of resources (who resides on
the resources and for how long) will need to be mon-
itored without consuming large amounts of resources
at the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
API forwarding is one solution that will facilitate
scheduling of accelerators.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This is because the mid-
dleware can intercept all accelerator function calls
made by an application and forward them to a suit-
able remote accelerator.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Given that the middleware
will be aware of the resource requirements, a moni-
toring entity that aggregates the requirements from
all applications at geographically nearby Edge nodes
may be used to create a more global view of the
requirements and resources available.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
A scheduling
plan could then be generated that would reduce re-
sponse times and guarantee Quality-of-Service (QoS),
so if an accelerator that hosts a distributed applica-
tion cannot satisfy the QoS requirements, then the
component of the application that is to be hosted on
an accelerator may be migrated to a diﬀerent accel-
erator.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
However, monitoring resources and migrating
applications for scheduling applications are both open
challenges.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Challenge 5 - Taming Accelerator Virtualiza-
tion Overheads
Virtualization inevitably introduces communication
overheads, and due to the use of additional mid-
dleware, the same is true for accelerator virtualiza-
tion.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Although the communication overhead between
CPUs and a GPU in the same node may be negligi-
ble because the PCI Express bus is used, this is not
the case when remote accelerator virtualization is em-
ployed.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The overheads will be compounded when a
large accelerator required by an Edge node is physi-
cally located in the micro-cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The network band-
width between the Edge node and the micro-cloud
will signiﬁcantly inﬂuence the overall performance of
the virtualized accelerator.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
For example, a large num-
ber of data transfers between the CPU of an Edge
node and a remote GPU in the micro-cloud could
potentially negatively aﬀect the overall performance
of the application.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The challenge in adopting acceler-
ator virtualization on the Edge is to keep overheads
to a minimum for meeting the QoS demands of an
application.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
In
supercomputing
facilities
and
centralized
Cloud data centers, the network overheads of virtual-
ization are mitigated by the use of high-performance
interconnects, but using these interconnects in a
global Edge context is simply not feasible.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Features
such as Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA),
which are used in high-performance interconnects,
could be adopted to reduce communication overheads
5


between Edge nodes and micro-clouds [10].
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This
would save CPU cycles and optimize end-to-end en-
ergy consumption.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Nonetheless, eﬃciently incorpo-
rating RDMA in the Fog architecture may pose new
challenges beyond the scope of this article.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Challenge 6 - Rethinking Accelerator Design
A key consideration for accelerator designers has been
to improve bandwidth between computing cores of
the accelerator and global memory, commonly re-
ferred to as data transfer bandwidth.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Maximizing
the data transfer bandwidth is essential for meeting
performance requirements of High-Performance Com-
puting (HPC) applications.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
However, HPC applications are not representa-
tive of the workloads that will utilize the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The
motivation for using the Edge is to facilitate com-
puting closer to user devices and augment comput-
ing of user devices.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Therefore, the class of applica-
tions best-suited for making use of the Edge will be
user-oriented, such as AR applications, for instance.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
These applications are inherently diﬀerent from HPC
workloads and therefore some accelerator character-
istics that are necessary for HPC workloads, such as
high data transfer bandwidth may not be so neces-
sary in Fog computing due to the inherently diﬀerent
nature of the workloads executed.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
For example, GPUs in Edge nodes are small and
have low power consumption, and, additionally, are
not expected to accelerate HPC applications.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Thus
it would seem that the primary design objective in
this context should not be simply improving features,
such as the data transfer bandwidth.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Instead, design-
ers should seek to surmount the challenge of minia-
turising more powerful GPUs and making dedicated
accelerators for workloads actually executed in this
context.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Looking forward, the challenge is to move
away from the use of generic accelerators, instead de-
signing Edge speciﬁc accelerators for targeted appli-
cation domains.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Opportunities
In light of the challenges, there are six avenues of op-
portunity for realising a complete end-to-end solution
for using accelerators in Fog computing.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Accelerator
virtualization is an enabler for all opportunities and
the solutions will need to take a holistic view of the
Fog architecture to avoid fragmented research.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Opportunity 1 - Feather-light Accelerator Vir-
tualization
Current solutions that oﬀer accelerator virtualiza-
tion for large-scale systems, such as Clusters or
Clouds, assume the availability of signiﬁcant com-
pute resources for management activities that sup-
port virtualization.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
These management activities
comprise a collection of tasks, such as monitoring the
performance of the system to meet QoS demands,
scheduling resources for an application that needs
to be hosted, and scaling resources based on ser-
vice demand.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
These tasks typically require signiﬁcant
amount of resources, we refer to as heavyweight, and
are usually placed on an observer system.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
While accelerator virtualization is demon-
strated to work reasonably well on Clouds
where there is an abundance of resources, it
may not be pragmatic to make use of heavy-
weight management tasks on resource scarce
Edge nodes.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Therefore, a lightweight ap-
proach to accelerator management is required
for the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
However, since the Edge could be resource con-
strained, a lightweight approach is required.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Not
only should management be lightweight, but the ac-
celerator virtualization technology also needs to be
lightweight.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
There are two main techniques that are
currently used for accelerator virtualization, namely
using virtual drivers and API forwarding.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Both
techniques require full knowledge of the accelerator
drivers.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The ﬁrst technique is completely platform
dependant and is less ﬂexible in dynamically accom-
modating more clients.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The second technique usu-
ally oﬀers a more comprehensive solution, but is com-
plex and does not easily work for proprietary accel-
erator drivers.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This hinders portability across dif-
ferent accelerator platforms and consequently their
widespread adoption.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
In light of the above drawbacks
and given that resources required for meaningfully
virtualizing accelerators have not been a major con-
cern on Clouds and clusters given the availability of
signiﬁcant resources, current accelerator virtualiza-
6


tion solutions may not be ﬁt for direct use on the
Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Edge nodes do not have the same computa-
tional capabilities as centralized resources and there-
fore development of a lightweight accelerator virtual-
ization technology is essential.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
We identify opportu-
nities in adopting a two-fold fundamentally diﬀerent
design approach for developing accelerator virtualiza-
tion for the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Firstly, by developing accelerator
virtualization mechanisms that focus on ﬂexibility so
that clients can be added or removed to cope with dy-
namic workloads as seen in Edge settings.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Secondly,
by developing platform and driver agnostic solutions
to integrate a wide variety of accelerators, represen-
tative of the Edge ecosystem, for achieving vendor
neutrality.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Adopting the above design approach, will
help materialize lightweight accelerator virtualization
solutions and make them more suitable for the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Opportunity
2
-
Trading
Performance
for
Throughput
In practice, virtualization could translate to reduced
application performance because an accelerator is
shared among diﬀerent applications.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Ideal acceler-
ation is achieved when an application can exclusively
use the accelerator on an Edge node or on a micro-
cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
But this may lead to reduced overall through-
put.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Exclusively using an accelerator for an appli-
cation does not necessarily mean that an ideal
overall throughput is achieved.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This is be-
cause applications might use accelerators for
very short time intervals and may consume
a very small fragment of the accelerator re-
sources.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
For example, image processing algorithms on
moderate and large GPUs, such as used for the AR
use-case, may not utilize the entire GPU memory.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Moreover, when applications need to be accelerated,
they typically wait until the preceding application
has ﬁnished using the GPU.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
There is opportunity
here for developing frameworks to support concurrent
execution of applications via multiple virtual GPUs
to improve accelerator utilization and service multi-
ple applications on the accelerator at the same time.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This results in a higher overall throughput without
noticeably degrading the performance of individual
applications [11].
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Additional research is required to
develop and implement co-scheduling strategies on
Edge nodes and to understand the impact of con-
sidering the overall throughput as against individual
performance of applications for meeting QoS objec-
tives.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Opportunity 3 - Matchmaking in the Fog Hi-
erarchy: Selective Hierarchical Oﬄoading
The Fog hierarchy is described in terms of layers with
diﬀerent computing capabilities in Figure 1.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Con-
trary to servers in a Cloud data center, power is an
essential design criteria for Edge nodes.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Unlike data
centers that host a large amount of resources, only
limited computing resources can be incorporated in
an Edge node.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
While in principle it would be advantageous
to have large amounts of resources to pro-
cess data closer to the source at the Edge, it
is practically impossible due to power limita-
tions at the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
For example, the Thermal
Design Power (TDP) of a home router will be
at least a magnitude lower than that of a large
accelerator.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This is a fundamental problem
that cannot be easily addressed.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Since Edge nodes are power limited, an applica-
tion will need to be carefully distributed across diﬀer-
ent layers for improving performance.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This requires
the selection of accelerators in the right layer for of-
ﬂoading an application, which if not carefully selected
would be detrimental to performance of the applica-
tion.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This naturally provides two avenues of oppor-
tunity in scheduling.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The ﬁrst avenue, related to the
initial deployment of an application, is referred to as
selective hierarchical oﬄoading.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This initial deploy-
ment can later be enhanced by the second avenue,
referred to as vertical elasticity, which dynamically
accounts for redeploying the accelerated component
of an application if required (this is considered further
in Opportunity 4).
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
We identify that opportunities for selective hier-
archical oﬄoading in the Fog may be based on both
functional and non-functional properties.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Functional
properties may include the computational intensity of
7


the application, which indirectly translates to execu-
tion time.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
If an application is expected to take more
than an acceptable target time on the accelerator in
an Edge node for servicing user requests, then remote
accelerators may be used from the micro-cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Non-
functional properties may include the consideration
of the class of applications.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
For example, the net-
work overhead may be less signiﬁcant for compute
bounded applications and therefore remote acceler-
ators may be beneﬁcial.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
On the other hand, band-
width bounded applications may be aﬀected by net-
work overheads and oﬄoading onto accelerators in
multiple layers may not be beneﬁcial.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This will need
to be underpinned by novel scheduling strategies that
select accelerators in the right Fog layers to meet ser-
vice objectives.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Opportunity 4 - Matchmaking in the Fog Hi-
erarchy: Harnessing Vertical Elasticity
In contrast to horizontal scaling, which is
adding resources of the same type used in
Cloud data centers, we recommend vertical
scaling for using the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
We deﬁne vertical
elasticity in the context of this article as auto-
matically scaling a workload across the Cloud-
Edge continuum, such that an Edge node may
remotely utilize accelerators in micro-clouds
or even the Cloud for satisfying QoS require-
ments.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
For example, if an application cannot
be serviced by a GPU on an Edge node, then
a larger GPU or a collection of GPUs from an
Edge micro-cloud may be accessed to service
the request.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
We anticipate opportunities in the development
of at least two diﬀerent approaches for achieving ver-
tical elasticity.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
In the ﬁrst approach, when an Edge
node receives a request that it cannot satisfy with
its own accelerator, the Edge node may simply for-
ward the request on to a micro-cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
We assume
that micro-clouds are closer to user devices than the
Cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
In this manner, we may still achieve low la-
tency.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
In a second approach, the Edge node may use
remote accelerator virtualization, for example, to use
the accelerators on the micro-cloud to service the re-
quest without forwarding the incoming request to the
micro-cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
In the former approach, the Edge node
is simply a proxy and the network traﬃc is sent as far
as the nodes that can satisfy the request.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Therefore,
the entire application is moved from an Edge node
to the micro-cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
In the latter, however, the Edge
node services the request by making use of acceler-
ators that are located elsewhere in the Edge ecosys-
tem.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Hence the CPU component of the application
is still executed on the Edge node but computational
intensive components that require the accelerator are
oﬄoaded to a remote accelerator, potentially in the
Edge micro-cloud.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
These approaches will need to be
further investigated for fully understanding their ben-
eﬁts for vertical elasticity.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Opportunity 5 - Just-In-Time Application Dis-
tribution
The execution environments that support distributed
applications usually make decisions during compila-
tion time on distributing the application via parti-
tioning across multiple nodes or heterogeneous hard-
ware and where each partition must be executed.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Support for distributing an application across
heterogeneous resources is available via the
programming model and programming lan-
guage.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The onus of determining an (or
the most) eﬃcient distribution currently rests
with the programmer.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Just-In-Time distribu-
tion may overcome this burden.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Runtime solutions in this space may cope with
variable sizes of input data for each partition, but
research in partitioning an application based on the
availability of diﬀerent hardware or even environ-
ment conditions, such as network traﬃc, is not ma-
ture.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Runtime solutions may either search the prob-
lem space exhaustively to determine an eﬃcient dis-
tribution plan or may predict performance of diﬀer-
ent combinations of partitions using a mathematical
model.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This is cumbersome and may not be suitable
for resource constrained and dynamic Edge environ-
ments.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
There are numerous opportunities in the Edge
context to research runtime distribution of applica-
tions, we refer to as ‘Just-in-Time’ (JIT) distribution.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
These include developing mechanisms to oﬄoad the
8


parallel component of an application to one or more
virtual and/or remote accelerators.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
The JIT distri-
bution could be based on reducing total execution
time of the application, ﬁnding optimal geographical
locations for placing partitions and availability of re-
sources for fulﬁlling QoS of the application, minimiz-
ing response times, and improving the overall energy
eﬃciency and performance.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
These mechanisms may
be used on a single node that contains an accelera-
tor or across multiple nodes to access remote virtual
accelerators.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
However, a key question that will still
need to be addressed is how to host individual par-
titions on accelerators with very little overheads in
the Edge ecosystem.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
In the context of CPU only
applications, container technology, such as Docker is
widely used to package and deploy partitions across
resources.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Containers are yet to become fully inter-
operable across heterogeneous resources.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Although
containers have lower overheads than VMs, in prac-
tice they require time in the order of a few seconds
to start up.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Accelerator supporting containers have
started to emerge, such as GPU-Enabled Docker con-
tainers, but are still in their infancy [12].
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Container
overheads will need to be reduced or a radically dif-
ferent interoperable technology similar to containers
will need to be developed.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This will facilitate JIT
distribution of applications.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Opportunity 6 - On-demand Service Caching
We identify service caching as an opportunity to re-
duce communication latencies and optimally make
use of accelerator resources at the Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
That is, ser-
vices in high demand making use of accelerators may
be cached on Edge nodes.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
However, not all services
can be cached given that accelerator resources avail-
able on an Edge node are limited.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Hence, the obvious
question needs to be answered assuming accelerator
multi-tenancy - which services should be cached on
an Edge node?
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Accelerator virtualization decouples the CPU and
accelerator components of an application thus allow-
ing for a more eﬃcient service caching in the following
two ways.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Firstly, by developing mechanisms to move
computation to remote accelerators on micro-clouds
so that they host services that cannot be cached on
the Edge node.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Secondly, by developing methods
to migrate services that require acceleration between
Edge nodes and micro-clouds based on demand.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
In
both cases, only the accelerator component of the
application is moved, whereas the CPU component
remains on the Edge node.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
For instance, less popu-
lar services may be cached on micro-clouds whereas
more popular services may reside on Edge nodes.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
If
user demand for a service increases, then it may be
migrated to the Edge node and swapped for a less
popular service.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Service caching in Fog computing is
currently untapped into and remains an open avenue
to be explored.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Accelerator virtualization facilitates service
caching on Edge nodes.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Instead of caching
the entire application, only the accelerator
component of the application is cached.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
This
is possible because the CPU and accelerator
components of an application are decoupled.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Therefore, the accelerator component can be
moved to any remote accelerator while the
CPU component resides on the Edge node.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Summary
How can enhanced analytics be possible at the Edge in
Fog computing?
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Application speciﬁc hardware accel-
erators designed for Edge nodes are key to achieving
this and accelerator virtualization is an enabling tech-
nology to facilitate a service oriented Edge.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

text:
Looking
forward, maintaining an end-to-end perspective of the
Fog architecture, from design to delivery, is essential
for conducting useful research in this area.
title: arXiv:1810.06046v1  [cs.DC]  14 Oct 2018

Sayed Chhattan Shah

Abstract  
Grid and cloud computing systems have been extensively used to solve large and complex 
problems in science and engineering areas.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
These systems include powerful computing resources 
connected through high speed networks.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Due to recent advances in mobile computing and 
networking technologies it has become feasible to integrate various mobile devices such as 
robots, aerial vehicles, sensors, and smart phones with grid and cloud computing systems.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
This 
integration enables design and development of next generation of applications through sharing of 
resources in mobile environments and also introduces several challenges due to dynamic and 
unpredictable network.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
This paper discusses applications, research challenges involved in design 
and development of mobile grid and cloud computing systems, and recent advances in the field.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Keywords: Cloud Robotics, Sensor Cloud, Mobile Distributed Systems, Ad hoc Networks  
 
 
1.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Introduction 
A distributed system consists of a collection of autonomous computers, connected through a 
network and distribution middleware, which enables computers to coordinate their activities and 
to share the resources of the system, so that users perceive the system as a single, integrated 
computing facility.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
One of the best examples of distributed system is an automated teller machine where user is 
provided with a simple and easy to use interface to perform numerous transactions.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
From user’s 
point view there is a single system but in background hundreds of different computing devices 
are connected through various networks to provide a range of financial services.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The distributed systems are divided into three main categories: cluster, grid and cloud computing 
system.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In cluster, distributed computing devices are connected through a high-speed local area 
network whereas in grid, geographically distributed resources are connected through a wide area 
network to solve large and complex problems.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
A layered architecture of cluster and grid computing systems is presented in Figures 1 and 2, 
respectively.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The resource layer includes computing devices which are connected through 
networking and communication technologies.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The middleware layer provides resource and task 
management services which include resource monitoring and discovery service, fault 
management service, resource allocation service and task migration service.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In addition, 
middleware hides all the complexities and provides a single system image to user and 
applications running on the system.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Resource and task management in clusters is usually based 
on a centralized architecture while grid relies on distributed architectures for resource and task 
management.

title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing 
 
Mobile Cloud Computing 
In mobile cloud computing, mobile devices are integrated with a cloud computing system 
through an infrastructure-based communication network such as cellular network.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The 
computationally intensive tasks are offloaded to a cloud for execution.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Architecture of mobile 
cloud system is given in Figure 6.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Mobile Grid and Cluster Computing 
In mobile grid computing, mobile devices are connected to a grid computing system through an 
infrastructure-based communication network such as cellular network.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The computationally 
intensive tasks are sent to grid computing system which after processing sends results back to the 
mobile device.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In mobile cluster computing, mobile devices are connected to cluster through an 
infrastructure-based network.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text: Architecture of mobile grid system is given in Figure 7.

The continuous increase in processing power of mobile devices, improved data transfer rates of 
wireless networks, and growing popularity of cloud computing systems and mobile devices has 
made it feasible and valuable to integrate mobile devices with traditional distributed systems.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The currently available mobile device such as iPhone 6 has more processing power than the 
supercomputer used in the early nineties [1] [2] while the current generation of wireless network 
such as 4G provides 100 megabits per second of data rate which is enough for streaming a video.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Several companies are already testing 5G networks that aim to provide 10 gigabits per second of 
data rate.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Figure 8 illustrates advances in mobile computing and communication technologies, 
worldwide forecast of mobile phones, and cloud computing market share.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Benefits 
Cloud computing systems provide vast amount of storage space and processing power on 
demand.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Integration of mobile devices with cloud would enable mobile devices to access vast 
data storage capacity and processing power.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In addition, mobile user would be able to execute 
data and computationally intensive applications such as image and video processing on mobile 
devices.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Data storage and execution of such applications on cloud would also improve reliability 
and would extend the battery life of mobile devices.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Figure 8: Illustrates advances in mobile computing and communication technologies, 
worldwide forecast of mobile phones, and cloud computing market share.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Cloud Robotics 
Cloud robotics is another interesting topic in area of mobile cloud computing.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In cloud robotics, 
robots are integrated with cloud computing system to access vast amount of processing power 
and data storage.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
This integration allows robots to offload heavy tasks such as image processing 
and voice recognition to cloud.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text: Block diagram of cloud robotics is given in Figure 9.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In addition to advantages discussed for mobile cloud computing, integration of robots with cloud 
provides several other advantages.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
1- Execution of computationally intensive tasks on cloud would result in cheaper, lighter 
and easy-to-maintain hardware, longer battery life, minimum software updates, and 
hassle-free and invisible CPU hardware upgrades.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
2- Shared object library: Assume a scenario in which a robot deployed in an urban 
environment encounters an unknown object and therefore is unable to manipulate it.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
To 
address this issue one option is to maintain information of commonly used objects on a 
robot which would require large amount of storage space and also processing power.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The 
second option is to maintain the information of commonly used objects on the cloud.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
When a robot encounters an unknown object, it can take a picture of object and send it to 
cloud which in turn will return the required information such as object name, 3D model, 
mass, materials, friction properties, and usage instructions required to operate the object.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The object library on the cloud can be shared by several robots and can be regularly 
updated by experts.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
3- Like object library, a library of numerous skills, navigation algorithms, and maps can also 
be maintained on the cloud.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
When a robot is deployed in unknown environment and is 
unable to navigate, it can directly download the required map and navigation algorithm to 
navigate in the environment.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In addition, library may include several navigation 
Figure 9: Cloud Robotics  


 
 
algorithms developed by numerous experts.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
For example, when robot has a limited 
battery power it may choose to download an energy efficient algorithm and if energy is 
not a concern a computationally intensive algorithm with a better performance can be 
used.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Sensor Grid and Cloud 
In sensor grid and cloud, sensor nodes are integrated with grid and cloud computing system 
through a gateway node.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Sensor nodes are used to collect data which is then sent to cloud for 
further processing.

title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Mobile Ad hoc Computational Grid and Cloud 
The mobile grid and cloud computing systems are restricted to infrastructure-based 
communication systems such as cellular network, and therefore cannot be used in mobile ad hoc 
environments.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
A mobile ad hoc computational grid [29] is a distributed computing infrastructure 
that enables mobile nodes to share computing resources without pre-existing network 
infrastructure whereas mobile ad hoc computational cloud is a distributed computing 
infrastructure in which multiple mobile devices interconnected through a mobile ad hoc network 
are presented as one powerful, unified computing resource.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The system architecture of mobile ad 
hoc computational cloud is given in Figure 11.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Figure 11:  illustrates a diagram of mobile ad hoc computational cloud in which multiple mobile devices 
interconnected through a mobile ad hoc network are presented as one powerful, unified computing 
resource.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Mobile ad hoc computational grid is a combination of computational grid and mobile ad hoc 
network.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Computational grid is a software infrastructure that allows distributed computing 
devices to share computing resources to solve computationally-intensive problems.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Whereas 
mobile ad hoc network is a wireless network of mobile devices that communicate with each 
other without any pre-existing network infrastructure.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text: Architecture of mobile ad hoc computational grid is presented in Figure 12.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Mobile nodes 
communicate with each other through a mobile ad hoc network which provides several 
communication services including transport, routing, and medium access.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The middleware layer, 
computational grid, provides resource management service which includes resource monitoring, 
resource discovery, and task management services, fault management service, mobility 
management service, communication service, and task migration service.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In addition, 
middleware hides all the complexities and provides a single system image to user and 
applications running on the system.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:

Success of a military or disaster relief operation depends on several factors including 
understanding of the physical environment and real-time detection and tracking of mobile and

stationary targets.

drones equipped with audio, video and environmental sensors are deployed to collect data which 
is then processed to construct a three dimensional map of environment in real-time.

text:
The 
collected data is also used to detect and track mobile and stationary targets which involve

4.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Research Challenges  
Compared to traditional parallel and distributed computing systems such as grid and cloud, 
mobile grid and cloud computing systems introduce several challenges due to global and local 
node mobility, high latency, limited power, and dynamic network environment.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
This section 
discusses the key research challenges.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
 
Global and local node mobility: Global node mobility refers to the movement of nodes 
across the coverage area whereas local node mobility refers to the movement of nodes 
within the coverage area.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Global node mobility results in failure of one or several tasks 
whereas local node mobility may increase data transfer cost and thus task completion 
time.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text: Effect of local node mobility is described in Figure 14.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Task migration or 
reallocation strategy can be used to manage task failure but this will introduce delay and 
will increase task completion time.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Global node mobility also introduces the problem of outdated information managed by 
resource discovery and monitoring system.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
To address the problem, continuous 
monitoring of resources is required but it will increase communication cost.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
An alternate 
approach is to enquire the status of resources during decision making but this will 
introduce delay.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text: Figure 14:  illustrates effect of local node mobility.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Tasks executing on Node 1 and Node 2 are 
communicating directly.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
During execution of task, Node 2 moves within the network coverage 
area and therefore is not directly accessible to Node 1.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
So, task executing on Node 1 
communicates with a task executing on Node 2 through two intermediate nodes, Node 3 and 4.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text: This would increase data transfer time and thus task completion time.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
To address the problems, an effective and robust resource allocation scheme is proposed 
in [23].
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The scheme uses history of user’s mobility patterns to select nodes that will 
remain connected for long period of time.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Since this scheme relies on user’s mobility 
history, it cannot be used in situations where mobility history is not available or user has 
random and irregular mobility patterns.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
 
Dynamic communication environment: Communication system of mobile ad hoc grid 
and cloud is unpredictable, dynamic and limited in performance due to low bandwidth, 
local and global node mobility, and lack of preexisting network infrastructure.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The 
connection quality at different network sections fluctuates over the time.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Even different 
nodes may experience different connection quality at the same time.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Due to these 
reasons, data transfer cost is critical for application performance.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
 
Power management: Communication energy consumption depends on two key factors: 
transmission power required to transmit data and communication cost induced by data 
transfers between tasks.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In literature, several mechanisms are proposed to address the 
problem but most of them are focused on the conservation of processing energy, while 
saving communication energy remains an open problem which becomes even more 
critical for data-oriented applications.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
To reduce communication energy consumption, an energy efficient resource allocation 
scheme is developed in [22].
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The main idea is to use transmission power control 
mechanism and allocate dependent tasks to nodes that are accessible at minimum 
transmission power.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
However, further investigation is required to incorporate the 
transmission power control mechanism in resource discovery, resource monitoring, 
failure management, and task migration services.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
 
Task migration: Task migration primarily involves transferring both code and data 
across the nodes.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Tasks are migrated for several reasons such as to improve application 
performance and resource utilization, balance load, conserve energy, and manage task 
failure.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Compared to traditional systems, design of migration service for mobile grid and 
cloud computing systems is difficult due to dynamic network environment.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The most 
common migration strategy is to estimate migration cost and determine task execution 
time with or without the migration.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The estimation of migration cost depends on 
estimation of data transfer time which is not straightforward particularly for data-
oriented applications.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
 
Computation offloading: One of the key challenges in mobile grid and cloud 
computing systems is to devise an efficient task offloading strategy.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In literature, 
several offloading strategies [39-49] are proposed which are classified based numerous 
factors such as:  
 
o Offloading objective: An application [39-41] or part of application [42-49] is 
offloaded to a remote system for several reasons such as to improve application 
performance, reduce energy consumption, or to avoid task failure.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
o Offloading client: Mobile node that uses offloading could be smart phone, mobile 
robot, autonomous aerial vehicle, or sensor.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
o Infrastructure for offloading: Mobile node may offload computation to a cluster 
[31-32, 51-52], grid [36-38], cloud computing system [39-42], or to a powerful 
computer connected through a wide or local area network [40].
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
o Type of applications: Various application types have been studied such as 
computationally intensive applications, data intensive applications, data parallel 
applications, and task parallel applications [49].
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
o Application partitioning mechanisms: To partition an application into tasks two 
key approaches have been proposed: static and dynamic.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
The later one is more 
flexible and suitable for dynamic and unpredictable environments.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
o Offloading decision: A decision to offload task could be made before runtime or 
during runtime.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In order to design an effective offloading strategy, several factors such as network 
bandwidth, available energy, processing speed of remote and host resource, task queue 
size, amount of data transfers between a task on client node and a task to be allocated on 
remote server node should be considered.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
 
Architecture: Every architecture have some pros and cons, for example, centralized 
architecture results in effective resource allocation decisions due to network wide view 
but suffers from scalability and single point of failure problems.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Whereas distributed 
architecture solves scalability and single point of failure problems but results into poor 
resource allocation decisions due to lack of network wide view.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Possible architectures 
for mobile ad hoc grid and cloud computing system are given in Figure 15.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
There is a 
need to develop an energy efficient, effective and robust architecture that should give 
maximum performance in a wide range of scenarios.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
 
Parallel programming model: Programming models developed for infrastructure-based 
computing systems cannot be used in dynamic and ad hoc network environments.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
There 
Figure 15: Architectural choices for mobile ad hoc grid and cloud computing system  


 
 
is need to design a programming model which provide lightweight migration and 
communication mechanisms and should support high mobility scenarios.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
 
Transport and routing protocols: Numerous transport and routing protocols have been 
developed either to reduce data transfer times or transmission energy consumption.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Most 
of these protocols are not adaptive to application or system’s requirements.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
There is need 
to develop adaptive transport and routing protocols.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Such protocols, for example, should 
reduce energy consumption either using multi hop communication or transmission 
power control mechanism if that does not cause tasks to miss the deadline, or send data 
through multiple routes when network becomes unstable.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In addition, the protocols 
should actively communicate with grid and mobility management systems in order to 
provide reliable and robust services.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
 
Wireless communication technologies: Several wireless communication technologies 
such as Wi-Fi Direct and Bluetooth with different characteristics are available to transfer 
data from one node to another in an ad hoc mode.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In addition, most of the devices 
provide an option to use and switch between multiple connections at the same time.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
In 
order to provide efficient and reliable data transmission, further work is required to 
investigate and adopt wireless communication technologies for mobile ad hoc grid and 
cloud.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
 
Development of simulation environment: Existing simulators allow simulation of 
either networking protocols or cloud related algorithms and schemes.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Simulators that 
support simulation of both, networking protocols and cloud management systems, are 
not designed for mobile ad hoc environments.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
Further work is required for the 
development of environment in which both networking and computational cloud related 
algorithms can be evaluated.
title: Recent Advances in Mobile Grid and Cloud Computing

text:
