Priority-based Fair Scheduling in Edge Computing
Arkadiusz Madej1, Nan Wang2, Nikolaos Athanasopoulos1, Rajiv Ranjan3, and Blesson Varghese1
1Queen’s University Belfast, UK; 2Durham University, UK; 3Newcastle University, UK
E-mail: amadej01@qub.ac.uk; nan.wang@durham.ac.uk; n.athanasopoulos@qub.ac.uk;
raj.ranjan@ncl.ac.uk; b.varghese@qub.ac.uk (Corresponding E-mail)
Abstract—Scheduling is important in Edge computing.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In
contrast to the Cloud, Edge resources are hardware limited and
cannot support workload-driven infrastructure scaling.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Hence,
resource allocation and scheduling for the Edge requires a
fresh perspective.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Existing Edge scheduling research assumes
availability of all needed resources whenever a job request is
made.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This paper challenges that assumption, since not all job
requests from a Cloud server can be scheduled on an Edge
node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Thus, guaranteeing fairness among the clients (Cloud
servers ofﬂoading jobs) while accounting for priorities of the
jobs becomes a critical task.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This paper presents four scheduling
techniques, the ﬁrst is a naive ﬁrst come ﬁrst serve strategy and
further proposes three strategies, namely a client fair, priority
fair, and hybrid that accounts for the fairness of both clients and
job priorities.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
An evaluation on a target platform under three
different scenarios, namely equal, random, and Gaussian job
distributions is presented.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The experimental studies highlight the
low overheads and the distribution of scheduled jobs on the Edge
node when compared to the naive strategy.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The results conﬁrm
the superior performance of the hybrid strategy and showcase
the feasibility of fair schedulers for Edge computing.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Index
Terms—edge
computing,
fair
scheduling,
priority
scheduling, fog computing
I.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
INTRODUCTION
Edge computing is a relatively recent distributed computing
paradigm that leverages resources at the edge of the network
for improving the overall performance of an application [1]–
[3].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Edge resources may include routers or base stations, or
dedicated micro clouds located at the network edge.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Typically, an application may be ofﬂoaded from the Cloud
to the Edge or from end user-devices to the Edge [4].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In the
former case of ofﬂoading, a service hosted in the Cloud is
brought closer to user-devices at the Edge for minimising
communication latency [5], [6] and reducing the volume of
data transferred to the Cloud [7].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The computational resources
available on the Edge are hardware limited (small form factor,
limited power, processing cores and storage) when compared
to large amounts of hardware available in a Cloud data
center [8].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In the latter case of ofﬂoading, computational jobs
that cannot be processed on battery powered user devices
are ofﬂoaded to Edge nodes that are powered via main
lines and consequently can host more resources with more
computational capacity than available on the device [9], [10].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This paper considers the case when services of an applica-
tion are ofﬂoaded from the Cloud to the Edge; these ofﬂoaded
services are explicitly referred to as a ‘jobs’ in this paper.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Edge computing jobs are different from traditional Cloud
workloads in that they are not entire applications, rather a
subset of the services of an application that may be latency
critical/bandwidth intensive.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Executing these jobs on the Edge
will result in an improvement in the Quality-of-Service (QoS)
of the entire application.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Incoming jobs to the Edge will
need to be efﬁciently scheduled on to the resources.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Although
there is a large body of research that tackles scheduling for
different parallel and distributed systems, such as Grids [11],
Clusters [12], and Clouds [13], scheduling on the resource
constrained Edge is more challenging [14].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Due to limited
hardware resources available on the Edge, it is not easy to
adopt the aforementioned approaches for Edge computing.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
There are various scheduling strategies that are considered
for computing systems.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In all cases, ensuring fairness is a
key prerequisite as many unwanted situations can otherwise
occur.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Consider for example when higher rates of incoming
jobs from a speciﬁc application are scheduled on the Edge
and deny access (or queue) to the ones that are less frequent.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
A large proportion of existing Edge scheduling research
implicitly assumes that all job requests can be successfully
scheduled on an Edge node; because resources are available
whenever a request is made.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
However, this paper makes the
assumption that not all incoming job requests from a Cloud
server can be scheduled on the Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This is because
Edge resources are hardware limited.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Therefore, there will
be signiﬁcant competition to gain access to these resources.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Developing scheduling strategies that ensure fairness among
clients, which is the objective of this paper, becomes essential.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Cloud and Edge resources are likely to be owned by differ-
ent operators or service providers; this translates to Cloud ap-
plication owners having to pay for using Edge resources [15].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Assuming a cost model in which users pay for Edge resources,
priorities will need to be accounted for since users may pay for
premium service (higher priority execution) on the Edge [15].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Although fair scheduling has been extensively studied in
Cloud computing [16], [17], it needs to be revisited within the
context of Edge computing [18].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This is because, as already
highlighted, Edge resources are hardware limited and therefore
it is a very hard task to dynamically auto-scale.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
For example,
some edge nodes, such as routers, will already host a trafﬁc-
routing service and may only be able to host some ofﬂoaded
workloads from the Cloud for a small amount of time.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In this paper, we consider fair scheduling for a large number
of relatively short running incoming job requests at the same
time to an Edge resource that need to be scheduled by taking
1
arXiv:2001.09070v1  [cs.DC]  24 Jan 2020


priorities of jobs into account without being unfair to any
speciﬁc type of incoming jobs.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Given a number of clients
that own different jobs, the scheduler proposed in this paper
determines which jobs of a client can be scheduled on to an
Edge node to ensure fairness among all clients.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The research
presented in this paper is concerned with the fairness of the
scheduling strategy on a single Edge resource.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Nonetheless,
it is noted that the proposed fair scheduling strategies can
be easily extended to undertake cooperative and fair load-
balancing across multiple Edge resources.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Four scheduling techniques are presented - the ﬁrst come
ﬁrst serve strategy used as a baseline and three additional
techniques are proposed that account for different notions of
fairness.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
They are: (i) a client fair strategy that accounts for
the fairness of the client submitting the job, (ii) a priority fair
strategy that accounts for the fairness of the priorities of the
job, and (iii) a hybrid strategy that accounts for priorities of
incoming jobs and the client submitting them.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
An experimental
study is carried out on a target platform to identify the
overheads and distribution of jobs.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Preliminary investigation
conﬁrms the feasibility of the proposed scheduling technique
and suggests the superior performance of the hybrid strategy.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Section II presents the
proposed scheduler.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Section III considers job management by
taking fairness of the client and priorities of the job into
account.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text: Section IV presents experimental results obtained.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Section VI concludes
this paper by presenting opportunities for future work.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
FAIR SCHEDULING ON THE EDGE
To effectively employ Edge computing, a research ques-
tion that needs to be answered is how to schedule different
workloads ofﬂoaded from multiple Cloud applications such
that they can share hardware resources on an Edge node in
a fair manner.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This section investigates the requirements for
fair scheduling in Edge computing and proposes an ‘Edge Fair
Scheduler (EFS)’ that can operate at the edge of the network.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Architecture
The proposed EFS is designed to be integrated in a three-
layer Edge architecture that consists of the Cloud layer, the
Edge layer and the User layer [19].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
With such an architecture,
a part or all of a Cloud application is ofﬂoaded from the
Cloud layer to the Edge layer when Edge computing services
are requested.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
When the ofﬂoaded application is deployed on
Edge nodes, the users connect to the Edge nodes instead of
the Cloud, which reduces the latency in communication by
allowing data to be processed closer to the users.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The EFS is required on each Edge
node to provide fair scheduling to all workloads that intend to
use Edge computing services on this Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The Cloud servers will host long-running applications, and
in this paper they are considered as clients of Edge computing
services.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
A client script is provided for each Cloud server to:
(i) request a new job to be started on an Edge node; (ii) deploy
an application onto an Edge node; (iii) terminate an application
Fig.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
1: Architecture of EFS in an Edge computing environment
that is currently running on an Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The applications
are hosted in Docker containers for the purpose of isolation.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
When requesting to use the Edge service on an Edge node, the
client can decide to either deploy all or a subset of workloads
of the Cloud application using containers.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The user device layer consists of end users devices that
communicate with the deployed applications on Edge nodes.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The users will be redirected from the Cloud to the Edge node
on which the application has been deployed.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The redirection
of users from the Cloud to Edge nodes is the responsibility of
the clients (i.e.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text: the Cloud server) deploying the applications.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The main components of the EFS on an Edge resource
comprises: (i) a request handler that listens to new requests
from any of the authorised clients, (ii) a scheduler that decides
which request will be processed next, (iii) a monitor that
detects and terminates idle jobs, and (iv) a number of appli-
cation servers deployed in Docker containers.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The Edge layer
will realistically comprise a large number of Edge resources.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
However, in this prototype of EFS, only a single Edge node
is considered.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
EFS on multiple nodes is not within the scope
of this paper.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The EFS components in detail are:
(i) Request Handler: this component handles all the incom-
ing client requests to the EFS.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
It only accepts new connections
that have the correct Secure Sockets Layer (SSL) certiﬁcates
to authorise the client.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This allows client identiﬁcation and
tracking of the frequency of client job execution.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The handler
will then perform the necessary action based on the request
type, for instance to start, deploy, or terminate a job.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Any new
job requests are queued in a database and are then further
2


handled by the Scheduler.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Requests to terminate jobs are also
queued in the database and then further processed by the
Monitor.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
All invalid requests are ignored and the client will
be notiﬁed that an invalid request has been made.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
(ii) Scheduler: performs the scheduling of queued job
requests.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
It monitors the database queue and schedules the
next job if the queue is not empty and resources are available.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text: The scheduling strategy is speciﬁed by a conﬁg ﬁle.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Based on
the selected scheduling strategy a corresponding algorithm is
executed to determine which job is the next to be executed.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The
different scheduling strategies considered in EFS are discussed
in the next section.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This component will also notify the clients
that the requested job is being started and will set up password-
less SSH access for the client to the container.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
(iii) Monitor: this component is responsible for the manage-
ment of already running job containers on the Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
It
detects idle containers, which will be queued for termination
once detected.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The second function is to monitor the termi-
nation queue and to terminate any of the queued containers.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The containers to be terminated may be the idle, which were
detected by the Monitor, or the jobs which have been requested
for termination by the client from the Cloud.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
(iv) Job Containers: this component is the pool of running
Docker containers that host the jobs ofﬂoaded from the Cloud.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
These containers provide an isolated and safe execution envi-
ronment for the applications.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Appropriate networking allows
for the services in the containers to be accessible by the end
users.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
A client is only allowed to access its corresponding con-
tainer which is handled by the Scheduler when the container
is booting up.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Once a container is terminated it is deleted
alongside all the data footprint on the node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
JOB MANAGEMENT IN THE SCHEDULER
The proposed EFS has three functionalities, namely job
request handling, the scheduling of jobs and the monitoring of
jobs.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Request handling refers to managing incoming requests
from authorised clients and handling them.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Scheduling jobs
is a main task of the EFS and the associated scheduling
strategies decide which queuing jobs are next executed.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In
general, job scheduling on a distributed system is an NP-
Complete problem and this assumption holds true for the Edge
computing scenario.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Monitoring jobs in the containers is to
release compute resources from containers that are either idle
or requested to be terminated.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Table I presents the notation
used in the algorithms presented in this section.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Request Handling
Algorithm 1 demonstrates the request handling process of
the EFS on an Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This allows the clients to make job
related requests to the Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
When the EFS is ﬁrst started
it reads a conﬁguration ﬁle which stores the required values
such as the maximum number of jobs that can be supported
by an Edge node maxjobs (Line 1).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Once the conﬁguration
is loaded then the request handling service starts running
continuously until being terminated by a SIGINT signal.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing
Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
When a new HTTP socket connection is established
(Line 3) the client is then asked for an SSL certiﬁcate (Line 4)
which should have previously been acquired from the Edge
service provider (i.e.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Edge node owner) for establishing a
secure encrypted connection.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The creation and distribution of
SSL certiﬁcates is the responsibility of the service provider.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The provider can either choose to sign the certiﬁcates using
OpenSSL or a third party SSL certiﬁcate signing authority.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Since the certiﬁcates are distributed to clients individually they
assist the identiﬁcation of which client is connecting.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Once a
secure connection is established using valid SSL certiﬁcates
the request handler awaits request from the client (Line 6).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
There are two valid requests – to start a new job (Line 7) or
to terminate a job (Line 14).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
If the client requests a new job to
be started (Line 7), the service ﬁrst checks if there is any space
left in the queue for anther job (Line 8).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
If a space is available
the job is added to the database, with the job requirements
received in the initial request to start this job.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Once the job is
queued the client is notiﬁed of the job ID which can be used
in the future to terminate the job (Line 10).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
If there is no space
in the queue, the client is notiﬁed of rejection due to the lack
of available space (Line 12).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
If the request is to terminate a job

title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Jobs that are already running on the Edge
node will instead be queued for termination (Lines 18-19).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Then the client is notiﬁed that the request has been accepted

title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Job Scheduling
The job scheduler is responsible for ﬁrstly identifying the
next job to be executed, and secondly provisioning hardware
resources of an Edge node for executing the job.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The decision
of which job is the next job to be scheduled affects the fairness
of the Edge resources.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Four scheduling strategies are presented
in this paper; the ﬁrst is the First Come First Serve (FCFS),
and the three remaining are proposed for EFS, namely the
fairness for the clients (referred to as Client Fair), fairness for
the jobs (referred to as Priority Fair), and a hybrid strategy.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
1) First Come First Serve: FCFS is a popularly adopted
baseline strategy in Edge research [20], [21].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This strategy
uses the time sequence of the jobs arrived to select the next
job to be executed.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
When the FCFS strategy is applied, the
scheduler considers fairness on the basis of the time of job
request submission.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
It looks up the oldest entry in the job
queue, along with the job requirements.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This entry in the
database is then moved from the queue into the history table.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
All of the job requirements are then passed to the scheduler
for launching an appropriate container for the job.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The FCFS-based scheduler does not consider where a
request is coming from.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
There may be a case that one user
sent 100 jobs to an Edge node slightly before the second user
tries to use Edge resources for its ﬁrst job.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
With the FCFS-
based scheduler, the Edge node would be exhausted by jobs
submitted from the ﬁrst user, leaving the second user in an
unfair competition.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Therefore, the origin of the job requests
(or users of the Edge) need to be considered.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing
Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This concept of fairness was initially proposed to ensure
that all users of a computing node will have a fair share of the
processing resources [22].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In the Edge computing environment
targeted in this paper, when the fairness for the client strategy
is applied, the scheduler ensures that between all of the clients
who request jobs on the Edge node an equal amount of jobs
from each client are executed providing sufﬁcient requests are
made.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This strategy prevents clients who make frequent job
requests from being favoured and allows new clients get a
chance of using Edge resources.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Algorithm 2 implements the fairness for the client strategy
in the EFS, referred to as the Client Fair algorithm.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Initially
a list of the currently waiting clients is created (Line 1).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
For
4


each of the clients in the list, the frequency of job executions
is calculated (Line 3).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The client whose jobs have been least
frequently executed is then selected (Line 5).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The oldest entry
in the job queue for that client is then selected along with the
job requirements (Line 6).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The job is then moved from the
queue into the job history (Line 7) before the job requirements
are returned to the scheduler (Line 8).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This Client Fair algorithm aims to provide equal frequency
of executing jobs for all users on an Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
However,
it does not distinguish the jobs (i.e.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
all jobs are assumed as
equally important).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
There could be a case that a client whose
jobs are all highly important is not executed on the Edge
node because by this algorithm another client whose jobs are
not important at all needs to be fairly treated.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Therefore, the
next scheduling strategy focuses on the importance of jobs by
prioritising them.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The complexity of the algorithm is O(1),
which is a constant assuming that the job queue is up-to-date
and queues the job in descending order of job arrival time.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
3) Priority Fair strategy: In contrast to the above strategy,
this strategy considers fairness on the basis of jobs with
different priorities.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Algorithm 3 demonstrates how fairness
is ensured for all jobs on an Edge node, referred to as the
Priority Fair algorithm.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In particular, three levels of priorities
are considered for the jobs to be executed on the Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Firstly the scheduler assigns a weight to each of the priority
levels (Line 1).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Starting at the highest priority value of 3 to the
lowest of 1, the weighting is set as follows: 50%, 35%, 15%.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This is necessary because only using the three priority levels
may cause a starvation problem for low-priority jobs when
there are too many high-priority jobs.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
By applying weights,
jobs with the lowest priority level will have a chance to use
Edge resources and meanwhile the probability of executed jobs
will still follow the pre-deﬁned three priority levels.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Similarly to the previous Client Fair scheduling strategy,
a list of waiting priorities is constructed (Line 3).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
For each
of the priorities in the constructed list, a job frequency
percentage is calculated (Lines 5-9).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Then the scheduler selects
an appropriate priority level, from which a job will be further
selected as the next job to be executed.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
To identify the priority
level, the selected job priority is ﬁrstly initialised with a value
of −1 (Line 12).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Then starting at the highest priority level, the
frequency of jobs having been executed for each priority level
is compared against the priority weightings.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
If a priority level
is below the weighting threshold conﬁgured, then this priority
level is selected (Lines 14-15).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Such a searching process for
the appropriate priority level is repeated until a valid priority
value is obtained.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In the case that the waiting priorities list is
exhausted, the highest priority level is selected as the next to
be executed (Lines 16-17).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This is because the priority level is
assumed to be purchased by clients and the more times high-
priority jobs are executed the more revenue can be generated
for the Edge service provider.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Once the next priority level of jobs to be executed is
selected, the oldest entry in the job queue for that priority
level is then selected and its job requirements are retrieved
(Line 22).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing
Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Following this the
job requirements are returned to the scheduler for starting the
job (Line 24).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The complexity of the algorithm is O(P), where
P is the number of priority levels considered in EFS.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Priority Fair is different from Client Fair as it focuses on the
importance of jobs and aims to ensure the relative priorities
of jobs while giving a reasonable share of Edge resources to
low-priority jobs.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
However, the priority fair algorithm does
not consider where these jobs come from, and thus there is
no guarantee of fairness for different users of an Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
A hybrid fair scheduling strategy is developed to consider the
fairness of both the clients and the jobs,
4) Hybrid strategy: To provide fairness for both the clients
and the priority of the jobs at the same time, this Hybrid Fair-
ness scheduling strategy combines the design of the Client Fair
and the Priority Fair strategies, as illustrated in Algorithm 4.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
When this strategy is applied, the scheduler ﬁrstly identiﬁes the
appropriate priority level of jobs to be executed next (Line 1).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Then instead of directly choosing the oldest entry in the job
queue for that priority level, the Hybrid Fairness scheduler
calculates the frequency of executed jobs for all clients.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Only
jobs submitted by the client having the least number of jobs
being executed is then further considered (Line 2).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Finally the
oldest entry in the job queue for the selected priority level and
5


the selected client is scheduled to be executed next (Lines 3-4).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
By doing so the probability of executing high-priority jobs is
kept and the clients are satisﬁed because no users of an Edge
node will receive a larger share of the resources than others.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The complexity of the algorithm is the sum of the complexities
of the priority fair and client fair algorithms presented above.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing
Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
A new
job will be executed if the maximum number of jobs that can
be supported on the Edge node is not exceeded and there are
resources available on the Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The selection of this
new job is done by the EFS using one of the four scheduling
strategies presented above.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Each strategy considers fairness in
a different way to demonstrate that fairness is subjective.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Once the next job has been selected a container is started
and all the requested ports are forwarded.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The container
automatically binds the ports to all available interfaces on the
Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text: An SSL session is established with the client.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Then
the client is notiﬁed of the container being started along with a
key-value store of the port mappings.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In return, the client sends
the EFS a public SSH key that is appended to the authorised
hosts ﬁle within the container for secure access.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Following this
set-up the client installs any dependencies, copies necessary
ﬁles and starts the application in the container.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text: This section presents job scheduling in the EFS.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The
scheduling strategies presented in this paper are executed on
the Edge nodes and they have been carefully designed to not
exhaust resources on the Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The jobs to be executed
on the Edge are expected to be short-running jobs due to
the dynamic nature of the Edge computing environment [5].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Therefore, the EFS Monitor is presented in the next section to
control the life cycle of the running jobs on an Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Monitoring and Terminating
The Monitor has two functions.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Firstly, it monitors all
running containers on an Edge node and identiﬁes inactive
ones for termination in a later stage, as shown in Algorithm 5.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
To not overload the Edge node, the monitoring process is per-
formed every two minutes (Line 20).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Each time the monitoring
process is carried out, CPU statistics of all the containers
running for at least one minute is gathered (Line 4).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The
one minute period allows clients to set up and deploy Edge
applications in the container.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
There is a 10-second interval
between the initial and updated CPU measurements for all
containers that have been running for at least one minute
(Line 9).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The CPU utilisation (in %) is obtained for all
containers that have valid CPU statistics in the key-value
stores previously and currently (Line 11).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Containers with a
utilisation of less than 10% are appended to a list of idle
containers (Lines 12-14).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Containers in the idle containers list
are queued for termination (Lines 16-19).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Algorithm 5: Stop Idle
Data: service, C, Cr, prevstats, currentstats,
percentages, idle
while service == True do
for C in Cr do
if C.uptime >= 1 minute then
prevstats[C] = get CPU stats(C);
end
wait 10s;
for C in Cr do
if C.uptime >= 1 minute then
currentstats[C] = get CPU stats(C);
end
percentages = compare stats(prevstats[],
currentstats[]);
for C in percentages[] do
if percentages[C] < 10.0 then
idle.append(C);
end
if idle.len() > 0 then
for C in idle[] do
queue for termination(C);
end
sleep 2 minutes;
end
Secondly, the Monitor stops containers in the termination
queue, either because of the Stop Idle process described above
or requested by the client directly.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
When terminating a job,
the container is stopped with a default timeout of 10 seconds
before forced termination by the SIGKILL command and
removed.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The termination request is then removed from the
termination queue and the client is notiﬁed of the successful
termination.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The complexity of Algorithm 5 is O(p) where p
is the number of active containers.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

The results will be evaluated on the amount of jobs

3) Assumptions: In this paper, we make the following four
assumptions for the experimental studies: (i) The scheduling
strategies operate for a single Edge resource.

The execution
of the scheduling strategies on multiple Edge resources will
be considered in the future.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

(ii) Each job requires the same
amount of CPU and memory resources on an Edge node.

This is assumed since we use synthetic workloads to evaluate

To change the resource allocation for

(iii) Each individual job does not execute for more

Results - The results obtained from the experimental studies
are organised as follows.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Firstly, the overheads of the schedul-
ing strategies are considered.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Next, the results for the different
scenarios considered above, namely for equal, random and
Gaussian job distributions, are presented.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The results highlight
the number of job requests of each client serviced and the per-
centage of jobs executed based on priorities by the scheduler.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
4) Overheads:
The
overheads
associated
with
each
scheduling strategy are ﬁrstly considered.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
A key contributing
factor to overheads are the database operations to manage the
job history, which increases as more entries are added to the
job history.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The overheads obtained for up to a million entries
in the job history are shown in Figure 2.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
It is immediately observed that the hybrid scheduling strat-
egy has the largest overhead of 2.8 seconds for a job history
of a million entries.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This is because the number of database
look-ups in the job history is twice when compared to the
other strategies.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The Client Fair (CF) and Priority Fair (PF)
strategies both have an overhead of approximately 1.5 seconds
(they require only a single look-up).
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The First Come First
Serve (FCFS) strategy has constant overhead of 0.015 seconds
as it retrieves the oldest entry in the job queue.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
If it is assumed that the time between scheduling jobs is
in the order of minutes, then the current overheads would not
signiﬁcantly impact scheduling.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The results above are obtained
on a single board computer, which in the experimental set up
is an Edge node.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The overheads can be reduced further if there
are additional resources available for scheduling on the edge.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
5) Scenario 1 - Equal job distribution: Figure 3a and

jobs executed based on priorities when each client makes an
equal number of job requests.

The FCFS strategy does not
schedule jobs in a fair manner as it selects the ﬁrst job request
and executes it.

If one client made a large number of requests
during the testing window, then a large proportion of jobs from
this client would be executed.

No job requests from Clients D,
E, and F were satisﬁed.

Although PL3 is the highest priority
more jobs from PL1 are executed than PL3.

text:
In relation to the client fair strategy it is observed at the end
of the testing window that an equal distribution was achieved
among all clients.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In the client fair strategy, no jobs with
priority PL3 were executed.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
If we consider the priority fair
strategy, then a larger proportion of jobs from Client A were
7


executed compared to the others; there is a steady decrease
in the number of jobs executed and no jobs from Client E or
Client F were executed.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
However, jobs with higher priorities
were executed; 50% of jobs with PL3 were executed, when
compared to the 15% and 35% of jobs with PL1 and PL2
respectively.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Both the client fair and priority fair strategy have
either not executed jobs of clients or have completely executed
jobs with certain priorities.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Considering the hybrid strategy for which it is observed
that jobs from all clients were executed and jobs with a
higher priority (PL3) have been executed in larger proportions
when compared to PL1 and PL2.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This strategy achieves the
combined beneﬁt of the client fair strategy (all clients executed

title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

6) Scenario 2 - Random job distribution: Figure 4a and
Figure 4b show the number of jobs executed and the per-
centage of jobs executed based on priorities when each client
makes a random number of job requests.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
It is observed that
there is more similarity in the outcome for different strategies.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This may be because the random pattern generated for each
client over time is the same.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In the FCFS strategy, Client A
has made more requests than other clients and hence a larger
number of jobs is executed.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

An equal percentage of jobs with different priorities have been
executed.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
This would naturally be unfair given that higher

title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Considering the client fair strategy, it is observed that the

The

Although the FCFS and client fair
strategies execute nearly equal number of jobs from all clients,

The priority
fair strategy on the other hand executes more jobs with higher

The hybrid strategy (similar to Scenario 1), shows that an

a smaller variation, and also executes more number of jobs

text:
When compared to other approaches,
the hybrid strategy is more fair for all clients and priorities.

7) Scenario 3 - Gaussian job distribution: The requests in

The client fair strategy demonstrates more fairness across

A higher
proportion of jobs with higher priorities are executed.

The hybrid strategy achieves a better balance, similar to

However, even with the

Further optimisations will

8) Summary: It is observed that EFS is suitable for hard-
ware limited Edge resources since there are negligible over-
heads for up to a 100,000 past job entries.

For a million job

RELATED WORK
Scheduling is commonly explored in distributed systems to
ﬁnd a mapping between job requests and resources.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
Numerous
strategies are proposed for clusters [12], clouds [13], and
more recently for cloud-edge (Fog) systems [14].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The aims
of scheduling are load balancing [24], maximising resource
utilisation [25] and energy efﬁciency [26], optimising execu-
tion costs [27], and maximising performance [28].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The need for scheduling arises when services need to be
successfully ofﬂoaded.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In edge computing research, services
can be ofﬂoaded either from the user devices to the edge or
from the cloud to the edge [4].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In the case of ofﬂoading from
user devices to edge resources, there is recent research that
develops mathematical models for reducing the job response
time, which is deﬁned as the time between releasing a job to
an edge node and the arrival of results on the user-device [29].
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The scheduling strategies required for ofﬂoading from the
user devices to the edge is vastly different from ofﬂoading
services from the cloud to the edge.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
The assumptions are
different in both cases.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
For example, it is unlikely that the
same user device would need to ofﬂoad multiple jobs at the
same time.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

text:
In the research presented in this paper, the focus
is on the scheduling strategy required when ofﬂoading occurs
from the cloud to the edge.
title: Priority-based Fair Scheduling Edge Computing

Comparisons and Evaluations
Qiheng Zhou1, Minxian Xu*1, Sukhpal Singh Gill2, Chengxi Gao1,
Wenhong Tian3, Chengzhong Xu1,4, and Rajkumar Buyya5
1Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, China

Abstract—Cloud Computing paradigm has revolutionized IT
industry and be able to offer computing as the ﬁfth utility.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
With the pay-as-you-go model, cloud computing enables to offer
the resources dynamically for customers anytime.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Drawing the
attention from both academia and industry, cloud computing is
viewed as one of the backbones of the modern economy.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
However,
the high energy consumption of cloud data centers contributes to
high operational costs and carbon emission to the environment.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Therefore, Green cloud computing is required to ensure energy
efﬁciency and sustainability, which can be achieved via energy
efﬁcient techniques.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
One of the dominant approaches is to apply
energy efﬁcient algorithms to optimize resource usage and energy
consumption.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Currently, various virtual machine consolidation-
based energy efﬁcient algorithms have been proposed to reduce
the energy of cloud computing environment.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
However, most
of them are not compared comprehensively under the same
scenario, and their performance is not evaluated with the same
experimental settings.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
This makes users hard to select the
appropriate algorithm for their objectives.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
To provide insights
for existing energy efﬁcient algorithms and help researchers to
choose the most suitable algorithm, in this paper, we compare
several state-of-the-art energy efﬁcient algorithms in depth from
multiple perspectives, including architecture, modelling and met-
rics.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
In addition, we also implement and evaluate these algorithms
with the same experimental settings in CloudSim toolkit.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
The
experimental results show the performance comparison of these
algorithms with comprehensive results.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Finally, detailed discus-
sions of these algorithms are provided.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Index Terms—Cloud Computing, Data Centers, Energy Efﬁ-
cient Algorithms, Virtual Machine Consolidation, QoS
I.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
INTRODUCTION
The emergence of cloud computing has contributed the
computing resources as a new utility, like electricity and
gas, and shaped the way how IT resources can be used by
customers.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Since its emergence, cloud computing has devel-
oped rapidly into one of the backbones of modern economy.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Cloud consumers including government, research institutes
and industry enterprises have all embraced and beneﬁted from

cloud computing signiﬁcantly.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Cloud computing also enables
new business to be established within a short time, facilitates
the expansion of enterprise globally, accelerates the progress
of scientiﬁc research, and promotes the creation of various
models and applications.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Cloud service providers are also
offering a variety of cloud services for customers with on-
demand access to resources based on the pay-as-you-go model
[1] [2] [3].
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text: The infrastructure of cloud computing is cloud data centers.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Currently, various cloud providers, including Amazon, Google,
Microsoft, establish large-scale cloud data centers to fulﬁll the
resources and services demands for customers.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
To ensure the
availability and reliability, cloud data centers are required to be
running 24/7.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Nowadays, the majority of data centers spread
of 300-4500 square meters containing hundreds to thousands
of physical machines.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
A typical data center can consume up
to 25,000 KWh per day.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
It is estimated that US data centers
can consume 140 million kWh by 2020, which equals to 50
coal-based power plants.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
It is also claimed that the carbon
footprint will reach 2-3% of global emission [4].
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
To relieve
the huge energy consumption and carbon emission, energy
efﬁcient techniques are required in cloud data centers [5] [6]
[7].
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Virtualization technology is an important part of green
cloud data centers to support energy efﬁciency via Virtual
Machine (VM) consolidation, where a VM is the software
implementation of a computer that running with an operating
system and applications [2].
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
VM consolidation is referred as
the process the VMs can be reallocated from one physical
machine to another without affecting the execution of users’
requests.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
VM consolidation has been identiﬁed as one of
the dominant energy efﬁcient solutions to reduce the energy
consumption of cloud data centers [5] [8].
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
As VMs are packed
on fewer physical machines via consolidation, idle physical
machines can be turned off or switched to the low-power mode
[9].
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
arXiv:2002.04860v1  [cs.DC]  12 Feb 2020


VM consolidation has been proven to be an effective
approach to reduce data center energy consumption, and
various energy efﬁcient algorithms based on VM consolida-
tion have been proposed.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
These algorithms aim to optimize
the placement of VMs to reduce the energy consumption
while ensuring other constraints, e.g.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Service Level Agreement
(SLA) violations.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Due to the uncontrolled network trafﬁc, it
is hard to conduct experiments under large-scale environment
and reproduce results.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Therefore, running experiments with
validated simulation toolkit is an acceptable and reasonable
way.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Simulation toolkit can be easily applied to construct
large-scale environment and generate reproducible results [10].
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Among all existing cloud data centers simulation toolk-
its, CloudSim [11] is the most widely used one.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
CloudSim
supports both system and behavior for cloud data centers,
including physical machines, virtual machines, workloads and
resource scheduling policies.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
The resource provisioning model
is also generic so that it can be extended with ease and
limited efforts.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
These attractive features have attracted users
from hundreds of universities and research institutes, and some
extended simulators complementing CloudSim have also been
developed, e.g.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
CloudAnalyst [12] and NetworkCloudSim
[13].
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
The motivation of this article is to analyze the problem
of rising energy consumption in depth through a comparison
of some state-of-the-art energy efﬁcient algorithms in cloud
data centers.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
This article is particularly motivated from the
following facts:
• The need and demand for understanding existing VM-
based energy efﬁcient algorithms for cloud data centers.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
• The proposed algorithms were evaluated in different
scenarios and conﬁgurations, thus their advantage and
disadvantage are not carefully examined.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
• The requirement for selecting the best suitable algorithm
based on different priorities.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
In
this
paper,
we
select
various
well-known
VM
consolidation-based energy efﬁcient algorithms and implement
experiments using CloudSim toolkit.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
The evaluated algorithms
are picked from state-of-the-art energy efﬁcient algorithms that
have shown good performance in energy efﬁciency.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
The main contributions of this work are as follows:
• Offering a cross-sectional view of the investigated VM
consolidation-based energy efﬁcient algorithms, which
present outstanding performance in cloud computing area.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
• Presenting a uniﬁed simulation-based analysis framework
based on CloudSim that allows evaluation and compari-
son of energy-efﬁcient VM consolidation algorithms in a
uniﬁed and unbiased way.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
• Discussing the advantages and disadvantages of the in-
vestigated algorithms to provide suggested algorithms for
different scenarios.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
The rest of the paper is organized as: We provide an
overview on VM consolidation-based energy efﬁcient algo-
rithm for cloud computing in Section 2.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
The investigated
algorithms are introduced in Section 3.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Section 4 discusses
the modelling of the investigated algorithms, and the adopted
metrics in the investigated algorithms are summarized in
Section 5.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Section 6 shows the performance comparison of
the investigated algorithms.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Finally, conclusions and future
research trends are given.

text:
Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms in Clouds
A few articles have conducted surveys or taxonomies on
energy efﬁcient algorithms based on VM consolidation for
cloud data centers.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
[14] introduced a survey
on resource management in cloud environment, and discussed
VM consolidation-based energy efﬁcient algorithms from
cloud management system level.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
[2] presented a
comprehensive survey for energy efﬁcient scheduling approach
in clouds, and compared some consolidation-based techniques,
including VM consolidation-based approach.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
[15] conducted a survey on techniques for improving the
energy efﬁciency for large-scale distributed systems, and sur-
veyed on VM migration algorithms for Clouds.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
[5]
proposed a taxonomy for sustainable cloud computing and
introduced a taxonomy for VM consolidation-based algorithms
without focusing on energy efﬁciency.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
[16] intro-
duced a survey on VM allocation in cloud data centers from

text:
[17] conducted a survey on VM migration
and server consolidation framework for cloud data centers, in

text:
However, these surveys and taxonomy focused on the

formance under experimental environments.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Thus, our work
advances the previous works by evaluating the state-of-the-
art algorithms not only from modelling perspective but also
with experimental comparisons.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
It also identiﬁes the merits
and demerits of investigated algorithms to provide suggestions
for research in related areas.

Beloglazov et al.

energy and SLA efﬁcient consolidation of VMs in cloud data

text:
[22] proposed a novel dynamic VM
consolidation approach based on Ant Colony Optimization to
reduce the energy consumption of data centers.

text:
In the performance evaluation of these algorithms, MBFD
has been evaluated as the baseline, however, these algorithms


are not compared and evaluated together, thus it is hard to

In this paper, we aim to compare
these algorithms in depth and evaluate them under the same
conﬁgurations to show the performance comparison.

• To ensure the evaluation results reproducible, the algo-
rithms were implemented in CloudSim or can be easily
evaluated in CloudSim.

• To make the algorithm comparable, the algorithms should
have been evaluated with the same baseline.

text:
MBFD
Modiﬁed Best Fit Decreasing (MBFD) [18] aims to reduce
the energy consumption of data centers while ensuring SLA.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
It solves the VM initial placement phase by regarding it as
a bin packing problem.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
MBFD is designed to assign the
VMs to the hosts that produce the minimum incrementation
of energy consumption.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
In the VM consolidation phase, the
algorithm optimizes the VM allocation via consolidation for
better energy efﬁciency, the target host is also selected as in the
initial placement.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
The motivation of the proposed algorithm
is due to the uncertainty of task lifecycles, some VMs are
likely to host an over-provisioned of applications while others
run with low resource utilization.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Unbalanced workloads in
cloud data centers result in a severe waste of resources and
performance degradation.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
The VM consolidation in this work
is a proactive process and can be applied with heterogeneous
workloads.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
MBFD has been evaluated as the baseline for many VM
consolidation-based energy efﬁcient algorithm.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
Various recent
algorithms were proposed to improve the performance of
this algorithm.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
The advantage of this algorithm is that it
considers the trade-offs between the reduced energy and SLA
violation and it is easy to implement.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
The limitation is that it
does not consider the holistic resource management, which is
complemented by recent research.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
EcoCloud
EcoCloud [19] is an energy efﬁcient scheduling policy
based on probabilistic procedures.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations

text:
VM assignment and VM
migration are the two phases in the algorithm.
title: Energy Efﬁcient Algorithms based Consolidation Cloud Computing: Comparisons Evaluations
