4
Experiments and Results
In this section, we introduce our seven benchmark tasks, strategies for generating the required
memory addresses, explain the experimental setup, and present our results.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
4.1
Benchmark Tasks
We evaluate reservoir memory machines (RMMs) on the following seven benchmark tasks:
latch [Paaßen and Schulz, 2020]
The input is a one-dimensional time series of length
9-200 that is always zero except for ones at 3 random time points.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
The desired output is zero
until the ﬁrst one in the input, where it switches to one, then back to zero at the next one,
and back to one at the third one.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
copy [Collier and Beel, 2018]
The input is a nine-dimensional time series of 1-20 random
vectors from {0, 1}8 on the ﬁrst eight channels, followed by zeros.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
The last input channel is
zero except for a one right before and after the input vectors.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
The desired output is a copy
of the ﬁrst eight channels as in Theorem 3.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
repeat copy [Collier and Beel, 2018]
The input is a nine-dimensional time series of 1-10
random vectors from {0, 1}8 on the ﬁrst eight channels, followed by zeros.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
The desired output
are 1 −10 copies of the ﬁrst eight input channels.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
Each copy is preceded by a one on the last
input channel, which is zero otherwise.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
associative recall [Collier and Beel, 2018]
The input is a seven-dimensional time series
with 2-6 random blocks á 3 random vectors from {0, 1}6 on the ﬁrst six channels, followed
by a one on the seventh channel and then a random repeated block from the previous input.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

dom wavelets of length 256 on the ﬁrst channel, followed by 1-10 blocks of 256 zeros each.

On the second channel, each block of 256 time steps ends with one of two marker wavelets
of length 32.

marker (one or two) otherwise.

FSMs
For ﬁnite state machine learning we construct Moore machines with Σ = Γ =
{(1, 0)T , (0, 1)T }, Q = {1, 2, 3, 4} and randomly sampled transition as well as output func-
tions.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
As training data, we construct all sequences with exactly one repeated state in the
Moore machine as suggested in Theorem 2.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
The test data consists of much longer sequences
of length 256 over Σ and the output the Moore machine would predict.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
We note that, among these tasks, only latch and FSM can be solved straightforwardly with
Moore machines.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
Copy, repeat copy, image recall, and associative recall require exponentially
many states by the same argument as in Theorem 3, and smooth associative recall is not
solvable with a Moore machine because there are inﬁnitely many smooth wavelets that could
be generated.

4.2
Generating Memory Addresses
To train RMMs, we require example memory address sequences for the training data.

text:
The
optimal strategy for such example address sequences depends on the task.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
We generally
recommend the following strategies:
For tasks with discrete and abstract outputs such as latch, we suggest to apply a clustering
on the target outputs.

More speciﬁcally, for latch the memory address sequence becomes the
training output +1 (i.e.

copy and repeat copy, we suggest to use the state sequence 1, .

equivalent to the proof of Theorem 3.

recall we suggest to store the state after each block in memory and load it when recalling
the block.

4.3
Experimental Setup
We use a standard RMM with 64 neurons for latch, smooth associative recall, and FSM
learning, a standard RMM with 256 neurons for copy and repeat copy, a standard RMM
with 512 neurons for image recall, and an associative RMM with 256 neurons for associative
recall.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
We compare against echo state networks [Jaeger and Haas, 2004, ESN] without an
external memory and the same number of neurons.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
We compare three kinds of reservoir,
namely Gaussian random numbers normalized to a spectral radius < 1 (rand), cycle reservoirs
with jumps [Rodan and Tiňo, 2012, CRJ], and Legendre delay networks [Voelker et al., 2019,
LDN].
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
In each case we optimize the reservoir hyperparameters via random search with 20
trials and 3 repeats per trial.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
An exception is the time horizon T of a Legendre delay network
because it follows logically from the task, namely the time series length for latch, 20 for copy,
10 for repeat copy, 6 · 3 for associative recall, 256 for smooth associative recall, 28 for image
recall, and 4 for FSMs.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
For RMMs, we add the kernel of the SVM classiﬁers (linear or RBF
with automatic bandwidth choice) to the hyperparameters to be trained.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
On the ﬁrst four tasks, we additionally compare against deep learning models with the
same number of neurons, namely a gated recurrent unit [Cho et al., 2014, GRU], and a deep
version of our reservoir memory machine with a GRU as a recurrent controller (GRU-MM),
a softmax state classiﬁer, and linear output.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
We train this GRU-MM to minimize the mean
squared error on the output plus the crossentropy loss on the state predictions.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
We train the
deep models with an ADAM optimizer with learning rate 10−3, weight decay of 10−8, and
minibatch size of 32.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text: We stop the training after 1000 minibatches or if the loss is below 10−3.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text: All models are trained on 90 training sequences and 10 test sequences from the data sets.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text: We repeat all experiments 20 times for the reservoir models and 3 times for the deep models.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
All experiments were performed on a desktop PC with Intel core i9-10900 CPU and 32 GB
RAM.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
All experimental source code and reference implementations are available at https://gitlab.com/bpaass

5
Conclusion
We introduced a novel reservoir memory machine (RMM) architecture which extends echo
state networks with an external memory and thereby becomes computationally strictly more
powerful than ﬁnite state machines, whereas contractive echo state networks cannot recognize
some regular languages.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
In addition to these theoretical results, we showed that RMMs can
solve several benchmark tasks of diﬀerentiable neural computers which are out of reach for
standard recurrent neural networks.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
These successes require a sacriﬁce, namely that examples
of memory access behavior need to be supplied as part of the training data.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
Future research
should investigate how optimal memory access behavior can instead be learned from data,
perhaps via heuristics.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

text:
Still, our model makes neural computation much more eﬃcient to train,
requiring both less time and less training data compared to diﬀerentiable neural computers.
title: arXiv:2009.06342v2  [cs.LG]  19 Jul 2021

ABSTRACT
Executing complex, burst-parallel, directed acyclic graph
(DAG) jobs poses a major challenge for serverless execution
frameworks, which will need to rapidly scale and schedule
tasks at high throughput, while minimizing data movement
across tasks.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We demonstrate that, for serverless parallel com-
putations, decentralized scheduling enables scheduling to be
distributed across Lambda executors that can schedule tasks
in parallel, and brings multiple benefits, including enhanced
data locality, reduced network I/Os, automatic resource elas-
ticity, and improved cost effectiveness.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We describe the im-
plementation and deployment of our new serverless parallel
framework, called Wukong, on AWS Lambda.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We show that
Wukong achieves near-ideal scalability, executes parallel
computation jobs up to 68.17× faster, reduces network I/O
by multiple orders of magnitude, and achieves 92.96% tenant-
side cost savings compared to numpywren.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Serverless computing enables a new way of build-
ing and scaling applications and services by allowing devel-
opers to break traditionally monolithic server-based appli-
cations into finer-grained cloud functions.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Developers write
function logic while the service provider performs the noto-
riously tedious tasks of provisioning, scaling, and managing
the backend servers that the functions run on [38].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Serverless computing solutions are growing in popularity
and finding their way into both commercial clouds (e.g., AWS
Lambda, Google Cloud Functions, and Azure Functions) and
open source projects (e.g., OpenWhisk).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
While serverless
platforms were originally intended for event-driven, state-
less applications [1], a recent trend is the use of serverless
computing for more complex, stateful, parallel applications.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Some types of compute- and data-intensive applications
are inherently parallelizable and can be structured as a di-
rected acyclic graph (DAG) of short, fine-grained tasks [2, 36,
39, 49].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The large-scale parallelism and auto-scaling services
provided by serverless platforms makes them well-suited
for such kinds of burst-parallel fine-grained tasks that char-
acterize DAG-based parallel computation workflows.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Burst-
parallel applications include data analytics [39], optimization
algorithms [13], and real-time machine learning classifica-
tions such as support vector machines (SVM) [20, 33, 55];
these applications typically demand low-latency schedul-
ing [49] with large-scale parallelism [26].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
FaaS providers charge function execution time at a fine
granularity – AWS Lambda bills on a per-invocation basis.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Workloads with short tasks can take advantage of this
fine-grained pay-per-use pricing model to keep monetary
costs low.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Consequently, serverless computing can be lever-
aged by next-generation, burst-parallel workloads in high-
performance computing (HPC) and data analytics.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Migrating such applications from a traditional serverful
deployment to a serverless platform presents unique oppor-
tunities.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Traditional serverful deployments rely on existing
workflow management frameworks such as MapReduce [34],
Apache Spark [54], Sparrow [49], and Dask [9] to provide

The scheduler dispatches ready tasks to Lambda ex-

the queued tasks.

text:
In (b), task scheduling is performed by a fleet of Lambda
executors that schedule and execute their assigned tasks
in parallel and cooperate to ensure that task dependen-
cies are satisfied.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Intermediate task inputs and outputs may
be stored inside the executors, which increases data local-
ity.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This approach also enables fine-grained and automatic
Lambda resource elasticity, as Lambda executors finish as-
signed tasks and return (e.g., Lambda 2).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
a logically centralized scheduler for managing task assign-
ments and resource allocation.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The scheduler traditionally
has various objectives, including load balancing, maximizing
cluster utilization, ensuring task fairness, and so on.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
However,
a traditional serverful scheduler is not required by serverless
computing.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This is because: (1) FaaS providers are responsi-
ble for managing the “servers” (i.e., where the task executors
are hosted); and (2) serverless platforms typically provide a
nearly unbounded amount of ephemeral resources.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
As a result,
a hypothetical serverless parallel computing framework may
not necessarily care about traditional “scheduling”-related
metrics (such as load balancing and cluster utilization), since
the framework has no control over where tasks are executed.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
(The service provider, of course, cares about these metrics.)
Yet, designing an efficient serverless-oriented parallel com-
puting framework introduces unique challenges.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
First, while
serverless platforms (e.g., AWS Lambda) promise to offer
superior elasticity and auto-scaling properties, the serverless
invocation model imposes non-trivial scheduling overhead.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Unlike a typical serverful parallel framework where the cen-
tral scheduler directly communicates with each worker pro-
cess using TCP [3, 34], in a serverless setup, the scheduler
can dispatch tasks to serverless workers in one of three ways.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Figure 1(a) depicts a high-level overview of all three meth-
ods.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In method #1, the scheduler invokes a Lambda func-
tion (using the HTTP protocol) to dispatch the task code
and execute the task.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Note that with this method, there is a
one-to-one association between tasks and Lambda functions.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Given an average invocation overhead of 50 ms (typical for
AWS Lambda functions), the scheduler could quickly become
a performance bottleneck, especially for large and complex
jobs with thousands of tasks.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
These observations indicate
that a naive attempt to simply port an existing serverful
DAG framework to serverless computing will be unsuccess-
ful.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In order to create a performant, cost-effective serverless
DAG engine, new techniques must be developed to fully take
advantage of the characteristics of the serverless platform.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In method #2, the scheduler launches short-lived1 Lambda
executors as workers that establish TCP connections with the
scheduler and receive RPC requests for task processing.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Ex-
ample frameworks include ExCamera [37] and PyWren [42].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Task executors within these frameworks may execute several
tasks as opposed to just one as with the first method.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Similarly, in method #3, the scheduler places tasks in a
shared work queue.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
These tasks are retrieved from the queue
by serverless executors; state-of-the-art systems such as
numpywren [52] launch stateless Lambda executors that
connect to a centralized shared queue and constantly re-
trieve tasks from the queue.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Frameworks using this method
may have a component separate from the central scheduler
that is responsible for invoking the AWS Lambda executors.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text: This is sometimes referred to as a “provisioner”.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In the latter
two approaches, as shown in Figure 1(a), a tightly synchro-
nized central scheduler tracks all task completions, updates
all task dependencies, and identifies any ready tasks.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The
scheduler dispatches ready tasks to Lambda executors, or the
scheduler deposits ready tasks into a shared work queue, and
a pool of Lambda executors contend for the queued tasks.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Intermediate task inputs and outputs are stored externally,
which reduces data locality.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The second challenge is that serverless platforms come
with inherent constraints, including bandwidth-limited, out-
bound only network connectivity; therefore, serverless work-
flows must rely on external cloud store for intermediate data
storage and exchange, which creates excessive data move-
ment overhead.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Data locality enhancement is thus critical
for minimizing communication costs.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing
Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing
SoCC ’20, October 19–21, 2020, Virtual Event, USA
however, these solutions do not fully address the aforemen-
tioned performance issues of efficient scheduling and data lo-
cality, which leads to long scale-out delays, sub-optimal per-
formance, and higher monetary cost.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
To this end, we design
and build a new serverless parallel computing framework
called Wukong2.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong is a serverless-oriented, decen-
tralized, locality-aware, and cost-effective parallel computing
framework.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The key insight of Wukong is that partitioning
the work of a centralized scheduler (i.e., tracking task comple-
tions, identifying and dispatching ready tasks, etc.) across a
large number of Lambda executors, can greatly improve perfor-
mance by permitting tasks to be scheduled in parallel, reducing
resource contention during scheduling, and making task sched-
uling data locality-aware, with automatic resource elasticity
and improved cost effectiveness.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Scheduling is decentralized by partitioning a DAG into
multiple, possibly overlapping, subgraphs.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Each subgraph is
assigned to a task Executor (implemented as an AWS Lambda
function runtime) that is responsible for scheduling and exe-
cuting tasks in its assigned subgraph.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This decentralization
brings multiple key benefits:
Enhanced data locality and reduced resource contention:
Decentralization improves the data locality of scheduling.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Unlike PyWren [42] and numpywren [52], which require
executors to perform network I/Os to obtain each task they
execute (since numpywren’s task executor is completely
stateless), Wukong preserves task dependency information
on the Lambda side.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This allows Lambda executors to cache
intermediate data and schedule the downstream tasks in their
subgraph locally, i.e., without constant remote interaction
with a centralized scheduler.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Harnessing scale and local optimization opportunities:
Decentralizing scheduling allows an Executor to make lo-
cal data-aware scheduling decisions about the level of task
granularity (or parallelism) appropriate for its subgraph.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Ag-
ile executors can scale out compute resources in the face of
burst-parallel workloads by partitioning their subgraphs into
smaller graphs that are assigned to other executors for an
even higher level of parallel task scheduling and execution.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Alternately, an executor can execute tasks locally, when the
cost of data communication between the tasks outweighs
the benefit of parallel execution.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Automatic resource elasticity and improved cost effec-
tiveness: Decentralization does not require users to explic-
itly tune the number of active Lambdas running as workers
and thus is easier to use, more cost effective, and more re-
source efficient.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text: We make the following contributions in this paper.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
• We thoroughly explore the problem space of serverless
parallel computing framework design.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For a range of
2https://mason-leap-lab.github.io/Wukong
parallel computation applications, we identify issues of
the state-of-the-art serverless frameworks—task sched-
uling, data locality, and resource efficiency (monetary
cost effectiveness).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
• We present the design and implementation of Wukong,
a new serverless parallel computing framework that
solves the identified issues.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong synergizes a set
of optimization techniques, including decentralized
scheduling, task clustering, and delayed I/O.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
These
techniques together achieve near-ideal scalability, re-
duce data movement over the network, enhance data
locality, and improve cost effectiveness.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text: • We evaluated Wukong extensively on AWS.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Our re-
sults show that Wukong reduces network I/O by many
orders of magnitude and achieves up to 68.17× higher
performance than numpywren, while reducing the
monetary cost by as much as 92.96%.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
2
BACKGROUND AND MOTIVATION
2.1
Why Serverless?
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Serverless Computing handles virtually all system admin-
istration tasks, making it easier for developers to use a near-
infinite amount of cloud resources, including bundled CPUs
and memory, object stores, and a lot more [43].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Service
providers provide a flexible interface for defining serverless
functions, which allows developers to focus on core appli-
cation logic.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Service providers in turn auto-scale function
executions in a demand-driven fashion, hiding tedious server
configuration and management tasks from the users.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Service providers
place limits on the use of cloud resources to simplify resource
management.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Take AWS Lambda for example: users config-
ure Lambda’s memory and CPU resources in a bundle.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Users
can choose a memory capacity between 128MB–3008MB in
64MB increments.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Lambda will then allocate CPU power
linearly in proportion to the amount of memory configured.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Each Lambda function can run at most 900 seconds and will
be forcibly stopped when the time limit is reached.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In addi-
tion, Lambda only allows outbound TCP network connec-
tions and bans inbound connections and the UDP protocol.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Running large-scale, burst-parallel compu-
tation jobs has long been challenging for domain scien-
tists due to the complexity of configuring, provisioning, and
managing compute clusters [17, 18].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
By taking over system
administration and automatically providing capability to
launch thousands of processes with no advance notice, the
emerging serverless computing model seems to provide a
foundation that will attract domain scientists and data an-
alysts.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
However, to fully unleash the potential of serverless
computing, an efficient serverless-optimized parallel comput-
ing framework is needed.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
2.2
Challenges
We build on our experience with serverless frameworks to
synthesize the performance requirement for an ideal, server-
less, parallel computing framework, and discuss why current
solutions are not able to meet these performance require-
ments of burst-parallel applications at both the task schedul-
ing and the data locality level.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
A family of burst-parallel
computation jobs (e.g., data analytics [49], machine learning
classifications [20], etc.) are dominated by short-lived tasks
with a span ranging from hundreds of milliseconds (ms) to
tens of seconds [39, 42, 49, 55].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Such applications pose a dif-
ficult scheduling challenge to the serverless computing plat-
forms.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This is because, while serverless computing promises
to deliver elastic auto-scaling feature in response to bursts
of concurrent workloads, serverless function invocations
incur non-negligible overhead, thus creating a scheduling
bottleneck with slow scaling out.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text: PyWren is a state-of-the-art serverless execution engine [42].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
PyWren enables users to program MapReduce-like applica-
tions on serverless platforms such as AWS Lambda.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Numpy-
wren [52] is a system for linear algebra built on top of Py-
Wren.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Numpywren uses PyWren’s existing infrastructure
to deploy their own serverless task executors, which run
as a user-defined function within PyWren’s own Lambda
executors.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In order for numpywren to scale the size of their
Lambda cluster, numpywren invokes additional PyWren ex-
ecutors (using PyWren’s own API) from their central sched-
uler.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Based on this design, numpywren relies heavily on
PyWren for Lambda scaling and management.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Figure 2 shows PyWren’s ability to schedule large num-
bers of no-op tasks on AWS Lambda-based executors.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Ideally,
an omniscient serverless scheduler should be able to take
full advantage of the massive parallelism offered by server-
less computing and rapidly scale to thousands of Lambda
executors in seconds in response to bursty, highly parallel
workloads.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
PyWren uses a centralized scheduling approach,
where it employs 64 threads for task scheduling and invoca-
tion; it takes almost 2 minutes to scale out to 10, 000 Lambda
executors3.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
To make it worse, a serverless framework like
3As did in [37], we also performed warmup operations to make sure each
Lambda invocation does not incur a cold start [22].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
PyWren cannot always keep thousands of Lambda execu-
tors actively running (unlike the worker servers to a typical
serverful parallel framework such as MapReduce [34]), so
it has to constantly invoke many Lambdas in response to
bursts of job tasks.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This serves to illustrate the failure of existing serverless
execution frameworks to fully utilize serverless computing’s
elastic auto-scaling property.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Parallel applications require intermediate data
exchange among tasks.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Direct task-to-task data communica-
tion is naturally supported in traditional serverful parallel
computing frameworks such as MPI [18], MapReduce [34],
and Dask [9].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
However, data exchange in serverless applica-
tions may be supported only indirectly, through the use of
remote cloud storage systems.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Consider the data exchanged during the execution of 25𝑘×
25𝑘GEMM (general matrix multiplication) and 8, 192𝑘× 128
TSQR (tall skinny QR) on numpywren.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Figure 3 and Figure 4
present a comparison between pure input and output sizes
and the amount of data transferred during the two workloads
respectively.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For GEMM, the total quantity of data read is
more than 25× the size of the input data while the total
quantity of data written is more than 20× the size of the
output.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text: This trend is further exemplified by TSQR.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
While
the amount of data read is only 2.88× greater than the input
data size, the amount of data written over 65𝑀× greater than
the output size.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This is because numpywren and PyWren
adopt a stateless Lambda executor design where a task can
be dispatched to any Lambda executor; once dispatched to a
Lambda, the task simply performs the following four steps: 1)
reads its input data (the intermediate data generated by one
or multiple upstream tasks) from cloud storage (numpywren
uses S3), 2) performs computation, 3) writes the intermediate
results (as output) to the cloud storage, and 4) returns.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
While
the stateless design seems to be a good fit for serverless
platforms, it does not preserve data locality, which results in
excessive data movement.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This stresses a strong need for reducing data movement and
increasing data locality in serverless frameworks.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

3.1
High-Level Design
Figure 5 shows the high-level design of Wukong.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The de-
sign consists of three major components: a static schedule
generator which runs on Amazon EC2, a pool of Lambda
Executors, and a storage cluster.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Scheduling in Wukong is decentralized and uses a combi-
nation of static and dynamic scheduling.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
A static schedule
is a subgraph of the DAG.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Each static schedule is assigned
to a separate Executor.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
An Executor uses dynamic sched-
uling to enforce the data dependencies of the tasks in its
static schedule.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
An Executor can invoke additional Execu-
tors to increase task parallelism, or cluster tasks to eliminate
any communication delay between them.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Executors store
intermediate task results in an elastic in-memory key-value
storage (KVS) cluster (hosted using AWS Fargate [5]; see
§3.4) and job-related metadata (e.g., counters) in a separate
KVS that we call metadata store (MDS).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
3.2
Static Scheduling
Wukong users submit a Python computing job to the DAG
generator, which uses the Dask library to convert the job
into a DAG.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The Static-Schedule Generator generates static
schedules from the DAG.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For a DAG with 𝑛leaf nodes, 𝑛static
schedules are generated.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
A static schedule for leaf node L
contains all of the task nodes that are reachable from L and
all of the edges into and out of these nodes.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The data for
a task node includes the task’s code and the KVS keys for
the task’s input data.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The schedule for L is easily computed
using a depth-first search (DFS) that starts at L.

text: Figure 6(a) shows a DAG with two leaf nodes.

text:
Figure 6(b)
shows the two static schedules that are generated from the
DAG: Schedule 1 (blue) and Schedule 2 (green).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
A static schedule contains three types of operations: task
execution, fan-in and fan-out.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
To simplify our description,
when DAG task Tx is followed immediately by task Ty, and
Tx (Ty) has no fan-out (fan-in), we add a trivial fan-out oper-
ation between Tx and Ty in the static schedule.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This fan-out
operation has one incoming edge from Tx and one outgoing
edge to Ty, i.e., there is no actual fan-out.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In Figures 6(a) and
(b), this is the case for DAG tasks T2 and T3.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
A fan-in task T may depend on tasks that will be executed
by different Executors, e.g., task T4 in Figure 6.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The dynamic
scheduling technique described below ensures that T’s data
dependencies are satisfied and that T is executed by only
one Executor.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Note also that a static schedule does not map
its tasks to processors; this mapping is done automatically
by the AWS Lambda platform when an Executor function
instance is invoked with the static schedule and placed on a
VM by AWS Lambda.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
3.3
Task Execution & Dynamic Scheduling
Task Execution.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong workflow execution starts when
the static scheduler’s Initial-Executor Invokers assign each
static schedule produced by the Static-Schedule Generator
to a separate Executor.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Recall that each static schedule be-
gins with one of the leaf node tasks in the DAG.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The Initial-
Executor invokes these "leaf node" Executors in parallel.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Af-
ter executing its leaf node task, each Executor then executes

the tasks along a single path through its schedule.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
An Ex-
ecutor may execute a sequence of tasks before it reaches a
fan-out operation with more than one out edge or it reaches
a fan-in operation.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For such a sequence of tasks, there is no
communication required for making the output of the earlier
tasks available to later tasks for input.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
All intermediate task
outputs are cached in the Executor’s local memory with in-
herently enhanced data locality.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Executors also look ahead
to see what data their tasks may need, which allows them to
discard data in their local memory that is no longer needed.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Furthermore, Executors can increase parallelism by sched-
uling and invoking new Executors to execute the task targets
of a fan-out.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
A group of Executors that reach a common fan-
in node decrease parallelism by scheduling one of them to
execute the fan-in task and the rest to stop.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong uses
dynamic scheduling to resolve conflict on the fly.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
More im-
portantly, this dynamic scheduling of the tasks in an Executor’s
static schedule leads to a decentralized scheduling model that
naturally fits serverless computing, eliminates the need for a
centralized scheduler processes that check data dependencies
and invoke ready tasks with improved scalability.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text: Dynamic Scheduling for Fan-Out Operations.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For fan-
out operations there are two cases:
Case 1: none of the 𝑛(where 𝑛> 1) fan-out edges is a fan-in
edge.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Then E “becomes” the Executor for one of the fan-out’s
tasks, say T, by executing T, and E “invokes” an Executor for
the other fan-out tasks.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Case 2: one or more of the fan-out edges is also a fan-in
edge.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For example, fan-out node 3 in Figure 6(a) has a fan-
out edge that is a fan-in edge to node 4.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The selection of a
“becomes” edge for E is based on the immediate availability
of the tasks targeted by the fan-out edges.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
If no task target’s
dependencies are satisfied then no task target is immediately
available for execution and none of the fan-out edges can be
selected as E’s “becomes” edge (the fan-in edges have fan-in
operations that will be executed next); otherwise, one of the
fan-out edges for the available target tasks is selected as the
“becomes” edge.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
An intermediate objects needed for input by an invoked
Executor is passed to the Executor as an argument if the size
of the object is less than the maximum allowed argument
size (256K);otherwise, the object is sent to the Storage Man-
ager, and the associated KVS keys are passed to the invoked
Executors as arguments.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Each of the𝑛−1 Executors invoked by E is assigned a static
schedule that begins with one of the 𝑛−1 fan-out edges.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Each
of these (possibly overlapping) static schedules corresponds
to a sub-graph of E’s static schedule.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Executor E continues
task execution and scheduling along the remaining fan-out
edge and executes the operation encountered on this edge.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In Figure 6(b), fan-out edges are labeled either “invokes”
or “becomes” to indicate whether the Executor invokes a
new Lambda Executor to execute a fan-out task or executes
the fan-out task itself.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Since Executor invocations, which are in the form of AWS
Lambda function invocations, incur a high overhead (e.g., in-
voking an AWS Lambda function takes about 50 milliseconds
with the Boto3 AWS Python API), we use a number of dedi-
cated Executor-Invoker processes that are co-located with
the Static Scheduler (Figure 5).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
When an Executor performs
a fan-out operation, and a large number of new Executors
must be invoked, the Executor delegates the invocations to
the Static Scheduler.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The Static Scheduler evenly distributes
task invocation responsibilities among the Invoker processes,
enabling (near-)linear speedup over sequential invocations.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text: Dynamic Scheduling for Fan-in Operations.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
If Task Ex-
ecutor E executes a fan-in operation with 𝑛(where 𝑛> 1)
in-edges, then E and the 𝑛−1 other Executors involved in
this fan-in operation cooperate to see which one of them
will continue their static schedules on the out edge of the
fan-in (e.g., node 4 in Figure 6).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For a fan-in operation executed by E for fan-in task T, E
atomically gets and updates a value in the KVS that tracks the
number of T’s input dependencies that have been satisfied
during execution There are two cases:
Case 1: all of the input dependencies of T have been satisfied.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Then E continues its static schedule by executing T
Case 2: all of the input dependencies of T have not been
satisfied.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Then E sends the intermediate object needed by T
to the Storage Manager.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In Figure 6(b), each fan-in task is labeled with the Executor
that executed the task.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Storing and retrieving large intermedi-
ate objects can be very costly.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong implements task
clustering to avoid large object storage.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
If the output
object of some fan-out task𝑇executed by Executor E is larger
than a user-defined threshold 𝑡(e.g., 200 MB), E will try to
cluster the target tasks of T’s fan-out edges, i.e., E will execute
the target tasks whose dependencies are satisfied instead of
invoking new Executors for these tasks.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For example, the
Executor that executes task C can also execute tasks F and G
to avoid the time and cost of communicating task C’s large
object output to tasks F and G.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In cases like this, the fan-out
edges will have multiple edges labeled “becomes”.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
If E executes a
fan-in operation for task T and the input dependencies of
a single task T have not been satisfied, then E sends the
intermediate object needed by T to the Storage Manager.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
If
this object is large, E then rechecks T’s input dependencies.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
If T’s input dependencies became satisfied while the large
intermediate object was being stored, E becomes the Executor
for T, This avoids the communication delay that would have
occurred when T retrieved the large object from storage, but


Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing
SoCC ’20, October 19–21, 2020, Virtual Event, USA
not the delay that occurs when R stored the object.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The delay
that occurred when the large object was stored by E can be
avoided if the storage operation can be delayed until after
T’s input dependencies become satisfied.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Suppose that when Executor E executes the fan-out oper-
ation it identifies multiple fan-out tasks that are also fan-in
tasks and that have input dependencies that are not satisfied.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
E will then execute any ready fan-out tasks it finds and delay
the decision about how to handle the fan-out tasks that are
not ready.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
(There may be many fan-out tasks that are not
also fan-in tasks or that are fan-in tasks with satisfied input
dependencies.)
Delayed I/O.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
After Executor E executes the ready tasks, E
will recheck whether the input dependencies of the unready
tasks have since become satisfied.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
If so, the newly ready tasks
can be executed.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
If at least one unready task becomes ready,
the ready task can be executed and the unready tasks can
be rechecked again, and so on, for a configurable number
of times.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Our profiling indicates that it is almost always
better to wait until all of the unready tasks become ready to
avoid the very large communication delay the occurs when
many large objects are stored and retrieved potentially at
the same time.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
A pattern of simultaneous large object writes
and reads occurred often in the DAG workloads that we
executed.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
If unready tasks remain when this process stops, E
must send the intermediate objects needed by the unready
tasks to storage; however, as described above, E can possibly
avoid the communication delay associated with retrieving
the objects from storage by checking the unready objects
one more time.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
3.4
Storage Management
Wukong’s Storage Cluster is built atop AWS Fargate [5], a
serverless container engine that can be elastically scaled out-
/in.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The Storage Cluster includes a number of AWS Fargate
tasks, each of which hosts a Redis instance, and a KV Store
Proxy Service.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The KV Store Proxy is executed within an EC2
VM along with an additional instance of Redis used exclu-
sively for storing static schedules and dependency counters.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The user can configure the size of the Fargate cluster to dy-
namically accommodate workloads of different sizes.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The
user simply specifies how many nodes they would like, and
Wukong ensures that these nodes are created and available.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The Fargate nodes are used for the storage of intermediate
data generated during a workload’s execution.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We opt to use
Redis instead of S3 as Redis can provide both high bandwidth
for large object workloads and high IOPS for small object
workloads [44, 50], whereas S3’s IOPS is throttled.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
However,
modifying Wukong to use S3 is trivial.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The KV Store Proxy performs various storage operations
on behalf of the Task Executors and the Scheduler.

title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Task Executors
publish their intermediate and final task output objects to the
KV Store.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Final outputs are relayed to a Subscriber process
in the Scheduler for presentation to the Client.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
When a Task Executor
performs a fan-out operation that has a small number of
out edges, the Task Executor makes the necessary Executor
invocations itself.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
When a fan-out has a
number of out edges that is larger than a user-specified
threshold, the Task Executor publishes a message that is
relayed to a Subscriber process in the Storage Manager that
then passes the message on to the Proxy.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This message con-
tains an ID that identifies the fan-out’s location in the DAG.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The Proxy uses the DAG and the fan-out ID to identify the
fan-out’s out edges in the DAG.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This allows the Proxy, with
the assistance of the Fan-out Invokers in the Storage Man-
ager, to make the necessary Task Executor invocations, in
parallel.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The Proxy passes to each Executor its intermediate
inputs (or their key values in the KV Store) and the Execu-
tor’s static schedule.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

3.5
Programming Model
Wukong reuses Dask’s Python programming interfaces [12]
(including high-level APIs, such as Dask libraries and data
structures, and low-level APIs, such as Dask.delayed) for
implementing parallel programs.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In general, any code written
for Dask should execute on Wukong.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Figure 7 shows an
example code snippet that implements tree reduction (TR)
(a detailed description of TR is in §4.1).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong also reuses
Dask’s DAG generator which translates high-level Python
code into a DAG [11].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Figure 8 depicts the DAG generated
for TR with an 8-element array.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
3.6
Fault Tolerance
For fault tolerance, we relied on the automatic retry mecha-
nism of AWS Lambda, which allows for up to two automatic
retries of failed function executions.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Investigating better fault
tolerance scheme is part of our future work.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

4
EVALUATION
Implementation.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We have implemented Wukong using
roughly 12𝑘lines of Python code (5, 349 LoC for the AWS
Lambda Executor Runtime, 3, 057 LoC for the Storage Man-
ager, and 3, 577 LoC for the Static Scheduler).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We use the Dask
library [9] to generate DAGs to use as the input computation
graph for Wukong.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
4.1
Experimental Goals and Methodology
Our evaluation was performed on AWS.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The static sched-
uler ran in an r5n.16xlarge EC2 VM.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We used a scale-out
Redis cluster (Multi-Redis) as Wukong’s intermediate stor-
age.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The Fargate nodes within the storage cluster were each
configured to have 30 GB of memory and 4 vCPUs.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For the
Multi-Redis setup, Wukong used 75 nodes for the storage
cluster, as we’ve determined this value to be both performant
and cost-effective for many workloads.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The MDS proxy was
co-located on the same r5n.16xlarge VM as a Redis instance
that was used for storing static schedules and dependency
counters.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Each Lambda function was allocated 3 GB of mem-
ory and a maximum execution time of seven minutes.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We compared the performance of Wukong against both
Dask distributed (which we refer to simply as “Dask”) and
numpywren [52] / PyWren [42].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We chose to compare our
performance against Dask as both Wukong and Dask use
the exact same input DAG and the same algorithms for their
computations.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We compared the end-to-end performance of
Wukong against numpywren, and we compared the scala-
bility of Wukong against PyWren, which is numpywren’s
underlying Lambda execution framework.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We chose to compare Wukong against numpywren be-
cause both are serverless DAG execution frameworks; how-
ever, there are significant differences between Wukong and
numpywren.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
One difference is that Wukong uses Dask DAGs,
which explicitly encode tasks and their dependencies.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Numpy-
wren, on the other hand, uses an implicit DAG representation
for its programs, which are all implemented in the LAmb-
daPACK language for linear algebra [52].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The nodes of the
DAG that represent a LAmbdaPACK program are generated
on-demand (at runtime).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Another difference is that numpywren uses AWS S3 as its
intermediate data store.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In order to make the comparison
between Wukong and numpywren more fair, we modified
numpywren to use a single instance of Redis as its interme-
diate object store.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We compared this version of numpywren,
which we refer to as “Numpywren Single Redis”, with a mod-
ified version of Wukong that also uses a single instance of
Redis for intermediate data storage.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In addition, we com-
pared numpywren S3 against “Wukong Multi-Redis”, which
uses a Fargate Redis cluster for its intermediate object store.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This second comparison was performed in order to show the
optimal performance achieved by each system.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Finally, numpywren only supports linear algebra algo-
rithms and only several of these algorithms are also available
in Dask.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
As a result, we are limited in which workloads we
can run on both Wukong and numpywren.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
To better understand Wukong’s performance, we com-
pared Wukong against 2 different Dask configurations.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Both
configurations used the same amount of CPU (2, 000 cores)
and memory (3, 000 GB memory).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This was the largest VM
cluster that we could configure.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The first configuration con-
sisted of 1, 000 2-core 3GB workers running on 125 c5.4xlarge
16-core 32 GB VMs.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing
Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The first configura-
tion was selected so that each worker was approximately as
powerful as the AWS Lambda functions used by Wukong; it
represents a worst-case scenario that stresses the Dask sched-
uler with many workers and incurs high communications
due to the lack of data locality, emulating a serverless envi-
ronment with centralized scheduling.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The second configura-
tion represents a best-case scenario where the relatively more
powerful workers could process larger data with improved
data locality and significantly reduced communications.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Additionally, we used the exact same input data partitions
for Dask and Wukong.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We scaled the problem size for each
benchmark by having each (Dask, Wukong, or numpywren)
worker assigned with (at least) one partition of the input
data.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
As such, a test used only a fraction of the 2, 000 cores
of the Dask cluster, until the problem size was large enough
to occupy all the resources.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The largest number of partitions
(of input data) used during our evaluation was 4, 096 for
16 𝑀TSQR (which will be described shortly).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This number
of partitions does not overwhelm either Dask configurations
as TSQR’s DAG features large fan-ins in the middle of the
job.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The large fan-ins result in the number of tasks allocated
to each worker decreasing as the workload progresses.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In our evaluation results, each data point is the average of
ten runs.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The error bars on the graphs of the results indicate
the biggest and smallest results obtained.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong is easy-
to-use as it exposes only two configuration knobs to the end
users—the input partition size and the number of Fargate
nodes.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
(A sensitivity analysis of these two configuration

Singular Value Decomposition (SVD): We evaluated two
variants of SVD.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The first variant (SVD1) computes the SVD
of a tall skinny matrix.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The second variant (SVD2) computes
the SVD of a square (i.e.,𝑛×𝑛) matrix using an approximation
algorithm provided by [40].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Note that Dask’s SVD algorithm
differs considerably from numpywren’s, and thus a direct
comparison between Wukong and numpywren for SVD is
impossible.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For reference, Wukong can execute SVD 256𝑘×
256𝑘in 88 seconds on average while [52] reports an average
of 77,828 seconds for the same problem size for SVD.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

learning workload.

able in the Dask-ML documentation [10].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

matrix multiplication, an important component of many lin-
ear algebra algorithms.

4.2
End-to-End Performance Comparison
TR.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text: The size of the array used for TR was 1024.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We also inten-
tionally added a delay to each task of TR.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This delay simulates
an increased amount of work performed per task.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We var-
ied the amount of delay between 0–500 ms.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Figure 9 shows
that both configurations of Dask outperforms Wukong by
a large margin for the base case.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This is because Dask uses
TCP to dispatch the 1024/2 = 512 addition tasks to work-
ers, whereas for Wukong the overhead of scaling out to 512
Lambda executors dominates.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
As we add increasing amounts
of delay to each task, the performance gap between Dask
and Wukong decrease.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Once the delay is 250 ms or more,
Wukong executes the workload faster than the 1, 000-worker
Dask cluster, as Wukong uses decentralized scheduling to
rapidly scale out to 512 workers.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This experiment shows an
interesting tradeoff between per-task execution time and
serverless scaling cost – Wukong performs best when each
task performs a non-trivial amount of work, as this compen-
sates for the overhead of spinning up additional Lambdas.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We tested seven problem sizes for both SVD1 and
SVD2 (see Figure 10 and Figure 11).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For nearly all problem
sizes, Wukong out-performed the 1, 000-worker Dask cluster,
completing the job anywhere from 62.02% to 69.09% faster
than Dask.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This performance difference results from the
benefits of Wukong’s decentralized scheduling techniques,
which greatly reduce the overhead of executing tasks on a
large number of workers.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The 1, 000-worker Dask was bot-
tlenecked by its central scheduler due to the increasing load
from the one thousand workers.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The 125-worker Dask cluster consistently outperformed
Wukong.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This is because each Dask worker is provisioned
with more resources (i.e., more CPUs, greater network band-
width, a larger amount of RAM per worker, etc.), which signif-
icantly increases data locality and reduces cross-worker com-
munications.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
More importantly, for SVD2, Wukong was able
to scale to considerably larger problem sizes than what the
1,000-worker Dask cluster was capable of handling (crosses
in Figure 11).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The results demonstrate Wukong’s ability to
provide competitive performance with traditional serverful
frameworks, while also scaling effectively for increasingly
large problem sizes.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong’s ability to scale effectively
here is largely because of its use of task clustering and de-
layed I/O.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
These techniques dramatically reduce data move-
ment and ensure all downstream tasks which depend on large
data are executed on the Task Executor that already has the
data in-memory.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
A quantitative analysis of the benefits of
these techniques is given later in §4.5.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
As with the previ-
ous benchmark, Dask was able to perform better for smaller
problem sizes; however, when we increased the problem size,
the performance gap between the two frameworks decreased.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
As the scale of the problems increased to 4.0𝑀samples and
beyond, Wukong began to scale more effectively than the
1, 000-worker Dask cluster.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Like TR, the results of our GEMM experiments iden-
tify a workload that is difficult to execute in a serverless en-
vironment.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
As shown in Figure 13, Wukong achieved worse
performance than Dask.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This is because GEMM natively re-
quires a number of large data objects to be communicated
between tasks before the computation can begin.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Due to the
limited bandwidth available to the intermediate data stor-
age, both Wukong and numpywren experience long delays
during this phase of the workload.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong’s performance greatly exceeded that of both
numpywren configurations for all problem sizes.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For the
largest problem size, Wukong (single Redis shard) executed
the workload 89.76% faster than numpywren (single Re-
dis shard).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong (with Fargate) was 51.51% faster than
numpywren (with S3) for 15𝑘×15𝑘matrices because Wukong
reduced the amount of data read from and written to the
intermediate KVS, and this reduction on I/Os directly trans-
lates to performance improvement.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
As shown in Figure 15,
Wukong read 49.39% less data than numpywren for the
smallest problem size and 45.24% for the largest; Wukong
reduced the amount of data written by as much as 85% for
the largest problem size.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Figure 14 shows that Wukong outperformed both
numpywren (with S3) and numpywren (single Redis shard)
for all problem sizes.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For the 4.1𝑀× 128 matrix, Wukong
(single Redis shard) was executing the workload 68.17×
faster, or in 98.53% less time, than numpywren (single Redis
shard); and Wukong (Fargate) is 9.19× faster, or in 89.11%
less time, than numpywren (S3).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Numpywren (single Redis
shard) failed to execute the next larger problem size, and
the largest workload numpywren (S3) was able to execute
was 16.7𝑀× 128.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For this workload, Wukong was 13.36×
faster, executing the workload in 92.51% less time.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This again,
is because of the significantly reduced reads and writes.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong’s “become” functionality allowed serial tasks along
a single subgraph path to execute locally on the same Lambda
Executor; whereas numpywren randomly assigned high pri-
ority tasks (which were ready to execute) to any stateless
Lambda executor.

Additionally, Wukong achieves faster
performance, lower cost, and more efficient CPU usage than

These results demonstrate Wukong’s pay-per-
use property.
