text:
By design, numpywren allows users to specify
the initial4 number of Lambda executors (workers) for a job.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text: We configured numpywren to use 50, 169, and 338 workers.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Numpywren-169 was selected because the maximum concur-
rency achieved by Wukong during this workload was 169
Lambdas.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We tested a scaled-out version of numpywren that
used twice as many starting workers (338) as well as a scaled-
down version using 50 workers.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Notably, numpywren-50 was
the fastest configuration, followed by numpywren-169 and
finally numpywren-338.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This suggests that increasing the
number of numpywren’s parallelism significantly increases
contention, possibly at the framework’s central queue or
scheduler, leading to performance degradation.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong was both cheaper and used less vCPUs during
the execution of the workload than all three numpywren con-
figurations.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Specifically, Wukong was 33.47% cheaper and
77.57% faster than the best-performing numpywren configu-
ration.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
More importantly, Wukong is autonomous and does
not require users to explicitly tune the parallelism, which
improves the usability.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
4One can configure the starting number of executors, a maximum number
of executors, and the policy used to scale the number of executors dynami-
cally during execution.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We opted to select the default scaling policy for all
numpywren runs.

text: Similarly, Figure 20 shows a comparison for TSQR 4.0𝑀.

The first configuration of numpywren used 128 workers
while the second used 256 workers.

These are based on the
number of leaf tasks in Wukong’s workload (512), though
we found that using 512 numpywren workers resulted in
worse performance.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong used less CPU resources and
was significantly cheaper than all other frameworks.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
It also
out-performed all other frameworks except for Dask-125.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Specifically, Wukong completed the workload in 87.41% less
time and 92.96% more cheaply than the best-performing
numpywren configuration (i.e., 14.22× cheaper and 7.94×
faster).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Lastly, while Wukong did not out-perform Dask-125,
Wukong was 95.67% cheaper than Dask-1000 and 45.70%
cheaper than Dask-125 for this workload.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong did not
reach more than 106 vCPUs during the workload’s execution
as many of the leaf tasks performed only a small amount of
work before writing their data to the KVS and exiting.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
That
is, by the time additional leaf tasks are scheduled, previously-
invoked leaf tasks were already finishing their execution,
forming a scheduling pipeline.

Elastic Scaling
We next evaluate Wukong’s scalability on traditional strong
/ weaking scaling and serverless scaling metrics, and com-
pare it against (Num)-PyWren.

text:
The maximum concurrency
we got from Amazon was 5, 000 concurrent Lambdas.

In this
experiment, for both (Num)-PyWren and Wukong, all the

title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
This is because: 1) 500-ms tasks tend to run
longer, and 2) with more Lambda executors and a fixed total
amount of tasks, each Lambda gets assigned less number of

For weak scaling, we executed ten tasks per

Notably, thanks to the decentralized
scheduling, Wukong was able to scale to 1, 000 Lambda ex-

das increased.

Finally, we test serverless scaling – ex-
ecuting 𝑁tasks on 𝑁Lambda executors, with each Lambda
effectively executing one single task.

We observe that (Num)-PyWren took an increas-

the efficacy of Wukong’s decentralized scheduling.

4.5
Factor Analysis
Task Clustering and Delay I/O.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Finally, we look at the
impact of task clustering and delaying I/O on Wukong’s
performance.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Clustering and delay I/O prevent tasks with
large intermediate data from writing their data to Redis.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Instead, these tasks attempt to execute downstream tasks
locally.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Any downstream tasks that cannot immediately be
executed because their dependencies are not satisfied are
put into a queue.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The dependencies of the queued tasks are
routinely rechecked until the dependencies are satisfied or
a maximum delay time is reached.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
By delaying I/O, more
tasks can be clustered and expensive network I/Os data can
be avoided, decreasing the workload runtime dramatically.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Figure 22 displays two aggregations of time for the activ-
ities performed for SVD2.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
In both cases, “publishing mes-
sages”, “task execution”, and “serialization/deserialization”
each took roughly the same amount of time (in aggregate);
however, the difference between the times for task invocation
and especially Redis I/O is significant.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
With the two opti-
mizations disabled, task invocations and Redis I/O made up
an aggregate 14.80 and 565.21 seconds, respectively.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
When
the optimizations were enabled, task invocation took an ag-
gregate 2.05 seconds while Redis I/O took just 20.36 seconds.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
There is 7.21× more aggregate time spent invoking tasks
and 27.76× more aggregate network I/O performed with
clustering disabled.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
We analyze Wukong’s performance by breaking down
the performance gap between a baseline and Wukong with
all optimizations enabled (Figure 23).
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
The use of the Fargate
multi-Redis storage cluster results in a 20.85% performance
improvement over using AWS ElastiCache for intermedi-
ate data storage.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
When using Fargate, the I/O performed
during the workload is spread across a large number of Re-
dis instances, resulting in reduced network contention and
consequently reduced I/O latency.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
(Using a large number of
ElastiCache instances is cost prohibitive.) When clustering
(without delayed I/O) is enabled, performance improves by
another 48.82% as a significant amount of large object I/Os is
eliminated.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Finally, enabling delayed I/O results in a 46.21%

improvement relative to the use of clustering and Fargate
alone.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Overall, Wukong is 4.6× faster when all optimizations
are used, demonstrating the effectiveness of these techniques.

text:
5
RELATED WORK
Researchers have identified new stateful parallel applica-
tions for serverless computing.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
These efforts have lead to
serverless parallel computing frameworks [6, 16, 25, 28, 30,
36, 37, 41, 42, 50, 52], which have been built using methods
2 and 3 describes in §1.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
However, none of them explicitly
addresses the data locality issue of stateful serverless parallel
applications.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong goes beyond existing work with a
novel locality-aware decentralized scheduling approach for
complex DAG jobs.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
funcX [32] is an open FaaS platform that enables high per-
formance “serverless supercomputing” over existing HPC
infrastructures.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong is orthagonal to funcX and should
be portable to existing commercial and open-source FaaS
platforms [4, 8, 15, 19, 35].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Porting Wukong to other server-
less platforms is part of our future work.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
SAND [24] is a serverless platform that increases data
locality by running some or all of the functions/tasks for a
given workload within the same container on the same server,
but as separate processes.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong is a serverless application
framework that increases data locality by executing multiple
dependent tasks in the same Wukong Executor function, and
hence in the same process, container, and server.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Thus, SAND
improves data locality in the serverless platform layer, while
Wukong improves locality in the application framework
layer running atop the serverless platform.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
InfiniCache [53] is a distributed memory cache that ex-
ploits the memory of serverless functions for object caching.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong complements InfiniCache in that Wukong can
use InfiniCache to cache intermediate data.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
General-purpose serverless orchestration frameworks in-
clude AWS Step Functions [6], Azure Durable Functions [7],
Fission Workflows [14], and HyperFlow [16, 47].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
But these
frameworks are not well-suited for supporting large, complex
jobs, because they require manual workflow configurations
(e.g., JSON) [46].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
A large body of research has explored distributed sched-
uling [27, 29, 48, 49, 51].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
However, these solutions all target
serverful scheduling with serverful deployment specific op-
timization objectives.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong targets serverless computing
and takes advantage of the massive parallelism of serverless
computing for high efficiency.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
6
DISCUSSION AND LESSONS
Wukong is not intended to replace established, serverful pro-
cessing frameworks such as Spark [54] and TensorFlow [23].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Rather, because Wukong is less powerful but easier to use
than these serverful frameworks, Wukong targets users
who lack a strong CS background, but who work on lighter-
weight and smaller computing-related problems, in areas
such as data analytics and machine learning, particularly
those whose solutions can be implemented using numerical
Python libraries.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Our initial attempt to port Dask to a serverless platform
was unsuccessful due to the poor performance of the re-
sulting framework [31].
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
There were several major bottle-
necks in this original design.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
For one, the use of a centralized
scheduler to assign tasks to Lambda executors was too slow
for all but the smallest workloads.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Specifically, the central-
ized scheduler was unable to process thousands of concur-
rent network connections with Lambda executors.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Addition-
ally, the centralized scheduler struggled to rapidly invoke
Lambda functions when scaling out for large workloads.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Fi-
nally, Lambda executors spent an overwhelming majority
of their time reading and writing intermediate data.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
[31]
presents a preliminary study about these performance bot-
tlenecks.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
To address these performance issues, we developed our
decentralized scheduling technique.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
While this technique
significantly improved performance, there were still bottle-
necks due to a lack of data locality.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Specifically, reading and
writing very large intermediate objects dominated end-to-
end execution time, particularly for workloads such as SVD.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
To address these bottlenecks, we developed task clustering
and delayed I/O.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Though these techniques have been used in
serverful contexts [29, 45], they had never been utilized in a
serverless context.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
With the addition of these two techniques,
large object reads and writes were eliminated, which greatly
improved performance and resource utilization.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
7
CONCLUSION
We have presented Wukong, a new serverless parallel com-
puting framework that uses locality-enhanced, decentral-
ized scheduling (atop AWS Lambda), task clustering, and de-
layed I/O to achieve high performance, near-ideal scalability,
and data locality while being cost-effective.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Our evaluation
demonstrates the effectiveness of decentralized scheduling,
task clustering, and delayed I/O in reducing both the execu-
tion time and cost of executing workloads.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Further, we have
shown that Wukong exhibits near-ideal scaling behavior,
reduces the execution time by as much as 98.53% compared
to numpywren, and reduces network I/O by multiple orders
of magnitude.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Finally, Wukong can reduce costs by upwards
of 92.96% and 95.67% compared to numpywren and Dask,
respectively.
title: Wukong: A Scalable and Locality-Enhanced Framework for Serverless Parallel Computing

text:
Wukong’s source code is available at:
https://mason-leap-lab.github.io/Wukong.

text:
The role of interactive super-computing in using
HPC for urgent decision making
Nick Brown1, Rupert Nash1, Gordon Gibb1, Bianca Prodan1, Max Kontak2,
Vyacheslav Olshevsky3, and Wei Der Chien3
1 EPCC, The University of Edinburgh, Bayes Centre, Edinburgh, UK
n.brown@epcc.ed.ac.uk
2 German Aerospace Center, High-Performance Computing Group, Cologne
3 KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
Abstract.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Technological advances are creating exciting new opportuni-
ties that have the potential to move HPC well beyond traditional com-
putational workloads.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
In this paper we focus on the potential for HPC to
be instrumental in responding to disasters such as wildﬁres, hurricanes,
extreme ﬂooding, earthquakes, tsunamis, winter weather conditions, and
accidents.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Driven by the VESTEC EU funded H2020 project, our re-
search looks to prove HPC as a tool not only capable of simulating dis-
asters once they have happened, but also one which is able to operate
in a responsive mode, supporting disaster response teams making urgent
decisions in real-time.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst this has the potential to revolutionise disas-
ter response, it requires the ability to drive HPC interactively, both from
the user’s perspective and also based upon the arrival of data.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
As such
interactivity is a critical component in enabling HPC to be exploited in
the role of supporting disaster response teams so that urgent decision
makers can make the correct decision ﬁrst time, every time.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Keywords: Urgent decision making, Disaster response, Interactive HPC,
VESTEC
1
Introduction
The ability to perform faster than real-time simulations of large-scale situations
is becoming a reality due to the technological advances that computing, and
speciﬁcally HPC, has enjoyed over the past decade.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This opens up a host of
opportunities including the ability to leverage HPC in the role of time-critical
decision support for unfolding emergency scenarios.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
However to do this one must
extend the state of the art in numerous ﬁelds such as in-situ HPC data analytics,
the assimilation and ingestion of data sources (e.g.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
from sensors measuring ac-
tual situational conditions), data reduction and statistical sampling for real-time
visualization.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The Visual Exploration and Sampling Toolkit for Extreme Computing (VESTEC)
project is exploring the fusion of HPC with real-time data for supporting urgent
decision makers in the role of disaster response.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
In this project we are concerned
arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020


2
N.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text: with three use-cases that drive our research in this area.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The ﬁrst one is the
spread of mosquito borne diseases, which is a major health challenge around
many parts of the world.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This spread is heavily inﬂuenced by weather and cur-
rent mosquito conditions, so being able to combine real world mosquito reports,
accurate temperature values and short range weather forecasts is critical when
simulating how the spread will progress in the short to medium term.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The second VESTEC use-case is the progression of forest ﬁres and the ability
to explore the impact of diﬀerent response scenarios.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Based on the successful
Wildﬁre Analyst application, this code is currently fed manually with data from
the ﬁeld, but this is a labour intensive process generating extra work for the
disaster response teams and inducing a time lag on information, limiting the
real-time use of this tool.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
By automating the process it will make this things
far more dynamic, reduce the load on the operators and enable a much greater
quantity of data to be exploited in the simulation of wildﬁres.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The third use-case
is that of space weather, for instance solar storms, which is very costly because
of the damage done to satellites.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst it is possible for satellites to be switched
oﬀ, thus protecting them, one needs prior warning and-so being able to ingest
the current space weather conditions and run this through simulation tools is a
very valuable proposition as it enables the estimation of risk to assets.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst these three use-cases represent very diﬀerent areas, all with novel chal-
lenges, there are a number of general similarities.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
All three involve the ingestion
of large volumes of data and, as it currently stands, all generate large volumes of
output data which is then processed oﬄine by downstream tools.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
All use-cases
involve coupled simulations where a number of distinct codes must be executed
in a speciﬁc order, for example the execution of a high resolution weather model
before feeding the results into the mosquito borne diseases simulation.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Lastly,
all models involve, to some extent, ensembles which need to be rapidly started
and stopped based on new data arriving unpredictably, and also steered by the
urgent decision maker.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
In order to fully leverage HPC for disaster response, one must embrace the
interactive nature of these workﬂows, selecting the appropriate tools and tech-
niques to support how these technologies can support emergency decision makers
in their work.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The rest of this paper is organised as follows, after brieﬂy con-
sidering related work and background in Section 2, we then explore the role of
interactivity in Section 3 by considering the three main interactivity challenges
one faces when using HPC for urgent decision making.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
In Section 4 we explore
the role of cloud computing in urgent decision making before drawing conclusions
in Section 5.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
2
Background and Related work
In Section 1 we highlighted the fact that the three VESTEC use-cases currently
write their data to disk for oﬄine processing at some later point.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
When moving
to exploiting HPC in a more real-time urgent decision responsive mode, where
operators need the results ASAP, then the overhead of IO makes this oﬄine


Role of interactive super-computing using HPC for urgent decision making
3
analytics approach prohibitive.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Therefore a logical starting point is to consider
the current state of the art in processing data from simulations in-situ.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This is
illustrated in Figure 1, where cores of a processor are shared between compute
(C) and data analytics (D).
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The general idea is that a number of compute cores
are serviced by a data analytics core, and these compute cores ﬁre and forget
their raw data over to the corresponding data core for analytics whilst the com-
putation proceeds.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The major beneﬁt of this is that the raw data is never written
to disk, thus avoiding the overhead of IO and the compute cores can continue to
work with data analytics proceeding concurrently.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Typically this data analytics
involves some form of data reduction, or live visualisation.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Existing frameworks such as XIOS [3], Damaris [6], ADIOS [5], and MONC
[4] are examples of in-situ data analytics commonly used by HPC simulation
codes.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
While these approaches have proven eﬀective and eﬃcient at interleaving
data analytics with running simulations none of them do so in real-time, address
the issues of ensemble simulation or, most importantly, support the assimilation
and incorporation of new data into running simulations.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
These limitations are
key requirements for a system that is required to support urgent decision making
and, as such, one needs to go further than the current state of the art in in-situ
data analytics.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
In-situ data analytics, where cores are shared between computation and data
handling
More generally there have been previous attempts at using HPC for urgent
decision making.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
One such example was the SPRUCE project [1], which agreed
with machine owners a priori that their resource could be used to run urgent
workloads.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Responders were given tokens which represented the amount of time
they had available on the speciﬁc machine for their workload.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The solution was
somewhat more nuanced than this because a number of modes of access were
supported.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
These ranged from jobs submitted with some sort of priority in the
batch queue, all the way to forcibly terminating already running jobs and re-
placing them for with the urgent job.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The more severe the mode, the more user
tokens were used up.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
However these previous uses of HPC for urgent decision making still involved
a batch processing model, where operators submit jobs, commonly with some
priority in the queue, and once these have completed the results are used to
inform response decisions.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
However this is not suﬃcient for our approach because,
to take advantage of the high velocity data and live data analytics methods which
are becoming commonplace, a much more interactive pattern must be embraced.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The traditional batch processing organisation, which has served classic HPC
workloads so well over many decades, is simply not appropriate here as we require
the execution of ensemble models driven by the unpredictable arrival of data and
chaining of HPC codes.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This is further complicated by the fact that, in order
for the results to be of use to the disaster response team, these urgent jobs
must run within a speciﬁc bounded time.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Furthermore, as simulations are then
progressing it is crucially important for a user to be able to interacting with
them and exploring numerous options and response techniques.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
3
The role of interactivity
We believe that using HPC for urgent decision making requires interactivity in
three main areas:
1.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
User interaction with running simulations: gaining feedback as the
code is running and the ability to modify the simulation state and parameters
as it is executing
2.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Dynamic ensemble simulations: where jobs can be started and stopped
on the ﬂy.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This is either driven directly by the user, or automatically based
on the arrival of sensor data
3.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Supporting an interactive workload: where the arrival of new data, or
completion of another code, such as a weather model, automatically starts
new jobs
These three points are illustrated in Figure 2, where a central VESTEC sys-
tem connects data sources and disaster response teams, to HPC machines.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Tak-
ing the Wildﬁre Analysist use-case as an example, it was highlighted in Section
2 that until now interaction with this code is manual, where ﬁrst line respon-
ders have to explicitly start new simulations based upon updated information
they have received and entered.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Instead, as per Figure 2, the ability to drive the
code dynamically, so that data is automatically picked up as it streams in and
leveraged according to some predeﬁned rules, relieves considerable pressure from
the disaster response team and potentially results in much more accurate, up to
date, perspective of the situation.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
In this section We explore the challenges and solutions associated with each of
these three components of interactivity in using HPC for urgent decision making.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
3.1
Interacting with running simulations
At many GBs in size, the data generated by the codes involved in our three
use-cases is substantial and, as discussed in Section 2, it is already understood


Role of interactive super-computing using HPC for urgent decision making
5
Fig.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Overview of interactivity involved in using HPC for urgent decision making
that, to enable eﬃcient data processing, then an in-situ method, where the data
is handled as it is generated rather than written out to disk ﬁrst, is crucial.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Furthermore, there is a requirement for feeding back from the user to the simu-
lation in order to modify the state on the ﬂy as the code is running.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The unique
requirements of urgent decision making means that driving this analysis and
interaction via a visual program is highly desirable and ParaView [7] is being
used for this in the VESTEC project.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
ParaView [7] is an open source data analysis and visualisation application
used in many diﬀerent application areas to analyze and visualize scientiﬁc data
sets.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Designed as a framework, tools are provided to build visualisations appro-
priate to speciﬁc application data analytics and then exploration can be per-
formed interactively in 3D or via ParaView’s batch processing capabilities.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Par-
aView supports execution over distributed memory and, as such, can handle very
large datasets, which is important in the context of disaster response.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Under the
hood, ParaView uses the highly popular Visualization ToolKit (VTK) for graph-
ics rendering and Qt for windowing support.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
In this project we are combining
ParaView with Catalyst [8], an in-situ library which orchestrates the simulation
with analysis and/or visualization and connects to ParaView.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
A major beneﬁt
of these tools is that the analysis and visualization tasks can be implemented in
a high level language such as Python or C++, or via the ParaView GUI.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The role of ParaView and Catalyst is illustrated in Figure 3, servicing a
number of ensemble simulations that are running on an HPC machine.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
These
ensembles are integrated with Catalyst and raw timestep data from each job
is passed to a user provided pipeline of analysis scripts which reduce it, for
instance via sampling.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This reduced data is then transmitted to the ParaView
GUI, typically running on a client machine and connected by TCP/IP, but it can
also pick up ﬁles using the ﬁle system or run directly on the HPC machine and
be forwarded via X11.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Depending on how the ParaView GUI has been set up


6
N.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020
arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst the
simulation itself still needs to implement the speciﬁc details of how to process
the user’s feedback, using the Catalyst tool means that they do not need to be
concerned with the mechanism of how the feedback is delivered.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
However, it is not just HPC technology that needs to be considered here,
as the data sizes involved mean that underlying data science and visualisation
techniques must also be addressed.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
For instance, the VESTEC project is also
researching novel data reduction techniques that support the identiﬁcation of
topologically relevant features from individual simulation step data.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This relies
on sampling raw data from topological proxies and then isolating the most rep-
resentative members from the ensembles and estimating the probabilities of the
appearance of speciﬁc features from this.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Furthermore, graphical techniques such
as in-situ ray tracing, must also be further developed to support scalable image
generation and fast access to full-resolution simulation state.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
3.2
Dynamic ensemble simulations
Previous research around using HPC for urgent decision making has identiﬁed
how important it is for simulations to be started quickly, rather than languish-
ing in the batch queue system [2].
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst using a dedicated machine for urgent
decision making might seem like an obvious choice, the relative rarity of these
disasters means that such a machine could be lightly used.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Furthermore, the


Role of interactive super-computing using HPC for urgent decision making
7
ability to run very large, high resolution jobs, is often desirable when it comes
to urgent decision workloads, and as such the use of existing HPC resources is
attractive.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
A common approach is to leverage queue priorities, such that jobs
submitted to speciﬁc queues will run ﬁrst or even terminate currently running
jobs.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
However, this approach requires signiﬁcant policy agreement with the indi-
vidual HPC machine operators, and the execution of urgent jobs will inevitably
cause disruption.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This might not matter too much with previous urgent decision
approaches, which involved running a small number of jobs, but our approach
involves running ensemble simulations which can be started unpredictably based
on sensor data streaming in over time, meaning that many runs over a not in-
signiﬁcant time period is likely.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
In VESTEC we have adopted the idea of a central VESTEC server federat-
ing over many HPC machines as per Figure 2.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This system periodically tracks
the utilisation of each HPC machine and, based upon this knowledge and the
speciﬁcs of the job, will submit to which ever machine is deemed most appro-
priate.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Federation is entirely hidden from the end-user and, whilst speciﬁc HPC
machines might still employ further measures such as high priority queue which
the VESTEC system can be aware of, the load will be spread out across mul-
tiple supercomputers if a signiﬁcant number of jobs need to be executed.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Being
a European project, it is our vision that all the major supercomputers of Eu-
rope would eventually sign up to such a scheme, although for the purposes of
the VESTEC research project we are federating over a smaller number of HPC
machines to develop and prove the underlying concepts.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This approach solves another challenge in using HPC machines for urgent
decision making, which is that of resilience.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Most general purpose HPC machines
simply do not operate with the guaranteed level of service availability required
for life saving workloads.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Even those that currently do, such as the Met Oﬃce,
are fairly crude in their approach of relying on a hot backup machine which
will clear itself of jobs and run the main workload if a failure is detected in the
other machine.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
By contrast, in our approach the federator tracks which jobs are
submitted to which machine, and if a supercomputer fails then not only will
no more jobs be submitted to it, but also any queued or running jobs will be
automatically resubmitted elsewhere.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
All of this is transparent to the user and
more generally a single job might also be submitted to more than one machine
speculatively, either to guard against machine failure or to simply hedge bets
about which system will run the job ﬁrst.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Of course there are still challenges involved and an open question is whether
this approach of polling machine status provides a level of control is ﬁne grained
enough to fully support the execution of codes within a bounded time frame.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
For instance, a major question which we are looking to answer in this project
is whether it will be possible to collect enough data and make accurate enough
predictions around machine state and queue times to provide this bounded exe-
cution time, or will some combination of special priority queues still be required
in the most critical of situations?
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Our federation approach does not get us entirely round the challenges of
machine policy either.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
For instance, many operators of supercomputers have
fairly strict policies around accounts and who may execute what.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
In some cases
it might not be possible to have a single VESTEC user per system as this could be
seen as account sharing which many systems disallow.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Instead, individual users
might still need their own accounts on the machines and their credentials then
provided to VESTEC system for accessing the HPC machines on their behalf.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst this is not a major blocker in the context of a research project, in order to
roll this approach out across very many machines, such as all supercomputers in
Europe which is our vision, then such challenges must be considered and solved.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
3.3
Supporting an interactive workload
When it comes to an interactive workload there are two concerns to bear in mind.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Firstly, new data arriving from sensors must be processed in some manner, either
by performing preliminary analysis or feeding it directly into simulation runs.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Secondly, it is desirable to chain the running of simulation codes together, for
instance, the execution of a weather model ﬁrst generates a forecast which is
then used by a simulation codes such as Wildﬁre Analyst, as details of the wind
signiﬁcantly impact how forest ﬁres progress.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Both of these requirements need
to be handled in a way that requires minimal intervention from the already busy
front line responders.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
We have identiﬁed that a workﬂow approach is appropriate here, where spe-
ciﬁc activities are performed and their status tracked.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Once activities have com-
pleted then their results can be used to drive further activities as per a set
of predeﬁned rules.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Figure 4 illustrates an example workﬂow for the forest ﬁre
use-case, where the arrival of new data will either update already running ensem-
ble simulations, or start new ones.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This is further complicated by the fact that
the data might require pre-processing and new instances of the high resolution
weather model might need to be executed too, and the weather forecast results
provided to new instances of Wildﬁre Analyst.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst there are very many workﬂow technologies available, arguably the two
most mature and ubiquitous are the Common Workﬂow Language (CWL) [10]
and Apache Taverna [11].
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
In fact CWL is not a speciﬁc technology per-se, but
instead a standard for describing workﬂows which numerous projects have im-
plemented.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
By contrast, Apache Taverna provides its own workﬂow description
language and ecosystem of tools such as GUIs for designing workﬂows.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
These
technologies have not grown from an HPC perspective and as such neither is
perfectly suited to our needs.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
When one considers the workﬂow in Figure 4, they
can observe a number of conditionals based on the state of the system or data.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
However, CWL does not support conditional branching in the workﬂows directly,
so its ability to fully describe the workﬂows of our use-cases is limited.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Apache
Taverna by contrast does have some support for conditionals in the workﬂow,
although this is not a commonly used feature, but Taverna is very heavy weight
and at the current time of writing uses a description interface which is cur-


Role of interactive super-computing using HPC for urgent decision making
9
Fig.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Example workﬂow for executing or updating Wildﬁre Analyst in response to
the arrival of new data
rently non-standard and in ﬂux as the technology matures and moves towards
full acceptance as an Apache project.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Therefore the approach we have adopted in the VESTEC project is to use
CWL, due to its standardised nature, but only use this to describe each indi-
vidual activity of the workﬂow and connect these using our own bespoke im-
plementation in the VESTEC system.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst this isn’t ideal, given the current
state of these technologies we believe it is the best work around and potentially
as these become more mature for HPC then we can move to standardising the
links between activities.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
4
The role of the cloud
From the discussions in Section 3 it might seem to the reader that many of
the requirements for fusing real-time data with HPC for urgent decision making
overlap with those of cloud computing.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Hence a natural question is whether the
adoption of some public cloud, such as Azure or AWS, could be appropriate
here.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
One could go even further and argue that much of the work we are doing
on the VESTEC system duplicates functionality already provided by the cloud,
for instance supporting elastic compute, and as such a cloud-ﬁrst solution could
be more appropriate.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
However, the cloud is not a silver bullet and there are speciﬁc limitations
that impact its overall suitability for this kind of high performance work load.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
One such limitation is the fact that the user must set up the entirely of the


10
N.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
infrastructure themselves and it is very easy to make decisions that, later down
the line, signiﬁcantly limit performance.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst the compute power of the cloud
hardware and the interconnect is of high performance, selecting and conﬁguring
an appropriate ﬁle system can be a major issue.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
As such, it can be challenging
to obtain high performance from codes that require signiﬁcant IO, which is
common place in HPC and involves all three of our VESTEC use-cases.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst
high performance ﬁle-systems are often available on the cloud, these must be
setup and conﬁgured by the user which is complex and beyond the capabilities
of many users and developers.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The common choice is to select a more common
parallel ﬁle-system technology, such as NFS, and whilst this is still a non-trivial
task to set up and conﬁgure, it is at-least doable in a realistic time frame.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Performance comparison, in Site Updates Per Second (higher is better) of
HemeLB running on Cirrus, Azure and Azure with no IO
Figure 5 illustrates a performance comparison for HemeLB [9], a CFD code
based on the lattice Boltzmann method, on Cirrus which is a HPE/SGI 8600
HPC system (36 Broadwell cores per node, connected via InﬁniBand), and Azure
(16 Haswell cores per node, connected via InﬁniBand.) In this experiment we
have picked a domain based on a 3d rotational angiography scan of an anonymous
patient with a cerebral aneurysm being treated at the National Hospital for
Neurology and Neurosurgery in London, UK.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The simulations are concerned
with modelling the region around the bifurcation of the internal carotid artery’s
bifurcation into the anterior cerebral artery and the middle cerebral artery and
the code is conﬁgured to use a block size of 8, block counts of 13, 26, and 27, and


Role of interactive super-computing using HPC for urgent decision making
11
650492 total ﬂuid sites.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This code is not speciﬁcally part of one of the VESTEC
use-cases, but we believe that this application area would be applicable to using
HPC for urgent decision making in the future.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst the processor technologies between Cirrus and Azure are diﬀerent,
we can still observe patterns here and draw some conclusions.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The Cirrus and
Azure runs are executing with IO in HemeLB enabled, whereas the Azure (no
IO) runs have had IO disabled at the application level.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
This last conﬁguration,
over Azure with no IO, is the fastest and this is because of the absence of IO,
which adds some overhead to the code regardless.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
However it can be seen that
when enabling IO on Azure the performance very signiﬁcantly decreases, 4.7
times slower at 576 cores.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The performance on Cirrus with IO enabled is 3.4
times faster than that of Azure with IO enabled.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst the Xeon processors
are the next generation on Cirrus (Broadwell vs Haswell), we are still using the
exact same number of cores and when proﬁling the code in more detail we found
that the vast majority of this time diﬀerence was due to the overhead of IO on
the cloud.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Another beneﬁt of the cloud is that of elasticity, where new VMs can be spun
up quickly rather than having to wait in a batch queue as per HPC machines.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
However, clouds are not always as elastic as they might initially seem and prior
resource requests often have to be made ahead of time for signiﬁcant amounts
of compute.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
When one considers that the cloud companies must still provision
the hardware and ensure that there is enough resource, then this isn’t hugely
surprising.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
It does however mean that requesting a very large amount of compute,
very infrequently and unpredictably, as would be the case with urgent decision
making for disaster response, is not what the cloud has been designed for.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
There is also the question of cost and Figure 6 illustrates a cost comparison
between HemeLB running on Cirrus, Azure and Azure with no IO.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The cost has
been normalised, so we can explore the diﬀerent conﬁgurations from a cost per-
spective irrespective of performance.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
It is important to note that the costs quoted
here are the full cost for Cirrus, including support, but Azure conﬁgurations only
depict the cost of the VMs.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Additional activities on the cloud after the job has
ﬁnished, such as data storage, ingress and egress will incur additional charges.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
It can be seen that, running on Cirrus is consistently the cheapest option, being
2.7 times cheaper than Azure without any IO and over 12 times cheaper than
Azure with IO at 576 cores.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The most costly conﬁguration is that of Azure with
IO enabled and this is because of the additional ﬁle server support VMs that
must be stood up.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst the numbers in Figures 5 and 6 illustrate the limitations of the cloud
for HPC workloads, the cloud does have a number of features which could be of
beneﬁt in the use of computing for disaster response.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Firstly, a cloud system could
be one of our target machines, with the VESTEC system then federating over
this exactly like the HPC machines.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Secondly, we believe that some technologies
which are closely tied with the cloud, such as object stores, will be very applicable
to the technology solution employed by VESTEC.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Normalised cost (lower is better) comparison of running HemeLB running on
Cirrus, Azure and Azure with no IO


Role of interactive super-computing using HPC for urgent decision making
13
In fact, in a way, the VESTEC system can be thought of a private cloud, with
machines that subscribe to this then providing the compute resource and our
VESTEC control system the overall marshaller.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst this does look diﬀerent
to public clouds such as Azure and AWS, there is an overlap of requirements and
features, and whilst the implementation of these will by necessity be diﬀerent,
it could be said that the ability to provide the ﬂexibility of the cloud but within
the HPC space, is highly desirable for disaster response.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
5
Conclusions
The use of HPC for urgent decision making is an exciting new domain for the
super-computing community.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
However there are numerous challenges and barri-
ers that need to be overcome in order for this to be a success, not least because
HPC machines, which traditionally favour throughput over individual job la-
tency, are not set up for this sort of workload.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
In this paper we have identiﬁed
three major challenges around interactivity that need to be addressed in order to
successfully use HPC for disaster response; interacting with running simulations,
dynamic ensemble control, and supporting an interactive workload.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
The role of interactivity is crucial here and, whilst no existing technologies
are absolutely perfect, with further enhancements they can be made to work
together but the devil is in the detail in terms of how one actually achieves
this.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
It is clear that this eﬀort requires expertise from across numerous domains,
from traditional simulation, to data analysis, to visualisation techniques, to real-
time computing, all these diﬀerent components must be considered if we are to
transform disaster response.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
We are currently building the VESTEC system and exploring the hypothesis
that by federating across multiple HPC machines, one addresses the limitations
of HPC for this type of workload.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Whilst it involves signiﬁcant eﬀort to further
develop the tools, techniques and technologies, the potential payoﬀfor the HPC
and disaster response communities is signiﬁcant if we are successful.
title: arXiv:2010.08774v1  [cs.DC]  17 Oct 2020

text:
Epistemology versus ontology in the quantum
computation context
In order to claim practical relevance, any notion and quantitative means
of “computation” has to be ultimately grounded in physics, because “in-
formation is physical”,1 and so is the manipulation of information.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
The
Church-Turing thesis – in Turing’s own words “a man provided with paper,
pencil, and rubber, and subject to strict discipline, is in eﬀect a universal
machine.”2 – is a conjecture attempting to achieve just this goal: connecting
physics to an appropriate formalism.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Yet such conceptualizations bear, in their very success, a dangerous ten-
dency to forget about the analogy and instead go for the formalism.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Thereby
nature is confused with formalism – indeed, our own partly formalized nar-
ratives about nature – just as theater3 is taken for life, or propaganda4 for
fact.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
This results in beliefs in theoretical and hypothetical conceptual en-
tities, “the existence of various religious stigmas and social pressures, that
taken together, amount[[ed]] to an evangelical crusade”.5
Thereby, issues related to the formal representability of physical enti-
ties and processes are far from settled, and “bordering on the mysterious”.6
Yet, unlike Wigner, I believe that there may be at least two handy but

mutually contradicting reasons for the eﬀectiveness of mathematics in the
natural sciences: one postulates that laws “emerge” from disorder.7–9 An-
other, apparently converse, reason for lawfulness is that we are inhabiting
a virtual reality simulated by a computational process.10–14 In this hypoth-
esis whatever “laws of nature” science might discover should be perceived
as epistemic, intrinsic reﬂections of, or correspondences to, this ontological,
extrinsic (to us) computation.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
The above rant served the purpose to suggest, and prepare the Reader
for, a cautious disengagement between epistemology and ontology – what
might be claimed and believed to be known on the one hand, and what
may be “lurking behind the detector clicks” on the other hand.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Even with
this proviso, one has to keep in mind that there is no “Archimedean point”
or “ontological anchor” upon which an “objective reality” (whatever that
is) can be based.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
In particular, whenever claims are issued about quantum resources, as-
sets, or features – such as quantum parallelism by coherent superposition
of classically distinct states, or entanglement as the relational encoding of
multi-partite states – which might go beyond operationally established clas-
sical means and could give rise to quantum advantages, caution is advisable.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Because in such cases the metaphor might supervene or “outperform” the
simulated, yielding improper expectations and overstated, almost evangel-
ical, claims.15

text:
Types of quantum oracles for randomness: pure states in
a superposition versus mixed states
There is a sombre fact of contemporary quantum physics: as of to-
day the “measurement problem”, as contemplated by von Neumann,16
Schr¨odinger,17,18 and repeated by Everett19,20 and Wigner,21 despite nu-
merous attempts to resolve it,22 remains disputed and unsolved.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
One of the
issues is the simple mathematical impossibility to achieve irreversibility –
the notorious “collapse of the wave function”, or state reduction at mea-
surement point23 – from a completely reversible temporal evolution.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Indeed
this should be indisputable from “group theory 101”: the concatenation of
unitary operators never yields outside of the realm of unitary and thus re-
versible transformations.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
For ﬁnite groups, Cayley’s theorem states that one
essentially is dealing with permutations, with one-to-one transformations,
with re-expressions, re-samplings of the same “message”.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Stated diﬀerently a nesting argument16,19–21 essentially “enlarges” the
domain of reversibility to include whatever resources or regions of (Hilbert


November 27, 2024
15:33
WSPC - Proceedings Trim Size: 9in x 6in
2020-vectorcomputation
3
or conﬁguration) space are necessary to re-establish reversibility, thereby
disputing any irreversibility postulated by quantum mechanics.24–32 For
all practical purposes33 quantum systems remain “epistemically” irre-
versible,34,35 but so are classically reversible statistical systems, for which
the entropy increase dissolves into thin air as one looks “closer” at individ-
ual constituents.36
Having just avoided the quantum Scylla of “irreversibility through re-
versibility” brings us closer to the quantum Charybdis of “quantum jel-
liﬁcation” by the prevailing quantum superposition of classically distinct
states of matter and mind, described so vividly in the late Schr¨odinger’s
Dublin seminars,18 repeating the cat paradox17 in terms of jellyﬁsh.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
With-
out measurement – how can we and everything around us “remain stable”
and not dissolve into the chasm of coherent superposition, and how come
that, despite this, we experience a fairly unique cognition and presence?
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Dirac’s “why bother?” objection33 to all of this might be to not bother at
the moment and leave the task of solving these issues to future generations.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Feynman went a step further and demanded to cease thinking about them,
thereby taking the formalism for granted (like a gospel) as given, and thus
eﬀectively shut-up and calculate.37–39
However, such a repression strategy has consequences: ﬁrst of all, as
mentioned earlier the deterministic, unitary evolution of quantum states
(through nesting) contradicts assumptions about irreversible measure-
ments.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Thereby the ontology of the alleged irreducible randomness of single
events through measurements of a coherent superposition of classically dis-
tinct or even mutually exclusive states remains open.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Under such circum-
stances no justiﬁcation for their stochastic character, no “quantum certiﬁca-
tion”40 of, in theologic terminology, creatio continua, can be given, because
consistency issues are unresolved and currently abolished, thereby either
relegating a resolution of the argument to the future or not addressing the
ontology at all.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Quantum uncertainty and random outcomes via irreversible
measurements of coherent superposition therefore remains conjectural.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text: Another related ontological issue regards the existence of mixed states.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
First of all, the same issues as for measurements are pertinent: how does one
obtain a mixed state from pure ones by one-to-one unitary state evolution?
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Claiming to be able to obtain mixed states from pure ones amounts to
pretending to get along with outright mathematical incorrectness.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
One formal way of generating mixed states from pure multi-partite
states is by taking the partial trace with respect to the Hilbert space of
one particle, a “beam dump” of sorts.34,35 As the trace is essentially a

4
many-to-one operation, irreversibility ensues.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
This can be easily corrobo-
rated by the non-uniqueness of puriﬁcation which can be envisioned as the
“quasi-inverse” (because, strictly speaking, due to non-uniqueness there is
no inverse) of the partial trace [41, Section 8.3.1].
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text: So what is the ontologic status of mixed quantum states?
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
This again is
unknown and may again, by the “why bother?” objection,33 be relegated
until some later times.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Again the question arises: how can we trust quantum
random sequences originating from mixed state measurements?
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Even more convoluted is the question if there is any criterion or diﬀer-
ence between sequences generated by measurement of pure states which are
in a coherent superposition on the one hand, and by measurement of mixed
quantum states on the other hand.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
As we cannot even formally grasp con-
sistently the notions of irreversible measurement and production of mixed
states we ought to accept our total loss to conceptualize the diﬀerences or
similarities between them.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
We are left with the hope that, as both issues
appear to have the same group-theoretic roots, any solution of one will, by
reduction, entail a solution of the other.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Another “fashionable” attempt to ascertain and thereby certify quan-
tum randomness involving “quantum contextuality”42,43 would be to as-
sume the co-existence of complementary observables and, relative to the re-
spective implicit assumptions (most notably context independence), prove
(by contradiction or statistical demonstration) the impossibility for any
value deﬁniteness of complementary, incompatible observables prior to mea-
surements.43–47 Suﬃce it to say that, as these hypothetical arguments go
they are contingent on the respective counterfactual conﬁgurations imag-
ined, and thus appear subjective and inconclusive.48

Questionable parallelism by views on a vector
From now on only pure states, represented by (unit) vectors spanning a one-
dimensional subspace of a vector space, will be considered.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

Schr¨odinger’s
aforementioned question regarding quantum jelliﬁcation,18 a variant of his
earlier “cat paradox”,17 might be brought to practical use for quantum par-
allelization: for the sake of irritation suppose, as is often alleged in quan-
tum computations, that the many mutually exclusive (classical) states in a
coherent superposition “be not alternatives but all really happen simultane-
ously .

if the laws of nature took this form for, let me say, a quarter of
an hour, we should ﬁnd our surroundings rapidly turning into a quagmire,
or sort of a featureless jelly or plasma, all contours becoming blurred, we
ourselves probably becoming jelly ﬁsh.”

One of the simplest answers that can be given to these concerns is that
this is just an epistemic question arising from a “wrong” viewpoint or per-
spective.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Because if one chooses an orthonormal basis of Hilbert space of
which the state vector is an element then the coherent superposition re-
duces to a single, unique term – namely that unit vector.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Unitary quantum
evolution amounts to “rotating” this vector in Hilbert space.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
There is no
“jelliﬁcation” of this state with respect to the “proper” bases (for dimen-
sions higher than 2 there is a continuum of bases) of which the state is
one part.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
In this view, there is no “simultaneous existence” of two or more
classically distinct states.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
All other probabilistic views are mere (continuity
of) multiplicities, projections of sorts.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
For a similar, more formalized, vision
see Gleason’s remarks on taking “the square of the norm of the projection”
in the second paragraph of Ref.49
Indeed, one can ﬁnd some hints on this solution in Schr¨odinger’s own
writings on the Vedantic vision [50, chapter V]: “the plurality that we per-
ceive is only an appearance; it is not real.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Vedantic philosophy, in which
this is a fundamental dogma has sought to clarify it by a number of analo-
gies, one of the most attractive being the many-faceted crystal which, while
showing hundreds of little pictures of what is in reality a single existent
object, does not really multiply that object.”
This might be considered bad news for quantum parallelism.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

Because
if any such parallelism is based upon epistemology – about appearance
without any substantial reality – all that remains as a resource is our ability
to measure properties of the vector from a “diﬀerent angle” than the one
this vector has been deﬁned.

This is particularly pertinent for the “extraction” of information in a
coherent superposition by classical irreversible measurements (cf.

Because what good is it to contemplate about such a counter-

text:
Computation by projective measurements of partitioned
state space
Nevertheless, even in this reduced scheme of parallelism, it might be pos-
sible to formulate relational queries corresponding to useful information
by appropriate partitioning of the state space.52–54 We may formulate the
fundamental problem of intrinsically operational vector encoding of a com-
putation aka quantum computation: under what circumstances is it possible
to derive “useful” information about (the components) of a vector?
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
It is not too unreasonable to suspect that an answer to this question
can be given in terms of relational properties of the vector encoding.55,56
Deutsch’s algorithm [41, Section 1.4.3] as well as the quantum Fourier trans-
form based on period ﬁnding [41, Section 5.4.1] may be examples for such
relational encodings realizable by state mismatches (“prepare one state,
measure another”).
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
More generally, the partitioning of ﬁnite groups by
cosets, in particular, the hidden subgroup problem [41, Section 5.4.3] maybe
a way to systematically exploit views on vectors, but so far there exists only
anecdotal evidence [41, Figure 5.5., p.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
There is a way to extract information from a quantum state by con-
structing proper (with respect to the computational task or query) sub-
spaces and the orthogonal projection operators onto such subspaces.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
How
ought this computational method be understood?
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
It will be argued that it
could be perceived in terms of (equi)partitioning the quantum state space,
and, as mentioned earlier, by using the respective projection operators as
ﬁlters.52–54
Suppose it is possible to encode (the solution to) a problem into a
Hilbert space spanned by a collection of pure state vectors encoding func-
tional instances and functional properties into one- and higher-dimensional
subspaces thereof.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
For instance, a binary function of several bits can be
encoded into quantum states (i) by state vectors whose ﬁrst components
with respect to an orthonormal basis (normalization aside) are either 0 or
1, depending on whether or not the function on the inputs evaluates to
0 or 1, and (ii) later “auxiliary” components are added to ensure mutual
orthogonality of the state vectors.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
That is, in order to obtain an orthonor-
mal basis one could, for instance, employ dimensional lifting, and thereby
enlarge the Hilbert space.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
This results in an orthonormal (after normaliza-
tion) basis of the aforementioned Hilbert space.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Therefore the elements of
the orthonormal basis represent the individual instances of the function or
problem.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Now if one forms the orthogonal projection operator as the sum of the

example of a much wider problem class associated with relational proper-
ties which can be represented or parametrized by partitioning appropriate
subspaces of Hilbert space.

Entanglement as relational parallelism across
multi-partite states
From a purely formal point of view, entangled particles are modeled by the
indecomposability of state vectors in a Hilbert space which is a non-trivial
tensor product of two or more Hilbert spaces.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Indecomposability means that
the respective state vector cannot be decomposed into a single product of

Instead, an entangled state
can be written as the coherent superposition (aka linear combination) of
such product states.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
This immediately suggests that whenever such indecomposable vectors
occur they can be “rotated” by unitary transformations into a single prod-
uct form; say a vector of the Cartesian standard basis in the respective
tensor product of two or more Hilbert spaces.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Any such transformation
cannot be expected to be acting “locally” in a single constituent space but
rather “globally” across the single constituent spaces.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Physically this means that we are not dealing with single-particle prop-
erties but again with relational properties; whereby relational information
is encoded across the multiple constituents of such a state.17,60 This can be
expected: as unitary transformations are deﬁned by rotations transforming
some orthonormal basis into another orthonormal basis61 this amounts to
a kind of “zero-sum game” between localized information aka properties on
individual constituents on the one hand, and relational information which
for instance refers to “common” or “diﬀerent” properties within collectives
or groups of constituents on the other hand.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
On partial views of vectors
In the context of state puriﬁcation the following more general question
arises: What kind of value might a partial knowledge of or about a vector
have?
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
After all, embedded observers11 may obtain only partial knowledge
and control of the degrees of freedom entailed by overseeing a “small” subset
of a “much larger” Hilbert space they inhabit.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Suppose an observer has acquired knowledge about an incomplete list
of components (relative to a particular basis) of a pure state vector.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
This
can be formalized either by a projection of this vector onto a subspace of
the Hilbert space or by “extraction” of the coordinates by the respective
vectors of the dual basis of the dual space.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
One possibility would be to “complete” the state vector by various pro-
cedures, such as the aforementioned puriﬁcation.
title: arXiv:2011.10569v1  [quant-ph]  19 Nov 2020

text:
Alternatively one might
consider the subspace spanned by both the given and the missing basis
elements.62

between points on two Keplerian orbits, is an impor-
tant practical tool measuring the closeness of two Ke-
plerian trajectories in the R3 space.

is frequently used in studies of Potentially Hazardous

e.g.

Also,
the MOID and MOID-like quantities can be used to
estimate possible visibility condition of one object
from another (Gronchi and Niederman, 2020).

The MOID is a minimum of some distance
or distance-like function ρ(u, u′) that depends on
two arguments, determining positions on two orbits.

However, methods of this class are rela-
tively vulnerable with respect to numeric uncertain-
ties through loosing real roots in nearly degenerate
cases.

This eﬀect appears because the equation for
u is quite complicated and has algebraic degree of
16 in the general case.

It often have close (almost
multiple) roots that are always diﬃcult for numeric
processing.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

The recent work by Baluev and Mikryukov
(2019) represents an eﬃcient solution of this issue
based on careful treatment of numeric errors appear-
ing on the way.

Basically, it represent a numeric im-
plementation of the algebraic approach presented by
Kholshevnikov and Vassiliev (1999), similar to the
one presented by Gronchi (2002, 2005).

this newer algorithm is only capable to process el-
liptic orbits.

This appears because the arguments u
and u′ have the meaning of eccentric anomaly that

Though the fraction of such
cases is small, they often escape from being self-

Simultaneously, the
Gronchi code appears somewhat slower than the al-

In this work we have a goal to extend the nu-
merically stable and fast code from (Baluev and

This relies on the work

Mathematical setting
Consider two confocal orbits: O determined by
the ﬁve geometric Keplerian elements a, e, i, Ω, ω,
and O′ determined analogously by the same vari-
ables with a stroke.

We need to compute the mini-

on the corresponding orbits, and the orbital positions
where this minimum is attained.

In this work we con-

we have four possible combinations: EE, EH, HE,
HH.

they appear degenerate both from the elliptic or hy-
perbolic point of view, resulting in reduced degree of

text:
Since the number of roots can be highly variable,
it is a frequent case when there are close roots that
cannot be easily resolved due to numeric errors.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
This
eﬀect was important in the EE case, where it could
lead to lost roots of g(u), due to their misclassiﬁ-
cation as complex rather than real.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
This eﬀect lead
sometimes to overestimated distance because some
critical points might appear lost.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
The solution was to
track numeric errors of the roots and to select the real
ones based on their estimated numeric uncertainty
(so that some formally complex roots of g(u) with
small imaginary part could be tested together with
purely real ones).

text:
In this work we expand this same
approach to the hyperbolic orbits as well.
