text:
Numerical algorithm
The general computing sequence remains the
same as in (Baluev and Mikryukov, 2019).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Compute the coeﬃcients of g(u) and their nu-
meric uncertainties by means of the Discrete
Fourier Transform (DFT).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Determining reasonable starting approxima-
tions for some of the g(u) roots.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Find all roots of the polynomial P(z) or Q(w)
in the complex plane by Newtonian iterations
(this task dominates, taking about 60% of com-
puting time).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Estimate roots uncertainties, and select those
roots that correspond to real orbital positions
(and lying on real hyperbola branches).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Among these roots, select the one providing
the minimum distance and perform Newtonian
2D iterations to reﬁne this minimum distance
and its position.

Now let us comment each stage of this sequence in
our updated algorithm.

text:
Determining polynomial coeﬃcients
The coeﬃcients of g(u) are computed by DFT as
if we always dealt with the EE case, just replacing
the deﬁnition of g appropriately.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
We compute a set
of values gk = g(uk) for equally spaced uk, and then
apply the DFT to obtain all ck.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
We use an excessive
number of uk to also compute a few ck with |k| > 8.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
These quantities should be zero in theory, so they can
be helpful to estimate numeric errors in ck.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
This scheme can be replicated literally in the EH
case, when g(u) is a trigonometric polynomial with
real coeﬃcients.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
In the HE and HH cases g(u)
becomes a hyperbolic polynomial, and u attains the
meaning of the hyperbolic anomaly.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
In this case we
could compute the coeﬃcients of P(z) or Q(w) by
performing their polynomial interpolation inside a
real segment.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
This would allow us to avoid com-
plex numbers, as all quantities become real-valued.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
However, this infers dealing with large diﬀerences
(large z and small z present simultaneously), so we
suspected that this scheme might appear less numer-
ically stable.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Therefore, we decided to consider g(u)
as a trigonometric polynomial of the imaginary argu-
ment (which has the meaning of eccentric anomaly).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
In this case gk become complex quantities, but the
DFT should always produce real ck, thanks to the
property g(iu) = g∗(−iu).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
The latter property can also
be used to halve the number of complex multiplica-
tions needed for the DFT.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
The numeric complexity of
this DFT remains the same as in the EE case, where
we used only real multiplications at this stage.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Determining starting approximations for the
roots
As shown in (Baluev and Mikryukov, 2019),
smart selection of starting approximations to the
roots of g(u) may signiﬁcantly improve performance
as well as numeric stability of the algorithm.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
In this
version of the library, we adopt generally the same
scheme here, though augmented in several aspects.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
This general scheme involves approximations for 4
complex roots extracted ﬁrst, then 4 guaranteed real
roots, and for the remaining roots we adopt the same
scheme as for the ﬁrst 4 ones.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
This allowed us to re-
duce the cumulative number of Newtonian iterations,
though we need to emphasize that this is merely a
statistical eﬀect, appearing when a lot of orbit pairs
are processed.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Some individual orbit pairs may re-
veal a speciﬁc behavior due to peculiar properties of
the roots.

z2 = 1/z∗

Thus
we intermittently extract small and large roots, ap-

text:
This scheme was based on
the empiric observation that complex roots concen-
trate near z = 0 and w = 0.

text:
This scheme is preserved
in the updated algorithm, and extended literally to
the EH case.

However, in the HE and HH cases

exp(0.4πi), z2 is started from z∗

In the HE case the value +i is replaced
by exp(0.6πi).

text:
Starting approximation for the 4 guaranteed real
roots are based on the assumption that critical points
are often located not far from the orbital nodes.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
But
the hyperbolic orbits introduce additional diﬃculties
in this concern.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
In particular, we should take care of
the real/imaginary hyperbola branches.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
In the HH
case exactly one starting point should be placed per
each branch combination, because we cannot guar-
antee that any combination has more than a single
critical points.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
In the HE and EH case we should
distribute two starting points per hyperbolic branch.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
So, depending on the orbital combination, we adopt
the following sets of starting approximations for crit-
ical points:
1.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
EE: two internodal distances, each lying en-
tirely on either side from the focus and two
distances connecting points separated by ±π/2
from the nodes (in true anomaly), and also ly-
ing on the same side from the focus.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
The ﬁrst
pair usually corresponds to two local minima,
while the second one usually describes saddle
points.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
EH or HE: if each H-branch passes through
just a single node then, per each branch, select
one internodal distance lying entirely on the
same side from the focus (usually minimum),
and another internodal distance containing the
focus (usually saddle point).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
HH: select all 4 possible internodal distances,
if they all refer to diﬀerent branch combina-
tions (that is, if each hyperbolic branch passes
through just a single orbital node).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
The conditions above may be violated if one
or both hyperbolic orbits pass through both its
nodes simultaneously, while the corresponding
imaginary branch does not intersect the other
orbital plane at all.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
In this case half of start-
ing approximations should necessarily involve
this imaginary branch.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Its orbital position is
selected relatively arbitrarily, through a half-
sum of hyperbolic anomalies corresponding to
the two nodes on the real branch.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Approximations of this “internodal type” should be
good for highly inclined orbit pairs, and they re-
vealed good eﬃciency in the testcase from (Baluev
and Mikryukov, 2019).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
However, it appeared that
we did not properly transform angular elements to
radians in that testcase (see Corrigendum to Baluev
and Mikryukov 2019).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
This does not mean that ini-
tial test results were wrong, as they just corresponded
to diﬀerent testcase.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
But in the corrected one such
initial approximations appeared less eﬃcient and did
not reduce the number of Newtonian iterations as de-
sired.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Obviously, this appeared because of typically
small orbital inclination in the asteroid belt.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Also, it
appeared that such starting solution are less eﬃcient
for hyperbolic orbits as well.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
We solved the issue by
pre-reﬁning every starting approximation through a
single 2D Newtonian iteration of ρ(u, u′).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
One might argue that this is no better than to
make more Newtonian iterations on P(z), but in ac-
tuality P(z) is less eﬃcient to iterate, because it typi-
cally contains close roots.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Such an eﬀect appears be-
cause each nodal u can be paired with either of two
nodal u′.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
That is, internodal critical points of ρ(u, u′)
usually project to two close pairs when considered
in terms of just u or just u′.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
But when dealing with
ρ(u, u′) they are separated well, thus avoiding the ef-
fect of close roots.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Hence, even a single 2D itera-
tion allowed to determine a good starting approxima-
tion for u.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
In turn, this approach allowed us to save
∼20 −30 Newtonian iteration of P(z) by the cost of
making just 4 additional 2D iterations of ρ(u, u′).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
The rest of the roots is determined automatically:
starting from near-zero z or near-zero w in case of
complex ck (EE or EH), or from a random point on
5


unit circle for real ck (HE or HH).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
The latter choice
was motivated by the observation that real roots are
often more diﬃcult to locate without a good starting
approximations.

Finding all complex roots
The roots of P(z) are found one by one, by means
of running the Newtonian root search with subse-
quent division of P(z) by the corresponding linear
factor z −zk.

text:
we introduced a few minor changes to
this scheme.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
First, we extract the roots until a quartic polyno-

title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
The last
four roots of the quartic polynomial are computed
using explicit formulae of the Ferrari method.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

Since
these formulae are more complicated and may have a

text:
Solving the quar-

Second, to further improve numeric stability, we
apply Newton iterations to either P(z), if |z| < 1, or
Q(w), if |z| > 1.

In the previous version of the algo-

lead to looping conditions, when we inﬁnitely jump
between the same points.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Now we avoided this is-

manner.

Namely, we keep the |z| < 1 mode until
|z|2 reaches 5, and the mode |z| > 1 is kept while
|z|2 > 1/2.

1 = z1/|z1|2, in
case when the ﬁrst orbit is hyperbolic it should be

1.

In addition to the basic fast method based on

Conclusions
In the end we would like to discuss further paths
of developing the distlink algorithm.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
We did not yet
consider parabolic orbits and other degenerate cases.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
However, there are many comets moving on near-
parabolic, and even if their eccentricity is not pre-
cisely unit, it can be approximated by unit at some
early stage.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
From the analytic theory, if either e = 1
or e′ = 1 the algebraic degree of the associated poly-
nomial is reduced to 12, and whenever both the or-
bits are parabolic the algebraic degree becomes 9
(Baluyev and Kholshevnikov, 2005).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
This would
imply certain simpliﬁcations and likely signiﬁcant
speedup of the computation.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
However, this also re-
quires a more speciﬁc treatment of such cases due to
the degeneracy.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Some performance increase to the basic algo-
rithm is still possible.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
It spends signiﬁcant time on
ﬁnding complex roots of g(u), and therefore one may
try to eliminate this unnecessary work at least partly.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
This is unfortunately not so easy because we can-
not control the order in which the roots are extracted.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Though we made some eﬀorts to extract 4 guaran-
teed real roots in the beginning, this optimization is
of a statistical type, i.e.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
it works in average but fre-
quently fails for individual conﬁgurations.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
However,
to increase the average performance one may simply
stop extracting the roots if the polynomial has none
real roots.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
In case when g(u) is hyperbolic with real coeﬃ-
cients ck, this can be veriﬁed by the Descartes’ rule
of signs, that is, if the coeﬃcients ck are all positive
or all negative then there are no positive real roots.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
In
case of trigonometric g(u), when ck are complex, one
need to verify the existence of roots with |z| = 1.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
This
can be done based on the available classic upper and
lower bounds on the polynomial roots; for example,
if at some point |zk| < zmax and zmax < 1 then there
is no roots with |z| = 1, hence no real roots remain
in g(u).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
However, approaches of this type require
to track uncertainties in each ck which are accumu-
lated after every root extraction (division of P(z) by
z −zk).
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
This may result in a loss of numeric reliabil-
ity due to unavoidable assumptions about errors, so
implementing this method would require a detailed
investigation of possible side eﬀects.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
Another way to increase the performance is opti-
mization of complex-valued arithmetics.
title: Fast error–safe MOID computation involving hyperbolic orbits

text:
It is cur-

Abstract 
 
The
Low-Power
Image
Recognition
Challenge
 
 
 
 
 
(LPIRC, ​https://rebootingcomputing.ieee.org/lpirc​) is
 
  
an
annual
competition
started
in
2015.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
competition identifies the best technologies that can
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
classify and detect objects in images efficiently (short
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
execution time and low energy consumption) and
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
accurately (high precision).
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Over the four years, the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
winners’ scores have improved more than 24 times.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
As
computer
vision
is
widely
used
in
many
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
battery-powered systems (such as drones and mobile
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
phones), the need for low-power computer vision will
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
become
increasingly
important.

text:
This
paper
 
 
 
 
 
summarizes LPIRC 2018 by describing the three
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
different tracks and the winners’ solutions.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Introduction 
 
Competitions are an effective way of promoting
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
innovation
and
system
integration.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
“Grand
 
 
 
 
 
Challenges” can push the boundaries of technologies
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
and
open
new
directions
for
research
and
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
development.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The DARPA Grand Challenge in 2004
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
opened the era of autonomous vehicles.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Since 2010,
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
the
ImageNet
Large
Scale
Visual
Recognition
 
 
 
 
 
 
Challenge (ILSVRC) has become a de facto standard
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
benchmark in computer vision.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The Low-Power
 
 
 
 
 
 
Image Recognition Challenge (LPIRC) started in
 
 
 
 
 
 
2015 as an annual competition identifying the best
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
system-level solution for detecting objects in images
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
while using as little energy as possible ​(Lu et al.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Although many competitions are held every
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
year, LPIRC is the only one integrating both image
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
recognition and low power.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
In LPIRC, a contestants’
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
system is connected to the referee system through an
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
intranet (wired or wireless).
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
​There is no restriction on
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
software or hardware.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
​The contestant’s system issues
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
HTTP GET commands to retrieve images from the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
referee system and issues HTTP POST commands to
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
send the answers.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
In the past four years, LPIRC has
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
experimented with different tracks with different
 
 
 
 
 
 
rules
and
restrictions.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
In
2015,
offloading
of
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
processing
was
allowed
but
only
one
team
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
participated.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
In 2016, a track displayed images on a
 
 
  
 
 
 
  
computer screen and a constantant’s system used a
 
 
  
 
 
  
camera to capture the images but only one team
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
participated in this track.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
These two tracks are no
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
longer offered.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Tracks in 2018 LPIRC 
 
Vision systems typically consist of three components:
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
model architecture (such as a neural network),
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
inference engine (such as a series of kernels that
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
evaluates neural network operations efficiently on a
 
 
 
 
 
  
specific
hardware),
and
the
carrying
hardware
 
 
 
 
 
 
LPIRC tracks prior to 2018 required system-level
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
improvements
that
did
not distinguish between
 
 
 
 
 
 
progress in individual components.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
In 2018, two new
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
tracks were offered that strategically focused on
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
model architecture and the inference engine.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
2.1 Track 1: TfLite Model on Mobile Phones 
 
This new track, also known as the On-device Visual
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Intelligence
Competition,
focused
on
model
 
 
 
 
 
architecture: contestants submit their inference neural
 
 
 
 
 
 
network model in TfLite format using Tensorflow
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
(​https://www.tensorflow.org/mobile/tflite/​).
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The
 
 
models were benchmarked on a fixed inference
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
engine (TfLite) and hardware model (Pixel 2 XL
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
phone).
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
submissions should strive to classify correctly as
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
many images as possible given a time budget of 30
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
ms per image.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The submissions were evaluated on a
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
1 


single core with a batch-size of one to mimic realistic
 
 
  
 
 
  
 
 
use cases on mobile devices.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Although the scoring
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
metric is based on inference latency rather than
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
energy consumption, the two are usually correlated
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
when the same benchmarks are used on the same
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
hardware.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Track
1’s
latency-based
metric
is
critical
to
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
accelerating
the
development
of
mobile
model
 
 
 
 
 
 
architectures.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Prior to this metric, there was no
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
common, relevant and verifiable metric to evaluate
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
the inference speed of mobile model architectures.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Numerous papers characterize inference efficiency
 
 
 
 
 
using unspecified benchmarking environments or
 
 
 
 
 
latency on desktop as a proxy.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Even the most
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
commonly used metric, MACs (multiply-add count)
 
 
 
 
 
 
do not correlate well with inference latency in the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
real-time (under 30 ms) range (Chen and Gilbert
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
2018).
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Track 1’s metric is the first to measures on-device
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
latency in a realistic use case in the real-time range.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
In addition, this track provides a benchmarking
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
platform (see Section 5.1) that allows for repeatable
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
measurements and fair comparison of mobile model
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
architectures.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The flexibility of submitting just the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
model and not the full system allows this track to be
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
an online competition.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
This convenience helps to
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
boost the submission count to 130 models within just
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
2 weeks.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The submissions also witness excellent quality,
 
 
 
 
 
 
establishing the new state-of-the-art in mobile model
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
architecture design.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Within the 30 ms latency range,
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
the best of track 1 submissions outperformed the
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
previous
state-of-the-art
based
on
quantized
 
 
 
 
 
MobileNet V1, by 3.1% on the hold-out test set.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The submissions have demonstrated a considerable
 
 
 
  
 
amount of diversity.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Slightly over half (51.7%) of the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
solutions are quantized.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Most of the
architectures
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
(74.1%) are variations of the existing Mobilenet
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
model
family,
namely
quantized
V2
(22.4%),
 
 
 
 
 
 
quantized V1 (24.1%) and float V2 (27.6%).
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
predominant
dependence
on
Mobilenets
is
not
 
 
 
 
 
 
surprising, considering their exceptional performance
 
 
 
 
 
on-device and the convenient support by TfLite.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
On
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
the other hand, to sustain long-term mobile vision
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
research,
track
1 should also serve to reward
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
previously under- or un-explored model architectures.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
In future installments of LPIRC, track 1 is looking to
 
 
 
 
 
   
  
implement mechanisms for facilitating the discovery
 
 
 
 
 
 
of novel architectures and rendering the platform
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
more inclusive to general vision researchers.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Accurate and fast image recognition on the edge
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
device requires several steps.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
First, a neural network
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
model needs to be built and trained to identify and
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
classify images (recognizing when a photo is of a dog
 
 
 
  
  
  
 
vs.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Then, the model should run as
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
accurate as possible on the actual hardware without
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
latency issues.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
As most neural networks are trained
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
on a floating-point model, they usually need to be
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
converted to fixed-point in order to efficiently run on
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
edge devices.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
For
this
competition,
the
model
is
based
on
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
MobileNet
V2,
but
is
modified
to
be
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
quantization-friendly.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Although Google's MobileNet
 
 
 
 
models
successfully
reduce
parameter size and
 
 
 
 
 
 
computation latency due to the use of separable
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
convolution,
directly
quantizing
a
pre-trained
 
 
 
 
 
MobileNet v2 model can cause huge precision loss.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The team analyzes and identifies the root cause of
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
accuracy loss due to quantization in such separable
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
convolution networks, and solved it properly without
 
 
 
  
 
 
utilizing quantization-aware re-training.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
In separable convolutions, depthwise convolution is
 
 
 
 
 
 
applied on each channel independently.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
However, the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
min and max values used for weights quantization are
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
taken collectively from all channels.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
An outlier in one
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
channel may cause a huge quantization loss for the
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
whole model due to an enlarged data range.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Without
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
correlation crossing channels, depthwise convolution
 
 
 
 
 
may be prone to produce all-zero values of weights in
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
  
one channel.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
This is commonly observed in both
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
MobileNet v1 and v2 models.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
All-zero values in one
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
channel means small variance.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
A large “scale” value
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
for that specific channel would be expected while
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
applying batch normalization transform directly after
 
 
 
 
 
 
depthwise convolution.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
This hurts the representation
 
 
 
 
 
 
power of the whole model.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
As a solution, the team proposes an effective
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
quantization-friendly
separable
convolution
 
 
 
architecture, where the nonlinear operations (both
 
 
 
 
 
 
batch normalization and ReLU6) between depthwise
 
 
 
 
 
 
and pointwise convolution layers are all removed,
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
letting the network learn proper weights to handle the
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
batch normalization transform directly.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
In addition,
 
 
 
 
 
 
ReLU6 is replaced with ReLU in all pointwise
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
convolution layers.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
From various experiments in
 
 
 
 
 
 
MobileNet v1 and v2 models, this architecture shows
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
a significant accuracy boost in the 8-bit quantized
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
pipeline.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Fixed-point inferencing while preserving a high level
 
 
 
  
 
 
of accuracy is the key to enable deep learning use
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
6 


cases on low power edge devices.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The team identifies
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
the industry-wide quantization issue, analyzes the
 
 
 
 
 
 
root cause, and solves it on MobielNets efficiently.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The
quantized
modified
MobileNet_v2_1.0_128
 
 
 
 
model can achieve 28 milliseconds per inference with
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
high
accuracy
(64.7%
on
ImageNet
validation
 
 
 
 
 
 
dataset) on a single ARM CPU of Pixel 2.

More
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
details
are

the

convolution
 
 
 
architecture

(​https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.08607​).

​Tucker
 
 
 
 
 
decomposition:
​It

1966)​, 2-D Tucker decomposition is used in the

network
throughput.

text:
NVIDIA
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
TensorRT (​https://developer.nvidia.com/tensorrt​) is a
 
   
high-performance deep learning inference optimizer
 
 
 
 
 
and
runtime
that
delivers
low
latency
and
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
high-throughput
for
deep
learning
inference
 
 
 
 
 
applications.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The inference time becomes much
 
 
 
 
 
 
shorter by using TensorRT and therefore saves
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
energy.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
TensorRT provides quantization operation for
 
 
 
 
 
 
the GPU inference engine.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The computation latency
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
is shortened because of less floating point arithmetic.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
In order not to reduce the mAP of the model, the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
team quantizes the weight to 16-bit while doing
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
inference.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The method reshapes the images before and after the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
inference process.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Since reshaping on the CPU is
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
costly, the method uses CPU multithreading to
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
accelerate the process.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The method generates two
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
threads on each CPU core and each thread process
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
one batch of data.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
TX 2 has 6 CPU cores and the
 
 
 
 
  
  
 
 
 
 
method creates 12 threads.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The inference on the GPU
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
can only work in a single thread; thus the method
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
takes the inference as a mutual process and different
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
threads need to compete for the GPU.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Applying multithreading method results in a 1.4x
 
 
 
 
  
 
speeding up (the fps without multithreading is 3.17
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
while the fps with multithreading is 4.41), not as high
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
as expected.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The reason is competition for the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
mutual recourse among the threads and constrains
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
acceleration.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Different threads need to wait for the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
inference process when it’s occupied and need to use
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
mutual lock to avoid the hazard.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

4.5 First and Second Prizes of Track 3 
 
The ETRI and KPST team wins both the first and the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
second prizes of Track 3.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The performance of object
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
detection can be evaluated using accuracy, speed and
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
memory.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The accuracy is a common measurement
 
 
 
  
 
 
and it has been widely used in comparing different
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
object
detection
architectures.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
However,
its
 
 
 
 
 
performance is dependent upon speed and memory as
  
 
 
 
 
 
 
well as accuracy for the given environments and
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
applications.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
In this competition, the performance is
 
 
 
 
 
  
measured
using
accuracy
(mAP)
and
energy
 
 
 
 
 
 
consumption (WH).
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The accuracy is influenced by
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
the detection architectures, an input resolution and a
 
 
 
 
 
 
  
base
network for feature extraction.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The more
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
complex structures with a high-resolution image may
 
 
  
 
 
 
achieve
higher
accuracy
at
higher
energy
 
 
 
 
 
 
consumption.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
To obtain a high score, it is necessary
 
 
  
 
   
 
to balance accuracy and energy consumption.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The team examines the score function and finds the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
most important factor is energy consumption.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
At the
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
same accuracy, the score is higher at lower energy
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
consumption.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Moreover, the accuracy is weighted by
 
 
 
  
 
 
the processed images ratio within 10 minutes.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
This
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
means that the detection architecture should be fast
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
and light and the trade-off between accuracy and
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
energy
consumption.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Accordingly,
single
stage
 
 
 
 
 
detectors such as SSD ​(Liu et al.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
2016) and YOLO
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
(Redmon and Farhadi 2017) are considered in the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
pipeline.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The team selects SSD as a detection
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
framework due to its simplicity and stable accuracy
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
among feature extractors ​(Huang et al.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
To
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
obtain the best score, the team performs three
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
optimization
steps:
1)
Detection
structure
 
 
 
 
 
optimization, 2) Feature extraction optimization, and
 
 
 
 
 
 
3) System and parameters optimization.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
For detection structure optimization, in the detection
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
structure, the original SSD is based on VGG and its
 
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
 
performance is well balanced in accuracy and speed.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

Its
speed
and
memory
can
be
improved
for
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
low-power and real-time environments.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

To speed up,
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
the team proposes efficient SSD (eSSD) by adding
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
additional feature extraction layers and prediction
 
 
 
 
 
 
layers in SSD.

Although

In
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
object

multiple
duplicate

obtained and Non-Maximal Suppression (NMS) with

process
between

increase the efficiency of network bandwidth.

After

5.1 Google Tensorflow Models 
 
Google provided technical support to Track 1 in two
 
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
aspects.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
First,
Google
open-sources
TfLite,
an
 
 
 
 
 
 
mobile-centric
inference
engine
for
Tensorflow
 
 
 
 
 
models.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
TfLite encapsulates optimal implementations
 
 
 
 
 
of standard operations such as convolutions and
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
depthwise-convolutions that shields the contestants
 
 
 
 
 
from such concerns.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
This effectively allows people
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
with no background in mobile optimization to
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
participate
in
the
competition.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
Second, Google
 
 
 
 
 
 
provides the mobile benchmarking system and it
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
allows repeatable measurement of the performance
 
 
 
 
 
 
metric.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The
system
comes
in
two
flavors:
a
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
stand-alone App that the contestants can run on their
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
local phones, and a cloud-based service where the
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
submissions will be automatically dispatched to a
 
 
 
 
 
  
Pixel 2 XL phone and benchmarked using the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
standardized environment.

text:
5.2
Facebook
AI
Performance
Evaluation
 
 
 
 
 
Platform 
 
Machine learning is a rapidly evolving area with
 
 
  
 
 
 
 
many moving parts: new and existing framework
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
enhancements, new hardware solutions, new software
 
 
 
 
 
 
backends, and new models.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
With so many moving
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
parts, it is very difficult to quickly evaluate the
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
performance of a machine learning model.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
However,
 
  
 
 
 
 
such
evaluation
is vastly important in guiding
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
resource allocation in: 
●
The development of the frameworks 
●
The optimization of the software backends 
●
The selection of the hardware solutions 
●
The iteration of the machine learning models 
 
Because of this need, Facebook has developed an AI
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
performance evaluation platform (FAI-PEP, open
 
 
 
 
 
sourced at ​https://github.com/facebook/FAI-PEP​) to
 
 
 
 
provide a unified and standardized AI benchmarking
  
 
 
 
 
 
methodology.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
FAI-PEP supports Caffe2 and TFLite frameworks,
 
 
 
 
 
 
the iOS, Android, linux, and windows operating
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
systems.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The FAI-PEP is modularly composed that
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
new frameworks and backends can be added easily.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
The built-in metrics collected by FAI-PEP are:
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
latency, accuracy, power, and energy.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
It also supports
 
 
 
 
  
 
 
reporting arbitrary metrics that the user desires to
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
collect.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

text:
With FAI-PEP, the benchmark runtime
 
 
 
 
 
 
condition can be specified precisely, and the ML
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
workload can be benchmarked repeatedly with low
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
variance.
title: 2018 Low-Power Image Recognition Challenge

Abstract
Evolutionary algorithm research and applications began over 50 years ago.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Like other artiﬁcial
intelligence techniques, evolutionary algorithms will likely see increased use and development due to
the increased availability of computation, more robust and available open source software libraries,
and the increasing demand for artiﬁcial intelligence techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
As these techniques become more
adopted and capable, it is the right time to take a perspective of their ability to integrate into
society and the human processes they intend to augment.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In this review, we explore a new taxonomy
of evolutionary algorithms and resulting classiﬁcations that look at ﬁve main areas: the ability to
manage the control of the environment with limiters, the ability to explain and repeat the search
process, the ability to understand input and output causality within a solution, the ability to manage
algorithm bias due to data or user design, and lastly, the ability to add corrective measures.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These
areas are motivated by today’s pressures on industry to conform to both societies concerns and new
government regulatory rules.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
As many reviews of evolutionary algorithms exist, after motivating this
new taxonomy, we brieﬂy classify a broad range of algorithms and identify areas of future research.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

1
Preface
When attempting to ﬁnd a perfect combination of chemicals for a speciﬁc problem, a chemist will un-
dertake a set of experiments.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
They know roughly what needs to be achieved but not necessarily how
to achieve it.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: A chemist will create a number of experiments.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Each experiment is a combination of
diﬀerent chemicals.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Following some theoretical basis for the experiments.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The experiments are played
out and the promising solutions are identiﬁed and gathered together.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These new chemical combinations
are then used as the basis for the next round of experiments.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This procedure is repeated until hopefully
a satisfactory chemical combination is discovered.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The reason this discovery method is adopted is because the interactions between the various chemicals
is too complicated and potentially unknown.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This eﬀectively makes the problem-domain too large to ex-
plore.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
An Evolutionary Algorithm (EA) replaces the decision making by the chemist, using evolutionary
principles to explore the problem-space.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs handle situations that are too complex to be solved with
current knowledge or capability using a form of synthetic digital evolution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The exciting part is that
the solutions themselves can be original, taking advantage of eﬀects or attributes previously unknown
to the problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs provide a framework that can be reused across diﬀerent domains, they are mostly
biologically-inspired algorithms that reside as a subbranch of Artiﬁcial Intelligence (AI).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Using Bertrand Russell’s method of deﬁning philosophy [46] i.e.“as soon as deﬁnite knowledge concerning
any subject becomes possible, this subject ceases to be called philosophy, and becomes a separate sci-
ence”.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: AI research lives in-between philosophy and science.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Ideas transition from philosophical thought
to applied science and truth.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Within Computer Science, the AI ﬁeld resides at the edge of knowledge
and as such includes a distinct part which is more philosophical and another which is more rooted in
science.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: In this review we cover one of the science aspects.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
AI science incorporates many areas of
research e.g.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Neural Networks, Bayesian Networks, Evolutionary Algorithms, Correlation, Game Theory,
Planning, Vision recognition, Decision making, Natural Language Processing, etc.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It is a dynamically
changing list as more discoveries are made or developed.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Thirdly, Machine Learning is the engineering
discipline which applies the science to a real world problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
One of the overriding motivators driving Machine Learning in recent years has been the desire to replace
rigid rule-based systems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A strong candidate has been emerging which is both adaptive and outcome-
based.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This technology relies on data-directed inputs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
JeﬀBezos, CEO of Amazon, succinctly described
this concept in a letter to shareholders in 2017 [44], ”Over the past decades computers have broadly
automated tasks that programmers could describe with clear rules and algorithms.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Modern Machine
Learning techniques now allow us to do the same for tasks where describing the precise rules is much
harder.”.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Also Kazuo Yano, Fellow and Corporate Oﬃcer of Hitachi Ltd, said in his keynote at the 2018
Genetic and Evolutionary Computation Conference (GECCO) [31] that the demand for more ﬂexibility
forces us to transition from traditional rule-oriented systems to future outcome-oriented ones.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The adaptability and transition to outcome-oriented systems means, from an end user perspective,
there is more uncertainly surrounding the ﬁnal result.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is construed as being either real or per-
ceived.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Rule-based systems are not impervious but tend to be deterministic and understandable e.g.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: the most notable being the area of safety-critical systems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This uncertainty creates the notion of User
Control Attributes (UCA).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The UCA include the concepts of limiters [65], explainability [26], causality
[3], fairness [27,64] and correction [45].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These attributes have seen a lot of scrutiny in recent years
due to high-proﬁle public errors, as detailed in the AI Now 2018 Report [45].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The report goes into the
details of fairness and highlights the various procedures, transparency and accountability required for
1


Machine Learning systems to be safely applied in real social environments.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Also worth mentioning is
the International Standard Organization (ISO), which has formed a study group focusing speciﬁcally
on Trustworthiness [51].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The study will be investigating methods to improve basic trust in Machine
Learning systems by exploring transparency, verify-ability, explainability, and control-ability.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The study
will also look at mitigation techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The goal is to improve overall robustness, resiliency, reliability,
accuracy, safety, security and privacy; and by doing so hopefully minimize source biases.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For this review
we will limit the focus to research, while at the same time being cognizant of the dangers of real world
deployment.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Control imposes a diﬀerent level of thinking, where researchers are not just given a problem to solve but
the solution requires a model justifying the outcome.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
That model has to provide the answers to the main
questions: Whether the algorithm stays within limits/restrictions?
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Can
the algorithm predict beyond historical data?
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Does the algorithm avoid system biases or even side-step
replicating human prejudices [83]?
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: And ﬁnally, can the algorithm be corrected?
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These attributes are
not mutually exclusive and in fact intertwine with each other.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
We can see a trend where modern Ma-
chine Learning algorithms will be rated not only on the quality of the results but on how well they cope
with the user demanded control attributes.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: These attributes are to be used as a basis for a new taxonomy.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This is a good point to start discussing the Computer Industry.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The industry itself is facing a set of new
challenges and simultaneously adding new capabilities, as summarized below:
• Silicon level: groups are starting to work on the problem of mass silicon production at the
3-nanometer scale and smaller [63].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This involves designing gates and transistors at a scale
unimaginable 10 or even 5-years ago, using enhanced lithographic techniques and grappling with
quantum tunneling issues.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These unprecedented improvements have allowed other areas higher
up the software stack to ﬂourish.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Unfortunately these advancements are slowing down, as the
current techniques hit both physical and economic limitations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This situation is called the End of
Moore’s Law (EoML) [61,62].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• System level: A number of levels above the silicon lies the system-level which also has seen some
impressive advancements with the world-wide web, network infrastructure and data centers that
connect everyone with everyone.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The scale of the system-level advancements has opened up the
possibility of mimicking small parts of the human brain.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
One such project is called SpiNNaker
[8].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
SpiNNaker was upgraded and switched on in November 2018, it now consists of a million
interconnected ARM cores each executing Spiking Neural Networks (SNN) [41].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Even with all the
hardware capability, estimates suggest that it is only equivalent to about 1% of a human brain.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• Software design level: Software design, at the other end of the spectrum, has been constantly
pursuing automation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The hope being that automation leads to the ability to handle more com-
plicated problems, which in turn provides more opportunities.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
New programming languages, new
software paradigms and higher level data-driven solutions all contribute to improving software
automation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: To handle these new challenges and capabilities requires a continuously changing toolbox of techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: EAs are one such tool and like other tools they have intrinsic advantages and disadvantages.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Recently
EAs have seen a resurgence of enthusiasm, which comes at an interesting time since other branches of
Machine Learning become mature and crowded.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This maturity forces some researchers to explore com-
binations of techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
As can be seen in this review a lot of the new focus and vigor is centered upon
2


hybrid solutions, especially important is the area of combining evolutionary techniques with Artiﬁcial
Neural Networks (ANNs).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
3


2
Introduction
EAs are not a new subject.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In fact as we look back at some of the early computing pioneers we see exam-
ples of evolutionary discovery.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For example both Alan Turing [39] and John von Neumann [40] formed
ideas around Biological Automation, Biological Mathematics and Machine Learning.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These forward
visionaries focused on the fact that exploitative methods could only go so far to solve diﬃcult problems
and more exploratory methods were required.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The main diﬀerence between the two techniques is that
exploitative focuses on direct local knowledge to obtain a solution whereas exploratory takes eﬀectively
a more stochastic approach (leaping into the unknown).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Figure 2.1: Hardware capability and algorithmic eﬃciency over an idealized time line
Figure 2.1 shows an idealized view of the changes to hardware capability and algorithmic eﬃciency over
a time period.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The ﬁgure shows the relationship between improvements in hardware and the types of
problems that can be addressed.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Before 2010, the computing industry mostly focused on exploitative
problems ”getting things to work eﬃciently”.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Today, due to hardware improvements, we can look at
exploratory algorithms that ”discover”.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
At the extremes of the X-Y axis, top-right and bottom-right lies
the respective future potentials of hardware and software i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
4


Note: End of Dennard Scaling [78] marks the point in time when transistor shrinkage no-longer sustained
a constant power density.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In other words, static power consumption dominates the power equation for
silicon.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Forcing the industry to use clever frequency and design duplication techniques to mitigate the
problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Deep Learning [79] represents the software resurgence of Neural Nets, due to hardware im-
provements and the availability of large training data sets.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The Hardware Capability top-right of the graph represents future hardware concepts, and requires subse-
quent manufacturing breakthroughs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These future concepts could include alternative computing models,
Quantum computing, Neuromorphic architectures, new exotic materials, Asynchronous processing, etc..
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
By contrast the Algorithmic Eﬃciency bottom-right represents future breakthroughs in subjects like
Artiﬁcial Life, Artiﬁcial General Intelligence (AGI), etc.; more philosophical goals than either science or
engineering.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Both require signiﬁcant advancements beyond what we have today.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
With these future developments, the desire is to set a problem-goal and let the ”system” ﬁnd the correct
answer.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This is extremely simple to state but highly complex to implement.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
And more importantly, next
to impossible to implement without direct insertion of domain speciﬁc knowledge into the algorithm in
question.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
No Free Lunch Theorem [74] states that no algorithm exists which outperforms every other algorithm
for every problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This means to be successful, each problem requires some form of domain speciﬁc
knowledge to be eﬃcient.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The more domain speciﬁc knowledge applied to an algorithm the greater the
likelihood of beating a stochastic algorithm.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A stochastic algorithm can search every problem, without
the requirement of domain knowledge.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: EAs are directed population-based stochastic search algorithms.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: As hardware capability increases more of these types of problems can be handled.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It is the constraints
of time and eﬃciency that forces domain knowledge to be inserted into an algorithm.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This paper provides an up-to-date review of the various EAs, there respective options and how they may
be applied to diﬀerent problem-domains.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs are a family of biologically-inspired algorithms that take
advantage of synthetic methods, namely management of populations, replication, variability and ﬁnally
selection.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: All based upon the fundamental theory of Darwinian evolution [5].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
As a general rule the
algorithms are often simple at a high-level but become increasingly complex as more domain knowledge
is put into the system.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Another term frequently used to describe these style of algorithms is metaheuristics.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Metaheauristics is a
higher-order concept, it is an algorithm that systematically pursues the identiﬁcation of the best solution
within a problem-space.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs obviously fall under this class of algorithms and a lot of the academic lit-
erature frequently refers to metaheuristics: the main diﬀerentiator being biologically inspired algorithms.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: For these algorithms to execute, some form of quantitative goal has to be set.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The success metric can also be used as a method to exit the algorithm but most often a
function of time is used.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The algorithm can also be designed to be continuous i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The goal itself can be made up of a single objective or multi-objectives.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For multi-objective the
search and optimization is towards the pareto optimal curve i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
attempting to satisfy all the objectives
in some degree.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
As an important side-note, EAs are mostly derivative-free, in that majority do not require a derivative
function to measure change to determine the optimal result.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
5


Lastly, GECCO 2018 [31], in Kyoto, saw a number of trends.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Neuroevolution being one of the more
notable ones, Neuroevolution is the method of using EAs to conﬁgure ANNs (see section 5.2).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These
new trends will be tracked in more detail in future reviews if they remain popular in the evolutionary
research community.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
2.1
Applications
EAs are applied to problems where traditional exploitative or pure stochastic algorithms fail or ﬁnd it dif-
ﬁcult to reach a conclusion.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is normally due to constraints on resources, high number of dimensions
or complex functionality.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Solving these problems would require exceeding the available resources.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In
other words, given inﬁnite resources and inﬁnite compute capability it could be possible for a traditional
exploitative or stochastic algorithm to reach a conclusion.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
By contrast, EAs can be thought of as the
algorithms-of-last-resort.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The problems in question are inherently complex, size of the problem-domain
is extreme or the mere number of objectives make the problem impossibly diﬃcult to explore.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In these
circumstances the solutions are more likely ”good enough” solutions rather than solutions with high
precision or accuracy (but this does not preclude precision or accuracy being a goal).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs tend to be
poor candidates for simple problems where standard techniques could easily be used instead.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: They can be applied to a broad set of problem types.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These types range from variable optimization
problems to creating new conceptual designs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In both instances, novelty can occur which may exceed
human understanding or ability.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These problem-domains can be broken-down into optimization, new
design and improvement.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• Variable optimization consists of searching a variable space for a ”good” solution, where the
number of variables being searched is large.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Potentially at a magnitude greater than a traditional
programming problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This is where the goal can be strictly deﬁned.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• New structural design consists of creating a completely new solution, for example like a pro-
gram or a mechanical design.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A famous example, of a non-anthropomorphized solution, is the
evolutionary designed NASA antenna [38].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The antenna design was not necessarily something a
human would have created.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is where a particular outcome is desired but it is unknown how
that outcome can be constructed.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• Improvement is where a known working solution is placed into the system and EAs explore
potential better versions.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is where a solution already exists and there is a notion that a
potential better solution can be discovered.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Being more speciﬁc on the applications side, EAs have been applied to a wide range of problems from
leading edge research on self-assembly cellular automata [67] to projecting future city landscapes for
town planners (see section 6.2.3).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
6


3
Fundamentals of Digital Evolution
Before diving directly into the fundamentals we should stress that there are two ways to describe evolu-
tion.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The ﬁrst is from a pure biology point-of-view dealing the various interactions of biological systems
and the other is from the Computer Science perspective.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In this paper we will keep the focus on
Computer Science with a hint of biology.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Other texts may approach the explanation from a diﬀerent
perspective.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Evolution is a dynamic mechanism that includes a population of entities (potential solutions) where
some form of replication, variation and selection occurs on those entities, as shown in ﬁgure 3.1.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This
is a stochastic but guided process where the desire is to move towards a ﬁxed goal.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• Replication: Is where new entities are formed, either creating a completely new generation of the
population or altering speciﬁc individuals within the same population (called steady-state).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • Variation: Making the population diverse.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There are in eﬀect two forms of variation, namely
recombination and mutation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Recombination, or more commonly called crossover, creates new
entities by combining parts of other entities.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
By contrast, mutation injects randomness into the
population by stochastic-ally changing speciﬁc features of the entities.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• Selection: Selection is based on Darwin’s natural selection, or Survival Of The Fittest, where
selected entities that show the most promise are carried forward, with variation on the selection
being used to create the children of the next generation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Figure 3.1: Idealized Darwinian Evolution
As a recap, digital evolution is one which a population of entities goes through generational changes.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Each change starts with a selection from the previous generation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Each entity is evaluated against a
known speciﬁc goal i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: the ﬁtness is established and used as input to the selection algorithm.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Once a
selection is made, replication occurs with diﬀerent degrees of variation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The variation is either by some
form of recombination from the parent selection and/or some stochastic mutation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
7


Figure 3.2: Basic Digital Process
Figure 3.2 shows the basic digital process that is adopted by many EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The high level synthetic evolu-
tionary process as-shown is a relatively straightforward and simple procedure.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Within the process there
are many complex nuances and variations, which are inﬂuenced by our understanding of evolutionary
biology.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
3.1
Population
A population is a set of solution candidates or entities.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Each population is created temporally and has
the potential to age with each evolutionary cycle i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The initial population is either seeded
randomly or is sampled from a set of known solutions.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There are two ways for the population to be
evolved.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This ﬁrst way consists of evolving the entire population to create the next generation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The
second way is to evolve individual entities within the population (called Steady-State).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Entities can die
or thrive between generations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The size of the population can be ﬁxed or dynamic throughout the evolutionary process.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Fixed is when
the number of entities is kept constant and dynamic is when the population size changes.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
If dynamic,
a larger initial population may bring some potential advantages.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is especially true when choosing
the ﬁrst strong candidates for further evolution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: A population can also be divided into subgroups, these subgroups are called demes.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A deme is a
biological term that describes a group of evolving organisms with the same taxonomy.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
They can evolve
in isolation within the population [1].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Demes can be made to interact with the other demes.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is often
described using an island and canoe metaphor, where the demes are the islands and the interactions
occur as canoes move between the islands depositing new entities.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
8


3.2
Population Entities
The population entities, or more commonly called phenotypes, can be any type provided that type al-
lows recombination and/or mutation to be applied.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The main styles are strings and programs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In this
context ”programs” is a loose term.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The strings are ﬁxed length and more likely represent variables
or parameters.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Eﬀectively any structure from a traditional
computer programming language to hardware layout, or even biological descriptions, can be a program.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Metaheuristics operate at a high-level making the process generic, allowing idea or concept can be
used as the evolved substrate.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Including concepts like Deep Learning Neural Network or potentially a
causality equation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs are neutral on the subject but when it comes to speciﬁc problems, the problems
themselves, tend to be strictly deﬁned.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There are two important concepts to consider with population entities, namely niching and crowding
[4].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: These terms are associated with diversity, which is brieﬂy mentioned in section 3.1.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Niching means
individual entities survive generations in distinct areas of the search space.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
By contrast, crowding means
replacing an individual entity with similar featured individuals.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
3.3
Generation
A generation is a speciﬁc step in an evolutionary population, where individuals in the population un-
dergo change via crossover and/or mutation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For EAs with a ﬁxed-run a restriction is imposed on
the number of generations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: By contrast, continuous EAs have no upper bounds.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs can vary from
small populations with high number of generations to large populations with signiﬁcantly lower number
of generations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: These trade-oﬀs need to be made in terms of computation time.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For example, some
scenarios will have expensive evaluation functions (so fewer generations with larger populations might
be preferred).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The number of generations required is both algorithmic and problem-domain speciﬁc.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The children in the next generation can also include the parents from the previous generation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is
called elitism, where the strongest entities remain in the population.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
3.4
Representation and the grammar
Representation, or more commonly called genotype, is what EAs manipulate.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There are diﬀerent types
of representations which include strings, tree structures, linear structures and direct-graphs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Each rep-
resentation has advantages and disadvantages, and is dependent on the speciﬁc problem-domain.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The
representation determines what actually gets manipulated when recombination occurs, some lend them-
selves more to fractal/recursive like procedures and the others are more sequential and linear.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: By contrast, the rules are deﬁned by the grammar.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs grammar provides the expressive boundaries for
the representation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For example, in a mathematical domain adding a function like sin(x) to the grammar
provides extra richness and complexity to the representation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Similarly, for string based representations
adding or removing a variable to the grammar changes the expressiveness.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Other decisions can be
made for structural EAs, such-as including more constructors (e.g.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: subtraction), vice-versa or more commonly keeping the grammar entirely balanced i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
same number of
constructors as destructors.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Possible grammars include a subset of Python or C, assembly instructions or even pure LLVM interme-
diate code [56].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
9


3.5
Fitness
Fitness is the measure of how close a result is to a desired goal.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A ﬁtness function is the algorithm used
to calculate the ﬁtness value.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Calculating the ﬁtness value for an entire population is a time consuming
activity.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The time taken is related to the complexity of the ﬁtness function and the size of the population
being evaluated.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The ﬁtness function is used to select individuals for inclusion in future populations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The function can be constant throughout the evolutionary process or it can change depending upon the
desired goal or situation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: It is the feature of ﬁtness function change that makes EAs highly adaptive.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The ﬁtness can be calculated using diﬀerent methods e.g.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Area Under the Curve (AUC) from a test
set, measurement of a robot responding to a set of trials, etc.; each method being problem dependent.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For supervised learning it is calculated as the diﬀerence between the desired goal and the actual result
obtained from the entity.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Conversely, for unsupervised learning there are other methods.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Once the
ﬁtness has been determined the entities can be ranked/sorted by strength.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The stronger candidates are
more likely to be chosen as parents for the next generation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
3.6
Selection
Selection is the method where individuals in the current population are chosen to be the starting par-
ents for the next generations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In digital evolution, parents are not restricted to two; any number can
be chosen.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A simple method is to use the ﬁtness value to order the population, this method is called
ranked selection.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: A population can be organized from the highest to lowest ﬁtness value.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The highest
entities are then used as the starting parents for the next generation and so forth.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
As mentioned in
section 3.3, elitism is where the chosen parents remain in the next population rather than being discarded.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Diversity [4] is an important concept when it comes to a healthy population.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Healthy populations
are important for discovering ”good” solutions.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In other words, a diverse population has a higher ex-
ploratory capability.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This tends to be important especially at the start of the search process.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Diversity
is directly associated with the amount of variation applied to the entities.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It can be argued that local
selection schemes [1,4] (steady-state) are naturally more likely to preserve diversity over global selection
scheme.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Local selection means evolution is potentially occurring at diﬀerent rates across the population.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: An example of a local selection scheme is called tournament selection.
