title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
As the name implies, selection
requires running a tournament between a randomly chosen set of individuals.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The ”winner” of each
tournament is then selected for further evolution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Note: there are other selection schemes, which are not covered here.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
3.7
Multi-objective
As the name implies multi-objective is the concept of not having a single objective but multiple objectives.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: These objectives may act against each other in complex ways i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It is this interaction which
makes multi-objective so complex.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A typical example in the mobile phone industry is ﬁnding the optimum
position between performance, power consumption (longevity) and cost.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These three objectives can
be satisﬁed to diﬀerent degrees, eﬀectively giving the end consumer a choice of options.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Too much
performance may sacriﬁce longevity + cost, low cost may sacriﬁce performance + longevity and so-on.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs are extremely good at exploring multi-objective problems where the ﬁtness is around a compromise
along the Pareto curve.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
10


3.8
Constraints
Constraints are the physical goals, as compared with the objectives which are the logical goals.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The
physical goals represent the real world limitations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
They take a theoretical problem and make it real-
istic.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Constraints are the limitations imposed on the entities.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A constraint could be code size, energy
consumption or execution time.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EA Researchers have discovered some of the most interesting and
potentially best solutions tend to lie somewhere at the edge of the constraint boundaries.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
3.9
Exploitative-exploratory search
EAs use recombination and mutation for exploitative and exploratory search.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The more mutation that
occurs the more exploratory the search, and correspondingly the less mutation the more exploitative the
search.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs can be at either end of the spectrum, with only recombination (more exploitative) or only
mutation (more exploratory).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The ratios of recombination and mutation can be ﬁxed or dynamic.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
By
making the ratios dynamic EAs can adapt to changing circumstances.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This shift may occur when the
potential ”good” solution is perceived to be either near or far.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Another way to view this is that mutation
is a local search and recombination (or crossover) is a global search.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Recombination, despite using only
existing genetic material, often takes much larger jumps in the search space than does mutation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
3.10
Execution environment, modularity and system scale
EAs can execute as a process within an Operating System, as a self-constructed dynamic program feed
into a language interpreter (e.g.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Python exec(open(”ea.py”).read())), or within a simulator, where the
simulator can be a physics simulator, biological simulator and/or a processor simulator.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs are generic
and literally any executing model can be used to explore a desired problem-domain.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: To handle larger problems some form of modularity has to be adopted.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There are many schemes in-
cluding ones that introduce tree based processing or Byzantine style algorithms i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Modularity tends to work best when the problem granularity is relatively small and concise, such as a
function-call.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The normal questions asked are (1) whether all the function-calls use the same input data,
(2) whether all information is shared between the functions, or (2) whether a hierarchy of evolution has
to be adopted i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: from function call to full solution or from local to global parameter conﬁguration.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: EAs can scale from one process to many processes running on several server clusters [42,70,75,76].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: These compute clusters are called islands.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: They operate in either a parallel and/or distributed fashion.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: A parallel system is a set of evolving islands working together towards a common goal.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Genetic material
or solutions can be shared.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
We should highlight that there are a few options when it comes to parallel
topologies.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
By comparison, the distributed approach, which can include parallel islands, is about the
physical aspect of running on various hardware systems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
With both approaches, scale-out co-ordination
becomes an important issue i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
the management of the islands becomes part of the performance equa-
tion.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Lastly, it is important to mention co-evolution in the context of scaling.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Co-evolution is where two or
more evolving populations (eﬀectively species) start interfering/cooperating with each other.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is
particular important when digital evolution is being used to build much larger systems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Both modu-
larity and system scale add an extra layer of complexity.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Scale is a required necessity to answer more
complicated problems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
11


3.11
Code bloat and clean-up
The EAs which play with structures can quite easily have to deal with the problem of bloat [84].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Bloat
is a byproduct of exploring a problem-domain.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Historically this was a major issue with the earlier algo-
rithms due to hardware limitations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Today, modern systems have an abundance of compute and storage.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This does not mean the limitation has gone away but it is mitigated to a certain extent.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Bloat may
be critically important to the evolutionary process.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In nature the more that is discovered the more it
seems that very little is actually wasted.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Non-coding regions are not bloat, they are crucial parts to the
process of molecular mechanisms.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There are structures or code sequences that have no value, as-in the result is circumvented by other
code or structures.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: These neutral or noneﬀective structures are called introns.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Intron is a biological term
referring to the noneﬀective fragments found in DNA.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For software programs, introns are code sequences
that are noneﬀective or neutral; these sequences can be identiﬁed and cleaned-up, i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The
elimination can occur either during the evolutionary process itself or at a ﬁnal stage.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Note, introns can
be critically important to the process, so early removal can be detrimental.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
3.12
Non-convergence, or early local optima
There has been a lot of research focusing on the problems of non-convergence and early-local-optima
solutions.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Non-convergence means that the evolving entities are not making enough progress towards
a solution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Early-local-optima means a sub-optimal solution has been found at the beginning of the
evolutionary process.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This sub-optimal solution has caused the algorithm to limit further exploration,
reducing the chance of ﬁnding a better solution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Non-convergence is caused by many factors including the possibility of not having the right data.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs
rely on stochastic processes to move toward, which means that the paths taken are unique, unrepeat-
able and non-deterministic; unique in the sense that the paths taken are always diﬀerent, unrepeatable
as-in randomness is used to determine the next direction, non-deterministic as-in the length of time to
solution is variable.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: To get to a potential solution may require reruns of the algorithm.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Each rerun
potentially requiring some form of ﬁne adjustment to help narrow into a good solution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In the end,
when everything else fails, more domain speciﬁc knowledge may have to be inserted before convergence
eventually occurs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It is important to stress that the ﬁnal solution may very well be deterministic and
repeatable, it is the evolutionary process to create the solution which may not be.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Similar to non-convergence is the problem of reaching a local extrema too early, and then EAs iterate
persistently around a point not discovering a better solution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Again, the techniques used for non-
convergence tend to be used to avoid the local optima scenario.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Identiﬁcation of a local optima can be
diﬃcult since the global optima is unknown.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
After multiple readjustments hopefully the global optima
can be discovered.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
3.13
Other useful terms
There are other terms which are worthy of a mention and brief descriptions.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The ﬁrst terms are the
Baldwin Eﬀect [12] and Lamarckian Evolution [13] both important concepts for digital evolution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The
Baldwin Eﬀect is about how learned behavior eﬀects evolution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is important for EAs that improve
towards a solution under techniques such as elitism (as brieﬂy mentioned in section 3.3).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
And Lamar-
ckian Evolution which theorizes that children can inherit characteristics from the experiences gained by
12


their parents.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Again, an important concept with direct implications for digital evolution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: By contrast, the term overﬁtting [18] describes a situation that should be avoided.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It is when the
data noise containing irrelevant information and what is actually being discovered combine into a result
(conﬁguration parameters).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs overﬁt when the discovered parameters satisﬁes the complete data-set
and not the data for the speciﬁc exploration, making it eﬀectively useless for any future prediction using
other input data sources.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The potential concern is the increased risk of a false-positive outcome.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Lastly, Genetic Drift [68,69] is a basic evolutionary mechanism found in nature, where some genotype
entries between generations leave more descendants or parts than others.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These descendants are in the
population by random chance.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
They are neither in the next generation because of a strong attribute nor
higher ﬁtness value.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: In nature this happens to all populations and there is little chance for avoidance.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs genetic drift can be as a result of a combination of factors, primarily related to selection, ﬁtness
function and representation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: It happens by unintentional loss of genotypes.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For example, random chance
that a good genotype solution never gets selected for reproduction.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Or, if there is a “lifespan” to a
solution and it dies before it can reproduce.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Normally such a genotype only resides in the population
for a limited number of generations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
13


4
Traditional techniques
In this section we brieﬂy cover the traditional and well known EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These EAs tend to be older and
more mature techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The techniques covered are frequently used by industry and research.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There
are numerous support frameworks available to experiment with [72,6,29,71].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Assume for each technique
discussed that there are many more variations available.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Figure 4.1: Relationships between traditional EA techniques
Figure 4.1 shows the relationships between the various traditional techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For this review we have
decided to focus more on Genetic Programming and the various sub-categories.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In future reviews this
emphasis will likely change.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
4.1
Evolutionary Strategy, ES
Evolutionary Strategy, ES [4,42,48] is one of the oldest EAs, developed in the 1960s at the Technical
University of Berlin; it usually only involves mutation and selection.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Entities are selected using trunca-
tion selection.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
After the entities are evaluated, the entries below the truncation point are systematically
removed from the population.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The remaining parents are mutated to buildup a new population.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Modern implementations include Co-variance Matrix Adaptation - Evolutionary Strategy CMA-ES [15]
and an alternative Co-variance Matrix Self Adaptation - Evolutionary Strategy CMSA-ES.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
CMA-ES is
thought to be complicated to implement, and CMSA-ES is a newer alternative and is believed to be
easier to implement [73].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: An ES is used to solve continuous parameter optimization.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A parameter
is deﬁned by its type and interval range (upper and lower bounds).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A continuous parameter can take
any value within the interval range.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The precision determines the minimum change value.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
14


4.2
Genetic Algorithms, GA
Genetic Algorithms, GA [4,24,42] is the most common and popular among the EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
GA applies evolution
to ﬁxed length strings.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The length of the string represents the dimensionality of the problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These
strings represent variables or parameters and are useful when exploring a large number problem-domain
space.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This space is normally beyond human or traditional methods.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
As well as being popular, GAs are
also the most commonly taught algorithm within the various EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Variables or parameters are converted
to ﬁxed length strings, the strings are entities in the population and are evolved using crossover windows
and mutation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Crossover is ubiquitous but explicit crossover windows are not.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
By comparison to an ES
(section 4.1), a GA tends to be more generic.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It should be noted that a recent trend has emerged, in both GAs and ESs, where crossover is dropped
and mutation is the sole mechanism for evolution (this diﬀers to the earlier thinking expressed in the
classical literature).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
GAs handle optimization and conﬁguration problems where there are
too many variables or parameters for a traditional method to succeed.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The variables or parameters may
interact making a potential solution much harder to identify.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
4.3
Genetic Programming, GP
Genetic Programming, GP [20,21,22,23] in contrast to GAs, manipulate structures and in-particular
executable programs or mathematical equations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Early GPs were based on tree representations and used
the LISP programming language as the grammar.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
LISP was chosen for its operator richness and was rel-
atively easily to manipulate.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
More recently there have been other representations introduced and newer
languages such as Python have become popular as the main target.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The recombination carries out the
global search, whereas the mutation covers the local search.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It is frequently common for mutation to be
limited to 5-10% of the population [20].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There are always exceptions, especially if the % mechanisms
are dynamically altered between generations [4].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: GPs apply evolutionary techniques to code or functions.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
GPs handle
the manipulation of programs, so that problems that are linear, tree or direct-graph based can be
explored.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
GPs can produce original source code, and in fact ﬁnd new novel solutions to any structural
style problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: In industry, GP are mostly used to discover best ﬁt mathematical equations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
4.4
Genetic Improvement, GI
Genetic Improvement, GI [17] is a subclass of GP (section 4.3), where instead of a random initial seeded
population, a working program is inserted as the starting point to spawn entities of the ﬁrst population.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is a powerful concept since it does not only search for a better optimized solution but also has the
potential to discover and correct faults in the original ”working” code.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Solves an interesting problem, where either the working code is
potentially un-optimized and a more optimized version is required or bringing legacy code up to current
standards.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
15


4.5
Grammatical Evolution, GE
Grammatical Evolution, GE [6] is a powerful technique.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It is yet another subclass of GP (section 4.3)
but instead of using a ﬁxed grammar to evolve-able solutions, the grammar itself is select-able.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A good
example of GE is the PonyGE2 [6] tool, written in Python.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It takes a standard Backus-Naur Form
(BNF) grammar [16] as an input and uses it to evolves solutions.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is a powerful method especially
when dealing with more obscure programming languages.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: GE can also carry out GI (see section 4.4).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Note the PonyGE2 source code is available on GitHub.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
GE solves the problem of evolving multiple programming languages
using the same tool.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: As long as the language has a BNF-style deﬁnition, it can be evolved.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This
makes GE ﬂexible across a number of problem-domains, and especially ones which require a speciﬁc
programming language.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
4.6
Linear Genetic Programming, LGP
Linear Genetic Programming, LGP [1] is a subclass of GP (section 4.3) and as the name implies uses
a linear structure representation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The linear structure has some advantages over the more complicated
tree or directed-graph structures.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: LGP is particularly useful for problems which are more sequential.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: For example, optimizing low level assembly output.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It also makes the problem of manipulating complex
structures easier since it is a linear ﬂow that is being evolved.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Constructs like if-style control ﬂow or
loops are superimposed onto the linear structure.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The linear aspect of this technique introduces an
ordering constraint, which potentially has Turing Machine and/or Turing complete ramiﬁcations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is particular useful for
optimizing programs and low level assembly style output.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Or any problem-domain where the problem
being explored is about sequential ordering.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
4.7
Cartesian Genetic Programming, CGP
Rather than linear or tree based, Cartesian Genetic Programming CGP [2] is based on Cartesian co-
ordinates and directed-graphs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: One basic characteristic is that the population is small (e.g.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The small population goes through a large number of generations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
CGP is uniquely
qualiﬁed to handle speciﬁc problems extremely well.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: EAs themselves can be temporal by default.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
CGP
introduces the concept of spatial awareness into EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
CGP has been shown to be useful at circuit layout design since the
logic components require some form of spatial awareness.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Interestingly since CGP is spatial it can also
be used to produce artistic designs/patterns.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Recent research shows that CGP can achieve competitive
results on the Atari benchmark set [28].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
CGP can also encode ANNs by adding weights to the links in
the graph, allowing them to do neuroevolution (see section 5.2).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
4.8
Diﬀerential Evolution, DE
Diﬀerential Evolution, DE [4,42] is an example of a non-biologically inspired algorithm but falls under
the metaheuristic category.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: It is based on iterating a population towards a quality goal.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The iteration
involves recombination, evaluation and selection.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A new candi-
date is based on a weighted diﬀerence between random candidates to create a third candidate, shifting
16


the population to a higher quality level.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Each new population eﬀectively self-organizes.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Works best on Boolean, Integer spaces and Reals.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
DE was developed
speciﬁcally to ﬁnd the Chebyshev polynomial coeﬃcients and the optimization of digital ﬁlter coeﬃcients.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
4.9
Gene Expression Programming, GEP
Gene Expression Programming, GEP [43,50] is a subclass of both GA (section 4.2) and GP (section 4.3).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This method borrows from both techniques, as-in it uses ﬁxed length strings which encode expression
trees.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The expression trees can be of varied size.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Evolution occurs on the simple linear, ﬁxed length
strings.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It oﬀers a powerful linear encoding which is guaranteed to pro-
duce valid programs, since GEP follows the syntactic rules of the speciﬁc programming language being
targeted.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This makes it easy to implement powerful genetic operators.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
17


5
Specialized techniques and concepts
In this section we cover some of the more exotic EAs and extended tools.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These EAs are new, hybrids
or just miscellaneous concepts.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is not an exhaustive list but a more holistic subset of ideas that
do not follow the traditional evolutionary methods.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A few of the techniques covered in this section are
not technically based on biological or synthetic evolution but play an important role in the process or
are placed here due to taxonomy convenience.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Figure 5.1: Relationships between specialized techniques and concepts
Figure 5.1 shows the relationships between the specialized techniques and concepts.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These relationships
are more tenuous than the relationships found between the various traditional EA techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
5.1
Auto-constructive Evolution
Auto-constructive Evolution [25] is where instead of having an overarching algorithm orchestrating the
artiﬁcial evolution process, entities themselves are given the ability to undergo evolution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This means
that children are constructed by their own parents.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Parents have an ability to produce children, without
the need of a master synthetic algorithm.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is in contrast to the more traditional EAs where the
artiﬁcial replication occurs at a higher level.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: What problems does auto-constructive evolution solve?
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Provides a method to carry out micro-
evolution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This type of evolution is more inline with the goal of building Artiﬁcial Life.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Potentially has
an advantage to scale since it requires no centralized coordination.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
5.2
Neuroevolution, or Deep Neuroevolution
Neuroevolution [53,30,47,59] is classed as a hybrid solution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It has become more popular in recent
years.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: It was a noticeably hot topic in GECCO 2018 [31].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Neuroevolution is the concept of using some
form of GA to discover the optimal way to setup a Deep Neural Network (DNN).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The entities being
18


optimized are artiﬁcial neural networks (ANNs).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Or, it can be used in combination with supervised
learning and reinforcement learning (RL) techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The family of neuroevolution algorithms can be
further classiﬁed based on how the candidate solutions are encoded and how much they can vary.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
As
mentioned previously, CGP (section 4.7) can also be an eﬀective way to evolve ANNs by adding weights
to the links.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• Direct encoding: parameters of every artiﬁcial neuron and connection are part of the solution
encoding.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • Indirect encoding: is a ”recipe” for generating ANNs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The topology can be either ﬁxed or
evolving.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Fixed means that only the connection weights are optimized, whereas evolving means
both the connection weights and the topology of the ANN are modiﬁed.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This latter class of
algorithms is commonly called Topology and Weight Evolving Artiﬁcial Neural Network algorithms
(TWEANNs).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Notable examples of TWEANNs are Neuroevolution of Augmenting Topologies (NEAT) [9] and its suc-
cessor HyperNEAT [10].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The former uses a direct encoding while the latter uses an indirect encoding
called ”Compositional Pattern Producing Networks” (CPPN) [57].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Another example of a TWEANN
approach using an indirect encoding is ”Evolutionary Acquisition of Neural Topologies” (EANT2) [58].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Neuroevolution combines ideas from Genetic Algorithms
and Artiﬁcial Neural Networks.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It can evolve both ANN weights and topologies making it an attractive
alternative to ML hyper-parameter hand-crafting.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
By contrast with backpropagation, neuroevolution is
not limited to diﬀerentiable domains [59].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
5.3
Self-replicating Neural Networks
Self-replicating Neural Networks [7] is a relatively new idea where the ANNs themselves re-conﬁgure.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Currently the idea is to have the network learn by producing their own weights as output also to have
regeneration.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Regeneration is the concept of training an ANN by inserting predictions of its own pa-
rameters.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This technique is still being researched and is at a very early stage.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Vigorous exploration is
still required but this idea has potential to be become more important.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Expect to see forward progress
in this area.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: What problems do Self-replicating Neural Networks solve?
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Early
research shows some promise in the area of continual ANN improvement using natural selection.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
5.4
Markov Brains
Markov Brains [32] is in an early stage.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Markov Brains belong to the same hybrid group as neuroevolu-
tion.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Based on ANNs with some signiﬁcant diﬀerences.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Normal ANNs are designed with layers built-up
from nodes with the same functional characteristic.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Markov Brains are networks built from nodes with
diﬀerent computational characteristics.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The components interact with each other, and can connect with
external sensors (physical inputs) and actuators (physical outputs).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is still relatively early days for Markov Brains but they
are showing some early promise especially in unsupervised learning.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
By being a more ﬂexible substrate
than ANNs, they could also lead to a more general understanding of the role recurrence plays in learning.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Looking forward to see the next papers on this subject.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
19


5.5
PushGP
PushGP [29] is a family of programming languages which have been speciﬁcally designed for evolution
to be applied-to i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Code is treated as a manipulated datatype.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It has been subjected to continuous research
over a number of years and so there are many iterations and implementations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These variations include
ones that allow for auto-constructive evolution (see section 5.1).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
PushGP is designed to be an evolutionary target language
rather than forcing a standard programming language to evolve.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In other words, instead of using an
existing programming language which is not evolutionary friendly, PushGP goes the other way by making
it evolutionary friendly.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
5.6
Simulated Annealing
Simulated Annealing [4] is not an evolutionary algorithm in itself but is frequently used in-conjunction
with EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It is where a problems starts being exploratory and as it gets nearer to a possible solution
moves more to being exploitative.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Meaning that more of a stochastic approach is adopted at the be-
ginning and as a good enough solution becomes nearer a more combinational approach is adopted (see
section 3.9).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: What problems does Simulated Annealing solve?
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Simulated Annealing is most useful when the
problem-domain requires more of an exploratory approach at the beginning but as the solution becomes
more in view a more exploitative approach is adopted.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
5.7
Tangled Program Graph, TPG
Tangled Program Graph (TPG) [52] is another relatively new technique.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A method of managing pro-
grams to scale.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The scale is used to handle more complicated tasks such as game playing.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Provides
a method to manage continuous evolution of independent and co-evolved populations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Shown to have
some promising results when compared with equivalent deep learning methods.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
And requires signiﬁ-
cantly lower computation requirement.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
TGP is both eﬃcient and proven to handle complex dynamic
problems such as the traditional game playing benchmarks.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is still an early research area and as
such should be monitored.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
5.8
Tabu search
Tabu search [66] is similar to Simulated Annealing (see section 5.6) in that it is often used in con-
junction with EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Tabu search relaxes the local search method by allowing a not-so-good solution to
progress-forward over solutions which have already been visited.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Tabu search solves the problem of getting oﬀa local
maxima by placing solutions which have already been visited onto a tabu list.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The list is used as a
method to avoid going down known previously explored search paths.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
20


5.9
Animal inspired algorithms
The Animal Inspired Algorithms [4] are biology inspired algorithms.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Never-the-less they deserve a refer-
ence within the context of EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: There are a surprisingly large number of animal inspired algorithms.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The
more famous are swarm, ant and frog algorithms but the actual list is considerably longer.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Each animal
inspired algorithm provides some unique quality like ﬂying, jumping or walking.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
They are important
algorithms; swarm algorithm, for instance, can be used to control a collection of drones.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Ant algorithms
can be used to explore an unknown terrain for searching useful resources.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: What problems do Animal Inspired Algorithms solve?
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is a broad group of specialized algorithms
which solve very speciﬁc problems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
21


6
Problem-domain mapping
The most important part of any algorithm is what can it accomplish.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In this section we attempt to map
speciﬁc problem-domains to potential techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
We must stress that this is not exhaustive and may
change dramatically between reviews.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: It will act as an important baseline for any future reports.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
6.1
Speciﬁc problem-domain mappings
Here we map the general problem-domains and the speciﬁc technique or techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These problem-
domains are traditional problems found in industry.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
6.1.1
Variable and parameter optimization
Parameter and variable optimization is a process of ﬁnding the best set of parameter values for a prob-
lem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The problems in themselves are complicated or the number of parameters is extremely large.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
If
neither is true then a more traditional method of optimization may be a better route to a solution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: ES or GA are the normal solutions for this type of problem-domain.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It has been shown that a GA can
handle up to a million variables, as discussed in the Tutorial on Next Generation Genetic Algorithms
GECCO 2018 [31,80].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This makes the search space diﬃcult or impossible for traditional methods and
the only remaining true competitor is a pure stochastic method.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
See sections,
• 4.1 Evolutionary Strategy, ES
• 4.2 Genetic Algorithms, GA
6.1.2
Symbolic and polynomial regression
This is the problem when given a data-set ﬁnding the equivalent mathematical equation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is a
particularly popular and important activity in many industries.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The requirement is to ﬁnd a matching
equation for the data.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: EAs are adopted when traditional regression methods fail.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The automotive in-
dustry are actively involved in this area since they frequently need to conﬁrm theoretical equations with
practical data.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The techniques help ﬁnd the equation that matches the real data independent of theory.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: GP and all subclasses can handle symbolic and polynomial regression.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
See sections,
• 4.3 Genetic Programming, GP
• 4.6 Linear Genetic Programming, LGP
• 4.7 Cartesian Genetic Programming, CGP
• 4.5 Grammatical Evolution, GE
• 5.5 PushGP
22


6.1.3
Automated code production
The goal is to produce new code without human involvement.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Once the programming language, repre-
sentation and goal have all been chosen, EAs can explore the problem-domain in search of an optimal
solution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: If a ﬁnal code solution is found then it will fall into one of three criteria i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
precise/accurate,
”good enough” or a multi-objective compromise (along the pareto curve).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Historically, EAs have mostly targeted programming languages such as LISP and low-level assembly
language.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Both have strict input-output formats which can simplify mutation and the joining of code
segments.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This avoids introducing syntax errors due to interface inconsistencies.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Today the popular
programming languages are Python (as a replacement for LISP) and Intermediate Representation (as a
replacement for assembler instructions).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Both oﬀer new opportunities and challenges.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: GP, LGP, GE, CGP, and PushGP are all techniques that produce code.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Due to the fact that the code
is automatically generated it is likely that the end result is diﬃcult or unreadable by humans.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
See sections,
• 4.3 Genetic Programming, GP
• 4.6 Linear Genetic Programming, LGP
• 4.5 Grammatical Evolution, GE
• 4.7 Cartesian Genetic Programming, CGP
• 5.5 PushGP
6.1.4
Regular expression
Automated generation of regular expression.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This can be achieved using Genetic Programming [60].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Where EAs are used to explore expression strings.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
See section,
• 4.3 Genetic Programming
6.1.5
Circuit design
Circuit design is similar to low-level assembly instructions (see section 6.1.3) in that it has been suc-
cessfully explored using EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The rules for circuit design is relatively simple and so EAs can explore the
problem space relatively easily.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This area was explored intensely in the 1990’s but has potential to see
a revival as system complexity increases.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
CGP is particularly good at exploring circuit design since it handles spatial problems using Cartesian
co-ordinates.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
See sections,
• 4.3 Genetic Programming, GP
• 4.7 Cartesian Genetic Programming, CGP
23


6.1.6
Code improvement and optimization
This is an up and coming area.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The evolutionary process starts from a working code base, as compared
with an initial random seed population.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The existing working code is optimized towards a set of new
objectives or is transitioned to ﬁt within a new set of constraints.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The new objectives could include
speciﬁc performance features or any other similar attributes.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The constraints could include new code
size restrictions or power consumption limitations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The working code is basically used as a seed for the
ﬁrst initial population.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Standard evolutionary operators are then applied to search the problem space
for a potentially better solution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
As a subtopic, legacy code improvement is about taking older existing code and ﬁnding a better alter-
native.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This better alternative can either be a metric improvement (e.g.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
faster, smaller code) or higher
quality (hidden or existing anomalies are removed).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs in this problem-domain act as extra engineers on the project, where they might or might not produce
a better answer from the original.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Similar to many parts of engineering, this technique relies heavily on
the quality of the goal and the associated test suites.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: GP, GI and GE are all referenced to handle code improvement and optimization.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
See sections,
• 4.3 Genetic Programming, GP
• 4.4 Genetic Improvement, GI
• 4.5 Grammatical Evolution, GE
6.1.7
Simulator testing
Simulation testing is an indirect/byproduct of using EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It turns out EAs can be extremely good at
ﬁnding simulator inconsistencies.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is because EAs explore the simulator in a diﬀerent way than an
engineer or scientist would explore a simulator.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In fact, there are a number of historical examples where
EAs are annoyingly good at discovering faults.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: All the EAs are capable of pushing the limits of a simulator.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
6.1.8
Walking robot
Robots learning to walk has been a traditionally hard problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs have been involved in learning
how to walk for decades.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs have two attributes which make them particularly useful in handling
these types of problems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
First, EAs can learn how to improve with each evolutionary cycle (incremental
improvements) and second they can adapt to changes in the environment.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For example, if a physical
component changes or malfunctions EAs can adapt to that change and can continue walking.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: GAs are used extensively in Robot Walking Algorithms, for both soft and hard robots.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
See section,
• 4.2 Genetic Algorithms, GA
24


6.1.9
Automated machine learning
EAs are starting to be used in the new subject of Automated Machine Learning (or more commonly
known as AutoML) [47,53].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: AutoML is the automation of machine learning to real problem-domains.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The goal is to avoid the labor intensive conﬁguration required to setup a Deep Neural Network (DNN).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This method also potentially bypasses the requirement for domain experts.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Google have shown that Au-
toML can successfully improve existing ML systems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Google has also shown how Evolutionary AutoML
can be used to improve Image Classiﬁers that were originally designed by humans.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is becoming an increasingly popular subject, especially as DNNs become more complicated and
larger.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
DNNs are more and more being adopted to solve interesting, real problems but the complexity of
setup is causing a slow down in application.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The quest today is applying and conﬁguring DNN to more
problems quicker and easier.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs are increasingly being used in this area to discover novel solutions
which are more eﬃcient.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: In research, GAs are an alternative way to conﬁgure a DNN.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For
example, in a Google Brain paper [53] aging the weaker entities from the population was introduced
to DNN conﬁguration.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
They found that GAs achieved better results, as compared with other methods,
when there is limited hardware resources.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
One of the more famous public tools in EAs to carry this is out is TPOT [33], source code available
on GitHub.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: It is designed to be a Data Science Assistant, written in Python.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The goal is to optimize
machine learning pipelines using GP.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
See sections,
• 4.2 Genetic Algorithms, GA
• 4.3 Genetic Programming, GP
• 5.2 Neuroevolution, or Deep Neuroevolution
6.2
Unusual and interesting problem-domain mappings
Here we highlight some of the more unusual problem-domain mappings that have appeared in recent
articles.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: It is expected that these mappings will change the most between reviews.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
6.2.1
Conﬁguring neuromorphic computers
Conﬁguration of a Neuromorphic Computer [34] is a more unusual problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Current techniques map
Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to Spiking Neural Networks (SNN).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These techniques avoid the
dynamic nature and complexity of SNNs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: A suggestion is to use an EA to perform these mappings.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs
are used to design simple ANNs to conﬁgure the platform.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This technique allows the full utilization of a
complex SNN to create small networks to solve speciﬁc problems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs can explore the entire parameter
space of the speciﬁc hardware.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
6.2.2
Forecasting ﬁnancial markets
GA are used by institutional quantitative traders and other areas of the ﬁnancial world [36].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Traders use
software packages to set parameters that are optimized using both historical data and a GA.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Depending
25


upon the problem, the optimization can vary from which parameters are being used and the associated
values to only optimizing the values.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Trading comes with some risk but identifying the right parameters
that relate to major market turns can be critical.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
6.2.3
Predicting future city landscapes
The Spanish Foundation For Science and Technology [37] have used EAs to predicts the upward growth
of cities.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
They discovered that increases in build height follows similar development as some living
systems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: A GA takes historical and economic data and uses it to predict the skyline of the future.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The
GA predicts how the skyscrapers and other buildings increase in height.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
6.2.4
Designing an optimized ﬂoor-plan
Using EAs to design internal building ﬂoor plans.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Floor plan can be complex due to building irregularities.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: A GA has been applied to optimize complex ﬂoor-plans [49].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The GA successfully designed oﬃce ﬂoor
plans that optimized walk times and hallways.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
6.2.5
Antenna design
Antennas are complicated and are mostly designed by hand.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is both time-consuming and requires
many resources.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs have been ”used to search the design space and automatically ﬁnd novel antenna
designs”.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In the paper entitled Automated Antenna Design with Evolutionary Algorithm [38], a group of
NASA scientist successfully achieve designing an antenna using digital evolution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The antenna turned
out to be eﬃcient for a variety of applications.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It was unique since the ﬁnal design would not have been
created by a human.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
6.2.6
Defect identiﬁcation of electron microscopy images
The US Department of Energy has been using a system called Multinode Evolutionary Neural Networks
for Deep Learning (MENNDL) [54] to identify defects in electron microscopy images.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
MENNDL uses
NNs to ﬁnd defects out of changing data.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The system runs on the Oakridge Summit supercomputer [55].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Fully utilizing all the available compute-nodes i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It analyzes millions of
networks using a ”scalable, parallel, asynchronous genetic algorithm augmented with a support vector
machine to automatically ﬁnd a superior deep learning network topology and hyper-parameter set.” [54].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The scale of this system makes this an impressive hybrid implementation.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
26


7
Challenges
Challenges include some personal opinions from the experience we have had navigating the subject of
EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The points laid out below are opinions so should be debated and discussed.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• It is our observation that the community is relatively small compared with other Machine Learning
communities.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The size of the community determines the level of vigor that can be applied to
validate a new idea or concept.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In other words, there is not enough experts in the subject to
vigorously prove or disprove a concept.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Many ideas, even extremely clever and good ones, go
unveriﬁed and unchecked by the community.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is a problem since good ideas can go missing
due to a lack of support.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • EAs have an inherent diﬃculty proving they are the best solution to a speciﬁc ”real-world” problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: There is no automatic methods to compare algorithms that is without any bias.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In other words
how do we prove, without doubt, that an EA performs better at achieving a time-to-solution than
a random search.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This has been a consistent issue since it is extremely diﬃcult to prove the results
from an EA experiment that is obviously without bias.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
What compounds the diﬃculty is that the
problem-domains targeted are in themselves inherently complex, that is why an EAs is being used
in the ﬁrst place.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• Recently a lot of work has gone into creating synthetic problem benchmarks but there is concern
less work has been applied to ”real world” problems with ”real world” constraints.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Where bench
marking and consistency is undoubtedly important, especially when comparing techniques, the
most important activity is always applying algorithms to real problems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• The community is an old community within Machine Learning, with ideas dating back to the early
1950’s but many of the original drawbacks of using evolutionary techniques have been removed
since modern hardware is both abundant and high performing.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This means experiments which
were constrained by the hardware resources at the time can now be feasible.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Population size and
maximum number of generations can be made considerably larger.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • Biology plays important an role but EAs are not organisms.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This makes crossing terms between
biology and Computer Science diﬃcult.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Computer Scientists will use the biological terms loosely
for their own purposes whereas the real biological meaning is much more complicated.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• EAs have been proven good at tackling some hard problems but they suﬀer from a diﬃculty-of-
scale.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In complex systems it is important to divide-and-conquer (break the problem down into
smaller elements) before attempting to produce a solution.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs at the bottom level make a lot
of sense but they become more problematic as we scale-up the problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Research work at bigger
scale problems is still immature and is also limited, for the most part, with the capabilities of the
current hardware available.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • Similar to many other AI disciplines, there is a constant struggle between make verses buy.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There
is a tendency for Researchers to re-invent the technology wheel, this is in part due to the required
learning curve to attain usefulness.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The amount of eﬀort to learn a new framework can be as
challenging and time consuming as creating a propriety framework from ﬁrst principles.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is
detrimental to the discipline, as a whole, since the re-invention slows down forward progress.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The
caveat is that over time frameworks become overly speciﬁc to a given problem domain, so applying
the same framework to a diﬀerent problem can be cumbersome.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
27


• Modularity is a method to handle more complex problems by breaking the problem into more man-
ageable components.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This falls under the divide-and-conquer strategy or scientiﬁc method.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs
solve problems using a bottom-up design and as-such are inherently more diﬃcult to modularize.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• EAs may be deterministic and provable, the process by how the solution was arrived at is non-
determinant and if the algorithm is run again there is no guarantee the same result will be found
or any result will be found.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This is the opposite of some other techniques in Machine Learning.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Proof and explainability is becoming increasingly more important.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Governments
are also stepping in with new regulations, for example the General Data Protection Regulation
(GDPR) [26].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
GDPR is a European regulation which has direct implications on Machine Learning
algorithms in general.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In Article 22 [27], of the regulation, calls for algorithmic fairness and
explainability.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: In other words, explain how the algorithm is correct, fair and unbiased.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• Being an old subject EAs inherently suﬀers from the reinvention and rediscovery of already known
concepts.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Keeping everyone current with what has been published is always a challenge, especially
as the amount of scientiﬁc information accelerates.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• Even-though EAs could potentially be the next big direction for Machine Learning, the general
low funding of the subject may hold back development.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is concerning since EAs are not as
well-known as other Machine Learning techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This situation makes obtaining core funding
for EA related research diﬃcult and very much a secondary focus.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The outcome is that only a few
full-time researchers worldwide focus solely on these techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Also, the broad interdisciplinary
knowledge base required is diﬃcult to attain.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
28


8
Predictions
In this section we look into the future.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: What may happen in the next few years with EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Again since
these are predictions they should be treated with more questions.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• It is likely that in the near future we will see more cross-pollination and collaboration between
Machine Learning researchers and molecular biologists, neuroscientists and evolutionary biologists.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: People are held back by their specializations and generally dangerous in other areas.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The philoso-
pher Paul Feyerabend argued that the most progress is made on the boundaries between subjects
[81].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It is at the boundary of biology and computer science where most advancements are likely
to occur.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• Pure research on DNNs will slow down and the DNN focus will shift to engineering and the
application side for the near-term.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There is a strong likelihood that Machine Learning research will
diversify and be more challenging.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Research problems will become hybrid, involving the merging of
many techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: A potential end goal for hybrid systems is Artiﬁcial General Intelligence (AGI).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • Artiﬁcial General Intelligence is a philosophical goal, or concern depending upon whom you ask.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This will potentially take decades and many stages before is can be reached, if at all.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
One stage
is the much smaller attainable goal of producing what we call Domain Speciﬁc Artiﬁcial Life
(DSAL).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Bringing together many disciplines in the desire to create solutions to a speciﬁc problem.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The term is a fun play on Domain Speciﬁc Architectures as advocated by some of the hardware
architecture community: small artiﬁcial lifeforms to solve speciﬁc problems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • New Artiﬁcial Neurons (AN) will be explored and developed.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There is potential for the ANs
themselves to be re-examined either by vastly increasing the number of interconnects or adding
interesting attributes like co-ordinates to the model.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Today’s ANs have limited interconnects,
whereas the biological neurons have substantially more interconnects.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: These are ideas that people like Julian Miller have put forward.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Whatever future
direction is taken, the AN model will most likely change over the next few years.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In all likelihood
we will end up with many AN models to choose from.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This change will occur as our understanding
of Neuroscience and biological mechanisms increases.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• As James Shapiro points out, there are many genetic mechanisms that could be incorporated into
existing and new EAs [82].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: One such concept is Horizontal Gene Transfer (HGT) [11].
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
HGT
becomes important to the community, as more advanced complex systems are attempted.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
HGT is
the ability for useful genes (or code segments) to quickly transfer across species (islands).
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There
are Computer Science implications for such ideas.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
As with Richard Feynman’s ”There’s plenty
of room at the bottom”, when referring to molecular chemistry, there is plenty of room with
evolutionary biology and its application to EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • EAs can potentially be used to explore causality.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Judea Pearl [3] has given the industry a challenge
to explain Machine Learning outcomes and identify the causes of the outcomes.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
In particular ideas
like counterfactual, where forward predictions about the future can be made by inserting a change
or deciding not to insert a change.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This involves not just providing data correlation but creating
a model on how the data was created.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • Obfuscation may allow EAs to get involved in security, privacy and data cloaking.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• EAs are already being used in the ﬁeld of Quantum Computing (QC), and we can expect more
activity in this area.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: Either to conﬁgure or to handle the complicated data output.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
2017 saw the
Humies Award [19] go to an Australian Team [35] using EAs applied to Quantum Computing.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
29


9
Final discussion and conclusion
The 2019 Evolutionary Algorithms Review is a baseline for future reports.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
We are cognizant that there
are many areas which were not covered or were only covered brieﬂy.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
These areas may become more
important as we consider the 2020 review.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Traditional EAs continue to provide useful solutions to hard
problems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
They are becoming particularly useful when placed on modern
hardware.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The newer trends appear to indicate that hybrid solution may provide the next future capa-
bility i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: combining evolutionary techniques with other techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Where EAs are used either to bring
knowledge-forwarding or optimizing complex Machine Learning conﬁgurations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: We dedicated most of the review to the landscaping of the various techniques.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This was planned to act
as a baseline for future review development.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
For problem-domains that aﬀect society, and subsequently
industry, we introduced UCA (User Control Attributes) criteria.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
lim-
iters, explainability, causality, fairness and correction.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
They impose an extra level of required thinking,
where the algorithms have to be both community friendly and adhere to new government regulations.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: The UCA will be used as a basis for a new taxonomy for EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Future algorithms will not only be rated
on their ability to produce an outcome but on the ability to satisfy the UCA criteria in some form or
other.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: More generally this taxonomy could be applied to other forms of Machine Learning.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Current thoughts on applying the UCA to EAs are as follows:
• Limiters is the concept of restricting the capability.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
It is still early days but as EAs handle more
problems that either aﬀect the physical environment (i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
control actuators), or are involved in
some privacy aspect, then methods of limiting the capability or cloaking the outcomes become
more important.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: This may require signiﬁcant external technology and thought.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • Explainability revolves around explaining how an algorithm produces an answer.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The output
solution from EAs are inherently provable since they solve a speciﬁc problem but as with all
algorithms of this class, explaining how the solution came about is problematic and diﬃcult to
repeat.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
• Causality is about moving to a higher order answer which adds the ”Why” component to the
answer being searched.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
The challenge has been set and causality will become more important as
we move forward with implementing real world EAs, driven by the desire for the EAs to do more
and to understand why a conclusion has been reached.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • Fairness is about producing an answer which is balanced and without human prejudice.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This may
come down to the actual input data selected and the ﬁtness function being used.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Algorithmic
fairness [45] has to be capable of detecting biases, contesting a decision and ﬁnally instigating
a potential remedy.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
A critical method of achieving fairness is making sure that the outcome is
vigorously tested.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
There is potential for a mathematical element of fairness to be incorporated into
the evolutionary frameworks.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Whereas the society aspects will remain in the human domain for the
foreseeable future and may well require careful deliberate biasing to produce a fair outcome.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Two
features related to fairness, not covered in this review, are the broader subjects of accountability
and transparency.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: A method of algorithmic fairness can be complicated.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is an area that
requires future monitoring.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Fairness may also involve studying the initial starting states, checking
that the biases are not injected right at the start of the process.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: • Correction is about correcting a problem once it has been identiﬁed.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
When an error is identi-
ﬁed/detected/contested, EAs can be assessed on how easily a remedy can be applied.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
EAs by
30


deﬁnition are adaptive, and so correction can occur as part of a continuous evolutionary process
(i.e.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
via environmental-changes) or more manually through a direct change to the ﬁtness function
and/or constraints.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Now that we have described the basics of the UCA, we will attempt in the 2020 review to apply them
to the various EAs outlined in this review.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text: There is a long way to go with-respect-to EAs.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
We are just forming a common language by which we
can communicate with the biologists.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is an exciting time since the discoveries in biochemistry and
synthetic biology are occurring at unprecedented rates and the capabilities of digital hardware are com-
ing to levels that can mimic parts of the biological system.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
Likewise, biology can also take advantage
of some of the newly gained insights from the Computer Science ﬁeld.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This means that the research runway is long but at the same time we have to realize that the hardware
gap in both ”eﬀective” processing and interconnects between biology and digital systems is still vast.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
We may have the vision to achieve biological equivalence but the current state of the hardware is both
diﬀerent and non-optimal for many types of problems.
title: arXiv:1906.08870v1  [cs.NE]  3 Jun 2019

text:
This is particularly interesting as we hit the End
of Moore’s Law and the possibility of diﬀerent compute-models being introduced and forced on the
industry.

Jeehun Kim, Sunkyu Lee, Weonjong Lee*
