SUMMARY AND DISCUSSION
In this work, we present enhancements to dynamic load balancing
for particle and mesh-based simulations targeting GPU architec-
tures.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
As a component of these improvements, we introduce several
GPU-applicable strategies for measuring the relative computational
costs of sub-domains of compute work.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
While as application de-
velopers we can find optimal hyperparameters for a specific setup
for heuristic cost-functions, we demonstrate that a measurement
of the actual kernel run time can be established.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
Especially, we
implemented a potentially vendor-neutral, in-situ, in-kernel mea-
surement of run time based on a GPU clock that shows negligible
load-balancing overhead in practice.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
Contrarily, a measurement ap-
proach based on Nvidia CUPTI added significant run time overhead
and is not vendor-neutral.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
We demonstrate our methods in the fully kinetic particle-in-cell
code WarpX and explore its performance.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
For the scientifically rele-
vant test case of laser-ion acceleration, we explore the performance
dependence of load balancing on several numerical parameters
and algorithm choices that enter into our routine, including cost
assignment strategy (heuristic cost assessment based on a weighted
linear sum of the number of particles and cells, GPU clock timing
to assess summed thread execution time, and CUPTI-based timing
to assess kernel execution time using NVIDIA’s CUPTI API), load
balance strategy (knapsack or SFC), the number of boxes per GPU
(equivalently, on a fixed domain, the box size in cells), the frequency
with which we call the load balancing routine, and the load balance
efficiency improvement required to communicate and update a pro-
posed distribution mapping.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
For the laser-ion acceleration that is
the focus of the present work, we measure a 3.8× speedup relative
to the baseline without dynamic load balancing and a 1.2× speedup
compared to the static load balancing baseline.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
To assess the performance of WarpX’s updated dynamic load
balancing, we introduce a performance model based on strong scal-
ing measurements of WarpX and link performance improvement
through strong scaling to the initial level of load imbalance in our
simulations, thereby predicting a theoretical maximum speedup
factor that is achievable through load balancing.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
We present the
weak scaling (from 24 up to 6144 GPUs on Summit) of our dynamic
load balancing performance relative to the baseline case without
load balancing, and find that dynamic load balancing improves per-
formance, with achieved improvement typically 62% to 74% of the
predicted maximum (88% when running on 6 GPUs); in particular,
several of our simulations demonstrate that dynamic load balancing
is de-facto a prerequisite for productive usage of distributed, locally
limited GPU memory at scale.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
In the present work, we focused on load balancing according
to the cost of GPU compute.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
Incorporating communication costs
into our load balancing routine will be a topic of future investiga-
tion, and may bring the performance of WarpX’s load balancing
closer to the theoretical limit of our presented performance model.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

text:
Further exploration of communication costs may also help to de-
mystify the relative performance of knapsack and SFC update for
the distribution mapping, which remains an open question.
title: In-Situ Assessment of Device-Side Compute Work for Dynamic Load Balancing in a GPU-Accelerated PIC Code

A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic
Algorithms
Tomohiro Haradaa,∗, Enrique Albab, Gabriel Luqueb
aFaculty of System Design, Tokyo Metropolitan University, Tokyo, Japan
bITIS Software, University of M´alaga, M´alaga, Spain
Abstract
This work proposes a novel approach to evaluate and analyze the behavior of multi-population parallel genetic algo-
rithms (PGAs) when running on a cluster of multi-core processors.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In particular, we deeply study their numerical and
computational behavior by proposing a mathematical model representing the observed performance curves.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In them, we
discuss the emerging mathematical descriptions of PGA performance instead of, e.g., individual isolated results subject
to visual inspection, for a better understanding of the eﬀects of the number of cores used (scalability), their migration
policy (the migration gap, in this paper), and the features of the solved problem (type of encoding and problem size).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The conclusions based on the real ﬁgures and the numerical models ﬁtting them represent a fresh way of understanding
their speed-up, running time, and numerical eﬀort, allowing a comparison based on a few meaningful numeric parame-
ters.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text: This represents a set of conclusions beyond the usual textual lessons found in past works on PGAs.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
It can be used
as an estimation tool for the future performance of the algorithms and a way of ﬁnding out their limitations.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Keywords:
Parallelism, genetic algorithms, run time, speed-up, numerical eﬀort, mathematical models
1.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Introduction
Most optimization tasks found in Industry and real-
world applications impose several constraints that usually
do not allow the utilization of exact methods [1, 2].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Ge-
netic Algorithms (GAs) are well-known population-based
techniques for providing accurate solutions to such prob-
lems [3].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
GAs make use of a population of solutions, with
the initial population being randomly generated (or cre-
ated with a greedy algorithm) and then enhanced through
an iterative process.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
At each generation of the process,
the whole population (or a part of it) is replaced by newly
generated individuals (often the best ones) [4].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
On the one hand, the use of a population of solutions
along with genetic operations makes GAs time-consuming
in order to reach an acceptable solution, but, on the other
hand, its implicit decentralized nature allows to paral-
lelize them as a promising approach for overcoming this
drawback.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Several parallel models have been then pro-
posed to build parallel GAs (PGAs) [5, 6, 7].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The most
popular type of algorithm is the island-based model, also
known as the distributed model [8].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In this scheme, the
whole population is divided into subpopulations (islands)

eat@lcc.uma.es (Enrique Alba), gabriel@lcc.uma.es (Gabriel
Luque)

(Tomohiro Harada)
distributed over diﬀerent processors.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
These islands run
a sequential GA, and after a predeﬁned interval (migra-
tion gap), they communicate in order to exchange some
search knowledge, e.g., individuals or search parameters.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
This communication or migration process [9, 10] usually
involves sending copies of a few selected individuals from
one island to another in a given topology of migration (e.g.,
a uni-directional ring).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Then, according to predeﬁned ac-
ceptance criteria (e.g., always, or just if they have better
quality than some other existing ones), the migrated indi-
viduals are integrated into the local subpopulation.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The parallel execution of a PGA reduces the total run
time by performing more steps per unit time and could
even allow for an improvement in the quality of the found
solutions since structuring the population in smaller sub-
populations leads to new and more eﬃcient ways of ex-
ploring the search space [5].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Most of the modern comput-
ing devices such as laptops and workstations are equipped
with multi-core processing units.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
They are also a com-
pact and easy way to develop high-performance computing
(HPC) in any present lab and company.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
However, they are
still not well known as the classical plain cluster of CPUs
linked by Ethernet for running PGAs.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
This paper ana-
lyzes the search performance of island-based PGAs run-
ning in a cluster of multi-core computers from the points
of view of their numerical eﬀort and computational eﬀort.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In particular, we comprehensively analyze the impact of
the number of cores used, part of their migration strategy,
and the type of search landscape of the targeted problem.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Our research questions are these:
Preprint submitted to Applied Soft Computing
June 21, 2021


RQ1: How do the number of cores, the problem size, and
the migration gap aﬀect the search performance of
PGAs?
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
RQ2: Can we get beyond the mere visual inspection of
graphs/tables to analyze speed-up in PGAs and other
metrics?
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
RQ3: How do the computational and numerical eﬀorts
relate to problem size and discrete nature?
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
To answer these research questions, we conduct exper-
iments using a cluster of multiprocessors, a commodity
MIMD (Multiple Instruction, Multiple Data) architecture.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
As a PGA method, this paper uses a distributed island-
based steady-state GA (dssGA).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Our experiments focus
on the two NP-hard problems: the P-PEAKS problem,
using a binary encoding, and the vehicle routing prob-
lem (VRP), which uses permutations.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
This choice is easy
to justify since they represent two very important fami-
lies of problems in combinatorial optimization.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
To answer
RQ1, we solve these two problems with diﬀerent sizes (di-
mensions) while also studying the migration gap and the
diﬀerent cores used (a high number of combinations and
independent runs needed).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Although a migration strategy
involves making many decisions (gap, selection policy, and
distributed topology), this paper focuses on the migration
gap as a ﬁrst approach to test our fresh understanding
of their performance under a wide set of conﬁgurations.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Indeed, the migration gap highly impacts the diversity of
the island-based PGA.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
For RQ2, we devise a mathematical
model that enables a higher level and quantitative analy-
sis beyond the usual comparison of ﬁgures in tables/graphs
found in the literature.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
We then used all that for a ﬁnal
study of PGAs to better understand their computational
and numerical eﬀorts (RQ3).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The rest of this document is organized as follows: the
next section discusses previous studies over the same topics
tackled in this work.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Section 3 presents some background
information about distributed GAs.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Section 4 proposes
our fresh way to understand PGA performance.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Sections 5
and 6 detail our benchmark and the experimental settings
used in this paper, respectively, while Sections 7 and 8 an-
alyze the results from diﬀerent points of view: wall-clock
time and numerical performance.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Finally, we will end this
work with a summary of the results (Section 10), general
conclusions, and future research in light of our results (Sec-
tion 11).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Related Works
This section focuses on existing scientiﬁc articles an-
alyzing the behavior of island-based PGAs and related
evolutionary algorithms.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
For this, we have performed a
systematic review looking for papers dealing with our top-
ics during the last ten years.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
“Speed-up,” “distributed
evolutionary algorithms,” and “island model” are some of
the terms that have been searched on traditional literature
platforms on this domain (IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Li-
brary, SCOPUS, Google Scholar...).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Most of the papers found focused on solving a spe-
ciﬁc problem instead of analyzing the running algorithm
to understand it: scheduling [11], clustering [12], satellite
design [13], and routing [14].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The main objective of these
studies was very diﬀerent from the proposed in our work;
however, they allow us to conclude on the good health
of PGAs nowadays for many application ﬁelds.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
This also
means that the kind of analysis we do in our paper can
beneﬁt many practitioners.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In this sense, we could ﬁnd
several works analyzing the behavior from two diﬀerent
perspectives: more theoretical studies and more experi-
mental analysis.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
From a formal point of view, the authors in [15] pre-
sented a method for analyzing the run time of parallel
evolutionary algorithms with a spatially structured pop-
ulation.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
This allowed an estimate of the speed-up under
diﬀerent migration topologies.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Moreover, in [16], the same
authors studied the inﬂuence of some migration parame-
ters using a theoretical run time analysis.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Both papers im-
proved the body of knowledge about parallel metaheuristic
based on the island model.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
However, they imposed some
assumptions which usually are not found in real-world sce-
narios, limiting their impact.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
This is a reason to also go
for mixed studies like this present one, where we combine
actual thousands of experimental runs with a mathemati-
cal understanding of their shown behavior.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In the rest of
this section, we will focus on a more experimental analysis
similar to the proposed one in this work.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
We can distinguish two kinds of analysis for parallel
metaheuristics: on the one hand, some papers analyzed the
eﬀect of the physical parallel platform (e.g., GPUs, multi-
cores, cloud), while on the other hand, other works studied
the design and the inﬂuence of the parameters in the per-
formance.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
With respect to the ﬁrst ones, we can cite [17]
for multiprocessors, [18] for GPUs, and [19] for cloud plat-
forms.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
All of them showed the advantages of using par-
allel models for reducing the execution time when using
a parallel platform.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
For example, in the last-mentioned
paper [19], the authors showed how using microservices,
container virtualization, and the publish/subscribe mes-
saging paradigm could even lead to super-linear speed-up
for a moderate number of islands (less than 64, after that
the speed-up decreased).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
This present paper uses a dif-
ferent hardware platform: a multi-core computer cluster
interconnected by high-speed network technology.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Finally, we end this section by describing some recent
works which discussed the inﬂuence of the migration pol-
icy on the performance of this kind of parallel technique.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
This was a diﬃcult choice since many migration parame-
ters exist, but simultaneously, each one will multiply a lot
of the needed experimental runs for the later mathematical
analysis.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
One of the most recent works studying migration
policies can be found in [20].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In this paper, the authors ex-
amined the solution quality, convergence speed, and pop-
ulation diversity of the island model EA with diﬀerent mi-
2


gration topologies, population sizes, migration rates, and
migration gaps on four benchmark functions of 1,000 di-
mensions.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Their results showed the relation between mi-
gration rate and migration gap, and the high importance
of the migration rate and the topology.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In our work, we
examine the migration gap due to its inﬂuence on the re-
sults, however, we analyze a genetic algorithm in contrast
to the diﬀerential evolution used in that work.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Others pa-
pers like [21] perform similar studies, but they focus on
other issues like fault tolerance.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Island-based Distributed Steady-State GA
This section explains the PGA technique used in this
work.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In particular, we use a standard distributed island-
based steady-state GA (dssGA) [8].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
We choose this type
of algorithm since it is one of the most popular PGAs used
in the literature and the Industry [7], thus improving our
knowledge on it could produce a high impact in multiple
domains.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Algorithm 1 shows a pseudo-code of the distributed
island-based steady-state GA (dssGA) implemented in this
work.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
A dssGA consists of many subpopulations (islands)
that evolve governed by a local steady-state GA in par-
allel.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
First, the initial population is generated, and the
required ﬁtness values are evaluated.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Then, a parent se-
lection method (e.g., binary tournament selection) selects
two parents, and crossover and mutation operations cre-
ate a new oﬀspring.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Finally, a newly generated oﬀspring
is evaluated and compared with a randomly selected in-
dividual in the population.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
If the oﬀspring is better than
the random member, the oﬀspring replaces it in the pop-
ulation.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Along with these iterative procedures, the migration
operation is performed to communicate with other islands
at a ﬁxed interval (i.e., migration gap, ∆T ).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The migration
operation selects an individual (called migrant) from the
local population and sends a copy of it to another island.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
When receiving a migrant from other islands, it is merged
into the population if its ﬁtness is better than an individual
randomly selected from the population.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The migration gap ∆T (also known as the migration
interval) determines how frequently each island communi-
cates with the other [22].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The smaller the migration gap is

text:
Proposed Analysis Methodology
This paper advances in how we can understand PGA
performance beyond simple inspections of tables/graphs.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In particular, since wall-clock time and speed-up are essen-
tial features in analyzing PGAs, it is worth going beyond
previous works and mathematically model these features
for running algorithms.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Usually, wall-clock time measures
the running time of a PGA until a given termination cri-
terion is met, e.g., reaching a maximum number of ﬁt-
ness evaluations or ﬁnding a good-enough solution.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
On
the other hand, speed-up represents a wider point of view,
3


Figure 1: Illustration of the island-based GA
allowing the understanding of the scalability of the algo-
rithm and even its quality as a piece of software.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
For that,
speed-up studies how wall-clock time evolves when using
a varying number of m processors.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The speed-up S(m)
when using m processors is calculated as:
S(m) =
˜T1
˜Tm
(1)
where Tm represents the wall-clock time when the PGA is
run on m cores, ideally, the speed-up is upper bounded by
the number of processing units, S(m) = m (linear speed-
up).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
However, in practice, it results in smaller values
(sub-linear speed-up) because of the added communica-
tion times between cores and some parts of the algorithm
that cannot be parallelized.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Thus, sub-linear values above,
e.g., 80% of the ideal value, are usually accepted as good
ones.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
On the contrary, an intriguing super-linear speed-
up value has been shown to be also possible for PGAs
(S(m) > m) [25] in some scenarios due to more eﬃcient
use of the hardware resources (e.g., when subpopulations
now ﬁt into caches and are no longer stored in main mem-
ory for access) and because the distributed search is expe-
riencing new drifting eﬀects or new paths leading till the
optimum solution.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Speed-up is usually studied as numeric ﬁgures in a table
or as a plotted line in a graph.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
However, we would like to
propose the routinary use of a mathematical understand-
ing of the observed speed-up as a way of fostering a more
explainable artiﬁcial intelligence.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The models that we will
use for this analysis are chosen as a result of the prelimi-
nary study (see our Appendix) and common mathematical
knowledge after inspecting the resulting graphs in the liter-
ature [26, 27].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In particular, we compare several families of
mathematical functions: linear, exponential, logarithmic,
and three variants of rational equations.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
From the prelimi-
nary study, the rational function of f(x) = (ax+b)/(x+c)
shows the lowest numerical error (and a reasonably low
number of free parameters) for both predictions of the
wall-clock time and the speed-up.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
For this reason, this pa-
per uses this rational function for understanding the PGA
performance.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Please see the detail of the model selection
presented in Appendix Appendix A.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:

by analyzing its relationship with the number of cores as
the rational equation of:
ˆT(x) = ax + b
x + c ,

text:
The beneﬁts of oﬀering a mathematical model of these
important PGA values are manifold: (i) they could allow
predicting the performance for the unknown number of
processor units without testing on them, (ii) they allow
analyzing the speed-up and wall-clock time by using only
a few parameters (three, in our model) instead of multiple
points/values in a curve/table, and (iii) they allow making
easier/quantitative comparisons between algorithms.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
To
summarize, a mathematical model for these metrics pro-
vides a powerful tool to understand and compare PGAs.

text:
Benchmark Problems
This paper uses two well-known benchmark problems:
the P-PEAKS problem [28] and the vehicle routing prob-
lem (VRP) [29].
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Both of them are discrete combinato-
rial problems but represent very diﬀerent search features
found in many other combinatorial tasks.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
First, regard-
ing the problem class, both problems are NP-Hard [30],
4


thus usually requiring metaheuristic algorithms.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Second,
P-PEAKS is encoded as a binary vector, while VRP needs
a diﬀerent permutation-based encoding.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
These problems
then represent two huge classes of combinatorial problems
solved with PGAs.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Finally, if we focus on the compu-
tational complexity of their ﬁtness functions, P-PEAKS
is quadratic (O(n2)) while VRP is linear (O(n)); whether
this is relevant for the time and speed-up of the algorithms
remains to be analyzed.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Again, a large number of prob-
lems have similar complexities in their ﬁtness functions,
thus completing a good handful of reasons to use them
for evaluating PGAs (our primary goal, we are not solving
these problems as the main goal in this study).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The follow-
ing subsections show brief descriptions of these problems.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:

The P-PEAKS problem [28] is a binary optimization
problem.

representing the location of P (abstract) peaks in the search
space.

setting P = 20 and N = 100, while a large problem is set

The vehicle routing problem [29] (VRP) consists of de-

times in practice for related classes of problems.

text:
These results show that a small migration gap (i.e., 64
or less) tends to reduce the wall-clock time for all problems.

On the other hand, when using a large number of cores
(i.e., 64 cores), the eﬀect of the migration gap on the wall-
clock time is not signiﬁcant.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
A signiﬁcant diﬀerence is found in all migration gaps
and all problems as to the diﬀerent number of utilized
cores.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In all problems, the wall-clock time is reduced
by using a large number of cores, as expected in a well-
programmed PGA.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In particular, the wall-clock time when
using 64 cores achieves the shortest wall-clock time.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Even
if it seems straightforward, implementing a PGA involves
many programming decisions that can easily ruin the re-
sulting running time.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
To summarize, we have observed that, as we expected,
the number of cores is the main factor in reducing the
execution time.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
However, when the available hardware re-
sources are reduced (a lower number of cores) and/or the
problem is more complex, the utilization of a more cou-
pled island model (a lower migration gap) also helps to
reduce the wall-clock time.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
This is because a lower migra-
tion gap fosters more interchange of information between
the islands, and faster convergence.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
We will verify this in
Section 8, which analyzes the number of ﬁtness evaluations
needed to ﬁnd a high-quality solution.

Both physical and algorithmic reasons

title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
From the physical aspect, when the algo-
rithm run is equally distributed among several cores, the
memory can be more eﬃciently managed, e.g., the cache
memory can be utilized because the memory needed in
each core decreases.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
On the other hand, many cores imply
an additional overhead mainly due to the communications.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

oﬀbetween the communication overhead and memory uti-
lization, and some of these cases produce the super-linear
speed-up.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
On the other hand, from the algorithmic aspect, asyn-
chronous communication used in the experiment may af-
fect the behavior of the speed-up.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
The asynchronous com-
munication allows each process to run the algorithm in-
dependently, which is more beneﬁcial to the search than
running it on a single core.

up.

Conclusion and Future Works
In this article, we have tried to address an analysis of
the parameters of the PGA (migration gap), the beneﬁts of
using a cluster of multi-core computers, and how all this re-
lates to the problem solved (binary and permutation-based
ones) at the same time (kind of holistic analysis of island
PGA).

We did it both in a descriptive manner, getting
conclusions on all that, but also in a compact mathemati-
cal way, by summarizing our outcomes in simple numerical
models to foster future research.

formance, i.e., a reduction of the number of evaluations.

Second, the migration parameters also have a high impor-
tance in these two metrics.

In this study, we have con-
sidered the migration gap, which determines how much
coupled the islands are.

(highly coupled islands) provides the most beneﬁcial search

properties, especially when the hardware resources are lim-

title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
An interesting ﬁnding of the
computational eﬀort is that the diﬀerence in the average
evaluation time of the solution is directly reﬂected in the
diﬀerence in execution times for VRPs of diﬀerent sizes.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
This suggests that it may be possible to predict the exe-
cution time by regarding problem size diﬀerences, for the
same class of problem instances.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
With respect to the speed-up, our results show that it
highly depends on the features of the problem, and while
P-PEAKS obtains large gains as more resources are added
(nearly linear, even with the high number of cores), VRP
only obtains small speed-up improvements when more than
32 cores are used.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
It is clear that each type of problem
has a range of computational resources worth using, which
suggests interesting types of research in this sense in the
future.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
With respect to RQ2, we have also provided a sim-
ple mathematical model for the wall-clock times and the
speed-up.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
These models allow studying these metrics in an
easy way and beyond the intuitive look-at-the-graph tradi-
tional way, which is hard to compare and exploit in future
studies.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Using our model, only three parameters should
be analyzed, and in many cases (e.g., with a medium/high
number of cores), we can focus on only a single parame-
ter (a).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Using this later value, we can compare diﬀerent
factors and problems as we did in Table 11 and get sound
conclusions that are easy to grasp.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
We already mentioned some future work, and more is to
come, e.g., in extending this analysis to the rest of the mi-
gration policy parameters, mainly the migration selection
and the topology.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In addition, increasing our benchmark
problems with others (having diﬀerent features) such as
continuous problems or black-box functions (e.g., simula-
tors), is expected to provide a more comprehensive study.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Model Selection
This appendix shows how we made the choice of the
mathematical model used to understand the wall-clock
time and the speed-up.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
First, we show the numerical
functions we considered in making this paper (there are
uncountable families of curves, we selected simple but ac-
curate ones).
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Then, we show the result of model ﬁtting for
the wall-clock time and the speed-up and choose the best
trade-oﬀmodel for our analysis in terms of simplicity and
accuracy.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
Used Functions
In this subsection, we discuss the mathematical func-
tions considered in this article.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
There are a lot of func-
tion families for ﬁtting any actual curve.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
We have tested
three function families for this study: linear, rational, and
exponential/logarithm ones attending to the results and
previous works.
title: A Fresh Approach to Evaluate Performance in Distributed Parallel Genetic Algorithms

text:
In particular, for modeling the wall-clock
time and the speed-up, we consider the following six math-
ematical models:
• Linear function (Linear)
f(x) = ax + b

A Systematic Literature Review of Empiricism and Norms of
Reporting in Computing Education Research Literature
SARAH HECKMAN, North Carolina State University
JEFFREY C.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
CARVER, University of Alabama
MARK SHERRIFF, University of Virginia
AHMED AL-ZUBIDY, University of Alabama
Context.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Computing Education Research (CER) is critical to help the computing education community and
policy makers support the increasing population of students who need to learn computing skills for future
careers.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
For a community to systematically advance knowledge about a topic, the members must be able to
understand published work thoroughly enough to perform replications, conduct meta-analyses, and build the-
ories.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
There is a need to understand whether published research allows the CER community to systematically
advance knowledge and build theories.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
The goal of this study is to characterize the reporting of empiricism in Computing Education
Research literature by identifying whether publications include content necessary for researchers to perform repli-
cations, meta-analyses, and theory building.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
We answer three research questions related to this goal: RQ1)
What percentage of papers in CER venues have some form of empirical evaluation?
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
RQ2) Of the papers that
have empirical evaluation, what are the characteristics of the empirical evaluation?
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
RQ3) Of the papers that
have empirical evaluation, do they follow norms (both for inclusion and for labeling of information needed
for replication, meta-analysis, and, eventually, theory-building) for reporting empirical work?
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
We conducted a systematic literature review of the 2014 and 2015 proceedings or issues of ﬁve
CER venues: Technical Symposium on Computer Science Education (SIGCSE TS), International Symposium on
Computing Education Research (ICER), Conference on Innovation and Technology in Computer Science Education
(ITiCSE), ACM Transactions on Computing Education (TOCE), and Computer Science Education (CSE).
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
We de-
veloped and applied the CER Empiricism Assessment Rubric to the 427 papers accepted and published at these
venues over 2014 and 2015.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Two people evaluated each paper using the Base Rubric for characterizing the
paper.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
An individual person applied the other rubrics to characterize the norms of reporting, as appropriate
for the paper type.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text: Any discrepancies or questions were discussed between multiple reviewers to resolve.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
We found that over 80% of papers accepted across all ﬁve venues had some form of empirical eval-
uation.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text: Quantitative evaluation methods were the most frequently reported.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Papers most frequently reported
results on interventions around pedagogical techniques, curriculum, community, or tools.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
There was a split
in papers that had some type of comparison between an intervention and some other data set or baseline.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Most papers reported related work, following the expectations for doing so in the SIGCSE and CER commu-
nity.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
However, many papers were lacking properly reported research objectives, goals, research questions, or
hypotheses; description of participants; study design; data collection; and threats to validity.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
These results
align with prior surveys of the CER literature.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
CER authors are contributing empirical results to the literature; however, not all norms for
reporting are met.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
We encourage authors to provide clear, labeled details about their work so that readers can
use the study methodologies and results for replications and meta-analyses.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
As our community grows, our
reporting of CER should mature to help establish computing education theory to support the next generation
of computing learners.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

1
INTRODUCTION
From 2009 to 2015, the number of bachelor’s degrees in Computer Science increased by 74 percent,
while overall growth across all ﬁelds of study only rose by 16 percent [50].
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Taulbee’s 2019 [75]
report shows an increase from a recent minimum of under 10,000 bachelor’s degrees conferred
in 2009 to over 30,000 degrees in 2019 (see Figure 1B [75]).
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
It is undeniable that there has been
a rapid increase in interest in computer science courses at higher-education institutions.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
We see
similar demand in K-12 with CSforAll1 initiatives.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Educators have struggled with how to cope with
new and exacerbated challenges in computing education - ranging from how to scale up to handle
new enrollments to which teaching techniques are best during this time of growth.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
The COVID-19
pandemic has added additional investigation into the challenges of online instruction.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
At the same time, attendance at the ACM SIGCSE Technical Symposium has continued to in-
crease year over year, coinciding with a similar increase in the number of submissions [25, 74].
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Computing faculty are eagerly trying new teaching methodologies to address the challenges they
face with growth in enrollment and with ever-emerging technologies.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Other computing education
research (CER) venues are also seeing increases.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
The SIGCSE Board 2 added a fourth conference to
its yearly schedule to address the growing need for CS education in parts of the world not served
by existing conferences [30].
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
There are many open questions in computing education that the CER
community must answer [9, 33].
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
While this growth in the CER community is exciting, the real beneﬁt comes when community
members report innovations in a manner that allows other researchers to build on them and educa-
tors to appropriately apply them in their own contexts.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
For a community to systematically advance
knowledge, its members must be able to understand published work thoroughly enough to perform
replications, conduct meta-analyses, and build theories [4, 8, 12, 16, 19, 21, 24, 29, 41, 42, 59].
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
In
education literature, this concept is referred to as the Scholarship of Teaching and Learning or SoTL.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
SoTL is broadly deﬁned as “posing [a problem] about an issue of teaching or learning, study of the
problem through methods appropriate to the disciplinary epistemologies, application of results to
practice, communication of results, self-reﬂection, and peer review” [8].
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
In 2004, Fincher and Petre posited that most CER publications lack the type of evidence or
replications required for meta-analysis or theory building [16].
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Clear also observed that many of
the standard research practices used to demonstrate rigor in “traditional”, non-human, computing
topic areas are ignored or even actively avoided when performing CER [11].
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
These observations
occurred just prior to the transition to what Guzdial and du Boulay [22] call the “modern era” of
CER in 2005 with the creation of the International Computing Education Research Conference
(ICER).
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Because this work was more than ten years ago, there is a need to understand how well
more recently published research provides the type of information necessary for the computing

text:
2We use SIGCSE to represent the ACM Special Interest Group in Computer Science Education as a community of computing

text:
We use SIGCSE Technical Symposium (SIGCSE TS) to represent the Technical
Symposium on Computer Science Education, which is commonly called SIGCSE.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
This diﬀerentiates the community from
the conference.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Empiricism in CER
3
education community to systematically advance knowledge.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Our work complements recent work
in understanding the quality of reporting in CER literature [4, 24, 29, 41, 42, 45] and more broadly [7,
12, 19, 60] to support replication.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Therefore, to provide insight into the current state of CER publications, the goal of this study
is:
To characterize the reporting of empiricism in Computing Education Research
literature by identifying whether publications include content necessary for re-
searchers to perform replications, meta-analyses, and theory building.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
To accomplish this goal, we ﬁrst deﬁned the CER Empiricism Assessment Rubric for analyzing
CER papers.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
The rubric identiﬁes the information necessary for replication, meta-analysis, and
theory building.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
We then applied the rubric to 427 papers published in the Technical Symposium
on Computer Science Education (SIGCSE TS), International Symposium on Computing Education Re-
search (ICER), Conference on Innovation and Technology in Computer Science Education (ITiCSE),
ACM Transactions on Computing Education (TOCE) and Computer Science Education (CSE) during
2014 and 2015 to categorize published work and identify whether information needed for repli-
cation is present and clearly labeled.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
We chose these years because they were the most recent
editions of the conference when we began our research.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
In addition, these years coincide with ten
years after the ﬁrst ICER [1, 2], a conference focused on empirical CER and just as the number of
empirical research papers published at the SIGCSE TS began to increase.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Therefore, the results of
this analysis will serve as a baseline against which we can compare the results of a similar analysis
in subsequent years.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
The contributions of this paper are:
• The CER Empiricism Assessment Rubric for evaluating the completeness of the empirical
content of CER papers;
• An analysis of the empiricism present in CER papers published during 2014 and 2015 in ﬁve
CER venues;
• A baseline for future analyses; and
• Overall observations that serve as suggestions for how the CER community can advance
scientiﬁc reporting standards.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
2
RELATED WORK
We explore related work in three ways: 1) CER literature reviews and community reﬂection; 2)
guidelines for reporting empirical work, particularly educational work, outside of computing; and
3) an overview of recommendations for replications.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
These views of the related literature show the
current eﬀorts in transforming and increasing the impact of CER results and transfer into practice
that support learners at a variety of levels and needs.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
We close the section with a discussion on
where our work ﬁts into the broader literature.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
2.1
CER Literature Reviews and Community Reflection
There have been many reviews of computing education literature, especially over the last 20
years.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
[28] and Clear [11] provide early reﬂections on CER and they note the biases
in the broader research community, including computing, against (computing) education research
as a distinct and robust research area [11, 28].
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Supporting the growth and recognition of CER and
researchers through literature reviews and community reﬂection continues the progress made by
the CER community in the last 15-20 years.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
4
Heckman, Carver, Sherriﬀ, and Al-Zubidy
For this section, our focus is on reviews that categorize or evaluate CER papers and reporting
quality, including the use of theories and measurements.
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
We do not include systematic literature
reviews on speciﬁc topics in computing education if they do not also include some discussion
on the quality of or challenges in aggregation due to reporting (e.g., reviews of K-12 [20, 70];
introductory programming [46, 53, 73]; teaching assistants [47]; tools, languages, environments in
K-12 [44]; meta-cognition and self-regulated learning [55]; and mapping of theories in CER [69]).
title: arXiv:2107.01984v1  [cs.CY]  2 Jul 2021

text:
Table 1 summarizes the reviews that include categorization or evaluation of CER papers from a
quality and reporting perspective.
